when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is associated or dissociated with the sphere of form (rūpāyatana).
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the sphere of form, much less observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the sphere of form!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated with the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the eye-element."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the eye-element, much less observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the eye-element.
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the realms of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated from the realms of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated with the form realm."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the realm of form, let alone observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the realm of form!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena, how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either associated with or dissociated from the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the eye-consciousness element."

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the eye-consciousness element, much less observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the eye-consciousness element.
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mental consciousness; how much less could one observe omniscience as being either associated or dissociated with the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mental consciousness!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with eye-contact."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of eye-contact, much less observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with eye-contact.
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, much less perceive all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition."

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of any feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, much less observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated from those feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the various feelings arising conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of any feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition; how much less could one observe omniscience as being either associated or dissociated from these feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated with the earth element."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the earth element, much less observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the earth element.
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness; how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with its causes and conditions."
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of causes and conditions, how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with causes and conditions!

One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), or the phenomena produced from these conditions.

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), or the phenomena produced from these conditions, how much less could one observe whether omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is associated or dissociated with the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, or the phenomena produced from these conditions!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is associated or dissociated with ignorance (avidyā)."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of ignorance, much less observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with ignorance!

One does not observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated with conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated with or dissociated from the perfection of generosity."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the perfection of generosity, much less observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the perfection of generosity!
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom; how much less could one observe all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated with the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as either associated with or dissociated from internal emptiness."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of internal emptiness, much less observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with internal emptiness!

One does not observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature; how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the four foundations of mindfulness."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the four foundations of mindfulness, much less observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with them!

One does not observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the four right efforts, let alone the eight branches of the noble path; how much less could one observe omniscience as being either associated or dissociated with the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated with the noble truth of suffering."

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the Noble Truth of Suffering, much less observe whether all-knowledge is associated with or dissociated from the Noble Truth of Suffering.
One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated with or dissociated from the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, or the Path.

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, how much less could one observe omniscience as being either associated or dissociated with the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as being either associated with or dissociated from the four dhyānas."

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, how much less could one observe omniscience as being either associated or dissociated with the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated from the eight liberations."

Since one does not even perceive the existence of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, how much less could one observe omniscience as being either associated or dissociated with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the emptiness gate of liberation, how much less could one observe whether omniscience is associated with or dissociated from the emptiness gate of liberation!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Why is this?

Since one does not even perceive the existence of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with them!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is associated or dissociated with any of the doors of dhāraṇī."
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of any dharani-gates, how much less could one observe whether omniscience and the dharani-gates are associated or dissociated!
One does not contemplate whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with any samādhi-gate. Why is this?
Since one does not even perceive the existence of any samādhi-gate, how much less could one contemplate whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with any samādhi-gate!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is associated with or dissociated from the Stage of Extreme Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi).

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the Stage of Utmost Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi), much less observe whether all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is associated or dissociated with the Stage of Utmost Joy!

One does not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the Stage of Purity (vimalā-bhūmi), the Stage of Radiance (prabhākari-bhūmi), the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (arciṣmatī-bhūmi), the Stage of Difficult Victory (sudurjayā-bhūmi), the Stage of Presence (abhimukhī-bhūmi), the Stage of Far-Going (dūraṅgamā-bhūmi), the Immovable Stage (acalā-bhūmi), the Stage of Good Intelligence (sādhumatī-bhūmi), or the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā-bhūmi).

Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud, how much less could one observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe all-knowledge as being either associated with or dissociated from the five eyes."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the five eyes, much less observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the five eyes.
One does not observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the six supernormal powers.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā), much less observe whether omniscience (sarvajñatā) is associated with or dissociated from the six supernormal powers! Śāriputra!
Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is associated or dissociated with the ten powers of a buddha."
Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the existence of the Buddha’s ten powers, much less contemplate whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with them!

One does not contemplate whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; how much less could one observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with the thirty-two marks of a great man."

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive the thirty-two marks of a great man, much less observe whether omniscience is associated with or dissociated from those thirty-two marks of a great man!
One does not observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the eighty minor marks. Why is this?

Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.

Why is this? Because one does not even perceive all-knowledge; how much less could one observe whether all-knowledge is associated or dissociated with all-knowledge!

Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as being either associated or dissociated from a Buddha."
Why is this? Since one does not even perceive the existence of a Buddha, how much less could one observe whether omniscience is associated or dissociated with the Buddha!

Why is this? Because all-knowledge is itself the Buddha, and the Buddha is himself all-knowledge.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the existence of causal conditions, nor do they cling to the non-existence of causal conditions. They do not cling to a self in causes and conditions, nor to a non-self in causes and conditions; they do not cling to a self in the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, or the phenomena produced from these conditions, nor to a non-self in the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, or the phenomena produced from these conditions.

They do not cling to the tranquility of causal conditions, nor do they cling to the non-tranquility of causal conditions; they do not cling to the tranquility of the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, and the phenomena produced from these conditions, nor do they cling to the non-tranquility of the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, and the phenomena produced from these conditions;

They do not cling to the signless nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices, nor do they cling to the signful nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices; they do not cling to the signless nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, nor do they cling to the signful nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.
They do not cling to the wishless nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices, nor do they cling to the wishful nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices;

they do not cling to the wishless nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, nor do they cling to the wishful nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.
Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not form this thought:
‘I am practicing the perfection of wisdom.’”
They do not form this thought:
"I am not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
They do not form this thought:
"I neither practice nor do not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I neither do not practice nor do not not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*."
"Śāriputra! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom is associated with such dharmas, it should be said that they are associated with the perfection of wisdom."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Six.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter One: Correspondence, Part Three, Section Four.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of giving; nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

“When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of internal emptiness; nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of suchness; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of entering the state of right determination; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of attaining the stage of non-retrogression; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of maturing sentient beings; and they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of purifying Buddha-fields."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four applications of mindfulness; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path;

they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the noble truth of suffering, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four dhyānas, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions."

"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eight liberations; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all the doors of samādhi."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the Ground of Extreme Joy; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, or the Ground of Dharma Clouds."

"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the fleshly eye; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the Dharma eye, or the Buddha eye."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ten powers of a Buddha; nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eighty secondary signs."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the state of constant equanimity."

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all-knowledge; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, the knowledge of all aspects, or the subtle knowledge of all aspects.”

"When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of transcending the fruit of a stream-enterer; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of transcending the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, nor for the sake of transcending the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of any bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas."
"Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive any differentiation in the nature of phenomena."
“Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of divine sight; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of the minds of others; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of recollecting past lives; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of miraculous powers; and they do not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the supernormal power of the realization of the exhaustion of outflows."

Why is this? Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not even perceive the existence of a "perfection of wisdom" being practiced; how much less could they perceive a bodhisattva performing the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) as cultivated by a Tathāgata!
“Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are associated with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form this thought:

'By means of the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the divine eye, I shall see everywhere in the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all sentient beings dying here and being born there.'"
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear-knowledge, I shall hear everywhere throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the sounds of the Dharma being preached by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds, I shall fully know the mental states and mental factors of all sentient beings in as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal knowledge of recollecting past lives, I shall universally recall all the matters concerning the past lives of all sentient beings in as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of miraculous feats, I shall go everywhere throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, to make offerings, pay homage, revere, and praise all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within those worlds."
They do not form this thought:

"By means of the supernormal power of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows, I shall universally observe all sentient beings in Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, to see whether their outflows are exhausted or not."
"Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom are associated with such dharmas as these, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), because they are in accord with this perfection of wisdom, they are well able to establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the realm of nirvana without remainder (anupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇadhātu). No evil Māras can gain any advantage over them; all afflictions (kleśa) are subdued and extinguished, and all worldly affairs are accomplished according to their wishes."

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in each of the ten directions, together protect and keep such a bodhisattva in mind, so that they do not fall back into the levels of any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha.
In each of the ten directions, throughout as many world-systems as there are sands in the Ganges River,
there were the Cāturmahārājakāyika devas, the Trāyastriṃśa devas, the Yāma devas, the Tuṣita devas, the Nirmāṇarati devas, the Paranirmitavaśavartin devas,
the Brahmakāyika devas, the Brahmapurohita devas, the Brahmakāyika devas, the Mahābrahmā devas, the Ābhāsvara devas, and the Parīttābha devas.

The Heaven [of the Four Great Kings], the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three,

the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Heaven of Brahmā’s Retinue, the Heaven of Brahmā’s Ministers, the Heaven of Great Brahmā, the Heaven of Limited Light, the Heaven of Infinite Light, the Heaven of Pervasive Light, the Heaven of Limited Purity, the Heaven of Infinite Purity, the Heaven of Universal Purity, the Heaven of Vastness, the Heaven of Limited Vastness,
the Heaven of Infinite Vastness, the Heaven of Vast Fruit, the Heaven Without Strife, the Heaven Without Heat, the Heaven of Excellent Appearance, and the Heaven of Excellent Vision.
The Akaniṣṭha Heaven and all other śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas shall together protect such a bodhisattva;
whatever they undertake shall be free from obstacles, and all physical and mental ailments shall be completely healed.
Should they have karmic offenses that would otherwise result in bitter retribution in future lives, these shall instead manifest as light experiences.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s compassion for all sentient beings is all-pervasive.

“Śāriputra! By the majestic power of practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), this bodhisattva mahāsattva, with little application of effort, is able to evoke the most excellent and sovereign gateways of dhāraṇī and samādhi, causing them to manifest swiftly. In whatever place they are born, they always succeed in serving all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, until they realize the sought-after unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), never being separated from the Buddhas throughout that interval.”

“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), because they are in accord with such a perfection of wisdom, they attain these and other immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, and subtle merits.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts as:
'There are phenomena that are either associated or dissociated with other phenomena, or equal or unequal.'"
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive any dharma that is either associated or dissociated with another dharma, nor any that is equal or unequal.
"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form such a thought as:
'I shall realize perfect awakening within the dharma-realm either quickly or not quickly.'"
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive even the slightest dharma that can manifest perfect awakening within the dharmadhātu.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any dharma that is separate from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), nor do they perceive the dharma-realm as existing apart from all dharmas. Furthermore, they do not perceive all dharmas as being identical to the dharma-realm, nor do they perceive the dharma-realm as being identical to all dharmas.
“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form this thought:
‘The dharma-realm can act as the causal condition for all phenomena.’”
They do not form this thought:
"All phenomena can act as causes and conditions for the dharma-realm.
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not form such thoughts.
"This dharma can realize the dharma-realm; this dharma cannot realize the dharma-realm.
Why is this so, Śāriputra?
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not even perceive dharmas, much less perceive any dharma that could either realize the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) or fail to realize it! "Śāriputra,
because these bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in association with such dharmas, they should be said to be associated with the perfection of wisdom."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive form as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with form;

they do not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."

"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the sense base of the eye as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the sense base of the eye;

they do not perceive the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind."

"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the sphere of form as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the sphere of form;

they do not perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eye-element as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the eye-element;

they do not perceive the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the realm of form as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the realm of form;

they do not perceive the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena."

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eye-consciousness element as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the eye-consciousness element;

they do not perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.”

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive eye-contact as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with eye-contact;

they do not perceive ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”

"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive that feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive that emptiness is associated with feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition;

they do not perceive that feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition are associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive that emptiness is associated with feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the earth element as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the earth element;

they do not perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive conditions as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with conditions;

they do not perceive the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, or the phenomena produced from conditions as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, the dominant condition, or the phenomena produced from conditions."
"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive ignorance as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with ignorance;

they do not perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."

"When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the perfection of generosity as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the perfection of generosity;

they do not perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive inner emptiness as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with inner emptiness.

They do not perceive outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as being associated with emptiness; nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive true suchness as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with true suchness;

they do not perceive the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the four foundations of mindfulness;

they do not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path."

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the noble truth of suffering as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the noble truth of suffering;

they do not perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four dhyānas as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the four dhyānas;

they do not perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eight liberations as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the eight liberations;

they do not perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the gate of liberation of emptiness as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the gate of liberation of emptiness;

they do not perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any dhāraṇī-doors as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with any dhāraṇī-doors;
they do not perceive any samādhi-doors as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with any samādhi-doors.”

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the Ground of Extreme Joy as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the Ground of Extreme Joy;

they do not perceive the Ground of Stainless Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-reaching Progress, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the Ground of Stainless Purity up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.”

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the five eyes as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the five eyes;
they do not perceive the six supernormal powers as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the six supernormal powers."

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the ten powers of a buddha as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the ten powers of a buddha;

they do not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the thirty-two marks of a great man as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the thirty-two marks of a great man;
they do not perceive the eighty secondary signs as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the eighty secondary signs."

"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the quality of non-forgetfulness;
they do not perceive the state of constant equanimity as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the state of constant equanimity."

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with all-knowledge;

they do not perceive the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.”

"When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the fruit of a stream-enterer as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the fruit of a stream-enterer;

they do not perceive the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, nor the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, as being associated with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being associated with the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, or the awakening of a pratyekabuddha."

“When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices;

they do not perceive the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as being conjoined with emptiness, nor do they perceive emptiness as being conjoined with the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.”
“Śāriputra! If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom can engage in such correspondence as this, it is the foremost correspondence with emptiness.”

“Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are thus conjoined with emptiness, they do not fall into the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; rather, they purify buddha-fields, mature sentient beings, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Śāriputra! Among all forms of mental engagement, the mental engagement with the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom is the foremost, the most honored, the most excellent, the highest, the most sublime, the supreme, the unsurpassed, the peerless, and the equal to the unequaled.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because this perfection of wisdom is the most supreme of all associations; it is the association with emptiness, the association with signlessness, and the association with wishlessness. For these reasons, it is the most supreme.

“Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are in accord with this perfection of wisdom, you should know that they have either received the prediction of their future buddhahood or are close to receiving it.”
“Śāriputra! By means of this correspondence, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring great benefit to immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings.”
“Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form the thought:
‘I am associated with the perfection of wisdom.’”
He does not form this thought:
"I have received the prediction; I shall certainly become a Buddha," or "I am close to receiving the prediction.
He does not form such thoughts:
"I am able to adorn and purify Buddha-fields," nor does he form the thought:
"I am able to bring sentient beings to maturity."
Nor does one form this thought:
"I shall realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment I seek, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."

"Why is this? Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma that is separate from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu); he does not perceive the dharma-realm as separate from all dharmas; he does not perceive all dharmas as being the dharma-realm, nor does he perceive the dharma-realm as being all dharmas. He does not perceive any dharma that practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā); he does not perceive any dharma that receives the prediction of buddhahood; he does not perceive any dharma that shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; he does not perceive any dharma that purifies a buddha-field; and he does not perceive any dharma that matures sentient beings."

"Why is this? Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the notion of a self, the notion of a sentient being, the notion of a life-principle, the notion of a living soul, the notion of a nourisher, the notion of a person, the notion of an individual, the notion of a mind-born, the notion of a youth, the notion of an agent, the notion of one who causes to act, the notion of an originator, the notion of one who causes to originate, the notion of an experiencer, the notion of one who causes to experience, the notion of a knower, or the notion of a seer."

Why is this? Because the self, sentient beings, and so forth are ultimately neither born nor do they perish. Since they are ultimately neither born nor do they perish, how could they possibly practice the *prajñāpāramitā* or attain various meritorious benefits?

“Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom because they do not perceive the arising of sentient beings; they practice the perfection of wisdom because they do not perceive the cessation of sentient beings; they practice the perfection of wisdom because they know all sentient beings are empty; they practice the perfection of wisdom because they know all sentient beings are non-self; they practice the perfection of wisdom because they know all sentient beings are unapprehendable; they practice the perfection of wisdom because they know all sentient beings are detached; they practice the perfection of wisdom because they know the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings is not the nature of sentient beings.”

“Śāriputra! Among all the meditative applications of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), that which is associated with emptiness is the foremost; that which is associated with the perfection of wisdom is the most honored and supreme, such that none can equal it.”

“Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice in such a manner, they are universally able to bring forth the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, the eighty minor marks, the quality of non-forgetfulness, the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas.”

“Śāriputra! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and are in accord with this perfection of wisdom, they ultimately do not give rise to obstructive thoughts of stinginess, immorality, anger, laziness, distraction, or wrong wisdom.
The perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom manifest spontaneously, continuously, and without interruption.”
4. Chapter on Rebirth, Part One: Chapter Four, Section One. At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
From where did those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwell securely in the perfection of wisdom pass away before being born here?
And from this place, after passing away, where will they be reborn?
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwell securely in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are some who pass away from other buddha-fields and are reborn here; some who pass away from Tuṣita Heaven and are reborn here; and some who pass away from among humans and are reborn among humans.”

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, passes away from a buddha-field in another direction and is reborn here, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly become conjoined with the perfection of wisdom.”

Because they are in union with the *prajñāpāramitā*, as soon as they are reborn, profound and wondrous Dharma gates swiftly manifest before them; from that time forward, they will constantly and rapidly remain in union with the *prajñāpāramitā*. In whatever place they are born, they will always encounter the Buddhas, making offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them, thereby enabling them to gradually bring the *prajñāpāramitā* to full completion.

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, passes away from Tuṣita Heaven and is reborn here, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is for the most part bound by only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*). The perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom appear before them with mastery and are never forgotten; likewise, all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi appear before them with mastery and are never forgotten.”

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, passes away from among humans and is reborn among humans, this bodhisattva mahāsattva—except for those who are non-retrogressive—is of dull faculties. Although they diligently cultivate the perfection of wisdom, they cannot quickly become attuned to it, nor have they yet attained mastery over all the doors of dhāraṇī and the doors of samādhi.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
As for what you asked later: 'Where will those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwell securely in the perfection of wisdom be reborn after they pass away from this world?'"

"Śāriputra, because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is constantly associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), when they pass away from this place, they are reborn in other buddha-fields, traveling from one buddha-field to another. In every place of birth, they always encounter the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, making offerings to them, honoring them, respecting them, and praising them; until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), they never depart from the Buddhas."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, because they lack skillful means, enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas; they are also able to practice the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has attained meditative concentration (dhyāna), they are reborn in the long-lived heavens; when their lifespan there is exhausted, they return to birth in the human realm, where they encounter various Buddhas, making offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them.

Although they practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, their faculties remain dull and obtuse rather than clear and sharp, and they lack supreme skillfulness in all that they do.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas, and are also able to practice the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva lacks skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), they abandon the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) and are born in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).

It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva likewise possesses dull and blunt faculties (*indriya*) rather than those that are very clear and sharp; whatever they undertake is not extremely skillful.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
they enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (maitrī), and enter the immeasurable states of compassion (karuṇā), sympathetic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekṣā)."
They enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
they practice the perfection of generosity, and practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

they abide in internal emptiness, and abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They abide in suchness; they abide in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

they practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they abide in the noble truth of suffering, and they abide in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
They practice the eight liberations; they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities;
they practice the door of liberation of emptiness, and they practice the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they practice all doors of dhāraṇī and they practice all doors of samādhi.
They cultivate the five eyes; they cultivate the six supernormal powers;

they cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha; they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness; and they cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
They practice the knowledge of all things (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), they are not reborn by the power of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), or the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*); rather, wherever they are born, they always encounter Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising them, and never remaining apart from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
"You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment within this Bhadrakalpa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
they enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness, and enter the immeasurable states of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;

they enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, and enter the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), he is not reborn by the power of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), or the formless attainments (*ārūpya*). Instead, he is reborn in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) within a great kṣatriya clan, a great brāhmaṇa clan, a great householder clan, or a great merchant clan, solely for the sake of maturing sentient beings, and not for the sake of being defiled by craving for future existence (*punarbhava*).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
they enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (maitrī), and enter the immeasurable states of compassion (karuṇā), sympathetic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekṣā).
They enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), they are not reborn by the power of the dhyānas, the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), or the formless attainments (*ārūpya*). Instead, they may be born among the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Thirty-three Gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, or the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods. For the sake of maturing sentient beings and for the sake of purifying the buddha-fields, they constantly encounter the Buddhas, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising them, never allowing such encounters to pass in vain.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
they enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (maitrī), and enter the immeasurable states of compassion (karuṇā), sympathetic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekṣā)."
They enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they pass away from this place and are reborn in the Brahma-world as a Great Brahmā King, whose majestic power and brilliance exceed those of the other Brahmās by many hundreds of thousands of times.

Traveling from their own celestial realms to various buddha-fields, and from one buddha-field to another, there are among them bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have not yet realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; they exhort them to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Furthermore, for those who have already realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment but have not yet turned the wheel of Dharma, they request them to turn the wheel of Dharma, desiring to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bound to one more birth who, by virtue of their skillful means, enter the first dhyāna, and enter the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
they enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness, and enter the immeasurable states of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity."

They enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the meditative absorption of the sphere of nothingness, and the meditative absorption of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
they practice the perfection of generosity, and practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

they abide in internal emptiness, and abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They dwell securely in suchness; they dwell securely in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the element of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm;

they practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they dwell securely in the noble truth of suffering, and they dwell securely in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
They practice the eight liberations; they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;
they practice the door of liberation of emptiness, and they practice the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they practice all doors of dhāraṇī and they practice all doors of samādhi.
They cultivate the five eyes; they cultivate the six supernormal powers;

they cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha; they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness; and they cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
They cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not born through the power of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), or the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*); rather, they manifest before, serve, attend upon, and make offerings to the present Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas. Having diligently practiced the holy life under these Buddhas, they pass away from that state and are reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.

Throughout the full span of his lifespan, his faculties remained unimpaired; endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, he was surrounded and escorted by immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of celestial beings. Sporting with supernatural powers, he descended to be born among humans, where he manifested the practice of asceticism, realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turned the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).

They are not born in the desire realm, nor are they born in the form realm, nor are they born in the formless realm. They travel through various buddha-fields, going from one buddha-field to another, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas. They cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and gradually realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) that they seek."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, having attained mastery over the six supernormal powers, travel from one buddha-field to another. In the buddha-fields they pass through, there are no names for śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or the like; there is only the Single Vehicle and those who practice true brahmacarya."

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in all buddha-fields; they practice the perfection of wisdom, gradually fulfilling and purifying the buddha-fields and bringing sentient beings to maturity, never flagging or becoming indolent.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained mastery over the six supernormal powers and sport therein, traveling from one buddha-field to another; the lifespan of the sentient beings in the buddha-fields they pass through is beyond calculation."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva makes offerings, shows respect, honors, and praises immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in all buddha-fields; while practicing the perfection of wisdom, they gradually fulfill and purify the buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity, never experiencing weariness or fatigue.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained mastery over the six supernormal powers and sport therein, traveling from one world-system to another. There are world-systems where the names of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha are not heard."

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva goes to that world to extol and praise the Triple Gem of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, causing all sentient beings to give rise to profound pure faith; by means of this, they will experience benefit and peace for a long night.

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva passes away from this life, he will be reborn in a buddha-field where he will cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, gradually realizing the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment he seeks, thereby bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,
from the first production of the thought of enlightenment, through courageous and diligent effort, attain the first dhyāna, and attain the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
they attain the immeasurable state of loving-kindness, and attain the immeasurable states of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity."

They attain the meditative concentration of the sphere of infinite space, and they attain the meditative concentrations of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
they practice the perfection of generosity, and they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

they abide in internal emptiness, and they abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
