They abide in suchness; they abide in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

They practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They abide in the noble truth of suffering; they abide in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
They practice the eight liberations; they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities;
they practice the gate of liberation of emptiness, and they practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they practice all doors of dhāraṇī, and they practice all doors of samādhi.

They practice the stage of Perfect Joy; they practice the stage of Freedom from Defilement, the stage of Radiant Light, the stage of Blazing Wisdom, the stage of Difficult to Conquer, the stage of Presence, the stage of Far-Going, the stage of Immovability, the stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the stage of Dharma Clouds.
They practice the five eyes; they practice the six supernormal powers;

they practice the ten powers of a Buddha; they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They practice the quality of non-forgetfulness; they practice the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
they practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); and they practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is not born in the desire realm, not born in the form realm, and not born in the formless realm; rather, they are always born in places where they can benefit sentient beings, bringing them profit, peace, and happiness.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have already practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; from their first production of the thought of awakening, they enter the bodhisattva’s state of certainty (*samyaktva-niyāma*) and even attain the stage of non-retrogression."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,

having previously cultivated the six pāramitās and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, are able from the very first production of the thought of enlightenment to successively realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, deliver immeasurable multitudes of beings, and enter parinirvāṇa within the realm of great nirvana without remainder."
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma he has taught shall remain in the world for one kalpa or more than one kalpa, bringing benefit and happiness to boundless sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!..."

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have previously cultivated the six pāramitās and other bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices; as soon as they first resolve their minds [upon enlightenment], they become endowed with the prajñāpāramitā. Surrounded before and behind by immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they travel through various buddha-fields, going from one buddha-field to another, making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, while bringing sentient beings to maturity and purifying buddha-fields.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Seven.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One, Chapter Four:

On the Transformation of Birth, Part Two "Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom and attain the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions. They enter and emerge from the nine successive attainments in both forward and reverse order with sovereign mastery and playful ease, a state that is not within the domain of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva sometimes enters the first dhyāna; arising from the first dhyāna, he enters the meditative absorption of cessation (nirodhasamāpatti);
arising from the meditative absorption of cessation, he enters the second dhyāna; arising from the second dhyāna, he enters the meditative absorption of cessation;
arising from the meditative absorption of cessation, he enters the third dhyāna; arising from the third dhyāna...
With focused attention, he enters the attainment of cessation; from the attainment of cessation, he arises and enters the fourth dhyāna;
from the fourth dhyāna, he arises and enters the attainment of cessation; from the attainment of cessation, he arises and enters the sphere of infinite space;
from the sphere of infinite space, he arises and enters the attainment of cessation; from the attainment of cessation, he arises and enters the sphere of infinite consciousness.

From the sphere of infinite space absorption, he emerges and enters the sphere of infinite consciousness absorption; from the sphere of infinite consciousness absorption, he emerges and enters the attainment of cessation;
from the attainment of cessation, he emerges and enters the sphere of nothingness; from the sphere of nothingness, he emerges and enters the attainment of cessation;
from the attainment of cessation, he emerges and enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception...
Emerging from the meditative absorption on the sphere of perception, he enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, he enters the first dhyāna. "Śāriputra!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, is skillful in means regarding all meditative attainments; he transcends them in succession with sovereign mastery, yet remains undefiled and unattached therein."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have already attained the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; although they have already attained the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness; although they abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; and although they have already attained the eight liberations, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities—yet they do not take up the fruit of stream-entry, nor the fruit of once-returning, nor the fruit of non-returning, nor the fruit of arhatship, nor the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha."

“By means of skillful means while practicing the perfection of wisdom, this bodhisattva mahāsattva causes sentient beings to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; to practice the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; to abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; and to practice the eight liberations, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, thereby attaining the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.”
“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already practiced the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence,
meditative concentration, and wisdom, and although he has already dwelled in internal emptiness and external emptiness...”
...emptiness of the internal and external, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth,
emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration,
emptiness of essential nature, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, and emptiness of the unapprehendable.
...emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
although they already abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas,
the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable—
Regarding the realm of deliberation: although they have already cultivated all the gates of dhāraṇī and the gates of samādhi;

and although they have already cultivated the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.
Although he has already cultivated the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

although he has already cultivated the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
and although he has already cultivated the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity.
Although they have already cultivated the knowledge of all things (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*),

and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they do not grasp at unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). This is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, through their skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) in practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), cause sentient beings to practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and even to practice the knowledge of all things, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects, thereby leading them to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Śāriputra! The fruit-knowledge of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is itself the patience (kṣānti) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Śāriputra, you should know this!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling on the stage of non-retrogression and securely established in the perfection of wisdom, is able to perform such deeds.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have long been established in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, as well as other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, and who have purified the Tuṣita heaven palace.
"Śāriputra!
You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment within this Bhadrakalpa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, have already attained the four dhyānas,
the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; they have already attained the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Having already cultivated the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
having already cultivated the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;
having already cultivated the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; having already cultivated the one...
The gates of all dhāraṇīs and the gates of samādhis; having already cultivated the stages of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
having already cultivated the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

and having already cultivated the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Regarding the unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*): they have already cultivated the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;

they have already cultivated all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), yet they have not yet fully realized the noble truths in the present.
"Śāriputra, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by only one more birth.
Furthermore, Śāriputra..."

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they travel through various worlds, proceeding from one buddha-field to another, purifying buddha-fields and establishing sentient beings in unsurpassed enlightenment.
"Śāriputra!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva must pass through immeasurable and incalculable great eons before realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they constantly apply themselves with vigor to benefit sentient beings, never uttering speech that leads to what is meaningless, and never giving rise to physical or mental actions that lead to what is meaningless.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), constantly and diligently exerting themselves to benefit sentient beings; they travel from one buddha-field to another, severing for all sentient beings the paths to the three evil destinies and skillfully establishing them upon the paths to the good destinies."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although abiding in the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā),
always take the perfection of generosity (dāna-pāramitā) as their foremost, practicing it with vigor and bestowing all forms of happiness upon all sentient beings."
Possessing constancy and without weariness, they provide food to all sentient beings who need food,
drink to those who need drink, vehicles to those who need vehicles, clothing to those who need clothing, flowers and perfumes to those who need flowers and perfumes,
necklaces to those who need necklaces, dwellings to those who need dwellings, and beds and couches to those who need beds and couches.
He provided bedding and furniture; he gave lamps to those who needed light; he gave wealth and grain to those who needed them;
he gave precious gems to those who needed them; he gave music and entertainment to those who needed them; and he gave attendants to those who needed them.
In accordance with their various needs for material requisites, he joyfully bestowed these gifts so that they lacked nothing, and having thus given, [he continued].
They exhort others to cultivate the path to *sambodhi*.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although abiding in the six *pāramitās*, take the *śīla-pāramitā* as their constant preeminent guide. They practice it with vigor, possessing the pure restraint of body, speech, and mind, and they exhort all sentient beings to likewise practice such restraint, causing them to swiftly reach fulfillment."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they abide in the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), take the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) as their constant preeminent guide. They practice it with vigor, remaining far removed from all thoughts of anger and malice, and they exhort all sentient beings to likewise practice such patience so that they may swiftly bring it to fulfillment."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they abide in the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), take the perfection of diligence (vīrya-pāramitā) as their constant preeminent guide. They practice with valor, fully cultivating all wholesome dharmas (kuśala-dharma), and they exhort all sentient beings to likewise cultivate such diligence so that it may be swiftly perfected."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they abide in the six perfections, always take the perfection of meditative concentration as their foremost; they practice with valor, fully cultivate all superior śamatha, and exhort all sentient beings to likewise cultivate such supreme samādhi, causing them to swiftly reach fulfillment."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although abiding in the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), take the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) as their constant preeminent guide. They practice with valor, fully cultivating all forms of insight (*vipaśyanā*), and they exhort all sentient beings to likewise cultivate such supreme wisdom, causing them to swiftly reach fulfillment."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, practicing the perfection of wisdom, through skillful means manifest bodies like those of Buddhas. They enter everywhere into the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and devas, preaching the true Dharma in the various languages of those beings to enable them to obtain supreme benefit and peace."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, manifest emanation bodies like those of a Buddha. They travel throughout as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River, proclaiming the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings; they make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they listen to the sublime Dharma in the presence of those Buddhas and purify Buddha-fields. Surveying the subtle and pure characteristics of the most excellent Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, they themselves bring forth supremely adorned and pure Buddha-fields, wherein they establish great bodhisattvas bound to only one more birth, causing them to swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they are fully adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, their faculties are sharp, preeminent, and utterly pure, such that all sentient beings who see them cannot help but feel love and reverence, giving rise to a pure mind. Through this guidance, according to their faculties and inclinations, they cause them to gradually realize the nirvana of the three vehicles."
“In this way, Śāriputra,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should train in the purification of the actions of body, speech, and mind.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; although they attain the most excellent and sharp faculties, they do not rely on these to hold themselves in high esteem or look down upon others."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,

from their first generation of the mind until they have attained the stage of non-retrogression, constantly abide in the perfections of generosity and ethical discipline, and at all times do not fall into the evil destinies."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from their first generation of the mind until they have attained the stage of non-retrogression, never abandon the ten paths of wholesome action."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfections of generosity and ethical discipline, become wheel-turning kings endowed with the seven treasures. They transform beings through the Dharma and not through what is contrary to the Dharma, establishing sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action, while also bestowing wealth and treasures upon those who are destitute."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, abiding in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, receive the retribution of hundreds of thousands of universal monarchs; they encounter immeasurable hundreds of thousands of buddhas, making offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them, never allowing such encounters to pass in vain."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwell securely in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. They constantly act as a lamp of Dharma for sentient beings blinded by false views, and they also hold this light to constantly illuminate themselves; until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they never abandon this illumination of the Dharma."
Śāriputra! By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly brings forth all the buddha-dharmas before him. "Therefore, Śāriputra!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, there is no possibility for sinful karma of body, speech, or mind to arise even momentarily.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
what are called the faulty bodily actions, faulty verbal actions, and faulty mental actions of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought as this:”
"This is the body; it is by means of this that I initiate bodily action.
This is speech; it is by means of this that I initiate vocal action.
This is the mind; it is by means of this that I initiate mental action."
"Śāriputra! These are called the blameworthy physical actions, the blameworthy verbal actions, and the blameworthy mental actions of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."
Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the body or bodily action, they do not apprehend speech or vocal action, and they do not apprehend the mind or mental action.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should acquire [the notion of] body, speech, mind, and their respective actions, and thereby give rise to thoughts of stinginess and greed, violation of precepts, anger and resentment, laziness, distraction, or corrupt wisdom—if such thoughts arise, they are not called a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Therefore, Śāriputra,
it is impossible for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom to give rise to such a thought.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,

it is impossible that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom would give rise to the three types of coarse heaviness (dauṣṭhulya) of body, speech, and mind.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they are able to purify all coarseness of body, able to purify all coarseness of speech, and able to purify all coarseness of mind.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness of body, speech, and mind?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, they do not apprehend the body nor the bodily dysfunctions; they do not apprehend speech nor the vocal dysfunctions; they do not apprehend the mind nor the mental dysfunctions.”
In this way, Śāriputra,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, they are able to purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness of body, speech, and mind.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first generation of the mind of awakening, constantly delights in upholding the ten paths of wholesome action; does not give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka, nor give rise to the mind of a pratyekabuddha; and always gives rise to a mind of compassion toward all sentient beings, desiring to extract them from suffering, and always gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness, desiring to bestow happiness upon them.

Śāriputra! I also say that such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to purify the three kinds of coarse heaviness (*dauṣṭhulya*) of body, speech, and mind, because their power of mind to benefit and bring happiness to sentient beings is superior.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, thereby purifying the path to enlightenment."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the bodhi-path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they do not apprehend physical action or the heaviness of physical action; they do not apprehend verbal action or the heaviness of verbal action; they do not apprehend mental action or the heaviness of mental action. They do not apprehend the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, or the perfection of wisdom. They do not apprehend śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas.”
Śāriputra! This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s path to awakening. Why is that?
Because one does not apprehend any phenomenon whatsoever through the path to enlightenment.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; no one is able to obstruct them as they proceed upon the path to enlightenment."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
for what reason is it that when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six pāramitās, no one is able to obstruct them as they proceed upon the path to enlightenment?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they do not cling to form (rūpa), nor do they cling to feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), mental formations (saṃskāra), or consciousness (vijñāna).”
They do not cling to the sense-base of the eye, nor do they cling to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
they do not cling to the sense-base of forms, nor do they cling to the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;
they do not cling to the eye-element, nor do they cling to the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
They do not cling to the realm of form, nor do they cling to the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena;
they do not cling to the realm of eye-consciousness, nor do they cling to the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness;
they do not cling to eye-contact, nor do they cling to the contacts of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
One does not cling to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; one does not cling to the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.
One does not cling to the earth element, nor to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

One does not cling to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), nor to the immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), or to the phenomena produced from these conditions.

They do not cling to ignorance; they do not cling to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
They do not cling to the perfection of generosity; they do not cling to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

He does not cling to internal emptiness; he does not cling to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

He does not cling to suchness; he does not cling to the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.

They do not cling to the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not cling to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path;
they do not cling to the noble truth of suffering, nor do they cling to the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
they do not cling to the four dhyānas, nor do they cling to the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
They do not cling to the eight liberations; they do not cling to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases;
they do not cling to the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor to the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they do not cling to any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor to any of the doors of samādhi.

He does not cling to the Ground of Extreme Joy; he does not cling to the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.
He does not cling to the five eyes; he does not cling to the six supernormal powers.

He does not cling to the ten powers of a Buddha; he does not cling to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They do not cling to the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor do they cling to the eighty secondary signs;
they do not cling to the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they cling to the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they do not cling to all-knowledge, nor do they cling to the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
They do not cling to the fruit of stream-entry; they do not cling to the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; they do not cling to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
they do not cling to any of the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and they do not cling to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
“Śāriputra! For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the six perfections, they flourish and blaze forth; no one is able to obstruct them as they proceed upon the path to enlightenment.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, dwelling securely in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are able to swiftly fulfill all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna)."

Because they have accomplished supreme wisdom, they close the gates to all perilous and evil destinies; they do not undergo poverty or lowly status among gods or humans, but possess all faculties complete and a dignified physical appearance, being universally honored, revered, and made offerings to by the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the supreme wisdom accomplished by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished this wisdom, he universally beholds all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges; he universally hears the true Dharma preached by those Buddhas; he universally beholds all the assemblies of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, and he also beholds the signs of the pure merit and adornments of those lands.”

Śāriputra! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished this wisdom, he does not give rise to the notion of a world; he does not give rise to the notion of a Tathāgata; he does not give rise to the notion of the True Dharma; he does not give rise to the notion of a bodhisattva; he does not give rise to the notion of a śrāvaka; he does not give rise to the notion of a pratyekabuddha; he does not give rise to the notion of self; he does not give rise to the notion of others; and he does not give rise to the notion of a buddha-field.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity, they do not apprehend the perfection of generosity;

and although they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they do not apprehend the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom."
“By means of this wisdom, although the bodhisattva mahāsattvas abide in internal emptiness, they do not apprehend internal emptiness;

and although they abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they do not apprehend external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in suchness (*tathatā*), they do not apprehend suchness;

although they abide in the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), immutability (*ananyathātva*), equality (*samatā*), the nature of being free from birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), they do not apprehend the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not apprehend the four foundations of mindfulness;

and although they cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they do not apprehend the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the noble truth of suffering, they do not apprehend the noble truth of suffering;
although they abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they do not apprehend the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”
"By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the four dhyānas, they do not apprehend the four dhyānas;
although they cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they do not apprehend the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments."
“By means of this wisdom, although the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the eight liberations, they do not apprehend the eight liberations;

although they cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they do not apprehend the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, they do not apprehend the gate of liberation of emptiness;
although they cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they do not apprehend the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate all dharanī-doors, they do not apprehend any dharanī-doors;
although they cultivate all samādhi-doors, they do not apprehend any samādhi-doors.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the Ground of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), they do not apprehend the Ground of Extreme Joy;

and although they cultivate the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the Ground of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), the Ground of Difficult Victory (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), the Ground of Far-Going (*dūraṃgamā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Immovability (*acalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), they do not apprehend the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the five eyes, they do not apprehend the five eyes;
although they cultivate the six supernormal powers, they do not apprehend the six supernormal powers.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, they do not apprehend the ten powers of a buddha;

and although they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they do not apprehend the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
"By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the thirty-two marks of a great man, they do not apprehend the thirty-two marks of a great man;
and although they cultivate the eighty secondary signs, they do not apprehend the eighty secondary signs."
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness, they do not apprehend the quality of non-forgetfulness;
although they cultivate the nature of constant equanimity, they do not apprehend the nature of constant equanimity.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they do not apprehend all-knowledge;

although they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they do not apprehend the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.”
“By means of this wisdom, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate all the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, they do not apprehend any such practices;
and although they cultivate the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, they do not apprehend that unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Śāriputra! This is called the supreme wisdom accomplished by bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

By accomplishing this wisdom, bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to swiftly fulfill all Buddha-dharmas; yet, although they are able to fulfill all Buddha-dharmas, they have no attachment to or grasping at any dharmas, because the intrinsic nature of all dharmas is empty.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,
practicing the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, attain the purification of the five eyes."
"What are these five?
They are the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the Dharma eye, and the Buddha eye.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure fleshly eye?
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
“Śāriputra! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and can clearly see one hundred yojanas;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and can clearly see two hundred yojanas;”
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and can clearly see three hundred yojanas;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and can clearly see four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, or even up to a thousand yojanas;
and there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and can clearly see the entire continent of Jambudvīpa.
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure flesh eye and can clearly see two great continents;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure flesh eye and can clearly see three great continents;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure flesh eye and can clearly see four great continents.
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and are clearly able to see a small thousand-world system;
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and are clearly able to see a medium thousand-world system;
and there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure fleshly eye and are clearly able to see a great thousand-world system.
“Śāriputra! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to attain the pure fleshly eye.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure divine eye?
The Buddha addressed the venerable Śāriputra, saying:

“Śāriputra! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye (*divyacakṣus*), by which they are able to see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Four Great Kings (*cāturmahārājakāyika*), and they know it as it truly is;

they are able to see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the gods of the Thirty-three (*trāyastriṃśa*), the Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens, and they know it as it truly is.”
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye, by which they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the Brahmakāyika devas, and they know it as it truly is;
they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika, and Mahābrahmā devas, and they know it as it truly is.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye, by which they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the Ābhāsvara devas, and they know it as it truly is;
they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Ābhāsvara devas, and they know it as it truly is.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye, by which they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the Śuddhāvāsa deities, and they know it as it truly is;
they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of all the Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna deities, and they know it as it truly is.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye, by which they are able to see everything seen by the divine eyes of the Bṛhatphala devas, and they know it as it truly is;
they are also able to see everything seen by the divine eyes of the Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Bṛhatphala devas, and they know it as it truly is.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye; they are able to see everything that the divine eyes of the gods of the realm of non-perception see, and they know it as it truly is.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye, by which they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of the gods of the Heaven Free from Strife (Abṛha), and they know it as it truly is;

they can see everything seen by the divine eyes of the gods of the Heaven Free from Heat (Atapa), the Good Appearance (Sudṛśa), the Good Vision (Sudarśana), and the Ultimate of Form (Akaniṣṭha) heavens, and they know it as it truly is.

“Śāriputra! There is that which is seen by the divine eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, which the divine eyes obtained by all beings from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven cannot see, nor can they know.”

Śāriputra! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the pure divine eye and are able to see, as they truly know it, how all classes of sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions die here and are reborn there.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure divine eye.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure eye of wisdom?
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
"Śāriputra! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have attained the pure eye of wisdom;
they do not perceive any phenomenon, whether conditioned or unconditioned, nor do they perceive any phenomenon, whether with outflows or without outflows, nor do they perceive any phenomenon..."
Whether mundane or supramundane, one does not perceive any dharma that is either faulty or faultless;
one does not perceive any dharma that is either defiled or pure; one does not perceive any dharma that is either with form or formless;
one does not perceive any dharma that is either with resistance or without resistance; one does not perceive any dharma.
Whether past, future, or present, one does not perceive any dharma—whether bound to the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm;
nor does one perceive any dharma that is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate;
nor does one perceive any dharma that is to be abandoned by vision or to be abandoned by cultivation.
If it is not something to be abandoned, one does not perceive any dharma— whether it be of the learner (*śaikṣa*), of the non-learner (*aśaikṣa*),
or neither of the learner nor the non-learner; indeed, regarding all dharmas, whether in their intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) or their specific distinctions (*viśeṣa*), nothing at all is perceived.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has attained the pure eye of wisdom; regarding all phenomena, he neither sees nor does not see, neither hears nor does not hear, neither cognizes nor does not cognize, and neither perceives nor does not perceive.
“Śāriputra! This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to attain the pure eye of wisdom.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure Dharma-eye?
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
“Śāriputra! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure Dharma-eye are able to know, as it truly is, the various distinctions among individuals (pudgala).
That is to say, they know, as it truly is:”
This is the follower by faith; this is the follower by dharma; this is the one who practices signlessness; this dwells in emptiness; this dwells in signlessness; this dwells in wishlessness.
Furthermore, he knows as it truly is:

"From this, by means of the door of liberation that is emptiness, the five faculties arise; from the five faculties, uninterrupted concentration arises; from uninterrupted concentration, the knowledge and vision of liberation arises; and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, the three fetters are permanently severed, and the fruit of stream-entry is attained."
The view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*), the clinging to precepts and rituals (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), and doubt (*vicikitsā*): these are called the three fetters (*saṃyojana*).

Furthermore, by means of the initial attainment of the path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one attenuates sensual desire and ill-will, thereby attaining the fruit of the once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmin*).
Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion, attaining the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*).
Moreover, by means of the supreme path of cultivation, one exhausts the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms, attaining the fruit of arhatship (*arhattvaphala*).
Sensual desire, desire for the formless, ignorance, conceit, and restlessness—these are called the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms.
Furthermore, one knows it as it truly is:

"From this, through the door of signless liberation, the five faculties arise; from the five faculties, uninterrupted concentration arises; from uninterrupted concentration, the knowledge and vision of liberation arises; and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, the three fetters are permanently severed, and the fruit of stream-entry is attained."
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation initially attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of a once-returner.
Moreover, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of a non-returner.

Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one exhausts the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of arhatship.
Moreover, one knows as it truly is:

"This arises from the door of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) giving rise to the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*); from the five faculties arises uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one permanently severs the three fetters (*trīṇi saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*)."
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation initially attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of once-returner.
Moreover, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of non-returner.

Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one exhausts the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of arhatship.
Moreover, one knows as it truly is:

"This [stream-entry] arises from the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*) produced through the gateways of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā*) and signlessness (*animitta*); from the five faculties arises the uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from the uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one eternally severs the three fetters (*trīṇi saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*)."
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation initially attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of a once-returner.
Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of a non-returner.
Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one exhausts the five higher fetters (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of arhatship.
Moreover, one knows it as it truly is:

"This [stream-entry] arises from the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*) through the gateways of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā*) and wishlessness (*apranihita*); from the five faculties arises immediate concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from immediate concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one eternally severs the three fetters (*trīṇi saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*)."
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation first attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of a once-returner.
Again, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of a non-returner.

Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one exhausts the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of arhatship.
Again, one knows as it truly is:

"This arises from the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*) through the gateways of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*); from the five faculties arises uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and through the knowledge and vision of liberation, one eternally severs the three fetters (*trīṇi saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*)."
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation first attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of once-returner.
Moreover, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion, thereby attaining the fruit of non-returner.

Furthermore, through the further path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), one exhausts the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of arhatship.
Moreover, one knows it as it truly is:

"This arises from the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*) produced by the doors of liberation—emptiness (*śūnyatā*), signlessness (*animitta*), and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*); from the five faculties arises uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from uninterrupted concentration arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and by means of the knowledge and vision of liberation, one eternally severs the three fetters (*trīṇi saṃyojanāni*) and attains the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*)."
Furthermore, by means of the path of cultivation initially attained, one attenuates sensual desire and aversion and realizes the fruit of once-returning.
Again, by means of the superior path of cultivation, one exhausts sensual desire and aversion and realizes the fruit of non-returning.

Furthermore, by means of the superior path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), they exhaust the five fetters pertaining to the higher realms (*pañca ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanāni*) and attain the fruit of arhatship. "Śāriputra,
this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva attaining the pure Dharma-eye."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure Dharma-eye can know things as they truly are:

that there is a certain class of *pudgala* who, by means of the gates of liberation—emptiness (*śūnyatā*), signlessness (*animitta*), and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*)—give rise to the five faculties (*pañcendriya*); from the five faculties, they give rise to uninterrupted concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*); from uninterrupted concentration, they give rise to the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*); and through this knowledge and vision of liberation, they are able to know as it truly is that all phenomena subject to origination (*samudaya-dharma*) are phenomena subject to cessation (*nirodha-dharma*)."
By knowing this, one attains the five supreme faculties that sever all afflictions, and progressively realizes the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
Śāriputra, this is what is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s attainment of the pure Dharma-eye.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the pure Dharma-eye can know things as they truly are:

'This bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having first resolved upon the awakening mind, practices the perfection of generosity and practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; because he has accomplished the faculty of faith, the faculty of diligence, and skillful means, he intends to take up a body that will increase wholesome qualities.'"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva may be born into a great kṣatriya clan,
or a great brāhmaṇa clan, or a great householder clan, or a great merchant clan;
or he may be born among the gods of the Four Great Kings, or the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, or the Yāma heaven, or the Tuṣita heaven...
In the Heaven of the Thirty-three, or among the Gods Who Delight in Emanation, or among the Gods Who Wield Power over Others' Emanations—
dwelling in such places, they bring sentient beings to maturity; according to what sentient beings delight in,
they are able to bestow various kinds of supreme and wonderful articles of pleasure, and are also able to adorn and purify various Buddha-fields with various superior...
By making offerings of exquisite articles and by honoring, respecting, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
they do not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and they never regress until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Dharma-eye.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having attained the pure Dharma-eye, are able to know things as they truly are:

"This bodhisattva-mahāsattva has already received the prediction regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is currently receiving the prediction regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; this bodhisattva-mahāsattva will receive the prediction regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has attained non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; this bodhisattva-mahāsattva may still retrogress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already established himself on the stage of non-retrogression; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet established himself on the stage of non-retrogression.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s supernormal powers are already perfected; this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s supernormal powers are not yet perfected.

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s supernormal powers are already perfected, he is able to travel to Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assemblies of bodhisattva mahāsattvas."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) are not yet perfected, he is unable to travel to the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and the assemblies of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; [the Tathāgata knows:
"this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained supernormal powers," and "this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained supernormal powers";

"this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*)," and "this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained superior faculties; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained superior faculties.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already purified a buddha-field; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet purified a buddha-field.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already brought sentient beings to maturity; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet brought sentient beings to maturity.
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained his great vows; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained his great vows.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already been praised by all the Buddhas; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet been praised by all the Buddhas.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already drawn near to the Buddhas; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet drawn near to the Buddhas."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s lifespan is immeasurable; this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s lifespan is measurable.

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, his community of bhikṣus will be immeasurable; when this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, his community of bhikṣus will be measurable.

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, there will be a community of bodhisattvas; when this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, there will be no community of bodhisattvas.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva exclusively cultivates the practice of benefiting others; this bodhisattva mahāsattva concurrently cultivates the practice of self-benefit;
this bodhisattva mahāsattva undergoes difficult and arduous practices; this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not undergo difficult and arduous practices;
this bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by only one more birth; this bodhisattva mahāsattva is bound by many births.
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already entered his final existence; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet entered his final existence.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already sat upon the seat of sublime enlightenment; this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet sat upon the seat of sublime enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from the interference of Māras; this bodhisattva mahāsattva is subject to the interference of Māras."
"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Dharma-eye.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the pure Buddha-eye?
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:

“Śāriputra! Immediately following the bodhicitta of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they enter the diamond-like samādhi (vajropama-samādhi) and attain the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). They accomplish the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and other immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and supreme merits. At that time, they achieve the unobstructed, unimpeded liberation of the Buddha-eye.”

By attaining such a purified Buddha-eye, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas transcend the sphere of wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; there is nothing they do not see, nothing they do not hear, nothing they do not perceive, and nothing they do not cognize, as they behold all aspects of all phenomena.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the pure Buddha-eye. Śāriputra!
“Only when bodhisattva mahāsattvas have attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment do they obtain such pure Buddha-eyes.

Śāriputra, if bodhisattva mahāsattvas wish to obtain such pure five eyes, they should diligently practice the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

these six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) encompass all pure and wholesome dharmas— namely, the wholesome dharmas of śrāvakas, the wholesome dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the wholesome dharmas of bodhisattvas, and the wholesome dharmas of tathāgatas.
Śāriputra! If one were to ask correctly:
"What dharma is able to encompass all wholesome dharmas?"
One should answer correctly:
"The profound Prajñāpāramitā. Why is this?
Śāriputra!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the birth-mother and foster-mother of all wholesome dharmas, for it is able to give birth to and nourish the *dāna*, *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitās*, as well as the five eyes and other immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable supreme merits.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain such pure five eyes, they should study the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Śāriputra!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should train in these five pure eyes. Śāriputra!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in these five pure eyes, they will certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Eight.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Nine.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The Fourth Chapter on the Arising of Transformations, Part Three:
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are able to bring forth the perfection of the six supernormal powers."
What are the six?
First, the perfection of the superknowledge of the realization of the power of miraculous feats (ṛddhividhi-jñāna-sākṣātkriyābhijñā-pāramitā).
Second, the perfection of the superknowledge of the realization of the power of the divine ear (divyaśrotra-jñāna-sākṣātkriyābhijñā-pāramitā).
Third, the perfection of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of others' minds;
fourth, the perfection of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of recollecting past lives;
and fifth, the perfection of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of the divine eye.
"Sixth is the perfection of the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

“What is the perfection of the supernormal power of the realization of knowledge through the psychic faculties (ṛddhividhi-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) that is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha addressed the venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!...”

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of miraculous feats (*ṛddhividhi-jñāna-abhijñā*), manifesting immeasurable kinds of great miraculous transformations. These include: shaking the great earth and all other things throughout the worlds of the ten directions, each as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; transforming one into many and many into one; appearing and disappearing with rapid, unimpeded ease; passing straight through mountain cliffs and walls as if through space; traveling back and forth through the air like a flying bird; emerging from and submerging in the earth as if in water; walking upon water as if on land; emitting smoke and flames from the body like a blazing high plateau; pouring forth streams of water from the body like the melting of the Snowy Mountains; eclipsing the brilliance of the sun and moon—whose divine merit and majestic power are otherwise difficult to withstand—by stroking them with the hand; and even attaining mastery over rebirth in the Śuddhāvāsa heavens. Such miraculous transformations are immeasurable and boundless.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such supernormal powers of the knowledge of the realm of phenomena (*ṛddhividhi-jñāna*), he does not exalt himself on account of them; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the realm of phenomena, nor to the objects of that supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the realm of phenomena, nor to the one who can attain such a supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the realm of phenomena. He is without attachment toward both attachment and non-attachment.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have realized that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, that their intrinsic nature is detached, and that their intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form such a thought as:

"I shall now manifest the supernormal power of the knowledge of psychic travel for my own amusement or for the amusement of others," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

"Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the superknowledge of the realization of supernormal powers (ṛddhividhi-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā) brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,

what is the perfection of the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear-wisdom (divya-śrotra-jñāna-abhijñā-pāramitā) when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!
There is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who possesses the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear-knowledge, which is most excellent, pure, and surpasses that of humans and devas.”
They are able to hear, exactly as they are, the various sounds of sentient and non-sentient beings throughout each of the worlds of the ten directions,
as numerous as the sands of the Ganges— namely, hearing all the sounds of the hells, the sounds of animals, the sounds of the realm of hungry ghosts,
the sounds of humans, the sounds of devas, the sounds of śrāvakas, the sounds of pratyekabuddhas, the sounds of bodhisattvas, and the sounds of tathāgatas.
The sound of rebuking and reviling birth-and-death; the sound of praising nirvāṇa; the sound of turning one's back on the conditioned;
the sound of advancing toward bodhi; the sound of wearying of outflows; the sound of delighting in the outflow-free;
the sound of extolling the Triple Gem; the sound of subduing heterodox paths; the sound of debating and discerning; and the sound of chanting the sūtras.
The sound of praise, the sound of exhorting the severance of all evils, the sound of teaching the cultivation of all virtues, the sound of rescuing others from suffering and distress,
and the sound of celebrating and comforting with joy— sounds such as these, whether great or small, can be heard everywhere without obstruction or hindrance.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such a function of the divine ear, he does not exalt himself therein; he does not cling to the nature of the supernormal power of the realization of the wisdom of the divine ear, nor does he cling to the matter of the supernormal power of the realization of the wisdom of the divine ear, nor does he cling to one who is able to attain such a supernormal power of the realization of the wisdom of the divine ear. He is without attachment in both clinging and non-clinging.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have realized that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, that their intrinsic nature is detached, and that their intrinsic nature is fundamentally unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form such a thought as:
"I shall now manifest the supernormal power of the divine ear for my own amusement or for the amusement of others," except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the supernormal power of the realization of the divine ear-wisdom that is evoked by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

What is the perfection of the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds (paracittajñāna-abhijñā-pāramitā) realized by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?"
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

There is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who possesses the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds, and is able to know, as they truly are, the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. That is to say, he thoroughly knows those other sentient beings: if they have a mind with attachment, he knows it as a mind with attachment; if they are free from attachment, he knows it as a mind free from attachment.”
If there is a mind of hatred, one knows as it truly is that there is a mind of hatred; if one is free from a mind of hatred, one knows as it truly is that one is free from a mind of hatred.
If there is a mind of delusion, one knows as it truly is that there is a mind of delusion; if one is free from a mind of delusion, one knows as it truly is that one is free from a mind of delusion.
If there is a mind of craving, one knows as it truly is that there is a mind of craving; if one is free from a mind of craving, one knows as it truly is that one is free from a mind of craving.
If there is a mind with grasping, he knows the mind with grasping as it truly is; if there is a mind free from grasping, he knows the mind free from grasping as it truly is.
If the mind is concentrated, he knows the concentrated mind as it truly is; if the mind is distracted, he knows the distracted mind as it truly is.
If the mind is small, he knows the small mind as it truly is; if the mind is great, he knows the great mind as it truly is.
If the mind is uplifted, he knows the uplifted mind as it truly is; if the mind is depressed, he knows the depressed mind as it truly is;
if the mind is tranquil, he knows the tranquil mind as it truly is; if the mind is not tranquil, he knows the untranquil mind as it truly is;
if the mind is agitated, he knows the agitated mind as it truly is; if the mind is not agitated, he knows the non-agitated mind as it truly is.
If the mind is concentrated, he knows the concentrated mind as it truly is; if the mind is not concentrated, he knows the unconcentrated mind as it truly is.
If the mind is liberated, he knows the liberated mind as it truly is; if the mind is not liberated, he knows the unliberated mind as it truly is.
If the mind is with outflows, he knows the mind with outflows as it truly is; if the mind is without outflows, he knows the mind without outflows as it truly is.
If there is a mind with blemish, he knows as it truly is that there is a mind with blemish; if there is no mind with blemish, he knows as it truly is that there is no mind with blemish.
If there is a superior mind, he knows as it truly is that there is a superior mind; if there is no superior mind, he knows as it truly is that there is no superior mind.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such applications of the knowledge of others' minds, he does not exalt himself therein; he is not attached to the nature of the supernormal power of realizing the knowledge of others' minds, nor is he attached to the phenomena of realizing the knowledge of others' minds, nor is he attached to those who can attain such realization of the knowledge of others' minds. He is without attachment in both attachment and non-attachment.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have realized that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, that their intrinsic nature is detached, and that their intrinsic nature is fundamentally unobtainable.
Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not form such a thought as:
"I shall now evoke the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds for my own amusement or for the amusement of others, except solely for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes."
"Śāriputra! This is the perfection of the supernormal power of the knowledge of others' minds, which is induced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

What is the perfection of the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of recollecting past lives, which is brought forth by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the recollection of past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā*), and are able to know, as they truly are, all the matters of the past lives of all sentient beings throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in each of the ten directions—namely, they recollect the matters of their own and others’ past lives for the duration of one thought-moment, ten thought-moments, a hundred thought-moments, a thousand thought-moments, or many hundreds of thousands of thought-moments.”
Or again, he may recollect various past lives spanning one day, ten days, a hundred days, a thousand days, or many hundreds of thousands of days;
or again, he may recollect various past lives spanning one month, ten months, a hundred months, a thousand months, or many hundreds of thousands of months;
or again, he may recollect various past lives spanning one year, ten years, a hundred years, a thousand years, or many hundreds of thousands of years.

Or again, they recollect the various past lives throughout one eon, ten eons, a hundred eons, a thousand eons, many hundreds of thousands of eons, even up to immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of eons; such are their recollections of former existences.

Furthermore, he recollects all past lives throughout the prior limit of existence—namely, at such a time, in such a place, with such a name, such a clan, of such a kind, eating such food, dwelling for such a duration, having such a life span, possessing such longevity, experiencing such pleasure, and undergoing such suffering; how he passed away from that place to be born here, and how he passed away from this place to be reborn there—with such physical characteristics and such speech, whether briefly or in detail, concerning himself or others—he is able to recollect all these past lives.

“Śāriputra! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such power of knowledge regarding past lives, he does not exalt himself therein.
