Is that which is called 'the conditioned' the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas? Is that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas a designation for the conditioned? Is that what a bodhisattva mahāsattva is?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that the designation 'the unconditioned' for all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the designation 'unconditioned' for the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas not also the designation for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it the case that all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, which are designations for the outflow-tainted (*sāsrava*), are themselves the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the designation 'outflow-tainted' applied to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas the same as that of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas which are the designation for 'outflow-free' (anāsrava) constitute a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One!
Is the untainted designation for the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas itself the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“No, World-Honored One!
Is that which is the designation for the arising of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that which is the designation for the arising of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas that is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the designation 'the cessation of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices' itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the designation 'the cessation of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas' the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One!
Is that which is called ‘the further increase of the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
"No, World-Honored One! Is the designation 'the excellent increase of the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas' itself the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One!
Is it not the case that the designation ‘not increasing in goodness’ for all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
"No, World-Honored One! Is it not the case that the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is a designation for 'wholesome,' and that this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it the case that 'the designation for all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that involve faults' refers to a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One! Is it the case that the unexcelled,
perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is a synonym for ‘fault’ for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it not the case that 'the designation for the faultless practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is the designation 'faultless' for the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas also the designation for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One!
Is it the case that the designation ‘having afflictions’ applied to all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas refers to those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?”
"No, World-Honored One! Is it the case that the unexcelled,
perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas has 'the increase of afflictions' as its designation, and that this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that the designation 'the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas being free from afflictions' refers to a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is the supreme,
perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas— which is a designation for the absence of afflictions— the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are merely designations for the mundane world, and that these are what constitute a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is the designation 'the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas' the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that the designation for all the supramundane practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is 'bodhisattva-mahāsattva'?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas— the transcendent designation for it— not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One!
Is that which is the designation for the increase of defilement in all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the designation for the defilement of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is that which is the designation for the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
“No, World-Honored One!
Is the pure designation for the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it not the case that all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are merely designations for being subject to birth and death? "Is this what constitutes a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas— which is a designation for birth-and-death— the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are merely designations for Nirvāṇa, and that these are the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas— which is a designation for nirvāṇa— the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that the designation 'all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' being within is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is it that the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, as an internal designation, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that the designation 'all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' being external constitutes a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is the designation 'the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas exists externally' the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it that the designation for all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas existing between these two extremes is itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is it the case that the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, as designated by the term 'between the two,' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is that which is called 'the increase of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' itself the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One! Is that which is called 'the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas' obtainable as a designation for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is it not the case that the designation 'the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' is unapprehendable— that this is what constitutes a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Is that which is the ineffable designation for the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
"No, World-Honored One!
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti:

“What meaning do you perceive when you say that the designation ‘form’ is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘feeling,’ ‘perception,’ ‘volitional formations,’ and ‘consciousness’ are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If form, or feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ultimately non-apprehendible because their nature does not exist, how much less so are there designations for form, or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether form is permanent or impermanent’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are permanent or impermanent’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether permanent or impermanent—and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for form as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent,’ or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasure or pain’ applied to form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether pleasure or pain’ applied to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether pleasant or painful—and if feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness—whether pleasant or painful—are ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be a designation for the pleasure or pain of form, or a designation for the pleasure or pain of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation of form as either self or non-self is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either self or non-self is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether as self or non-self—and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether as self or non-self—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so are there any designations for form as ‘self’ or ‘non-self,’ or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as ‘self’ or ‘non-self’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as self or as non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as self or as non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether form is pure or impure’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are pure or impure’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether pure or impure—and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether pure or impure—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of form, or a designation for the purity or impurity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether form is empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are empty or not empty’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form is empty or not empty, or if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty or not empty—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for ‘form being empty or not empty,’ or designations for ‘feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness being empty or not empty’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form, whether with marks or without marks, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether with marks or without marks, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so can there be a designation for form as being ‘with marks’ or ‘without marks,’ or a designation for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being ‘with marks’ or ‘without marks’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether form has aspiration or lacks aspiration, or whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness have aspiration or lack aspiration—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘form having aspiration or lacking aspiration,’ or designations for ‘feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness having aspiration or lacking aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether form is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether form is tranquil or not tranquil, or whether feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of form, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether form is tranquil or not tranquil" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are tranquil or not tranquil" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether form is detached or not detached’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are detached or not detached’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether form is detached or not detached, whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are detached or not detached—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of form, or a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either detached or non-detached is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as either detached or non-detached is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of form, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designations of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether conditioned or unconditioned—and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether conditioned or unconditioned—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for form as conditioned or unconditioned, or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as conditioned or unconditioned?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of form, whether with outflows or without outflows, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, whether with outflows or without outflows, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether with outflows or without outflows—and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for form with outflows or without outflows, or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness with outflows or without outflows?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of form,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or the cessation of form’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘the arising or the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of form, or the arising and ceasing of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designation ‘arising and ceasing of form’ and the designations ‘arising and ceasing of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the arising or ceasing of form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the arising or ceasing of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘form that is wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for ‘feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are wholesome or unwholesome’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether blameworthy or blameless—and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether blameworthy or blameless—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for form as ‘blameworthy’ or ‘blameless,’ or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as ‘blameworthy’ or ‘blameless’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as either faulty or faultless is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as either faulty or faultless is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether with afflictions or without afflictions” applied to form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designation “whether with afflictions or without afflictions” applied to feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘form with afflictions or without afflictions,’ or designations for ‘feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness with afflictions or without afflictions’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation of form, whether mundane or supramundane, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether mundane or supramundane, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether mundane or supramundane—and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for mundane or supramundane form, or designations for mundane or supramundane feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of form, or the defilement and purification of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of form, or a designation for the defilement and purification of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of form, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Furthermore,

based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘form belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If form belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for form belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of form as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether form is internal, external, or between the two” is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations “whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are internal, external, or between the two” are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

If form—whether internal, external, or between the two—is ultimately unapprehendable because its nature does not exist, how much less so can there be a designation for form being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness being internal, external, or between the two?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of form—

whether internal, external, or in between— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness— whether internal, external, or in between— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether form is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are obtainable or unobtainable’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If form is either obtainable or unobtainable, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are either obtainable or unobtainable—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation of ‘form being obtainable or unobtainable,’ or designations of ‘feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness being obtainable or unobtainable’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether form is obtainable or unobtainable" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are obtainable or unobtainable" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
