The First Part: Chapter Seven on Instruction and Teaching, Number Fourteen.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, with what meaning in mind do you say: [that all phenomena are empty]?"

Is it that the designation "eye-base" is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and likewise, the designations "ear-base," "nose-base," "tongue-base," "body-base," and "mind-base" are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“Blessed One!

Since the eye-base, as well as the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-base, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-base is permanent or impermanent’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is permanent or impermanent’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-base is permanent or impermanent, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are permanent or impermanent—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the eye-base, or designations for the permanence or impermanence of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasant or painful’ applied to the eye-base is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether pleasant or painful’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure or pain of the eye-base, or the pleasure or pain of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, cannot ultimately be apprehended because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure or pain of the eye-base, or designations for the pleasure or pain of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that the designation "pleasure" or "pain" in relation to the eye-base is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "pleasure" or "pain" in relation to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the sense-base of the eye is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-base is self or non-self, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are self or non-self—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the eye-base as ‘self’ or ‘non-self,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as ‘self’ or ‘non-self’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "self" or "non-self" regarding the sense base of the eye is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "self" or "non-self" regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to the eye-base is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the purity or impurity of the eye-base, or the purity or impurity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, is ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the eye-base, or designations for the purity or impurity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base as pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-base is empty or not empty’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-base is empty or not empty’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-base is empty or not empty, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty or not empty, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the eye-base being empty or not empty, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases being empty or not empty?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the eye-base is empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or without signs’ applied to the eye-base is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with signs or without signs’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the sense-base of the eye has characteristics or lacks characteristics, or whether the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind have characteristics or lack characteristics—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be the designation ‘the sense-base of the eye has characteristics or lacks characteristics,’ or the designations ‘the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind have characteristics or lack characteristics’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the eye-base is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the eye-base is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of the eye has aspiration or lacks aspiration, and if the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind have aspiration or lack aspiration—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the sphere of the eye having aspiration or lacking aspiration, or designations for the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind having aspiration or lacking aspiration?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether there is aspiration or no aspiration" regarding the eye-base is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether there is aspiration or no aspiration" regarding the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-base is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-base is tranquil or not tranquil, whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the eye-base, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base as either tranquil or non-tranquil is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as either tranquil or non-tranquil is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-base is detached or not detached’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is detached or not detached’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-base is detached or not detached, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are detached or not detached—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the eye-base, or a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases?”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the eye-base is detached or not detached' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is detached or not detached' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ applied to the eye-base is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of the eye, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the conditioned or unconditioned nature of the sense-base of the eye, or designations for the conditioned or unconditioned natures of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind?
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the eye-base is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of the eye—whether with outflows or without outflows—and the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the sense-base of the eye as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or designations for the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the sense-sphere of the eye,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the sense-spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the eye-base’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the eye-base, or the arising and ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘arising and ceasing of the eye-base,’ or the designations ‘arising and ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the eye-base is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the sense base of the eye is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-base, whether wholesome or unwholesome, and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, whether wholesome or unwholesome, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-base as ‘wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as ‘wholesome or unwholesome’?”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the eye-base is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of the eye—whether it be blameworthy or blameless—and if the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—whether they be blameworthy or blameless—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the blameworthy or blameless nature of the sphere of the eye, or designations for the blameworthy or blameless nature of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the eye-base is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of the eye—whether it has afflictions or is free from afflictions—and the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—whether they have afflictions or are free from afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the sense-base of the eye having afflictions or being free from afflictions, or designations for the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind having afflictions or being free from afflictions?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the eye-base is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of the eye-base, whether mundane or supramundane, is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designations of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, whether mundane or supramundane, are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of the eye, whether mundane or supramundane, and the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, whether mundane or supramundane, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the sense-base of the eye as mundane or supramundane, or designations for the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as mundane or supramundane!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the defilement or purification of the eye-base’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the defilement or purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the eye-base, or the defilement and purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the eye-base, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the eye-base belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, or mind-base belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-base belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the eye-base belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-base as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether the eye-base is internal, external, or between the two” is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is internal, external, or between the two” are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-base exists internally, externally, or in between the two; or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base exists internally, externally, or in between the two—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-base existing internally, externally, or in between the two, or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base existing internally, externally, or in between the two!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the eye-base,

whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that the designations "the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, whether internal, external, or between the two, are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-base is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-base can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended—since these are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the eye-base, or a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the eye-base is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Furthermore, Subhūti!

Based on what meaning do you say that the designation for the sense-base of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Venerable Subhūti replied: “Blessed One,

if even the sense-base of form, or the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less so can there be a designation for the sense-base of form, or designations for the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the sense-base of form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations for the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the sphere of form is permanent or impermanent’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or phenomena are permanent or impermanent’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form—whether permanent or impermanent—and the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the sphere of form, or a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the sense-sphere of form as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasant or painful’ applied to the sense base of form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pleasant or painful’ applied to the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of the sphere of form, or the pleasure and pain of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of the sphere of form, or a designation for the pleasure and pain of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the sense-sphere of form is pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the sense base of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the self and non-self of the sphere of form, and the self and non-self of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘self and non-self’ for the sphere of form, and the designations ‘self and non-self’ for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the sense-base of form as self or as non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as self or as non-self are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to the sense-base of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the purity or impurity of the sphere of form, and the purity or impurity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the sphere of form, or designations for the purity or impurity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the sphere of form— whether pure or impure— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena— whether pure or impure— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the sphere of form is empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or mental phenomena are empty or not empty’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the sphere of form is empty or not empty, or whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty or not empty—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sphere of form, or a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the sphere of form is empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether with signs or signless” applied to the sense-base of form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designation “whether with signs or signless” applied to the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the form-base (rūpāyatana), whether with signs or signless, and if the sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental-object bases (śabdāyatana, gandhāyatana, rasāyatana, spraṣṭavyāyatana, dharmāyatana), whether with signs or signless, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘with signs’ or ‘signless’ for the form-base, and the designations ‘with signs’ or ‘signless’ for the sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental-object bases!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form-base as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, or mental-object-base as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the sphere of form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether there is aspiration or lack of aspiration regarding the sphere of form, or whether there is aspiration or lack of aspiration regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be a designation for ‘aspiration or lack of aspiration’ regarding the sphere of form, or a designation for ‘aspiration or lack of aspiration’ regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the sense-sphere of form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the sphere of form is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the sphere of form is tranquil or not tranquil, or whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects are tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the sphere of form, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form base as either tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases as either tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the sphere of form is detached or not detached’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or phenomena are detached or not detached’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the sphere of form is detached or not detached, or whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are detached or not detached—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the sphere of form, or a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the sense-base of form—

whether it is detached or not detached— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena— whether they are detached or not detached— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the sphere of form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the conditioned and unconditioned aspects of the sense-base of form, and the conditioned and unconditioned aspects of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations for the conditioned and unconditioned aspects of the sense-base of form, and the designations for the conditioned and unconditioned aspects of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for the sense-base of form, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation for the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the sense-sphere of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of form—whether with outflows or without outflows—and the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the sense-base of form as ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or designations for the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena as ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the sense-base of form—

whether with outflows or without outflows— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designations of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena— whether with outflows or without outflows— are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the sphere of form’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or ceasing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the sphere of form, or the arising and ceasing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the sphere of form, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the sphere of form is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation of form-constituent as either wholesome or unwholesome is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designations of sound, odor, taste, tangible object, and mental-object constituents as either wholesome or unwholesome are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ‘wholesome or unwholesome’ of the sphere of form, or designations for the ‘wholesome or unwholesome’ of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the sense-base of form— whether wholesome or unwholesome— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena— whether wholesome or unwholesome— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the sphere of form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form—whether blameworthy or blameless—and the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—whether blameworthy or blameless—are ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the blameworthy or blameless nature of the sphere of form, or designations for the blameworthy or blameless nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the sphere of form as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! What meaning do you perceive such that you say:

‘The designation of the sense-base of form as having afflictions or being without afflictions is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as having afflictions or being without afflictions are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the sphere of form has afflictions or is free from afflictions, or whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena have afflictions or are free from afflictions—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the sphere of form having afflictions or being free from afflictions, or designations for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena having afflictions or being free from afflictions!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the sphere of form has afflictions or is free from afflictions is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena have afflictions or are free from afflictions is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether mundane or supramundane’ for the sphere of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether mundane or supramundane’ for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of form—whether mundane or supramundane—and the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the mundane or supramundane sense-base of form, or designations for the mundane or supramundane sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation for the sense-base of form, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations for the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, whether mundane or supramundane, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to the sphere of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the sphere of form, or the defilement and purification of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the sphere of form, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the sphere of form, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the sense-base of form belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form belongs to birth-and-death or belongs to nirvana, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena belong to birth-and-death or belong to nirvana—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the sphere of form belonging to birth-and-death or belonging to nirvana, or a designation for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena belonging to birth-and-death or belonging to nirvana!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the sphere of form belongs to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations 'whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena belong to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa' are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “whether the sphere of form is internal, external, or between the two” is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are internal, external, or between the two” are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form—whether internal, external, or between the two—is ultimately unobtainable because its nature does not exist, how much more so is there a designation for the sphere of form being internal, external, or between the two, or even a designation for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena being internal, external, or between the two?!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the sphere of form is internal, external, or between the two' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are internal, external, or between the two' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether the sphere of form can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations “whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended” are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the obtainability or unobtainability of the sphere of form, or a designation for the obtainability or unobtainability of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation (*adhivacana*) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the sphere of form is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

On what basis do you say that the designation 'eye-element' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations 'ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-element' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ‘eye-element,’ or designations for the ‘ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that the designation "eye-element" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-element" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element is permanent or impermanent’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is permanent or impermanent’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-element is permanent or impermanent, or whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is permanent or impermanent—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the eye-element, or designations for the permanence or impermanence of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element,

whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
"Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

'The designation of the eye-sphere as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; likewise, the designation of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-spheres as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva'?"
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of the eye-element, or the pleasure and pain of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of the eye-element, or designations for the pleasure and pain of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the eye-element is pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element is pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the eye-element is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the self or non-self of the eye-element, or the self or non-self of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be such designations as ‘self or non-self’ for the eye-element, or designations as ‘self or non-self’ for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element as self or as non-self" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element as self or as non-self" are a bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ regarding the eye-element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ regarding the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-element is pure or impure, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements are pure or impure—since these are ultimately non-apprehensible because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the eye-element, or designations for the purity or impurity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-element as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element is empty or not empty’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is empty or not empty’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-element is empty or not empty, or whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is empty or not empty—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element being empty or not empty, or a designation for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element being empty or not empty!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the eye-element is empty or not empty" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is empty or not empty" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element has signs or is signless’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element has signs or is signless’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element, whether with signs or without signs, and if the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, whether with signs or without signs, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element as ‘with signs’ or ‘without signs,’ or designations for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements as ‘with signs’ or ‘without signs’!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element, whether with signs or without signs," is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designations "the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, whether with signs or without signs" are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the eye-element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-element has aspiration or lacks aspiration, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element has aspiration or lacks aspiration—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element having aspiration or lacking aspiration, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element having aspiration or lacking aspiration?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the eye-element has aspiration or is without aspiration" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element has aspiration or is without aspiration" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is tranquil or not tranquil’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-element is tranquil or not tranquil, or whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element being tranquil or not tranquil, or designations for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element being tranquil or not tranquil!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-element as either tranquil or non-tranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements as either tranquil or non-tranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element is detached or not detached’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is detached or not detached’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-element is distant or not distant, or whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are distant or not distant—since these are ultimately non-apprehensible because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element being distant or not distant, or a designation for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements being distant or not distant!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element is either detached or not detached" is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designations "the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are either detached or not detached" are a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Twenty-Four.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Division: Chapter Seven on Instruction and Teaching, Part Fifteen.
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say this?”

Is it that the designation "conditioned" or "unconditioned" applied to the eye-element is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and likewise, the designation "conditioned" or "unconditioned" applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element as conditioned or unconditioned, or a designation for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements as conditioned or unconditioned?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the eye-element— whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements— whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the eye constituent is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind constituents are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element—whether with outflows or without outflows—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element as ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements as ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-element,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the eye-element’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or ceasing of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the eye-element, or the arising and ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, are ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be such designations as ‘the arising and ceasing of the eye-element’ or ‘the arising and ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the arising or ceasing of the eye-element" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the arising or ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the eye constituent is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind constituents are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and likewise the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehensible because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element as ‘wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements as ‘wholesome or unwholesome’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether wholesome or unwholesome" applied to the eye-element is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether wholesome or unwholesome" applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element has faults or is without faults’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element has faults or is without faults’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element—whether with fault or without fault—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements—whether with fault or without fault—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element being with fault or without fault, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements being with fault or without fault!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-element as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the eye-element with afflictions’ or ‘the eye-element without afflictions’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element being ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements being ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element,

whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that the designations "the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element, whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether worldly or supramundane” applied to the eye-element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designation “whether worldly or supramundane” applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element—whether mundane or supramundane—and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the mundane or supramundane eye-element, or designations for the mundane or supramundane ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the eye-element—

whether mundane or supramundane— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements— whether mundane or supramundane— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element is afflicted or purified’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is afflicted or purified’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the eye-element, and the defilement and purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the eye-element, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-element, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

‘The designation “the eye-element, whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,” is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,” are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa, these are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist; how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation 'the eye-element,

whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations 'the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,' are a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “eye-consciousness-element” whether it is internal, external, or between the two is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-elements” whether they are internal, external, or between the two are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element—whether internal, external, or between the two—is ultimately unobtainable because its nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-element being internal, external, or between the two, or designations for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element being internal, external, or between the two?
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element, whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that the designations "the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, whether internal, external, or between the two, are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-element is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element is obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended, and if the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended—since these are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the eye-element, or a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the eye-element,

whether obtainable or unobtainable" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, whether obtainable or unobtainable" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
On what basis do you say:

'The designation for the realm of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations for the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva'?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied,

“World-Honored One! If the realm of form, or the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the realm of form, or designations for the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the realm of form is permanent or impermanent’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or phenomena are permanent or impermanent’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the permanence or impermanence of the form realm, or the permanence or impermanence of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘permanence or impermanence’ for the form realm, and the designations ‘permanence or impermanence’ for the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation of ‘pleasure’ or ‘suffering’ regarding the realm of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations of ‘pleasure’ or ‘suffering’ regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of the form realm, or the pleasure and pain of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of the form realm, or designations for the pleasure and pain of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of "whether pleasant or painful" regarding the realm of form is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of "whether pleasant or painful" regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the realm of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the self and non-self of the form realm, and the self and non-self of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be designations for the self and non-self of the form realm, or designations for the self and non-self of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "self" or "non-self" regarding the form realm is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designations "self" or "non-self" regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ regarding the realm of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the purity or impurity of the form realm, or the purity or impurity of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the form realm, or a designation for the purity or impurity of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the realm of form is empty or not empty’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are empty or not empty’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the realm of form is empty or not empty, or whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are empty or not empty—all these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less so could there be a designation for the ‘emptiness or non-emptiness of the realm of form,’ or designations for the ‘emptiness or non-emptiness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as either empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as either empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the realm of form is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sign-possessing and signless aspects of the form realm, and the sign-possessing and signless aspects of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘sign-possessing’ and ‘signless’ for the form realm, and the designations ‘sign-possessing’ and ‘signless’ for the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as having signs or being signless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena as having signs or being signless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the form realm is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether there is aspiration or non-aspiration in the form realm, or whether there is aspiration or non-aspiration in the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for ‘aspiration or non-aspiration in the form realm,’ or designations for ‘aspiration or non-aspiration’ in the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether there is aspiration or no aspiration" regarding the form realm is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether there is aspiration or no aspiration" regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the realm of form is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or phenomena are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the realm of form is tranquil or not tranquil, or whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be an expression for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the realm of form, or expressions for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as either tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena as either tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the realm of form is detached or not detached’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena are detached or not detached’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the realm of form is distant or not distant, or whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena are distant or not distant—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the distance or non-distance of the realm of form, or designations for the distance or non-distance of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as either secluded or not secluded is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms as either secluded or not secluded is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation for the form realm, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations for the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the conditioned and unconditioned of the form realm, and the conditioned and unconditioned of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations for the conditioned and unconditioned of the form realm, and the designations for the conditioned and unconditioned of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation for the form realm—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations for the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms— whether conditioned or unconditioned— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti!
