Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the form realm is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the tainted and untainted form realm, and the tainted and untainted realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tainted and untainted form realm, or designations for the tainted and untainted realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the form realm—

whether with outflows or without outflows— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms— whether with outflows or without outflows— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or the ceasing of the form-element’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or the ceasing of the sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, or phenomenon-element’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the form realm, or the arising and ceasing of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the form realm, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the realm of form is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation of whether the form-element (rūpadhātu) is wholesome or unwholesome is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations of whether the sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, or mental-object-element (dharmadhātu) are wholesome or unwholesome are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the wholesome or unwholesome nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and likewise the wholesome or unwholesome nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), are ultimately unobtainable because their intrinsic nature does not exist, how much more so the designations for the wholesome or unwholesome nature of the form realm, and the designations for the wholesome or unwholesome nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the form realm—

whether wholesome or unwholesome— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena— whether wholesome or unwholesome— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation of the form realm as either faulty or faultless is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms as either faulty or faultless are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the offense or non-offense of the form realm, and the offense or non-offense of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations of ‘offense’ or ‘non-offense’ for the form realm, and the designations of ‘offense’ or ‘non-offense’ for the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether guilty or non-guilty" regarding the realm of form is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether guilty or non-guilty" regarding the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the realm of form is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the existence or non-existence of afflictions within the realm of form, and the existence or non-existence of afflictions within the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be such designations as ‘the existence or non-existence of afflictions in the realm of form’ or ‘the existence or non-existence of afflictions in the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm,

whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental-object realms, whether with afflictions or without afflictions, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the form realm, whether mundane or supramundane,’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms, whether mundane or supramundane,’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the mundane and supramundane realms of form, and the mundane and supramundane realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the mundane and supramundane realm of form, or designations for the mundane and supramundane realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the form realm—

whether mundane or supramundane— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental-object realms— whether mundane or supramundane— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘the defilement or purification of the realm of form’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the defilement or purification of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the form realm, as well as the defilement and purification of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the form realm, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the defilement or purification of the form realm is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation for the defilement or purification of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation “the form realm, whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “the sound, odor, taste, tactile, and mental-object realms, whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,” are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the form realm belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the form realm belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the form realm as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object realms as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation of the form-element (rūpadhātu), whether it be internal, external, or between the two, is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations of the sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, and mental-object-elements (śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, dharmadhātu), whether they be internal, external, or between the two, are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the realm of form (*rūpa-dhātu*)—whether internal, external, or between the two—and if the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharma-dhātu*)—whether internal, external, or between the two—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation (*adhivacana*) for a realm of form being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects being internal, external, or between the two!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "whether the realm of form is internal, external, or between the two" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designations "whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or phenomena are internal, external, or between the two" are a bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the realm of form can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and phenomena can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the realm of form can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended, and if the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended—since these are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the realm of form, or a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the form-element is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental-object element is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Furthermore, Subhūti!

Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘eye-consciousness element’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element, as well as the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "eye-consciousness element" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-consciousness element is permanent or impermanent’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element is permanent or impermanent’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether permanent or impermanent—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the eye-consciousness element is permanent or impermanent" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element is permanent or impermanent" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasant or painful’ for the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pleasant or painful’ for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of the eye-consciousness element, or the pleasure and pain of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of the eye-consciousness element, or a designation for the pleasure and pain of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "pleasure" or "pain" in relation to the eye-consciousness element is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "pleasure" or "pain" in relation to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the eye-consciousness element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether self or non-self—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether self or non-self—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as ‘self’ or ‘non-self,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as ‘self’ or ‘non-self’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element as either self or non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as either self or non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ regarding the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ regarding the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-consciousness element is pure or impure, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element is pure or impure—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the eye-consciousness element, or designations for the purity or impurity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the eye-consciousness element is pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element is pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-consciousness element is empty or not empty’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element is empty or not empty’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-consciousness element is empty or not empty, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are empty or not empty, they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element being empty or not empty, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements being empty or not empty!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the eye-consciousness element is empty or not empty is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element is empty or not empty is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or without signs’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with signs or without signs’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-consciousness element has characteristics or lacks characteristics, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements have characteristics or lack characteristics—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element having characteristics or lacking characteristics, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements having characteristics or lacking characteristics!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the visual consciousness element as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as ‘with aspiration’ or ‘without aspiration,’ or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as ‘with aspiration’ or ‘without aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the eye-consciousness element is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-consciousness element is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element is tranquil or not tranquil’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-consciousness element is tranquil or not tranquil, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the eye-consciousness element, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element as either tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as either tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-consciousness element is detached or not detached’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element is detached or not detached’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the eye-consciousness element is distant or not distant, or whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are distant or not distant—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element being distant or not distant, or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements being distant or not distant!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the very designation of whether the eye-consciousness element is detached or not detached is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the very designation of whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element is detached or not detached is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the eye-consciousness element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation of ‘conditioned’ or ‘unconditioned’ for the eye-consciousness element, or a designation of ‘conditioned’ or ‘unconditioned’ for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element,

whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether with outflows or without outflows—and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the eye-consciousness element’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or ceasing of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the eye-consciousness element, or the arising and ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the eye-consciousness element, or designations for the arising and ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the arising or ceasing of the eye-consciousness element" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the arising or ceasing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as ‘wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as ‘wholesome or unwholesome’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the visual consciousness element as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether with fault or without fault—and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether with fault or without fault—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault,’ or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the visual consciousness element as either with fault or without fault is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements as either with fault or without fault is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the element of eye-consciousness—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and if the elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the element of eye-consciousness as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or designations for the elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the visual consciousness element as being either with afflictions or without afflictions is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements as being either with afflictions or without afflictions is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether worldly or supramundane’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether worldly or supramundane’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element—whether mundane or supramundane—and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element as ‘mundane’ or ‘supramundane,’ or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as ‘mundane’ or ‘supramundane’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element,

whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to the eye-consciousness element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the eye-consciousness element, and the defilement and purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the defilement and purification of the eye-consciousness element, or any designation for the defilement and purification of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element,

whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the eye-consciousness element belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the eye-consciousness element belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the eye-consciousness element as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘eye-consciousness element,’ whether it be internal, external, or between the two, is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements,’ whether they be internal, external, or between the two, are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element is found neither internally, nor externally, nor in between the two; and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are likewise found neither internally, nor externally, nor in between the two—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for an eye-consciousness element being internally, externally, or in between the two, or a designation for the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements being internally, externally, or in between the two!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the eye-consciousness element,

whether internal, external, or in between, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that the designations "the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, whether internal, external, or in between, are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-consciousness element is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element is obtainable or unobtainable’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the ‘obtainability’ or ‘unobtainability’ of the eye-consciousness element, or a designation for the ‘obtainability’ or ‘unobtainability’ of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the eye-consciousness element is obtainable or unobtainable" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness element is obtainable or unobtainable" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Twenty-Five.
16. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Twenty-Six.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Part: Chapter Seven on Instruction and Teaching, Number Sixteen.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, with what meaning in mind do you say: [that all dharmas are unproduced]?"

Is it that the designation "eye-contact" is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations "ear-contact," "nose-contact," "tongue-contact," "body-contact," and "mind-contact" are also not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

Since even eye-contact, or ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designations ‘eye-contact’ or the designations ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of eye-contact is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether eye-contact is permanent or impermanent’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is permanent or impermanent’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether eye-contact is permanent or impermanent, or whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is permanent or impermanent—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of eye-contact, or designations for the permanence or impermanence of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasant or painful’ for eye-contact is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pleasant or painful’ for ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of eye-contact, or the pleasure and pain of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of eye-contact, or a designation for the pleasure and pain of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact?”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding eye-contact is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact as self or non-self, and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as self or non-self, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘eye-contact as self or non-self,’ or the designations ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as self or non-self’!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation 'self' or 'non-self' regarding eye-contact is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'self' or 'non-self' regarding ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to eye-contact is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the purity or impurity of eye-contact, or the purity or impurity of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, is ultimately unobtainable because its nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of eye-contact, or a designation for the purity or impurity of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact is pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether eye-contact is empty or not empty’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is empty or not empty’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether eye-contact is empty or not empty, or whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is empty or not empty, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for ‘eye-contact being empty or not empty,’ or designations for ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact being empty or not empty’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is empty or not empty is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact is empty or not empty is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

‘The designation of eye-contact, whether it has signs or is signless, is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact, whether they have signs or are signless, are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether eye-contact has characteristics or lacks characteristics, or whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact has characteristics or lacks characteristics, these are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for ‘eye-contact having characteristics or lacking characteristics,’ or designations for ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact having characteristics or lacking characteristics’!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to eye-contact is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to eye-contact is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether eye-contact has aspiration or is without aspiration, or whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact has aspiration or is without aspiration—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be an expression for ‘eye-contact having aspiration or being without aspiration,’ or expressions for ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact having aspiration or being without aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether there is aspiration or no aspiration' regarding eye-contact is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether there is aspiration or no aspiration' regarding ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether eye-contact is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is tranquil or not tranquil’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the contact of the eye is quiescent or not quiescent, and whether the contacts of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are quiescent or not quiescent—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the quiescence or non-quiescence of the contact of the eye, or a designation for the quiescence or non-quiescence of the contacts of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the eye-contact is detached or not detached’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is detached or not detached’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether eye-contact is secluded or not secluded, or whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is secluded or not secluded—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the seclusion or non-seclusion of eye-contact, or a designation for the seclusion or non-seclusion of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether detached or non-detached' from eye-contact is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether detached or non-detached' from ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! What meaning do you perceive when you say that the designation ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for eye-contact is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘eye-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned,’ or designations for ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of eye-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to eye-contact is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even eye-contact—whether with outflows or without outflows—and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘eye-contact with outflows or without outflows,’ or designations for ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact with outflows or without outflows’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of eye-contact,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact, whether with outflows or without outflows, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or the ceasing of eye-contact’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or the ceasing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of eye-contact, or the arising and ceasing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘arising and ceasing of eye-contact,’ or the designations ‘arising and ceasing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of eye-contact is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation of eye-contact, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, whether wholesome or unwholesome, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘eye-contact that is wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact that is wholesome or unwholesome’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to eye-contact is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the offense or non-offense of eye-contact, and the offense or non-offense of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the offense or non-offense of eye-contact, or a designation for the offense or non-offense of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether eye-contact is faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘eye-contact,

whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether eye-contact has affliction or is free from affliction, or whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact has affliction or is free from affliction—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for eye-contact having affliction or being free from affliction, or designations for ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact having affliction or being free from affliction!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation 'eye-contact,

whether with affliction or without affliction,' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations 'ear-contact,' 'nose-contact,' 'tongue-contact,' 'body-contact,' or 'mind-contact, whether with affliction or without affliction,' are a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of eye-contact, whether mundane or supramundane, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, whether mundane or supramundane, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact—whether mundane or supramundane—and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘mundane or supramundane eye-contact,’ or designations for ‘mundane or supramundane ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact’!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of eye-contact, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified eye-contact’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether defiled or purified ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of eye-contact, and the defilement and purification of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of eye-contact, or a designation for the defilement and purification of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of eye-contact, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “eye-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,” is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,” are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas’?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be such designations as ‘eye-contact belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,’ or designations such as ‘ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation 'eye-contact,

whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations 'ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,' are a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘eye-contact,’ whether internal, external, or between the two, is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘ear-contact,’ ‘nose-contact,’ ‘tongue-contact,’ ‘body-contact,’ and ‘mind-contact,’ whether internal, external, or between the two, are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact—whether internal, external, or between the two—is ultimately unobtainable because its nature does not exist, how much less could there be an expression for eye-contact being internal, external, or between the two, or expressions for ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact being internal, external, or between the two?!”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of eye-contact— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether eye-contact is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be an expression for the obtainability or unobtainability of eye-contact, or expressions for the obtainability or unobtainability of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact!”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether eye-contact is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti, based on what meaning do you say:

'The designation for the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designations for the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva'?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied: “World-Honored One,

if even those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or those feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition, are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or designations for feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether permanent or impermanent—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for ‘the permanence or impermanence of feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or any designation for ‘the permanence or impermanence of feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact— whether permanent or impermanent— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact— whether permanent or impermanent— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whatever feelings—

whether pleasant or painful— arise conditioned by eye-contact’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whatever feelings— whether pleasant or painful— arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even the various feelings of pleasure and pain produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the various feelings of pleasure and pain produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the various feelings of pleasure and pain produced with eye-contact as a condition, or any designation for the various feelings of pleasure and pain produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings— whether pleasant or painful—

arisen with eye-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings— whether pleasant or painful— arisen with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition being self or non-self, or the feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions being self or non-self—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation of ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ for the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or a designation of ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ for the feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'self' or 'non-self' regarding the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'self' or 'non-self' regarding the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure feelings produced with eye-contact as condition’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether pure or impure—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether pure or impure—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ‘purity or impurity’ of feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or a designation for the ‘purity or impurity’ of feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact— whether pure or impure— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact— whether pure or impure— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition are empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty or not empty, or whether the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition are empty or not empty—since these are ultimately unobtainable and their nature is non-existent—how much less could there be a designation for ‘the emptiness or non-emptiness of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or a designation for ‘the emptiness or non-emptiness of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether empty or non-empty, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether empty or non-empty, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “whether with signs or signless” applied to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designation “whether with signs or signless” applied to all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether characterized by signs or signless—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions—whether characterized by signs or signless—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designations ‘characterized by signs’ or ‘signless’ for the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the designations ‘characterized by signs’ or ‘signless’ for the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions?”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether with signs or signless, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether with signs or signless, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether they have an aspiration or are without aspiration—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions—whether they have an aspiration or are without aspiration—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition having an aspiration or being without aspiration,’ or a designation for ‘feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions having an aspiration or being without aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact—whether they be tranquil or untranquil—is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact—whether they be tranquil or untranquil—is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’?”
“Blessed One!

Whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are tranquil or untranquil, or whether the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition are tranquil or untranquil—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘the tranquility or lack of tranquility of feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or a designation for ‘the tranquility or lack of tranquility of feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact— whether they be tranquil or untranquil— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact— whether they be tranquil or untranquil— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether detached or not detached’ regarding the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designation ‘whether detached or not detached’ regarding the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”

“Bhagavān! Whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are detached or not detached, or whether the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition are detached or not detached—even these are ultimately non-existent, because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are detached or not detached is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition are detached or not detached is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether conditioned or unconditioned—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether conditioned or unconditioned—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation (*adhivacana*) for these feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, whether conditioned or unconditioned, or any designation for these feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition, whether conditioned or unconditioned?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact—whether with outflows or without outflows—is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact—whether with outflows or without outflows—is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If even those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether they be outflowing (*sāsrava*) or non-outflowing (*anāsrava*)—and those feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether they be outflowing or non-outflowing—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation (*adhivacana*) for those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition that are outflowing or non-outflowing, or a designation for those feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition that are outflowing or non-outflowing!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact— whether with outflows or without outflows— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact— whether with outflows or without outflows— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of whatever feelings are produced with eye-contact as condition’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of whatever feelings are produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of those various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of those various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise or cease conditioned by eye-contact is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise or cease conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘wholesome or unwholesome feelings arising with eye-contact as condition’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘wholesome or unwholesome feelings arising with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for ‘wholesome or unwholesome feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or any designation for ‘wholesome or unwholesome feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ for those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ for those feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether blameworthy or blameless—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether blameworthy or blameless—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘blameworthy or blameless feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or a designation for ‘blameworthy or blameless feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition’?!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether blameworthy or blameless, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether blameworthy or blameless, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether accompanied by afflictions or free from afflictions—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether accompanied by afflictions or free from afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition being accompanied by afflictions or free from afflictions,’ or a designation for ‘feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition being accompanied by afflictions or free from afflictions’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

‘The designation for all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition—whether worldly or supramundane—is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designation for all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition—whether worldly or supramundane—is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!
