If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether mundane or supramundane—and the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘mundane or supramundane feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or a designation for ‘mundane or supramundane feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition’?!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact— whether worldly or supramundane— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact— whether worldly or supramundane— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation for the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition—whether defiled or purified—is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designation for the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions—whether defiled or purified—is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot ultimately be found—because their nature does not exist—and likewise for the defilement and purification of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions, how much less could there be a designation (adhivacana) for the defilement and purification of feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or a designation for the defilement and purification of feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether defiled or pure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether defiled or pure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designation “whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—and if the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—these are ultimately non-existent, because their nature is not real. How much less could there be a designation for ‘feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,’ or a designation for ‘feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa’?!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact, whether internal, external, or in between, are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva,” as well as the designation “whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, whether internal, external, or in between, are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva”?’”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether internal, external, or in between—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition that are internal, external, or in between, or a designation for those feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition that are internal, external, or in between?!”
Since this designation (*adhivacana*) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by eye-contact— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whatever feelings arise conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“Blessed One!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended, and if the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended—since these are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature is non-existent—how much less could there be a designation for ‘the apprehendability or non-apprehendability of feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition,’ or a designation for ‘the apprehendability or non-apprehendability of feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are obtainable or unobtainable' is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition are obtainable or unobtainable' is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

In what sense do you say that the designation 'earth element' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations 'water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
"World-Honored One!

If even the earth element, or the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element, or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?"
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that the designation "earth element" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements" are a bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the earth element is permanent or impermanent’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are permanent or impermanent’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the earth element is permanent or impermanent, or whether the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are permanent or impermanent—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the earth element as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent,’ or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the earth element is permanent or impermanent" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are permanent or impermanent" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasure or pain’ applied to the earth element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pleasure or pain’ applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be pleasure or pain in the earth element, or pleasure or pain in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be such designations as ‘pleasure or pain in the earth element,’ or designations as ‘pleasure or pain in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the self or non-self of the earth element, or the self or non-self of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the self or non-self of the earth element, or designations for the self or non-self of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element as either self or non-self is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as either self or non-self are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-Six.
17. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Part: Chapter Seven on Instruction and Admonition, Section Seventeen.
“Subhūti, for what reason do you say this?”

Is it that the designation "pure" or "impure" applied to the earth element is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and likewise, is it that the designations "pure" or "impure" applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the purity or impurity of the earth element, or the purity or impurity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the earth element, or designations for the purity or impurity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element, whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the earth element is empty or not empty’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are empty or not empty’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the earth element is empty or not empty, or whether the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty or not empty—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element being empty or not empty, or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements being empty or not empty!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the earth element,
whether empty or non-empty," is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, whether empty or non-empty," is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the earth element is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element, whether with signs or signless, and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, whether with signs or signless, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘the earth element with signs or signless,’ or the designations ‘the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements with signs or signless’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the earth element is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the earth element has aspiration or lacks aspiration, or whether the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements have aspiration or lack aspiration—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be the designation ‘the earth element has aspiration or lacks aspiration,’ or the designations ‘the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements have aspiration or lack aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to the earth element is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the earth element is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the earth element is tranquil or not tranquil, or whether the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are tranquil or not tranquil—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the earth element, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the earth element is tranquil or not tranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are tranquil or not tranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the earth element is detached or not detached’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are detached or not detached’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the earth element is distant or not distant, or whether the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are distant or not distant, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the earth element being distant or not distant, or a designation for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements being distant or not distant!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element as being either distant or not distant is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as being either distant or not distant is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the conditioned and unconditioned earth element—and likewise the conditioned and unconditioned water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the conditioned and unconditioned earth element, or designations for the conditioned and unconditioned water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element, whether with outflows or without outflows, and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, whether with outflows or without outflows, are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element as ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the arising or the cessation of the earth element’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or the cessation of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the earth element, or the arising and ceasing of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘arising and ceasing of the earth element’ or the designations ‘arising and ceasing of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation for the arising or ceasing of the earth element is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation for the arising or ceasing of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element as ‘wholesome’ or ‘unwholesome,’ or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as ‘wholesome’ or ‘unwholesome’?”
Since this designative term does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designative term for the earth element, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designative term for the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element—whether guilty or blameless—and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—whether guilty or blameless—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element as ‘guilty’ or ‘blameless,’ or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as ‘guilty’ or ‘blameless’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element as either guilty or guiltless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as either guilty or guiltless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the earth element with afflictions’ or ‘the earth element without afflictions’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements with afflictions’ or ‘the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements without afflictions’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the earth element is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the earth element,

whether mundane or supramundane’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, whether mundane or supramundane’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element, whether mundane or supramundane, and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, whether mundane or supramundane, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the mundane or supramundane earth element, or designations for the mundane or supramundane water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ for the earth element is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether defiled or purified’ for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the earth element, and the defilement and purification of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the defilement and purification of the earth element, or any designation for the defilement and purification of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation for the earth element—

whether defiled or purified— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements— whether defiled or purified— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the earth element, whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—even these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the earth element belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘the earth element,

whether internal, external, or between the two’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, whether internal, external, or between the two’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the earth element is internal, external, or between the two; or whether the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are internal, external, or between the two—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the earth element being internal, external, or between the two, or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements being internal, external, or between the two?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element—

whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the earth element is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the earth element as ‘obtainable’ or ‘unobtainable,’ or designations for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as ‘obtainable’ or ‘unobtainable’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the earth element—

whether it is obtainable or unobtainable— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements— whether they are obtainable or unobtainable— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation 'conditioned origination' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations 'immediately preceding condition,' 'object condition,' and 'dominant condition' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied, “World-Honored One! Since even the causal condition,

the immediately preceding condition, the objective condition, and the dominant condition are ultimately non-apprehendible because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘causal condition’ or the designations ‘immediately preceding condition,’ ‘objective condition,’ and ‘dominant condition’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "conditioned cause" (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
or that the designations "immediately preceding condition" (samanantara-pratyaya), "object condition" (ālambana-pratyaya), and "dominant condition" (adhipati-pratyaya) are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) were permanent or impermanent—if even the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the object condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) were permanent or impermanent—they would ultimately be unobtainable, because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be such designations as ‘the causal condition is permanent or impermanent,’ or designations such as ‘the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition are permanent or impermanent’!”

Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "whether permanent or impermanent" applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;

or that the designation "whether permanent or impermanent" applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasure or pain’ for the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether pleasure or pain’ for the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the designation ‘pleasure and pain arising from causes and conditions’—whether it be pleasure and pain arising from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition—is ultimately unfindable because its nature does not exist, how much less could there be such designations as ‘pleasure and pain arising from causes and conditions’ or ‘pleasure and pain arising from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition’?”

Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of "whether pleasant or painful" regarding the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;

or that the designation of "whether pleasant or painful" regarding the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the self and non-self of the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, and if the self and non-self of the equal-and-immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) are likewise ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the self and non-self of the causal condition, or a designation for the self and non-self of the equal-and-immediate, objective, and dominant conditions!”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "self" or "non-self" applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;

or that the designation "self" or "non-self" applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! What meaning do you perceive such that you say:

‘The designation of whether the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is pure or impure is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; likewise, the designation of whether the equal-and-immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are pure or impure is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the purity or impurity of causal conditions (*hetu-pratyaya*), as well as the purity or impurity of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of causal conditions, or designations for the purity or impurity of the immediately preceding, objective, and dominant conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), or the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what meaning do you base your statement that the designations ‘whether empty or not empty’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether empty or not empty’ applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether causal conditions are empty or not empty, or whether the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are empty or not empty, they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less could there be a designation for causal conditions being empty or not empty, or designations for the immediately preceding, object, and dominant conditions being empty or not empty!”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether empty or non-empty" applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designations "whether empty or non-empty" applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) with or without characteristics, as well as the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) with or without characteristics, are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for a causal condition with or without characteristics, or designations for the immediate, objective, and dominant conditions with or without characteristics!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with marks or without marks" applied to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with marks or without marks" applied to the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘with aspiration’ or ‘without aspiration’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘with aspiration’ or ‘without aspiration’ applied to the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are also not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) having a vow or being without a vow, as well as the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) having a vow or being without a vow, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the causal condition having a vow or being without a vow, or designations for the immediately preceding condition, the objective condition, and the dominant condition having a vow or being without a vow!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designations "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to the immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the causal condition is tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘whether the immediately preceding condition, the objective condition, or the dominant condition are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If causal conditions—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—and if the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for causal conditions that are quiescent or non-quiescent, or a designation for the immediately preceding, object, and dominant conditions that are quiescent or non-quiescent!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the causal condition is tranquil or untranquil" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "whether the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition are tranquil or untranquil" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether separated from or not separated from the causal condition’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether separated from or not separated from the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the causal condition being distant or not distant, or whether it be the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition being distant or not distant—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the causal condition being distant or not distant, or designations for the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition being distant or not distant?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether distant from or not distant from causes and conditions" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether distant from or not distant from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what meaning do you base your statement that the designations for conditioned or unconditioned phenomena—

whether they be the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), the equal-and-immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), or the predominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*)— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If conditioned and unconditioned phenomena arising from causes and conditions, as well as the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition—whether conditioned or unconditioned—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for 'conditioned and unconditioned phenomena arising from causes and conditions,' or designations for the 'immediately preceding condition,' the 'object-condition,' and the 'dominant condition'—whether conditioned or unconditioned!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of "conditioned or unconditioned" applied to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of "conditioned or unconditioned" applied to the immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even conditioned causes and conditions—whether tainted or untainted—as well as the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition—whether tainted or untainted, are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for 'tainted or untainted conditioned causes and conditions,' or a designation for 'tainted or untainted immediately preceding conditions, object-conditions, and dominant conditions'!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "whether with outflows or without outflows" applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva mahāsattva;

or that the designations "whether with outflows or without outflows" applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the causal condition’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘the arising or ceasing of the immediately preceding condition,’ ‘the object-condition,’ and ‘the dominant condition’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of causal conditions (*hetu-pratyaya*)—or even the arising and ceasing of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*)—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘arising and ceasing of causal conditions’ or the designations ‘arising and ceasing of the immediately preceding, objective, and dominant conditions’!”

Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist, how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*)—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and likewise the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*)—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation (*adhivacana*) for a causal condition that is wholesome or unwholesome, or designations for the immediately preceding, objective, and dominant conditions that are wholesome or unwholesome?”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the object condition (ālambana-pratyaya), or the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
"Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation 'whether with fault or without fault' applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,

and that the designations 'whether with fault or without fault' applied to the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are also not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?"
“World-Honored One!

If the causes and conditions for being guilty or non-guilty, as well as the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for causes and conditions being guilty or non-guilty, or designations for the equal-and-immediate, object, and dominant conditions being guilty or non-guilty!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "whether with fault or without fault" applied to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;

or that the designation "whether with fault or without fault" applied to the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the predominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If, regarding causal conditions, the presence or absence of afflictions is ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the presence or absence of afflictions in causal conditions, nor a designation for the presence or absence of afflictions in immediate conditions, objective conditions, or dominant conditions? This is because their nature is non-existent.”

Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "whether with afflictions or without afflictions" applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designation "whether with afflictions or without afflictions" applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘mundane or supramundane conditions-in-flux’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘immediately-antecedent condition,’ ‘object-condition,’ and ‘dominant condition,’ whether mundane or supramundane, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since causal conditions—whether mundane or supramundane—and likewise the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘mundane or supramundane causal conditions’ or a designation for ‘mundane or supramundane equal-and-immediate, object, and dominant conditions’?”

Since this designation does not exist at all, how can it be said that the designation for "whether mundane or supramundane" applied to the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation for "whether mundane or supramundane" applied to the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether afflicted or purified’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether afflicted or purified’ applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of causal conditions (*hetu-pratyaya*), as well as the defilement and purification of the immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designations for the defilement and purification of causal conditions, or any designations for the defilement and purification of the immediate, objective, and dominant conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya), whether defiled or purified,

is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya), whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa’ applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa’ applied to the immediate condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are also not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If causal conditions (hetu-pratyaya) belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa—even the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa—cannot ultimately be found because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for causal conditions belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, or designations for the immediately preceding, objective, and dominant conditions belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya), whether it belongs to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the object-condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya), whether they belong to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether internal, external, or between the two’ does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘immediately preceding condition,’ ‘object condition,’ and ‘dominant condition,’ whether internal, external, or between the two, do not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If causes and conditions—whether internal, external, or between the two—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘internal, external, or between the two’ for causes and conditions, nor the designations ‘internal, external, or between the two’ for the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), or the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*)? Since these do not exist by nature, they are utterly unfindable.”
Since this designation (*adhivacana*) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), or the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) are obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If causes and conditions—whether they be obtainable or unobtainable—and if the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition—whether they be obtainable or unobtainable—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘causes and conditions being obtainable or unobtainable,’ or designations for the ‘immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition being obtainable or unobtainable’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether obtainable or unobtainable" applied to the causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether obtainable or unobtainable" applied to the immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), the objective condition (ālambana-pratyaya), and the dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
On what basis do you say that the designation for 'dharmas produced through conditions' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One,

since even phenomena produced through conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended, because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for phenomena produced through conditions!”
"Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that 'the designation for the dharmas produced through conditions is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva'?
"Subhūti! [The Buddha replied:]

"What further meaning do you perceive when you say that the designation 'whether the phenomena produced by conditions are permanent or impermanent' is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva? [Subhūti replied:
"World-Honored One!"

Since even the permanence or impermanence of phenomena produced by conditions is ultimately unfindable—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for "permanence" or "impermanence" regarding phenomena produced by conditions!
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that the designation "whether permanent or impermanent" applied to phenomena produced through conditions is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasant or painful’ for phenomena produced through conditions is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the pleasure and pain produced by conditions cannot ultimately be found, because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of whether the phenomena produced by conditions are pleasant or painful is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding phenomena produced through conditions is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the self and non-self of dependently arisen phenomena are ultimately unfindable—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the self and non-self of dependently arisen phenomena!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,
how can it be said that "the designation of 'self' or 'non-self' applied to phenomena produced through conditions is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation of phenomena produced through conditions— whether pure or impure— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since even the purity and impurity of phenomena produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended, as their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of whether the phenomena produced by conditions are pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the phenomena produced through conditions are empty or not empty’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the emptiness or non-emptiness of phenomena produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended—because their intrinsic nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of whether the phenomena produced through conditions are empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Furthermore,
based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to phenomena produced through conditions is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the characteristics of conditioned phenomena produced by causes and conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for such phenomena as ‘having characteristics’ or ‘being without characteristics’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation 'whether having marks or being markless' applied to phenomena produced through conditions is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether there is aspiration or no aspiration regarding phenomena produced through conditions’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since even the dharmas produced by conditions—whether they possess aspiration or lack aspiration—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for dharmas produced by conditions as ‘possessing aspiration’ or ‘lacking aspiration’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that the designation "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to phenomena produced through conditions is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the phenomena produced by conditions are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the tranquility or non-tranquility of dharmas produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of dharmas produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that the designation for whether the phenomena produced by conditions are tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:
‘Is it not the case that the designation “whether phenomena produced by conditions are distant from or not distant [from suchness]” is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?’”
“World-Honored One!

Since the remoteness or non-remoteness of phenomena produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the remoteness or non-remoteness of phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the very dharmas produced through conditions— whether they are remote from or not remote from this designation— are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:
‘The designation for conditioned or unconditioned phenomena that arise in dependence is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

Since conditioned and unconditioned phenomena produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended, because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for conditioned and unconditioned phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation for conditioned or unconditioned phenomena produced through conditions is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation for phenomena produced through conditions— whether they be with outflows or without outflows— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Even conditioned phenomena arising from conditions—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately non-existent, because their nature does not exist; how much less could there be a designation for such conditioned phenomena arising from conditions as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of phenomena produced through conditions— whether with outflows or without outflows— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of phenomena produced through conditions’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the arising and ceasing of phenomena produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended, because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of the arising or ceasing of phenomena produced through conditions is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation of phenomena produced through conditions— whether wholesome or unwholesome— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since even the wholesome and unwholesome dharmas produced by conditions cannot ultimately be apprehended, because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for wholesome or unwholesome dharmas produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation for phenomena produced through conditions— whether wholesome or unwholesome— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether dharmas produced through conditions are faulty or faultless’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since even the dharmas produced by conditions—whether they be with fault or without fault—cannot ultimately be apprehended, because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for dharmas produced by conditions as being ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of whether the dharmas produced by conditions are with fault or without fault is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to phenomena produced through conditions is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Even the dharmas produced by conditions—whether they possess afflictions or are free from afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable, because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for dharmas produced by conditions as ‘possessing afflictions’ or ‘being free from afflictions’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to phenomena produced through conditions is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:
‘Are the designations for phenomena produced through conditions—whether mundane or supramundane—not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?’”
“World-Honored One!

Since even the mundane and supramundane phenomena produced by conditions are ultimately unobtainable—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for mundane and supramundane phenomena produced by conditions?”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation for phenomena produced through conditions— whether mundane or supramundane— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what meaning do you base your statement that the designation for phenomena produced through conditions— whether they be defiled or purified— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Since the defilement and purification of phenomena produced by conditions are ultimately non-existent—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation for phenomena produced through conditions— whether defiled or purified— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘dharmas arisen from conditions,’ whether they pertain to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Even dharmas produced by conditions—which belong to birth-and-death and belong to nirvāṇa—are ultimately non-existent, because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be a designation for dharmas produced by conditions that ‘belong to birth-and-death’ or ‘belong to nirvāṇa’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation for those dharmas produced through conditions— whether they belong to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:
‘Is it that the designation for dharmas produced through conditions—whether internal, external, or between the two—is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?’”
“World-Honored One!

Conditioned phenomena produced by causes and conditions cannot ultimately be found within, without, or between the two, because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for conditioned phenomena produced by causes and conditions being within, without, or between the two!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of the dharmas produced through conditions— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the phenomena produced through conditions are obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Even the obtainability or unobtainability of phenomena produced by conditions is ultimately unobtainable, because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be a designation for the obtainability or unobtainability of phenomena produced by conditions!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the dharmas produced by conditions are obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-Seven.
18. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Part: Chapter Seven on Instruction and Teaching, Number Eighteen.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, for what reason do you say:
[that the Tathāgata does not perceive any dharma as a Tathāgata]?"

Is it that the designation "ignorance" is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and likewise, are the designations "volitional formations," "consciousness," "name-and-form," "the six sense bases," "contact," "feeling," "craving," "clinging," "existence," "birth," and "aging-and-death" not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance, formative forces, and so forth, up to old age and death, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘ignorance’ or the designations for ‘formative forces’ up to ‘old age and death’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation 'ignorance' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations from 'volitional formations' up to 'old age and death' are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether ignorance is permanent or impermanent’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘whether [the links from] formations up to old age and death are permanent or impermanent’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance—whether permanent or impermanent—and even the formations up to old age and death—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘ignorance is permanent or impermanent,’ or the designations ‘the formations up to old age and death are permanent or impermanent’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "ignorance is either permanent or impermanent" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "from formations up to old age and death are either permanent or impermanent" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether pleasure or pain’ for ignorance is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pleasure or pain’ for formations up to old age and death are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance as pleasure or suffering, and even formations up to old age and death as pleasure or suffering, are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘ignorance as pleasure or suffering,’ or designations for ‘formations up to old age and death as pleasure or suffering’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of ignorance as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of [everything from] formations up to old age and death as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘ignorance is either self or non-self’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘volitional formations’ up to ‘old age and death are either self or non-self’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance—whether as self or non-self—and even conditioned formations up to old age and death—whether as self or non-self—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designations ‘ignorance as self or non-self’ or the designations ‘conditioned formations up to old age and death as self or non-self’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "ignorance—
whether as self or as non-self— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "conditioned phenomena up to old age and death— whether as self or as non-self— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to ignorance is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to formations up to old age and death are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance—whether pure or impure—and even the formations up to old age and death—whether pure or impure—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of ignorance, or a designation for the purity or impurity of the formations up to old age and death!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of ignorance as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of [the links from] volitional formations up to old age and death as either pure or impure is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether ignorance is empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether formations up to old age and death are empty or not empty’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance—whether empty or not empty—and if the formative forces up to old age and death—whether empty or not empty—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘ignorance being empty or not empty,’ or a designation for ‘the formative forces up to old age and death being empty or not empty’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether ignorance is empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether [the links from] formations through to old age and death are empty or not empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to ignorance is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to formations up to old age and death are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance—whether characterized by marks or markless—and even the formations up to old age and death—whether characterized by marks or markless—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘ignorance with marks or without marks,’ or designations for ‘the formations up to old age and death with marks or without marks’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of ignorance as having marks or being without marks is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of [the links from] volitional formations through to old age and death as having marks or being without marks is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to ignorance are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to volitional formations up to old age and death are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—and even the formations up to old age and death—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘ignorance with aspiration or without aspiration,’ or a designation for ‘the formations up to old age and death with aspiration or without aspiration’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
