If the arising and ceasing of true thusness, or the arising and ceasing of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature is non-existent, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of true thusness, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the arising or ceasing of suchness" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the arising or ceasing of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to suchness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness (tathatā) as wholesome or unwholesome, and if the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), as wholesome or unwholesome, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation (adhivacana) for ‘true thusness as wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for ‘the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, as wholesome or unwholesome’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether suchness is wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’ applied to suchness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’ applied to the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness—whether with fault or without fault—and even the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—whether with fault or without fault—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature is non-existent, how much less could there be a designation for true thusness as ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault,’ or a designation for the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm as ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether guilty or innocent' applied to suchness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether guilty or innocent' applied to the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to suchness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and if the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature is non-existent, how much less could there be a designation for true thusness as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or a designation for the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to suchness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘That which is the designation for whether it is the world or the supramundane regarding suchness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; that which is the designation for whether it is the world or the supramundane regarding the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness—whether mundane or supramundane—and if the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘mundane or supramundane true thusness,’ or a designation for ‘the mundane or supramundane dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether worldly or supramundane' applied to suchness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether worldly or supramundane' applied to the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘That which is a designation for whether the suchness is defiled or purified is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; that which is a designation for whether the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is defiled or purified is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If even the defilement and purification of suchness, or the defilement and purification of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of suchness, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of suchness, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation “whether it belongs to saṃsāra or whether it belongs to nirvāṇa” applied to suchness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and the designations “whether it belongs to saṃsāra or whether it belongs to nirvāṇa” applied to the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness (tathatā) belonged to saṃsāra or belonged to nirvāṇa, and if the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), belonged to saṃsāra or belonged to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation (adhivacana) such as ‘true thusness belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,’ or a designation such as ‘the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'suchness,' whether it pertains to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations 'the dharma-realm' up to 'the inconceivable realm,' whether they pertain to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation “whether the suchness is internal, external, or between the two” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designation “whether the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is internal, external, or between the two” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness—whether internal, external, or between the two—and if the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—whether internal, external, or between the two—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature is non-existent, how much less could there be a designation for true thusness as being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm as being internal, external, or between the two!”
Since this designation (*adhivacana*) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether True Suchness is internal, external, or between the two' is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the Dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is internal, external, or between the two' is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the true nature (tathatā) can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness (tathatā) is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to and including the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation (adhivacana) for ‘true thusness being obtainable or unobtainable,’ or a designation for ‘the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, being obtainable or unobtainable’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the suchness can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended' is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation 'the four applications of mindfulness' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

and that the designations 'the four right endeavors,' 'the four bases of power,' 'the five faculties,' 'the five powers,' 'the seven factors of awakening,' and 'the eightfold noble path' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and even the eight branches of the noble path are ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘four foundations of mindfulness’ and the designations ‘four right efforts’ up to the ‘eight branches of the noble path’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the four foundations of mindfulness" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "the four right endeavors" up to "the eightfold noble path" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designations ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’ applied to the four applications of mindfulness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’ applied to the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether permanent or impermanent—and even the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘pleasure’ or ‘suffering’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘pleasure’ or ‘suffering’ applied to the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure or pain of the four foundations of mindfulness, or even the pleasure or pain of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, cannot ultimately be apprehended because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure or pain of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the pleasure or pain of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the four applications of mindfulness as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the self and non-self of the four foundations of mindfulness, and even the self and non-self of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the self and non-self of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the self and non-self of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness as either self or non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as either self or non-self is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘pure’ or ‘impure’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘pure’ or ‘impure’ applied to the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the purity or impurity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or even the purity or impurity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the purity or impurity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four applications of mindfulness,
whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether empty or not empty’ of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether empty or not empty’ of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether empty or not empty—and even the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—whether empty or not empty—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether empty or non-empty" of the four foundations of mindfulness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether empty or non-empty" of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness, whether with signs or signless, and the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, whether with signs or signless, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as being ‘with signs’ or ‘signless,’ or a designation for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as being ‘with signs’ or ‘signless’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—and even the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as ‘with aspiration or without aspiration,’ or a designation for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as ‘with aspiration or without aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the four foundations of mindfulness are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘whether the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness, whether tranquil or non-tranquil, and even the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, whether tranquil or non-tranquil, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the four foundations of mindfulness, whether tranquil or untranquil," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation "the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, whether tranquil or untranquil," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether distant from or not distant from the four foundations of mindfulness’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether distant from or not distant from the four right endeavors’ up to ‘the eightfold noble path’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the four foundations of mindfulness are distant or not distant, or whether the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are distant or not distant—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the distance or non-distance of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the distance or non-distance of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness as being either secluded or not secluded is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path as being either secluded or not secluded is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation of the four applications of mindfulness—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path— whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as ‘conditioned’ or ‘unconditioned,’ or a designation for the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path as ‘conditioned’ or ‘unconditioned’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness,

whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations for the four applications of mindfulness—

whether with outflows or without outflows— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path— whether with outflows or without outflows— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether with outflows or without outflows—and the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as ‘with outflows or without outflows,’ or a designation for the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as ‘with outflows or without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the four applications of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness, or even the arising and ceasing of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the four applications of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether wholesome or unwholesome—and even the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—whether wholesome or unwholesome—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as ‘wholesome or unwholesome,’ or a designation for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as ‘wholesome or unwholesome’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness—

whether wholesome or unwholesome— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path— whether wholesome or unwholesome— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the four applications of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether with fault or without fault—and even the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—whether with fault or without fault—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault,’ or a designation for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, as either faulty or faultless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and if the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or a designation for the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations for the four foundations of mindfulness—

whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path— whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness—whether mundane or supramundane—and the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as mundane or supramundane, or a designation for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as mundane or supramundane!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness,

whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 29 [and] Scroll 33.
Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The Seventh Chapter on the Initial Instruction and Teaching,
Part Twenty: "Subhūti,
for what reason do you say this?"

Is it that the designations for the four foundations of mindfulness—whether as afflicted or as purified—are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and is it that the designations for the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path—whether as afflicted or as purified—are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the four foundations of mindfulness, and even the defilement and purification of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four applications of mindfulness,

whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the four foundations of mindfulness belong either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa’ does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the four right endeavors,’ up to and including ‘the eightfold noble path,’ belong either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa do not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa, and if the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness as belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or a designation for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether internal,

external, or between the two’ applied to the four foundations of mindfulness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether internal, external, or between the two’ applied to the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness cannot ultimately be found—whether abiding internally, externally, or in between—because their nature does not exist, how much less can there be the designation ‘abiding internally, externally, or in between’ for the four foundations of mindfulness, nor the designation ‘abiding internally, externally, or in between’ for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path? This is because their nature does not exist.”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the four foundations of mindfulness," whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation "the four right efforts" up to "the eightfold noble path," whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the four foundations of mindfulness are obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness are neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the ‘obtainability’ or ‘unobtainability’ of the four foundations of mindfulness, or a designation for the ‘obtainability’ or ‘unobtainability’ of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the four foundations of mindfulness are obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

In view of what meaning do you say that the designation 'the noble truth of suffering' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations 'the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If even the noble truth of suffering, or the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering, or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the noble truth of suffering is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to the noble truth of suffering is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether permanent or impermanent—and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent,’ or any designation for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the Noble Truth of Suffering,

whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the Noble Truths of Origin, Cessation, and the Path, whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of the noble truth of suffering as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as either pleasure or pain are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering is the pleasure of suffering, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are the pleasure of suffering, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be such designations as ‘the noble truth of suffering is the pleasure of suffering,’ or ‘the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are the pleasure of suffering’!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering as either pleasure or pain is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as either pleasure or pain is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering is ‘self’ or ‘non-self,’ and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are ‘self’ or ‘non-self,’ these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less could there be such designations as ‘the noble truth of suffering is self or non-self,’ or the designations ‘the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are self or non-self’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the noble truth of suffering as "self" or "non-self" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as "self" or "non-self" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether pure or impure’ applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether pure or impure—and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether pure or impure—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation of ‘purity’ or ‘impurity’ for the noble truth of suffering, or any designation of ‘purity’ or ‘impurity’ for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path!”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that the designation "whether pure or impure" applied to the Noble Truth of Suffering is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether pure or impure" applied to the Noble Truths of Origin, Cessation, and the Path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the noble truth of suffering is empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty or not empty’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering is empty or not empty, and if the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty or not empty, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering being empty or not empty, or designations for the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path being empty or not empty!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering as either empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as either empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of the noble truth of suffering as having marks or being markless is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as having marks or being markless are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering, whether with marks or without marks, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, whether with marks or without marks, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘with marks’ or ‘without marks,’ or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘with marks’ or ‘without marks’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the Noble Truth of Suffering,

whether with signs or signless, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, whether with signs or signless, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘with aspiration’ or ‘without aspiration,’ or a designation for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘with aspiration’ or ‘without aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the noble truth of suffering is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
"Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation 'the noble truth of suffering,

whether it be tranquil or not tranquil,' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations 'the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, whether they be tranquil or not tranquil,' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘quiescent’ or ‘non-quiescent,’ or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘quiescent’ or ‘non-quiescent’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the Noble Truth of Suffering as either tranquil or non-tranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as either tranquil or non-tranquil is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the noble truth of suffering is detached or not detached’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are detached or not detached’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the noble truth of suffering is distant or not distant, or whether the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are distant or not distant—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering being distant or not distant, or a designation for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path being distant or not distant?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering as being either secluded or not secluded is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either secluded or not secluded is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether conditioned or unconditioned’ for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as conditioned or unconditioned, or a designation for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as conditioned or unconditioned!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering,

whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation of the noble truth of suffering, whether with outflows or without outflows, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, whether with outflows or without outflows, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering, whether with outflows or without outflows, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, whether with outflows or without outflows, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the Noble Truth of Suffering,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or the cessation of the noble truth of suffering’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the arising or the cessation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path’ are not bodhisattva mahāsattvas?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the noble truth of suffering, or the arising and ceasing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the noble truth of suffering, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the arising or ceasing of the noble truth of suffering is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the arising or ceasing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are neither wholesome nor unwholesome—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘wholesome or unwholesome,’ or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘wholesome or unwholesome’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the Noble Truth of Suffering,

whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether with fault or without fault—and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether with fault or without fault—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the noble truth of suffering as being ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault,’ or any designation for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the Noble Truth of Suffering, whether with fault or without fault," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designations "the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, whether with fault or without fault" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say:

‘The designation “whether with afflictions or without afflictions” applied to the noble truth of suffering is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designation “whether with afflictions or without afflictions” applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the noble truth of suffering is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of the noble truth of suffering—whether mundane or supramundane—is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether mundane or supramundane—are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering—whether mundane or supramundane—and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering as ‘mundane’ or ‘supramundane,’ or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as ‘mundane’ or ‘supramundane’?”
Since this designation does not exist at all,

how can it be said that "the designation of the Noble Truth of Suffering, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the Noble Truths of Origin, Cessation, and the Path, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the noble truth of suffering,

whether defiled or purified’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, whether defiled or purified’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the noble truth of suffering, and the defilement and purification of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designations for the defilement and purification of the noble truth of suffering, or any designations for the defilement and purification of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering—

whether as defiled or purified— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path— whether as defiled or purified— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation of the noble truth of suffering as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering were to belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path were to belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa, they would still ultimately be unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the noble truth of suffering belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or designations for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa!”
Since this designation does not exist at all, how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering—

whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path— whether belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “whether the noble truth of suffering is internal, external, or between the two” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the designations “whether the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are internal, external, or between the two” are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the Noble Truth of Suffering—whether internal, external, or between the two—is ultimately unobtainable because its nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the Noble Truth of Suffering as being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as being internal, external, or between the two?
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the Noble Truth of Suffering—

whether internal, external, or between the two— is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the noble truth of suffering can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended, and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path can be apprehended or cannot be apprehended—since these are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the noble truth of suffering, or a designation for the apprehension or non-apprehension of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the noble truth of suffering—

whether it is obtainable or unobtainable— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path— whether they are obtainable or unobtainable— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti! In view of what meaning do you say that the designation 'the four dhyānas' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations 'the four immeasurables' and 'the four formless attainments' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If even the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas, or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’ applied to the four dhyānas are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘permanent’ or ‘impermanent’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether permanent or impermanent, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether permanent or impermanent, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the four dhyānas as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘pleasure’ or ‘suffering’ applied to the four dhyānas are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘pleasure’ or ‘suffering’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of the four dhyānas, or the pleasure and pain of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the pleasure and pain of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?”
Since these designations do not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "pleasure" or "suffering" regarding the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "pleasure" or "suffering" regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the four dhyānas are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the self and non-self of the four dhyānas, as well as the self and non-self of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the self and non-self of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the self and non-self of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments!”
Since these designations do not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "self" or "non-self" applied to the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "self" or "non-self" applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘pure’ or ‘impure’ applied to the four dhyānas are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘pure’ or ‘impure’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the purity and impurity of the four dhyānas, as well as the purity and impurity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity and impurity of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the purity and impurity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,
whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether empty or not empty’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether empty or not empty’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas—whether empty or not empty—and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—whether empty or not empty—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ‘emptiness or non-emptiness of the four dhyānas,’ or a designation for the ‘emptiness or non-emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether empty or non-empty" regarding the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether empty or non-empty" regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘with signs’ or ‘signless’ applied to the four dhyānas are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘with signs’ or ‘signless’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether with signs or signless, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with signs or signless, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘the four dhyānas with signs or signless,’ or the designation ‘the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments with signs or signless’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with aspiration or without aspiration’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether with aspiration or without aspiration, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with aspiration or without aspiration, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas as ‘with aspiration or without aspiration,’ or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as ‘with aspiration or without aspiration’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with aspiration or without aspiration' applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the four dhyānas are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas—whether tranquil or non-tranquil—and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—whether tranquil or non-tranquil—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,

whether tranquil or untranquil, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether tranquil or untranquil, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation “whether detached or not detached” regarding the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designation “whether detached or not detached” regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the four dhyānas are secluded or not secluded, or whether the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are secluded or not secluded, they are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the seclusion or non-seclusion of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the seclusion or non-seclusion of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,

whether secluded or not secluded, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether secluded or not secluded, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations for the four dhyānas—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments— whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas as conditioned or unconditioned, or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as conditioned or unconditioned?”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the four dhyānas, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether with outflows or without outflows, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with outflows or without outflows, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows,’ or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as being ‘with outflows’ or ‘without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the arising or the cessation of the four dhyānas’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘the arising or the cessation of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the four dhyānas, or the arising and ceasing of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the four dhyānas is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation for the arising or ceasing of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what meaning do you base your statement that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the wholesome and unwholesome states of the four dhyānas, as well as the wholesome and unwholesome states of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ‘wholesome and unwholesome states of the four dhyānas’ or a designation for the ‘wholesome and unwholesome states of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,

whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether with fault or without fault, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with fault or without fault, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas as being ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault,’ or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as being ‘with fault’ or ‘without fault’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the four dhyānas,

whether with fault or without fault" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with fault or without fault" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,

whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations for the four dhyānas—

whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments— whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas, whether mundane or supramundane, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether mundane or supramundane, are ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be designations for the four dhyānas as mundane or supramundane, or designations for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as mundane or supramundane!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation for the four dhyānas, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to the four dhyānas is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether defiled or purified’ applied to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the four dhyānas, as well as the defilement and purification of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the four dhyānas, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas,

whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation “the four dhyānas, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and the designation “the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,” is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas belonging to saṃsāra and belonging to nirvāṇa, as well as the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions belonging to saṃsāra and belonging to nirvāṇa, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas belonging to saṃsāra and belonging to nirvāṇa, or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions belonging to saṃsāra and belonging to nirvāṇa!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas—

whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions— whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether within,

without, or between’ does not apply to the four dhyānas as a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether within, without, or between’ does not apply to the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas—whether internal, external, or between the two—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the four dhyānas being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments being internal, external, or between the two?
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the four dhyānas—

whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments— whether internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti!
