with what meaning in mind do you say that the designation ‘whether there is aspiration or no aspiration’ for the Stage of Utmost Joy is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether there is aspiration or no aspiration’ for the Stage of Freedom from Defilement up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the aspiration or non-aspiration of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or the aspiration or non-aspiration of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, cannot ultimately be apprehended because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the aspiration or non-aspiration of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or a designation for the aspiration or non-aspiration of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether there is a vow or no vow in the Stage of Utmost Joy is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether there is a vow or no vow in the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say:

‘The designation of the Ground of Utmost Joy, whether it be tranquil or not tranquil, is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; the designations of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, whether they be tranquil or not tranquil, are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the tranquility or non-tranquility of the Ground of Extreme Joy, and the tranquility or non-tranquility of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the Ground of Extreme Joy, or a designation for the tranquility or non-tranquility of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the first ground, the Ground of Extreme Joy,

whether tranquil or untranquil" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "the second ground, the Ground of Purity," up to "the Ground of Dharma Clouds, whether tranquil or untranquil" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the Stage of Utmost Joy is distant or not distant’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the Stage of Freedom from Defilement up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma are distant or not distant’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether it be the detachment or non-detachment of the Ground of Utmost Joy, or the detachment or non-detachment of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation (*adhivacana*) for the detachment or non-detachment of the Ground of Utmost Joy, or any designation for the detachment or non-detachment of the Grounds from Freedom from Defilement up to the Dharma-Cloud!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether detached or non-detached" regarding the Stage of Utmost Joy is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designations "whether detached or non-detached" regarding the Stage of Purity up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation of the first stage, the Stage of Extreme Joy, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; and that the designations of the stages from the Stage Free from Defilement up to the Cloud of Dharma, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the conditioned and unconditioned of the Stage of Utmost Joy, and even the conditioned and unconditioned of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the conditioned and unconditioned of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or a designation for the conditioned and unconditioned of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the first stage,

the Joyous (Pramuditā), whether conditioned or unconditioned, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the stages from the Stainless (Vimalā) up to the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā), whether conditioned or unconditioned, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation of the Ground of Utmost Joy, whether with outflows or without outflows, is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva;
and that the designations of the Ground of Purification through Virtue up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, whether with outflows or without outflows, are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the outflowing and non-outflowing states of the Stage of Utmost Joy, and the outflowing and non-outflowing states of the Stage Free from Defilement up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designations for the outflowing and non-outflowing states of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or any designations for the outflowing and non-outflowing states of the Stage Free from Defilement up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the first bhūmi,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the second bhūmi up to the dharmameghā bhūmi, whether with outflows or without outflows, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the Stage of Extreme Joy’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘the arising or ceasing of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement,’ up to ‘the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma,’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or the arising and ceasing of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be the designation ‘arising and ceasing of the Stage of Utmost Joy’ or the designation ‘arising and ceasing of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma’?

Since these designations do not exist, how can it be said that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the Stage of Utmost Joy’ is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma’ is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ for the Stage of Extreme Joy is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ for the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the goodness and non-goodness of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or the goodness and non-goodness of the Stage Free from Defilement up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the goodness and non-goodness of the Stage of Utmost Joy, or any designation for the goodness and non-goodness of the Stage Free from Defilement up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the First Ground,

whether virtuous or non-virtuous, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the Second Ground up to the Ground of Dharma-Cloud, whether virtuous or non-virtuous, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ for the Stage of Extreme Joy is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ for the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the presence or absence of fault in the Stage of Utmost Joy, and the presence or absence of fault in the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the presence or absence of fault in the Stage of Utmost Joy, or a designation for the presence or absence of fault in the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether there is fault or no fault in the Stage of Utmost Joy is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether there is fault or no fault in the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the Stage of Extreme Joy is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the Stage of Purification through Virtue up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the afflictions or the absence of afflictions in the Stage of Utmost Joy, or the afflictions or the absence of afflictions in the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘afflictions or the absence of afflictions in the Stage of Utmost Joy,’ or a designation for ‘afflictions or the absence of afflictions in the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the Stage of Utmost Joy is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the Stage of Freedom from Defilement up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘the Stage of Utmost Joy,’ whether mundane or supramundane, is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘the Stage of Purification’ up to ‘the Cloud of Dharma,’ whether mundane or supramundane, are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even the worldly and world-transcending First Ground of Extreme Joy, and the worldly and world-transcending grounds from the Second Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the worldly and world-transcending First Ground of Extreme Joy, or designations for the worldly and world-transcending grounds from the Second Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the worldly or supramundane designations for the Stage of Utmost Joy are the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the worldly or supramundane designations for the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation for the first ground, the Ground of Extreme Joy—whether it be its defilement or its purification—is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations for the second ground, the Ground of Purity, up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud—whether they be their defilement or their purification—are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the Stage of Extreme Joy, and the defilement and purification of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the Stage of Extreme Joy, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the first ground,

the Joyous, whether in its defiled or purified state, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the grounds from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, whether in their defiled or purified states, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the Ground of Perfect Joy,’ whether it pertains to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘the Ground of Purification’ up to ‘the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma,’ whether they pertain to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the Ground of Perfect Joy belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa, and if the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud belongs to saṃsāra or belongs to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the Ground of Perfect Joy belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa, or a designation for the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the Ground of Utmost Joy as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the Ground of Utmost Joy,’ whether it be internal, external, or between the two, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations from ‘the Ground of Purification’ up to ‘the Ground of the Dharma Cloud,’ whether they be internal, external, or between the two, are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the Ground of Extreme Joy cannot ultimately be found within, without, or between the two, because its nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the Ground of Extreme Joy as being within, without, or between the two, or a designation for the Grounds from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma as being within, without, or between the two?”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the Ground of Utmost Joy," whether internal, external, or between the two, is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; or that the designations "the Ground of Stainless Purity" up to "the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud," whether internal, external, or between the two, are the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the Ground of Supreme Joy is obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud are obtainable or unobtainable’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the Ground of Utmost Joy is neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be any designation for the ‘obtainability’ or ‘unobtainability’ of the Ground of Utmost Joy, or any designation for the ‘obtainability’ or ‘unobtainability’ of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether the Stage of Utmost Joy is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether the Stage of Freedom from Defilement up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma is obtainable or unobtainable' is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
On what basis do you say that the designation 'five eyes' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation 'six superknowledges' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If even the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so can there be the designations ‘five eyes’ or the designations ‘six supernormal powers’!”
Since this designation does not exist,
how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva" or "the designation of the six supernormal powers is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the five eyes are permanent or impermanent’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the six supernormal powers are permanent or impermanent’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether permanent or impermanent, and the six sense-bases, whether permanent or impermanent, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be any designation for the permanence or impermanence of the five eyes, or any designation for the permanence or impermanence of the six sense-bases!”
Since these designations do not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the five eyes,
whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "the six supernormal powers, whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation of the five eyes as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation of the six supernormal powers as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the pleasure and pain of the five eyes, or the pleasure and pain of the six supernormal powers, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations for the pleasure and pain of the five eyes, and the designations for the pleasure and pain of the six supernormal powers!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the five eyes as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the six supernormal powers as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the five eyes are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the six supernormal powers are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the selfhood or non-selfhood of the five eyes, or the selfhood or non-selfhood of the six supernormal powers, is ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘selfhood or non-selfhood of the five eyes’ and the designations ‘selfhood or non-selfhood of the six supernormal powers’!”
Since these designations do not exist,

how can it be said that "the designations of the five eyes as self or as non-self are the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of the six supernormal powers as self or as non-self are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations for whether the five eyes are pure or impure are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for whether the six supernormal powers are pure or impure are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the five eyes are pure or impure, or whether the six supernormal powers are pure or impure—since these are ultimately unattainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be any designations for the purity or impurity of the five eyes, or any designations for the purity or impurity of the six supernormal powers!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the five eyes are pure or impure is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the six superknowledges are pure or impure is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the five eyes are empty or not empty’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the six supernormal powers are empty or not empty’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the five eyes are empty or not empty, or whether the six supernormal powers are empty or not empty, they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be any designations for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the five eyes, or any designations for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the six supernormal powers!”
Since these designations do not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the five eyes are empty or not empty" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether the six supernormal powers are empty or not empty" is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the five eyes is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the six supernormal powers is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether with marks or without marks, and the six supernormal powers, whether with marks or without marks, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designation ‘the five eyes with marks or without marks’ and the designation ‘the six supernormal powers with marks or without marks’!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes,

whether they have signs or are signless, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six supernormal powers, whether they have signs or are signless, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say:

‘The designation of the five eyes, whether with aspiration or without aspiration, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designation of the six supernormal powers, whether with aspiration or without aspiration, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether with aspiration or without aspiration, and the six supernormal powers, whether with aspiration or without aspiration, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be a designation for the five eyes being with or without aspiration, or a designation for the six supernormal powers being with or without aspiration?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the five eyes have a vow or no vow is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the six supernormal powers have a vow or no vow is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the five eyes are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the six supernormal powers are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the five eyes are quiescent or non-quiescent, or whether the six supernormal powers are quiescent or non-quiescent, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less so could there be a designation for the quiescence or non-quiescence of the five eyes, or a designation for the quiescence or non-quiescence of the six supernormal powers!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the five eyes—
whether they are tranquil or untranquil— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the six superknowledges— whether they are tranquil or untranquil— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the five eyes are distant or not distant’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the six supernormal powers are distant or not distant’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the five eyes are distant or not distant, or whether the six supernormal powers are distant or not distant, these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist; how much less so could there be a designation for the distance or non-distance of the five eyes, or a designation for the distance or non-distance of the six supernormal powers!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the five eyes are distant from or not distant from [emptiness] is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the six supernormal powers are distant from or not distant from [emptiness] is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations for the five eyes—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the six supernormal powers— whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and the six supernormal powers, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the five eyes as conditioned or unconditioned, or a designation for the six supernormal powers as conditioned or unconditioned!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the five eyes—
whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the six supernormal powers— whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation of the five eyes—

whether with outflows or without outflows— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation of the six supernormal powers— whether with outflows or without outflows— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether with outflows or without outflows, and the six supernormal powers, whether with outflows or without outflows, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designations for the five eyes as being with or without outflows, or any designations for the six supernormal powers as being with or without outflows!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six superknowledges, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the five eyes’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the six supernormal powers’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the five eyes, or the arising and ceasing of the six supernormal powers, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so could there be any designation for the arising and ceasing of the five eyes, or any designation for the arising and ceasing of the six supernormal powers?!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the arising or ceasing of the five eyes is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the arising or ceasing of the six supernormal powers is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the five eyes is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the six supernormal powers is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—and the six supernormal powers—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘five eyes, virtuous or non-virtuous’ and ‘six supernormal powers, virtuous or non-virtuous’!”
Since this designation (adhivacana) does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or "the designation of the six supernormal powers, whether wholesome or unwholesome, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the five eyes is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the six supernormal powers is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether guilty or guiltless, and the six supernormal powers, whether guilty or guiltless, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be any designation for the five eyes being guilty or guiltless, or any designation for the six supernormal powers being guilty or guiltless!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes as either guilty or guiltless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six superknowledges as either guilty or guiltless is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the five eyes is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the six supernormal powers is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and the six supernormal powers—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be any designation of the five eyes as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions,’ or any designation of the six supernormal powers as ‘with afflictions’ or ‘without afflictions’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes,

whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six supernormal powers, whether with afflictions or without afflictions, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations for the five eyes—
whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the six superknowledges— whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes, whether mundane or supramundane, and the six superknowledges, whether mundane or supramundane, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be any designation for the mundane or supramundane five eyes, or any designation for the mundane or supramundane six superknowledges?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes,
whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six supernormal powers, whether mundane or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation of the five eyes,
whether defiled or purified, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation of the six supernormal powers, whether defiled or purified, is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the five eyes, or the defilement and purification of the six supernormal powers, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the five eyes, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the six supernormal powers!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes,
whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six superknowledges, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘the five eyes belong either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa’ does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘the six supernormal powers belong either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa’ does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa, and if the six supernormal powers belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—even these cannot ultimately be apprehended because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be the designation ‘the five eyes belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa,’ or the designation ‘the six supernormal powers belonging to saṃsāra or belonging to nirvāṇa’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six supernormal powers as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designation of the five eyes—whether internal, external, or between the two—is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; the designation of the six supernormal powers—whether internal, external, or between the two—is not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes—whether internal, external, or between the two—and the six supernormal powers—whether internal, external, or between the two—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the five eyes being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for the six supernormal powers being internal, external, or between the two?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the five eyes—

whether they are internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the six supernormal powers— whether they are internal, external, or between the two— is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the five eyes are obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the six supernormal powers are obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes are neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the six supernormal powers are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be the designation ‘the five eyes are obtainable or unobtainable,’ or the designation ‘the six supernormal powers are obtainable or unobtainable’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the five eyes are obtainable or unobtainable is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the six supernormal powers are obtainable or unobtainable is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation 'the ten powers of a Buddha' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations 'the four fearlessnesses,' 'the four analytical knowledges,' and 'the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If even the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ten powers of a Buddha, or designations for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "the ten powers of a Buddha" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designations "the four fearlessnesses," "the four analytical knowledges," and "the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha" are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the ten powers of a Buddha are permanent or impermanent’ does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are permanent or impermanent’ do not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether permanent or impermanent—and the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the permanence or impermanence of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the ten powers of a Buddha, whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation "the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether permanent or impermanent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation of the ten powers of a Buddha as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as either pleasure or pain is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even the pleasure and pain of the Buddha’s ten powers, or the pleasure and pain of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the pleasure and pain of the Buddha’s ten powers, or a designation for the pleasure and pain of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the ten powers of a Buddha as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the ten powers of a Buddha are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ of the Buddha’s ten powers cannot ultimately be apprehended—because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ of the Buddha’s ten powers, or designations for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as being ‘self’ or ‘non-self’? This is because their nature is non-existent.”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the ten powers of a Buddha as either "self" or "non-self" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as either "self" or "non-self" is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations for whether the ten powers of a Buddha are pure or impure are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure or impure are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the ten powers of a Buddha are pure or impure, or whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure or impure—since these are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the purity or impurity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or designations for the purity or impurity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the ten powers of a Buddha are pure or impure is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure or impure is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether the ten powers of a Buddha are empty or not empty’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,

and that the designations ‘whether the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty or not empty’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the ten powers of a Buddha are empty or not empty, or whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty or not empty—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the emptiness or non-emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the ten powers of a Buddha—whether they be empty or non-empty—is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether they be empty or non-empty—is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with signs or signless’ applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether with marks or without marks—and if the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether with marks or without marks—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the ten powers of a Buddha as being ‘with marks’ or ‘without marks,’ or any designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as being ‘with marks’ or ‘without marks’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with signs or signless" applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 32. 23. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 33.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Division: Chapter Seven on Instruction and Teaching, Part Twenty-three.
"Subhūti! For what reason do you say this?"

Is it that the designations "with aspiration" or "without aspiration" applied to the ten powers of a Buddha do not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva? Is it that the designations "with aspiration" or "without aspiration" applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether they have a wish or are without a wish—and if the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether they have a wish or are without a wish—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ten powers of a Buddha having a wish or being without a wish, or a designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha having a wish or being without a wish?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether with aspiration or without aspiration" applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the ten powers of a Buddha are tranquil or not tranquil’ is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are tranquil or not tranquil’ are not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—and the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the quiescence or non-quiescence of the ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the quiescence or non-quiescence of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of whether the ten powers of a Buddha are tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are tranquil or untranquil is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the ten powers of a Buddha are remote or not remote’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are remote or not remote’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether the ten powers of a Buddha are distant or not distant, or whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are distant or not distant—these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist. How much less could there be a designation for the distance or non-distance of the ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the distance or non-distance of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation "whether the ten powers of a Buddha are distant or not distant" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation "whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are distant or not distant" is a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designations for the ten powers of a Buddha—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha— whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-existent because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designations for the conditioned or unconditioned ten powers of a Buddha, or any designations for the conditioned or unconditioned four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, and eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of the Buddha’s ten powers—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or that the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha— whether conditioned or unconditioned— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether with outflows or without outflows—and the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the ten powers of a Buddha as being ‘with outflows or without outflows,’ or any designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as being ‘with outflows or without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of the Buddha's ten powers,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the ten powers of a Buddha’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘the arising or ceasing of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the arising and ceasing of the Buddha’s ten powers, or the arising and ceasing of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the arising and ceasing of the Buddha’s ten powers, or a designation for the arising and ceasing of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the arising or ceasing of the ten powers of a Buddha is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the arising or ceasing of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether wholesome or unwholesome’ applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—and the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ten powers of a Buddha as ‘virtuous or non-virtuous,’ or a designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as ‘virtuous or non-virtuous’?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the Buddha’s ten powers as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as either wholesome or unwholesome is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether they be blameworthy or blameless—and if the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether they be blameworthy or blameless—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the blameworthy or blameless nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the blameworthy or blameless nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the ten powers of a Buddha, whether guilty or innocent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation "the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether guilty or innocent," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the ten powers of a Buddha does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether with afflictions or without afflictions’ applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—and likewise the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether with afflictions or without afflictions—are ultimately unfindable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designation for the ten powers of a Buddha being with or without afflictions, or any designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha being with or without afflictions?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the ten powers of a Buddha is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation 'whether with afflictions or without afflictions' applied to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations for the ten powers of a Buddha—

whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha— whether mundane or supramundane— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether mundane or supramundane—and the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—whether mundane or supramundane—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the mundane or supramundane ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the mundane or supramundane four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, and eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the ten powers of a Buddha, whether worldly or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether worldly or supramundane, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designations for the ten powers of a Buddha—

whether defiled or pure— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha— whether defiled or pure— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the defilement and purification of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the defilement and purification of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the defilement and purification of the ten powers of a Buddha, or a designation for the defilement and purification of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the Buddha’s ten powers, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, whether defiled or purified, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘the ten powers of a Buddha, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,’ does not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designations ‘the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa,’ do not refer to a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa, and if the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha belong to saṃsāra or belong to nirvāṇa—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be a designation for the ten powers of a Buddha belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, or a designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha belonging to saṃsāra or nirvāṇa?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of the Buddha's ten powers as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as belonging either to saṃsāra or to nirvāṇa is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether the ten powers of a Buddha are internal, external, or between the two’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; and that the designation ‘whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are internal, external, or between the two’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha—whether internal, external, or between the two—are ultimately unapprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the ten powers of a Buddha being internal, external, or between the two, or a designation for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha being internal, external, or between the two?”
Since this designation does not exist at all, how can it be said that the designation "the ten powers of a Buddha,

whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that the designation "the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether internal, external, or between the two, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designation ‘whether the ten powers of a Buddha are obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation ‘whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are obtainable or unobtainable’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha are neither obtainable nor unobtainable, and if the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are neither obtainable nor unobtainable—since they are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist—how much less could there be any designation for the ‘obtainability or unobtainability’ of the ten powers of a Buddha, or any designation for the ‘obtainability or unobtainability’ of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "the ten powers of a Buddha, whether they are obtainable or unobtainable," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designation "the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whether they are obtainable or unobtainable," is the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
"Furthermore, Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation 'great loving-kindness' is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
and that the designations 'great compassion,' 'great sympathetic joy,' and 'great equanimity' are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied:
“World-Honored One!

If even great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so are there designations for ‘great loving-kindness,’ or designations for ‘great compassion,’ ‘great sympathetic joy,’ and ‘great equanimity’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to great loving-kindness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether permanent or impermanent’ applied to great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness—whether permanent or impermanent—and if great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether permanent or impermanent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so can there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness as permanent or impermanent,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as permanent or impermanent’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as either permanent or impermanent is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations for great loving-kindness—

whether as pleasure or as pain— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations for great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity— whether as pleasure or as pain— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even great loving-kindness that delights in suffering, or great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity that delight in suffering cannot ultimately be found—because their nature does not exist—how much less can there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness that delights in suffering,’ or designations for ‘great compassion,’ ‘great sympathetic joy,’ and ‘great equanimity that delight in suffering’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as either pleasure or pain is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to great loving-kindness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘self’ or ‘non-self’ applied to great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ‘self’ and ‘non-self’ of great loving-kindness, or the ‘self’ and ‘non-self’ of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so could there be the designations ‘self’ and ‘non-self’ for great loving-kindness, or the designations ‘self’ and ‘non-self’ for great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity!”
Since these designations do not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness as self or as non-self is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designations of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as self or as non-self are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation of ‘great loving-kindness’—

whether pure or impure— is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations of ‘great compassion,’ ‘great sympathetic joy,’ and ‘great equanimity’— whether pure or impure— are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even great loving-kindness—whether pure or impure—and great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether pure or impure—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness, pure or impure,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, pure or impure’!”
Since these designations do not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness, whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, whether pure or impure, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Based on what meaning do you say that the designations ‘great loving-kindness is either empty or not empty’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are either empty or not empty’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness—whether empty or not empty—and if great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether empty or not empty—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be any designations for ‘great loving-kindness being empty or not empty,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity being empty or not empty’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness as either empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as either empty or non-empty is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designations ‘having marks’ or ‘being markless’ applied to great loving-kindness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘having marks’ or ‘being markless’ applied to great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness, whether with signs or signless, and if great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, whether with signs or signless, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘great loving-kindness with signs or signless’ and the designations ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity with signs or signless’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as having marks or being markless is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether there is a vow or no vow’ for great loving-kindness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether there is a vow or no vow’ for great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether great loving-kindness has a vow or no vow, or whether great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity have a vow or no vow—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness having a vow or no vow,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity having a vow or no vow’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness—

whether with aspiration or without aspiration— is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designations of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity— whether with aspiration or without aspiration— are the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether great loving-kindness is tranquil or untranquil’ is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity are tranquil or untranquil’ are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—and if great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether quiescent or non-quiescent—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less so can there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness being quiescent or non-quiescent,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity being quiescent or non-quiescent’?”

Since these designations do not exist, how can it be said that the designation "great loving-kindness," whether quiescent or non-quiescent, is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; or that the designations "great compassion," "great sympathetic joy," and "great equanimity," whether quiescent or non-quiescent, are the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! For what reason do you say that the designation ‘whether great loving-kindness is distant from it or not distant from it’ is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity are distant from it or not distant from it’ are not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

Whether great loving-kindness is detached or not detached, or whether great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are detached or not detached—since these are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of great loving-kindness, or a designation for the detachment or non-detachment of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation "great loving-kindness," whether it is detached or not detached, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designations "great compassion," "great sympathetic joy," and "great equanimity," whether they are detached or not detached, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designations for great loving-kindness—

whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and that the designations for great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity— whether conditioned or unconditioned— are not the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness, whether conditioned or unconditioned, and if great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, whether conditioned or unconditioned, are ultimately non-apprehendable because their nature does not exist, how much less so can there be a designation for great loving-kindness as conditioned or unconditioned, or designations for great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity as conditioned or unconditioned?”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, whether conditioned or unconditioned, is a bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! On what basis do you say that the designation ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to great loving-kindness is not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with outflows or without outflows’ applied to great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even great loving-kindness—whether with outflows or without outflows—and great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether with outflows or without outflows—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less could there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness with or without outflows,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity with or without outflows’?”
Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that "the designation of great loving-kindness,

whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva," or that "the designation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, whether with outflows or without outflows, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva"?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designation for the arising or cessation of great loving-kindness is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designation for the arising or cessation of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity is not a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If even the arising and ceasing of great loving-kindness, or the arising and ceasing of great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designation ‘arising and ceasing of great loving-kindness,’ and the designations ‘arising and ceasing of great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity’!”
Since this designation does not exist,

how can it be said that the designation of the arising or ceasing of great loving-kindness is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or that the designation of the arising or ceasing of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say:

‘The designations for great loving-kindness—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the designations for great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva’?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness that is non-virtuous, or great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity that are virtuous yet non-virtuous, are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much more so the designations ‘great loving-kindness that is non-virtuous’ and the designations ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity that are virtuous yet non-virtuous’!”

Since this designation does not exist, how can it be said that the designation of "great loving-kindness," whether virtuous or non-virtuous, is the bodhisattva mahāsattva; or that the designations of "great compassion," "great sympathetic joy," and "great equanimity," whether virtuous or non-virtuous, are the bodhisattva mahāsattva?

“Subhūti! Upon what basis do you say that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to great loving-kindness are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and that the designations ‘whether with fault or without fault’ applied to great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness—whether it has faults or is without fault—and if great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—whether they have faults or are without fault—are ultimately unobtainable because their nature does not exist, how much less can there be a designation for ‘great loving-kindness having faults or being without fault,’ or designations for ‘great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity having faults or being without fault’?”
Since this designation does not exist,
