Why is this? World-Honored One!
The sense base of the eye is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense base of the eye, and so on, up to the sense base of the mind being empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense base of the mind.

“World-Honored One! This eye-base is empty of the eye-base; this emptiness of the eye-base is not the eye-base. The eye-base is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the eye-base. The eye-base is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the eye-base. It is the same for the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the sense-base of the eye, nor should they dwell upon any of them up to the sense-base of the mind.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not dwell in the sphere of form; they should not dwell in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form, and so on, up to the sphere of phenomena being empty of the nature of the sphere of phenomena.

"Bhagavān! This sphere of form (rūpāyatana) is empty of the sphere of form; this emptiness of the sphere of form is not the sphere of form. The sphere of form is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the sphere of form. The sphere of form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the sphere of form. It is the same for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana)."
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the sphere of form, nor should they abide in any sphere up to and including the sphere of phenomena.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not abide in the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, nor in eye-contact, nor in the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The eye-sphere is empty of the nature of the eye-sphere; even so, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

World-Honored One! This eye-element is empty of the eye-element; this emptiness of the eye-element is not the eye-element. The eye-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the eye-element. The eye-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the eye-element. It is the same for the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
Therefore, World-Honored One,

bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the eye-element, nor should they dwell in anything up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“Blessed One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, nor in ear-contact, nor in the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element; even so, the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.

World-Honored One! This ear-element is empty of the ear-element; this emptiness of the ear-element is not the ear-element. The ear-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the ear-element. The ear-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the ear-element. It is the same for the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the ear-element, nor should they dwell in any feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nor in nose-contact, nor in the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element; even so, the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“World-Honored One! This nose-element is empty of the nose-element; this emptiness of the nose-element is not the nose-element. The nose-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the nose-element. The nose-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the nose-element. It is the same for the odor-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the nose-element, nor should they dwell in any feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Bhagavān, bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, nor upon tongue-contact, nor upon the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The tongue-element is empty of the nature of the tongue-element; even so, the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

"Bhagavān! This tongue-element is empty of the tongue-element; this emptiness of the tongue-element is not the tongue-element. The tongue-element does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the tongue-element. The tongue-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the tongue-element. It is the same for the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition."
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not abide in the tongue-element, nor should they abide in any sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“Blessed One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The body-element is empty of the nature of the body-element; even so, the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

"Bhagavān! This body-element is empty of a body-element; this emptiness of the body-element is not the body-element. The body-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the body-element. The body-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the body-element. It is the same for the contact-element and even for all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition."
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not abide in the body-element, nor should they abide in any sensations produced with body-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the realm of mind, the realm of phenomena, the realm of mental consciousness, nor in mental contact, nor in the various sensations produced with mental contact as a condition.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The mental faculty (*manodhātu*) is empty of the nature of the mental faculty; even up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are empty of the nature of the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition.

"Bhagavān! This mind-element (*manodhātu*) is empty of the mind-element; this emptiness of the mind-element is not the mind-element. The mind-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the mind-element. The mind-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the mind-element. It is the same for the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) and even for all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition."
Therefore, World-Honored One,

bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the mental faculty, nor should they abide in anything up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the earth element; they should not abide in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

World-Honored One! This earth element is empty of the earth element; this emptiness of the earth element is not the earth element. The earth element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the earth element. The earth element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the earth element. It is the same for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the earth element, nor should they dwell in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the noble truth of suffering, nor should they abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.

“World-Honored One! This Noble Truth of Suffering is empty of the Noble Truth of Suffering; this emptiness of the Noble Truth of Suffering is not the Noble Truth of Suffering. The Noble Truth of Suffering does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the Noble Truth of Suffering. The Noble Truth of Suffering is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the Noble Truth of Suffering. It is the same for the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the noble truth of suffering, nor should they dwell in the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in ignorance; they should not abide in volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance; likewise, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair—all these are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“World-Honored One! This ignorance is empty of ignorance; this emptiness of ignorance is not separate from ignorance. Ignorance does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from ignorance. Ignorance is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself ignorance. It is the same for the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,

bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not abide in ignorance, nor should they abide in anything up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four dhyānas, nor should they abide in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

“World-Honored One! These four dhyānas are empty of the four dhyānas; this emptiness of the four dhyānas is not the four dhyānas. The four dhyānas are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the four dhyānas. The four dhyānas are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the four dhyānas. It is likewise with the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the four dhyānas, nor should they dwell in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not dwell in the five eyes, nor should they dwell in the six supernormal powers.”
Why is this so? World-Honored One!
The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes; the six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers.

“World-Honored One! These five eyes are not the emptiness of the five eyes; the emptiness of the five eyes is not the five eyes. The five eyes are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the five eyes. The five eyes are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the five eyes. The six supernormal powers are likewise so.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the five eyes, nor should they dwell upon the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of giving; they should not abide in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
The perfection of giving is empty of the nature of the perfection of giving, and so on, up to the perfection of wisdom being empty of the nature of the perfection of wisdom.

"Bhagavān! This perfection of giving is not empty of the perfection of giving; the emptiness of the perfection of giving is not the perfection of giving. The perfection of giving is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the perfection of giving. The perfection of giving is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the perfection of giving. It is the same for the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom."
Therefore, World-Honored One,

bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) should not abide in the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), nor should they abide in anything up to and including the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān, bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four foundations of mindfulness; they should not abide in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, and so on, up to the eight branches of the noble path being empty of the intrinsic nature of the eight branches of the noble path.

“World-Honored One! These four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the four foundations of mindfulness; the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the four foundations of mindfulness. It is the same for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor should they abide in anything up to the eightfold noble path.

“Bhagavān! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) should not abide in the ten powers of a Buddha; they should not abide in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā), or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, and so on, up to the knowledge of all aspects, which is empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects.

“World-Honored One! These ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the ten powers of a Buddha; the emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha is not the ten powers of a Buddha. The ten powers of a Buddha do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the ten powers of a Buddha. The ten powers of a Buddha are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the ten powers of a Buddha. It is the same for the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the ten powers of a Buddha, nor should they dwell in anything up to and including all-aspect omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon syllables, nor should they dwell upon what is conveyed by syllables—whether conveyed by a single word, conveyed by two words, or conveyed by many words.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
All syllables are empty of the nature of syllables; that which is produced by syllables is empty of the nature of being produced by syllables.

World-Honored One! These syllables are not the emptiness of syllables; the emptiness of syllables is not the syllables themselves. Syllables do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from syllables. Syllables are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the syllables. It is the same for all that is induced by syllables.
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon syllables, nor should they dwell upon that which is derived from syllables.

“Bhagavān, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in any phenomena as either permanent or impermanent; they should not abide in any phenomena as either pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or secluded or non-secluded.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

All phenomena, whether permanent or impermanent, are empty of the nature of permanence or impermanence; even all phenomena, whether detached or non-detached, are empty of the nature of detachment or non-detachment.

World-Honored One! These dharmas—whether permanent or impermanent—are empty of being permanent or impermanent; this emptiness of the permanence and impermanence of these dharmas is not itself permanent or impermanent. The permanence and impermanence of all dharmas do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the permanence and impermanence of all dharmas. The permanence and impermanence of all dharmas are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the permanence and impermanence of all dharmas. It is likewise for all dharmas, whether suffering or pleasure, even unto whether they are detached or non-detached.
Therefore, World-Honored One,

bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom-prajñāpāramitā should not abide in the permanence or impermanence of phenomena, nor should they abide in anything from the remoteness to the non-remoteness of phenomena.
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in suchness; they should not abide in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the limit of reality, the nature of equality, or the nature of transcendence.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
True Suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness; even the nature of being free from arising is empty of the nature of being free from arising.

World-Honored One! True Suchness is empty of non-true suchness; the emptiness of true suchness is not true suchness itself. True suchness does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from true suchness. True suchness is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself true suchness. It is the same for everything from the dharma-realm up to the nature of detachment from arising.
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in suchness, nor should they abide in anything up to and including the nature of detachment from birth.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom should not abide in any of the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor should they abide in any of the gateways of samādhi.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
All dharani-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dharani-doors; all samadhi-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all samadhi-doors.

“World-Honored One! These gates of all dhāraṇīs are not empty of the emptiness of all dhāraṇīs; the emptiness of all dhāraṇīs is not separate from the gates of all dhāraṇīs. The gates of all dhāraṇīs do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the gates of all dhāraṇīs. The gates of all dhāraṇīs are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the gates of all dhāraṇīs. It is the same for all gates of samādhi.”
Therefore, World-Honored One,
bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in any dharanī-doors, nor should they abide in any samādhi-doors.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping at 'I' and 'mine,' their mind then dwells upon form, and dwells upon feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."
Because of dwelling in this way, one applies effort toward form, and applies effort toward feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, their mind dwells upon the sense base of the eye, and dwells upon the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
Because they dwell in this way, they apply effort toward the sense base of the eye, and so on, up to applying effort toward the sense base of the mind.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to practice the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to bring the *prajñāpāramitā* to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the sphere of forms, and dwells upon the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.”
Because of dwelling in this way, one applies effort toward the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), and so on, up to applying effort toward the sphere of phenomena (*dharmāyatana*).

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
Because they dwell in this manner, they apply effort toward the eye constituent, and so on, up to applying effort toward the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect knowledge.

“Bhagavān, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
Because they dwell in this way, they apply effort toward the ear-element, and so on, up to applying effort toward the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells in the nose element, dwells in the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as in nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Because they dwell in this way, they apply effort toward the nose element, and so on, up to applying effort toward the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience.
“Blessed One,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the tongue element, dwells upon the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Because they dwell in this way, they apply effort toward the tongue element, and so on, up to applying effort toward the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā).

“Bhagavān, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the body element, dwells upon the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

Because of dwelling in this manner, one applies effort toward the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), and so on, up to applying effort toward the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to practice the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to bring the *prajñāpāramitā* to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the mental element (*manodhātu*), dwells upon the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mental-consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition.”
Because of dwelling in this way, one applies effort toward the mind-element (*manodhātu*), and so on, up to applying effort toward the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, their mind dwells upon the earth element, and dwells upon the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
Because of this dwelling, one applies effort toward the earth element, and so on, up to applying effort toward the consciousness element.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to practice the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to bring the *prajñāpāramitā* to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“Blessed One,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping at ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the noble truth of suffering, and dwells upon the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
Because of dwelling in this way, one applies effort toward the Noble Truth of Suffering, and applies effort toward the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells in ignorance, and it dwells in volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
Because they abide in this way, they apply effort toward ignorance, and so on, up to applying effort toward old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind will abide in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.”
Because they abide in this way, they apply themselves to the four dhyānas and apply themselves to the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.

Due to such application, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind then dwells upon the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.”
Because they abide in this way, they apply themselves to the five eyes and apply themselves to the six supernormal powers.

Due to such application, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all aspects.

“Bhagavān, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the perfection of generosity, and dwells upon the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Because of abiding in this state, one applies oneself to the perfection of generosity, and so forth, up to applying oneself to the perfection of wisdom.

Due to such application, one is unable to grasp the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all aspects.

“Bhagavān, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the four foundations of mindfulness, and dwells upon the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.”
Because of dwelling in this way, one applies oneself to the four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including applying oneself to the eight branches of the noble path.

Due to such application, one is unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom, unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience.

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon the ten powers of a buddha; it dwells upon the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”
Because they abide in this way, they apply themselves to the ten powers of a Buddha, up to applying themselves to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Due to such application, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all aspects.
“Blessed One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping at ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon syllables and is led away by those syllables—whether led by a single word, two words, or many words.”
Because of dwelling in this way, one applies effort toward the syllables and applies effort toward what is induced by those syllables.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to practice the *prajñāpāramitā*, unable to bring the *prajñāpāramitā* to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind dwells upon phenomena as either permanent or impermanent; it dwells upon phenomena as either pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, and as secluded or non-secluded.”

Because they abide in this way, they apply effort to [conceptualizing] all phenomena as either permanent or impermanent, and so on, up to applying effort to [conceptualizing] all phenomena as either detached or non-detached.

Due to such application of effort, they are unable to embrace the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, because they are entangled by the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ their mind then dwells upon all the doors of dhāraṇī and dwells upon all the doors of samādhi.”
Because of dwelling in this state, one applies effort toward all doors of dhāraṇī and applies effort toward all doors of samādhi.

Due to such application of effort, one is unable to grasp the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), unable to practice the perfection of wisdom, unable to bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and unable to accomplish the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).
"Why is this? World-Honored One!
Form should not be grasped; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness should not be grasped."

Since form should not be grasped, it is not form; since feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness should not be grasped, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
Furthermore, one should not grasp at any of the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor should one grasp at any of the gateways of samādhi.
If the gateways of dhāraṇī were not to be grasped, they would not be gateways of dhāraṇī; if the gateways of samādhi were not to be grasped, they would not be gateways of samādhi.
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is empty.

That which is grasped as the perfection of the cultivation of the *prajñāpāramitā* should likewise not be grasped; since such a *prajñāpāramitā* should not be grasped, it is not [inherently] the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
"In this way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should contemplate all phenomena through the emptiness of intrinsic nature."
When practicing this contemplation, the mind finds no place of movement within any phenomena; this is called the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of Non-appropriation.
This samādhi is subtle, supreme, vast, and immeasurable; it can gather infinite and unimpeded functions, which are not shared with any Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.

That which accomplishes all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) should likewise not be grasped; since all-aspect omniscience should not be grasped in this way, it would then no longer be all-aspect omniscience.

Why is this? It is because of internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.
For what reason?
World-Honored One,
this knowledge of all aspects is not attained through the cultivation of grasping at signs.
Why is this so? All grasping at signs is affliction.
What are these signs?

What are called the marks of form, the marks of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, up to and including the marks of all dharani-doors and the marks of all samadhi-doors—clinging to these various marks is called affliction.
"If one were to cultivate the attainment of the knowledge of all aspects by grasping at signs, the brahmin Jayasena would not have faith and understanding in the knowledge of all-knowledge.
What, then, is called the mark of that faith and understanding?"

This means that one generates profound pure faith in the *prajñāpāramitā* and, through the power of resolute conviction (*adhimukti*), contemplates and examines the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), neither by means of signs (*nimitta*) nor by means of non-signs, because both signs and non-signs are equally ungraspable.

Although this brahmin Jayasena has turned toward the Buddha-dharma through the power of faith and understanding and is thus called a "follower by faith," he is nevertheless able to enter into the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) by means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Having thus attained realization, they do not grasp at the marks of form, nor do they grasp at the marks of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; indeed, they do not grasp at the marks of any dhāraṇī doors, nor do they grasp at the marks of any samādhi doors.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*), and both the grasper and the grasped are unobtainable.

"In this way, O Brahmin, one does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) by attaining realization internally; one does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by attaining realization externally; one does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by attaining realization both internally and externally; one does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by attaining realization through non-knowledge; one does not contemplate the knowledge of all modes by attaining realization through anything else; nor does one contemplate the knowledge of all modes by not attaining realization."

Why is this? This brahmin Jayasena does not see the omniscient wisdom that is observed, nor does he see the prajñā that observes, nor does he see the observer or the basis upon which observation depends.

This brahmin Jitāri does not contemplate the knowledge of all-knowledge within internal form; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all-knowledge within internal feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

He does not contemplate the knowledge of all-knowledge within external form; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all-knowledge within external feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

He does not contemplate the knowledge of all-knowledge within both internal and external form; he does not contemplate the knowledge of all-knowledge within both internal and external feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Nor does one contemplate the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) apart from form; nor does one contemplate the knowledge of all modes apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
This extends to not contemplating the knowledge of all modes within any of the internal doors of dhāraṇī, nor contemplating the knowledge of all modes within any of the internal doors of samādhi;
nor contemplating the knowledge of all modes within any of the external doors of dhāraṇī, nor contemplating the knowledge of all modes within any of the external doors of samādhi.
One does not contemplate all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) by means of any internal or external dharanī-gates, nor does one contemplate all-knowledge by means of any internal or external samādhi-gates;
furthermore, one does not contemplate all-knowledge apart from all dharanī-gates, nor does one contemplate all-knowledge apart from all samādhi-gates.
Why is this? Because whether internal, external, both internal and external, or apart from both internal and external, none of these can be apprehended.
Thus, through such gateways of detachment as these, the brahmin Jayasena conceived deep faith and understanding in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Through this faith and understanding, one has no grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, because the true nature of all phenomena (*dharmatā*) is unattainable.

Thus, O Brahmin, having attained faith and understanding in the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) by means of the gate of signlessness (*animitta*), one does not grasp at signs regarding any phenomena, nor does one contemplate signlessness; for both phenomena characterized by signs and those characterized by signlessness are unattainable.

In this way, by the power of his resolute conviction (*adhimukti*), the brahmin neither grasps nor rejects any phenomena, for within the reality of the true nature (*dharmatā*) there is no grasping or rejecting.
At that time, that brahmin did not even cling to his own conviction, up to and including nirvāṇa itself.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty and cannot be grasped.
"World-Honored One!..."
The Prajñāpāramitā of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also like this: it has no grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, for it is able to go from this shore to the other shore;
if there were even the slightest grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, one would not be able to reach the other shore.

Therefore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not grasp at any form (rūpa), nor do they grasp at any feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), or consciousness (vijñāna), because all phenomena (dharmas) are without anything to be grasped;
this extends even to not grasping at any doors of dhāraṇī or any doors of samādhi, likewise because all phenomena are without anything to be grasped.

Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp anything—whether collectively or individually—with respect to all forms, all feelings, perceptions, formations, and consciousness, up to and including all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;

yet, because the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path practiced through their original vows are not yet perfected, and because the ten powers of a buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects realized through their original vows are not yet accomplished, they do not enter parinirvāṇa in the interim by means of non-grasping at any signs.

Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fulfill the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path, and are able to accomplish the ten powers of a buddha up to all-aspect omniscience, they do not perceive the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path, nor do they perceive the ten powers of a buddha up to all-aspect omniscience.

Why is this? Because these four foundations of mindfulness are not four foundations of mindfulness; up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, which are not the eight branches of the noble path; and the ten powers of a Buddha, which are not the ten powers of a Buddha; up to and including all-aspect omniscience, which is not all-aspect omniscience—because all phenomena are neither phenomena nor non-phenomena.
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, although there is nothing to be grasped among all phenomena, they are nevertheless able to accomplish all activities.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Thirty-Seven;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Thirty-Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
10. Chapter on the Characteristics of the Practice of Prajñā, Part One: Chapter Ten, Part One, on the Characteristics of the Practice of Prajñā.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of prajñā, they should perform this contemplation: "
What is this *prajñāpāramitā*?
For what reason is it called *prajñāpāramitā*?
To whom does this *prajñāpāramitā* belong?
"For what purpose is this perfection of wisdom used?

Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they examine it with precise scrutiny: "If a phenomenon is non-existent and unapprehendable, that is the perfection of wisdom; within that which is non-existent and unapprehendable, what can be questioned or criticized?"
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"In this context, what dharma is non-existent and unobtainable?
Subhūti replied:

"This means that the phenomena of the perfection of wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended; the phenomena of the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity do not exist and cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? It is because of internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the beginningless and endless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Śāriputra! The dharma of form does not exist and cannot be apprehended; the dharmas of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended. Śāriputra!”
The phenomena of the eye-base are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are non-existent and unapprehendable.
The phenomena of the form-base are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases are non-existent and unapprehendable.

“Śāriputra! The phenomena of the eye-element are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The phenomena of the ear-element are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

The phenomena of the nose element are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The phenomena of the tongue element are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The phenomena of the body element are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The mind-element (*manodhātu*) and phenomena (*dharma*) do not exist and are unapprehendable; the phenomenon-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition do not exist and are unapprehendable.

"Śāriputra! The phenomena of the earth element do not exist and cannot be apprehended; the phenomena of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements do not exist and cannot be apprehended."
“Śāriputra! The dharma of the noble truth of suffering is non-existent and unapprehendable; the dharmas of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Śāriputra! The phenomenon of ignorance does not exist and cannot be apprehended; the phenomena of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not exist and cannot be apprehended.”

“Śāriputra! Within the dharma of internal emptiness, there is nothing that exists and nothing that can be apprehended. Within the dharmas of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is nothing that exists and nothing that can be apprehended.”
“Śāriputra! The dharmas of the four dhyānas do not exist and cannot be apprehended; the dharmas of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“Śāriputra! The dharmas of the five eyes do not exist and cannot be apprehended; the dharmas of the six supernormal powers do not exist and cannot be apprehended. Śāriputra!”

The phenomena of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-existent and unapprehendable; the phenomena of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-existent and unapprehendable.

“Śāriputra! The dharmas of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-existent and unapprehendable; the dharmas of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Śāriputra! True thusness (tathatā) is non-existent and unapprehendable; the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), equality (samatā), and the nature of freedom from arising (anabhinirvṛtti)—these dharmas are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Śāriputra! The dharma of stream-entry does not exist and cannot be apprehended; the dharmas of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddhahood do not exist and cannot be apprehended."
“Śāriputra! The dharmas of a bodhisattva do not exist and cannot be apprehended; the dharmas of a Tathāgata do not exist and cannot be apprehended. Śāriputra!”
To state it briefly: whether permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful,
self or non-self, pure or impure, empty or non-empty, signless or with signs,
wishless or with wishes, tranquil or not tranquil, or secluded or...
It is not apart from— whether defiled or pure, arising or ceasing, conditioned or unconditioned,
with outflows or without outflows, wholesome or unwholesome,
faulty or faultless, mundane or supramundane, pertaining to birth-and-death or pertaining to nirvāṇa.
Whether past, future, or present; whether wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate;
whether bound to the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm; whether of the learner, the non-learner, or neither learner nor non-learner;
whether to be abandoned by vision, abandoned by cultivation, or not to be abandoned; or if it is...
Whether internal, external, or in between, all such phenomena are non-existent and unobtainable. Why is this so?

By virtue of internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the beginningless and endless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Śāriputra!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and thus scrutinizes all phenomena as being non-existent and unapprehendable, if their mind does not sink into despondency nor feel regret, and their mind is neither startled, terrified, nor afraid, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to never abandon the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"By what cause and condition do you know that these bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are able to never abandon the perfection of wisdom?"

Subhūti replied, “When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they know the perfection of wisdom as it truly is to be devoid of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom; they know the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity as they truly are to be devoid of the intrinsic natures of meditative concentration through to generosity.”
Śāriputra! By this you should know that these bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are able to never abandon the perfection of wisdom.

“Śāriputra! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they know form as it truly is to be free from the intrinsic nature of form; they know feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are to be free from the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

They know the sense-base of the eye as it truly is to be free from the intrinsic nature of the sense-base of the eye; they know the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as they truly are to be free from the intrinsic nature of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
One knows, as it truly is, that the sense-base of form is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the sense-base of form;

one knows, as it truly is, that the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena;

one knows, as it truly is, that the eye-element is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the eye-element; and one knows, as it truly is, that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.

He knows the ear-element as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the ear-element; he knows the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the sound-element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as condition.

He knows the nose-element as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the nose-element; he knows the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the odor-element up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as condition.

He knows the tongue-element as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the tongue-element; he knows the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition, as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the taste-element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition.

He knows the body-element as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the body-element; he knows the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as condition, as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the touch-element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as condition;

he knows the mind-element as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the mind-element; he knows the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the mental-object-element up to the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition;

he knows the earth-element as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the earth-element; he knows the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements.

One knows the Noble Truth of Suffering as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the Noble Truth of Suffering; one knows the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path;

one knows ignorance as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of ignorance; and one knows volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

One knows internal emptiness as it truly is, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness; one knows external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of external emptiness up to the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

one knows the four dhyānas as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas; and one knows the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

He knows the five eyes as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the five eyes; he knows the six supernormal powers as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers.

He knows the four foundations of mindfulness as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; he knows the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path.

He knows the ten powers of a Buddha as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; he knows the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects as they truly are, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects.

One knows *tathatā* (suchness) as it truly is, as being free from the intrinsic nature of *tathatā*; one knows the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthiti*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), equality, and the state beyond birth (*anabhisambhava*) as they truly are, as being free from the intrinsic nature of the *dharmadhātu* up to the state beyond birth;

one knows the stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*) as they truly are, as being free from the intrinsic nature of a stream-enterer; one knows the once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmin*), the non-returner (*anāgāmin*), the arhat, and the pratyekabuddha as they truly are, as being free from the intrinsic nature of a once-returner up to that of a pratyekabuddha;

one knows the bodhisattva as they truly are, as being free from the intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva; and one knows the Tathāgata as they truly are, as being free from the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata.

He knows, as they truly are, the phenomena of permanence and impermanence, and he knows that their intrinsic nature is free from permanence and impermanence; he knows, as they truly are, pleasure and suffering, self and non-self, purity and impurity, emptiness and non-emptiness, signlessness and having signs, wishlessness and having wishes, tranquility and non-tranquility, detachment and non-detachment, defilement and purification, arising and ceasing, the conditioned and the unconditioned, the out-flowing and the non-out-flowing, the wholesome and the unwholesome, the blameworthy and the blameless, the mundane and the supramundane, and the phenomena belonging to saṃsāra and those belonging to nirvāṇa, and he knows that their intrinsic nature is free from pleasure and suffering, up to and including the phenomena belonging to saṃsāra and those belonging to nirvāṇa.

He knows, as they truly are, the phenomena of the past, future, and present, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the past, future, and present; he knows, as they truly are, the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate; those bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; the trainee, the beyond-training, and that which is neither trainee nor beyond-training; those to be abandoned by vision, those to be abandoned by cultivation, and those not to be abandoned; and the internal, external, and intermediate phenomena, as being devoid of the intrinsic nature of the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, up to the internal, external, and intermediate phenomena themselves.
Śāriputra! By this you should know that those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom are able to never abandon the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"What is the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom?
What is the intrinsic nature of the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity?"
"Furthermore, what is the intrinsic nature of those phenomena that are internal, external, or both?

Subhūti replied, "The absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāvatā*) is the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*); the absence of intrinsic nature is the intrinsic nature of the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity; and so on, up to the fact that the absence of intrinsic nature is the intrinsic nature of those phenomena that are internal, external, or both."

Śāriputra! By this you should know that the perfection of wisdom is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom; the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the perfections from meditative concentration down to generosity; and even all phenomena—whether internal, external, or both—are devoid of the intrinsic nature of being internal, external, or both.

Śāriputra! The perfection of wisdom is devoid of the characteristic of the perfection of wisdom; the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are devoid of the characteristics of meditative concentration through to generosity; and so on, up to internal, external, and intermediate phenomena being devoid of the characteristics of internal, external, and intermediate phenomena.

Śāriputra! Self-nature is also free from self-nature; characteristics are also free from characteristics; self-nature is also free from characteristics; characteristics are also free from self-nature; and both self-nature and characteristics are free from characteristics and self-nature; and characteristics and self-nature are also free from self-nature and characteristics.
Then, Śāriputra said to Subhūti:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this, they will be able to accomplish all-aspect omniscience.”
Subhūti replied: "So it is! So it is!"
It is exactly as you have said.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this, they will be able to accomplish all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). Why is that?
"Śāriputra! This is because the bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all phenomena are without arising and without accomplishment.
Śāriputra said:
"For what reason are all phenomena neither produced nor brought to completion?
Subhūti replied:
"Because form is empty, the production and completion of form cannot be apprehended."
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty, the arising and accomplishment of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended.
Because the eye-base is empty, the arising and accomplishment of the eye-base cannot be apprehended;
because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty, the arising and accomplishment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases cannot be apprehended.
Because the sense base of form is empty, the production and accomplishment of the sense base of form cannot be apprehended;

because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty, the production and accomplishment of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended.

Because the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are empty, the production and accomplishment of the eye-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended.

Because the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are empty, the production and accomplishment of the ear-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended.

Because the nose-element, the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are empty, the production and accomplishment of the nose-element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended.

Because the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition, are empty, the production and accomplishment of the tongue element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition cannot be apprehended;

because the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and all feelings produced with body-contact as condition, are empty, the production and accomplishment of the body element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as condition cannot be apprehended;

because the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, as well as mind-contact and all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are empty, the production and accomplishment of the mind element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition cannot be apprehended.
Because the earth element is empty, the production, generation, and accomplishment of the earth element cannot be apprehended;

because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty, the production, generation, and accomplishment of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements cannot be apprehended.
Because the noble truth of suffering is empty, the arising, existence, and accomplishment of the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty, the arising, existence, and accomplishment of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended.
Because ignorance is empty, the production and accomplishment of ignorance cannot be apprehended;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty, the production and accomplishment of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cannot be apprehended.
“Because internal emptiness is empty, the production and accomplishment of internal emptiness cannot be apprehended;

because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are empty, the production and accomplishment of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended.”
“Because the four dhyānas are empty, the generation and accomplishment of the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty, the generation and accomplishment of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended.”
Because the five eyes are empty, the production and accomplishment of the five eyes cannot be apprehended;
because the six supernormal powers are empty, the production and accomplishment of the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended.
Because the perfection of giving is empty, the production and accomplishment of the perfection of giving cannot be apprehended;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty, the production and accomplishment of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom cannot be apprehended.
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty, the arising and accomplishment of the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are empty, the arising and accomplishment of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended.
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are empty, the production, generation, and accomplishment of the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty, the production, generation, and accomplishment of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended.
Because true thusness is empty, the production, generation, and accomplishment of true thusness cannot be apprehended;

because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), equality (samatā), and the state beyond birth (anupapatti) are empty, the production, generation, and accomplishment of the realm of phenomena up to the state beyond birth cannot be apprehended.
“Because the stream-enterer is empty, the accomplishment of the state of a stream-enterer cannot be apprehended;
because the once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha are empty, the accomplishment of the states from once-returner up to pratyekabuddha cannot be apprehended.”
“Because the bodhisattva is empty, the arising, formation, and accomplishment of a bodhisattva cannot be apprehended;
because the Tathāgata is empty, the arising, formation, and accomplishment of a Tathāgata cannot be apprehended.
Because the dharmas of permanence and impermanence are empty, the arising, formation, and accomplishment of the dharmas of permanence and impermanence cannot be apprehended.”

Because the dharmas—ranging from pleasure and suffering, self and non-self, purity and impurity, emptiness and non-emptiness, signlessness and having signs, wishlessness and having wishes, tranquility and non-tranquility, detachment and non-detachment, affliction and purification, arising and ceasing, conditioned and unconditioned, outflowing and non-outflowing, wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, mundane and supramundane, to those belonging to saṃsāra and those belonging to nirvāṇa—are empty, it is impossible to find the production or accomplishment of these dharmas, from pleasure and suffering up to those belonging to saṃsāra and those belonging to nirvāṇa.
Because past, future, and present phenomena are empty, the arising, production, and accomplishment of past, future, and present phenomena cannot be apprehended;

because wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena; phenomena bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; phenomena of those in training, those beyond training, and those who are neither; phenomena to be abandoned by seeing, by cultivation, and those not to be abandoned; and phenomena that are internal, external, or both, are empty, the arising, production, and accomplishment of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena, up to those that are internal, external, or both, cannot be apprehended.
“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the *prajñāpāramitā* in this manner, they draw near to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
To the extent that this bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the knowledge of all aspects, to that same extent they attain purity of body, purity of speech, purity of mind, and purity of marks.”
