To the extent that this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains purity of body, purity of speech, purity of mind, and purity of marks, to that same extent he does not give rise to a mind associated with greed, does not give rise to a mind associated with hatred, does not give rise to a mind associated with delusion, does not give rise to a mind associated with pride, does not give rise to a mind associated with flattery and deception, does not give rise to a mind associated with stinginess and covetousness, and does not give rise to any mind associated with dogmatic views.

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to a mind associated with craving, nor even a mind associated with any of the various views, they will ultimately never fall into a woman’s womb, but will always undergo miraculous birth, and will also never be born in any of the perilous and evil realms.

Except for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings, they shall travel from one Buddha-field to another, making offerings to, revering, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields, until they attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, never being separated from the Buddhas.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain such meritorious benefits as these, they should study the perfection of wisdom and must not abandon it.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they course in form or course in the characteristics of form, they are not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.”

If one courses in feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, or if one courses in the characteristics of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, one is not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.

"If one practices with regard to form as being permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the mark of form as being permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the marks of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom."
If one practices with regard to the pleasure or pain of form, or practices with regard to the characteristic of pleasure or pain in form, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if one practices with regard to the pleasure or pain of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, or practices with regard to the characteristic of pleasure or pain in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding form, or practices with the mark of self or non-self regarding form, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or practices with the mark of self or non-self regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of form, or practices with regard to the marks of the purity or impurity of form, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, or practices with regard to the marks of the purity or impurity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with the thought that form is empty or not empty, or if one practices with the mark that form is empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with the thought that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty or not empty, or if one practices with the mark that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that form is signless yet possesses signs, or if one practices with the notion that the signlessness of form possesses signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are signless yet possess signs, or if one practices with the notion that the signlessness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness possesses signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with the wish for form while it is wishless, or practices with the sign of wishing for form while it is wishless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the wish for feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness while they are wishless, or practices with the sign of wishing for feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness while they are wishless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to whether form is tranquil or not tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of form being tranquil or not tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to whether feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are tranquil or not tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness being tranquil or not tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to form as being either detached or non-detached, or practices with regard to the characteristic of form as being either detached or non-detached, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being either detached or non-detached, or practices with regard to the characteristic of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being either detached or non-detached, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they course in the sense-field of the eye or course in the characteristics of the sense-field of the eye, they are not coursing in the perfection of wisdom;

if they course in the sense-fields of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, or course in the characteristics of the sense-fields of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, they are not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to the sense-base of the eye as permanent or impermanent, or if one practices with regard to the characteristic of the sense-base of the eye as permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as permanent or impermanent, or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the eye-base as pleasure or pain, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the eye-base as pleasure or pain, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with regard to the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as pleasure or pain, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as pleasure or pain, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the sense base of the eye as "self" or "non-self," or if one practices with the sense base of the eye as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self," one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as "self" or "non-self," or if one practices with the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self," one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the sense base of the eye, or practices with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the sense base of the eye, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or practices with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-base of the eye, or practices with regard to the mark of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-base of the eye, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or practices with regard to the mark of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of signs regarding the signless eye-base, or practices with the notion of the sign of signlessness regarding the signless eye-base, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of signs regarding the signless ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, or practices with the notion of the sign of signlessness regarding the signless ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the wish for the sphere of the eye while it is wishless, or practices with the mark of wishing for the sphere of the eye while it is wishless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the wish for the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind while they are wishless, or practices with the mark of wishing for the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind while they are wishless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the eye-base as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the eye-base as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-base as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-base as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the sense-base of the eye as being detached or non-detached, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the sense-base of the eye as being detached or non-detached, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being detached or non-detached, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being detached or non-detached, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with respect to the sense-base of form, or practices with respect to the characteristics of the sense-base of form, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if one practices with respect to the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, or practices with respect to the characteristics of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the spheres of form as being permanent or impermanent, or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the sphere of form, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as being permanent or impermanent, or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the pleasure and pain of the sense-base of forms, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure and pain of the sense-base of forms, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the pleasure and pain of the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure and pain of the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the sense-base of forms, or practices with regard to the signs of purity or impurity in the sense-base of forms, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, or practices with regard to the signs of purity or impurity in the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sphere of forms, or practices with regard to the mark of emptiness or non-emptiness of the sphere of forms, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, or practices with regard to the mark of emptiness or non-emptiness of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the sphere of form is signless yet possesses signs, or if one practices with the notion that the sphere of form is signless yet possesses the signs of being signless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are signless yet possess signs, or if one practices with the notion that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are signless yet possess the signs of being signless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with the thought of wishing for form while it is wishless, or if one practices with the mark of wishing for form while it is wishless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the thought of wishing for sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena while they are wishless, or if one practices with the mark of wishing for sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena while they are wishless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the spheres of form as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the spheres of form as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the sense bases of forms as being either detached or non-detached, or practices with regard to the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment in the sense bases of forms, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena as being either detached or non-detached, or practices with regard to the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment in the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and if they course in the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; or if they course in the characteristics of the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, they are not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether they are permanent or impermanent—or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with respect to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as eye-contact and the various feelings of pleasure or pain arising conditioned by eye-contact; or if one practices with respect to the characteristics of the eye-element up to the various feelings of pleasure or pain arising conditioned by eye-contact—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notions of self or non-self regarding the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; or if one practices with the marks of self or non-self regarding the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the contact of the eye, as well as the pure or impure feelings arising conditioned by that eye-contact; or if one practices with regard to the signs of purity or impurity in the eye-element, up to the signs of purity or impurity in the feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the contact of the eye, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are either empty or not empty; or if one practices with the notion of the marks of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, are signless or have signs; or if one practices with the notion that these—the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition—possess the characteristic of being signless or having signs, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, whether with the notion of wishlessness or the notion of wishing; or if one practices with the characteristics of wishlessness or wishing regarding the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether they are tranquil or untranquil—or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the tranquility or lack of tranquility of the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether regarding them as being detached or not detached, or practicing with the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment regarding the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

"If one courses in the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition; or if one courses in the characteristics of the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition—that is not coursing in the perfection of wisdom."

If one practices with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether regarding them as permanent or impermanent, or practicing with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with respect to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings of pleasure and pain arising conditioned by ear-contact; or if one practices with respect to the characteristics of the ear element up to the various feelings of pleasure and pain arising conditioned by ear-contact—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—conceiving them as "self" or "non-self"—or if one practices by way of the characteristics of "self" or "non-self" regarding the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with regard to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as the pure or impure feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of purity or impurity of the ear element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether regarding them as signless or with signs, or practicing with the characteristic of being signless or with signs regarding the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether wishing for them or not wishing for them—or if one practices with the signs of wishing for or not wishing for the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether they are tranquil or untranquil—or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, whether they are tranquil or untranquil, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether regarding them as being detached or not detached, or practicing with the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment regarding the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“If one courses in the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, or if one courses in the characteristics of the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, this is not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to the sphere of the nose, the sphere of odors, the sphere of nose-consciousness, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—whether regarding them as permanent or impermanent, or practicing with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the sphere of the nose up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one courses in the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings of pleasure or pain arising with nose-contact as their condition; or if one courses in the characteristics of the nose element up to the various feelings of pleasure or pain arising with nose-contact as their condition, this is not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; or if one practices with the marks of self or non-self regarding the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and the contact of the nose, as well as the pure or impure feelings produced with that nasal contact as a condition; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the nose element up to the pure or impure feelings produced with nasal contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and the contact of the nose, as well as the various feelings produced with that nose-contact as a condition; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the nose element up to the various feelings produced with that nose-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and the contact of the nose, as well as the various feelings produced with that nasal contact as a condition—whether regarding them as signless or as having signs, or practicing with the characteristic of being signless or having signs regarding these factors from the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nasal contact as a condition—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the element of the nose, the element of odors, the element of nose-consciousness, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—or if one practices with the characteristics of the element of the nose up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—whether with aspiration or without aspiration—one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the sphere of the nose, the sphere of odors, the sphere of nose-consciousness, and the contact of the nose—as well as the various feelings produced with that nasal contact as a condition—whether they are tranquil or untranquil; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the sphere of the nose up to the various feelings produced with nasal contact as a condition, whether they are tranquil or untranquil, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—whether in terms of being detached or not detached from them, or practicing with the signs of detachment or non-detachment regarding the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“If one courses in the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition; or if one courses in the characteristics of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition—this is not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to the element of the tongue, the element of taste, the element of tongue-consciousness, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether they are permanent or impermanent—or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the element of the tongue up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with respect to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings of pleasure or pain produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or if one practices with respect to the characteristics of the tongue element up to the various feelings of pleasure or pain produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether conceiving them as self or non-self—or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as being self or non-self, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; or if one practices with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are either empty or not empty; or if one practices with the mark of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition being either empty or not empty, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the signless or with signs regarding the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; or if one practices with the characteristic of being signless or having signs regarding the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the desire for the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether characterized by the absence of aspiration or the presence of aspiration—or if one practices with the characteristics of the absence of aspiration or the presence of aspiration regarding the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the serenity or lack of serenity of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of serenity or lack of serenity in the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether practicing their separation or non-separation; or if one practices with the characteristics of the separation or non-separation of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

"If one practices with respect to the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, or if one practices with respect to the characteristics of the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom."

If one practices with regard to the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—whether they are permanent or impermanent—or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with respect to the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings of pleasure and pain arising with body-contact as their condition, or if one practices with respect to the characteristics of the body element up to the various feelings of pleasure and pain arising with body-contact as their condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, [conceiving of them] as self or non-self; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition as being self or non-self, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with regard to the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings—whether pure or impure—arising conditioned by body-contact, or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the body element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by body-contact, whether pure or impure, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are either empty or not empty; or if one practices with the mark that the body element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are either empty or not empty—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—whether they are signless or with signs, or whether one practices with the characteristic of being signless or with signs regarding the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the wishful or wishless regarding the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; or if one practices with the signs of wishfulness or wishlessness regarding the body element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the serenity or lack of serenity of the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of serenity or lack of serenity in the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—whether regarding them as being detached or not detached, or practicing with the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment regarding the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

"If one practices with regard to the mind-element, the phenomena-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom."

If one practices with the notion that the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are either permanent or impermanent; or if one practices with the notion that the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition possess the characteristics of being permanent or impermanent—this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the mind-element, the phenomena-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings of pleasure and pain arising with mental contact as their condition, or if one practices with regard to the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings of pleasure and pain arising with mental contact as their condition, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notions of self or non-self regarding the mind-element (*manodhātu*), the phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising conditioned by mental contact; or if one practices with the marks of self or non-self regarding the mind-element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by mental contact—one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with the mental faculty element (*manodhātu*), the phenomena element (*dharmadhātu*), the mental consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced conditioned by mental contact—whether pure or impure—or if one practices with the characteristics of the mental faculty element up to the various feelings produced conditioned by mental contact, whether pure or impure, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with the notion that the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are either empty or not empty; or if one practices with the notion of the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition being either empty or not empty, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the idea that the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are signless or have signs; or if one practices with the idea that the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition possess the characteristic of being signless or having signs, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the intention that the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are either wishless or possessed of wishes; or if one practices with the characteristic that these—from the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—are either wishless or possessed of wishes, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the intention that the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are either tranquil or untranquil; or if one practices with the characteristic that the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are either tranquil or untranquil, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—whether in terms of being detached or not detached, or whether in terms of the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment regarding the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—that is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they course in the earth element or course in the characteristics of the earth element, they are not coursing in the perfection of wisdom;

whether they course in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, or course in the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, they are not coursing in the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to the earth element as permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the earth element as permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the pleasure and pain of the earth element, or practices with regard to the characteristics of pleasure and pain of the earth element, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if one practices with regard to the pleasure and pain of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, or practices with regard to the characteristics of pleasure and pain of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding the earth element, or if one practices with the notion of the characteristic of self or non-self regarding the earth element, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, or if one practices with the notion of the characteristic of self or non-self regarding the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the earth element, or practices with regard to the signs of purity or impurity of the earth element, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, or practices with regard to the signs of purity or impurity of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the earth element as empty or non-empty, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the earth element as empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if one practices with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as empty or non-empty, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the earth element is signless yet possesses signs, or if one practices with the notion that the earth element has the characteristic of being signless yet possessing signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are signless yet possess signs, or if one practices with the notion that these elements have the characteristic of being signless yet possessing signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the thought that the earth element is wishless yet possesses a wish, or if one practices with the mark that the earth element is wishless yet possesses a wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the thought that the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are wishless yet possess a wish, or if one practices with the mark that the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are wishless yet possess a wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the element of earth as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the element of earth as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the earth element as being distant or not distant, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the earth element as being distant or not distant, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as being distant or not distant, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as being distant or not distant, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Scroll Thirty-Eight (and Thirty-Nine) Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The Tenth Chapter of the First Division, "Characteristics of the Practice of Prajñāpāramitā," Part Two:
"World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they practice the Noble Truth of Suffering or practice the characteristics of the Noble Truth of Suffering, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom."

If one practices the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, or practices the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the noble truth of the suffering of conditioned formations is permanent or impermanent, or if one practices with the notion of the characteristic of permanence or impermanence regarding the noble truth of the suffering of conditioned formations, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path are permanent or impermanent, or if one practices with the notion of the characteristic of permanence or impermanence regarding the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the noble truth of suffering as pleasure or suffering, or practices the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as pleasure or suffering, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as pleasure or suffering, or practices the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as pleasure or suffering, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the Noble Truth of Suffering as "self" or "non-self," or if one practices the Noble Truth of Suffering with the characteristic of "self" or "non-self," one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as "self" or "non-self," or if one practices the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path with the characteristic of "self" or "non-self," one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the noble truth of suffering as pure or impure, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as pure or impure, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as pure or impure, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as pure or impure, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the thought that the noble truth of suffering is empty or not empty, or practices with the mark that the noble truth of suffering is empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the thought that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty or not empty, or practices with the mark that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the noble truth of suffering as signless yet with signs, or if one practices the noble truth of suffering as having the characteristic of being signless yet with signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as signless yet with signs, or if one practices the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as having the characteristic of being signless yet with signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the Noble Truth of Suffering with the thought of wishing for something, or practices the Noble Truth of Suffering with the characteristic of wishing for something, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path with the thought of wishing for something, or practices the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path with the characteristic of wishing for something, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the noble truth of suffering as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the noble truth of suffering as being either detached or non-detached, or practices the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as being either detached or non-detached, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either detached or non-detached, or practices the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either detached or non-detached, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, if they practice ignorance, or practice the characteristics of ignorance, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, or aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—or if they practice the characteristics of volitional formations up to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
If one practices with regard to ignorance as permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the mark of ignorance as permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the marks of volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices with a fondness for ignorance and suffering, or if one practices with the characteristic of ignorance and suffering, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices with a fondness for volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, or if one practices with the characteristics of volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding ignorance (*avidyā*), or if one practices with the characteristic of self or non-self regarding ignorance, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with the notion of self or non-self regarding volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*), or if one practices with the characteristic of self or non-self regarding volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of ignorance, or practices with regard to the mark of purity or impurity of ignorance, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with regard to the purity or impurity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; or if one practices with regard to the mark of purity or impurity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to whether ignorance is empty or not empty, or if one practices with regard to the mark of ignorance being empty or not empty, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with regard to whether volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty or not empty, or if one practices with regard to the marks of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair being empty or not empty, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion that ignorance is signless yet possesses signs, or if one practices with the notion that the signlessness of ignorance possesses signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with the notion that volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are signless yet possess signs, or if one practices with the notion that the signlessness of these factors from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair possesses signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the wish for [the attainment of] ignorance while practicing without a wish, or if one practices with the characteristic of wishing for ignorance while practicing without a wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with the wish for [the attainment of] formative forces (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair while practicing without a wish, or if one practices with the characteristic of wishing for formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair while practicing without a wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the tranquility or non-tranquility of ignorance (*avidyā*), or practices with regard to the marks of the tranquility or non-tranquility of ignorance, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with regard to the tranquility or non-tranquility of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or if one practices with regard to the marks of the tranquility or non-tranquility of [these factors] from volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with the notion of detachment or non-detachment regarding ignorance (*avidyā*), or practices with the characteristic of detachment or non-detachment regarding ignorance, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices with the notion of detachment or non-detachment regarding formative forces (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*), or practices with the characteristic of detachment or non-detachment regarding formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they practice the four dhyānas or the characteristics of the four dhyānas, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

whether they practice the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions, or the characteristics of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices the four dhyānas as permanent or impermanent, or practices the four dhyānas with the marks of permanence or impermanence, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) as permanent or impermanent, or practices the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions with the marks of permanence or impermanence, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the pleasure and pain of the four dhyānas, or practices the characteristics of the pleasure and pain of the four dhyānas, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the pleasure and pain of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), or practices the characteristics of the pleasure and pain of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the four dhyānas with the notion of self or non-self, or if one practices the four dhyānas with the mark of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments with the notion of self or non-self, or if one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments with the mark of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the four dhyānas as pure or impure, or practices the signs of the four dhyānas as pure or impure, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) as pure or impure, or practices the signs of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as pure or impure, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the four dhyānas as being empty or non-empty, or practices the signs of the four dhyānas as being empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as being empty or non-empty, or practices the signs of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as being empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four dhyānas with signs or without signs, or practices the four dhyānas with the characteristic of being with signs or without signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments with signs or without signs, or practices the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments with the characteristic of being with signs or without signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four dhyānas with the wish for something while being without the wish [for liberation], or if one practices the four dhyānas with the characteristics of being without the wish while having the wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) with the wish for something while being without the wish, or if one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments with the characteristics of being without the wish while having the wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four dhyānas with regard to their being tranquil or non-tranquil, or if one practices the four dhyānas with regard to the marks of their being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) with regard to their being tranquil or non-tranquil, or if one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions with regard to the marks of their being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four dhyānas with or without detachment, or practices the characteristics of the four dhyānas with or without detachment, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) with or without detachment, or practices the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions with or without detachment, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they practice the four foundations of mindfulness or the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

whether they practice the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, or whether they practice the characteristics of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as permanent or impermanent, or if one practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the characteristic of permanence or impermanence, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as permanent or impermanent, or if one practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the characteristic of permanence or impermanence, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as being pleasant or painful, or practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the characteristic of being pleasant or painful, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being pleasant or painful, or practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the characteristic of being pleasant or painful, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the notion of self or non-self, or if one practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the mark of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path with the notion of self or non-self, or if one practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the mark of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as pure or impure, or practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the marks of purity or impurity, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as pure or impure, or practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the marks of purity or impurity, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as empty or non-empty, or practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the characteristics of being empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as empty or non-empty, or practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the characteristics of being empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as being signless yet possessing signs, or if one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as having the characteristic of being signless yet possessing signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path as being signless yet possessing signs, or if one practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as having the characteristic of being signless yet possessing signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness with a wish for something to be attained, or if one practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the characteristic of wishing for something to be attained, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path with a wish for something to be attained, or if one practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the characteristic of wishing for something to be attained, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices the four foundations of mindfulness with the characteristic of being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the characteristic of being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness with detachment or non-detachment, or practices the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path with detachment or non-detachment, or practices the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment regarding the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“Blessed One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they practice the perfection of generosity or the mark of the perfection of generosity, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, or the marks of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices the perfection of generosity as permanent or impermanent, or practices the perfection of generosity with the mark of permanence or impermanence, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as permanent or impermanent, or practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the mark of permanence or impermanence, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity while taking pleasure in suffering, or practices the perfection of generosity while taking pleasure in the characteristic of suffering, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while taking pleasure in suffering, or practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while taking pleasure in the characteristic of suffering, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity while conceiving of self or non-self, or if one practices the perfection of generosity while conceiving of the marks of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while conceiving of self or non-self, or if one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while conceiving of the marks of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity with notions of purity or impurity, or practices the perfection of generosity with the marks of purity or impurity, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with notions of purity or impurity, or practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the marks of purity or impurity, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity as empty or non-empty, or practices the perfection of generosity with the characteristic of being empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as empty or non-empty, or practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the characteristic of being empty or non-empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity with signs while it is signless, or practices the perfection of generosity with the characteristic of having signs while it is signless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with signs while they are signless, or practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the characteristic of having signs while they are signless, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity with a wish while being without a wish, or if one practices the perfection of generosity with the mark of being without a wish while having a wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with a wish while being without a wish, or if one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the mark of being without a wish while having a wish, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or if one practices the perfection of generosity with the characteristic of being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or if one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the characteristic of being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfection of generosity with detachment or non-detachment, or if one practices the perfection of generosity with the characteristic of detachment or non-detachment, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with detachment or non-detachment, or if one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the characteristic of detachment or non-detachment, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they practice the five eyes or the characteristics of the five eyes, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
whether they practice the six supernormal powers or the characteristics of the six supernormal powers, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices with regard to the five eyes as being permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the five eyes as being permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
