If one practices with regard to the six faculties (ṣaḍāyatana) as being permanent or impermanent, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the six faculties as being permanent or impermanent, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the pleasure or pain of the five eyes, or practices the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the five eyes, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if one practices the pleasure or pain of the six supernormal powers, or practices the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the six supernormal powers, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the five eyes with the thought of self or non-self, or if one practices the five eyes with the mark of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the six supernormal powers with the thought of self or non-self, or if one practices the six supernormal powers with the mark of self or non-self, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the purity or impurity of the five eyes, or practices the marks of purity or impurity of the five eyes, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one practices the purity or impurity of the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā), or practices the marks of purity or impurity of the six supernormal powers, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the five eyes as being empty or not empty, or practices with regard to the mark of the five eyes as being empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if one practices with regard to the six supernormal powers as being empty or not empty, or practices with regard to the mark of the six supernormal powers as being empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the five eyes as being signless yet having signs, or if one practices the five eyes as having the characteristic of being signless yet having signs, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the six superknowledges as being signless yet having signs, or if one practices the six superknowledges as having the characteristic of being signless yet having signs, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the five eyes with the thought of wishing or the mark of wishing, or if one practices the five eyes with the thought of wishing or the mark of wishing, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the six supernormal powers with the thought of wishing or the mark of wishing, or if one practices the six supernormal powers with the thought of wishing or the mark of wishing, this is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the five eyes as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the five eyes as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices with regard to the six supernormal powers as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices with regard to the characteristics of the six supernormal powers as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the five eyes with regard to remoteness or non-remoteness, or practices the characteristics of remoteness or non-remoteness regarding the five eyes, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the six supernormal powers with regard to remoteness or non-remoteness, or practices the characteristics of remoteness or non-remoteness regarding the six supernormal powers, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, whether they practice the ten powers of a buddha or the characteristics of the ten powers of a buddha, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects, or if they practice the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

If one practices the ten powers of a Buddha as permanent or impermanent, or practices the characteristics of permanence or impermanence regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as permanent or impermanent, or practices the characteristics of permanence or impermanence regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the pleasure or pain of the ten powers of a Buddha, or practices the characteristic of pleasure or pain of the ten powers of a Buddha, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices the pleasure or pain of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), or practices the characteristic of pleasure or pain of these from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the ten powers of a Buddha as "self" or "non-self," or if one practices the ten powers of a Buddha with the notion of "self" or "non-self" characteristics, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects as "self" or "non-self," or if one practices from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects with the notion of "self" or "non-self" characteristics, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one practices the purity or impurity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or practices the signs of purity or impurity of the ten powers of a Buddha, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the purity or impurity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects, or practices the signs of purity or impurity of these from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices whether the ten powers of a Buddha are empty or not empty, or practices the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha as being empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices whether the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are empty or not empty, or practices the characteristics of these—from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects—as being empty or not empty, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the ten powers of a Buddha as being signless yet having signs, or if one practices the ten powers of a Buddha as having the characteristic of being signless yet having signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects as being signless yet having signs, or if one practices from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects as having the characteristic of being signless yet having signs, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the ten powers of a Buddha with aspiration while they are without aspiration, or if one practices the ten powers of a Buddha with the mark of aspiration while they are without aspiration, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects with aspiration while they are without aspiration, or if one practices from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects with the mark of aspiration while they are without aspiration, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the ten powers of a Buddha as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as being tranquil or non-tranquil, or practices the characteristics of these qualities from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects as being tranquil or non-tranquil, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one practices the ten powers of a Buddha as being distant or not distant, or practices the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha as being distant or not distant, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as being distant or not distant, or practices the characteristics of these from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects as being distant or not distant, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“Bhagavān, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and should form this thought:
‘I am practicing the perfection of wisdom.’”
"Such a mode of practice characterized by apprehension is not the practice of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
If one forms the thought:
'I am a bodhisattva mahāsattva.'"
"This is a mode of practice characterized by apprehension; it is not the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If one forms this thought:
'That person practices the perfection of wisdom'..."
This is a mode of practice characterized by apprehension; it is not the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If one should form this thought:
"That is a bodhisattva mahāsattva," [it is likewise not the practice of the perfection of wisdom].
This is a mode of practice characterized by apprehension; it is not the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If one forms this thought:
"Practicing in such a manner is the practice of the perfection of wisdom," [one is still practicing with apprehension].
“World-Honored One, this is a mode of practice characterized by apprehension; it is not the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

World-Honored One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in such a manner, one should know that this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti said to Śāriputra:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and if they dwell upon a conceptual conviction regarding form, they then apply effort toward form;
if they dwell upon a conceptual conviction regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, they then apply effort toward feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and dwells upon the eye-base with perception and conviction, they apply effort toward the eye-base;
if they dwell upon the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base with perception and conviction, they apply effort toward the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base."
Due to such application, one is unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.
If one dwells upon a perception or conviction regarding the sphere of form, one applies effort toward the sphere of form;

if one dwells upon a perception or conviction regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, one applies effort toward those respective spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and if they dwell in conceptualization, conviction, and resolve regarding the eye constituent, the form constituent, the eye-consciousness constituent, as well as eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they are thereby applying effort toward the eye constituent up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition."
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

If one dwells upon, conceives of, and resolves upon the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, then one applies oneself to the ear element and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

If one dwells in perception, conception, and resolute conviction regarding the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and the nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, then one applies oneself to the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Due to such application of effort (*prayoga*), one is unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

If one dwells in perception, conceptualization, and resolute conviction (*adhimokṣa*) regarding the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, then one applies effort toward the tongue-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, aging, sickness, death, and future suffering.

If one dwells upon, conceives, and resolves upon the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, then one applies oneself to the body element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
Due to such application, one is unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

If one dwells in perception, conceptualization, and resolute conviction regarding the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mind-contact and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, then one applies oneself to the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and dwells upon the perception of and conviction in the earth element, they apply themselves to the earth element;
if they dwell upon the perception of and conviction in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, they apply themselves to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements."
Due to such application, one cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and dwells upon the perception and conviction of the noble truth of suffering, they then apply themselves to the noble truth of suffering;
if they dwell upon the perception and conviction of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they then apply themselves to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, if they dwell upon and resolve upon ignorance, they apply themselves to ignorance;

if they dwell upon and resolve upon volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, they apply themselves to those factors from volitional formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and dwells upon the conceptual resolution of the four dhyānas, they apply themselves to the four dhyānas;
if they dwell upon the conceptual resolution of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, they apply themselves to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and forms a conceptual attachment to dwelling in the four applications of mindfulness, they then apply themselves to the four applications of mindfulness;

if they form a conceptual attachment to dwelling in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, they then apply themselves to the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and dwells upon the conceptualization of and conviction in the perfection of generosity, they then apply themselves to the perfection of generosity;

if they dwell upon the conceptualization of and conviction in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they then apply themselves to ethical discipline up to and including the perfection of wisdom."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and dwells upon the conceptualization and conviction of the five eyes, they apply themselves to the five eyes;
if they dwell upon the conceptualization and conviction of the six supernormal powers, they apply themselves to the six supernormal powers."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and if they dwell in conceptualized conviction regarding the ten powers of a buddha, they apply themselves to the ten powers of a buddha;

if they dwell in conceptualized conviction regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, they apply themselves to the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects."
Due to such application, they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, and if they dwell upon the perception of and resolve toward śrāvakas and their dharmas, they will apply themselves to śrāvakas and their dharmas;

if they dwell upon the perception of and resolve toward pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, tathāgatas, and their dharmas, they will apply themselves to pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, tathāgatas, and their dharmas."
Due to their preparatory application (*prayoga*), they are unable to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, and future suffering. "Śāriputra!
Such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot even realize the stage of parinirvāṇa of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; it is impossible that they should attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in such a manner as this, you should know that he is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"How should one know that bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom with skillful means?"

Subhūti replied, “If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, does not course in form, nor courses in the marks of form— this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom;

if they do not course in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor course in the marks of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness— this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”
Not practicing the notion that form is permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the characteristic of form as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the notion that feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the characteristic of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or suffering of form, and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure or suffering of form—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or suffering of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure or suffering of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing [the notion of] "self" or "non-self" regarding form, not practicing the characteristics of "self" or "non-self" regarding form—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing "self" or "non-self" regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, not practicing the characteristics of "self" or "non-self" regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of form, and not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of form—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, and not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing that form is empty or not empty, and not practicing the mark of form being empty or not empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing that feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are empty or not empty, and not practicing the mark of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness being empty or not empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing that form is signless yet has signs, nor practicing that form is signless yet has the characteristic of having signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing that feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are signless yet have signs, nor practicing that feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are signless yet have the characteristic of having signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not to practice the wishless regarding form while harboring a wish, nor to practice the characteristics of the wishless regarding form while harboring a wish—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not to practice the wishless regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness while harboring a wish, nor to practice the characteristics of the wishless regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness while harboring a wish—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to whether form is tranquil or not tranquil, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of form being tranquil or not tranquil—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to whether feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness are tranquil or not tranquil, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness being tranquil or not tranquil—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the separation or non-separation of form, and not practicing the characteristic of the separation or non-separation of form—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the separation or non-separation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, and not practicing the characteristic of the separation or non-separation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Form is empty of the nature of form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Śāriputra!

This form is empty of form; this emptiness of form is not form. Form is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from form. Form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also thus.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not course in the sense-base of the eye, nor do they course in the characteristics of the sense-base of the eye; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not course in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, nor do they course in the characteristics of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

To not practice regarding the sense-base of the eye as permanent or impermanent, and not to practice regarding the characteristic of the sense-base of the eye as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice regarding the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as permanent or impermanent, and not to practice regarding the characteristics of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or pain of the sense-base of the eye, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of pleasure or pain in the sense-base of the eye, is the practice of the perfection of wisdom;

not practicing with regard to the pleasure or pain of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of pleasure or pain in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the sense bases of the eye as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with regard to the sense bases of the eye as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with regard to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the sense-base of the eye, and not practicing with regard to the mark of purity or impurity of the sense-base of the eye—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and not practicing with regard to the mark of purity or impurity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-base of the eye, and to not practice the mark of emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-base of the eye—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and to not practice the mark of emptiness or non-emptiness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the sense base of the eye as being signless or having signs, and not practicing with regard to the sense base of the eye as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being signless or having signs, and not practicing with regard to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not to practice with the wish for the absence of aspiration or the presence of aspiration regarding the sphere of the eye, nor to practice with the sign of the wish for the absence of aspiration or the presence of aspiration regarding the sphere of the eye—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not to practice with the wish for the absence of aspiration or the presence of aspiration regarding the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, nor to practice with the sign of the wish for the absence of aspiration or the presence of aspiration regarding the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the eye-faculty as being either tranquil or untranquil, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of the eye-faculty as being either tranquil or untranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-faculties as being either tranquil or untranquil, and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-faculties as being either tranquil or untranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the eye-base as being either distant or not distant, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of the eye-base as being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as being either distant or not distant, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base; the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are empty of the nature of the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base.

Śāriputra! This eye-base is empty of the eye-base; this emptiness of the eye-base is not the eye-base. The eye-base is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the eye-base. The eye-base is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the eye-base. It is the same for the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not course in the sense-base of form, nor do they course in the characteristics of the sense-base of form; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not course in the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, nor do they course in the characteristics of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to the impermanence or permanence of the sense-base of form, and not practicing with regard to the mark of impermanence or permanence in the sense-base of form—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the impermanence or permanence of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and not practicing with regard to the mark of impermanence or permanence in the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or pain of the sense-base of forms, not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the sense-base of forms—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or pain of the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena, not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to the sense bases of form as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with respect to the sense bases of form as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with respect to the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the sphere of form, and not practicing with regard to the signs of purity or impurity in the sphere of form—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and not practicing with regard to the signs of purity or impurity in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to whether the sphere of form is empty or not empty, and not practicing with respect to the mark of the sphere of form being empty or not empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty or not empty, and not practicing with respect to the marks of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena being empty or not empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with the notion that the sphere of form is signless or has signs, nor practicing with the notion that the sphere of form has the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with the notion that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are signless or have signs, nor practicing with the notion that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena have the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not to practice with the thought that the sphere of form is wishless yet possesses a wish, nor to practice with the mark that the sphere of form is wishless yet possesses a wish—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not to practice with the thought that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are wishless yet possess a wish, nor to practice with the mark that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are wishless yet possess a wish—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to whether the sphere of form is tranquil or not tranquil, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of the sphere of form being tranquil or not tranquil—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to whether the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena are tranquil or not tranquil, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena being tranquil or not tranquil—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the notion that the sphere of form is either distant or not distant, and to not practice the characteristic of the sphere of form being either distant or not distant—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

To not practice the notion that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are either distant or not distant, and to not practice the characteristic of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena being either distant or not distant—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this?

Śāriputra! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

Śāriputra! This sphere of form is empty of the sphere of form; this emptiness of the sphere of form is not the sphere of form. The sphere of form is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the sphere of form. The sphere of form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the sphere of form. It is the same for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Thirty-Nine (and Scroll Forty-Three) Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Scroll Forty-Three Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree by Command of the Emperor.
The Tenth Chapter on the Characteristics of the Practice of Prajñāpāramitā, Part Three. "Śāriputra!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not engage with the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, nor with eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. They do not engage with the characteristics of the eye-element, up to and including the characteristics of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom."

To not practice with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as being either permanent or impermanent; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the eye-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not engaging with the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, nor with eye-contact and the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—that arise conditioned by eye-contact; not engaging with the characteristics of the eye-element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Not practicing with regard to the eye constituent, the form constituent, the eye-consciousness constituent, and the eye-contact, nor the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as being self or non-self; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the eye constituent up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition as being self or non-self—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the contact of the eye, nor the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the contact of the eye, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the marks of emptiness or non-emptiness of the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the eye-contact, nor the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—whether they are signless or with signs—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of being signless or with signs in the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with the wish for or the wish against the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; and to not practice with the characteristics of wishing for or wishing against the eye-element, up to and including the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the eye-contact, nor the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as being either tranquil or non-tranquil; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition as being tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the distancing or non-distancing of the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; and to not practice the characteristic of distancing or non-distancing regarding the eye-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The eye-element is empty of the nature of the eye-element; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are empty of the nature of the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Śāriputra! This eye-element is not empty of the eye-element; the emptiness of the eye-element is not the eye-element. The eye-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the eye-element. The eye-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the eye-element. It is the same for the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not engage with the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, nor with ear-contact or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; they do not engage with the characteristics of the ear element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, nor the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition as being permanent or impermanent; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the ear element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, nor the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—arisen with ear-contact as their condition; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the ear element up to the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—arisen with ear-contact as their condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, nor the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as being "self" or "non-self"; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the ear element, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as being "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of purity or impurity of the ear element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the auditory contact, nor the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition—whether as signless or with signs—and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the signless or with signs of the ear-element up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, nor with regard to the various feelings produced conditioned by ear-contact—neither wishing for them nor not wishing for them—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of these elements from the ear-element up to the various feelings produced conditioned by ear-contact—neither wishing for them nor not wishing for them—is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, nor the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether they are peaceful or not peaceful—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the ear element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—whether they are peaceful or not peaceful—is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Not practicing with regard to the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, nor with regard to the various feelings produced conditioned by ear-contact—neither as being distant from them nor as not being distant from them—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of distance or non-distance from the ear-element up to the various feelings produced conditioned by ear-contact: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this?

Śāriputra! The ear element is empty of the nature of the ear element; the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition—these, from the sound element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, are empty of their own nature.

Śāriputra! This ear-element is empty of the ear-element; this emptiness of the ear-element is not the ear-element. The ear-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the ear-element. The ear-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the ear-element. It is the same for the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not engage with the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nor with nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; they do not engage with the characteristics of the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition—whether they are permanent or impermanent—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—that arise conditioned by nose-contact; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the nose element up to the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—that arise conditioned by nose-contact: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—conceiving them as self or non-self; not practicing with regard to the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition by way of their marks of self or non-self: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of purity or impurity of the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the marks of emptiness or non-emptiness of the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and the contact of the nose, nor the various feelings produced with that nose-contact as condition—whether they are signless or with signs—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the nose element up to the characteristics of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

To not practice with the wish or the absence of wish regarding the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; and to not practice with the sign of the wish or the absence of wish regarding the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the quietude or non-quietude of the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the marks of quietude or non-quietude of the nose element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings arising conditioned by nose-contact—neither as being detached nor as being non-detached; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment from the nose element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by nose-contact—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this?

Śāriputra! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. The odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—all these, from the odor element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are empty of their own nature.

Śāriputra! This nose-element is empty of the nose-element; this emptiness of the nose-element is not the nose-element. The nose-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the nose-element. The nose-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the nose-element. It is the same for the fragrance-element and even for all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not engage with the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, nor with tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; they do not engage with the characteristics of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether they are permanent or impermanent—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, nor the various feelings of pleasure and pain produced with tongue-contact as a condition; not practicing with respect to the characteristics of the tongue element up to the various feelings of pleasure and pain produced with tongue-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, nor the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—regarding them as self or non-self; not practicing with respect to the characteristics of the tongue-element, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as being self or non-self: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, nor the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the tongue element, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; and to not practice with regard to the marks of emptiness or non-emptiness of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and the contact of the tongue, nor the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether they are signless or with signs—and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the signlessness or the presence of signs in these factors from the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

To not practice with the wish for or the wish against the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; and to not practice with the characteristic of wishing for or wishing against the tongue-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

To not practice with regard to the quiescence or non-quiescence of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, nor the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the quiescence or non-quiescence of the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, nor the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—neither regarding them as distant nor non-distant; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of distance or non-distance from the tongue element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—from the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature.

Śāriputra! This tongue-element is empty of the tongue-element; this emptiness of the tongue-element is not the tongue-element. The tongue-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the tongue-element. The tongue-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the tongue-element. It is the same for the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not engage in the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, nor in body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; they do not engage in the characteristics of the body element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

To not engage with the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, as being either permanent or impermanent; and to not engage with the characteristics of the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition as being permanent or impermanent—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing with regard to the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—that arise conditioned by body-contact; and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the body-element up to the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—that arise conditioned by body-contact: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—whether as self or non-self; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—whether as self or non-self: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of purity or impurity of the body element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the body element, the touch element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the marks of emptiness or non-emptiness of the body element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—whether they are signless or with signs—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the body-element up to the characteristics of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, whether they are signless or with signs: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings arising conditioned by body-contact—whether they are wishless or with-wish—and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the body element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by body-contact—whether they are wishless or with-wish, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the stillness or non-stillness of the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings arising conditioned by body-contact; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of stillness or non-stillness of the body element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by body-contact—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—neither regarding them as distant nor non-distant; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of distance or non-distance from the body-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The body element is empty of the nature of the body element; the object-element of touch, the consciousness-element of the body, as well as body-contact and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition—these, from the object-element of touch up to all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition, are empty of their own nature.

Śāriputra! This body-element is empty of a body-element; this emptiness of the body-element is not the body-element. The body-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the body-element. The body-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the body-element. It is the same for the object-element of touch, and even for all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, does not course in the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, nor in mental contact or the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition; and if they do not course in the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

To not engage with the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, as being either permanent or impermanent; and to not engage with the characteristics of permanence or impermanence regarding the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the mind-element, the dharma-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, nor with regard to mental contact and the various feelings—whether pleasant or painful—that arise conditioned by mental contact; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings arising conditioned by mental contact—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, nor the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as being "self" or "non-self"; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition as being "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the mind-element, the dharma-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, nor with regard to mental contact and the pure or impure sensations produced with mental contact as a condition; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of purity or impurity of the mind-element up to the sensations produced with mental contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the emptiness or non-emptiness of the mind-element, the phenomena-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition; and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the mind-element, the dharma-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, nor with regard to mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition—whether they are signless or with signs—and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of being signless or with signs in the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the mind-element, the phenomena-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, nor with regard to mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—neither regarding them as wishless nor as having wishes—and to not practice with regard to the characteristics of the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition as being either wishless or having wishes: this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the stillness or non-stillness of the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; not practicing with regard to the characteristics of stillness or non-stillness of the mind-element up to the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To practice neither the distancing nor the non-distancing of the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition; and to practice neither the characteristic of distancing nor the characteristic of non-distancing regarding the mind-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this?

Śāriputra! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—up to the feeling produced with mental contact as a condition—are empty of the nature of those feelings.

Śāriputra! This mind-element (manodhātu) is empty of the mind-element; this emptiness of the mind-element is not the mind-element. The mind-element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the mind-element. The mind-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the mind-element. It is the same for the dharma-element (dharmadhātu) and even for all feelings produced with mind-contact as their condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not course in the earth element, nor do they course in the characteristics of the earth element; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not course in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor do they course in the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to the earth element as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of the earth element as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or pain of the earth element, and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the earth element—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the pleasure or pain of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to the earth element as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with respect to the earth element as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with respect to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as having the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the earth element, and not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the earth element—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, and not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
To not practice the emptiness or non-emptiness of the earth element, nor to practice the mark of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the earth element—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the emptiness or non-emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor to practice the mark of the emptiness or non-emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the earth element as being signless or having signs, nor practicing with regard to the earth element as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being signless or having signs, nor practicing with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the earth element as being wishless or having wishes, and not practicing with regard to the earth element as having the characteristics of being wishless or having wishes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being wishless or having wishes, and not practicing with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as having the characteristics of being wishless or having wishes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the earth element as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and to not practice with regard to the characteristic of the earth element as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice with regard to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and to not practice with regard to the characteristic of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the separation or non-separation of the earth element, and not practicing the characteristic of the separation or non-separation of the earth element—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the separation or non-separation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, and not practicing the characteristic of the separation or non-separation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this?

Śāriputra! The earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

Śāriputra! This earth element is empty of the earth element; this emptiness of the earth element is not the earth element. The earth element is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the earth element. The earth element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the earth element. It is the same for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
