“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not engage in the noble truth of suffering, nor do they engage in the characteristics of the noble truth of suffering; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not engage in the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, nor do they engage in the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing the noble truth of suffering as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the characteristic of permanence or impermanence in the noble truth of suffering—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the characteristic of permanence or impermanence in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truth of suffering as pleasure or suffering, and not practicing the noble truth of suffering as having the characteristic of pleasure or suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path as pleasure or suffering, and not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path as having the characteristic of pleasure or suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truth of suffering as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the noble truth of suffering with the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path with the characteristic of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the noble truth of suffering as pure or impure, and to not practice the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as pure or impure—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as pure or impure, and to not practice the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as pure or impure—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the noble truth of suffering as empty or non-empty, and to not practice the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as empty or non-empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as empty or non-empty, and to not practice the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as empty or non-empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truth of suffering as signless or with signs, and not practicing the noble truth of suffering as having the characteristic of being signless or having the characteristic of being with signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as signless or with signs, and not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as having the characteristic of being signless or having the characteristic of being with signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the noble truth of suffering as being wishless or having wishes, and to not practice the noble truth of suffering as having the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being wishless or having wishes, and to not practice the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as having the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truth of suffering as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truth of suffering as being either distant or not distant, and not practicing the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering as being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either distant or not distant, and not practicing the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) with skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.

Śāriputra! This noble truth of suffering is empty of the noble truth of suffering; this emptiness of the noble truth of suffering is not the noble truth of suffering. The noble truth of suffering is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the noble truth of suffering. The noble truth of suffering is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the noble truth of suffering. It is the same for the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not engage with ignorance, nor do they engage with the characteristics of ignorance; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not engage with volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; nor do they engage with the characteristics of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to ignorance as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing with regard to the mark of ignorance as permanent or impermanent—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing with regard to the marks of volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as permanent or impermanent—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the pleasure or suffering of ignorance, and not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure or suffering of ignorance—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as pleasure or suffering; and not practicing the characteristics of volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as pleasure or suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to ignorance as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with regard to the characteristic of ignorance as "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing with regard to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing with regard to the characteristics of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of ignorance, and not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of ignorance—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing with regard to the purity or impurity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and not practicing with regard to the marks of purity or impurity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the emptiness or non-emptiness of ignorance, and not practicing the characteristic of the emptiness or non-emptiness of ignorance—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the emptiness or non-emptiness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and not practicing the characteristic of the emptiness or non-emptiness of volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the signless as having signs regarding ignorance, and not practicing the sign of the signless as having signs regarding ignorance—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the signless as having signs regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and not practicing the sign of the signless as having signs regarding volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the absence of aspiration for ignorance while having aspiration, and to not practice the characteristic of the absence of aspiration for ignorance while having aspiration—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

To not practice the absence of aspiration for volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair while having aspiration, and to not practice the characteristic of the absence of aspiration for volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair while having aspiration—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice regarding ignorance as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and to not practice regarding the mark of ignorance as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and to not practice regarding the marks of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the separation from or non-separation from ignorance, and not practicing the characteristic of the separation from or non-separation from ignorance—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing the separation from or non-separation from volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), existence (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and not practicing the characteristic of the separation from or non-separation from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?
Śāriputra!

Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are likewise empty of the nature of old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Śāriputra! This ignorance is empty of ignorance; this emptiness of ignorance is not separate from ignorance. Ignorance does not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from ignorance. Ignorance is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself ignorance. It is the same for the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not practice the four dhyānas, nor do they practice the characteristics of the four dhyānas; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not practice the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions, nor do they practice the characteristics of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Not practicing the four dhyānas as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the four dhyānas with the marks of permanence or impermanence—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments with the marks of permanence or impermanence—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the pleasure or pain of the four dhyānas, and not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the four dhyānas—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the pleasure or pain of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the four dhyānas as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the four dhyānas with the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments with the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the purity or impurity of the four dhyānas, and not practicing the marks of purity or impurity of the four dhyānas—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the purity or impurity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and not practicing the marks of purity or impurity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing that the four dhyānas are empty or not empty, and not practicing the mark that the four dhyānas are empty or not empty—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty or not empty, and not practicing the mark that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty or not empty—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four dhyānas as being signless or having signs, and not practicing the four dhyānas as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as being signless or having signs, and not practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four dhyānas as being without aspiration or with aspiration, and not practicing the four dhyānas with the characteristics of being without aspiration or with aspiration—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions as being without aspiration or with aspiration, and not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions with the characteristics of being without aspiration or with aspiration—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four dhyānas as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the characteristic of the four dhyānas as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the characteristic of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four dhyānas as being either distant or not distant, and to not practice the characteristics of the four dhyānas as being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as being either distant or not distant, and to not practice the characteristics of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

Śāriputra! These four dhyānas are empty of the four dhyānas; this emptiness of the four dhyānas is not the four dhyānas. The four dhyānas are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the four dhyānas. The four dhyānas are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the four dhyānas. It is the same for the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not practice the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they practice the signs of the four foundations of mindfulness; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, nor do they practice the signs of the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

To not practice the four foundations of mindfulness as permanent or impermanent, and to not practice the four foundations of mindfulness with the marks of permanence or impermanence—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as permanent or impermanent, and to not practice the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path with the marks of permanence or impermanence—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four foundations of mindfulness as pleasure or suffering, and not practicing the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness as pleasure or suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as pleasure or suffering, and not practicing the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as pleasure or suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four foundations of mindfulness as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the four foundations of mindfulness with the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path with the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the purification or impurity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and not practicing the signs of purification or impurity of the four foundations of mindfulness, is the practice of the perfection of wisdom;

not practicing the purification or impurity of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path, and not practicing the signs of purification or impurity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the emptiness or non-emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness, and to not practice the characteristic of emptiness or non-emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the emptiness or non-emptiness of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, and to not practice the characteristic of emptiness or non-emptiness of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four foundations of mindfulness as being signless or having signs, and to not practice the four foundations of mindfulness as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being signless or having signs, and to not practice the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four foundations of mindfulness as being either wishless or with-wish, and not to practice the four foundations of mindfulness as having the characteristics of being either wishless or with-wish—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being either wishless or with-wish, and not to practice the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as having the characteristics of being either wishless or with-wish—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four foundations of mindfulness as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the aspect of the four foundations of mindfulness as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the aspect of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four foundations of mindfulness as being distant or not distant, and not practicing the characteristic of the four foundations of mindfulness as being distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being distant or not distant, and not practicing the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as being distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?
Śāriputra!

The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the nature of the four right efforts through to the eightfold noble path.

Śāriputra! These four foundations of mindfulness are not empty of the four foundations of mindfulness; the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the four foundations of mindfulness. It is the same for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Forty.
[Fascicle Forty-One] Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Part: Chapter Ten on the Characteristics of the Practice of Prajñāpāramitā, Section Four.

“Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, he does not practice the perfection of giving, nor does he practice the characteristic of the perfection of giving; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, and not practicing the signs of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the mark of permanence or impermanence in the perfection of generosity—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the mark of permanence or impermanence in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity with a delight in suffering, and not practicing the perfection of generosity with a perception of delight in suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with a delight in suffering, and not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with a perception of delight in suffering—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity with respect to "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the perfection of generosity with respect to the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with respect to "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with respect to the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the purity or impurity of the perfection of generosity, and not practicing the mark of purity or impurity of the perfection of generosity—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the purity or impurity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and not practicing the mark of purity or impurity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity as empty or not empty, and not practicing the perfection of generosity with the mark of being empty or not empty—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as empty or not empty, and not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with the mark of being empty or not empty—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity as being signless or having signs, and not practicing the perfection of generosity as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being signless or having signs, and not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as having the characteristic of being signless or having signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity with the thought of non-aspiration or aspiration, nor practicing the perfection of generosity with the mark of non-aspiration or aspiration—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with the thought of non-aspiration or aspiration, nor practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom with the mark of non-aspiration or aspiration—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfection of generosity as being tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the sign of the perfection of generosity as being tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as being tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the signs of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as being tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the perfection of generosity as being either distant or not distant, and to not practice the perfection of generosity with the characteristic of it being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being either distant or not distant, and to not practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with the characteristic of them being either distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means. Why is that?

Śāriputra! The perfection of generosity is empty of the nature of the perfection of generosity; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Śāriputra! This perfection of giving is not empty of the perfection of giving; the emptiness of the perfection of giving is not the perfection of giving. The perfection of giving is not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the perfection of giving. The perfection of giving is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the perfection of giving. It is the same for the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not practice the five eyes, nor do they practice the characteristics of the five eyes; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
They do not practice the six superknowledges, nor do they practice the characteristics of the six superknowledges; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing the five eyes as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the characteristic of the five eyes as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Not practicing the six sense bases as permanent or impermanent, and not practicing the characteristic of the six sense bases as permanent or impermanent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the pleasure or pain of the five eyes, and not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the five eyes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the pleasure or pain of the six supernormal powers, and not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure or pain of the six supernormal powers—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the five eyes as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the five eyes as having the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the six superknowledges as "self" or "non-self," and not practicing the six superknowledges as having the mark of "self" or "non-self"—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the purity or impurity of the five eyes, and not practicing the marks of purity or impurity of the five eyes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the purity or impurity of the six supernormal powers, and not practicing the marks of purity or impurity of the six supernormal powers—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing whether the five eyes are empty or not empty, and not practicing the mark of the five eyes being empty or not empty—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing whether the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are empty or not empty, and not practicing the mark of the six supernormal powers being empty or not empty—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the five eyes as being signless or with signs, and not practicing the five eyes as having the characteristic of being signless or with signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the six supernormal powers as being signless or with signs, and not practicing the six supernormal powers as having the characteristic of being signless or with signs—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the five eyes with the wish for non-wishing or the wish for wishing, and to not practice the five eyes with the characteristics of the wish for non-wishing or the wish for wishing—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the six supernormal powers with the wish for non-wishing or the wish for wishing, and to not practice the six supernormal powers with the characteristics of the wish for non-wishing or the wish for wishing—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the five eyes as being either quiescent or non-quiescent, and not practicing the characteristic of the five eyes as being either quiescent or non-quiescent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the six supernormal powers as being either quiescent or non-quiescent, and not practicing the characteristic of the six supernormal powers as being either quiescent or non-quiescent—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Not practicing the five eyes as being distant or not distant, and not practicing the characteristic of the five eyes as being distant or not distant—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the six supernormal powers as being distant or not distant, and not practicing the characteristic of the six supernormal powers as being distant or not distant—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is that?
Śāriputra! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes; the six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Śāriputra!

These five eyes are not the emptiness of the five eyes; the emptiness of the five eyes is not the five eyes. The five eyes do not depart from emptiness, and emptiness does not depart from the five eyes. The five eyes are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the five eyes. The six supernormal powers are also like this.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not course in the ten powers of a buddha, nor do they course in the characteristics of the ten powers of a buddha; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

They do not course in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects; nor do they course in the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

To not practice the ten powers of a buddha as permanent or impermanent, and not to practice the characteristics of the ten powers of a buddha as permanent or impermanent—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

To not practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects as permanent or impermanent, and not to practice the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects as permanent or impermanent—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the pleasure and pain of the ten powers of a Buddha, not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure and pain of the ten powers of a Buddha—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Not practicing the pleasure and pain of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects; not practicing the characteristics of the pleasure and pain of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the thought that the ten powers of a Buddha are self or non-self, and not practicing the mark of self or non-self regarding the ten powers of a Buddha—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the thought that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are self or non-self, and not practicing the mark of self or non-self regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the purity or impurity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and to not practice the marks of purity or impurity of the ten powers of a Buddha—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the purity or impurity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, and to not practice the marks of purity or impurity from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing that the ten powers of a Buddha are empty or not empty, and not practicing the characteristic of the ten powers of a Buddha being empty or not empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty or not empty, and not practicing the characteristic of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects being empty or not empty—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the ten powers of a buddha as being signless or having signs, and not practicing the ten powers of a buddha as being characterized by the sign of "signlessness" or "having signs"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects as being signless or having signs, and not practicing [them] as being characterized by the sign of "signlessness" or "having signs"—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the ten powers of a Buddha as being wishless or having wishes, and not practicing the ten powers of a Buddha with the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects as being wishless or having wishes, and not practicing from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects with the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the ten powers of a Buddha as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the characteristic of the ten powers of a Buddha as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects as being either tranquil or non-tranquil, and not practicing the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects as being either tranquil or non-tranquil—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the ten powers of a buddha as being distant or not distant, and not to practice the characteristics of the ten powers of a buddha as being distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

To not practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects as being distant or not distant, and not to practice the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects as being distant or not distant—this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means. Why is this?
Śāriputra!

The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects—from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects—are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects.

Śāriputra! These ten powers of a buddha are not the ten powers of a buddha because they are empty; the emptiness of the ten powers of a buddha is not the ten powers of a buddha. The ten powers of a buddha are not separate from emptiness, and emptiness is not separate from the ten powers of a buddha. The ten powers of a buddha are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the ten powers of a buddha. It is the same for the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience.
Śāriputra! In this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means is able to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at the existence of all phenomena, nor do they grasp at their non-existence; they do not grasp at both existence and non-existence, nor do they grasp at neither existence nor non-existence; and they do not even grasp at this non-grasping.”
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"By what causes and conditions does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), not grasp at anything whatsoever among all phenomena?"
Subhūti replied:
"Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena cannot be apprehended. Why is that?"
Because all phenomena have the absence of intrinsic nature as their very essence, for this reason,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they apprehend all phenomena as existent, or as non-existent, or as both existent and non-existent, or as neither existent nor non-existent, or if they apprehend by way of non-apprehension, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are entirely devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be grasped. Śāriputra!

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at practicing the perfection of wisdom, nor do they grasp at not practicing it, nor do they grasp at both practicing and not practicing it, nor do they grasp at neither practicing nor not practicing it; they do not even grasp at this non-grasping.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, does he not grasp at anything whatsoever within the perfection of wisdom?"
Subhūti replied:
"Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended. Why is that?"
Because the *prajñāpāramitā* has non-existence as its intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*),

for this reason, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, if they grasp at practicing it, or grasp at not practicing it, or grasp at both practicing and not practicing it, or grasp at neither practicing nor not practicing it, or grasp at not grasping— these are not practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? Because the perfection of wisdom has no intrinsic nature whatsoever and is therefore ungraspable. Śāriputra!

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they grasp at nothing and have no attachment toward any phenomena or the perfection of wisdom itself; this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s samādhi of non-grasping and non-attachment toward all phenomena.
This samādhi is subtle, sublime, vast, and immeasurable; it can gather boundless and unimpeded functions that are not shared with any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
“Śāriputra!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly dwells in and does not abandon this samādhi, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"Do these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening by dwelling constantly and never relinquishing only this one samādhi, or are there other samādhis as well, which they dwell in constantly and never relinquish, that also cause bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening?"
Subhūti replied, "It is not only by means of this one samādhi;
rather, there are further other samādhis in which bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly abide and do not abandon them, thereby swiftly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Śāriputra asked,
"Which ones are they?
Subhūti replied:
"Namely: the samādhi of the Heroic Gait, the samādhi of the Jewel Seal, the samādhi of the Lion’s Play,
the samādhi of the Wondrous Moon, the samādhi of the Lunar Banner Mark, the samādhi of the Ocean of All Dharmas,
the samādhi of Contemplating the Summit, the samādhi of the Certainty of the Dharma Realm, and the certainty..."
The dhvaja-lakṣaṇa samādhi, the vajra-upama samādhi, the dharma-mudrā-praveśa samādhi,
the samādhirāja samādhi, the su-pratiṣṭhita samādhi, the supratiṣṭhita-samādhirāja samādhi,
the raśmi-pramuñcana samādhi, the asaṃpramoṣa samādhi, and the raśmi-pramuñcanāsaṃpramoṣa [samādhi].
The samādhi of non-loss, the samādhi of the power of diligence, the samādhi of the power of adornment, the samādhi of equal surging forth,
the samādhi of entering the determination of all speech, the samādhi of entering the determination of all names and terms,
the samādhi of observing the directions, and the samādhi of the seal of dhāraṇī.
The samādhis of the ocean-seal of all phenomena, the royal seal, the all-pervading sky,
the vajra wheel, the purity of the three wheels,
immeasurable light, non-attachment and non-obstruction, and the severing of the turning of all phenomena; these and others...
The Samādhi of the Earth, the Samādhi of Discarding Jewels, the Samādhi of Universal Illumination, the Samādhi of the Unblinking Eye,
the Samādhi of Abiding in Signlessness, the Samādhi of Non-Conceptualization, the Samādhi of Subduing the Four Māras,
the Samādhi of the Stainless Lamp, the Samādhi of Boundless Light, and the Samādhi of Radiating Light.
the samādhi of equanimity, the samādhi of universal illumination, the samādhi of pure firmness, the samādhi of the lion’s spring,
the samādhi of the lion’s stretch, the samādhi of the lion’s yawn,
the samādhi of stainless light, the samādhi of sublime bliss, and the samādhi of the lightning lamp.
The Samādhi of the Inexhaustible, the Samādhi of the Mark of the Supreme Banner, the Samādhi of the Imperial Mark,
the Samādhi of Accordance with the Right Flow of Illumination, the Samādhi of Possessing Majestic Radiance, the Samādhi of Freedom from Exhaustion,
the Samādhi of Immovability, the Samādhi of Tranquility, and the Samādhi of Being Without Flaw.
The earth-samādhi, the sun-lamp samādhi, the moon-purity samādhi, the pure-eye samādhi, the pure-light samādhi,
the moon-lamp samādhi, the illumination-producing samādhi, the samādhi of what should and should not be done,

The samādhi of abiding mind, the samādhi of universal illumination, the samādhi of sublime establishment, the samādhi of jewel accumulation,
the samādhi of the seal of the sublime Dharma, the samādhi of the equality of the nature of all phenomena,
the samādhi of relinquishing attachment to dust, the samādhi of the perfection of the surge of Dharma, and the entry into the Dharma.
The Samādhi of the Summit, the Samādhi of the Jewel Nature, the Samādhi of Abandoning Strife, the Samādhi of Dispersion,
the Samādhi of Discerning the Phrases of the Dharma, the Samādhi of Certainty, the Samādhi of Stainless Conduct,
