with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the contact of the eye, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, the characteristics of wishlessness and the characteristic of having wishes are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the contact of the eye, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, the characteristics of tranquility and the characteristic of non-tranquility are unapprehendable.

With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, neither the characteristic of being detached nor the characteristic of not being detached can be apprehended.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing such profound teachings on the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being either permanent or impermanent;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being either pleasant or painful.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), one contemplates that within the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the contact of the ear, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the contact of the ear, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the contact of the ear, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, and finds no obtainable characteristic of signlessness or sign-possessing;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, and finds no obtainable characteristic of wishlessness or wishing;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, and finds no obtainable characteristic of tranquility or non-tranquility.

With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, finding no sign of either remoteness or non-remoteness.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing such a profound teaching on the perfection of wisdom.

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being either permanent or impermanent;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being either pleasant or painful."

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, finding no sign of self or non-self;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, finding no sign of purity or impurity;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, finding no sign of emptiness or non-emptiness.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and finds that the characteristics of signlessness and having signs are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and finds that the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and finds that the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable.

With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and finds that neither the characteristic of being detached nor the characteristic of not being detached can be apprehended.
Subhūti!

Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the constant and impermanent characteristics of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the pleasant and painful characteristics of the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are unapprehendable.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and finds no sign of either signlessness or having signs;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and finds no sign of either wishlessness or having wishes;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and finds no sign of either tranquility or non-tranquility.

With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, finding no such thing as the mark of being detached or not detached.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing such a profound exposition of the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the element of body, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being permanent or impermanent;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the element of body, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being pleasant or painful.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that within the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, the characteristics of self and non-self (*ātman-anātman-lakṣaṇa*) are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity (*śubha-aśubha-lakṣaṇa*) are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness (*śūnyatā-aśūnyatā-lakṣaṇa*) are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the body element, the touch element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, the characteristics of signlessness and sign-possessing are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the body element, the touch element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, the characteristics of wishlessness and wish-possessing are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the body element, the touch element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable.

With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the body-element, the tangibility-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and finds that their characteristics of being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the mental faculty element (*manodhātu*), the phenomena element (*dharmadhātu*), the mental consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and the contact of the mind (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*)—as well as the various feelings produced with that mental contact as a condition—are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the mental faculty element, the phenomena element, the mental consciousness element, and the contact of the mind—as well as the various feelings produced with that mental contact as a condition—are unapprehendable.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that within the mind-element (*manodhātu*), the phenomenon-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as condition, the characteristics of self and non-self (*ātma-anātma-lakṣaṇa*) are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the mind-element, the phenomenon-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings arising with mental contact as condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity (*śubha-aśubha-lakṣaṇa*) are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the mind-element, the phenomenon-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings arising with mental contact as condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness (*śūnyatā-aśūnyatā-lakṣaṇa*) are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the characteristics of signlessness and having signs are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the sphere of the mind, the sphere of phenomena, the sphere of mental consciousness, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, finding no obtainable characteristic of either separation or non-separation.
“Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the earth element are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the earth element are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unapprehendable.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the earth element the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; one contemplates that within the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.
