With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the earth element, the characteristics of being detached or not detached cannot be apprehended; one likewise contemplates that within the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, the characteristics of being detached or not detached cannot be apprehended.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing the teaching of such profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they perceive that the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended as having the characteristic of permanence or impermanence; they perceive that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended as having the characteristic of permanence or impermanence.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they perceive that the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended as having the characteristic of pleasure or pain; they perceive that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended as having the characteristic of pleasure or pain.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates the noble truth of suffering and finds that the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; one contemplates the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and finds that the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the noble truth of suffering and finds that the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; one contemplates the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and finds that the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the noble truth of suffering and finds that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; one contemplates the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and finds that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates the Noble Truth of Suffering as signless and yet possessing signs, such that no sign can be apprehended; one contemplates the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as signless and yet possessing signs, such that no sign can be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the Noble Truth of Suffering as wishless and yet possessing the characteristic of wishing, such that no characteristic of wishing can be apprehended; one contemplates the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as wishless and yet possessing the characteristic of wishing, such that no characteristic of wishing can be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the Noble Truth of Suffering as tranquil and yet not tranquil, such that no characteristic of tranquility or non-tranquility can be apprehended; one contemplates the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as tranquil and yet not tranquil, such that no characteristic of tranquility or non-tranquility can be apprehended.

With a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the noble truth of suffering as being neither characterized by detachment nor non-detachment, such that no such characteristic can be apprehended; one likewise contemplates the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being neither characterized by detachment nor non-detachment, such that no such characteristic can be apprehended.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in ignorance (*avidyā*) are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in formative forces (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in ignorance are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in formative forces, and so on, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are unapprehendable.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that the characteristics of self and non-self regarding ignorance are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of self and non-self regarding the formations, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of purity and impurity regarding ignorance are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of purity and impurity regarding the formations, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding ignorance are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the formations, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind that accords with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that ignorance is signless (*animitta*) and its having signs is unapprehendable; one contemplates that the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are signless and their having signs is unapprehendable.

By means of the mind that accords with the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that ignorance is wishless (*apraṇihita*) and its having the characteristic of wishing is unapprehendable; one contemplates that the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are wishless and their having the characteristic of wishing is unapprehendable.

By means of the mind that accords with the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that ignorance is tranquil (*śānta*) and its characteristic of being non-tranquil is unapprehendable; one contemplates that the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are tranquil and their characteristic of being non-tranquil is unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of the distancing or non-distancing of ignorance cannot be apprehended; one contemplates that the characteristics of the distancing or non-distancing of formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, cannot be apprehended.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are unapprehendable.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that within the four dhyānas, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; they observe that within the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that within the four dhyānas, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; they observe that within the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that within the four dhyānas, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; they observe that within the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that within the four dhyānas, neither signlessness nor the presence of signs can be apprehended; one contemplates that within the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, neither signlessness nor the presence of signs can be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the four dhyānas, neither wishlessness nor the presence of wishes can be apprehended; one contemplates that within the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, neither wishlessness nor the presence of wishes can be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the four dhyānas, neither tranquility nor the lack of tranquility can be apprehended; one contemplates that within the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, neither tranquility nor the lack of tranquility can be apprehended.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the characteristics of being detached or not detached from the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended; one observes that the characteristics of being detached or not detached from the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended.
"Subhūti!

Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Forty-two [and] Scroll Forty-three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The First Division, Chapter Eleven on Similes, Part Two: "Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four applications of mindfulness are unapprehendable; they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable."

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of self and non-self in the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of self and non-self in the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of purity and impurity in the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of purity and impurity in the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of signlessness and having signs regarding the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of signlessness and having signs regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes regarding the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility in the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one observes that the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility in the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the signs of detachment and non-detachment in the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable; one observes that the signs of detachment and non-detachment in the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable.
Subhūti!

Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they perceive that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence cannot be found within the gate of liberation of emptiness; they perceive that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence cannot be found within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they perceive that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering cannot be found within the gate of liberation of emptiness; they perceive that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering cannot be found within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the gate of liberation of emptiness and finds that the marks of self and non-self are unattainable; one contemplates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and finds that the marks of self and non-self are unattainable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the gate of liberation of emptiness and finds that the marks of purity and impurity are unattainable; one contemplates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and finds that the marks of purity and impurity are unattainable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the gate of liberation of emptiness and finds that the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness are unattainable; one contemplates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and finds that the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness are unattainable.

By means of the mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates the liberation door of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) and finds that the characteristics of being signless (*animitta*) or having signs (*sanimitta*) are unapprehendable; one contemplates the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) and finds that the characteristics of being signless or having signs are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the liberation door of emptiness and finds that the characteristics of being wishless or having wishes are unapprehendable; one contemplates the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness and finds that the characteristics of being wishless or having wishes are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates the liberation door of emptiness and finds that the characteristics of being tranquil (*śānta*) or not tranquil are unapprehendable; one contemplates the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness and finds that the characteristics of being tranquil or not tranquil are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one observes that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the characteristics of being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended; one observes that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the characteristics of being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they perceive that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the perfection of giving are unapprehendable; they perceive that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they perceive that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the perfection of giving are unapprehendable; they perceive that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one observes that the characteristics of self and non-self in the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) are unapprehendable; one observes that the characteristics of self and non-self in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the characteristics of purity and impurity in the perfection of generosity are unapprehendable; one observes that the characteristics of purity and impurity in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness in the perfection of generosity are unapprehendable; one observes that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the signless and the signful aspects of the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended; one contemplates that the signless and the signful aspects of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the wishless and the wishful aspects of the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended; one contemplates that the wishless and the wishful aspects of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one observes that the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility in the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) are unapprehendable; one observes that the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the signs of remoteness and non-remoteness in the perfection of generosity are unapprehendable; one observes that the signs of remoteness and non-remoteness in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing such a profound exposition of the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the five eyes cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of permanence or impermanence; they observe that the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of permanence or impermanence.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the five eyes cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of pleasure or suffering; they observe that the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of pleasure or suffering.”

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that the marks of self and non-self regarding the five eyes are unapprehendable, and contemplates that the marks of self and non-self regarding the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the marks of purity and impurity regarding the five eyes are unapprehendable, and contemplates that the marks of purity and impurity regarding the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable;

with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the five eyes are unapprehendable, and contemplates that the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that the five eyes have neither the mark of signlessness nor the mark of having signs, as these marks are unattainable; one contemplates that the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) have neither the mark of signlessness nor the mark of having signs, as these marks are unattainable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the five eyes have neither the mark of wishlessness nor the mark of wishing, as these marks are unattainable; one contemplates that the six supernormal powers have neither the mark of wishlessness nor the mark of wishing, as these marks are unattainable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the five eyes have neither the mark of tranquility nor the mark of non-tranquility, as these marks are unattainable; one contemplates that the six supernormal powers have neither the mark of tranquility nor the mark of non-tranquility, as these marks are unattainable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the five eyes cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being either detached or non-detached; one contemplates that the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended as having the characteristics of being either detached or non-detached.
Subhūti!

Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they do not apprehend the marks of permanence or impermanence in the ten powers of a buddha; they do not apprehend the marks of permanence or impermanence in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, the knowledge of all things, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, they do not apprehend the marks of pleasure or suffering in the ten powers of a buddha; they do not apprehend the marks of pleasure or suffering in the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects.”

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that within the ten powers of a Buddha, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; one contemplates that from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the ten powers of a Buddha, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; one contemplates that from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that within the ten powers of a Buddha, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; one contemplates that from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), one contemplates that the ten powers of a Buddha are signless and yet possess signs, such that no sign can be apprehended; one contemplates that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), are signless and yet possess signs, such that no sign can be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the ten powers of a Buddha are wishless and yet possess the characteristic of wishing, such that no characteristic of wishing can be apprehended; one contemplates that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects, are wishless and yet possess the characteristic of wishing, such that no characteristic of wishing can be apprehended.

With a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, one contemplates that the ten powers of a Buddha are tranquil and yet possess the characteristic of non-tranquility, such that no characteristic of non-tranquility can be apprehended; one contemplates that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects, are tranquil and yet possess the characteristic of non-tranquility, such that no characteristic of non-tranquility can be apprehended.

By means of the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, one observes that the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended as having either the characteristic of being distant or not distant; likewise, one observes that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects, cannot be apprehended as having either the characteristic of being distant or not distant.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, because they possess skillful means, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing such a profound teaching on the perfection of wisdom."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this contemplation, he further gives rise to this thought:

'I shall, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, for the sake of all sentient beings, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in all phenomena are unapprehendable; the characteristics of pleasure and suffering are unapprehendable; the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; the characteristics of signlessness and having signs are unapprehendable; the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes are unapprehendable; the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable; and the characteristics of detachment and non-detachment are unapprehendable.'"
"Subhūti! This is the perfection of generosity without attachment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom."

Thus, because this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses skillful means through this perfection of giving, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not, with the mind of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, perceive the characteristics of permanence or impermanence in all phenomena as being unobtainable; the characteristics of pleasure or suffering as unobtainable; the characteristics of self or selflessness as unobtainable; the characteristics of purity or impurity as unobtainable; the characteristics of emptiness or non-emptiness as unobtainable; the characteristics of signlessness or having signs as unobtainable; the characteristics of wishlessness or having wishes as unobtainable; the characteristics of tranquility or non-tranquility as unobtainable; and the characteristics of detachment or non-detachment as unobtainable—because they employ the means of non-apprehension.”
Subhūti! This is the perfection of pure ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom, which is characterized by non-attachment.

In this way, because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess skillful means through this perfection of ethical discipline, their minds are not startled, terrified, or frightened when they hear this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in all phenomena are unapprehendable; the characteristics of pleasure and suffering are unapprehendable; the characteristics of self and selflessness are unapprehendable; the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; the characteristics of signlessness and having signs are unapprehendable; the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes are unapprehendable; the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable; and the characteristics of detachment and non-detachment are unapprehendable. They are thus able to find patient acceptance and delight therein.”
Subhūti! This is the perfection of patience without attachment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom.

In this way, because this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses skillful means through this perfection of patience, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, they observe that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in all phenomena are unapprehendable; the characteristics of pleasure and suffering are unapprehendable; the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; the characteristics of signlessness and having signs are unapprehendable; the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes are unapprehendable; the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable; and the characteristics of detachment and non-detachment are unapprehendable. Although they employ this method of non-apprehension, they never abandon the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes.”
Subhūti! This is the perfection of diligence without attachment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom.

In this way, because of this perfection of diligence and their skillful means, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom, their minds are not startled, not terrified, and not afraid.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not, with the mind of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, perceive the signs of permanence or impermanence in all phenomena as being unobtainable; the signs of pleasure or suffering as unobtainable; the signs of self or non-self as unobtainable; the signs of purity or impurity as unobtainable; the signs of emptiness or non-emptiness as unobtainable; the signs of signlessness or having signs as unobtainable; the signs of wishlessness or having wishes as unobtainable; the signs of tranquility or non-tranquility as unobtainable; and the signs of detachment or non-detachment as unobtainable. Because they employ the means of non-apprehension, they do not give rise within that state to the mind of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, nor to any other unwholesome mind, thereby avoiding distraction.”
Subhūti! This is the perfection of meditative concentration without attachment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Thus, because this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses skillful means through this perfection of meditative concentration, upon hearing such an exposition of the profound perfection of wisdom, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate in this way:
‘It is not because form is empty that form is empty; rather, form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is form. It is the same for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.’”

It is not that the eye-base is empty because it is separate from emptiness; rather, the eye-base is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the eye-base. It is the same for the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

It is not that the sphere of form is empty because it is separate from emptiness; rather, the sphere of form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the sphere of form. It is the same for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

It is not because the eye-element is empty that the eye-element is empty; rather, the eye-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the eye-element. It is likewise for the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition.

It is not that the ear-element is empty because it is separate from emptiness; rather, the ear-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the ear-element. It is the same for the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

It is not because the nose-element is empty that the nose-element is empty; rather, the nose-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the nose-element. The same applies to the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, as well as nose-contact and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

It is not because the tongue-element is empty that the tongue-element is empty; rather, the tongue-element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the tongue-element. The same applies to the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, as well as tongue-contact and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

It is not because the body element is empty that the body element is empty; rather, the body element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the body element. It is the same for the touch element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

It is not that the mind-element is empty because of something external to it; rather, the mind-element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the mind-element. The same applies to the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.

The earth element is empty because it is not the earth element; the earth element is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the earth element. It is the same for the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

It is not because of emptiness that the noble truth of suffering is empty; rather, the noble truth of suffering is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the noble truth of suffering. The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise so.

It is not because of emptiness that ignorance is empty; rather, ignorance itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ignorance. The same applies to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Because the four dhyānas are not empty of themselves, the four dhyānas are empty; the four dhyānas are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the four dhyānas. The same applies to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are not [inherently] empty, the four foundations of mindfulness are empty; the four foundations of mindfulness are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the four foundations of mindfulness. The same applies to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

Because the gate of liberation through the emptiness of emptiness is empty, the gate of liberation through emptiness is itself empty; the gate of liberation through emptiness is identical to emptiness, and emptiness is identical to the gate of liberation through emptiness. It is the same for the gates of liberation through signlessness and wishlessness.

It is not because of emptiness that the perfection of generosity is empty; rather, the perfection of generosity is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the perfection of generosity. It is the same for the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
It is not because of emptiness that the five eyes are empty; rather, the five eyes are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the five eyes.

The same applies to the six supernormal powers. It is not because of emptiness that the ten powers of a Buddha are empty; rather, the ten powers of a Buddha are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself the ten powers of a Buddha. The same applies to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
"Subhūti! This is the non-attachment to the perfection of wisdom when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom."

In this way, because a bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses skillful means through this perfection of wisdom, upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are sustained by virtuous friends, such that upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"The virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in form are unapprehendable, and teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in form are unapprehendable, and teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable."

It is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self in form are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity in form are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness in form are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable.

He teaches that form is signless and that the sign of being signless is unapprehendable; he teaches that feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are signless and that the sign of being signless is unapprehendable.

He teaches that form is wishless and that the sign of wishing is unapprehendable; he teaches that feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are wishless and that the sign of wishing is unapprehendable.

He teaches that form is tranquil and that the sign of non-tranquility is unapprehendable; he teaches that feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are tranquil and that the sign of non-tranquility is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of form being detached or non-detached cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness being detached or non-detached cannot be apprehended; and one is exhorted to rely upon this Dharma to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, being sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the sense base of the eye are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are unapprehendable.

They teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the sense base of the eye are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are unapprehendable."

It is taught that in the sense-base of the eye, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the sense-base of the eye, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the sense-base of the eye, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the sense-base of the eye, there is no characteristic of signlessness and the characteristic of having signs cannot be apprehended; it is taught that in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, there is no characteristic of signlessness and the characteristic of having signs cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that in the sense-base of the eye, there is no characteristic of wishlessness and the characteristic of having wishes cannot be apprehended; it is taught that in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, there is no characteristic of wishlessness and the characteristic of having wishes cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that in the sense-base of the eye, there is no characteristic of tranquility and the characteristic of non-tranquility cannot be apprehended; it is taught that in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, there is no characteristic of tranquility and the characteristic of non-tranquility cannot be apprehended.

He teaches that the characteristics of being detached or non-detached regarding the sense base of the eye cannot be apprehended; he teaches that the characteristics of being detached or non-detached regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended; and he exhorts them to rely on this Dharma to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but solely for the realization of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The spiritual friends of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the sense base of form are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are unapprehendable.

They teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the sense base of form are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are unapprehendable."

It is taught that in the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the sphere of form, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the sphere of form, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is signless (*animitta*), yet its sign of being signless cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are signless, yet their signs of being signless cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that the sphere of form is wishless (*apraṇihita*), yet its sign of being wishless cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are wishless, yet their signs of being wishless cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that the sphere of form is quiescent (*śānta*), yet its sign of being quiescent or non-quiescent cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are quiescent, yet their signs of being quiescent or non-quiescent cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the sense-base of form are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are unapprehendable. Furthermore, one is exhorted to rely on these teachings to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, ensuring they are not dedicated toward the vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely directed toward the realization of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence of the eye-element are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering of the eye-element are unapprehendable; and they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the form-element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the eye-element, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the eye-element, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the eye-element is signless and with signs, yet the characteristic of being signless or with signs is unapprehendable; it is taught that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are signless and with signs, yet the characteristic of being signless or with signs is unapprehendable;

it is taught that the eye-element is wishless and with wishes, yet the characteristic of being wishless or with wishes is unapprehendable; it is taught that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are wishless and with wishes, yet the characteristic of being wishless or with wishes is unapprehendable;

it is taught that the eye-element is tranquil and not tranquil, yet the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil is unapprehendable; it is taught that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are tranquil and not tranquil, yet the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the form-element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are unapprehendable. Furthermore, one is exhorted to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*), not directing them toward the level of a Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such good friends, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are good friends to bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the ear-element are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain in the ear-element are unapprehendable; and they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain in the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the ear-element, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the ear-element, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the ear-element is signless, yet the characteristic of having signs is unapprehendable; it is taught that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are signless, yet the characteristic of having signs is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the ear-element is wishless, yet the characteristic of having wishes is unapprehendable; it is taught that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are wishless, yet the characteristic of having wishes is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the ear-element is tranquil, yet the characteristic of being non-tranquil is unapprehendable; it is taught that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are tranquil, yet the characteristic of being non-tranquil is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of the ear-element being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the characteristics of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended; and one is exhorted to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, by means of the non-apprehension [of objects], teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are unapprehendable.

They teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the nose-element are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the nose element, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the nose element, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the nose element is signless; yet the sign of being signless cannot be apprehended. It is taught that the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are signless;

yet the sign of being signless cannot be apprehended. It is taught that the nose element is wishless; yet the sign of being wishless cannot be apprehended. It is taught that the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are wishless;

yet the sign of being wishless cannot be apprehended. It is taught that the nose element is tranquil; yet the sign of being tranquil or not tranquil cannot be apprehended. It is taught that the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are tranquil; yet the sign of being tranquil or not tranquil cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are unapprehendable. Furthermore, one is exhorted to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the level of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the tongue-element are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain in the tongue-element are unapprehendable; and they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the tongue element, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the tongue element, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the tongue element, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is signless (*animitta*) and that the characteristic of being with signs (*sanimitta*) is unapprehendable; it is taught that the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) arising conditioned by tongue-contact are signless and that the characteristic of being with signs is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the tongue element is wishless (*apraṇihita*) and that the characteristic of being with wishes (*sapranihita*) is unapprehendable; it is taught that the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings arising conditioned by tongue-contact are wishless and that the characteristic of being with wishes is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the tongue element is quiescent (*śānta*) and that the characteristic of being non-quiescent (*aśānta*) is unapprehendable; it is taught that the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings arising conditioned by tongue-contact are quiescent and that the characteristic of being non-quiescent is unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of the tongue element being distant or not distant are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition being distant or not distant are unapprehendable. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is taught that the body-element is wishless (apraṇihita), yet the characteristic of being wishful is unapprehendable; it is taught that the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are wishless, yet the characteristic of being wishful is unapprehendable.
