It is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the body element are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are unapprehendable; and one is exhorted to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the level of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and is sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are good friends to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, by means of non-apprehension as their expedient, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and the mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*)—as well as the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising conditioned by that mental contact—are unapprehendable.

They teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain in the mind-element are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain in the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact—as well as the various feelings arising conditioned by that mental contact—are unapprehendable."

He teaches that within the mind-element (*manodhātu*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; he teaches that within the dharma-element, the consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

He teaches that within the mind-element, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; he teaches that within the dharma-element, the consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

He teaches that within the mind-element, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; he teaches that within the dharma-element, the consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

He teaches that the mind-element is signless and that the characteristic of being with signs is unapprehendable; he teaches that the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and all feelings produced with mental-contact as condition are signless and that the characteristic of being with signs is unapprehendable.

He teaches that the mind-element is wishless and that the characteristic of being with wishes is unapprehendable; he teaches that the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and all feelings produced with mental-contact as condition are wishless and that the characteristic of being with wishes is unapprehendable.

He teaches that the mind-element is tranquil and that the characteristic of being non-tranquil is unapprehendable; he teaches that the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and all feelings produced with mental-contact as condition are tranquil and that the characteristic of being non-tranquil is unapprehendable.

He explains that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are unapprehendable; he explains that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are unapprehendable. Furthermore, he exhorts them to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the level of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely for the realization of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, being sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the earth element are unapprehendable, and teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence in the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the earth element are unapprehendable, and teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering in the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the earth element, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the earth element, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the earth element, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the earth element is signless (*animitta*) and that its sign of being with signs (*sanimitta*) is unapprehendable; it is taught that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are signless and that their signs of being with signs are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the earth element is wishless (*apraṇihita*) and that its sign of being with wishes (*sapranihita*) is unapprehendable; it is taught that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are wishless and that their signs of being with wishes are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the earth element is tranquil (*śānta*) and that its sign of being non-tranquil (*aśānta*) is unapprehendable; it is taught that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are tranquil and that their signs of being non-tranquil are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of the earth element being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements being distant or not distant cannot be apprehended; and one is exhorted to diligently cultivate roots of goodness based on these dharmas, not directing them toward the level of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the marks of permanence and impermanence regarding the noble truth of suffering are unapprehendable; they teach that the marks of permanence and impermanence regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are unapprehendable.

They teach that the marks of pleasure and suffering regarding the noble truth of suffering are unapprehendable; they teach that the marks of pleasure and suffering regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are unapprehendable."

When one teaches the Noble Truth of Suffering, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; when one teaches the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

When one teaches the Noble Truth of Suffering, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; when one teaches the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

When one teaches the Noble Truth of Suffering, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; when one teaches the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that regarding the noble truth of suffering, the signless and the having-signs are both unapprehendable; it is taught that regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, the signless and the having-signs are both unapprehendable.

It is taught that regarding the noble truth of suffering, the wishless and the having-wishes are both unapprehendable; it is taught that regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, the wishless and the having-wishes are both unapprehendable.

It is taught that regarding the noble truth of suffering, the peaceful and the non-peaceful are both unapprehendable; it is taught that regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, the peaceful and the non-peaceful are both unapprehendable.

He teaches that the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended in terms of being distant or not distant; he teaches that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended in terms of being distant or not distant; and he exhorts them to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, ensuring they do not dedicate them toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only so that they may realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding ignorance are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding ignorance are unapprehendable; and they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding formative forces, up to and including old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are unapprehendable."

It is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self cannot be apprehended in ignorance; it is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self cannot be apprehended in anything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

It is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity cannot be apprehended in ignorance; it is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity cannot be apprehended in anything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

It is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness cannot be apprehended in ignorance; it is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness cannot be apprehended in anything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

It is taught that in ignorance there is no characteristic of signlessness, for the characteristic of having signs cannot be apprehended; it is taught that from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, there is no characteristic of signlessness, for the characteristic of having signs cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that in ignorance there is no characteristic of wishlessness, for the characteristic of having wishes cannot be apprehended; it is taught that from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, there is no characteristic of wishlessness, for the characteristic of having wishes cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that in ignorance there is no characteristic of tranquility or non-tranquility, for such characteristics cannot be apprehended; it is taught that from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, there is no characteristic of tranquility or non-tranquility, for such characteristics cannot be apprehended.

It is taught that the characteristics of being separated from or not separated from ignorance cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the characteristics of being separated from or not separated from anything from formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair cannot be apprehended; and one is exhorted to rely on this Dharma to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the levels of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but solely to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and is sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

The Eleventh Chapter on Similes, Part One, Section Three:

"Furthermore, Subhūti, those who are good friends to bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; and they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are unapprehendable."

It is taught that the characteristics of pleasure and pain cannot be apprehended in the four dhyānas; it is taught that the characteristics of pleasure and pain cannot be apprehended in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

It is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self cannot be apprehended in the four dhyānas; it is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self cannot be apprehended in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

It is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity cannot be apprehended in the four dhyānas; it is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity cannot be apprehended in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

It is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of signlessness and having signs regarding the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of signlessness and having signs regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes regarding the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; it is taught that the characteristics of wishlessness and having wishes regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are unapprehendable.

He teaches that the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility in the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; he teaches that the characteristics of tranquility and non-tranquility in the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are unapprehendable.

He teaches that the characteristics of seclusion and non-seclusion in the four dhyānas are unapprehendable; he teaches that the characteristics of seclusion and non-seclusion in the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are unapprehendable. Furthermore, he exhorts them to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but solely for the realization of the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such good friends, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four applications of mindfulness are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable.

They teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the four applications of mindfulness are unapprehendable, and they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the four foundations of mindfulness, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the four foundations of mindfulness, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the four foundations of mindfulness, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, the characteristics of being signless and having signs are unapprehendable; it is taught that regarding the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, the characteristics of being signless and having signs are unapprehendable.

It is taught that regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, the characteristics of being wishless and having wishes are unapprehendable; it is taught that regarding the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, the characteristics of being wishless and having wishes are unapprehendable.

It is taught that regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, the characteristics of being tranquil and not tranquil are unapprehendable; it is taught that regarding the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, the characteristics of being tranquil and not tranquil are unapprehendable.

He teaches that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended; he teaches that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, cannot be apprehended; and he exhorts them to diligently cultivate roots of goodness based on these dharmas, not directing them toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but solely so that they may realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the characteristics of permanence and impermanence are unapprehendable; they teach that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the characteristics of permanence and impermanence are unapprehendable.

They teach that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the characteristics of pleasure and suffering are unapprehendable; they teach that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the characteristics of pleasure and suffering are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the marks of self and non-self are unobtainable; it is taught that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the marks of self and non-self are unobtainable.

It is taught that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the marks of purity and impurity are unobtainable; it is taught that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the marks of purity and impurity are unobtainable.

It is taught that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness are unobtainable; it is taught that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness are unobtainable.

It is taught that within the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the signs of signlessness and the presence of signs are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*), the signs of signlessness and the presence of signs are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signs of wishlessness and the presence of wishes are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the signs of wishlessness and the presence of wishes are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable; it is taught that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility are unapprehendable.

He teaches that within the gate of liberation of emptiness, the characteristics of distancing or not distancing cannot be apprehended; he teaches that within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the characteristics of distancing or not distancing cannot be apprehended; and he exhorts them to diligently cultivate roots of goodness by relying on these dharmas, ensuring they do not dedicate them toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only toward the realization of the knowledge of all modes.
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended.

They teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended."

It is taught that in the perfection of generosity, the marks of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the marks of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the perfection of generosity, the marks of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the marks of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that in the perfection of generosity, the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the marks of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the signless and the sign-possessing aspects of the perfection of generosity are unapprehendable; it is taught that the signless and the sign-possessing aspects of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the wishless and the wish-possessing aspects of the perfection of generosity are unapprehendable; it is taught that the wishless and the wish-possessing aspects of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the tranquil and non-tranquil aspects of the perfection of generosity are unapprehendable; it is taught that the tranquil and non-tranquil aspects of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the characteristics of being distant from or not distant from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended; and one is exhorted to diligently cultivate roots of virtue based on these dharmas, not directing them toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but solely for the attainment of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).
“Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, being sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence of the five eyes are unapprehendable, and teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence of the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering of the five eyes are unapprehendable, and teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering of the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable."

It is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self regarding the five eyes are unattainable; it is taught that the characteristics of self and non-self regarding the six supernormal powers are unattainable.

It is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity regarding the five eyes are unattainable; it is taught that the characteristics of purity and impurity regarding the six supernormal powers are unattainable.

It is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the five eyes are unattainable; it is taught that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the six supernormal powers are unattainable.

It is taught that the five eyes, whether signless or with signs, have no signs that can be apprehended; it is taught that the six supernormal powers, whether signless or with signs, have no signs that can be apprehended.

It is taught that the five eyes, whether wishless or with wishes, have no characteristics of wishing that can be apprehended; it is taught that the six supernormal powers, whether wishless or with wishes, have no characteristics of wishing that can be apprehended.

It is taught that the five eyes, whether tranquil or untranquil, have no characteristics of tranquility that can be apprehended; it is taught that the six supernormal powers, whether tranquil or untranquil, have no characteristics of tranquility that can be apprehended.

He explains that the characteristics of being detached or non-detached regarding the five eyes are unapprehendable, and he explains that the characteristics of being detached or non-detached regarding the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable; furthermore, he exhorts them to rely on this Dharma to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but solely for the realization of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the ten powers of a buddha are unapprehendable; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are unapprehendable;

they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the ten powers of a buddha are unapprehendable, and they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects are unapprehendable."

It is taught that within the ten powers of a Buddha, the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable; it is taught that from the four fearlessnesses up to all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), the characteristics of self and non-self are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the ten powers of a Buddha, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable; it is taught that from the four fearlessnesses up to all-aspect omniscience, the characteristics of purity and impurity are unapprehendable.

It is taught that within the ten powers of a Buddha, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable; it is taught that from the four fearlessnesses up to all-aspect omniscience, the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the ten powers of a Buddha are signless and possess signs, yet their signs are unapprehendable; it is taught that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), are signless and possess signs, yet their signs are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the ten powers of a Buddha are wishless and possess wishes, yet their signs are unapprehendable; it is taught that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are wishless and possess wishes, yet their signs are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the ten powers of a Buddha are tranquil and non-tranquil, yet their signs are unapprehendable; it is taught that the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are tranquil and non-tranquil, yet their signs are unapprehendable.

It is taught that the characteristics of being detached or non-detached regarding the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended; it is taught that the characteristics of being detached or non-detached regarding the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), cannot be apprehended. Furthermore, one is exhorted to rely on this Dharma to diligently cultivate roots of goodness, not directing them toward the level of a Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha, but solely for the realization of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are good friends to bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension, teach that although the cultivation of the four dhyānas is unapprehendable and the cultivation of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is unapprehendable, they nevertheless exhort them to diligently cultivate roots of goodness based on these dharmas, ensuring they do not dedicate them toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only toward the realization of the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)."
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, those who are the virtuous friends of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that although the cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness is unapprehendable, and the cultivation of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is unapprehendable, they nevertheless encourage one to diligently cultivate roots of goodness based on these dharmas; they do not allow them to be dedicated toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only cause them to realize the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)."
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the good friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the practice of the liberation door of emptiness is unapprehendable and teach that the practice of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is unapprehendable; yet they encourage one to diligently cultivate roots of goodness based on these dharmas, not allowing them to be dedicated toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only leading one to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).”
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are good friends to bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the cultivation of the dharma of the perfection of giving is unapprehendable, and teach that the cultivation of the dharmas of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are unapprehendable; yet they encourage them to diligently cultivate roots of virtue based on these dharmas, not allowing them to dedicate [the merit] toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only causing them to realize the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)."
Subhūti! These are the virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such virtuous friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The virtuous friends of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that the cultivation of the five eyes is unapprehendable and teach that the cultivation of the six supernormal powers is unapprehendable; yet they encourage one to diligently cultivate roots of goodness based on these dharmas, not allowing them to be dedicated toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only for the realization of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)."
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by such good friends, their mind is not startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Those who are the virtuous friends of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who, employing the method of non-apprehension, teach that although the cultivation of the Buddha’s ten powers is unapprehendable, and they teach that the cultivation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is unapprehendable, yet they exhort [the bodhisattvas] to rely on these dharmas to diligently cultivate roots of virtue, not allowing them to dedicate [their merit] toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only causing them to realize the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatājñāna*)."
Subhūti! These are the good friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are sustained by such good friends, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

how is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, due to a lack of skillful means, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, practices the perfection of wisdom apart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and has something to grasp or relies upon in the practice of the perfection of wisdom, doing so by means of grasping;

or if they practice the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity apart from the mind directed toward omniscience, and have something to grasp or rely upon in the practice of meditative concentration up to the perfection of generosity, doing so by means of grasping.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, lacking skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they practice the four dhyānas apart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), yet they have apprehension and reliance regarding the cultivation of the four dhyānas, because they employ apprehension as their means.

They practice the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) apart from the mind directed toward omniscience, yet they have apprehension and reliance regarding the cultivation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, because they employ apprehension as their means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) while practicing the four applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), because they apprehend something in the practice of the four applications of mindfulness and rely upon it, taking that apprehension as their means.

They depart from the mind directed toward omniscience while practicing the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), the five faculties (*indriya*), the five powers (*bala*), the seven factors of awakening (*bodhyaṅga*), and the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), because they apprehend something in the practice of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path and rely upon it, taking that apprehension as their means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they practice the liberation door of emptiness apart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and if they have apprehension or reliance regarding the practice of the liberation door of emptiness, taking such apprehension as their means;

or if they practice the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness apart from the mind directed toward omniscience, and if they have apprehension or reliance regarding the practice of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, taking such apprehension as their means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, lacking skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the five eyes, having a sense of attainment and reliance regarding the cultivation of the five eyes, using such attainment as their means;

they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience while practicing the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā), having a sense of attainment and reliance regarding the cultivation of the six supernormal powers, using such attainment as their means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are apart from the mind directed toward omniscience (sarvajñatā) when practicing the ten powers of a buddha, because they have apprehension and reliance regarding the practice of the ten powers, taking apprehension as their means.

They are apart from the mind directed toward omniscience when practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), because they have apprehension and reliance regarding the practice of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, taking apprehension as their means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, lacking skillful means, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and afraid."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are separated from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and while contemplating the internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence regarding form, they apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of form and rely upon it, taking such apprehension as their means; [then they do not practice the perfection of wisdom]."

Having departed from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), they contemplate feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being empty internally, up to and including emptiness of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*); yet, in contemplating the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, they have something to grasp and something to rely upon, because they employ grasping at something to be attained as their means.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the eye-base as empty of internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, yet they have an apprehension and a reliance regarding that contemplation of the emptiness of the eye-base, because they employ apprehension as a means;

and if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as empty of internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, yet they have an apprehension and a reliance regarding that contemplation of the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, because they employ apprehension as a means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and contemplate the internal emptiness of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and if they have a grasping and a reliance upon that contemplation of the emptiness of the sphere of form, doing so by means of grasping;

or if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the internal emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature, and if they have a grasping and a reliance upon that contemplation of the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, doing so by means of grasping.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, lacking skillful means, upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and afraid."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind that corresponds to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) while contemplating the inner emptiness of the eye-element up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*). If, while contemplating the emptiness of the eye-element, they have apprehension or reliance upon it, doing so by means of apprehension;

or if they depart from the mind that corresponds to the knowledge of all modes while contemplating the emptiness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—from their inner emptiness up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature—and if, while contemplating the emptiness of the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they have apprehension or reliance upon them, doing so by means of apprehension.
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, lacking skillful means, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and contemplate the inner emptiness of the ear-element up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature and the absence of intrinsic nature, and if they have apprehension or reliance regarding that contemplation of the emptiness of the ear-element—using apprehension as their means;

or if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the emptiness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature and the absence of intrinsic nature, and if they have apprehension or reliance regarding that contemplation of the emptiness of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—using apprehension as their means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, lacking skillful means, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) by contemplating the internal emptiness of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature in its own-being (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*). Yet, they apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of the nose-element and rely upon it, using such apprehension as a means.

They depart from the mind directed toward omniscience by contemplating the internal emptiness of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature in its own-being. Yet, they apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of the odor-element, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, and rely upon it, using such apprehension as a means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should remain apart from a mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) while contemplating the tongue-element as empty internally, up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*). Yet, they might apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of the tongue-element and rely upon it, using such apprehension as a means.

They should remain apart from a mind directed toward omniscience while contemplating the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as empty internally, up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature. Yet, they might apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of the taste-element, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and rely upon it, using such apprehension as a means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and contemplate the internal emptiness of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature in its own-being (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and if they have apprehension regarding the contemplation of the emptiness of the body-element and rely upon it—taking such apprehension as their means;

or if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the internal emptiness of the element of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the element of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature in its own-being, and if they have apprehension regarding the contemplation of the emptiness of the element of tangibles, up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and rely upon it—taking such apprehension as their means.”
“Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind that corresponds to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā-jñāna*) and contemplate the internal emptiness of the mental faculty (*manas-dhātu*), up to its emptiness of the nature of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*); and if, in contemplating the emptiness of the mental faculty, they have apprehension and reliance, using such apprehension as a means;

or if they depart from the mind that corresponds to the knowledge of all modes and contemplate the emptiness of the realm of phenomena (*dharma-dhātu*), the mental-consciousness realm (*mano-vijñāna-dhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥ-saṃsparśa*), and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, up to their emptiness of the nature of non-existence of intrinsic nature; and if, in contemplating the emptiness of the realm of phenomena up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, they have apprehension and reliance, using such apprehension as a means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and contemplate the earth element as empty internally, up to its emptiness of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and if they perceive something to be attained or rely upon that contemplation of the emptiness of the earth element—doing so by means of such attainment;

or if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as empty internally, up to their emptiness of intrinsic nature, and if they perceive something to be attained or rely upon that contemplation of the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—doing so by means of such attainment.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (sarvajñatā) and contemplate the noble truth of suffering as inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; and if, in contemplating the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering, they have apprehension and reliance, using apprehension as their means;

or if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; and if, in contemplating the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they have apprehension and reliance, using apprehension as their means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and contemplate the inner emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) regarding ignorance (*avidyā*), and if they perceive something to be attained or rely upon the contemplation of the emptiness of ignorance because they employ attainment as a means;

or if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence regarding formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*), and if they perceive something to be attained or rely upon the contemplation of the emptiness of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair because they employ attainment as a means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, lacking skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they distance themselves from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā*) while contemplating the four dhyānas as empty—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—and if they apprehend and rely upon the emptiness of the four dhyānas, doing so by means of apprehension;

or if they distance themselves from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes while contemplating the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as empty—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—and if they apprehend and rely upon the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, doing so by means of apprehension.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they distance themselves from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) while contemplating the four applications of mindfulness—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and if, in contemplating the emptiness of the four applications of mindfulness, they have apprehension and reliance, taking such apprehension as their means;

or if they distance themselves from the mind directed toward omniscience while contemplating the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and if, in contemplating the emptiness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, they have apprehension and reliance, taking such apprehension as their means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (sarvajñajñāna) while contemplating the emptiness liberation gate—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and they find something to grasp and rely upon within the emptiness of the contemplation of the emptiness liberation gate, using such grasping as their means.

They depart from the mind directed toward omniscience while contemplating the signless and wishless liberation gates—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and they find something to grasp and rely upon within the emptiness of the contemplation of the signless and wishless liberation gates, using such grasping as their means.”
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and contemplate the emptiness of the perfection of giving—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and if they apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of the perfection of giving, relying upon it, because they employ apprehension as a means;

and if they depart from the mind directed toward omniscience and contemplate the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and if they apprehend something in their contemplation of the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, relying upon it, because they employ apprehension as a means.”
Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, lacking skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they are separated from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) while contemplating the five eyes as empty of internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and if they have apprehension and reliance regarding the emptiness of the five eyes, using such apprehension as their means;

or if they are separated from the mind directed toward omniscience while contemplating the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) as empty of internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and if they have apprehension and reliance regarding the emptiness of the six supernormal powers, using such apprehension as their means.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, if they lack skillful means, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they distance themselves from the mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) while contemplating the ten powers of a buddha—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence—and if they apprehend and rely upon the emptiness of the ten powers of a buddha, doing so by means of apprehension;”

Being apart from the mind of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they contemplate the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*). Yet, in their contemplation of the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, they have apprehension and reliance; they do so by means of apprehension as their method.
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, lacking skillful means, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and afraid."
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

how is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are influenced by evil friends such that, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind becomes startled, terrified, and afraid?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"The evil friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who teach them to become weary of and turn away from the dharmas associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or who teach them to become weary of and turn away from the dharmas associated with the perfections of meditative concentration (dhyāna), diligence (vīrya), patience (kṣānti), ethical discipline (śīla), and generosity (dāna), saying to them: 'Hey!'"
"Good sons!
You should not train yourselves in these dharmas associated with the six pāramitās. Why is that? Because..."

This teaching is certainly not spoken by the Tathāgata; it is a fabrication concocted by a poet. Therefore, you should not listen to it, nor should you accept it, nor recite it, nor contemplate it, nor investigate it, nor explain or reveal it to others.
"Subhūti! These are the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, is influenced by such evil friends, their mind will experience alarm, fear, and terror upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The evil friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are those who do not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra; that is to say, there is an evil Māra who assumes the form of a Buddha and comes to instruct the bodhisattva-mahāsattva to become weary of and detached from the six pāramitās, saying:
'Good son!'"
"What use have you now for practicing this perfection of wisdom?
What use have you now for practicing these perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity?"
"Subhūti! If one does not explain such matters as these to bring about awakening, this is an evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), is influenced by such an evil friend, their mind will experience alarm, fear, and terror upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

As for the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, they are those who do not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra—namely, when an evil Māra assumes the form of a Buddha and comes to the bodhisattva mahāsattva to preach the teachings associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, such as the sūtras up to the upadeśas, analyzing and revealing them while exhorting [the bodhisattva] to practice and study them."
"Subhūti!
If one does not explain such matters as these to bring about awakening, this is an evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), is influenced by such an evil friend, their mind will be startled, terrified, and frightened upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom explained."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, as for the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva:
they do not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra; that is to say, an evil Māra assumes the form of a Buddha, comes to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva is, and says:
'Good son!'"
"You lack the lineage of a bodhisattva and lack the genuine mind of enlightenment; you cannot realize the stage of non-retrogression, nor can you realize unsurpassed enlightenment."
"Subhūti! If one does not explain such matters as these to cause awakening, this is an evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), is taken hold of by such an evil friend, then upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, as for the evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva:
it is one who does not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra; that is, an evil Māra assumes the form of a Buddha, comes to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva is, and says:
'O son of good family!'"
Form is empty, without self or what belongs to a self; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty, without self or what belongs to a self.
The eye-base is empty, without self or what belongs to a self; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty, without self or what belongs to a self.
The form-base is empty, without self or what belongs to a self; the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases are empty, without self or what belongs to a self.

The eye-element is empty of self and what belongs to self; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are empty of self and what belongs to self.

The ear-element is empty of self and what belongs to self; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are empty of self and what belongs to self.

The nose-element is empty of self and what belongs to self; the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are empty of self and what belongs to self.

The tongue element is empty, devoid of self and what belongs to self; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are empty, devoid of self and what belongs to self.

The body element is empty, devoid of self and what belongs to self; the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are empty, devoid of self and what belongs to self.

The mind element is empty, devoid of self and what belongs to self; the mental-phenomena element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, and all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are empty, devoid of self and what belongs to self.
The earth element is empty of self and what belongs to self; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of self and what belongs to self.
The noble truth of suffering is empty of self and what belongs to self; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of self and what belongs to self.

Ignorance is empty of self and what belongs to self; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of self and what belongs to self.
The four dhyānas are empty of self and what belongs to self; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty of self and what belongs to self.

The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of self and what belongs to self; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are empty of self and what belongs to self.
The gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of self and what belongs to self; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of self and what belongs to self.

The perfection of generosity is empty of self and what belongs to self; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of self and what belongs to self.
The five eyes are empty of self and what belongs to self; the six superknowledges are empty of self and what belongs to self.

The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of self and what belongs to self; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of self and what belongs to self.
"Behold!
Son of good family!
All phenomena are empty, devoid of self and what belongs to a self; who then is able to cultivate the six pāramitās?"
"Who, moreover, could realize unsurpassed bodhi?
Even if one were to realize bodhi, what would it be used for?
"Subhūti! [the Buddha said.]
If one does not explain such matters as these to bring about awakening, this person is an evil friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), is influenced by such an evil friend, their mind will experience alarm, fear, and terror upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

As for the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, they are those who do not explain the deeds and faults of Māra; that is to say, there is an evil Māra who assumes the form of a pratyekabuddha and comes to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva is, saying:
'Good son!'"
"The ten directions are all empty; the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, and the assembly of śrāvakas do not exist at all. Subhūti!
If one does not explain such matters to bring about awakening, this is an evil friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, is influenced by such evil friends, their mind will experience alarm, fear, and terror upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, as for the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva:

they do not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra; that is to say, an evil Māra takes the form of a śrāvaka, comes to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva is, disparages the mental engagement with the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) so as to cause deep revulsion toward it, and praises the mental engagement with the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha vehicles so as to cause extreme attachment to them."
"Subhūti!
If one does not explain such matters as these to bring about awakening, this is an evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, is taken under the influence of such an evil friend, their mind will experience alarm, fear, and terror upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom explained."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are those who do not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra; rather, there are certain evil Māras who assume the forms of preceptors or teachers and come to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells, instructing him to become weary of and abandon the sublime practices of a bodhisattva—namely, the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, and the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom—and further instructing him to become weary of and abandon all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), namely, the five eyes, the six superknowledges, the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), teaching him instead to practice only the three doors of liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness."

"By studying this Dharma, you shall swiftly realize the fruit of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha, which is ultimate peace and happiness; why then do you toil so hard to seek the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
"Subhūti! If one does not explain such matters as these to bring about awakening, this is a bad friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), is influenced by such a bad friend, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Forty-four [and] Scroll Forty-five.
