Chapter Eleven: The Parable, Part Four "Furthermore, Subhūti, as for the evil friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, they are those who do not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra.
That is to say, there may be an evil Māra who assumes the form of a father or a mother and comes to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva is, saying: "
"Son! Son!

You should diligently strive to realize the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; this will suffice for you to forever leave behind the great suffering of birth and death and swiftly realize the ultimate peace and bliss of nirvana. Why go so far as to seek unsurpassed bodhi?"

Those who seek Bodhi must pass through immeasurable and innumerable great kalpas, circulating through birth and death to teach and transform sentient beings; they sacrifice their bodies and lives, severing limbs and joints—all this is but toil and hardship for themselves alone, so who shall bear your kindness?
"Whether the sought-after bodhi is attained or not. Subhūti!
If one does not cause [a bodhisattva] to awaken by explaining such matters as these, this is an evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, is influenced by such evil friends, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, as for the evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva:

it is one who does not explain the deeds of Māra or the faults of Māra—namely, when an evil Māra, assuming the form of a bhikṣu or other such appearance, comes to where the bodhisattva mahāsattva is and, employing the means of 'apprehending something,' says that the characteristics of permanence or impermanence of form can be apprehended; or that the characteristics of permanence or impermanence of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness can be apprehended;

or, employing the means of 'apprehending something,' says that the characteristics of pleasure or suffering of form can be apprehended; or that the characteristics of pleasure or suffering of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness can be apprehended."

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in form; they teach that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the characteristics of purity and impurity can be apprehended in form; they teach that the characteristics of purity and impurity can be apprehended in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness can be apprehended in form; they teach that the characteristics of emptiness and non-emptiness can be apprehended in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Using the attainment of something as a means, they teach that form is signless yet possesses signs that can be apprehended; they teach that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are signless yet possess signs that can be apprehended.

Using the attainment of something as a means, they teach that form is wishless yet possesses the sign of wishing that can be apprehended; they teach that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are wishless yet possess the sign of wishing that can be apprehended.

Using the attainment of something as a means, they teach that form is tranquil yet possesses the sign of non-tranquility that can be apprehended; they teach that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are tranquil yet possess the sign of non-tranquility that can be apprehended.

Taking attainment as a means, they teach that the characteristics of form being detached or non-detached can be apprehended; they teach that the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness being detached or non-detached can be apprehended.

"By means of the expedient of apprehending something as real, they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the sense-base of the eye; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something as real, they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering can be apprehended in the sense-base of the eye; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering can be apprehended in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something as real, they teach that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the sense-base of the eye; they teach that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind."

Using the attainment of something as a means, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of purity and impurity in the sense-base of the eye, and speak of the obtainability of the signs of purity and impurity in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;

using the attainment of something as a means, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness in the sense-base of the eye, and speak of the obtainability of the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;

using the attainment of something as a means, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of signlessness and having signs in the sense-base of the eye, and speak of the obtainability of the signs of signlessness and having signs in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

Using the apprehension of something as a means, they teach that the characteristic of wishing or not wishing can be apprehended in the sense-base of the eye; they teach that the characteristic of wishing or not wishing can be apprehended in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

Using the apprehension of something as a means, they teach that the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil can be apprehended in the sense-base of the eye; they teach that the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil can be apprehended in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

Using the apprehension of something as a means, they teach that the characteristic of being secluded or not secluded can be apprehended in the sense-base of the eye; they teach that the characteristic of being secluded or not secluded can be apprehended in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

"By means of the expedient of apprehending something, they say that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the sphere of form; they say that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something, they say that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering can be apprehended in the sphere of form; they say that the characteristics of pleasure and suffering can be apprehended in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something, they say that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the sphere of form; they say that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects."

Using the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the signs of purity and impurity can be apprehended in the sense-field of form; they teach that the signs of purity and impurity can be apprehended in the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

Using the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness can be apprehended in the sense-field of form; they teach that the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness can be apprehended in the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

Using the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the signs of signlessness and having signs can be apprehended in the sense-field of form; they teach that the signs of signlessness and having signs can be apprehended in the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

Using the apprehension of something to be attained as a means, they teach that the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) has the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes to be attained; they teach that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) have the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes to be attained.

Using the apprehension of something to be attained as a means, they teach that the sphere of form has the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil to be attained; they teach that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena have the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil to be attained.

Using the apprehension of something to be attained as a means, they teach that the sphere of form has the characteristic of being secluded or not secluded to be attained; they teach that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena have the characteristic of being secluded or not secluded to be attained.

"By means of the expedient of apprehending something as real, they say that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the eye-element; they say that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something as real, they say that the characteristics of pleasure and pain can be apprehended in the eye-element; they say that the characteristics of pleasure and pain can be apprehended in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something as real, they say that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the eye-element; they say that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition."

Using the approach of apprehending something as existent, they teach that the signs of purity and impurity in the eye-element can be apprehended; they teach that the signs of purity and impurity in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition can be apprehended.

Using the approach of apprehending something as existent, they teach that the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness in the eye-element can be apprehended; they teach that the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition can be apprehended.

Using the approach of apprehending something as existent, they teach that the signs of signlessness and having signs in the eye-element can be apprehended; they teach that the signs of signlessness and having signs in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition can be apprehended.

Using the approach of apprehending something as a means, they speak of the eye-element as having the characteristic of being either wishless or possessing wishes; they speak of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as having the characteristic of being either wishless or possessing wishes.

Using the approach of apprehending something as a means, they speak of the eye-element as having the characteristic of being either tranquil or not tranquil; they speak of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as having the characteristic of being either tranquil or not tranquil.

Using the approach of apprehending something as a means, they speak of the eye-element as having the characteristic of being either detached or not detached; they speak of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as having the characteristic of being either detached or not detached.

"By means of the expedient of apprehending something, one speaks of the ear-element as having the characteristics of permanence or impermanence that can be apprehended; one speaks of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as conditions as having the characteristics of permanence or impermanence that can be apprehended.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something, one speaks of the ear-element as having the characteristics of pleasure or pain that can be apprehended; one speaks of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as conditions as having the characteristics of pleasure or pain that can be apprehended.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something, one speaks of the ear-element as having the characteristics of self or non-self that can be apprehended; one speaks of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as conditions as having the characteristics of self or non-self that can be apprehended."

Using the method of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the signs of purity and impurity of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) are obtainable; they teach that the signs of purity and impurity of the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), and the sensations produced with ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) as a condition are obtainable.

Using the method of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness of the ear-element are obtainable; they teach that the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are obtainable.

Using the method of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the signs of signlessness and having signs of the ear-element are obtainable; they teach that the signs of signlessness and having signs of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are obtainable.

Using the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the ear-element has the characteristic of being either wishless or having wishes, and they teach that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being either wishless or having wishes;

using the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the ear-element has the characteristic of being either tranquil or not tranquil, and they teach that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being either tranquil or not tranquil;

using the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the ear-element has the characteristic of being either detached or not detached, and they teach that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being either detached or not detached.

"By means of the method of apprehension, they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the nose-element; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

By means of the method of apprehension, they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain can be apprehended in the nose-element; they teach that the characteristics of pleasure and pain can be apprehended in the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

By means of the method of apprehension, they teach that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the nose-element; they teach that the characteristics of self and non-self can be apprehended in the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition."

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they say that the pure and impure characteristics of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) are obtainable; they say that the pure and impure characteristics of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are obtainable.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they say that the empty and non-empty characteristics of the nose-element are obtainable; they say that the empty and non-empty characteristics of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are obtainable.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they say that the characteristic of signlessness and the characteristic of having signs of the nose-element are obtainable; they say that the characteristic of signlessness and the characteristic of having signs of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are obtainable.

Using the attainment of something as a means, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of wishlessness and wishing within the nose-element; they speak of the obtainability of the signs of wishlessness and wishing within the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Using the attainment of something as a means, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility within the nose-element; they speak of the obtainability of the signs of tranquility and non-tranquility within the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Using the attainment of something as a means, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of detachment and non-detachment within the nose-element; they speak of the obtainability of the signs of detachment and non-detachment within the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

"By means of the expedient of apprehending something, they say that the characteristics of permanence or impermanence can be apprehended in the tongue-element; they say that the characteristics of permanence or impermanence can be apprehended in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something, they say that the characteristics of pleasure or pain can be apprehended in the tongue-element; they say that the characteristics of pleasure or pain can be apprehended in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

By means of the expedient of apprehending something, they say that the characteristics of self or non-self can be apprehended in the tongue-element; they say that the characteristics of self or non-self can be apprehended in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition."

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of purity and impurity in the tongue-element; they speak of the obtainability of the signs of purity and impurity in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness in the tongue-element; they speak of the obtainability of the signs of emptiness and non-emptiness in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they speak of the obtainability of the signs of signlessness and having signs in the tongue-element; they speak of the obtainability of the signs of signlessness and having signs in the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the tongue-element has the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes, and that the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being wishless or having wishes;

using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the tongue-element has the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil, and that the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being tranquil or not tranquil;

using the approach of apprehending something as an object, they teach that the tongue-element has the characteristic of being detached or not detached, and that the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being detached or not detached.

"By means of the approach of apprehending something as real, they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the body-element; they teach that the characteristics of permanence and impermanence can be apprehended in the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), is influenced by such an evil friend, their mind will be startled, terrified, and afraid upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom explained."
Therefore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should swiftly abandon all evil friends.
Chapter Twelve: The Chapter on Bodhisattvas, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"What is the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva'?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"The meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is the absence of any meaning."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Because awakening is non-arising and sentient beings do not exist, the meaning of "non-phrase" is the meaning of "bodhisattva."
"Subhūti!
Just as the referent of the term 'bird's track in the sky' does not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."
"Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term 'illusory phenomenon' does not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."
"Subhūti!

Just as the referent of the term 'dream,' the referent of the term 'mirage,' the referent of the term 'reflection,' the referent of the term 'flower in the sky,' the referent of the term 'image,' the referent of the term 'echo,' the referent of the term 'city of Gandharvas,' and the referent of the term 'magical creation' do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."
"Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term 'suchness' does not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term "dharma-realm," the referent of the term "dharma-nature," the referent of the term "dharma-abiding," the referent of the term "dharma-stability," the referent of the term "non-falsity," the referent of the term "non-alteration," the referent of the term "nature free from birth," the referent of the term "equality," and the referent of the term "reality-limit" do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as the referent of the term 'form' for a phantom person does not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the terms for the illusory person’s feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘eye-base’ (cakṣur-āyatana) for a phantom person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind of an illusory person are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘form’ is non-existent and unapprehendable for an illusory person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

Subhūti! Just as the referents of the terms for the bases of illusory persons—sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referents of the term "bodhisattva" are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘eye-sphere’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended in a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘ear-element’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended in an illusory person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the realm of sounds, the realm of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition—belonging to a phantom person—is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘nose-element’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended in a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the realm of fragrance, the realm of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable for a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘tongue-element’ for an illusory person does not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘body-element’ for an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘mental faculty’ (manodhātu) for a phantom person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the realm of illusion, the realm of mental consciousness, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘earth element’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended in a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the terms for the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘the noble truth of suffering’ for an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the terms for the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and path of a phantom being is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘illusionist’ is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the terms for a magical illusion, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the four dhyānas of an illusory person is non-existent and unobtainable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the terms for the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions of an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the observation that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable is likewise.”

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘four applications of mindfulness’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended in a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-existent and unapprehendable for an illusory person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term 'liberation door' for an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the phrases and meanings of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—belonging to a phantom person are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of 'bodhisattva' are non-existent and unapprehendable."

The Second Part of the Twelfth Chapter on the Bodhisattva: "Subhūti,

just as the meaning of the term 'perfection of giving' for an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of an illusory person are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘five eyes’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended in a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the terms for the six supernormal powers of an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the ten powers of a Buddha is non-existent and unobtainable for a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the referents of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they observe that the referent of 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the term 'illusory person' practicing the emptiness of the internal is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the observation that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable is likewise."
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the terms for the emptiness of external objects, internal-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—all of which are non-existent and unapprehendable—so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the referential meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘four dhyānas’ is non-existent and unapprehendable for an illusory person who practices them, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning and referent of a phantom person practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning and referent of 'bodhisattva' are non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term 'four applications of mindfulness' is non-existent and unapprehendable for an illusory person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the terms for the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path practiced by an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘phantom person’ practicing the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the observation that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable is likewise.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the terms for the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—as practiced by a phantom person, is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the observation that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable is likewise."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘illusory person’ practicing the perfection of generosity is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the terms for the practice of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom by a phantom being is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the phrase ‘a phantom person practicing the five eyes’ is non-existent and unobtainable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the phrase ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unobtainable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the meaning of the phrases regarding the six supernormal powers of an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the observation that the meaning of the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable is likewise."

"Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the ten powers of a Buddha practiced by an illusory person is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects is non-existent and unapprehendable for a phantom person, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as the referent of the term 'form' (rūpa) is non-existent and unapprehendable for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the referent of the term 'Bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the marks, phrases, and meanings of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

"Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term 'eye-base' (cakṣurāyatana) is non-existent and unattainable for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), he contemplates that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unattainable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘form-base’ (rūpāyatana) is non-existent and unapprehendable for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the sphere of phenomena (dharmāyatana) do not exist and are unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' has no existence and is unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the Tathāgata’s, Arhat’s, and Samyaksaṃbuddha’s eye-element are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the form-realm, the eye-consciousness-realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the ear-element of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition have no reality and are unapprehendable in their characteristics, terms, and meanings, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the term 'bodhisattva' has no reality and is unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the sign, the phrase, and the referent of the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), he contemplates that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
“Subhūti!

"Subhūti! Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the essential meaning of the term 'tongue-element' is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the essential meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition have no marks, phrases, or referents, and are non-existent and unapprehendable; so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he observes that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' has no marks, phrases, or referents, and is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term ‘body-element’ (kāyadhātu) for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the object, the referent, and the meaning of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact—and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the object, the referent, and the meaning of 'bodhisattva' are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term for the mental constituent (*manodhātu*) of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they contemplate that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the dharmadhātu, the mental consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition have no defining characteristics or referents and are unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ has no defining characteristics or referents and is likewise unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term for the earth element is non-existent and unapprehendable for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-existent and unapprehendable by a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the noble truth of suffering are non-existent and unattainable for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unattainable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of 'bodhisattva' do not exist and cannot be apprehended."

"Subhūti! Just as the meaning of the term 'ignorance' (avidyā) does not exist and cannot be apprehended in the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

Subhūti! Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of "bodhisattva" are non-existent and unapprehendable.

"Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the four dhyānas of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase "bodhisattva" is non-existent and unapprehendable.

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the four foundations of mindfulness of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”

Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase "bodhisattva" is non-existent and unapprehendable.

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the liberation door of emptiness belonging to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the marks, phrases, and meanings of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates that the phrases and meanings of 'bodhisattva' are non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the perfection of giving of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the five eyes of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the six supernormal knowledges of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of 'bodhisattva' are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ do not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha’s four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of which are non-existent and unapprehendable—in the same way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the meaning of the term 'inner emptiness' (adhyātma-śūnyatā) is non-existent and unattainable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is likewise non-existent and unattainable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the meaning of the phrases regarding the characteristics of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates that the meaning of the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the four dhyānas practiced by a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, when practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, finds that their characteristics, phrases, and meanings do not exist and are unapprehendable, so too, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' has no existence and is unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the four foundations of mindfulness practiced by a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, when practicing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, finds that their characteristics, phrases, and meanings are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha does not find, nor can he apprehend, any mark, phrase, or meaning of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase ‘bodhisattva’ has no existence and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—when practicing the signless and wishless doors of liberation—finds that the characteristics, phrases, and meanings are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates that the phrases and meanings of 'bodhisattva' are non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha’s practice of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they contemplate that the phrases and meanings of ‘bodhisattva’ do not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
"Subhūti!

Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha finds that the characteristics, words, and meanings of practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the characteristics, words, and meanings of a 'bodhisattva' are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the five eyes of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."
"Subhūti!

Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the six supernormal powers of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrases and meanings of 'bodhisattva' are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! Just as the characteristics, phrases, and meanings of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha acting as a Buddha are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

Subhūti! Just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—when practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects—finds no such thing as a basis for these terms and cannot apprehend them, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the basis for the term "bodhisattva" likewise does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as within the realm of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtadhātu*), the referent of the term 'unconditioned realm' (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) does not exist and cannot be apprehended, and within the unconditioned realm, the referent of the term 'conditioned realm' does not exist and cannot be apprehended—so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Just as the meanings of the phrases ‘non-arising’ and ‘non-ceasing,’ ‘uncreated’ and ‘unconditioned,’ ‘non-attainment’ and ‘non-grasping,’ and ‘non-defilement’ and ‘non-purity’ are all non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

What dharma is it that is without arising and without cessation, without action and without conditioning, without attainment and without grasping, without defilement and without purification—a term and meaning that is non-existent and unobtainable?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“Form is without arising and without cessation, without activity and without conditioning, without acquisition and without grasping, and without defilement and without purification; the meaning of these terms is non-existent and unapprehendable. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are without arising and without cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; the meaning of these terms is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! The meaning of the term ‘the sense base of the eye’ is without arising and without cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; it is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meanings of the terms ‘the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind’ are likewise without arising and without cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; they are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! The meaning of the term 'the sphere of form'—its non-arising and non-ceasing, up to its non-defilement and non-purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the terms 'the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena'—their non-arising and non-ceasing, up to their non-defilement and non-purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! The meaning of the term 'the eye-element'—being without arising and without cessation, up to being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the terms 'the form-element,' 'the eye-consciousness-element,' 'eye-contact,' and 'all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition'—being without arising and without cessation, up to being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! The ear element has no arising and no cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; the referent of these terms is non-existent and unapprehendable. The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, have no arising and no cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; the referent of these terms is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! The dhātu of the nose has no arising and no cessation, and so forth, up to: it has no defilement and no purification; the referent of these terms is non-existent and unapprehendable. The dhātu of odors, the dhātu of nose-consciousness, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition have no arising and no cessation, and so forth, up to: they have no defilement and no purification; the referent of these terms is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! The linguistic meaning of the non-arising and non-ceasing, up to the non-defilement and non-purification, of the tongue element is non-existent and unapprehendable. The linguistic meaning of the non-arising and non-ceasing, up to the non-defilement and non-purification, of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! The meaning of the term ‘the body-element (kāyadhātu)’—being without arising and without cessation, even up to being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the terms ‘the object-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu),’ ‘the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu),’ ‘body-contact (kāyasparśa),’ and ‘all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition’—being without arising and without cessation, even up to being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! The meaning of the term ‘the mind-element (manodhātu)’—being without arising and without cessation, even up to being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the term ‘the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), and mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition’—being without arising and without cessation, even up to being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! The meaning of the phrase ‘the earth element is without arising and without cessation, even to the point of being without defilement and without purification’ is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the phrases ‘the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are without arising and without cessation, even to the point of being without defilement and without purification’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering has no birth and no cessation, and so forth, up to: it has no defilement and no purification; its meaning and its linguistic expression are non-existent and unapprehendable. The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path have no birth and no cessation, and so forth, up to: they have no defilement and no purification; their meaning and their linguistic expressions are non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! The meaning of the phrases 'ignorance is without arising and without cessation,' up to 'without defilement and without purification,' is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the phrases 'formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are without arising and without cessation,' up to 'without defilement and without purification,' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas have no arising and no cessation, up to and including no defilement and no purification; the referents of these phrases are non-existent and unapprehendable. The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments have no arising and no cessation, up to and including no defilement and no purification; the referents of these phrases are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! The meaning of the phrases 'unborn and unceasing,' up to 'unstained and unpurified,' regarding the four applications of mindfulness does not exist and cannot be apprehended. The meaning of the phrases 'unborn and unceasing,' up to 'unstained and unpurified,' regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

“Subhūti! The meaning of the term ‘the gate of liberation of emptiness’—from its being without arising and without cessation, up to its being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the terms ‘the gate of liberation of signlessness’ and ‘the gate of liberation of wishlessness’—from their being without arising and without cessation, up to their being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! The meaning of the term ‘the perfection of giving’—from its being without arising and without cessation, up to its being without defilement and without purification—is non-existent and unapprehendable. The meaning of the terms for the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—from their being without arising and without cessation, up to their being without defilement and without purification—is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! The five eyes have no arising and no cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; the referents of these terms do not exist and are unapprehendable. The six supernormal powers have no arising and no cessation, and so on, up to being without defilement and without purification; the referents of these terms do not exist and are unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! The meaning of the phrases ‘unborn and unceasing,’ up to ‘unstained and unpurified,’ regarding the ten powers of a Buddha does not exist and cannot be apprehended. The meaning of the phrases ‘unborn and unceasing,’ up to ‘unstained and unpurified,’ regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”

“Subhūti! Just as these dharmas are without arising and without cessation, without action and without conditioning, without attainment and without grasping, and without defilement or purification—such that their meaning and referents are non-existent and unapprehendable—in the same way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning and referent of ‘bodhisattva’ are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Just as the referential meaning of the ultimate purity of form is non-existent and unapprehendable, and the referential meaning of the ultimate purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term ‘ultimate purity’ for the sense-base of the eye does not exist and cannot be apprehended, and the referent of the term ‘ultimate purity’ for the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind does not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”

"Subhūti! Just as the referent of the term 'the ultimate purity of the sense-sphere of form' does not exist and cannot be apprehended, and the referent of the terms 'the ultimate purity of the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena' do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referent of the term 'bodhisattva' does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

“Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the defining characteristic of the phrase ‘eye-element’ is non-existent and unapprehendable, and just as the ultimate purity of the defining characteristic of the phrases for ‘form-element,’ ‘eye-consciousness-element,’ ‘eye-contact,’ and ‘all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition’ are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the defining characteristic of the phrase ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the ear-element (śrotra-dhātu) is non-existent and unapprehendable in its essential meaning, and just as the sound-element (śabda-dhātu), the ear-consciousness-element (śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu), ear-contact (śrotra-saṃsparśa), and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are ultimately pure and non-existent and unapprehendable in their essential meaning, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the essential meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the term and its referent for the nose-element is non-existent and unapprehendable, and the ultimate purity of the term and its referent for the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the term and its referent for 'bodhisattva' are likewise non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the defining characteristics and the referential meaning of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is non-existent and unapprehendable, and the ultimate purity of the defining characteristics and the referential meaning of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable—so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they observe that the referential meaning of ‘bodhisattva’ is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! Just as the term and meaning of the ‘ultimate purity’ of the body-element (kāyadhātu) do not exist and cannot be apprehended, so too the term and meaning of the ‘ultimate purity’ of the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), body-contact (kāyasparśa), and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended; it is in this same way that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they observe that the term and meaning of a ‘bodhisattva’ do not exist and cannot be apprehended.”

“Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the characteristics and referents of the element of mind (*manodhātu*) is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too are the ultimate purity of the characteristics and referents of the element of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the element of mental consciousness (*manovijñānadhātu*), and the sensations produced with mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśapratyaya*) as their condition non-existent and unapprehendable. When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they observe that the referent of the term ‘bodhisattva’ is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the earth element is non-existent and unapprehendable in its essential meaning, and the ultimate purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is non-existent and unapprehendable in their essential meanings, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate that the essential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

"Subhūti! Just as the ultimate purity of the meaning of the term 'noble truth of suffering' is non-existent and unapprehendable, and the ultimate purity of the meaning of the terms 'noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path' are non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti! Just as the phrase and meaning of the ultimate purity of ignorance is non-existent and unapprehendable, and the phrase and meaning of the ultimate purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are non-existent and unapprehendable—so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the phrase and meaning of ‘bodhisattva’ are non-existent and unapprehendable.”

"Subhūti! Just as the referential meaning of the ultimate purity of the four dhyānas is non-existent and unapprehendable, and the referential meaning of the ultimate purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is non-existent and unapprehendable, so too, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they observe that the referential meaning of 'bodhisattva' is non-existent and unapprehendable."

“Subhūti!
