The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Forty-Eight.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One: Mahāsattva Chapter Thirteen, Section Two.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this practice of the perfection of generosity together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), being utterly without stinginess regarding their bodies, lives, or anything else."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of giving by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of giving.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of generosity by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method. They dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and they do not give rise to the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas regarding the practice of generosity."
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of the perfection of ethical discipline donned by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of generosity.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of giving,

they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of giving by means of non-apprehension as their expedient, dedicating it together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and maintaining faith, patience, desire, and delight in the dharma of giving."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of patience by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of generosity.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this practice of the perfection of generosity together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi), diligently cultivating the practice of generosity without ceasing."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of diligence by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of generosity.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of generosity, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this practice of the perfection of generosity together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). In their practice of generosity, they single-mindedly dedicate it toward the knowledge of all modes, without intermingling it with the mental orientations of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of meditative concentration by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of generosity.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of giving, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of giving by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). They dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi*). Regarding the phenomenon of giving, they abide in the perception that it is like an illusion, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like a flower in the sky, like a city of Gandharvas, and like a magical transformation; they do not perceive a giver, a recipient, or a gift."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of generosity.
“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of giving, he fully dons the great armor of the six perfections.”

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, practices the perfection of generosity while neither grasping at nor clinging to the characteristics of the six perfections, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the great armor of merit.
"Śāriputra!
This is called the donning of the great armor of merit by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of ethical discipline together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). To protect their pure ethical discipline, they harbor no attachment whatsoever toward anything that exists.
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of generosity by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of ethical discipline.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā-jñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of ethical discipline together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). In their practice of ethical discipline, they do not even seek the path of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, much less that of ordinary worldlings!"
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of ethical discipline by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of ethical discipline.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of ethical discipline together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and they possess faith, patience, desire, and delight in the dharma of pure ethical discipline."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of patience by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of ethical discipline.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, they dedicate this practice of the perfection of ethical discipline together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi), diligently cultivating the conduct of ethical discipline without ceasing."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of diligence by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of ethical discipline.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of ethical discipline together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksambodhi*). In their practice of ethical discipline, they take great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) as their primary guide; they do not even allow themselves to be interspersed with the mental orientations of the two vehicles, much less those of ordinary worldlings (*pṛthagjana*)."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of meditative concentration by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of ethical discipline.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Using the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of ethical discipline together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). They dwell in the dharma of ethical discipline with the perception that it is like an illusion, like a dream, like an image, like an echo, like a reflection of light, like a flower in the sky, like a city of Gandharvas, and like a magical transformation. Regarding pure ethical discipline, they neither rely upon nor cling to it; regarding the evil of broken precepts, they neither feel aversion toward nor grasp at it, because both observance and violation are empty by their very nature."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of ethical discipline.
“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā), they are fully armored with the great armor of the six perfections.”

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, practices the perfection of ethical discipline while neither grasping nor clinging to the characteristics of the six perfections, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the great armor of merit.
“Śāriputra!
This is called the donning of the great armor of merit by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā-jñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of patience together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), remaining without attachment even to their own bodies or lives in order to accomplish patience.
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of generosity by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of patience.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of patience, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this perfection of patience together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and in their practice of patience, they do not intermingle it with the inferior mental orientations of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or those of other inferior births."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of ethical discipline by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of patience.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of patience together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and they maintain faith, patience, and aspiration for the dharma of patience."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of patience by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of patience.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of patience, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes. Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this practice of patience together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, diligently cultivating the conduct of patience without ceasing."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of diligence by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of patience.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of patience together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). Concentrating the mind on a single object, they cultivate the practice of patience; even when encountering painful circumstances, they do not allow their focus to shift to other objects."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of meditative concentration by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of patience.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Using the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha) as their skillful means, they dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). Regarding the dharma of patience, they abide in the perception that it is like an illusion, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like a flower in the sky, like a city of Gandharvas, and like a magical transformation. Desiring to cultivate and accumulate all Buddha-dharmas and desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, they contemplate the emptiness of all phenomena and do not cling to enmity or harm."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of patience.
“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of patience, he is fully equipped with the great armor of the six perfections.”

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, practices the perfection of patience while neither grasping nor clinging to the characteristics of the six perfections, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the great armor of merit.
“Śāriputra!
This is called the donning of the great armor of merit by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of diligence, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes; employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, diligently practicing various difficult deeds of giving.
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of the perfection of generosity donned by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of diligence.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of diligence, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of diligence by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, and together with all sentient beings, they dedicate this toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while diligently upholding pure moral discipline."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of ethical discipline by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of diligence.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of diligence,

they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of diligence by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, and dedicating it together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while diligently cultivating various difficult practices of patience."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of patience by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of diligence.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of diligence,

they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of diligence by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, and dedicating it together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while fervently and diligently cultivating beneficial and difficult ascetic practices."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of diligence by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of diligence.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of diligence,

they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the perfection of diligence by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, and dedicating it together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while diligently cultivating various meditative concentrations and attainments."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of meditative concentration by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of diligence.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of diligence, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), practicing the perfection of diligence by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). They dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), diligently practicing wisdom free from grasping."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of diligence.
“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of diligence, he is fully armored with the great armor of the six perfections.”

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, practices the perfection of diligence while neither grasping nor clinging to the characteristics of the six perfections, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the great armor of merit.
"Śāriputra!
This is called the donning of the great armor of merit by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of meditative concentration together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksambodhi*). Abiding in a tranquil mind, they practice generosity, ensuring that the defilement of stinginess no longer manifests.
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of the perfection of generosity donned by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha) as their skillful means, they dedicate this practice together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarasamyaksambodhi). By the power of pure concentration, they maintain the precepts, ensuring that the defilement of violating the precepts no longer manifests."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of ethical discipline by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha), they dedicate this practice together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi). Abiding in the meditative absorption of loving-kindness and compassion (maitrīkaruṇā-samādhi), they cultivate patience (kṣānti), ensuring that anger and other such afflictions no longer manifest."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of patience by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of meditative concentration together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksambodhi*). Abiding in meditative stability and diligently cultivating meritorious qualities, they cause all forms of indolence never to manifest again."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of diligence by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Using the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha) as their skillful means, they dedicate this practice together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarasamyaksambodhi). By relying on meditative concentration and other factors, they induce superior samādhis, ensuring that the obstacles of attachment to the flavors [of meditation] and mental distraction no longer manifest."
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of the perfection of meditative concentration donned by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha), they dedicate this practice of the perfection of meditative concentration together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (anuttarasamyaksambodhi). Relying on meditative concentration and the like, they bring forth superior wisdom (prajñā) and contemplate all phenomena as being like illusions and so forth, ensuring that erroneous wisdoms no longer manifest."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of meditative concentration.
“Śāriputra! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of dhyāna, they are fully equipped with the great armor of the six perfections.”

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, practices the perfection of meditative concentration while neither grasping nor clinging to the characteristics of the six perfections, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the great armor of merit.
“Śāriputra!
This is called the great armor of merit donned by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), practicing the perfection of wisdom by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method. They dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and they practice giving while the three spheres are pure, perceiving neither the giver, nor the recipient, nor the gift.
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of generosity by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate this together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). They do not perceive the distinction between those who uphold the precepts and those who break them, practicing pure ethical discipline with a mind free from attachment."
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of the perfection of ethical discipline donned by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatājñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension, they dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). Not perceiving such things as the one who endures or that which is endured, they cultivate patience through the superior wisdom of emptiness."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of patience by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatājñāna). Using the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha) as their skillful means, they dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi). They contemplate all phenomena as ultimately empty and practice diligence with a heart of great compassion."
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of the perfection of diligence that bodhisattva mahāsattvas don when practicing the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatājñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha) as their skillful means, they dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). They cultivate meditative attainments (samāpatti), observing that the entry into, abiding in, and emergence from meditative concentration, as well as the objects of concentration, are all ultimately empty."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of meditative concentration by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of wisdom.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatājñāna). Employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha) as their skillful means, they dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). Regarding all phenomena, all sentient beings, and all perfections, they dwell in the perception that they are like an illusion, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like a flower in the sky, like a city of Gandharvas, and like a magical creation; thus they cultivate various forms of wisdom free from grasping."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas when they practice the perfection of wisdom.
“Śāriputra! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are fully armored with the great armor of the six perfections.”

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, practices the perfection of wisdom while neither grasping nor clinging to the characteristics of the six perfections, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has donned the great armor of merit.
Śāriputra! This is called the great armor of merit donned by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings. Śāriputra!

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas thus abide in each of the pāramitās, they cultivate all six pāramitās so that they may be brought to full completion; for this reason, they are said to "don the great armor of merit."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), they do not relish them, nor are they led away by their power, nor do they take birth in accordance with their power."
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, dons the great armor of the perfection of wisdom through skillful means.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, although bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), they abide in the vision of seclusion, the vision of tranquility, and the vision of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, yet they do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). They do not enter the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but rather surpass and subdue all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
Śāriputra! This is called the donning of the great armor of the perfection of wisdom through skillful means by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of meditative concentration.
“Śāriputra! Because Bodhisattvas don such great armor of merit for the sake of the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, they are further called Mahāsattvas.”

“Śāriputra! Thus, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has donned the great armor of merit is universally praised with joy by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout worlds in each of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who speak these words in the midst of great assemblies:

‘In such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a world, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named so-and-so who, desiring to benefit and bring happiness to all sentient beings, has donned the great armor of merit; he brings sentient beings to maturity, purifies Buddha-fields, and performs his duties through the playful exercise of supernormal powers.’”
Thus, as the sound spread from one to another until it pervaded the ten directions, the multitudes of devas, humans, and others who heard it were all filled with joy and spoke these words:
"Such a bodhisattva shall swiftly become a Buddha, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings."
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra:
"What is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings?"
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra said: "Śāriputra!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, has donned the great armor of the six pāramitās. Furthermore, for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, he—free from desire and unwholesome states, with directed thought and sustained evaluation, and possessing the joy and happiness born of seclusion—enters and dwells in the first dhyāna."

With the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, through internal serenity and mental unification, being without applied or sustained thought, one enters and dwells in the second dhyāna, which is born of concentration and characterized by joy and bliss.

Free from joy, one dwells in equanimity, mindful and clearly aware; experiencing bliss with the body, of which the Noble Ones say, "One who dwells in equanimity and mindfulness lives in bliss," one enters and dwells in the third dhyāna.

Having abandoned both pleasure and pain, and with the prior disappearance of joy and grief, one enters and dwells in the fourth dhyāna, which is neither painful nor pleasant and possesses the purity of equanimity and mindfulness.

Furthermore, relying on meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), he gives rise to a mind associated with loving-kindness (*maitrī*), whose mental aspect (*ākāra*) is vast, non-dual, and immeasurable; it is free from enmity, harm, resentment, and vexation. Having thoroughly cultivated this state so that it is pervasive and its resolute conviction (*adhimokṣa*) is universal, it overflows throughout the ten directions, reaching the end of space and the limit of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). He dwells fully endowed with this resolute conviction of a loving mind.
The mental aspects of the resolute convictions associated with compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*) are likewise.

Based on this preparatory practice, he further transcends all perceptions of form, extinguishes perceptions of sensory resistance, and does not attend to perceptions of diversity; he enters and dwells, having fully attained the sphere of infinite space.
Transcending the entire sphere of infinite space, he enters the sphere of infinite consciousness and dwells, having fully attained the sphere of infinite consciousness.
Transcending the entire sphere of infinite consciousness, he enters the sphere of nothingness and dwells, having fully attained the sphere of nothingness.
Transcending the sphere of nothingness, he enters and dwells fully in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Śāriputra, by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method, this bodhisattva mahāsattva takes these meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, and together with all sentient beings, dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, desiring to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, first personally abide in these meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and formless attainments (*ārūpya*). Having attained mastery through thoroughly discerning and knowing the modes of entry, abiding, and emergence, as well as their activities, characteristics, and signs, they further reflect:

"I shall, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and with great compassion as my foremost guide, teach these meditative concentrations, immeasurables, and formless attainments for the sake of severing all afflictions of sentient beings; I shall analyze and reveal them so that they may thoroughly understand the gratification, the peril, and the escape regarding these meditative absorptions, as well as their modes of entry, abiding, and emergence, along with their activities, characteristics, and signs."

"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of meditative concentration, cultivates the perfection of generosity, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings."

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as their foremost guide, teaches the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, they are not interrupted by the minds of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of meditative concentration, cultivates the perfection of ethical discipline, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as their foremost priority, teaches the various meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments, they will have faith, patience, desire, and delight in such dharmas."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of meditative concentration, cultivates the perfection of patience, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and with great compassion as their primary motivation, cultivates the various meditative concentrations (dhyāna), the immeasurables (apramāṇa), and the formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), they dedicate their own roots of virtue for the sake of sentient beings, seeking unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and they diligently cultivate those roots of virtue without ceasing."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of meditative concentration, cultivates the perfection of diligence, setting out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, relies upon the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*), and thereby brings forth superior meditative absorptions (*samāpatti*), meditative stabilizations (*samādhi*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), and bases of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*), attaining mastery over entering, abiding in, and emerging from them, yet does not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of meditative concentration, cultivates the perfection of meditative concentration, having set out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, cultivates the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*), then regarding those meditative concentrations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and their constituent factors, they observe them as they truly are through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, selflessness, emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; yet, without abandoning great compassion, they do not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of meditative concentration, cultivates the perfection of wisdom and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva,
with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, enters the meditative concentration of loving-kindness, they form this thought:
'I shall rescue and deliver all sentient beings, causing them to attain peace and happiness.'"
When entering the meditative absorption of compassion, one forms this thought:
"I shall rescue and deliver all sentient beings, causing them to be free from suffering.
When entering the meditative absorption of joy, one forms this thought:
"I shall praise and exhort all sentient beings so that they may attain liberation.
When entering the meditative absorption of equanimity (*upekṣā-samādhi*), he forms this thought:
"I shall benefit all sentient beings equally so that they may sever all outflows (*āsrava*)."

"Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on immeasurable concentrations, cultivates the perfection of generosity and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings."

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as their foremost guide, enters, dwells in, and emerges from the four immeasurables, they never incline toward the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but seek only unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on immeasurable concentrations, cultivates the perfection of ethical discipline and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as their foremost priority, enters, abides in, and emerges from the four immeasurables without being distracted by the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and single-mindedly believes in, endures, and desires unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;”

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on immeasurable meditative concentrations, cultivates the perfection of patience and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, diligently abandons unwholesome dharmas and diligently cultivates wholesome dharmas while entering, abiding in, and emerging from the four immeasurables, they single-mindedly proceed toward enlightenment without ever abandoning it for even a moment.”

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on immeasurable concentrations, cultivates the perfection of diligence and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes and with great compassion as the foremost, enters, abides in, and emerges from the four immeasurables, they can induce various meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) and attainments (*samāpatti*), attaining great mastery therein. They are not led away or carried off by those states of concentration, nor do they undergo rebirth according to their power or influence.”

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on immeasurable concentrations, cultivates the perfection of dhyāna and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, cultivates the four immeasurables, and within those immeasurables observes them as they truly are through the aspect of impermanence, the aspect of suffering, the aspect of selflessness, the aspect of emptiness, the aspect of signlessness, and the aspect of wishlessness, yet does not abandon great compassion and does not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha."

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on immeasurable concentrations, cultivates the perfection of wisdom and sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

"Śāriputra! By relying on such skillful means as these, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the six perfections and set out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, fully cultivates all types of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, employing the method of non-apprehension, and together with all sentient beings, dedicates this toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, fully cultivates all aspects of the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness—employing non-apprehension as the skillful means—and together with all sentient beings dedicates [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; [this is how they set out].
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, fully cultivates all forms of giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and cooperation, employing the method of non-apprehension, and together with all sentient beings dedicates [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, fully cultivates all types of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, employing the method of non-apprehension, dedicates these together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost, fully cultivates all aspects of the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*),
gives rise to the wisdom of internal emptiness, the wisdom of external emptiness, the wisdom of internal-and-external emptiness,
the wisdom of the emptiness of emptiness, the wisdom of great emptiness, the wisdom of ultimate emptiness, the wisdom of conditioned emptiness, and the wisdom of unconditioned [emptiness]...
The wisdom of emptiness, the wisdom of ultimate emptiness, the wisdom of boundless emptiness, the wisdom of dispersed emptiness,

the wisdom of unchanging emptiness, the wisdom of intrinsic emptiness, the wisdom of emptiness of specific characteristics, the wisdom of emptiness of common characteristics, the wisdom of the emptiness of all phenomena,
the wisdom of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the wisdom of the emptiness of non-existence, and the wisdom of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
With the wisdom of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-nature, taking non-apprehension as the skillful means,
they dedicate [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, gives rise to a wisdom regarding all phenomena that is neither distracted nor fixed, and employing the method of non-apprehension, dedicates [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension, gives rise to the wisdom that all phenomena are neither eternal nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with vows nor vowless, neither quiescent nor non-quiescent, and neither detached nor non-detached—employing the method of non-apprehension—he dedicates this together with all sentient beings toward anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, knows the past through wisdom, knows the future through wisdom, and knows the present through wisdom—yet this wisdom does not fail to know the phenomena of the three periods of time, employing non-apprehension as its method—and dedicates [the merit] together with all sentient beings toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, does not perceive wisdom as wholesome, does not perceive wisdom as unwholesome, and does not perceive wisdom as indeterminate—yet it is not that they do not know the phenomena of the three natures; [this is their practice].
Wisdom does not know the desire realm, wisdom does not know the form realm, and wisdom does not know the formless realm, yet it is not that it does not know the phenomena of the three realms;

wisdom does not know the learner, wisdom does not know the non-learner, and wisdom does not know that which is neither learner nor non-learner, yet it is not that it does not know the phenomena of learners, non-learners, and those who are neither learners nor non-learners;

wisdom does not know what is abandoned by seeing, wisdom does not know what is abandoned by cultivation, and wisdom does not know what is not to be abandoned, yet it is not that it does not know the phenomena abandoned by seeing, abandoned by cultivation, and those not to be abandoned.
Using non-apprehension as the skillful means, one together with all sentient beings dedicates [the merit] toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Śāriputra!
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), possesses a wisdom that does not perceive the world and a wisdom that does not perceive the supramundane—yet is not ignorant of worldly or supramundane phenomena—and employs the method of non-apprehension to dedicate [merit] together with all sentient beings toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, does not perceive form with wisdom, nor does he perceive the formless with wisdom, yet it is not that he does not know the dharmas of form and the formless; [this is his practice].
Wisdom does not know the view of existence, nor does wisdom know the view of non-existence, yet it is not that wisdom is ignorant of the dharmas of existence and non-existence;
wisdom does not know the resistant, nor does wisdom know the non-resistant, yet it is not that wisdom is ignorant of the dharmas of resistance and non-resistance;
wisdom does not know the out-flowing, nor does wisdom know the non-out-flowing, yet it is not that wisdom is ignorant of the dharmas of out-flowing and non-out-flowing.
Wisdom does not know the conditioned, nor does wisdom know the unconditioned; yet it is not that it does not know conditioned and unconditioned phenomena.
By taking non-apprehension as its skillful means, it dedicates [merit] together with all sentient beings toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings. Śāriputra!

Because bodhisattvas, through such skillful means as these, set out upon the Great Vehicle with the desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, they are further called "mahāsattvas" (great beings).

“Śāriputra! Thus, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who have set out in the Great Vehicle are universally praised with joy by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the great assemblies throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in each of the ten directions. They speak thus:

‘In such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a world, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named so-and-so who has set out in the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings; he brings sentient beings to maturity, purifies Buddha-fields, and performs what is to be done through the play of supernormal powers.’”
Thus the sound spread in succession throughout the ten directions; when the multitudes of devas, humans, and others heard it, they were all filled with joy and spoke these words:
"Such a bodhisattva shall soon become a Buddha, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume 48 (and Volume 49),
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The Thirteenth Chapter on the Great Beings, Part One, Section Three.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra:
"In what way is it said that a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings?"
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra said: “Śāriputra!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatājñāna), with great compassion as their foremost guide, and employing the method of non-apprehension. Riding upon the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), they do not apprehend the act of giving, they do not apprehend the perfection of giving, they do not apprehend the giver, they do not apprehend the recipient, they do not apprehend the object given, and they do not apprehend any obstructed phenomena.”
Śāriputra! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mounting upon the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), with great compassion as their foremost priority, and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). They mount upon the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) without apprehending ethical discipline, without apprehending the perfection of ethical discipline, without apprehending one who maintains ethical discipline, without apprehending one who violates ethical discipline, and without apprehending any prohibited phenomena.
Śāriputra! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mounting upon the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*), they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā-jñāna*), with great compassion as their foremost guide, and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). They mount upon the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), yet they do not apprehend patience, they do not apprehend the perfection of patience, they do not apprehend the one who is patient, they do not apprehend the object of patience, and they do not apprehend the phenomena that are to be restrained.
Śāriputra! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mounting upon the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*), with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatājñāna*), with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they mount the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*) without apprehending diligence, without apprehending the perfection of diligence, without apprehending one who is diligent, without apprehending one who is indolent, and without apprehending any obstructed phenomena.
Śāriputra! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mounting upon the perfection of diligence.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do so with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as their foremost guide, and employing non-apprehension as their skillful means. They mount upon the perfection of meditative concentration, yet they do not apprehend meditative concentration, nor do they apprehend the perfection of meditative concentration; they do not apprehend one who cultivates concentration, nor one who is distracted; they do not apprehend the objective sphere of concentration, nor do they apprehend any phenomena that are to be excluded.
Śāriputra! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of the dhyāna-pāramitā.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the prajñā-pāramitā, they [should] apply themselves to a single...
The mind of omniscient wisdom has great compassion as its foremost guide; employing non-apprehension as its skillful means, it rides upon the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Therein, one does not apprehend *prajñā*, nor does one apprehend *prajñāpāramitā*;
one does not apprehend the one who cultivates wisdom, nor does one apprehend the one who is deluded; one does not apprehend the past, nor the future...
Regarding future and present phenomena, one does not apprehend wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate phenomena;

one does not apprehend phenomena of the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm; one does not apprehend phenomena of those in training (*śaikṣa*), those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), or those who are neither;
one does not apprehend phenomena to be abandoned by seeing, abandoned by cultivation, or not to be abandoned. Not...
One attains mundane and supramundane dharmas, yet does not attain dharmas of the realm of form or the formless realm;
one does not attain dharmas of visibility or invisibility; one does not attain dharmas of resistance or non-resistance;
one does not attain dharmas that are outflows or without outflows; one does not attain conditioned or unconditioned dharmas; and one does not attain any obstructed dharma.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva rides upon the perfection of wisdom.
Śāriputra, you should know this!
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness for the sake of relinquishing cultivation; and for the sake of relinquishing cultivation, he cultivates the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path."
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness in order to eliminate cultivation, and cultivates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness in order to eliminate cultivation.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, practices the four dhyānas for the purpose of relinquishing cultivation, and practices the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions for the purpose of relinquishing cultivation.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, practices the perfection of generosity for the sake of relinquishing cultivation; and practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom for the sake of relinquishing cultivation.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, cultivates the five eyes and cultivates the six supernormal powers in order to relinquish cultivation.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, mounts the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, cultivates the ten powers of a buddha for the sake of relinquishing cultivation; and for the sake of relinquishing cultivation, cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension for the sake of relinquishing cultivation, cultivates the wisdom of internal emptiness, the wisdom of external emptiness, the wisdom of internal and external emptiness, the wisdom of the emptiness of emptiness, the wisdom of great emptiness, the wisdom of ultimate emptiness, the wisdom of conditioned emptiness, the wisdom of unconditioned emptiness, the wisdom of absolute emptiness, the wisdom of boundless emptiness, the wisdom of dispersed emptiness, the wisdom of unchanging emptiness, the wisdom of essential emptiness, the wisdom of self-characteristic emptiness, the wisdom of common characteristic emptiness, the wisdom of the emptiness of all phenomena, the wisdom of the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the wisdom of the emptiness of non-existence, the wisdom of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the wisdom of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension to observe as it truly is that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation, a conventional expression, because both "bodhi" and "sattva" are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, observes that form is merely a provisional name, a designation, and a conventional expression, because form cannot be apprehended;

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness exist only as provisional designations, expressions, and conventional speech, because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended. Śāriputra!
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, mounts the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and with great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as a skillful means, they observe the sphere of the eye (*cakṣur-āyatana*) as being merely a conventional designation, a provisional establishment, and a verbal expression, because the sphere of the eye cannot be apprehended;

and they observe the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being merely conventional designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions, because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, correctly observes that the sphere of form exists merely as a provisional name, a designation, and a conventional expression, because the sphere of form is ultimately unapprehendable;

The bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena exist only as provisional designations and verbal expressions, because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are ultimately unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, correctly observes that the eye-element is merely a conventional designation, a verbal expression, because the eye-element cannot be apprehended;

The form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition exist merely as provisional designations, verbal expressions, and conventional parlance; for the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, observes the realm of the ear as being merely a conventional designation, a verbal expression, because the realm of the ear is unapprehendable;

The sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition exist merely as provisional designations, conventions, and verbal expressions; for from the sphere of sound up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, nothing can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, observes the nose-element as it truly is—seeing that it is merely a conventional designation, a provisional expression, because the nose-element cannot be apprehended;

The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition exist only as provisional designations, expressions, and conventional speech; for the fragrance element, up to and including all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, observes the tongue-element as being merely a conventional designation, a provisional construct, and a verbal expression—because the tongue-element is unapprehendable;

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition exist merely as provisional designations, conventional expressions, and verbal designations; for from the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, nothing can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, observes the realm of the body (*kāyadhātu*) as it truly is—seeing that it is merely a provisional designation, a conventional expression, because the realm of the body is unapprehendable;

The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition exist only as provisional designations, conventional expressions, and verbal conventions; for from the element of tangibles up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, nothing can be apprehended.

Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, observes the realm of mind (*manodhātu*) as it truly is—seeing that the realm of mind exists only as a provisional designation, a conceptual construct, and a verbal expression; because the realm of mind is unapprehendable; ... [and so on] ... [The text continues in this manner regarding the other sense bases and elements. ... [the bodhisattva] observes the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) as it truly is—seeing that the realm of phenomena exists only as a provisional designation, a conceptual construct, and a verbal expression; because the realm of phenomena is unapprehendable. Śāriputra, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, mounts the Great Vehicle. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend even the name "bodhisattva," nor do they apprehend the name "Great Vehicle. Why is this? Because these names are merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom. They do not apprehend the perfection of wisdom, nor do they apprehend the bodhisattva, nor do they apprehend the Buddha, nor do they apprehend the Dharma, nor do they apprehend the Sangha. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the six perfections, nor do they apprehend the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, nor do they apprehend the four noble truths, nor do they apprehend the ten powers of a Tathāgata, nor do they apprehend the four fearlessnesses, nor do they apprehend the four analytical knowledges, nor do they apprehend the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the fruit of a Stream-enterer, nor do they apprehend the fruit of a Once-returner, nor do they apprehend the fruit of a Non-returner, nor do they apprehend Arhatship, nor do they apprehend Pratyekabuddhahood, nor do they apprehend Buddhahood. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the world of desire, nor do they apprehend the world of form, nor do they apprehend the formless world. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the past, nor do they apprehend the future, nor do they apprehend the present. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the realm of sentient beings, nor do they apprehend the realm of space, nor do they apprehend the realm of phenomena. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the realm of the Tathāgatas, nor do they apprehend the realm of all dharmas. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of a Stream-enterer, nor do they apprehend the dharma of a Once-returner, nor do they apprehend the dharma of a Non-returner, nor do they apprehend the dharma of an Arhat, nor do they apprehend the dharma of a Pratyekabuddha, nor do they apprehend the dharma of a Buddha. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of the world of desire, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the world of form, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the formless world. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom.
