Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of the past, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the future, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the present. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of the realm of sentient beings, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the realm of space, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the realm of phenomena. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of the Tathāgatas, nor do they apprehend the dharma of all dharmas. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of the dharma of a Stream-enterer, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the dharma of a Once-returner, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the dharma of a Non-returner, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the dharma of an Arhat, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the dharma of a Pratyekabuddha, nor do they apprehend the dharma of the dharma of a Buddha. Why is this? Because these are all merely conventional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions; they are empty of intrinsic nature and lack any substantial reality. Śāriputra, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of wisdom. Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this way, they do not apprehend the dharma of the dharma of the world of desire, nor

The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, exist only as provisional designations, conventions, and verbal expressions; for from the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, nothing can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, observes the earth element as being merely a conventional designation, a provisional establishment, and a verbal expression—because the earth element is ultimately unapprehendable;

The elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness exist only as provisional designations, verbal expressions, and conventional parlance, because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are ultimately unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, mounts the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, observes the Noble Truth of Suffering as being merely a provisional designation, a conceptual construct, and a verbal expression—because the Noble Truth of Suffering is unapprehendable;

The noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path exist only as provisional designations, expressions, and conventional speech, because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended. Śāriputra!
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, they observe according to reality that ignorance is merely a provisional name, a designation, and a conventional expression, because ignorance is unapprehendable;

likewise, they observe that formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are merely provisional names, designations, and conventional expressions, because everything from formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing non-apprehension as the skillful means, correctly observes that internal emptiness exists only as a provisional designation, a conventional expression, because internal emptiness is unapprehendable;

Outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of essential nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unobtainable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are merely conventional designations, expressions, and verbal usages; for from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nothing can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, observes reality as it truly is: that suchness is merely a provisional designation, a conventional expression, because suchness cannot be apprehended;

The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the dharma-constancy, the dharma-abiding, the nature of transcendence from birth, equality, and the limit of reality exist only as provisional designations, verbal expressions, and conventional speech; for from the dharma-realm up to the limit of reality, nothing can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! It is for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings that a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs non-apprehension as a skillful means, observes the four dhyānas as being merely conventional designations and verbal expressions, because the four dhyānas are unapprehendable;

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions exist only as provisional designations, conventions, and verbal expressions, because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, correctly observes that the four foundations of mindfulness exist only as provisional designations, verbal expressions, and conventional speech, because the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable;

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path exist only as provisional designations, conceptual constructs, and verbal expressions, because from the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, they are ultimately unfindable.
Śāriputra! It is for this reason that a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, correctly observes that the gate of liberation of emptiness is merely a conventional designation and verbal expression, because the gate of liberation of emptiness cannot be apprehended;

The gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness possess only conventional designations and verbal expressions, because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are unattainable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), correctly observes that the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) is merely a conventional designation, a verbal expression, because the perfection of giving cannot be apprehended;

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom exist only as provisional designations and verbal expressions, because from ethical discipline up to wisdom, they are ultimately unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as a skillful means, observes that the five eyes are merely conventional designations, verbal expressions, and provisional establishments, because the five eyes are ultimately unapprehendable;
The six supernormal powers exist only as provisional designations, expressions, and verbal conventions, because the six supernormal powers are unattainable. Śāriputra,
this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, observes according to reality that the ten powers of a buddha are merely provisional designations established by verbal expression, because the ten powers of a buddha cannot be apprehended;

and observes that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are merely provisional designations established by verbal expression, because everything from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended.”
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost, employs the method of non-apprehension, observes according to reality that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is merely a provisional designation, a conventional expression, because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment cannot be apprehended;
"Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi" is merely a conventional designation and a verbal expression, for an Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbuddha cannot be apprehended. Śāriputra!
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, taking great compassion as the foremost and employing the method of non-apprehension, from the first production of the thought of enlightenment until the realization of unsurpassed awakening, constantly cultivates and perfects non-retrogressive supernormal powers; matures sentient beings and purifies buddha-fields; travels from one buddha-field to another, making offerings, paying respect, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; and at the presence of those Buddhas, listens to and receives the teachings corresponding to the Great Vehicle; and having received them, reflects upon them according to the principle and diligently practices and studies them.
Śāriputra! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva mounts the Great Vehicle for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings. Śāriputra!

In this way, although a bodhisattva mahāsattva rides upon the Great Vehicle, traveling from one buddha-field to another to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; and while listening to and receiving the true Dharma from those Buddhas, maturing sentient beings and adorning and purifying buddha-fields, their mind never gives rise to any conceptualization of "buddha-fields" or the like.

Śāriputra! Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells on the stage of non-duality, they observe which body among all sentient beings would bring them benefit and meaning, and they immediately manifest and assume that form to enable them to obtain such benefit.

Śāriputra! In this way, from the time a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains even the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they do not depart from the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) in whatever place they are born. Śāriputra!
In this way, before long, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas shall attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and turn the wheel of the true Dharma for the sake of humans, devas, and others.

Such a wheel of Dharma cannot be turned by any in the entire world—neither by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, śramaṇas, brahmins, Māras, Brahmās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, or non-humans.

Śāriputra! Because these bodhisattvas, through such skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings and ride upon the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), they are further called *mahāsattvas*.

“Śāriputra! Thus, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have mounted the Great Vehicle are universally praised with joy by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the great assemblies throughout worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. They speak thus:

‘In such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a world, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of such-and-such a name who, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, has mounted the Great Vehicle; before long he shall attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and turn the wheel of the true Dharma for gods, humans, and others—a wheel that none among the worldly hosts of gods, humans, Māras, Brahmās, or Śrāvakas can turn.’”
Thus, as the sound spread from one to another until it pervaded the ten directions, the assemblies of devas, humans, and others heard it and were all filled with joy, saying:
"Such a bodhisattva shall before long attain the wisdom of all-knowledge and turn the wheel of the true Dharma to benefit and bring peace to all sentient beings."
14. Chapter on the Armor of the Mahāyāna, Part One: The First Section of the Chapter on the Armor of the Mahāyāna, Number Fourteen. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
As it has been said: "A bodhisattva mahāsattva who dons the armor of the Great Vehicle"—how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is said to don the armor of the Great Vehicle?
The Buddha said:
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen.]..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the perfection of generosity, and dons the armor of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, Subhūti!
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.
Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the four dhyānas, and dons the armor of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—Subhūti!
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.

"Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the four foundations of mindfulness, dons the armor of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—Subhūti!"
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of internal emptiness, and dons the armor of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—Subhūti! [this is called donning the armor of the Mahāyāna]."
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the five eyes and dons the armor of the six supernormal powers, Subhūti!..."
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the ten powers of a buddha; dons the armor of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects—Subhūti!"
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the merits of the physical marks of a Buddha’s body, Subhūti!"
This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons such armor of various merits, they emit a great radiance that illuminates the entire trichiliocosm and causes this world-system to undergo the six kinds of earthquakes."

Within those hells, the fires and other instruments of suffering, as well as the physical and mental anguish of the sentient beings therein, were all extinguished. Knowing that they had been freed from these manifold sufferings, the Bodhisattva praised the merits of the Triple Gem. Having heard this, their bodies and minds became peaceful and blissful; they passed away from their own realm and were reborn among gods and humans, where they immediately obtained the opportunity to behold the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, personally receiving offerings and hearing the sounds of the True Dharma.

Among those in the animal realm, who were subject to mutual slaughter, flogging, and coercion, all their immeasurable sufferings were extinguished. Once the Bodhisattva knew they were free from these various miseries, he further extolled the merits of the Triple Gem. Having heard this, their bodies and minds became peaceful and joyful; they passed away from their own destinies and were reborn among gods and humans, where they immediately gained the opportunity to behold the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, personally receiving offerings and hearing the sounds of the True Dharma.

Within that realm of hungry ghosts, their terrors, hunger, thirst, and the physical and mental anguish of their parched afflictions were all extinguished. Knowing that they had been freed from these manifold sufferings, the Bodhisattva further extolled the merits of the Triple Gem; having heard this, their bodies and minds became peaceful and joyful. They passed away from their own destination and were reborn among gods and humans, where they immediately obtained the opportunity to behold the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, personally receiving offerings and hearing the sounds of the True Dharma.
“Subhūti! This is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons such armor of merit, they emit a great radiance that shines throughout as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River, and they also cause those worlds to undergo the six kinds of triple earthquake.”

Within them, all the various sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts were extinguished. Knowing that they had been freed from these many sufferings, the Bodhisattva further praised the merits of the Triple Gem; having heard this, their bodies and minds attained peace and bliss, and they passed away from their respective realms to be reborn among gods and humans, where they immediately gained the opportunity to behold the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, personally receiving offerings and hearing the sounds of the True Dharma.
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Suppose a skilled illusionist or his disciple, at a crossroads before a great assembly, were to conjure through illusion countless sentient beings in the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts, each undergoing various sufferings; he would likewise emit light that causes the great earth to tremble, causing all those sentient beings' sufferings to cease. He would further praise the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, so that upon hearing it, their bodies and minds become peaceful and blissful. They would then pass away from their respective destinies and be reborn among gods and humans, where they serve and make offerings to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, receiving the sounds of the true Dharma from the presence of those Buddhas.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons such armor of merit as these, they emit great radiance that shakes the great earth, rescuing sentient beings in immeasurable worlds from the sufferings of the three evil realms. They cause them to be born among gods or humans so that they may see the Buddha and hear the Dharma; yet, although there is this activity, not a single thing therein is real.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of all phenomena is empty, being like an illusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in the perfection of generosity, he universally transforms the trichiliocosm so that it is like vaidūrya, and likewise transforms himself into a wheel-turning monarch, surrounded by a retinue of the seven treasures. Among those sentient beings therein, he gives food to those who need food, drink to those who need drink, clothing to those who need clothing, and vehicles to those who need vehicles. He gives ointments, powdered incense, burning incense, flower garlands, dwellings, bedding, lamps, medicine, gold, silver, pearls, coral, jade, and all other various requisites for life, giving everything according to their needs."

Having performed this giving, he further proclaims for them the Dharma associated with the six *pāramitās*, so that upon hearing it, they may eventually realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and never again abandon the Dharma associated with the six *pāramitās*.
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

It is like a skilled illusionist or his apprentice who, at a crossroads before a great assembly, conjures various sentient beings—poor, destitute, with impaired faculties or limbs, and afflicted by disease—and bestows upon them, according to their needs, whatever they require, all through the power of illusion.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in the perfection of generosity, they may transform worlds into vaidūrya or transform themselves into universal monarchs and the like, bestowing upon sentient beings whatever they require; and likewise, they proclaim the teachings corresponding to the six perfections. Although there is such activity, not a single thing therein is real.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of all phenomena is empty, being like an illusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, abiding themselves in the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings,
is born into the family of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) and succeeds to the rank of a universal monarch, establishing immeasurable hundreds [of beings in virtue]..."
He establishes thousands of koṭīs of nayutas of sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action;
or again, he establishes immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭīs of nayutas of sentient beings in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless absorptions;
or again, he establishes immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭīs of nayutas of sentient beings in...
The four foundations of mindfulness; or the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;

or alternatively, establishing immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings in the gate of liberation of emptiness, or in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Or again, they establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings in the perfection of generosity,
or in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration,
and wisdom; or again, they establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings in the five...
The eye, or the six supernormal powers; or again, establishing immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings in the ten powers of a Buddha,
or in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion,
great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and omniscience.
Having established them in the knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and so forth, until they attain unexcelled,
perfect, and complete enlightenment, he never abandons them from such dharmas.
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Suppose a skilled illusionist or his apprentice, at a crossroads before a great assembly, were to conjure up immeasurable sentient beings through illusion and cause them to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action, or even cause them to abide in the four dhyānas up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“For the sake of sentient beings, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is born into the family of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) and succeeds to the rank of a universal monarch, establishing immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action; or again, he establishes immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings in the four dhyānas, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). Although there is that which is performed, not a single thing is real.”
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the nature of all phenomena is empty, for they are all like illusions.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides themselves in the perfection of patience, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in the perfection of patience."

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva abide themselves in the perfection of patience, and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in the perfection of patience?
"Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first generation of the mind of awakening until the realization of the knowledge of all modes, dons the armor of patience and constantly reflects:

'Even if all sentient beings were to come with swords, staves, clods of earth, and so forth to inflict harm upon me, I shall never give rise to even a single thought of anger, and I shall exhort all sentient beings to likewise practice such patience.'"

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva experiences no contradiction between the objects as conceived by the mind and their actual contact; he exhorts all sentient beings to abide in such patience, and until they realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he never abandons them from within that patience."
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Suppose a skilled illusionist or his disciple, at a crossroads before a great assembly, were to conjure various types of sentient beings through illusion, each of whom took up swords, staves, clods of earth, or other weapons to harm the illusionist or his disciple. At that time, the illusionist and others would not give rise to even a single thought of seeking revenge against those illusory beings; rather, they would exhort them to abide in such patience.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“A bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of patience; dwelling themselves in the perfection of patience, they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to dwell in the perfection of patience. This constant non-abandonment is likewise such that, although there is activity, not a single thing is real.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of all phenomena is empty, being like an illusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides themselves in the perfection of diligence, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to abide in the perfection of diligence."

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell themselves in the perfection of diligence, and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to dwell in the perfection of diligence?
"Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, applies physical and mental diligence to sever all unwholesome dharmas and cultivate all wholesome dharmas, and furthermore encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to practice such physical and mental diligence, never abandoning such diligence until they realize unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment."
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Just as a skilled illusionist or his disciple, at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure various kinds of sentient beings through illusion, while that skilled illusionist himself manifests a body and mind ablaze with vigorous diligence, and also exhorts those he has conjured to cultivate such blazing diligence.
"Subhūti, what do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“A bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind corresponding to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), applies physical and mental diligence to sever all unwholesome dharmas and cultivate all wholesome dharmas. He likewise encourages sentient beings to practice such physical and mental diligence, never abandoning it; yet, although he performs these deeds, not a single one is real.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of all phenomena is empty, being just like an illusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides personally in the perfection of meditative concentration, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in the perfection of meditative concentration."
"Subhūti!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva abide themselves in the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in the perfection of meditative concentration?"
"Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in the samādhi of equality regarding all phenomena, perceiving no phenomenon as either concentrated or distracted, and constantly cultivates this perfection of dhyāna, while also exhorting immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to cultivate such equal dhyāna, until they attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, never abandoning this samādhi."
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Just as a skilled illusionist or his disciple, at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure various kinds of sentient beings through illusion, yet that skilled illusionist himself remains manifest in the meditative absorption of the equality of phenomena (*dharmasthiti-samādhi*), and likewise exhorts those conjured beings to cultivate such an equalizing concentration.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“A bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in the samādhi of equality regarding all phenomena, and likewise encourages sentient beings to practice such meditative concentration of equality; he never abandons this, and though he performs various deeds, not one of them has any reality.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of all phenomena is empty, being like an illusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides themselves in the perfection of wisdom, and also encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in the perfection of wisdom."

Subhūti! How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva abide in the perfection of wisdom themselves, and also encourage immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in the perfection of wisdom?
"Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides personally in the non-conceptualizing (*niṣprapañca*) prajñāpāramitā, does not perceive any phenomena as having arising or ceasing, or being defiled or purified, and does not apprehend the distinction between this shore and the other shore, and furthermore encourages immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings to abide in such non-conceptualizing wisdom—until they realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—they shall never abandon such wisdom."
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Just as a skilled illusionist or his disciple, at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure various kinds of sentient beings through illusion, yet that skilled illusionist himself remains established in non-conceptual wisdom and also exhorts those conjured beings to practice such *prajñā*.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“A bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells himself in the non-conceptualization (*aprapañca*) of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and likewise encourages sentient beings to cultivate such non-conceptual wisdom; he never abandons this practice, and although he performs all manner of deeds, not a single one has any reality.”
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the nature of all phenomena is empty, for they are all like illusions.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the aforementioned virtues, he uses his supernormal powers to transform his own body so that it pervades all Buddha-worlds in the ten directions, each as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. He manifests himself according to the inclinations of sentient beings; while abiding himself in the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*), he exhorts those who are stingy to abide in generosity;
while abiding himself in the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), he exhorts those who violate the precepts to abide in ethical discipline."
Abiding themselves in the perfection of patience, they encourage those who are violent and wicked to abide in patience;
abiding themselves in the perfection of diligence, they encourage those who are indolent to abide in diligence;
abiding themselves in the perfection of meditative concentration, they encourage those with distracted minds to abide in meditative concentration.
Abiding themselves in the *prajñāpāramitā*, they encourage those who are deluded to abide in sublime wisdom.

In this way, after the bodhisattva-mahāsattva has established sentient beings in the six *pāramitās*, they further preach the Dharma associated with the six *pāramitās* in accordance with the various languages of those beings. Having heard it, those beings shall never again abandon the Dharma associated with the six *pāramitās* until they realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Subhūti! This is what is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva donning the armor of the Great Vehicle. Subhūti!"

Just as a skilled illusionist or his apprentice, at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure various kinds of sentient beings through illusion, yet that skilled illusionist himself remains established in the six perfections and also exhorts those conjured sentient beings to likewise remain established in them.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“A bodhisattva mahāsattva universally manifests his own body in all the buddha-worlds of the ten directions, each as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. He dwells in accordance with the various types [of beings] within the six pāramitās and likewise exhorts sentient beings to dwell therein. This remains so until he attains unsurpassed awakening, never abandoning them; yet, although there is that which is done, not a single thing is real.”
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the nature of all phenomena is empty, for they are all like illusions.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the aforementioned virtues, with the mind of omniscience as the objective, with great compassion as the foremost priority, and employing the method of non-apprehension to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, without mixing in the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."
That is to say, one does not form such thoughts as:
"I shall establish this many sentient beings in the perfection of generosity, while I shall not establish that many sentient beings."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the perfection of generosity.
One does not form this thought:

"I shall establish all those sentient beings in the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; yet there are those sentient beings whom I should not establish [in them]."
They should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the pure precepts, and so forth, up to the perfection of wisdom."
One does not form this thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in internal emptiness, and I shall not establish so many sentient beings.
Rather, one forms this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in internal emptiness.
He does not form this thought:

"I shall establish so many sentient beings in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; nor shall I fail to establish so many sentient beings [in these]."
They should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence."
They do not form such a thought as:
"I shall establish this many sentient beings in the four dhyānas, and I shall not establish that many sentient beings."
One should simply think:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the four dhyānas.
One should not think:
"One should not think, 'I shall establish this many sentient beings in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, while I shall not establish that many sentient beings.
Rather, one should simply form this thought:
'I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.'"
One does not form this thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in the four foundations of mindfulness, and I shall not establish so many sentient beings."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the four foundations of mindfulness.
One does not form this thought:

"I shall establish all those sentient beings in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; there are no sentient beings who should not be so established."
He should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path."
They do not form this thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and so many sentient beings I shall not establish."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the gate of liberation that is emptiness.
One does not form this thought:
"I shall establish all those sentient beings in the gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; yet, there are no sentient beings who should be established.
Rather, one should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."
He does not form this thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in the five eyes, and I shall not establish so many sentient beings.
He forms only this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the five eyes," yet he does not form the thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in the six supernormal powers, and so many sentient beings I shall not establish."
He merely forms this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the six supernormal powers.
He does not form this thought:
"One should not think, 'I shall establish this many sentient beings in the ten powers of a Buddha, but I shall not establish that many.
Rather, one should simply form this thought:
'I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the ten powers of a Buddha.'"
They do not form this thought:

"I shall establish all those sentient beings in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; yet there are some sentient beings whom I shall not establish."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings in the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience."
They do not form such thoughts as:
"I shall establish this many sentient beings in the fruit of stream-entry, and I shall not establish that many sentient beings."
He merely forms this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the fruit of stream-entry.
He does not form such a thought as:

"I shall establish all those sentient beings in the fruit of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, and in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; yet there are those sentient beings whom I shall not so establish."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha."
They do not form this thought:
"I shall establish so many sentient beings in the bodhisattva path and unsurpassed enlightenment, but I shall not establish so many sentient beings."
One should simply form this thought:
"I shall establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the bodhisattva path and unsurpassed bodhi."
"Subhūti! This is called the donning of the great armor by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti!"

Just as a skilled illusionist or his apprentice, at a crossroads before a great assembly, might conjure by magic an immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless number of sentient beings, and establish them in the six perfections, even up to establishing them in unsurpassed enlightenment.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Does such an illusory phenomenon have any reality?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"A bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, establishes immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the six perfections; even so, he likewise establishes immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in unsurpassed enlightenment. Although there is that which is done, not a single thing is real."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of all phenomena is empty, being like an illusion.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 49 [and] Scroll 53.
Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The First Part of the Mahāyāna Armor Chapter, Number Fourteen, Part Two.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, one should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not don the armor of merit, they are truly donning the armor of the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Because all dharmas are empty of their own specific characteristics. Why is this so?
World-Honored One!
Form is empty of the characteristic of form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
The eye-base is empty of the characteristic of the eye-base; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty of the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

The form-base is empty of the characteristic of the form-base; the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and phenomena-bases are empty of the characteristics of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and phenomena-bases.

The eye-element is empty of the characteristic of the eye-element; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are empty of the characteristics of the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

The ear-element is empty of the characteristic of the ear-element; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are empty of the characteristics of the sound-element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

The nose-element is empty of the characteristic of the nose-element; the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are empty of the characteristics of the odor-element up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

The tongue element is empty of the characteristic of the tongue element; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—from the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—are empty of their respective characteristics.

The body element is empty of the characteristic of the body element; the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—from the tangible-object element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are empty of their respective characteristics.

The mind element is empty of the characteristic of the mind element; the mental-phenomena element, the mind-consciousness element, and mind-contact, as well as all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition—from the mental-phenomena element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition—are empty of their respective characteristics.

The earth element is empty of the characteristic of the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

The noble truth of suffering is empty of the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

Ignorance is empty of the characteristic of ignorance; the formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the characteristics of the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Internal emptiness is empty of the characteristic of internal emptiness; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the characteristic of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are likewise empty.

The four dhyānas are empty of the characteristics of the four dhyānas; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the characteristic of the four foundations of mindfulness; the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the characteristics of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.

The emptiness liberation door is empty of the characteristic of the emptiness liberation door; the signless and wishless liberation doors are empty of the characteristics of the signless and wishless liberation doors.

The perfection of generosity is empty of the characteristic of the perfection of generosity; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—from the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom—are empty of the characteristics of the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom.
The five eyes are empty of the characteristic of the five eyes; the six supernormal powers are empty of the characteristic of the six supernormal powers;

the ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the characteristic of the ten powers of a Buddha; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects—from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects—are empty of the characteristic of [the four fearlessnesses] up to the knowledge of all aspects;
the bodhisattva is empty of the characteristic of a bodhisattva; and the donning of the armor of merit is empty of the characteristic of donning the armor of merit.
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, one should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not don the armor of merit, they are truly donning the armor of the Mahāyāna.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."

"Subhūti, you should know that the knowledge of all modes is without creation or activity, and all sentient beings are likewise without creation or activity; it is for this purpose that bodhisattva mahāsattvas don the armor of the Great Vehicle."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,

for what reason is the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) uncreated and unconditioned, and why are all sentient beings also uncreated and unconditioned, such that the bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of the Great Vehicle for this purpose?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because an agent cannot be apprehended, the knowledge of all modes is neither created nor fashioned, and all sentient beings are likewise neither created nor fashioned.”
Why is that? "Subhūti!
I neither create nor do not create; I neither act nor do not act."
Why is this? Because a self is ultimately unapprehendable.

Sentient beings, life-principles, living beings, nourishers, persons, individuals, mind-born ones, youths, agents, instigators of action, originators, instigators of origination, experiencers, instigators of experience, knowers, and seers neither create nor do not create; they neither act nor do not act.
Why is this? Because sentient beings, up to and including the "seer," are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!
An illusory phenomenon is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because an illusory phenomenon is ultimately unattainable.
Dreams, reflections, echoes, shadows, optical illusions, mirages, cities of Gandharvas, and transformations are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because dream-objects, and even transformed phenomena, are ultimately unattainable.
"Subhūti!..."
Form is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because form is ultimately unapprehendable.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ultimately unapprehendable.
“Subhūti! The eye-base is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the sense-base of the eye is ultimately unobtainable,
the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Subhūti!..."
The sphere of form is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the sphere of form is ultimately unobtainable.
The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are ultimately non-apprehendable.
“Subhūti! The eye-element is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the eye-element is ultimately unapprehendable,
the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from the realm of form up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, none are ultimately to be found.
"Subhūti!..."
The ear-element is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the ear-element is ultimately unapprehendable.
The sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings arisen with ear-contact as condition are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!
The nose element is neither conditioned nor unconditioned, neither created nor uncreated. Why is this?
Because the nose element is ultimately unapprehendable.
The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the realm of fragrance, up to and including the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Subhūti!..."
The tongue element is neither conditioned nor unconditioned, neither created nor uncreated. Why is this?
Because the tongue element is ultimately unapprehendable.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the taste element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are ultimately non-apprehendable. "Subhūti!
The body-element (kāyadhātu) is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the body-element is ultimately unapprehendable.
The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the sphere of tangibles, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!
The mind-element (manodhātu) is neither created nor uncreated, neither produced nor unproduced. Why is this?
Because the mind-element is ultimately unapprehendable.

The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm, up to and including all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Subhūti!..."
The earth element is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the earth element is ultimately unapprehendable.
The elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are ultimately unapprehendable.
“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the noble truth of suffering is ultimately unattainable.
The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!
Ignorance is neither created nor not created; it is neither made nor not made."
Why is this? Because ignorance is ultimately unattainable.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, these are ultimately unattainable. "Subhūti!
Internal emptiness is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because internal emptiness is ultimately unapprehendable.

Outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are ultimately unapprehendable. "Subhūti!
The four dhyānas are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the four dhyānas are ultimately unattainable.
The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are ultimately unattainable.
"Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are ultimately unapprehendable,

the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are ultimately unattainable.
"Subhūti!..."
The gate of liberation of emptiness is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is ultimately unattainable.
The gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Subhūti! The perfection of giving is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the perfection of giving is ultimately unapprehendable,
the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because from pure ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, they are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The five eyes are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the five eyes are ultimately unattainable.
The six supernormal powers are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the six supernormal powers are ultimately unattainable.
“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha are neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade. Why is this?
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are ultimately unattainable,

the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are neither created nor uncreated, neither produced nor unproduced.
Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Subhūti!..."
Suchness is neither created nor uncreated, neither made nor unmade.
Why is this? Because Suchness ultimately is not non-making.
Why is this? Because from the dharma-realm up to the limit of reality, they are ultimately unapprehendable.
"Subhūti!..."
A bodhisattva neither creates nor does not create; neither acts nor does not act.
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva is ultimately unapprehendable.

Because the natures of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are all non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because internal emptiness is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities, is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation;

because internal emptiness is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities, is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation;

because internal emptiness is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities, is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the emptiness of the internal is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the emptiness of the internal is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the emptiness of the internal is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the emptiness of the internal is without cessation, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is without cessation, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the emptiness of the internal is without defilement, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is without defilement, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the emptiness of the internal is without purification, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is without purification, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“World-Honored One!
The four dhyānas are neither bound nor liberated; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
"World-Honored One!

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation."

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is wishlessness, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is wishlessness, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is non-extinction, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is non-extinction, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is undefiled, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is undefiled, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four dhyānas is not pure, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not pure, they are neither bound nor liberated.
“World-Honored One!

The four foundations of mindfulness are neither bound nor liberated; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are neither bound nor liberated.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness does not exist, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path does not exist, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is detachment, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is detachment, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is tranquility, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is tranquility, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is emptiness, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is emptiness, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is signless, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is signless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-extinguished, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is non-extinguished, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“World-Honored One!
The liberation door of emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
"Bhagavān!

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation."

Because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the natures of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the natures of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the natures of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is non-arising, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is non-ceasing, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is non-ceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is unstained, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door is without purification, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is without purification, they are neither bound nor liberated.
