The First Part of the Mahāyāna Armor Chapter, Number Fourteen, Section Three:
“World-Honored One!
The perfection of giving is neither bound nor liberated; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are neither bound nor liberated.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because the nature of the perfection of giving is non-existent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is remote, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are remote, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is tranquil, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are tranquil, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is empty, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are empty, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is signless (*animitta*), it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline (*śīla*) up to wisdom (*prajñā*) are signless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is wishless (*apranihita*), it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is unborn (*anutpanna*), it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are unborn, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is non-extinguished, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline (*śīla*) up to wisdom (*prajñā*) are non-extinguished, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is unstained, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is unpurified, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
“World-Honored One!
The five eyes are neither bound nor liberated; the six supernormal powers are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this so?
“World-Honored One!
Because the nature of the five eyes is non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated.
Because the nature of the five eyes is detached, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is detached, they are neither bound nor liberated.”
Because the nature of the five eyes is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Because the nature of the five eyes is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Because the nature of the five eyes is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Because the nature of the five eyes is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated.
Because the nature of the five eyes is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is non-arising, they are neither bound nor liberated.
Because the nature of the five eyes is non-ceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is non-ceasing, they are neither bound nor liberated.
Because the nature of the five eyes is unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated.
Because the nature of the five eyes is not purified, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the six supernormal powers is not purified, they are neither bound nor liberated.
“World-Honored One!

The ten powers of a Buddha are neither bound nor liberated; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are neither bound nor liberated.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to all-aspect omniscience is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is tranquil, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to all-aspect omniscience is tranquil, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to all-aspect omniscience is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is signless, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, is signless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, is unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is non-extinguished, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects is non-extinguished, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“World-Honored One!

True Suchness (tathatā) is neither bound nor liberated; the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-false nature, the unchanging nature, the fixed nature of dharmas, the abiding nature of dharmas, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), and the unconditioned nature (asaṃskṛtatva) are all neither bound nor liberated.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Because the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is non-existent, it is neither bound nor liberated. Because the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, the nature of non-falsity, the nature of immutability, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), and the unconditioned nature (*asaṃskṛtatva*) are all non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of *tathatā* is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to the nature of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of *tathatā* is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to the nature of the unconditioned, is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Because the nature of *tathatā* is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to the nature of the unconditioned, is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is signless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), up to and including the nature of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), is signless, it is neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of *tathatā* is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the nature of the unconditioned, is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of *tathatā* is unborn, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the nature of the unconditioned, is unborn, it is neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is non-extinguishable, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), up to and including the unconditioned nature (*asaṃskṛta*), is non-extinguishable, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of *tathatā* is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the unconditioned nature, is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of *tathatā* is not purified, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the unconditioned nature, is not purified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“World-Honored One!
Awakening is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

"Bhagavān! Because the nature of bodhi is non-existent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is detached, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is quiescent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is empty, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is signless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is unarisen, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is unceasing, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is unstained, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of bodhi is unpurified, it is neither bound nor liberated."
“World-Honored One!
A sattva is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

"Bhagavān! Because the nature of a sattva is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is remote, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is unceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a sattva is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation."
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

“World-Honored One! Because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is unceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is unstained, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.”
“World-Honored One!
Unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
World-Honored One!

Because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-existent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is detached, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is quiescent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is empty, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is signless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is unarisen, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is unceasing, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is undefiled, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is unpurified, it is neither bound nor liberated.
“World-Honored One!
The Unsurpassed Perfectly Complete Enlightenment is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
World-Honored One!

Because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is non-existent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is detached, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is quiescent, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is signless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is unarisen, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is unceasing, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is undefiled, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is unpurified, it is neither bound nor liberated.
“World-Honored One!
To state it briefly, all dharmas are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

“World-Honored One! Because the nature of all dharmas is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is unceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is undefiled, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of all dharmas is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.”
At that time, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra asked Subhūti:
"Venerable sir, do you say that form is neither bound nor liberated? Do you say that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise neither bound nor liberated?"
Subhūti replied: "So it is! So it is!"
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra said:
"What is form that is neither bound nor liberated?
What are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are neither bound nor liberated?"
Subhūti replied:
"Just as illusory form is neither bound nor liberated, so too illusory feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated;
just as dream-like form is neither bound nor liberated, so too dream-like feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated."
Just as the form of a reflected image is neither bound nor liberated, so too are the feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness of a reflected image neither bound nor liberated;
just as the form of an echo is neither bound nor liberated, so too are the feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness of an echo neither bound nor liberated;
just as the form of a shadow is neither bound nor liberated, so too are the feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness of a shadow neither bound nor liberated.
Just as the form of a flower in the sky is neither bound nor liberated, so too are the sensation, perception, formations, and consciousness of a flower in the sky neither bound nor liberated;
just as the form of a mirage is neither bound nor liberated, so too are the sensation, perception, formations, and consciousness of a mirage neither bound nor liberated;
just as the form of a city of Gandharvas is neither bound nor liberated, so too are the sensation, perception, formations, and consciousness of a city of Gandharvas neither bound nor liberated.

Just as the form of a magical transformation is neither bound nor liberated, so too the sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness of a magical transformation are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

Because the nature of illusory form, up to the nature of form as a magical creation, is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of illusory feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as a magical creation, is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of illusory form, up to the nature of form as a magical creation, is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of illusory feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as a magical creation, is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is signless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is signless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is wishless, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is wishless, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is unceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is unceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is unstained, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of form, from that which is like an illusion up to that which is like a magical creation, is not pure, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, from those like an illusion up to those like a magical creation, is not pure, they are neither bound nor liberated.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
Past form is neither bound nor liberated; past feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Future form is neither bound nor liberated; future feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.”
Present form is neither bound nor liberated; present feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this so, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra?

Because the nature of form (*rūpa*) in the past, future, and present is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) in the past, future, and present is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form (*rūpa*) in the past, future, and present is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) in the past, future, and present is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is signless (*animitta*), there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is wishless (*apraṇihita*), there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of form (*rūpa*) in the past, future, and present is unarisen, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) in the past, future, and present are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is undestroyed, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present are undestroyed, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is unstained, it is neither bound nor liberated; because the natures of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present are unstained, they are neither bound nor liberated.

Because the nature of form in the past, future, and present is without purity, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness in the past, future, and present is without purity, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
Wholesome form is neither bound nor liberated; wholesome feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Unwholesome form is neither bound nor liberated; unwholesome feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.”
Indeterminate form is neither bound nor liberated; indeterminate feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? O Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form (*rūpa*) is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) is non-existent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is quiescent, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is non-arising, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is non-arising, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is non-ceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is non-ceasing, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is undefiled, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is undefiled, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate form is without purity, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is without purity, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
There is defilement that is neither bound nor liberated; there is defiled feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are neither bound nor liberated.
There is non-defilement that is neither bound nor liberated; there is non-defiled feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are neither bound nor liberated.”
Tainted form is neither bound nor liberated; tainted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Untainted form is neither bound nor liberated; untainted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Contaminated form is neither bound nor liberated; contaminated feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Uncontaminated form is neither bound nor liberated; uncontaminated feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Defiled form is neither bound nor liberated; defiled feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Pure form is neither bound nor liberated; pure feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Worldly form is neither bound nor liberated; worldly feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Supramundane form is neither bound nor liberated; supramundane feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this so? Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

Because the nature of defiled form, up to the nature of supramundane form, does not exist, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of defiled feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, does not exist, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of afflicted form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of afflicted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is detached, there is neither bondage nor liberation;

because the nature of afflicted form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is tranquil, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of afflicted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is tranquil, there is neither bondage nor liberation;

because the nature of afflicted form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of afflicted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is empty, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of contaminated form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is signless (*animitta*), there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of contaminated feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is signless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of contaminated form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is wishless (*apraṇihita*), there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of contaminated feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is wishless, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of contaminated form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is unarisen (*anutpanna*), there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of contaminated feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is unarisen, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of tainted form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is non-extinguished, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of tainted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is non-extinguished, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of tainted form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is untainted, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of tainted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is untainted, there is neither bondage nor liberation.

Because the nature of tainted form, up to the nature of supramundane form, is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation; because the nature of tainted feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, up to the nature of supramundane feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is unpurified, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

In this way, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated. You should know that it is likewise with the sense-base of the eye up to the sense-base of the mind;
the sense-base of forms up to the sense-base of phenomena; and the eye-element, the form-element, [and so forth].”
The eye-consciousness element and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition;
and so on up to the mind-element, dharma-element, and mind-consciousness element, as well as mind-contact and all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition;
the earth element up to the consciousness element; the noble truth of suffering up to the noble truth of the path; and ignorance up to old age.
Death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
the four dhyānas up to the four formless attainments; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path;
the gates of liberation of emptiness up to the gate of liberation of wishlessness; the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom.
The *pāramitās*, the five eyes, the six supernormal powers, the ten powers of a Buddha, up to all-aspect omniscience;

from suchness up to the unconditioned; the bodhisattva, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and the one who has attained unsurpassed perfect enlightenment—all these phenomena, according to their respective natures.
It is likewise with neither bondage nor liberation.
"Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

Regarding this dharma-gate of neither bondage nor liberation, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should, by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, know it as it truly is: as neither bondage nor liberation."

One should diligently train in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eight branches of the noble path, the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the five eyes, the six superknowledges, the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), employing the method of non-apprehension.
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, should abide in the four dhyānas that are neither bound nor liberated, and so on, up to abiding in the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) that is neither bound nor liberated;

taking non-apprehension as their skillful means, they should bring to maturity sentient beings who are neither bound nor liberated, they should purify buddha-fields that are neither bound nor liberated, they should attend upon and make offerings to Buddhas who are neither bound nor liberated, and they should listen to and receive the Dharma-gates that are neither bound nor liberated.”

“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is never separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who are neither bound nor liberated; he is never separated from the pure five eyes, which are neither bound nor liberated; he is never separated from the sublime six supernormal powers, which are neither bound nor liberated; he is never separated from the doors of dhāraṇī, which are neither bound nor liberated; and he is never separated from the doors of samādhi, which are neither bound nor liberated.”
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva shall give rise to the knowledge of the aspects of the path that is neither bound nor liberated; he shall realize all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects that are neither bound nor liberated; he shall turn the wheel of Dharma that is neither bound nor liberated; and he shall establish all sentient beings within the three vehicles of the Dharma that are neither bound nor liberated.”
“Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās that are neither bound nor liberated, they are able to realize that which is neither bound nor liberated. Because all phenomena are non-existent, because they are remote, because they are quiescent, because they are empty, because they are signless, because they are wishless, because they are unarisen, because they are unceasing, because they are undefiled, and because they are unpurified, they are neither bound nor liberated.”
"Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra!
You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is called one who has donned the armor of the Great Vehicle, which is neither bound nor liberated.
Chapter 15: Distinguishing the Great Vehicle, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How should one know the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
How should one know the setting forth of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva into the Great Vehicle?”
From where does such a Mahāyāna emerge?
To what place does it go and abide?
In what does such a Mahāyāna dwell?
"Who, moreover, shall mount this Great Vehicle and depart?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "You ask:
'How should one know the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?'"
These refer to the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) as the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are the six? They are:

the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*), the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*), the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*), and the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*).
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the perfection of giving of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), with great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), personally bestows all internal and external possessions, and likewise encourages others to bestow all internal and external possessions, and then takes these roots of goodness and dedicates them together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).”
“Subhūti! This is the perfection of giving of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of pure ethical discipline?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva generates the mind directed toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), with great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension, personally abides in the ten paths of wholesome action and also encourages others to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action, and dedicates these roots of goodness together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).”
“Subhūti!
This is the perfection of ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
The Buddha said:

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva generates the mind directed toward omniscience, with great compassion as the foremost, employing the method of non-apprehension, personally perfects superior patience and also encourages others to perfect superior patience, and dedicates these roots of goodness together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment."
“Subhūti! This is the perfection of patience of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s perfection of diligence?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva generates the mind directed toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), with great compassion as the foremost, and employing the method of non-apprehension, personally and unceasingly exerts themselves in the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), and likewise encourages others to unceasingly exert themselves in the six perfections, and dedicates these roots of virtue together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).”
“Subhūti! This is the perfection of diligence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā)?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to the mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, with great compassion as the foremost priority, and by means of the skillful method of non-apprehension, is himself able through skillful means to enter the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*), yet never takes birth under the influence of those states; and furthermore, is able to encourage others to enter the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments with the same skillfulness as himself, and taking these roots of goodness, dedicates them together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).”
"Subhūti! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā).
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to the mind directed toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), with great compassion as the foremost, and by means of the method of non-apprehension, is able to personally observe the nature of all phenomena (dharmatā) as it truly is, remaining without attachment to the nature of any phenomenon; and likewise encourages others to observe the nature of all phenomena as it truly is, remaining without attachment to the nature of any phenomenon; and takes these roots of goodness and, together with all sentient beings, dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).”
"Subhūti! This is the prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti, you should know this!"
This is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. "Furthermore, Subhūti, the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is as follows:

namely, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is internal emptiness?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
‘Internal’ refers to internal phenomena, namely: the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
In this context, the eye is empty of the eye.
Why? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
“Subhūti! This is called internal emptiness.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is external emptiness?
The Buddha said:
"Subhūti! 'External' refers to external phenomena, namely: form, sound, odor, taste, tangible objects, and mental phenomena.
Among these, form is empty of form."
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
Sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Subhūti!
"This is called external emptiness.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is internal-and-external emptiness?
The Buddha said, "Suvīra!"
"Internal and external" refers to internal and external phenomena, namely the six internal bases and the six external bases.
Among these, the six internal bases are empty of the six external bases. Why is this so?
Because it is neither permanent nor subject to destruction, such being its intrinsic nature.
The six external bases are empty of the six internal bases. Why is this?
Because it is neither eternal nor subject to destruction by its very nature,
Subhūti, this is called internal-and-external emptiness (adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā).
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the emptiness of emptiness?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
‘Emptiness’ refers to the emptiness of all phenomena.”
This emptiness is empty by means of the emptiness of emptiness. Why?
Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
"Subhūti! This is what is called 'emptiness of emptiness'.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is great emptiness?
The Buddha said:
"Subhūti! 'Great' refers to the ten directions, namely: east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
Among these, the eastern direction is empty by virtue of the eastern direction."
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.

The south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir are empty by virtue of the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir being empty.
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Subhūti!
"This is called the Great Emptiness.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is the emptiness of the ultimate truth?
The Buddha said, "Sudhana!"
The ultimate truth refers to nirvāṇa.
This ultimate truth is empty of the ultimate truth. Why is this?
Because it is neither eternal nor subject to destruction, its very nature is such.
Subhūti, this is called the emptiness of the ultimate truth (paramārtha-śūnyatā).
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the emptiness of the conditioned?”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti, the conditioned refers to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.”
In this regard, the desire realm is empty of the desire realm.
Why? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
The realm of form and the formless realm are empty of the realm of form and the formless realm.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
"Subhūti! This is called the emptiness of the conditioned.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā)?
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! The unconditioned refers to that which is without arising, without abiding, without alteration, and without cessation.
This unconditioned is empty of the unconditioned.”
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Subhūti!
"This is called the emptiness of the unconditioned.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is ultimate emptiness?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
"Ultimate" refers to the fact that all phenomena are ultimately unapprehendable.
This ultimacy is [empty] by way of ultimate emptiness. Why is this?
Because it is neither eternal nor subject to destruction by its very nature, Subhūti,
this is called ultimate emptiness.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the emptiness of the limitless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā)?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
‘Limitless’ means that no beginning, middle, or end can be apprehended, and no limit of coming or going can be apprehended.”
This "limitless" is empty of the "limitless.
Why? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
"Subhūti! This is called the emptiness of the limitless.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the emptiness of dispersion?
The Buddha said:
"Subhūti! 'Scattering' means that there is releasing, there is discarding, and there is relinquishing to be found.
This scattering is empty by virtue of the emptiness of scattering."
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Subhūti!
"This is the emptiness of dispersion.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
“What, Subhūti, is the emptiness of non-alteration?
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!”
Non-alteration means that no letting go, no discarding, and no relinquishing can be found.
This non-alteration is empty of non-alteration. Why is this?
Because it is neither permanent nor subject to destruction, its very nature is such. Subhūti,
this is called the emptiness of non-alteration.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the emptiness of intrinsic nature?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

‘Intrinsic nature’ refers to the intrinsic nature of all phenomena. Whether it be the nature of conditioned phenomena or the nature of unconditioned phenomena, none is created by śrāvakas, none by pratyekabuddhas, none by bodhisattvas, none by tathāgatas, nor is it created by anyone else.”
This intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature.
Why? Because its intrinsic nature is such that it is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
"Subhūti! This is what is called 'emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the emptiness of self-characteristics?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! ‘Own-characteristic’ refers to the own-characteristics of all phenomena (*dharma*). For example, transformation and resistance are the own-characteristic of form (*rūpa*); experiencing is the own-characteristic of feeling (*vedanā*); grasping signs is the own-characteristic of perception (*saṃjñā*); conditioning is the own-characteristic of formations (*saṃskāra*); and discerning is the own-characteristic of consciousness (*vijñāna*). Such are the own-characteristics of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta-dharma*) and the own-characteristics of unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).”
This intrinsic characteristic is empty of its own intrinsic characteristic. Why?
Because it is neither permanent nor subject to destruction; such is its very nature.
"Subhūti! This is what is called 'emptiness of self-characteristic.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the emptiness of common characteristics?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! ‘Common characteristics’ refers to the common characteristics of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*). For example, suffering is the common characteristic of contaminated phenomena (*sāsravadharma*); impermanence is the common characteristic of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*); emptiness and selflessness are the common characteristics of all phenomena. In this way, there are immeasurable such common characteristics.”
This common characteristic is empty of common characteristics. Why?
Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
"Subhūti! This is called the emptiness of common characteristics.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
in what way are all dharmas empty?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! ‘All phenomena’ refers to the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements—whether they are with form or formless, visible or invisible, resistant or non-resistant, outflowing or non-outflowing, and conditioned or unconditioned phenomena.”
All these phenomena are empty of all phenomena.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
"Subhūti! This is what is meant by the emptiness of all phenomena.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the emptiness of the unobtainable?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! ‘Inapprehensible’ refers to the fact that herein all dharmas are inapprehensible; if they are inapprehensible in the past, they are inapprehensible in the future, and they are inapprehensible in the present.
If they are inapprehensible in the past, there is no future or present that can be apprehended.”
If it is the future, the past and present cannot be apprehended;
if it is the present, the past and future cannot be apprehended.
This non-apprehension is due to the emptiness of non-apprehension.
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Subhūti!
"This is called the emptiness of the unapprehendable.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“What is the emptiness of non-existence?
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
"Non-existence" means that herein not even the slightest existence can be found.
This non-existence is empty of non-existence. Why is this?
Because it is neither eternal nor subject to destruction, its very nature is such.
Subhūti, this is called the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*).
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the emptiness of intrinsic nature?”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti! ‘Intrinsic nature’ refers to that which can bring about the synthesis of the intrinsic natures of all phenomena.”
This intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature. Why?
Because its very nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction.
“Subhūti! This is what is called ‘emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence?
The Buddha said:
"Subhūti! 'The self-nature of non-existence' refers to the fact that all phenomena lack any nature capable of being compounded, yet possess a self-nature as that which is compounded.
This self-nature of non-existence is empty of the self-nature of non-existence."
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Subhūti!
"This is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Existence is empty of existence;
non-existence is empty of non-existence; intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature; and other-nature is empty of other-nature."
What is the emptiness of existence by means of existence?

Existence refers to the five aggregates (*pañcaskandha*). This existence is empty of existence because the nature of arising of the five aggregates cannot be apprehended; this is what is meant by the emptiness of existence by means of existence.
What is the emptiness of non-existence by means of non-existence?
Non-existence refers to the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*); this non-existence is empty of non-existence. This is called the emptiness of non-existence by means of non-existence.
What is the emptiness of intrinsic nature by way of intrinsic nature?

It means that all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature; this emptiness is not produced by wisdom, not produced by views, nor produced by anything else. This is called the emptiness of intrinsic nature by way of intrinsic nature.
What is the emptiness of other-nature by means of other-nature?

It refers to the fact that whether a Buddha appears in the world or does not appear, all phenomena abide as phenomena, are fixed as phenomena, possess the nature of phenomena, the realm of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature of phenomena free from birth, suchness, non-falsity, immutability, and the limit of reality—all these are empty by virtue of other-nature. This is called the emptiness of other-nature by means of other-nature.
Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
what is called the 'Heroic Stride' samādhi?"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

When one abides in this samādhi, one is able to apprehend the objects of all samādhis, accomplish boundless and sublime heroic strides, and serve as the leader of all concentrations; therefore, it is called the ‘Heroic Stride Samādhi.’”
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘jewel-seal samādhi’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen.]”

It is said that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to seal all objects of samādhi as well as the activities performed through the characteristics of meditative concentration; therefore, it is called the Jewel Seal Samādhi (*ratnamudrā-samādhi*).

That is to say, when one abides in this samādhi, one sports with mastery over all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the Lion’s Play Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Exquisite Moon Samādhi’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is as follows:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it universally illumines all meditative concentrations like the pure full moon; therefore, it is called the 'Exquisite Moon Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Moon Banner Mark' (*candradhvajaketu*) samādhi?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally uphold the marks of all meditative concentrations, like the pure full moon hanging down its banner of wondrous light; therefore, it is named the Moon Banner Mark Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Surge of All Dharmas’? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, all samādhis are universally brought forth, like a great spring or pond from which various waters gush out; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of the Gushing Forth of All Dharmas."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the ‘Contemplation of the Summit’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to contemplate the summit of all samādhis; therefore, it is called the 'Contemplation of the Summit' (Mūrdhāvalokana) samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of the Determination of the Dharma-realm'?
"Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one definitively illuminates the entire dharma-realm; therefore, it is named the 'Samādhi of the Determination of the Dharma-realm.'"
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the mark of the banner of certainty? “Excellent One!

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to decisively maintain the characteristic banner of all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of the Decisive Banner Characteristic."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the vajra-like samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it can destroy all other meditative concentrations and cannot itself be overcome by them; therefore, it is called the Vajra-like Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Entering the Seal of Dharmas'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is universally able to realize and enter the seal of all dharmas; therefore, it is called the Samādhi of Entering the Seal of Dharmas."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘King of Samādhis’ samādhi?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one exercises sovereign mastery over all meditative concentrations as a king does; therefore, it is called the "King of Samādhis" samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of ‘well-established’? “Subhūti!
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one maintains all meritorious qualities so that they do not waver; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Excellent Abiding.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of the Well-Established King of Concentrations'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is well able to establish oneself among all the kings of concentration; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of the Well-Established King of Concentrations'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Radiant Light Samādhi’? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally illuminate all the lights of meditative concentration; therefore, it is called the 'Emission of Light' Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'samādhi of non-forgetfulness'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to remember all the objective spheres and modes of activity of all samādhis without any omission; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi of non-forgetfulness'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Emitting Light Without Forgetfulness’?
“Excellent One!”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one emits the light of supreme concentration to illuminate sentient beings, causing them to remember and retain events they have previously experienced; therefore, it is called the "Light-Emitting Non-Forgetfulness Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the power of diligence?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to generate the power of diligence for all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of the Power of Diligence.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Adornment Power' samādhi?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one can bring forth the power of adornment for all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is named the 'Adornment Power' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Equal Surging’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all samādhis emerge in equal measure; therefore, it is called the 'Equal Emergence' (Samatābhyudgata) Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called 'the samādhi of entering the certainty of all verbal expressions'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally penetrate and enter into all certain verbal expressions; therefore, it is called 'the samādhi of entering the certainty of all verbal expressions.'"
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘entry into the determination of all names’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to universally penetrate all definitive names; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of entering the definitiveness of all names."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of observing the directions?
“Excellent One!”
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to universally observe all directions of meditative concentration; therefore, it is called the 'Observation of Directions' Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Seal of Retention' (dhāraṇīmudrā) samādhi?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to maintain and uphold all seals of sublime concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Seal of Retention' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called ‘the samādhi of the ocean seal that all dharmas equally enter’? “Subhūti!

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all supreme concentrations and so forth are caused to enter therein, just as the ocean seal receives and contains all flowing streams; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of the Ocean Seal into Which All Dharmas Equally Enter."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the King’s Seal Samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all undertakings become certain; like obtaining a royal seal, whatever one desires is accomplished. Therefore, it is called the Royal Seal Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Pervading and Covering Space’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it is able to universally cover and protect all other samādhis, without any discrimination, just like great empty space; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi that Universally Covers Empty Space."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the Vajracakra Samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[It is as follows:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is universally able to sustain all supreme concentrations so that they do not disintegrate, like a vajra-wheel; therefore, it is named the Vajra-Wheel Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the purity of the three wheels?
“Excellent One!

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not grasp at the meditative absorptions, the meditator, or the objects of meditation; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of the Purity of the Three Spheres."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Immeasurable Light’?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it emits various kinds of light in quantities beyond measure; therefore, it is called the 'Immeasurable Light Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'unattached and unobstructed samādhi'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, there is no grasping and no hindrance regarding all phenomena; therefore, it is called the 'unattached and unobstructed samādhi'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘the severing of the turning of all dharmas’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to sever all phenomena of cyclic existence; therefore, it is named the "samādhi that cuts off the turning of all phenomena."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of relinquishing precious jewels’?
“Suvīra! [Listen.]”

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one discards even all the characteristics of meditative concentrations, let alone failing to discard the characteristics of the afflictions; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Discarding Precious Jewels."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Universal Illumination’?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it universally illuminates all meditative concentrations, causing them to shine forth; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Universal Illumination.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Unblinking Samādhi' (*animiṣa-samādhi*)?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, the mind is single-pointed within this meditative concentration (*samādhi*), without grasping for or seeking after other concentrations or other dharmas; therefore, it is called the Unblinking Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of dwelling in the signless?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not perceive even the slightest characteristic of any dharmas of meditative concentration in which to abide; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of dwelling in the signless."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of non-mental-conception’? “Excellent One!
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, no mind or mental factors arise; therefore, it is called the 'Non-Conceptualizing Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi that Subdues the Four Māras'?
"Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to subdue all four māra-enemies; therefore, it is named the 'Samādhi that Subdues the Four Māras'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Stainless Lamp Samādhi’?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it is like holding a pure lamp that illuminates all concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Stainless Lamp Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Infinite Light Samādhi'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one can emit a great light that illuminates infinite boundaries; therefore, it is called the 'Infinite Light Samādhi'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Radiant Samādhi’?
“Excellent One!”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, it illuminates all meditative concentrations (samādhis) so that they become uninterrupted, thereby eliciting various kinds of sublime radiance; therefore, it is called the "Radiant" (Prabhākara) Samādhi.

"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally illumine all gateways of meditative concentration; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Universal Illumination.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'samādhi of pure firmness'?
"Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one attains the pure equality of all samādhis; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi of pure firmness'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Lion’s Sport Samādhi’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”

It is said that when one dwells in this samādhi, one casts off all defilements with ease and spontaneity, like a lion king leaping with sovereign power; therefore, it is called the Lion’s Leap Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Lion’s Yawn’ samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one gives rise to supreme supernormal powers, mastery, and fearlessness, thereby subduing all violent and malevolent māra armies; therefore, it is called the Lion’s Yawn Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Lion’s Yawn Samādhi’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one draws forth sublime eloquence and remains fearless in the midst of the assembly, crushing and destroying all the false tenets of external paths; therefore, it is called the Lion’s Yawn Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Stainless Light Samādhi’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally eliminate all defilements of meditative concentration and can also universally illumine all supreme samādhis; therefore, it is called the "Stainless Light Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Sublime Joy’? “Excellent One!
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one experiences the sublime bliss of all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Sublime Bliss Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Lightning Lamp' samādhi?
Subhūti, it is when, while abiding in this samādhi, one illuminates all meditative concentrations like the flame of a lightning lamp; therefore, it is called the 'Lightning Lamp' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Inexhaustible Samādhi’? “Sudhana!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one brings forth the inexhaustible merits of all samādhis, yet does not perceive any sign of exhaustion or non-exhaustion; therefore, it is named the Inexhaustible Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Mark of the Supreme Banner’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen.]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it surpasses the characteristics of all other meditative concentrations like a most excellent banner; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of the Most Excellent Banner Characteristic."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Imperial Sign Samādhi’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one attains the characteristic of mastery over all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Imperial Mark' (Kauśalya) Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the samādhi that accords with the flow of clear illumination?

Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one accords with and follows along with clear illumination and the correct flow; therefore, it is named the samādhi that accords with the flow of clear illumination."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of possessing majestic radiance? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, its majestic radiance alone is most preeminent among all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi Endowed with Majestic Radiance.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the samādhi of being free from exhaustion?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives all samādhis as entirely inexhaustible, yet does not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristic of being exhausted or inexhaustible; therefore, it is called the samādhi of being free from exhaustion."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘immovable samādhi’? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations to be unmoving, unattached, non-retrogressive, and free from conceptual proliferation; therefore, it is called the "Unshakeable Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of tranquility?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives all meditative absorptions as tranquil; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Tranquility.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Flawless' samādhi?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations to illuminate without flaw; therefore, it is named the 'Flawless' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Sun-Lamp Samādhi’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, light is emitted from all gateways of concentration and shines everywhere; therefore, it is called the 'Sun-Lamp Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Pure Moon' samādhi?
Subhūti, it is said that when one dwells in this samādhi, it dispels the darkness of all meditative concentrations like the moon; therefore, it is named the 'Pure Moon' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Pure Eye’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it enables all five eyes to become completely pure; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of the Pure Eye.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Pure Light'?

Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one attains the four kinds of unimpeded knowledge regarding all meditative concentrations, and causes those concentrations to be fully activated; therefore, it is named the Samādhi of Pure Light."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the Moon-Lamp Samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it dispels the ignorance and darkness of all sentient beings like the moon; therefore, it is called the Moon Lamp Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
"What is called the 'Illumination-Producing' samādhi?

Subhūti, it is when, while abiding in this samādhi, one causes the gateways of all concentrations to produce illumination and shine everywhere; therefore, it is named the 'Illumination-Producing' samādhi."
