It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one knows which meditative concentrations (samādhis) should be practiced and which should not, and also causes all concentrations to accomplish their respective tasks accordingly; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of What Should and Should Not Be Done."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the characteristics of wisdom?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives all the marks of wisdom belonging to all samādhis; therefore, it is called the 'Wisdom-Mark Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Vajramālā Samādhi'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one penetrates all meditative concentrations and all phenomena, yet perceives neither the concentration nor the phenomena at all; therefore, it is named the Vajramālā Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of abiding mind?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, the mind does not waver, does not turn, does not illuminate, nor is it diminished; one does not even think of the existence of a mind. Therefore, it is called the "samādhi of dwelling in the mind."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the Samādhi of Universal Radiance?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to universally illuminate and clearly perceive all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is named the Samādhi of Universal Illumination.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Excellent Establishment' (Suvyavasthita-samādhi)?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to excellently establish all other samādhis; therefore, it is named the Samādhi of Excellent Establishment."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the Jewel-Heap Samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one sees all meditative absorptions as being like a heap of jewels; therefore, it is called the Jewel-Heap Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of the Seal of the Sublime Dharma' (*saddharmamudrā-samādhi*)?

"Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to seal all meditative concentrations (*samādhi*), because it seals them with the seal of non-sealing; therefore, it is called the Samādhi of the Seal of the Sublime Dharma."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the equality of all phenomena?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Tathāgata says:]”
This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not perceive any phenomenon apart from the nature of equality; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of the equality of all phenomena."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Abandoning Attachment to Dust’?
“Excellent One!
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one abandons attachment to the dust of all meditative states; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of abandoning attachment to the dust."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of the perfect outpouring of the Dharma’? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”
It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all the Buddha-dharmas surge forth and become perfectly complete; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of the Perfect Surge of Dharmas."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of entering the summit of the Dharma?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one can forever extinguish the darkness of all phenomena and transcend all meditative concentrations to become their preeminent leader; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Entering the Pinnacle of Dharmas."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘jewel-nature samādhi’?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one can produce boundless great jewels of merit; therefore, it is called the Jewel-Nature Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Abandoning Quarrels and Strife'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one abandons all the various quarrels and strife of the world; therefore, it is named the 'Samādhi of Abandoning Quarrels and Strife'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘dispersing’ samādhi? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all clinging to dharmas within all other samādhis is dispersed; therefore, it is called the 'Dispersing Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Discerning the Phrases of Dharma' (*dharmapadavibhakti-samādhi*)?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is well able to discern the phrases of all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is named the Samādhi of Discerning the Phrases of Dharma."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Certainty’?
“Excellent One!”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one attains certainty regarding the dhāraṇīs of all phenomena; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Certainty.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Stainless Conduct' samādhi?
Subhūti, it is when, while abiding in this samādhi, one can give rise to boundless, pure, and sublime practices; therefore, it is called the 'Stainless Conduct' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the equal characteristic of syllables?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one attains the mark of equality of the syllables of all samādhis; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of the Mark of Equality of Syllables."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of being free from the marks of words?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, not a single syllable can be apprehended within any of the meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of being free from the marks of letters."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi that severs the object of focus?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, all signs of the objects of focus of various meditative concentrations are severed; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi that severs the object of focus.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'unchanging samādhi'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not perceive the characteristics of change in any phenomena; therefore, it is called the unchanging samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi without categories’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not perceive the distinct characteristics of the various categories of phenomena; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi Without Categories.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Entering Names and Characteristics'?

Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one realizes and enters the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) regarding the names and characteristics of all phenomena; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Entering Names and Characteristics'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of non-action’?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, all activities whatsoever are entirely stilled; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi of non-action.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'samādhi of entering into definitive names'?

Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one realizes that the definitive names of all phenomena are entirely non-existent and are merely conventional designations; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi of entering into definitive names'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of signless practice? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives no signs whatsoever in any meditative absorptions; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Signless Practice.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'samādhi free from cataracts and darkness'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all cataracts and darkness within the various concentrations are eliminated without exception; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi free from cataracts and darkness.'"
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of ‘endowed with practice’?
“Excellent One!
It is said that when one dwells in this samādhi, although one sees within all meditative practices, one does not see them; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi Endowed with Practice."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘unwavering samādhi’?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one perceives no fluctuation in any of the meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Unwavering Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi that Transcends Objects'?
Subhūti, it means that when one abides in this samādhi, one transcends the objective spheres of all other meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi that Transcends Objects'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi that gathers all merits’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to gather all the merits of every meditative concentration, yet regarding all phenomena, there is no perception of gathering; therefore, it is called the "samādhi that gathers all merits."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the concentration of dwelling without mind?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, the mind neither shifts nor falls away from any meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi of dwelling without mind.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the samādhi of 'residing in certainty' (*niyatavihāra*)?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, although the mind remains certain within all meditative concentrations, one knows that its characteristics are utterly unapprehendable; therefore, it is called the samādhi of 'residing in certainty.'"
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Pure and Wondrous Flower’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations (samādhis) to become pure, adorned and radiant like exquisite flowers; therefore, it is called the "Pure Exquisite Flower Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi endowed with the factors of enlightenment?
“Excellent One!

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations to swiftly attain perfection in the seven factors of enlightenment; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi Endowed with the Factors of Enlightenment."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of boundless eloquence?
“Excellent One!
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one attains boundless eloquence regarding all phenomena; therefore, it is called the 'Boundless Eloquence Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Infinite Lamp' samādhi?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to illuminate and comprehend all phenomena as clearly as a bright lamp; therefore, it is called the 'Infinite Lamp' samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Unequaled’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations (samādhis) to become unequaled with the unequaled; therefore, it is named the "Unequaled-with-the-Unequaled" (Asamasama) Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi that Transcends All Phenomena'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to transcend all phenomena within the three realms; therefore, it is named the 'Samādhi that Transcends All Phenomena'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of definitive discernment of all dharmas?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives all supreme concentrations and all phenomena as being non-confused through discernment for the sake of all sentient beings; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Decisively Determining All Phenomena."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Dispelling Doubts’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, all nets of doubt regarding all meditative concentrations and all phenomena are able to be dispersed; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi that Dispels Doubt."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of non-abiding’?
“Excellent One! [Listen.]”
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not perceive any place where phenomena abide; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Non-abiding.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi Adorned with a Single Characteristic'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not perceive any phenomena as having two characteristics; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi Adorned with a Single Characteristic'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the aspect of elicitation?
“Excellent One!

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, although one can manifest various modes of activity regarding all meditative concentrations and all phenomena, one does not perceive at all any agent who manifests them; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of manifesting modes of activity."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the single mode?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives all meditative absorptions as having a non-dual mode of activity; therefore, it is called the 'Single Mode of Activity Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'samādhi free from all signs of conditioned activity' (*sarvasaṃskāranimittavivarjita-samādhi*)?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives that all meditative absorptions (*samādhi*) are entirely devoid of signs of conditioned activity; therefore, it is called the 'samādhi free from all signs of conditioned activity.'"
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of sublime conduct’?
“Excellent One!

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, although various subtle and sublime practices are performed within all meditative concentrations, there is no grasping; therefore, it is called the "Sublime Practice" (Caryā) Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of penetrating the depths of all existences and remaining far removed from them’?
“Excellent One! [The Buddha replied:]

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one attains the wisdom of thorough penetration regarding all meditative concentrations and all phenomena. Having attained this wisdom, one thoroughly penetrates the state of detachment from all existing phenomena; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of penetrating the depths of existence and detachment."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Entry into All Designations and Linguistic Expressions’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one penetrates all dharmas of samādhi and employs conventional designations and language without relying upon them; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of entering all conventional designations and language."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Firm Jewel’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, it can draw forth boundless, non-retrogressive, and indestructible jewels of subtle, excellent, and sublime merit; therefore, it is named the "Firm Jewel Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of non-attachment to all phenomena?
“Excellent One!

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, there is no grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, because all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature and characteristics; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of non-attachment toward all phenomena."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi Adorned with Lightning Flashes’?
“Excellent One! [Listen.]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, various kinds of light are emitted to illuminate all darkness, and it is further adorned with immeasurable merit; therefore, it is called the "Lightning-Flame Adornment Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi of elimination’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one eliminates the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of boundless afflictions; therefore, it is called the 'Elimination Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Dharma-torch Samādhi'?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one illuminates and realizes the specific and general characteristics of all phenomena; therefore, it is called the Dharma-torch Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Lamp of Wisdom’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one illuminates and realizes the principle that all phenomena are empty and without self; therefore, it is called the 'Wisdom Lamp' Samādhi.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is called the samādhi that proceeds toward non-retrogressive supernormal powers?
Subhūti, it is this:

when one dwells in this samādhi, one can bring forth immeasurable, non-retrogressive, and invincible supreme supernormal powers; therefore, it is called the samādhi that proceeds toward non-retrogressive supernormal powers."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of liberation from sounds, words, and letters? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one perceives all meditative concentrations as being liberated from all sounds, words, and signs, which are entirely tranquil; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Liberation from Sounds and Words."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Blazing Torch Samādhi’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, its majestic power alone is preeminent among all meditative concentrations; it illuminates all states of concentration like a blazing torch. Therefore, it is called the "Blazing Torch Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the purified and adorned marks? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one purifies the characteristics of all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Purifying Characteristics.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the signless samādhi?
Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not perceive any signs within any meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the signless samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the mark of unpolluted patience?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one attains the patience free from turbidity regarding all phenomena; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of the mark of patience free from turbidity."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Endowed with All Sublime Marks’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all the sublime characteristics of meditative concentrations are fully possessed; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi Possessing All Sublime Characteristics."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi endowed with dhāraṇī?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is as follows:]”

"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally sustain the superior qualities of all meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi Endowed with Universal Retention' (Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha-samādhi).
World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of Not Delighting in Any Suffering or Pleasure'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not delight in observing the characteristics of suffering or pleasure within any meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of Not Delighting in Any Suffering or Pleasure'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the aspect of inexhaustible practice?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not perceive any exhaustion in the characteristics of the various meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Exhaustless Characteristics."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi that subdues all correct and erroneous natures? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, regarding the correctness or incorrectness of all meditative concentrations, it subdues all views so that they do not arise; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi that Subdues All Correct and Incorrect Natures."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi that severs hatred and attachment’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

This means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not perceive any signs of aversion or attachment toward the dharmas of concentration; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Severing Aversion and Attachment."

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not perceive any signs of opposition or conformity among the various dharmas of concentration; therefore, it is called the "samādhi free from opposition and conformity."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘stainless radiance samādhi’?
“Excellent One! [Listen.]”
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one perceives neither clarity nor defilement in any meditative concentrations; therefore, it is called the "Stainless Clarity Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Extremely Firm Samādhi’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen.]”
"It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations (samādhis) to be without exception firm; therefore, it is called the 'Extremely Firm Samādhi.
" "World-Honored One!"
"What is called the 'Samādhi of the Pure Light of the Full Moon'?

Subhūti, it means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations to be fully endowed with merit, just as the pure full moon increases the waters of the great ocean; therefore, it is called the 'Samādhi of the Pure Light of the Full Moon'."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Great Adornment Samādhi’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations to accomplish various subtle, marvelous, and great matters of adornment; therefore, it is named the Great Adornment Samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Heatless Lightning Flash’ samādhi?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it emits pure and cool light that illuminates sentient beings, causing all darkness, poison, and heat to subside; therefore, it is named the "Heatless Lightning-Light Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi that can illuminate all worlds?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, it illuminates all meditative concentrations and all phenomena, causing all classes of sentient beings to attain clear understanding; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi Capable of Illuminating All Worlds."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi that Rescues All Worlds’?
“Excellent One!
It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to rescue the world from its various sorrows and sufferings; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi That Rescues All Worlds."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the equality of concentration?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]”
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one does not perceive any distinction between concentration and distraction; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of the equality of concentration."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of the principle of equality between the dustless and that which has dust? “Subhūti!

This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one thoroughly realizes the principle of equality regarding whether all meditative concentrations and all phenomena possess objects or are devoid of objects; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of the Principle of Equality of Being Devoid of Objects and Possessing Objects."
“Bhagavān, what is the samādhi called ‘the principle of equality between the non-contentious and the contentious’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

That is to say, when one dwells in this samādhi, one does not perceive any distinction between the characteristics of contention or non-contention in all phenomena or in any meditative concentration; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of the Principle of Equality Between Non-Contention and Contention."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘samādhi without a nest, without signs, and without attachment’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one destroys all nests, abandons all banners and signs, and severs all attachments and delights without any grasping; therefore, it is called the "nestless, signless, and delightless samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of being definitively established in suchness?
“Excellent One!

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one never abandons the true mark of suchness regarding all meditative concentrations and all phenomena; therefore, it is called the "samādhi of definitive abiding in suchness."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Emerging from within a Vessel’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, it causes all meditative concentrations to produce meritorious qualities, just as food surges from within a vessel through the power of celestial merit; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of What Surges Forth from Within a Vessel."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi that burns away all afflictions?
“Excellent One!
It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, all afflictions are incinerated until not even a trace of ash remains; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi that Incinerates All Afflictions."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of the Great Wisdom Torch’?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
That is to say, when one dwells in this samādhi, one emits the light of wisdom that illuminates all things; therefore, it is called the "Great Wisdom Torch Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi that gives birth to the ten powers? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”
This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, the ten powers of a Buddha are swiftly brought to full perfection; therefore, it is called the "Samādhi of Producing the Ten Powers."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘Samādhi of Elucidation’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

It means that when one abides in this samādhi, one is able to expound the essential points of the Dharma for sentient beings, causing them to swiftly attain liberation from the great suffering of birth and death; therefore, it is named the "Expounding Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi ‘Destruction of Evil Conduct of the Body’?
“Excellent One! [The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”
This means that when one dwells in this samādhi, although no body is perceived, one ceases bodily misconduct; therefore, it is called the "samādhi that destroys bodily misconduct."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of destroying speech and evil conduct?
“Excellent One!
It means that when one abides in this samādhi, although no sound is perceived, verbal misconduct is stilled; therefore, it is called the "samādhi that destroys verbal misconduct."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi that destroys mental misconduct?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is as follows:]”
It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, although no mind is perceived, the mental misconduct is stilled; therefore, it is called the "samādhi that destroys mental misconduct."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the samādhi of skillful observation?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

It is said that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to skillfully observe the faculties, natures, and inclinations of all sentient beings and deliver them; therefore, it is named the "Samādhi of Skillful Observation."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘space-like samādhi’? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Tathāgata says:]”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one is able to universally benefit all sentient beings, and the mind is as impartial as great empty space; therefore, it is named the "Space-like Samādhi."
“World-Honored One!
What is called the ‘space-like samādhi of non-attachment’? “Excellent One!
[The Buddha replied: “Excellent One!”

It means that when one dwells in this samādhi, one contemplates that all phenomena are entirely non-existent, like space—untainted and unattached; therefore, it is called the "Space-like Untainted and Unattached Samādhi."
“Subhūti! Such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of samādhis should be known as the marks of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
The characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva refers to the four foundations of mindfulness.
What are the four? They are:
the foundation of mindfulness of the body, the foundation of mindfulness of feelings, the foundation of mindfulness of the mind, and the foundation of mindfulness of phenomena.

"Subhūti! Regarding the application of mindfulness to the body: when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they take non-apprehension as their means; although they abide in the contemplation of the body within the internal body, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with the body. They exert fervent diligence, possessing mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they take non-apprehension as their means; although they abide in the contemplation of the body within the external body, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with the body. They exert fervent diligence, possessing mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow."

When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they employ the method of non-apprehension; although they abide in the contemplation of the body with respect to the internal and external body, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with the body. With ardent diligence, mindfulness, and clear comprehension, they act for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Subhūti! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s application of mindfulness to the body. Subhūti!"

Regarding the foundation of mindfulness of feelings (*vedanā-smṛtyupasthāna*): when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), using the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as their skillful means, although they dwell observing feelings internally, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with feeling; they exert fervent diligence, possessing mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, using the method of non-apprehension as their skillful means, although they dwell observing feelings externally, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with feeling; they exert fervent diligence, possessing mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they employ the method of non-apprehension; although they dwell observing feelings internally and externally, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with feeling. With ardent diligence, mindfulness, and clear comprehension, they act for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Subhūti! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s application of mindfulness to feelings. Subhūti!"

Regarding the application of mindfulness to the mind: when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, although they abide in the internal mind observing the mind, they ultimately do not give rise to mental discursive thoughts; with ardent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, it is for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, although they abide in the external mind observing the mind, they ultimately do not give rise to mental discursive thoughts; with ardent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, it is for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they employ the method of non-apprehension; although they dwell in the contemplation of the mind by following the mind internally and externally, they ultimately do not give rise to any mental discursive thoughts. With ardent diligence, mindfulness, and clear comprehension, they act for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Subhūti! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s application of mindfulness to the mind. Subhūti!"

Regarding the application of mindfulness to phenomena (*dharmasmṛtyupasthāna*): when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), although they abide in the contemplation of phenomena regarding internal phenomena, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with those phenomena; they exert fervent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, in order to subdue worldly greed and sorrow.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, although they abide in the contemplation of phenomena regarding external phenomena, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with those phenomena; they exert fervent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, in order to subdue worldly greed and sorrow.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they employ the method of non-apprehension; although they abide in the contemplation of phenomena regarding internal and external dharmas, they ultimately do not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with those dharmas. Blazing with diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, they do so for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Subhūti! This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s application of mindfulness to phenomena (*dharmasmṛtyupasthāna*).
*The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 52.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 53.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One: Chapter Fifteen on Distinguishing the Mahāyāna, Section Three.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva,

when practicing the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, abide in the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena— both internally and externally— and practice the contemplation of the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena, with ardent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, taking non-apprehension as the means, they carefully observe their own body: when walking, they know they are walking; when standing, they know they are standing; when sitting, they know they are sitting; and when lying down, they know they are lying down. In whatever way there are differences in the deportments of their own body, in that very way they possess mindfulness and clear comprehension.”
"Subhūti!

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in diligence, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, taking non-apprehension as the means, they carefully observe their own body: they are clearly aware of coming and going; clearly aware of looking ahead and looking aside; clearly aware of bending and stretching; clearly aware of wearing the saṃghāṭī robe, holding the outer robe and the alms bowl, and consuming food and drink; clearly aware of lying down and resting, walking up and down, sitting and rising, receiving guests, waking and sleeping, speaking and remaining silent, and entering and emerging from various meditative concentrations—all with mindfulness and clear awareness."
"Subhūti!

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in vigor, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they carefully observe their own body: when breathing in, they truly know as it is that they are breathing in; when breathing out, they truly know as it is that they are breathing out;
when the inhalation is long, they truly know as it is that the inhalation is long; when the exhalation is long, they truly know as it is that the exhalation is long."
When the inhalation is short, he knows as it truly is, "the inhalation is short"; when the exhalation is short, he knows as it truly is, "the exhalation is short.

It is like a wheelwright or his apprentice, who, when the momentum of the wheel is long, knows as it truly is, "the momentum of the wheel is long," and when the momentum of the wheel is short, knows as it truly is, "the momentum of the wheel is short."

When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they take non-apprehension as their skillful means; they carefully observe whether their own inhalations and exhalations are long or short, and they likewise know them as they truly are through mindfulness.
"Subhūti!

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells contemplating the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in energy, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the purpose of subduing worldly greed and sorrow."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, they carefully observe their own body and, in accordance with reality, mindfully know the distinctions between the four elements: namely, the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the wind element."

Just as a skilled butcher or his apprentice, having taken the life of an ox, uses a sharp knife to analyze its body and dissect it into four parts, whether sitting or standing, observes and knows them as they truly are.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they use non-apprehension as their skillful means to examine their own bodies; they likewise contemplate and know, in accordance with reality, the distinctions between the four elements of earth, water, fire, and wind in this same manner.
"Subhūti!

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, with ardent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they carefully contemplate their own body, knowing it as it truly is: from the feet to the crown of the head, it is filled with various kinds of impurities, externally enveloped by a thin skin. That is to say, there are only hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, blood, sinews, veins, bones, and marrow; heart, liver, lungs, kidneys, spleen, gallbladder, bladder, stomach, large intestine, small intestine, excrement, urine, nasal mucus, saliva, spittle, tears, filth, sweat, phlegm, pus, fat, lymph, brain, membranes, and spinal cord—thus the body is filled with such impurities."

It is like a farmer or a householder whose granary is filled to the brim with various kinds of grain—namely rice, hemp, millet, beans, wheat, and so forth—and when one with clear vision opens the granary and looks within, they know exactly as it is that there are only these various grains such as rice, hemp, and millet.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they employ the skillful means of non-apprehension to scrutinize their own bodies. From the soles of the feet to the crown of the head, they contemplate them as they truly are, realizing that they are likewise filled with various impure and foul substances. What wise person would cherish or play with such a body?
"It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent, energetic, mindful, and clearly comprehending, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground and observes a discarded corpse that has been dead for one day, or two days, up to seven days; its body is bloated, its color has turned bluish-black, it is putrid and rotting with the skin pierced, and pus and blood are flowing out."

Having seen this, he reflects: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish and play with this body?"
It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells contemplating the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in energy, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they go to a charnel ground to observe discarded corpses that have been dead for one day, or two days, or even up to seven days, being pecked at or clawed by various birds and beasts—such as vultures, eagles, crows, magpies, hawks, owls, tigers, leopards, foxes, wolves, jackals, and dogs—as their flesh and bones lie in disarray, being torn apart and devoured."

Having seen this, he reflects to himself: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such characteristics; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What person of wisdom would cherish or play with this body?"
It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells contemplating the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent, energetic, mindful, and clearly comprehending, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground and observes a discarded corpse that has been devoured by birds and beasts; it is impure and putrid, with pus and blood flowing out and countless kinds of maggots emerging from it, its foul stench being more loathsome than that of a dead dog."

Having seen this, one reflects: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish or play with this body?"
It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in energy, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground to observe a discarded corpse: its flesh has been devoured by worms and maggots until the bones are exposed; the limbs and joints remain connected, bound together by sinews and smeared with blood, with only putrid flesh remaining."

Having seen this, he reflects to himself: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish and play with this body?"
It is only the deluded and confused fools who are attached to it!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent and resolute, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground and observes a discarded corpse that has become a skeleton, with all flesh and blood gone, remaining only as bones connected by sinews.

Having seen this, he reflects to himself: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish or play with this body?"
It is only the deluded and mistaken fools who are attached to it!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in vigor, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the purpose of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they go to a charnel ground and observe a discarded corpse that remains as nothing but a skeleton; its color is as white as snow, a conch shell, or a pearl oyster, with all tendons rotted away and the joints separated."

Having seen this, he reflects: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish and play with this body?"
It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent, energetic, mindful, and clearly comprehending, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground and observes a discarded corpse that has become bleached white bones, with the limbs and joints scattered and fallen apart in various directions—namely, the bones of the feet, the calves, the knees, the thighs, the hips, the spine, the ribs, the chest, the shoulders, the upper arms, the hands, the neck, the jaw, the cheeks, and the skull, each lying in a different place."

Having seen this, he reflects: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish and play with this body?"
It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells contemplating the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent, with clear mindfulness and situational awareness, for the purpose of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground and observes discarded corpses: their bones scattered in disarray, blown by the wind, bleached by the sun, drenched by rain, and encrusted by frost for many years, until they have become the color of white jade or snow."

Having seen this, he reflects to himself: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish or play with this body?"
It is only the deluded and mistaken foolish worldlings who are attached to them!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells observing the body within the body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent and resolute, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, he goes to a charnel ground and observes discarded corpses. After many hundreds or many thousands of years, the remaining bones are scattered upon the earth; their appearance has turned bluish, resembling the color of a pigeon, or they have become rotten and crumbled into dust, so mixed with the soil that they can no longer be distinguished."

Having seen this, he reflects to himself: "My own body possesses such a nature and is endowed with such qualities; until liberation is attained, it will ultimately end in this way. What wise person would cherish and dally with this body?"
It is only the foolish who are deluded and attached!

Subhūti, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells contemplating the body in the internal body by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, ardent in vigor, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow.
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do so by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method.

Just as they dwell observing the body internally with its various distinctions—ardently diligent, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow—they likewise dwell observing the body externally, and they dwell observing the body both internally and externally, ardently diligent, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension, for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow; it is also thus according to what is appropriate.”

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they take non-apprehension as their skillful means. They dwell in the contemplation of feelings, mind, and phenomena—both internally, externally, and both together—with regard to feelings, mind, and phenomena. With ardent diligence, endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, they do so for the sake of subduing worldly greed and sorrow; all of this should be explained in detail according to what is appropriate.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they abide in the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena—both internally and externally—and when they contemplate the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena, although they perform this contemplation, there is nothing to be apprehended.”
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the four right endeavors.
What are these four? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they generate desire, exert effort, arouse right diligence, and apply themselves with mental uplift and mental sustenance so that unarisen evil and unwholesome states do not arise; this is the first [basis of power].

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they generate desire, exert effort, arouse right diligence, and apply themselves with mental exertion and mental sustenance for the sake of permanently abandoning all evil and unwholesome states that have already arisen; this is the second [basis of power].

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they generate desire, exert effort, arouse right diligence, and apply themselves with resolve and sustainment of the mind, in order to bring about the arising of wholesome dharmas that have not yet arisen; this is the third [basis of power].

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they generate the desire, exert themselves, arouse right effort, and apply themselves with mental exertion and mental maintenance, so that already arisen wholesome dharmas may remain stable, not be forgotten, and be further increased, expanded, repeatedly cultivated, and brought to fulfillment; this is the fourth [basis of power].
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti:"
The characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas refer to the four bases of supernormal power (*ṛddhipāda*).
What are these four? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they cultivate the basis for supernatural power consisting of concentration on desire and the volitional formations of abandonment; this is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment—this is the first.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they cultivate the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration through exertion and the accomplishment of the formative forces of abandonment; relying on seclusion, relying on dispassion, relying on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment—this is the second.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they cultivate the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration of mind and the volitional formations of abandonment; relying on seclusion, relying on dispassion, relying on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment—this is the third.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they cultivate the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration through the cultivation of insight and the accomplishment of the formations of abandonment; relying on seclusion, relying on dispassion, relying on cessation, and resulting in relinquishment—this is the fourth.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the five faculties.
What are these five? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the faculty of faith, the faculty of diligence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the five powers.
What are these five? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the power of faith, the power of diligence, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, and the power of wisdom by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the seven factors of enlightenment.
What are these seven? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of the method of non-apprehension, they cultivate the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of phenomena, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquility, the awakening factor of concentration, and the awakening factor of equanimity; these are based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and result in relinquishment.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the eightfold noble path.
What are these eight? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they cultivate right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration; these are based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and dedicated to relinquishment.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Subhūti, the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the three samādhis.
What are these three? Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, they contemplate all phenomena as empty of their own specific characteristics; with the mind thus dwelling in peace, this is called the gate of liberation of emptiness and is also called the samādhi of emptiness—this is the first.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they contemplate all phenomena as being without marks because their specific characteristics are empty; with the mind thus dwelling in peace, this is called the liberation door of signlessness and is also called the samādhi of signlessness. This is the second.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of the skillful method of non-apprehension, they observe that all phenomena are empty of their own characteristics and thus have no object of aspiration; their mind abides in peace, which is called the door of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*), and is also called the samādhi of wishlessness. This is the third.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

The characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva are as follows: namely, the knowledge of phenomena (dharma-jñāna), subsequent knowledge (anvaya-jñāna), conventional knowledge (saṃvṛti-jñāna), knowledge of others' minds (paracitta-jñāna), knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-jñāna), knowledge of the origin (samudaya-jñāna), knowledge of cessation (nirodha-jñāna), knowledge of the path (mārga-jñāna), knowledge of exhaustion (kṣaya-jñāna), knowledge of non-arising (anutpāda-jñāna), and knowledge of reality as it is (yathābhūta-jñāna). These are the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
what is the knowledge of phenomena (dharmajñāna)?"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as its skillful method, knows the turning of the differentiated characteristics of the five aggregates and so forth, this is called dharma-knowledge.”
“World-Honored One!
What is subsequent knowledge? “Excellent One!

If wisdom takes non-apprehension as its skillful means and knows that the aggregates, elements, bases, and all dependent originations—whether collectively or individually—are impermanent and so forth, this is called subsequent knowledge (*anvaya-jñāna*).
“World-Honored One!
What is conventional knowledge?
“Excellent One!”
"If wisdom takes non-apprehension as its skillful means and knows that all phenomena are merely provisional designations, this is conventional knowledge.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is the knowledge of others' minds?

" 'Subhūti, it is that wisdom which, by means of non-apprehension as its skillful method, knows the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings, as well as their cultivation and realization of cessation; this is called the knowledge of others' minds. "
“World-Honored One!
What is the knowledge of suffering?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Tathāgata says:]”
"If wisdom takes non-apprehension as its skillful means and knows that suffering should not arise, this is the knowledge of suffering.
"World-Honored One,
what is the knowledge of origination?"
“Subhūti! If wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, knows that origination should be eternally abandoned, this is the knowledge of origination.
“World-Honored One!”
"What is the knowledge of cessation? Subhūti,
if one employs the skillful means of non-apprehension to know that cessation is to be realized, this is the knowledge of cessation."
“World-Honored One!
What is the knowledge of the path?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
"If wisdom takes non-apprehension as its skillful means and knows that the Path should be cultivated, this is the knowledge of the Path.
"World-Honored One!
What is the knowledge of exhaustion?"
“Subhūti! If wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as its expedient, knows that greed, hatred, and delusion are exhausted, this is the knowledge of exhaustion (kṣayajñāna).
“World-Honored One!”
"What is the knowledge of non-arising? Subhūti,
if one employs the method of non-apprehension to know that there is no further arising of the realms of existence, this is the knowledge of non-arising."
“World-Honored One!
What is knowledge as it truly is?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The Tathāgata’s all-knowledge and knowledge of all aspects— this is knowledge as it truly is.
"Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the three untainted faculties (*anāsrava-indriya*).
What are these three?
"Namely, the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown,' the faculty of 'knowing,' and the faculty of 'one who has known.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“What is the faculty of ‘I shall come to know the unknown’?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If those in training have not yet realized the noble truths and have not yet attained the fruits of the noble ones, their faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom constitute the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (ājñāsyāmīndriya).
“World-Honored One!
What is the faculty of one who has already known? “Subhūti!

When those in training have attained clear realization of the noble truths and have attained the fruits of the noble ones, their faculty of faith, faculty of energy, faculty of mindfulness, faculty of concentration, and faculty of wisdom constitute the faculty of one who has already known.
“World-Honored One!
What is the faculty of one who possesses complete knowledge? “Subhūti!

This refers to the faculty of faith, the faculty of diligence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom belonging to those beyond training—whether they be arhats, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas who have already dwelled in the ten stages, or Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas. These constitute the faculty of one who has fully realized knowledge.
“Subhūti! These three faculties, when practiced by means of non-apprehension, should be known as the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the mark of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of the three samādhis.
What are these three?

"Namely: the samādhi with applied thought and sustained thought, the samādhi without applied thought and with only sustained thought, and the samādhi without applied thought and without sustained thought.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is the concentration with directed thought and sustained examination?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."

If, having detached from sensual desires and unwholesome states, one enters and dwells in the first dhyāna, which is accompanied by vitarka and vicāra and possesses the joy and happiness born of seclusion, this is called the samādhi with vitarka and vicāra.
“World-Honored One!
What is the samādhi without vitarka and with only vicāra?
“Excellent One!
“If the first dhyāna and the intermediate dhyāna between the first and second dhyānas constitute the samādhi with vitarka and no vicāra,
then, Blessed One,
what is the samādhi without vitarka and without vicāra?”
“Subhūti! If one enters the second dhyāna up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, this is the samādhi without applied thought and without sustained thought. Subhūti!”
If these three samādhis are practiced by taking non-apprehension as the means, one should know that this constitutes the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the mark of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of the ten recollections.
What are these ten?

That is to say: recollection of the Buddha, recollection of the Dharma, recollection of the Saṅgha, recollection of ethical discipline, recollection of relinquishment, recollection of the devas, recollection of tranquility and disenchantment, recollection of inhalation and exhalation, recollection of the body, and recollection of death.
"Subhūti!
These ten recollections, when practiced by means of non-apprehension, should be known as the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of all wholesome dharmas, namely: the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities. One should know that when these are practiced with non-apprehension as the means, this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the ten powers of a Buddha.
What are these ten?

That is to say: the power of knowledge regarding what is possible and impossible; the power of knowledge regarding the maturation of karma; the power of knowledge regarding the various elements; the power of knowledge regarding the various inclinations; the power of knowledge regarding the superior and inferior faculties; the power of knowledge regarding the paths leading everywhere; the power of knowledge regarding the defilement and purification of meditative concentrations, liberations, samādhis, and attainments; the power of knowledge regarding the recollection of past lives; the power of knowledge regarding death and rebirth; and the power of knowledge regarding the exhaustion of the outflows.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the power of knowledge regarding what is possible and what is impossible?”
The Buddha said:
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one understands, in accordance with reality, the characteristics of what is possible and what is impossible regarding dharmas such as cause and effect, this is the power of knowledge regarding the possible and the impossible.”
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of knowing the maturation of karma? ‘Subhūti!

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one understands as they truly are the various characteristics of causes and effects regarding the past, future, and present karmic dharmas and experiences of all classes of sentient beings, this is the power of knowing the maturation of karma.

“World-Honored One! What is the power of knowledge regarding the various elements? ‘Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Tathāgata knows] that these sentient beings possess the element of desire, those possess the element of hatred, and those possess the element of delusion; he knows that these sentient beings have a small amount of desire, those have a large amount of desire, and so on, up to those who have abandoned all desire. He knows that these sentient beings possess a small amount of hatred, those possess a large amount of hatred, and so on, up to those who have abandoned all hatred. He knows that these sentient beings possess a small amount of delusion, those possess a large amount of delusion, and so on, up to those who have abandoned all delusion. He knows that these sentient beings possess a small amount of faculties, those possess a large amount of faculties, and so on, up to those who have perfected all faculties. He knows that these sentient beings are of dull faculties, those are of sharp faculties, and so on, up to those who have perfected all faculties. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior faculties, those are of middling faculties, and those are of superior faculties. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior conduct, those are of middling conduct, and those are of superior conduct. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior aspiration, those are of middling aspiration, and those are of superior aspiration. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior intention, those are of middling intention, and those are of superior intention. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior application, those are of middling application, and those are of superior application. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior resolve, those are of middling resolve, and those are of superior resolve. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior practice, those are of middling practice, and those are of superior practice. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior attainment, those are of middling attainment, and those are of superior attainment. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior lineage, those are of middling lineage, and those are of superior lineage. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior birth, those are of middling birth, and those are of superior birth. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior wealth, those are of middling wealth, and those are of superior wealth. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior retinue, those are of middling retinue, and those are of superior retinue. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior support, those are of middling support, and those are of superior support. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior companions, those are of middling companions, and those are of superior companions. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior associates, those are of middling associates, and those are of superior associates. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior attendants, those are of middling attendants, and those are of superior attendants. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior service, those are of middling service, and those are of superior service. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior livelihood, those are of middling livelihood, and those are of superior livelihood. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior resources, those are of middling resources, and those are of superior resources. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior fortune, those are of middling fortune, and those are of superior fortune. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior merit, those are of middling merit, and those are of superior merit. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior wisdom, those are of middling wisdom, and those are of superior wisdom. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior understanding, those are of middling understanding, and those are of superior understanding. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior realization, those are of middling realization, and those are of superior realization. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior liberation, those are of middling liberation, and those are of superior liberation. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior liberation through wisdom, those are of middling liberation through wisdom, and those are of superior liberation through wisdom. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior liberation through both ways, those are of middling liberation through both ways, and those are of superior liberation through both ways. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior faculties, those are of middling faculties, and those are of superior faculties. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior powers, those are of middling powers, and those are of superior powers. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior limbs of enlightenment, those are of middling limbs of enlightenment, and those are of superior limbs of enlightenment. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior paths, those are of middling paths, and those are of superior paths. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior vehicles, those are of middling vehicles, and those are of superior vehicles. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior destinations, those are of middling destinations, and those are of superior destinations. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior births, those are of middling births, and those are of superior births. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior lineages, those are of middling lineages, and those are of superior lineages. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior families, those are of middling families, and those are of superior families. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior castes, those are of middling castes, and those are of superior castes. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior classes, those are of middling classes, and those are of superior classes. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior stations, those are of middling stations, and those are of superior stations. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior abodes, those are of middling abodes, and those are of superior abodes. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior realms, those are of middling realms, and those are of superior realms. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior inclinations, those are of middling inclinations, and those are of superior inclinations. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior dispositions, those are of middling dispositions, and those are of superior dispositions. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior intentions, those are of middling intentions, and those are of superior intentions. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior applications, those are of middling applications, and those are of superior applications. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior practices, those are of middling practices, and those are of superior practices. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior attainments, those are of middling attainments, and those are of superior attainments. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior roots of goodness, those are of middling roots of goodness, and those are of superior roots of goodness. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior accumulations of merit, those are of middling accumulations of merit, and those are of superior accumulations of merit. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior accumulations of wisdom, those are of middling accumulations of wisdom, and those are of superior accumulations of wisdom. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior accumulations of both merit and wisdom, those are of middling accumulations of both merit and wisdom, and those are of superior accumulations of both merit and wisdom. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior faculties, those are of middling faculties, and those are of superior faculties. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior powers, those are of middling powers, and those are of superior powers. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior limbs of enlightenment, those are of middling limbs of enlightenment, and those are of superior limbs of enlightenment. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior paths, those are of middling paths, and those are of superior paths. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior vehicles, those are of middling vehicles, and those are of superior vehicles. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior destinations, those are of middling destinations, and those are of superior destinations. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior births, those are of middling births, and those are of superior births. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior lineages, those are of middling lineages, and those are of superior lineages. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior families, those are of middling families, and those are of superior families. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior castes, those are of middling castes, and those are of superior castes. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior classes, those are of middling classes, and those are of superior classes. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior stations, those are of middling stations, and those are of superior stations.
