He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior abodes, those are of middling abodes, and those are of superior abodes. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior realms, those are of middling realms, and those are of superior realms. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior inclinations, those are of middling inclinations, and those are of superior inclinations. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior dispositions, those are of middling dispositions, and those are of superior dispositions. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior intentions, those are of middling intentions, and those are of superior intentions. He knows that these sentient beings are of inferior applications,

If, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, one understands, in accordance with reality, the characteristics of the infinite realms of sentient beings, this is the power of knowledge regarding the diversity of elements (*nānādhātujñānabala*).
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of knowing the various inclinations? “Subhūti!

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one understands, in accordance with reality, the characteristics of the immeasurable inclinations of all classes of sentient beings, this is the power of knowledge regarding the various inclinations.
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of knowing the superior and inferior faculties?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]”

If, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one understands, in accordance with reality, the superior and inferior characteristics of the faculties of various sentient beings, this is the power of knowing the superior and inferior faculties.
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of knowledge regarding the practice of universal application? “Excellent One!

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one understands as they truly are the pervasive modes of conduct of all classes of sentient beings, this is the power of knowledge regarding the pervasive modes of conduct.
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of knowledge regarding the defilement and purification of the dhyānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments?
“Excellent One! [The Buddha replied:]

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one understands, in accordance with reality, the characteristics of all sentient beings’ meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis (*samādhi*), attainments (*samāpatti*), afflictions (*saṃkleśa*), purifications (*vyavadāna*), faculties (*indriya*), powers (*bala*), factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and factors of the path (*mārgāṅga*), this is the power of knowing meditative concentrations, liberations, samādhis, attainments, afflictions, and purifications.
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of the knowledge of recollecting past abodes?
“Suvīra! [The Buddha said:]”

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one knows, in accordance with reality, the immeasurable and innumerable characteristics of the past lives of all sentient beings, this is the power of knowledge regarding the recollection of past abodes.
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of knowledge regarding death and rebirth?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If, by means of the skillful method of non-apprehension, one understands as they truly are the immeasurable and innumerable phenomena of the death and birth of all sentient beings, this is the power of knowledge regarding death and birth.
“World-Honored One!
What is the power of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, one understands as it truly is that all outflows (*āsrava*) are forever exhausted, and attains liberation of mind through the absence of outflows and liberation of wisdom through the absence of outflows, dwelling in the fulfillment of personal realization within this very life, and is able to correctly know: "Birth for me has been exhausted, the holy life has been established, what was to be done has been accomplished, and there will be no further existence"—this is called the power of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows.
“Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
The characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva refers to the four fearlessnesses.
What are the four? They are:

the fearlessness of being perfectly awakened, the fearlessness regarding the exhaustion of outflows, the fearlessness regarding obstructive dharmas, and the fearlessness regarding the path that leads to the end of suffering.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the fearlessness of the Perfectly Enlightened One?”

The Buddha said, “Subhūti! If one, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, declares oneself to be a Truly Perfectly Awakened One, then even if there should be a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a deva, a Māra, a Brahmā, or anyone else in the world who, according to the Dharma, raises an objection or calls for recollection, saying that this Dharma is not that of a Truly Perfectly Awakened One, I see no grounds for such an objection.”

Because there is no basis for such challenges being seen therein, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he proclaims himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he rightly roars the lion’s roar, turning the sublime Brahma-wheel. This wheel is pure, correct, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, Brahmas, or anyone else in the world, none are able to turn it according to the Dharma. This is the fearlessness of the Perfectly Enlightened One.
“World-Honored One!
What is the fearlessness regarding the exhaustion of outflows?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If, by means of the practice of non-apprehension, one claims for oneself that all outflows (*āsrava*) have been eternally exhausted, then even if there should be a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a deva, a Māra, a Brahmā, or anyone else in the world who, according to the Dharma, raises an objection or brings it to mind, saying that such outflows have not yet been eternally exhausted, I see no basis for responding to that objection.

Because there is no basis for such challenges, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he declares himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he truly roars the lion’s roar and turns the sublime Brahma-wheel. This wheel is pure, correct, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, Brahmās, or anyone else in the world, none are able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma. This is the fearlessness regarding the exhaustion of the outflows (*āsravakṣayābhaya*).
“World-Honored One!
What is the fearlessness regarding the dharmas that constitute obstacles? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If one employs the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as a skillful means, one explains to the disciples the dharmas that obstruct the Path. Should any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world, according to the Dharma, raise an objection or cause one to reflect, saying, "Practicing these dharmas cannot obstruct the Path," I see no grounds for such an objection.

Because there is no basis for such challenges being seen therein, he dwells in peace, free from fear and dread; he proclaims himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he rightly roars the lion’s roar, turning the sublime Brahma-wheel. This wheel is pure, correct, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, Brahmas, or anyone else in the world, none are able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma. This is the fearlessness regarding the unobstructed teaching of the Dharma.
“World-Honored One!
What is the fearlessness regarding the path that exhausts suffering?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension, one teaches the path to the exhaustion of suffering to the disciples, then should any śramaṇa, brāhmaṇa, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world, according to the Dharma, raise an objection or attempt to provoke recollection by claiming that practicing this path cannot exhaust suffering, I see no grounds for such an objection.

Because there is no basis for such challenges being seen therein, he dwells in security, free from fear and dread; he declares himself to occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, and amidst the great assembly, he rightly utters the lion’s roar and turns the sublime Brahma-wheel. This wheel is pure, upright, true, and unsurpassed; among all śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, Brahmas, or anyone else in the world, none are able to turn it in accordance with the Dharma. This is the fearlessness regarding the path to the exhaustion of suffering.
“Subhūti, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
The characteristic of the Mahāyāna of a bodhisattva mahāsattva refers to the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*).
What are the four? They are:

the analytical knowledge of meaning (*artha-pratisaṃvid*), the analytical knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*), the analytical knowledge of expression (*nirukti-pratisaṃvid*), and the analytical knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*).
"Subhūti!
These four analytical knowledges, when practiced with the method of non-apprehension, should be known as the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, the characteristics of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; the five eyes, the six supernormal powers, all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)."
"Subhūti!
When such dharmas as these are practiced with non-apprehension as the means, you should know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the mark of the Great Vehicle of a bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma).
What are these eighteen?

That is to say, from the night I, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, first attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, until the night I finally entered the great parinirvāṇa without remainder after having accomplished all that was to be done—in the interval between these two times:

He is always free from error; he has no abrupt or violent speech; he is without loss of mindfulness; he has no unconcentrated mind; he has no manifold perceptions; he has no equanimity lacking discernment; his aspiration does not regress, his diligence does not regress, his mindfulness does not regress, his wisdom does not regress, his liberation does not regress, and his knowledge and vision of liberation do not regress. All his bodily actions are preceded by wisdom and follow after wisdom; all his verbal actions are preceded by wisdom and follow after wisdom; all his mental actions are preceded by wisdom and follow after wisdom. His knowledge and vision regarding the past are unattached and unimpeded; his knowledge and vision regarding the future are unattached and unimpeded; his knowledge and vision regarding the present are unattached and unimpeded.

Subhūti! These eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are all without exception characterized by the method of non-apprehension; you should know that this is the mark of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of the dhāraṇī-doors of all syllables.
At that time, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the dhāraṇī-gateway of letters?
The Buddha said:
"Subhūti! The equality of letters, the equality of speech, and the equality of the principles of verbal expression that enter into all gateways of letters—this is the dhāraṇī gateway of syllables."
“World-Honored One!
How does one enter the gateways of all syllables?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, they enter the gateway of the letter *ṅa*, realizing that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen;
they enter the gateway of the letter *la*, realizing that all phenomena are free from dust and defilement;
they enter the gateway of the letter *pa*, realizing that all phenomena are the teaching of ultimate truth.
The letter-gateway *ra* is for realizing that all dharmas are without birth or death;
the letter-gateway *na* is for realizing that all dharmas are far removed from names and signs and are without gain or loss;
the letter-gateway *la* is for realizing that all dharmas transcend the world, as the causal conditions of the branches of craving never again appear.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ḍa*, for one realizes that all phenomena are tamed, quiescent, suchness, equal, and non-discriminative;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ba*, for one realizes that all phenomena are free from bondage;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ṭa*, for one realizes that all phenomena are free from feverish affliction and impurity, thereby attaining purity.
One enters the gateway of the letter *sa*, realizing that all phenomena are without obstruction;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ba*, realizing that the path of speech and sound for all phenomena is severed;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ṣa*, realizing that all phenomena are the immovable true suchness (*tathatā*).
One enters the letter-gateway *ja*, because one realizes that all phenomena are, in reality, unarisen;
one enters the letter-gateway *ṣṭha*, because one realizes that the characteristics of the restraint and maintenance of all phenomena are unapprehendable;
one enters the letter-gateway *ka*, because one realizes that an agent of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *sa*, for one realizes that the temporal equality of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ma*, for one realizes that the nature of self and what belongs to self in all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ga*, for one realizes that the nature of activity and grasping in all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the letter-da gate, because one realizes that the location of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the letter-ja gate, because one realizes that the arising of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the letter-śva gate, because one realizes that the nature of stability of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Da, because one realizes that the nature of all dharmadhātus is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Śa, because one realizes that the nature of the tranquility of all dharmas is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Kha, because one realizes that the nature of all dharmas as being like space is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *caṇ*, for one awakens to the fact that the nature of all phenomena being utterly exhausted is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *sāḍhu*, for one awakens to the fact that the nature of all phenomena—which sustain what is possible and what is impossible so as not to be moved—is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ña*, for one awakens to the fact that the nature of all phenomena as that which is to be known is unattainable.
One enters the letter-portal *la*, realizing that the nature of attachment to all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the letter-portal *ha*, realizing that the causal nature of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the letter-portal *ba*, realizing that the destructible nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ca* (綽), because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena being covered by desire and pleasure is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *sma* (颯磨), because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena being subject to recollection is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *kha* (嗑縛), because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena being subject to invocation is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Ca, because the courageous and vigorous nature of all phenomena is found to be unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Kha, because the thick and equal nature of all phenomena is found to be unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter Cha, because the accumulative nature of all phenomena is found to be unattainable.

Entering the letter-gateway NA, one realizes that all dharmas are free from all clamor and contention, for there is no going and no coming, and walking, standing, sitting, or lying down cannot be apprehended;
entering the letter-gateway PHA, one realizes that all dharmas are all-pervasive, for their karmic retribution cannot be apprehended;
entering the letter-gateway SKA, one realizes that all dharmas are accumulations, for the nature of the aggregates cannot be apprehended.
One enters the gateway of the letter *iṣa*, because one realizes that the nature and characteristics of senescence and decay in all phenomena are unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ca*, because one realizes that the traces of accumulation in all phenomena are unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ṭha*, because one realizes that the nature of mutual oppression in all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ca* because the ultimate locus of all phenomena cannot be apprehended. "Subhūti!

Such a gateway of letters is that by which one may realize the limit of the emptiness of phenomena; apart from the expression of this letter, nothing further regarding the emptiness of all phenomena can be found."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Such meanings of words cannot be proclaimed, cannot be displayed, cannot be grasped, cannot be written down or maintained, and cannot be observed, because they are free from all marks (*lakṣaṇa*).
"Subhūti!

Just as space is the destination to which all things return, so too are these gateways of letters; it is only by entering these gateways that the meaning of the emptiness of all phenomena becomes fully manifest."
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Entering this syllable *kṣa* and others is called entering the gateways of all syllables.
Suvikrāntavikrāmin!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains skillful wisdom regarding such entry into the gates of all syllables, they will be without obstruction in all spoken sounds and their expressed or indicated meanings; they will be able to fully realize and maintain the equal emptiness of all phenomena, and will attain skillfulness in all forms of speech and sound.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to hear such seals of the gateways into all syllables and their corresponding phrases, and having heard them, receives, maintains, recites, masters, and explains them to others without craving for fame or profit, they will, by virtue of these causes and conditions, attain twenty kinds of sublime merit.”
What are the twenty? They are: attaining powerful mindfulness; attaining superior shame and remorse; attaining firm strength; attaining the essential purport of the Dharma;
attaining superior awakening; attaining distinguished wisdom; attaining unimpeded eloquence; and attaining the gateways of dhāraṇī.
One attains freedom from doubt; one attains the state where neither anger nor attachment arises toward words that are disagreeable or agreeable;
one attains dwelling in equanimity, free from high and low; one attains skillfulness regarding the vocal expressions of sentient beings;

and one attains skillfulness regarding the aggregates (*skandha*), skillfulness regarding the sense bases (*āyatana*), skillfulness regarding the elements (*dhātu*), skillfulness regarding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), skillfulness regarding causes (*hetu*), and skillfulness regarding conditions (*pratyaya*).

He attains skill in the Dharma; he attains skill in the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties, skill in the knowledge of others' minds, skill in the observation of stellar astrology, skill in the knowledge of the divine ear, skill in the knowledge of recollecting past lives, skill in the knowledge of supernormal powers, skill in the knowledge of death and rebirth, and skill in the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows. He attains...
He is said to be skilled in the knowledge of what is possible and what is impossible, and he attains skill in the modes of deportment such as coming and going.
"Subhūti! These are the twenty kinds of sublime qualities attained."
"Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, the dhāraṇī-doors of syllables that they obtain—know that this is the characteristic of the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"Regarding your question, 'How should one know when a bodhisattva mahāsattva has set out upon the Great Vehicle?'— Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the six pāramitās, proceeds from one stage to the next stage, it should be known that this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s setting out upon the Great Vehicle.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the six pāramitās, proceed from one stage to the next?"
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all phenomena come from nowhere and go nowhere.”
Why is this? Because all phenomena have neither going nor coming, neither departure nor arrival, due to the fact that those phenomena are subject to no transformation or decay.

Thus, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely upon or conceptualize the ground from which he departs or to which he proceeds; although he cultivates the karmic activities for purifying the grounds, he does not perceive that ground.
"Subhūti!
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the six pāramitās, proceeds from one stage to the next.
"World-Honored One!"
"What is meant by the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation and purification of the deeds of the stages? "Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the first stage, the 'Extremely Joyful,' they should skillfully cultivate and purify ten kinds of superior deeds."
What are the ten?

First, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the activity of the superior intention (*adhyāśaya*), because the entity of the superior intention cannot be apprehended.
Second, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the mental karma of equality toward all sentient beings, because all sentient beings are unapprehendable.
Third, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the karma of giving, because the giver, the recipient, and the gift cannot be apprehended.

Fourth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the practice of associating with spiritual friends, because there is no dualistic appearance between spiritual friends and evil associates.
Fifth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, they cultivate the practice of seeking the Dharma, because all dharmas sought cannot be apprehended.
Sixth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, they cultivate the practice of always delighting in leaving home, because the home one abandons cannot be apprehended.
Seventh, by taking non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the activity of cherishing the Buddha’s body, because the primary marks and secondary signs are unapprehendable.
Eighth, by taking non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the activity of expounding the Dharma teachings, because the dharmas that are conceptually differentiated are unapprehendable.
Ninth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the karma of destroying pride, because all phenomena of prosperity and success are unapprehendable.
Tenth, by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates and purifies the karma of constant truthful speech, because the nature of all speech is unapprehendable.
“Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the first stage, the Stage of Extreme Joy, they should skillfully cultivate these ten kinds of supreme activities.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the second stage, the Stainless (vimalā), they should contemplate and cultivate eight dharmas so as to quickly bring them to fulfillment.
What are these eight?
First, purity of the precepts;
second, recognizing kindness and repaying it;
third, abiding in the power of patience.
Fourth, experiencing supreme joy;
fifth, not abandoning sentient beings;
sixth, constantly giving rise to great compassion.
Seventh, one should serve, attend to, and make offerings to all teachers and elders with a mind of reverence and faith, regarding them as if they were the Buddha.
Eighth, one should diligently seek to practice and cultivate the pāramitās.
"Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the second stage, the Stainless (vimalā), they should contemplate and cultivate these eight dharmas so as to swiftly bring them to fulfillment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the third stage, the Radiant, they should abide in five dharmas.
What are these five?
First, he diligently seeks out extensive learning without ever becoming weary or satisfied, yet he does not cling to the literal words of the teachings he hears.
Second, with a mind free from defilement, he constantly practices the gift of Dharma; though he extensively transforms and guides others, he never exalts himself.
Third, for the sake of adorning and purifying the buddha-fields and planting all roots of goodness, although one employs dedication, one does not exalt oneself.
Fourth, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, although one does not grow weary of the boundless cycle of birth and death, one does not become self-important.
Fifth, although they abide in a sense of shame and dread of blame, they remain without attachment. Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the third stage, the Radiant, they should constantly abide in these five dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the fourth stage, the Radiant Wisdom (Arciṣmatī), they should dwell in ten dharmas, constantly practicing them without relinquishing them.
What are these ten?
First, dwelling in forest hermitages and never abandoning them;
second, having few desires;
third, being content.
Fourth, they never abandon the virtues of the ascetic practices (*dhūtaguṇa*).
Fifth, they never forsake any of the training rules (*śikṣāpada*).
Sixth, they develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures.
Seventh, they constantly delight in giving rise to a mind associated with quiescence.
Eighth, they relinquish all that they possess.
Ninth, their minds do not stagnate or sink.
Tenth, they have no attachment or longing for anything whatsoever. Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the fourth stage, the Radiant Intelligence (Arciṣmatī), they should abide in these ten dharmas and constantly practice them without relinquishing them.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 53 [and] Scroll 54.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter Fifteen: Distinguishing the Mahāyāna, Part Four.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the fifth stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā*), they should remain far removed from ten things.
What are the ten?
First, one should distance oneself from household life.
Second, one should distance oneself from bhikṣuṇīs.
Third, one should distance oneself from stinginess regarding households.
Fourth, one should distance oneself from anger and contention within assemblies.
Fifth, one should distance oneself from praising oneself and disparaging others.
Sixth, one should distance oneself from the ten unwholesome paths of action.
Seventh, one should distance oneself from overweening pride and arrogance.
Eighth, one should distance oneself from inverted views.
Ninth, one should distance oneself from hesitation.
Tenth, one should distance oneself from greed, hatred, and delusion. Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the fifth stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer, they should always remain far removed from these ten dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the sixth stage, the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī*), they should fulfill six dharmas. What are these six?
First, they should fulfill the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*).
Second, one should fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*).
Third, one should fulfill the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).
Fourth, one should fulfill the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*).
Fifth, one should fulfill the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*).
Sixth, one should fulfill the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Furthermore, one should distance oneself from six things.
What are the six?
First, one should distance oneself from the mind of a śrāvaka.
Second, one should distance oneself from the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
Third, one should distance oneself from a mind of feverish affliction.
Fourth, when seeing a beggar approach, one’s heart should not feel weary or distressed.
Fifth, when giving away all one's possessions, one should have no sense of grief or regret.
Sixth, one should never deceive those who come seeking [help]. "Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the sixth stage, the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī*), they should fulfill these six dharmas and should also distance themselves from these six dharmas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the seventh stage, the Far-Reaching (Dūraṃgamā), they should remain far removed from twenty things.
What are these twenty?
First, one should distance oneself from the grasping at a self, the grasping at a sentient being, and so forth, up to the grasping at a knower and the grasping at a viewer.
Second, one should distance oneself from the grasping at annihilation.
Third, one should distance oneself from the attachment to permanence.
Fourth, one should distance oneself from the perception of signs.
Fifth, one should distance oneself from the attachment to views such as [the belief in] causes.
Sixth, one should distance oneself from attachment to name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*).
Seventh, one should distance oneself from attachment to the aggregates (*skandha*).
Eighth, one should distance oneself from attachment to the sense bases (*āyatana*).
Ninth, one should distance oneself from attachment to the elements (*dhātu*).
Tenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to the truths (*satya*).
Eleventh, one should distance oneself from attachment to dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*).
Twelfth, one should distance oneself from attachment to and grasping at the three realms.
Thirteenth, one should distance oneself from grasping at all phenomena (*dharma*).
Fourteenth, one should distance oneself from grasping at all phenomena as being either in accordance with or contrary to reality.
Fifteenth, one should distance oneself from clinging to views based on the Buddha.
Sixteenth, one should distance oneself from clinging to views based on the Dharma.
Seventeenth, one should distance oneself from clinging to views based on the Sangha.
Eighteenth, one should distance oneself from attachment to views based on the precepts.
Nineteenth, one should distance oneself from fear of the dharma of emptiness.
Twentieth, one should distance oneself from contravening emptiness.
"Furthermore, one should fulfill twenty qualities.
What are these twenty?
First, one should fulfill the thorough penetration of emptiness."
Second, one should fulfill the realization of signlessness (*animitta*).
Third, one should fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness (*apraṇihita*).
Fourth, one should fulfill the purity of the three spheres (*trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi*).
Fifth, one should fulfill compassion for sentient beings, as well as non-attachment toward sentient beings.
Sixth, one should fulfill the vision of the equality of all phenomena, as well as non-attachment within that [vision].
Seventh, one should fulfill the impartial view toward all sentient beings, as well as remain unattached therein.
Eighth, one should fulfill the thorough penetration of the principle of reality, as well as remain unattached therein.
Ninth, one should fulfill the wisdom of the endurance of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Tenth, one should fulfill the principle of the single characteristic (*ekalakṣaṇa-naya*) of all phenomena.
Eleventh, one should fulfill the elimination of conceptual discrimination (*vikalpa*).
Twelfth, one should fulfill the complete distancing from all conceptualizations.
Thirteenth, one should fulfill the complete distancing from all views.
Fourteenth, one should fulfill the complete distancing from all afflictions.
Fifteenth, one should fulfill the stage of śamatha and vipaśyanā.
Sixteenth, one should fulfill the taming of the mental continuum.
Seventeenth, one should fulfill the pacification of the mental continuum.
Eighteenth, one should fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom.
Nineteenth, one should fulfill freedom from all attachment and defilement.
Twentieth, one should fulfill the ability to travel to any buddha-field at will and manifest one's own body within the assemblies of those buddhas.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the seventh stage, the Dūraṃgamā (Far-Reaching), they should distance themselves from these twenty dharmas and should bring to perfection these other twenty dharmas.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the eighth stage, the Immovable (Acalā), they should fulfill four dharmas.
What are these four?
First, one should fulfill the realization of the mental activities of all sentient beings.
Second, one should fulfill the playful mastery of the various supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
Third, one should fulfill the vision of all Buddha-fields, and according to what is seen therein, personally adorn and purify various Buddha-fields.
Fourth, one should fulfill the service and offerings to all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and observe the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is.
Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the eighth stage, the Immovable, they should fulfill these four dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the ninth stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (sādhumatī), they should fulfill four dharmas.
What are these four?
First, one should fulfill the knowledge that discerns the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings.
Second, one should fulfill the purification of Buddha-fields.
Third, one should fulfill the frequent entry into various meditative concentrations, such as the illusion-like samādhi.
Fourth, in order to bring the roots of virtue of all sentient beings to maturity as appropriate, they should enter into various states of existence and manifest through spontaneous birth.
Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the ninth stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī*), they should fulfill these four dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā), they should fulfill twelve dharmas.
What are these twelve?
First, one should fulfill the great vow to encompass infinite realms, causing every aspiration to be realized in its entirety.
Second, one should fulfill the knowledge of the diverse languages of all classes of beings—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
Third, one should fulfill the wisdom of unimpeded eloquence.
Fourth, one should fulfill the perfection of entering the womb.
Fifth, one should fulfill the perfection of birth.
Sixth, one should fulfill the perfection of family.
Seventh, one should fulfill the perfection of lineage.
Eighth, one should fulfill the perfection of retinue.
Ninth, one should fulfill the perfection of the physical body.
Tenth, one should fulfill the perfection of renunciation.
Eleventh, one should fulfill the perfection of adorning the bodhi tree.
Twelfth, one should fulfill the complete accomplishment and perfection of all merits. Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma, they should fulfill these twelve dharmas.
“Subhūti, you should know that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has fully perfected the tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā), should be said to be no different from the Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and purify the karma of the superior intention?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, cultivates and accumulates all roots of goodness, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation and purification of the activity of the superior intention.”
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and purify the karma of an impartial mind toward all sentient beings?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, brings forth the four immeasurables—loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity—this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the karma of a mind of equality toward all sentient beings.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and purify the karma of giving?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices giving toward all sentient beings without making any conceptual distinctions, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation and purification of the practice of giving.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and attend to the karma of associating with virtuous friends?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees various spiritual friends exhorting and transforming sentient beings, causing them to cultivate the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), he immediately draws near to them, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising them, and receiving the true Dharma from them; attending upon them day and night with a mind free from weariness—this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the practice of drawing near to spiritual friends.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and purify the activity of seeking the Dharma?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, diligently seeks the unsurpassed true Dharma of the Tathāgata and does not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the activity of seeking the Dharma.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and purify the practice of always delighting in leaving the household life?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, in all places of birth, always feels weary of the household life as a noisy and cluttered prison, and constantly delights in the pure renunciation of the Buddha-dharma without anything being able to obstruct them, this is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s cultivation of the practice of always delighting in renunciation.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the practice of loving and delighting in the Buddha’s body? “Suvīra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having beheld the form of a Buddha even for a single moment, never abandons the mental attention directed toward the Buddha until they realize unsurpassed awakening, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the practice of cherishing the Buddha’s body.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and expound the activity of the Dharma teaching?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, whether while the Buddha is in the world or after his parinirvāṇa, expounds the Dharma teachings for the sake of all sentient beings—teachings that are excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, skillful in both word and meaning, pure, complete, and the pristine holy life—namely: the sūtras, geyas, vyākaraṇas, gāthās, udānas, nidānas, avadānas, itivṛttakas, jātakas, vaipulyas, adbhutadharmas, and upadeśas; this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the activity of expounding the Dharma teachings.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate and purify the practice that destroys arrogance?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva always maintains humility and respect, subduing the mind of pride, they will consequently not be born into a low caste or inferior lineage; this is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s cultivation and purification of the practice that destroys pride.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva speaks in accordance with what they know, so that their words and deeds correspond, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the karma of speech characterized by constant truthfulness.
“World-Honored One!”
“What is the pure ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor any other factors that violate ethical discipline and obstruct awakening, this is the pure ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva recognize kindness and repay it?
“Excellent One!
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, while practicing the bodhisattva path, does not forget to repay even a small kindness received, how much less would they fail to requite a great favor!
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva recognizes kindness and repays it.
"World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva abide in the power of patience?"

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, even when sentient beings come to assault and insult him, harbors no heart of anger or malice toward them, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to abide in the power of patience.”
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva experience supreme joy? “Sudhana!

If the sentient beings whom a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has transformed have attained maturity, and their bodies and minds are at ease and they experience supreme joy, this is called the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s experience of supreme joy.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not abandon sentient beings?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind of rescuing sentient beings never abandons them, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva not to abandon sentient beings.
“World-Honored One! [The interlocutor asked.]
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly give rise to great compassion?
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva conduct, they form this thought:"

"For the benefit of each and every sentient being, even if I must remain in the great hells for as many immeasurable and innumerable *gaṅgā* sands of kalpas as there are beings, undergoing all manner of agonizing sufferings—whether being burned, boiled, cut, severed, pierced, suspended, ground, or pounded—I would endure such immeasurable miseries in order to cause them to ascend the Buddha Vehicle and attain parinirvāṇa. Even until the entire realm of sentient beings is exhausted, my heart of great compassion shall never grow weary."
“This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly gives rise to great compassion.
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind of reverent faith toward all teachers and elders, consult them, receive their instructions, and make offerings to them as if they were the Buddha?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, seeking unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, shows reverent obedience to teachers and elders without any regard for personal interest, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to consult, receive instruction from, and make offerings to all teachers and elders with a mind of reverence and faith, regarding them as one would the Buddha.”
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seek and practice the pāramitās?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with single-minded devotion, seeks to study the various pāramitās while remaining far removed from all other matters, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seeking to cultivate the pāramitās.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently seeks out extensive learning without ever becoming weary or satisfied, yet remains unattached to the words of the teachings they have heard?”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts diligent effort and forms this thought:

‘Whether in this buddha-field or in the worlds of the ten directions, I shall listen to, study, recite, and uphold all the true Dharma taught by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, yet I shall not become attached to the words therein.’”

"This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to diligently seek extensive learning without ever becoming weary or satisfied, and not to cling to the literal words of the teachings they have heard.
"World-Honored One!"
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly practice the gift of Dharma with an undefiled mind, so that although they extensively transform and guide others, they do not become conceited?
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen:]..."

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, when proclaiming the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, does not even dedicate these roots of goodness toward their own enlightenment, much less seek any other matter!

Though he extensively transforms and guides others, he does not rely on this as a basis for self-conceit; this is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s constant practice of the gift of Dharma with an undefiled mind, whereby he widely opens the way for transformation and edification yet remains free from self-exaltation.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva plants various roots of goodness in order to adorn and purify a buddha-field, and although he employs dedication, does not exalt himself?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all roots of goodness with courageous diligence, desiring to adorn the pure lands of all Buddhas and to purify the mental realms of both self and others, yet does not become conceited despite doing these things—this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to plant roots of goodness to adorn and purify a land, dedicating them without exalting himself.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, does not grow weary despite the boundless cycle of birth and death, yet does not become conceited?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, plants various roots of goodness to adorn and purify buddha-fields, and until they have fulfilled all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), undergoes the diligent hardships of boundless birth and death without weariness or self-exaltation—this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in order to transform sentient beings, not to weary of boundless birth and death while remaining free from self-exaltation.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in shame and modesty yet remains without attachment?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva single-mindedly seeks unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they never for a moment give rise to the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas because they possess a sense of shame and remorse; yet, even within those states, they remain without attachment. This is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to abide in shame and remorse while remaining without attachment.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell in the forest hermitage (āraṇya) without ever abandoning it?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, seeking unexcelled perfect enlightenment and in order to transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, never abandons the forest hermitage (araṇya), this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dwelling in the forest hermitage without ever forsaking it.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva have few desires?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not even seek great enlightenment for his own sake, much less worldly gain, reputation, or similar matters—
this is what constitutes the fewness of desires of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice contentment? “Sudhana!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, solely for the sake of realizing all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), remains unattached to other matters, this is the contentment of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandon the merits of the dhūtas?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly gives rise to the patience of analytical investigation regarding the profound Dharma, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s constant non-abandonment of the dhūta qualities.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandons the various points of training?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva maintains the precepts they have studied with firm resolve without wavering, yet is able to remain non-apprehensive of signs therein, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva never abandoning the points of training.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to a mind of desire toward sublime sensual pleasures, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s profound development of weary detachment toward all sensual pleasures.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva always manage to give rise to a mind associated with tranquility?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes that all phenomena have never arisen or been produced, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly being able to give rise to a mind associated with quiescence.

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva have no attachment or longing for anything that exists?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always remain far removed from bhikṣuṇīs, not dwelling with them even for the duration of a finger-snap, and furthermore never give rise to improper thoughts toward them—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s need to remain far removed from bhikṣuṇīs.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from stinginess regarding one’s home?
“Suvīra! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:

"I should, throughout the long night, bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings; now, these sentient beings have, by the power of their own merit, encountered such an excellent householder as a donor, and therefore I ought not to feel stinginess or envy toward them."
“This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from stinginess regarding households.
“World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from anger and strife within assemblies?”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:

‘If there are śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas within this assembly, or if the essential teachings corresponding to their vehicles are being expounded therein, it may cause me to fall away from the mind of great enlightenment; therefore, I must certainly distance myself from such assemblies.’”
Again, he formed this thought:

"Those who engage in anger and strife cause sentient beings to give rise to hatred and harm, thereby committing various kinds of evil and unwholesome karma; they not only oppose the happy realms, but even more so, the Great Enlightenment!"
"Therefore, one must certainly remain far removed from anger and contention.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from anger and contention within assemblies.
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid self-praise and disparaging others? "Subhūti!

Since a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives nothing at all regarding internal or external phenomena, they should avoid self-praise and disparaging others; this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should avoid self-praise and disparaging others."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the ten unwholesome paths of action?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects thus:
"These ten unwholesome dharmas obstruct even the path to the happy realms and the noble path of the Two Vehicles, let alone Great Enlightenment!"
"Therefore, one should remain far removed from them.
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the ten unwholesome paths of action.
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from overweening pride and arrogance? "Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma that could give rise to pride and arrogance, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from overweening pride and arrogance."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from perversions?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives that the phenomena of perversion are entirely unobtainable, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s detachment from perversions.
“World-Honored One!”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from hesitation? Subhūti,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives that the objects of hesitation are entirely unfindable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from hesitation."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive at all the phenomena of greed, hatred, and delusion, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to remain far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the six pāramitās? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Furthermore, by abiding in these six perfections, the Buddhas and those of the two vehicles are able to cross the oceanic shore of the five kinds of objects of knowledge (jñeya).
What are the five?
First, the past; second, the future.
Third, the present;
fourth, the unconditioned;
fifth, the ineffable.
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the six pāramitās.
"World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the mind of a śrāvaka?"
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'The minds of śrāvakas are not those that realize the path to unexcelled great enlightenment, and therefore they should be shunned.'"
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should distance himself from the mind of a śrāvaka.
"World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from the mind of a pratyekabuddha?"
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘The minds of all pratyekabuddhas can certainly never attain the knowledge of all modes; therefore, I should now remain far removed from them.’”
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
"World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from a mind of feverish affliction?"
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘A mind that fears the feverish afflictions of birth and death does not realize the path to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; therefore, it should be abandoned.’”
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from a mind of feverish distress.
"World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid feeling weary or dejected when seeing a beggar approach?"
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘This mind of weariness and dejection is not the path capable of realizing great enlightenment; therefore, I must now certainly distance myself from it.’”
"This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not feel weary or distressed in mind when seeing a beggar come.
World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva give away all possessions without a heart of sorrow or regret?"
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘This mind of regret will certainly constitute an obstacle to realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; therefore, I should abandon it.’”
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all possessions without a mind of sorrow or regret.
World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva never deceive those who come seeking?"
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
‘This deceitful mind is certainly not the path to anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
Why is this? When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva first gives rise to the mind of unsurpassed enlightenment, they make this vow:
"Whatever I possess, I shall give to those who come seeking it, fulfilling their desires without fail."
"How could one now deceive them with falsehood?
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva never deceives those who come seeking [their help].
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from grasping at a self, grasping at a sentient being, and so forth, up to grasping at a knower and grasping at a viewer?
"Subhūti! [The Buddha replied:]

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that a self, sentient beings, and even a knower or a seer are ultimately unapprehendable, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s thorough relinquishing of attachment to a self, attachment to sentient beings, and even attachment to a knower or a seer.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from clinging to annihilation?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all phenomena are ultimately unarisen because they possess no meaning of cessation, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the attachment to cessation.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all phenomena as being impermanent by nature, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of remaining far removed from the attachment to permanence.
“World-Honored One!”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the perception of signs? Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives that the nature of affliction (saṃkleśa) is unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from the perception of signs."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from the attachment to views such as [the belief in] causes?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not perceive the nature of any views whatsoever, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s thorough distancing from the attachment to views such as those concerning causes.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to name-and-form?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

“If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of name-and-form (nāmarūpa) is entirely unapprehendable, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice of remaining far removed from attachment to name-and-form.
“World-Honored One!”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to the aggregates? "Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of the five aggregates is entirely unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to the aggregates."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to places?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of the twelve bases is entirely unobtainable, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s detachment from attachment to the bases.
“World-Honored One!”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to the elements (*dhātu*)? "Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives that the nature of the eighteen elements and so forth is entirely unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to the elements."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from clinging to the truths?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
"If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all truths is entirely unobtainable, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s detachment from clinging to truths.
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to dependent origination? "Subhūti,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all dependently originated phenomena is unapprehendable, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should remain far removed from attachment to dependent origination."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance themselves from dwelling in attachment to the grasping of the three realms?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of the three realms is entirely unapprehendable, this is for the bodhisattva mahāsattva to remain far removed from attachment and clinging to the three realms.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from all attachment to dharmas?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is like space and is entirely unapprehendable, this is what it means for a bodhisattva-mahāsattva to remain far removed from all attachment to phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance themselves from all conceptual attachments regarding what is correct and what is incorrect with respect to all phenomena?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is entirely unapprehendable, such that there is no nature that conforms to reality nor any that does not conform to reality, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s avoidance of all attachment to phenomena as being either conforming to reality or not conforming to reality.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from the attachment to views based on the Buddha?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that by relying on the attachment to views regarding the Buddha, one cannot truly see the Buddha, this is what constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of remaining far removed from reliance on and attachment to views regarding the Buddha.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from attachment to views based on phenomena?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha said:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes that the true nature of dharmas (dharmatā) is invisible, this constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of remaining far removed from attachment to views based on the Dharma.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from attachment to views based on the Saṃgha?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the harmonious assembly is signless, unconditioned, and invisible, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s avoidance of reliance on and attachment to views regarding the Saṃgha.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from clinging to views based on the precepts?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the natures of both transgression and merit are neither existent nor non-existent, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s proper distancing from attachment to views based on the precepts.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva remain far removed from fear regarding the dharma of emptiness?
“Sudhana! [The Buddha replied: “Sudhana!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all empty phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature, and realizes that the objects of fear ultimately do not exist, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who should remain far removed from fear of empty phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva distance himself from contradicting emptiness?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, and because there is no contradiction between non-emptiness and emptiness, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s avoidance of contradicting emptiness.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the thorough penetration of emptiness?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the thorough penetration of emptiness.
“World-Honored One!”
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the realization of the signless?
Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not mentally engage with any signs, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the realization of the signless.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the knowledge of wishlessness?
“Excellent One!
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind dwells nowhere amidst the phenomena of the three realms, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the knowledge of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!”
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the purity of the three spheres?

Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva is fully endowed with the ten paths of wholesome action that are completely pure, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to fulfill the purity of the three spheres."
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill compassion for sentient beings, as well as remain without attachment toward sentient beings? “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained great compassion and the adornment of a pure land, this constitutes the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of compassionate concern for sentient beings and non-attachment toward sentient beings.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the equal vision of all phenomena, and how should they remain without attachment therein?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither increases nor decreases any dharma, and within this neither grasps nor dwells, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the vision of the equality of all dharmas, as well as being without attachment therein.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the equal vision toward all sentient beings, and how should they remain without attachment therein?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither increases nor decreases [the nature] of sentient beings, and within this state neither grasps nor dwells, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the vision of equality toward all sentient beings, as well as being without attachment therein.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the thorough penetration of the principle of reality, and how should they remain without attachment therein?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the true principle of all phenomena, thoroughly penetrates it as it truly is yet has nothing to penetrate, and within this state neither grasps nor dwells—this is what is meant for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to fulfill the thorough penetration of the true principle and to remain without attachment therein.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the wisdom of the endurance of non-arising?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva endures that all phenomena are without arising, without cessation, and without anything created, and realizes that name-and-form are ultimately non-arising, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the wisdom of the endurance of non-arising (anutpattika-dharmakṣānti).
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the principle of the single characteristic of all phenomena? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the non-dual characteristic regarding all phenomena, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the principle of the single characteristic of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the eradication of conceptual discrimination?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the complete elimination of conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete distancing from all conceptualizations?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from all notions of small, great, and immeasurable, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of being far removed from all notions.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete distancing from all views?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from all views of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the like, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of remaining far removed from all views.
