If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abandons all outflows, afflictions, and the continuity of habitual tendencies, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of being far removed from afflictions.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the stages of śamatha and vipaśyanā?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), this constitutes the stage of śamatha and vipaśyanā that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the taming of the mental continuum?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva finds no delight in and remains unmoved by the phenomena of the three realms, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the subduing of the mental continuum.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the nature of a tranquil mind?
“Excellent One! [The Buddha replied:]
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva skillfully restrains the six sense faculties, this is what constitutes a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the nature of a tranquil mind.
"World-Honored One!"
“How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom? “Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates and attains the Buddha-eye, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should fulfill the nature of unimpeded wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill being free from attachment?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to skillfully relinquish the six external sense bases, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of being free from attachment.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the ability to go to all buddha-fields according to his heart’s desire, manifesting his own body within the assemblies of those Buddhas?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the sublime supernormal powers, proceeding from one buddha-field to another buddha-field to make offerings, show respect, honor, and praise to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and requests them to turn the wheel of Dharma for the benefit of all beings—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of going to any buddha-field at will and manifesting their own body within the assemblies of those Buddhas.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the thorough entry into the mental activities of all sentient beings?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of a single-minded wisdom, knows as they truly are the minds and mental factors of all sentient beings, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the realization of the mental activities of all sentient beings.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the mastery of the various supernormal powers?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sports with various sovereign supernormal powers, traveling from one buddha-field to another for the sake of seeing the Buddhas, yet does not give rise to the thought of "wandering through buddha-fields," this is what is meant by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of sporting in the various supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the vision of all buddha-fields, and in accordance with what is seen, personally adorn and purify various buddha-fields?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while dwelling in a single buddha-field, is able to see the boundless buddha-fields of the ten directions and can also manifest therein without ever giving rise to the notion of ‘buddha-fields,’ and furthermore, for the sake of maturing sentient beings, manifests the position of a wheel-turning monarch within a trichiliocosm to adorn himself, yet is also able to relinquish it without attachment—this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who should fulfill the vision of all buddha-fields, and according to what he sees, personally purify various buddha-fields.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the worship and service of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and observe the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, correctly discerns the meaning and intent of the Dharma, this is called serving and honoring the Buddhas with the offering of the Dharma. Furthermore, to contemplate the Dharma-body of the Buddhas with clear observation—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfilling the service and honor of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and observing the body of the Tathāgata as it truly is.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the knowledge that discerns the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings? “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, abiding in the ten powers of a buddha, understands as they truly are the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the knowledge that discerns the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete purification of a buddha-field?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, purifies the mental activities of all sentient beings, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the purification of the buddha-field.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the meditative concentration on illusion and repeatedly enter various samādhis? “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in this samādhi, although they can accomplish all activities, their mind remains unmoving; furthermore, because they have cultivated this samādhi to the point of full maturity, it manifests repeatedly without the need for further application of effort. This is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the illusion-like samādhi and the frequent entry into various meditative concentrations.
“World-Honored One!

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the practice of entering into various states of existence by manifesting spontaneous birth, in order to bring the roots of goodness of all sentient beings to maturity?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to bring to maturity the sublime roots of goodness in all classes of sentient beings, enters into various states of existence and manifests birth therein according to what is appropriate for them.”
"This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in accordance with the maturation of the roots of goodness of sentient beings, enters into various states of existence and manifests through spontaneous birth.
"World-Honored One!"
"How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the great vow of encompassing infinite locations, so that whatever they vow is all brought to fulfillment?
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha said:]..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already fully cultivated the six pāramitās to the point of ultimate perfection, then whether for the purpose of purifying the buddha-fields or for the purpose of maturing sentient beings, all that is wished for by their mind shall be fulfilled. This is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the great vow to encompass infinite locations, such that whatever they wish for is made to be completely fulfilled.
“World-Honored One!

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the knowledge of the diverse languages of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and other such classes of beings?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme analytical knowledge of language and is well-versed in the distinctions among the vocal expressions of sentient beings, this is what is meant by a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the knowledge of the diverse sounds of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the wisdom of unimpeded eloquence?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the supreme analytical knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*), being able to teach inexhaustibly for the sake of all sentient beings, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the wisdom of unimpeded eloquent discourse.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of entering the womb?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, although in reality always born by transformation in all places of birth, manifests entry into a womb for the benefit of sentient beings, and therein possesses all manner of supreme qualities, this is called the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of entering the womb.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of birth?
“Suvīra! [The World-Honored One replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, at the time of emerging from the womb, manifests various rare and sublime events, causing all sentient beings who see them to rejoice and obtain great benefit and happiness—this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of birth.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of a noble lineage?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is born into a great kṣatriya clan or a great brāhmaṇa clan, and the parents from whom he is descended are beyond reproach, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of family lineage.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of the endowment of noble lineage?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is always born into the lineage of the great bodhisattvas of the past, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of lineage.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of having a complete retinue?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has as his retinue exclusively immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattvas, and not various other classes of beings, this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of a retinue.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of the physical body? ‘Subhūti!...”

If, at the time of his first birth, a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s body is endowed with all the primary and secondary marks, emitting a great radiance that illuminates boundless buddha-worlds and causes those worlds to undergo the six kinds of earth-movements, such that no sentient being who encounters it fails to receive benefit—this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of the birth-body.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of renunciation?
“Excellent One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, at the time of going forth, is followed by immeasurable and incalculable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and so forth as they proceed to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), shaves off their hair and beard, dons the three dharma robes, and takes up the alms bowl; and if they lead immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to mount the three vehicles and proceed toward parinirvāṇa—this is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s perfection of the full endowment of going forth.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the complete adornment of the bodhi tree?
‘Subhūti!...”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through the power of their preeminent roots of goodness and vast aspirations, brings forth such a wondrous tree of enlightenment—with lapis lazuli for its trunk and pure gold for its roots; with branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all composed of the seven supreme jewels; a tree so tall and wide that it completely covers the trichiliocosm Buddha-field, its radiance shining throughout the worlds of the Ganges-sand number of Buddhas in the ten directions—this is the perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s complete adornment of the tree of enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfill the perfection of all merits?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills the sublime provisions of merit and wisdom, matures sentient beings, and purifies buddha-fields, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s fulfillment of the perfection of all qualities.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 54; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 55.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Fifteen: Distinguishing the Mahāyāna, Part Five.
"World-Honored One!
How should one know that a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who has already perfected the tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā), is to be spoken of as no different from all Tathāgatas?"
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already perfected the six pāramitās; he has already perfected the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions;
he has already perfected the four foundations of mindfulness and the four right endeavors...”
He has perfected the [four] bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
he has perfected the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he has perfected the five eyes and the six supernormal knowledges; and he has perfected the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and the four... [analytical knowledges].
The analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha,
all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects— because he has already perfected all Buddha-dharmas, and furthermore,
because he has forever severed the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies, he abides as a Buddha.
"Ground.
Therefore, you should know that a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has already perfected the tenth ground, the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā), is to be spoken of as no different from all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva in the tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā), proceed toward the stage of a Tathāgata?
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, through skillful means, practices the six pāramitās and cultivates the dhyānas,
the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the three gates of liberation.”
Having studied the five eyes, the six supernormal powers, the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses,
the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*),
the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as all the Buddha-dharmas.
Because of this perfection, one transcends the stage of pure observation, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having seen the truth,
the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the solitary realizer, and the ten stages of the bodhisattva;
having forever severed the continuity of the habitual tendencies of afflictions, one becomes a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha.
"Awakened!
Subhūti, it is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva on the tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma, proceeds toward the stage of a Tathāgata."
"Subhūti, you should know that this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out upon the Great Vehicle.
Furthermore, Subhūti,"
Regarding your question as to where this Great Vehicle emerges from and where it abides, Subhūti:

this Great Vehicle emerges from within the three realms and abides within the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). It is because it emerges from the three realms for the sake of the knowledge of all modes that it does so; yet, because there is no duality, there is neither emerging nor arriving.

Why is this so? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these two dharmas are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta). In the dharma of signlessness, there is no departing and no arriving.
Why is this? Subhūti!
A dharma that is signless has not already emerged or arrived, will not emerge or arrive, and does not emerge or arrive in the present.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they would likewise wish for true thusness (tathatā) to have an emergence or an arrival. Why is this? Because...”
Suchness cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Suchness is empty of its own intrinsic nature, Subhūti.

Should anyone wish to cause the signless dharma to emerge or to arrive, they would thereby wish to cause the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the state beyond arising, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, the unconditioned realm, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, original non-arising, and the limit of reality to emerge or to arrive.
Why is this so? Because from the dharma-realm up to the limit of reality, they cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the dharma-realm is empty of the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, and so on, up to the limit of reality being empty of the intrinsic nature of the limit of reality.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for form to have emergence and arrival. Why is this? Because...”
Form cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
"Subhūti, because each and every form is empty of its own intrinsic nature,
whoever wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness to have an emergence or an arrival."
Why is this? Feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they would likewise wish for the sense base of the eye to have emergence or arrival. Why is that?
The eye-base cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The eye-base is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-base. Subhūti!
Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) to have emergence and arrival. Why is that?
The sphere of form cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of omniscience.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The sphere of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form. Subhūti!
Whoever wishes for signless phenomena to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects to have emergence and arrival.
Why is this? The sense bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they would thereby wish for the eye-element to have emergence and arrival. Why is this?
The eye-element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The eye-element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-element. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they wish for the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because the form realm, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The realm of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realm of form, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, which are empty of the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they would likewise wish for the ear-element to have an emergence or an arrival. Why is that?
The ear-element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The ear-element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the ear-element. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they would thereby wish for the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the sphere of sound is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of sound, and so on, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition being empty of the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they would likewise wish for the nose-element to have emergence and arrival. Why is that?
The nose-element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The nose element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the nose element. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because the realm of fragrance, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The realm of fragrance is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realm of fragrance, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, which are empty of the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they would likewise wish for the tongue-element to have emergence and arrival. Why is this so?
The tongue-element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of omniscience.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The tongue element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the tongue element. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The taste element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, which are empty of the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the body-element to have emergence and arrival. Why is that? Because...”
The body-element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The body element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the body element. Subhūti!

One who wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, would thereby wish for the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with the sphere of tangibles as a condition, up to and including those produced with body-contact as a condition, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The sphere of tangibles is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of tangibles, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as a condition, which are empty of the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as a condition.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the mental element (manodhātu) to have emergence and arrival. Why is that?
The mind-element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of omniscience.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The mind-element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the mind-element. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for signless phenomena to have emergence or arrival, they thereby wish for the dharma-realm, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact—as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—to have emergence or arrival.

Why is this? Because the dharma-realm, and even the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes of being (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The dharma-realm is empty of the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, which are empty of the intrinsic nature of the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they would be wishing for the earth element to have an emergence or an arrival. Why is that?
The earth element cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of omniscience.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The earth element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the earth element. Subhūti!
Whoever wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness to have an emergence or an arrival.
Why is this? Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide in the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is that? Subhūti!
Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the Noble Truth of Suffering to have emergence and arrival.”
Why is this? The Noble Truth of Suffering cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Subhūti!"
Whoever wishes for the dharma of signlessness to have emergence or arrival, wishes for the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path to have emergence and arrival.

Why is this? The noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
"Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for ignorance to have emergence and arrival. Why is this? Because..."
Ignorance cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Ignorance is empty of the intrinsic nature of ignorance. Subhūti,

whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair to have an emergence or an arrival.

Why is this? Because conditioned phenomena, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, cannot lead one out from within the three realms, nor can they cause one to abide in the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The nature of the practice of formations is empty; even up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for illusory phenomena to have emergence and arrival. Why is this? Because...”
An illusory phenomenon cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because illusory phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of illusory phenomena. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for signless dharmas to have emergence or arrival, they would likewise wish for dreams, images, echoes, reflections, flowers in the sky, mirages, cities of the gandharvas, and transformations to have emergence or arrival.
Why is this? Because dream-objects, and even things produced by transformation, cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the dream-object is empty of the intrinsic nature of a dream-object, and so on, up to the fact that a conjured phenomenon is empty of the intrinsic nature of a conjured phenomenon.
"Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for internal emptiness to have emergence and arrival. Why is that?
Internal emptiness cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of omniscience.
Why is this? Subhūti!
"Subhūti, inner emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of inner emptiness. Subhūti, whoever wishes for a signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival,

would thereby wish for outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature to have an emergence or an arrival."

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can it reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

External emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of external emptiness, up to and including the fact that the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) to have emergence and arrival.”
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of being.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because the perfection of giving is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving.
"Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom to have an emergence or an arrival."

Why is this? Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti,

it is because the self-nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is empty of the self-nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the four dhyānas to have emergence and arrival.”
Why is this? The four dhyānas cannot lead one out from within the three realms, nor can they bring one to abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Why is that?
“Subhūti! The four dhyānas are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas. Subhūti!”
If anyone wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence and arrival, they would likewise wish to cause the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions to have emergence and arrival.

Why is this? Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions cannot lead one out from within the three realms, nor can they cause one to abide in the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is that? Subhūti!
This is because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they thereby wish for the four foundations of mindfulness to have emergence and arrival.”
Why is this? The four foundations of mindfulness cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Why is that?
"Subhūti! The four applications of mindfulness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Subhūti!"

Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path to have an emergence and an arrival.

Why is this so? Because the four right endeavors, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

This is because the four right efforts are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts, and so on, up to the eightfold noble path being empty of the intrinsic nature of the eightfold noble path.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the gate of liberation that is emptiness to have emergence or arrival.”
Why is this? The gate of liberation of emptiness cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Subhūti!"
If one wishes to cause the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, then one wishes to cause the signless and wishless doors of liberation to have an emergence or an arrival.
Why is this? The gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the gateways of liberation— signlessness and wishlessness— are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gateways of liberation— signlessness and wishlessness.
"Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they wish for the five eyes to have emergence or arrival. Why is that? "
The five eyes cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The five eyes are empty of the intrinsic nature of the five eyes. Subhūti!
Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, wishes for the six supernormal powers to have emergence and arrival.
Why is this? Because the six supernormal powers cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The six supernormal powers are empty of the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers. Subhūti!"
If there were anyone who wished for the dharma of signlessness to have emergence or arrival, they would be wishing for the Buddha’s ten powers to have emergence or arrival. Why is this?
The ten powers of a Buddha cannot emerge from within the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of intrinsic nature. Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, wishes for the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects to have emergence and arrival.
Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!

This is because the four fearlessnesses are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses, and so on, up to the fact that all-aspect omniscience is empty of the intrinsic nature of all-aspect omniscience.
"Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, wishes for the stream-enterer to have an emergence or an arrival in the states of miserable rebirth."
Why is this? Because one who has entered the stream cannot escape birth in the evil destinies from within the three realms, nor can they abide in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because the rebirth in the evil destinies of a stream-enterer is empty of the intrinsic nature of the rebirth in the evil destinies of a stream-enterer.

Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have emergence, arrival, or reaching, would likewise wish for the once-returner to come back frequently, for the non-returner to be born in the desire realm, for the Mahāsattva’s birth for his own benefit, and for the Arhat, the Pratyekabuddha, and the Samyaksaṃbuddha to have subsequent birth, emergence, or reaching.

Why is this? Because one who has attained the stage of Once-returner (sakṛdāgāmin) returns to birth repeatedly; even up to the stage of Samyaksaṃbuddha, there remains further birth from which they cannot emerge out of the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the once-returner who repeatedly returns to birth is empty; even up to the perfectly awakened Buddha (*samyaksaṃbuddha*), the nature of the perfectly awakened Buddha is empty.
"Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they wish for the one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry to have an emergence or an arrival."

Why is this? Those who have entered the stream (srotāpanna) and those who abide in the fruit of stream-entry cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they reach and abide within the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

This is because the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry itself, and the intrinsic nature of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry are all empty.
"Subhūti!

Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, would thereby wish for the fruit of a once-returner and the path leading thereto, the fruit of a non-returner and the path leading thereto, the fruit of an arhat and the path leading thereto, the fruit of a pratyekabuddha and the path leading thereto, or for bodhisattvas and tathāgatas to have an emergence or an arrival."

Why is this? Because one who is a candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to and including a Tathāgata, cannot emerge from the three realms, nor can they abide within the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñajñāna).
Why is this? Subhūti!

The candidate for the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, and the candidate for the fruit of once-returning are empty of their own intrinsic nature, up to and including the Tathāgata, who is empty of his own intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti! Whoever wishes for the signless dharma to have an emergence or an arrival, they wish for names, designations, conventions, and verbal expressions to have an emergence or an arrival.”

Why is this? Names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions cannot emerge from within the three realms, nor can they reach and abide in the wisdom of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!

This is because names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions are empty of the intrinsic nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions.

“Subhūti! Whoever wishes to cause the signless dharma to have emergence or arrival, they would thereby wish to cause that which is unborn and unceasing, unstained and unpurified, signless and unconditioned to have emergence or arrival.”

Why is this? Because that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and without marks and unconditioned, cannot emerge from the triple world, nor can it abide within the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Subhūti!

It is because that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, without marks and unconditioned—being without arising, without cessation, without defilement, without purification, without marks, and unconditioned—is empty of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! For this reason, this Great Vehicle emerges from the triple world and abides within the knowledge of all modes; yet because it is non-dual, there is neither emergence nor arrival, for the signless dharma is without movement or transition.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Regarding your question as to where this Great Vehicle dwells:
Subhūti, this Great Vehicle does not dwell anywhere at all."
Why is this? Because all phenomena are without any place of abiding.
For what reason?
Because the abiding place of all phenomena cannot be apprehended, Subhūti!
This Great Vehicle, however, abides in non-abiding.
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of suchness neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of true thusness neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is empty of the nature of *tathatā*. Subhūti!

Just as the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of wishlessness, the realm of the unconditioned, the realm of security, the realm of tranquility, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), primordial non-arising, and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) are neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the nature of the limit of reality, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The nature of the dharma-realm is empty of the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the nature of the limit of reality being empty of the nature of the limit of reality. Subhūti!"
Just as the nature of form neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of form has neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because the nature of form is empty of the nature of form.
"Subhūti!
Just as the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness neither abides nor does not abide, so too it is with the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this? "
Because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. "Subhūti!
Just as the nature of the eye-base neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-base neither abides nor does it not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
This is because the nature of the eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Subhūti!"
Just as the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
The nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
"Subhūti! Just as the nature of the sense base of form neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of form neither abides nor does it not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti! This is because the nature of the sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Subhūti!"

Just as the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Mahāyāna: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty of the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
"Subhūti, just as the nature of the eye-sphere neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-element neither abides nor does it not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The nature of the eye-element is empty of the nature of the eye-element. Subhūti!"

Just as the nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*): it is neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), up to the nature of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the form realm is empty of the nature of the form realm, up to and including the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, which is empty of the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition."
"Subhūti! Just as the nature of the ear-element neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the ear-element neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element, Subhūti!

Just as the nature of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition neither abide nor do not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this so? Because the nature of the sound-element, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the sound-element is empty of the nature of the sound-element, and so on, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition being empty of the nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition."
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of the nose-element is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of the nose-element neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the nose-element is empty of the nature of the nose-element. Subhūti!

Just as the nature of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the nature of the fragrance-element, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the fragrance-element is empty of the nature of the fragrance-element, up to and including the nature of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, which is empty of the nature of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition."
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of the tongue-element neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the tongue-element neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the tongue-element is empty of the nature of the tongue-element. Subhūti!

Just as the nature of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, neither abide nor do not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the nature of the taste-element, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the taste element is empty of the nature of the taste element, up to and including the nature of all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, which is empty of the nature of all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition."
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of the body element neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the body-element neither abides nor does it not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The nature of the body-element is empty of the nature of the body-element. Subhūti!

Just as the nature of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact—and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of tangibles, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the sphere of tangibles is empty of the nature of the sphere of tangibles, up to and including the nature of the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as a condition being empty of the nature of those various feelings produced with body-tangibles as a condition."
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of the element of consciousness neither abides nor does not abide, so it is with the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the mental faculty has neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Subhūti!

Just as the nature of the dharma-realm, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact—and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, up to the nature of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the dharma-realm is empty of the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition being empty of the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition."
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of the earth element neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the earth element neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element. Subhūti!
Just as the natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements neither abide nor do not abide, so too it is with the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the natures of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness neither abide nor do not abide. Why is this so?
"Subhūti!
The nature of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is empty because the nature of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is emptiness. Subhūti!"
Just as the nature of the Noble Truth of Suffering neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the Noble Truth of Suffering has neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering.
"Subhūti!
Just as the nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this? "
Because the nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path is empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
"Subhūti, just as the nature of ignorance neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this so? Because the nature of ignorance neither abides nor does it not abide.
For what reason?
"Subhūti!
Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Subhūti!"

Just as the nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Why is this? Because the nature of volitional formations, up to and including the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this so?

Subhūti! The nature of volitional formations is empty of the nature of volitional formations, up to and including the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, which is empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. This is because they are so.
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of an illusory phenomenon neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of illusory phenomena neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Because the nature of illusory phenomena is empty of the nature of illusory phenomena. Subhūti!

Just as the nature of dreams, reflections, echoes, optical illusions, flowers in the sky, mirages, cities of the gandharvas, and transformations neither abides nor does not abide, so too it is with the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the nature of dream-objects, up to and including the nature of transformed phenomena, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The nature of a dream is empty of the nature of a dream, up to and including the nature of a transformation is empty of the nature of a transformation. Subhūti!"
Just as the emptiness of the internal is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the internal has neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is that? Subhūti!
Because the emptiness of the internal is empty of the emptiness of the internal.
"Subhūti!

Just as the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle; it is neither abiding nor non-abiding."
Why is this? Because from the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, there is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this so?
"Subhūti!

The emptiness of external phenomena is empty of the emptiness of external phenomena, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature being empty of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. Subhūti!"
Just as the nature of the perfection of giving neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the perfection of generosity is neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the perfection of giving is empty of the nature of the perfection of giving.

Subhūti, just as the natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom neither abide nor do not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

This is because the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is empty of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“Subhūti! Just as the nature of the four dhyānas is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
Because the nature of the four dhyānas is neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the four dhyānas is empty of the nature of the four dhyānas.
Subhūti, just as the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this so? Because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are by nature neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments. Subhūti!"
Just as the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is without abiding and without non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This is because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness.
"Subhūti!

Just as the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the nature of the eightfold noble path, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!

The nature of the four right endeavors is empty of the nature of the four right endeavors, up to and including the nature of the eight branches of the noble path being empty of the nature of the eight branches of the noble path. Subhūti!"
Just as the nature of the emptiness liberation door is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
Because the nature of the emptiness liberation door has neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness.
"Subhūti!
Just as the nature of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding."
Why is this? Because the nature of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is neither abiding nor non-abiding.
For what reason?
“Subhūti!
The nature of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is signless; it is empty of the nature of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Subhūti!”
Just as the nature of the five eyes neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?
Because the nature of the five eyes neither has an abiding nor a non-abiding.
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the nature of the five eyes is empty of the nature of the five eyes.
"Subhūti!
Just as the nature of the six supernormal powers neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this? Because..."
Because the nature of the six supernormal powers neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the nature of the six supernormal powers is empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers.
"Subhūti, just as the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide."
Why is this? Because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?
"Subhūti!
This is because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is empty of the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers. Subhūti!"

Just as the nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle neither abiding nor non-abiding.
Why is this? Because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to the nature of the knowledge of all aspects, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

Subhūti! The nature of the four fearlessnesses is empty of the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the nature of all-aspect omniscience being empty of the nature of all-aspect omniscience.

“Subhūti! Just as the nature of rebirth in the evil destinies for a stream-enterer is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so it is with the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
For one who has entered the stream, there is neither abiding nor non-abiding in the nature of birth in the miserable realms.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The nature of birth in the miserable realms for a stream-enterer is empty of the nature of birth in the miserable realms for a stream-enterer. Subhūti!

Just as the nature of birth in the frequent-returning realm for a once-returner, the nature of birth in the desire realm for a non-returner, the nature of birth for the benefit of oneself by a mahāsattva, and the nature of subsequent birth for an arhat, a pratyekabuddha, or a samyaksaṃbuddha—neither abides nor does not abide—so too it is with the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.

Why is this? Because for one who has attained the stage of Once-returner, from the nature of being subject to further births up until the state of Samyaksambuddha, there is no abiding and no non-abiding regarding the nature of future existence.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the nature of one who returns once more (sakṛdāgāmin) to be born again is empty of that nature of returning once more to be born again; and so on, up to the nature of a perfectly awakened Buddha (samyaksaṃbuddha) to have further births is empty of that nature of a perfectly awakened Buddha to have further births.

“Subhūti! Just as the nature of one who has entered the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is this?
Because the nature of one who is a candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself neither abides nor does not abide.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Because the nature of one entering the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the nature of one entering the stream, and the fruit of stream-entry are empty.

Subhūti! Just as the nature of one entering the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning; one entering the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning; one entering the fruit of arhatship, the fruit of arhatship; one entering the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood, the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood; a bodhisattva, and a tathāgata—does not abide and does not not abide—so too it is with the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does it not abide.
Why is this so? Because the nature of one who is heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to and including the nature of a Tathāgata, neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that?

Subhūti! This is because the nature of one who is practicing for the fruit of once-returning is empty of the nature of one who is practicing for the fruit of once-returning, and so on, up to the nature of a Tathāgata being empty of the nature of a Tathāgata.

“Subhūti! Just as the nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions neither abides nor does not abide, so too is the Great Vehicle: it neither abides nor does not abide.”
Why is this so? Because names, conceptualizations, designations, and verbal expressions have a nature that neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this?

Subhūti! This is because names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions are empty of the nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions.

“Subhūti! Just as that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and whose unconditioned nature is neither abiding nor non-abiding, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither abiding nor non-abiding.”
Why is this? Because it is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, without marks and unconditioned; its nature neither abides nor does not abide. Why is this so?
Subhūti!

It is because that which is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and whose nature is signless and unconditioned, is empty of being without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and signless and unconditioned.
“Subhūti! For this reason, although this Great Vehicle has no abode whatsoever, it abides in non-abiding.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
Regarding your question, "Who, moreover, rides upon this Great Vehicle and departs? Subhūti,
there is absolutely no one who rides upon this Great Vehicle and departs.

Why is this so? Whether it be the vehicle that is mounted upon, the one who mounts it, the means by which or for the sake of which [one travels], the place from which one departs, the destination reached, or the time of departure and arrival—all such things are non-existent and entirely unobtainable.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because all phenomena are non-existent and entirely unapprehendable, being ultimately pure, how could one speak of a vehicle, a traveler, the means by which one travels, the destination reached, or the time of reaching that destination?
“Subhūti, you should know that because ‘I’ do not exist and cannot be apprehended, one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Thus, because sentient beings, life-principles, born beings, nourished beings, persons, individuals, mind-born beings, young scholars, agents, those who cause to act, originators, those who cause to originate, experiencers, those who cause to experience, knowers, and seers do not exist and cannot be apprehended, even one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended.
Why is that? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because true thusness is non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Because the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, equality, the state beyond birth, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of wishlessness, the unconditioned realm, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, original non-arising, and the limit of reality are all non-existent and unapprehendable, so too is the one who rides the Great Vehicle unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because form is non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
In this way, because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the eye-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
In this way, because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the sense-base of form does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
In this way, because the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the eye-faculty does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because they are ultimately pure.

In this way, because the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the ear-element is non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure (*atyanta-viśuddhi*).

In this way, because the realm of fragrance, the realm of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the tongue element is non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the element of taste, the element of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the body-element (kāyadhātu) is non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the mind-element (manodhātu) is non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Thus, because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 55.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One: Chapter Fifteen, Distinguishing the Mahāyāna, Section Six.
“Subhūti, you should know that because the earth element does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.
Thus, because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Sudhana, you should know this!"
Because the Noble Truth of Suffering is non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
Because these noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are non-existent and unobtainable, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle is unobtainable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because ignorance does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because they are ultimately pure.
