Thus, because volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because illusory phenomena are non-existent and unobtainable, those who ride the Great Vehicle are likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

Just as these dream-visions, reflections, echoes, shadows, optical illusions, flowers in the sky, mirages, cities of the Gandharvas, and conjured phenomena are non-existent and unattainable, so too is the one who rides the Great Vehicle unattainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because internal emptiness is non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

Thus, because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the perfection of giving is non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the four dhyānas and the state of nothingness are unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.
Because these four immeasurables and four formless absorptions are non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the four foundations of mindfulness do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because they are ultimately pure.

Since these four right efforts, four bases of power, five faculties, five powers, seven factors of enlightenment, and eightfold noble path do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle likewise cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent and unattainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
In this way, because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-existent and unattainable, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is unattainable. Why is this so?
Because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because the five eyes do not exist and cannot be apprehended, even one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because they are ultimately pure.
Since these six supernormal powers are non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because they are ultimately pure.

In this way, because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because for a stream-enterer, rebirth in the evil destinies does not exist and cannot be found, even one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be found. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the birth of a once-returner, a frequent-returner, a non-returner, a self-benefiting Mahāsattva, an Arhat, a Pratyekabuddha, or a Samyaksaṃbuddha is ultimately non-existent and unobtainable, even one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself are non-existent and unobtainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the candidate for the fruit of once-returner, the once-returner, the candidate for the fruit of non-returner, the non-returner, the candidate for the fruit of arhatship, the arhat, the candidate for the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood, the pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva, and the Tathāgata are all non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

Because names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti,

you should know that because there is no arising and no cessation, no defilement and no purity, no mark and no unconditioned, and nothing that exists or can be apprehended, even the one who rides the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the prior, middle, and subsequent limits do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who rides the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because coming and going do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know that because going and staying are non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because non-arising, non-existence, and non-apprehensibility are [themselves] unapprehendable, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because increase and decrease do not exist and cannot be apprehended, even one who mounts the Great Vehicle cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure. "Subhūti,
you should know that because the Stage of Extreme Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi) does not exist and cannot be apprehended, even the one who mounts the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.

Thus, because the Stainless Ground, the Radiant Ground, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Immovable Ground, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are non-existent and unattainable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unattainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the Stage of Pure Observation is non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.

In this way, because the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of possessing vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of having completed what was to be done, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, and the stage of the Tathāgata are non-existent and unobtainable, the one who rides the Great Vehicle is likewise unobtainable.
Why is this? Because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"
Because the maturation of sentient beings is non-existent and unapprehendable, the one who mounts the Great Vehicle is likewise unapprehendable. Why is this?
Because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti, you should know that because the purification of buddha-fields is non-existent and unattainable, those who ride the Great Vehicle are likewise unattainable. Why is this?
“Because it is ultimately pure.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
“Because what dharma cannot be apprehended, is it said that the self and so forth cannot be apprehended?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the nature of a self cannot be apprehended, it is said that a self cannot be apprehended;
and so on, up to: because the nature of a seer cannot be apprehended, it is said that a seer cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because the nature of the self, up to the nature of the seer, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of suchness cannot be apprehended, it is said that suchness is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the nature of the limit of reality cannot be apprehended, it is said that the limit of reality is unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of suchness, up to and including the nature of the limit of reality, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of form cannot be apprehended, it is said that form cannot be apprehended;
and so on, up to: because the nature of consciousness cannot be apprehended, it is said that consciousness cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because the nature of form, up to and including the nature of consciousness, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-base is unapprehendable, it is said that the eye-base is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the intrinsic nature of the mind-base is unapprehendable, it is said that the mind-base is unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of the eye, up to the nature of the sense-base of the mind, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form cannot be apprehended, one says that the sphere of form is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the intrinsic nature of the sphere of mental phenomena cannot be apprehended, one says that the sphere of mental phenomena is unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of form, up to the nature of the sense-base of mental phenomena, has not been obtained, will not be obtained, and is not currently obtainable, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of the eye-element is unapprehendable, it is said that the eye-element is unapprehendable;

and so on, up to: because the nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is unapprehendable, it is said that all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-element, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that the ear-element is unapprehendable;

and so on, up to: because the nature of all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition (*śrotra-saṃsparśa-pratyaya-ja-vedanā*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the ear-element, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is unapprehendable, it is said that the nose-element is unapprehendable;

up to and including, because the nature of all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is unapprehendable, it is said that all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the nose element, up to and including the nature of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, because they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that the tongue-element is unapprehendable;

up to and including, because the nature of all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition (*jihvā-saṃsparśa-pratyaya-ja-vedanā*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the tongue-element, up to and including the nature of the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, because they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the body element (*kāyadhātu*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that the body element is unapprehendable;

and so on, up to: because the nature of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended, it is said that the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the body element, up to the nature of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that the mind-element is unapprehendable;

and so on, up to: because the nature of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition cannot be apprehended, it is said that all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the mental faculty element (*manodhātu*), up to the nature of the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the earth element is unapprehendable, it is said that the earth element is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the nature of the consciousness element is unapprehendable, it is said that the consciousness element is unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the earth element, up to and including the nature of the consciousness element, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended, it is said that the noble truth of suffering is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the nature of the noble truth of the path cannot be apprehended, it is said that the noble truth of the path is unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering, up to the nature of the noble truth of the path, cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being about to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being presently attained, because they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of ignorance cannot be apprehended, it is said that ignorance cannot be apprehended;

and so on, up to: because the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair cannot be apprehended, it is said that old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because the nature of ignorance, up to and including the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of an illusory phenomenon cannot be apprehended, one says that an illusory phenomenon is unapprehendable;
up to and including, because the nature of a transformation cannot be apprehended, one says that a transformation is unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of illusory phenomena, up to and including the nature of transformed phenomena, cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the internal is unapprehendable, one says that the internal is unapprehendable;
up to and including, because the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is unapprehendable, one says that the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the internal nature up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and is not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended, it is said that the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended;
and so on, up to: because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended, it is said that the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of generosity up to the nature of the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended, it is said that the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended;
and so on, up to the fact that because the nature of the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended, it is said that the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four dhyānas, up to and including the nature of the four formless attainments, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended, it is said that the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the intrinsic nature of the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended, it is said that the eight branches of the noble path are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the nature of the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness cannot be apprehended, it is said that the gate of liberation of emptiness is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of wishlessness cannot be apprehended, it is said that the gate of liberation of wishlessness is unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness, up to and including the nature of the gate of liberation of wishlessness, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of the five eyes cannot be apprehended, it is said that the five eyes are unapprehendable;
because the nature of the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended, it is said that the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of the five eyes and the nature of the six supernormal powers are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended, it is said that the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended;
and so on, up to: because the nature of all-aspect omniscience cannot be apprehended, it is said that all-aspect omniscience cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers, up to and including the nature of all-aspect omniscience, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of birth in the miserable realms cannot be apprehended in a stream-enterer, it is said that birth in the miserable realms cannot be apprehended for a stream-enterer;

and so on, up to: because the nature of further birth after attaining perfect enlightenment (samyaksaṃbuddha) cannot be apprehended, it is said that further birth after attaining perfect enlightenment cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because for one who has entered the stream (srotāpanna), the nature of rebirth in the evil destinies, up to and including the nature of further rebirth after attaining perfect enlightenment (samyaksaṃbuddha), is neither obtainable in the past, nor obtainable in the future, nor obtainable in the present; for it is ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of one who has entered the stream and the fruit of stream-entry are unapprehendable, it is said that one who has entered the stream and the fruit of stream-entry are unapprehendable;
up to and including, because the nature of a Tathāgata is unapprehendable, it is said that a Tathāgata is unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of one who has entered the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, up to and including the nature of a Tathāgata, is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti! Because the nature of names, designations, conventions, and verbal expressions cannot be apprehended, it is said that names, designations, conventions, and verbal expressions are unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the nature of names, conceptual designations, provisional establishments, and verbal expressions cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present; for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of non-arising and non-ceasing, non-defilement and non-purity, and signlessness and unconditionedness cannot be apprehended, it is said that non-arising and non-ceasing, non-defilement and non-purity, and signlessness and unconditionedness cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because the nature that is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, and without marks and unconditioned, cannot be obtained in the past, cannot be obtained in the future, and cannot be obtained in the present; for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the prior, middle, and posterior limits cannot be apprehended, it is said that the prior, middle, and posterior limits are unapprehendable. Why is this?

The nature of the past, present, and future limits cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being about to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being currently attained, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti!..."
Because the nature of coming and going cannot be apprehended, it is said that coming and going cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
The nature of coming and going is not already apprehendable, will not be apprehendable, and is not presently apprehendable, because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of going and staying cannot be apprehended, it is said that going and staying cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
The nature of going and staying cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of death and birth cannot be apprehended, one says that death and birth are unapprehendable."
Why is this? The nature of birth and death cannot be apprehended in the past, cannot be apprehended in the future, and cannot be apprehended in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti!..."
Because the nature of increase and decrease cannot be apprehended, it is said that increase and decrease are unapprehendable. Why is this?
The nature of increase and decrease is not apprehended in the past, will not be apprehended in the future, and is not apprehended in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the Ground of Great Joy is unapprehendable, it is said that the Ground of Great Joy is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, because its nature is unapprehendable, it is said that the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma is unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the nature of the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of the stage of pure observation (*śuklavidarśanābhūmi*) cannot be apprehended, it is said that the stage of pure observation is unapprehendable;
and so on, up to: because the nature of the stage of the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended, it is said that the stage of the Tathāgata is unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the stage of pure observation (*śuddhadarśana-bhūmi*) up to the nature of the stage of the Tathāgata is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of maturing sentient beings cannot be apprehended, it is said that the maturation of sentient beings cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The nature of sentient beings that has reached maturity cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as being about to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being presently attained, because it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti!..."
Because the nature of the purification of Buddha-fields is unobtainable, one speaks of the unobtainability of the purification of Buddha-fields. Why is this?
The nature of the purification of Buddha-fields is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Because the nature of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that generosity up to the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended;

and so on, until: because the nature of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that generosity up to the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because herein the nature of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.

"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended;

and so on, up to: because the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because within this, the natures of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, it is said that the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended;

and so on, because the intrinsic nature of the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because herein, the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because it is ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is unapprehendable within internal emptiness, one says that the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unapprehendable;

and so on, up to: because the nature of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is unapprehendable within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, one says that the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? Because the nature of these doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that the five eyes and the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended;

and so on, up to: because the nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that the five eyes and the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because herein, the nature of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended;

and so on, up to: because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because herein, the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects is not something that has been attained, will be attained, or is being attained now, because it is ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of the stream-enterer candidate and the fruit of stream-entry, the once-returner candidate and the fruit of once-returning, the non-returner candidate and the fruit of non-returning, the arhat candidate and the fruit of arhatship, the pratyekabuddha candidate and the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood, and the bodhisattva-tathāgata-nature cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that the stream-enterer candidate and the fruit of stream-entry, up to the bodhisattva-tathāgata, cannot be apprehended.

Furthermore, because the nature of the stream-enterer candidate and the fruit of stream-entry, the once-returner candidate and the fruit of once-returning, the non-returner candidate and the fruit of non-returning, the arhat candidate and the fruit of arhatship, the pratyekabuddha candidate and the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood, and the bodhisattva-tathāgata-nature cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that the stream-enterer candidate and the fruit of stream-entry, up to the bodhisattva-tathāgata, cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because herein, the state of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; the state of one entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning; the state of one entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning; the state of one entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship; the state of one entering pratyekabuddhahood and the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood; and the nature of a bodhisattva and a tathāgata—these are not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Manifestation, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud cannot be apprehended;

and so on, because the nature of the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Manifestation, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that the Stage of Extreme Joy up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Because herein, the nature of the Ground of Perfect Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud cannot be apprehended as having been attained, cannot be apprehended as yet to be attained, and cannot be apprehended as being currently attained, because they are ultimately pure.

"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the stage of pure observation (*śuklavidarśanā-bhūmi*), the stage of the lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamaka-bhūmi*), the stage of having vision (*darśana-bhūmi*), the stage of refinement (*tanū-bhūmi*), the stage of freedom from desire (*vītarāga-bhūmi*), the stage of completion (*kṛtāvi-bhūmi*), the stage of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha-bhūmi*), the stage of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattva-bhūmi*), and the stage of the Tathāgata (*tathāgata-bhūmi*) cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), it is said that the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended.

Furthermore, because the intrinsic nature of the stage of pure observation, the stage of the lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, and the stage of the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*), it is said that the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? Because herein, the natures of the stage of pure observation, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of possessing vision, the stage of attenuation, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of having accomplished what was to be done, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, and the stage of the Tathāgata are not obtainable in the past, will not be obtainable in the future, and are not obtainable in the present, because they are ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of maturing sentient beings cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, it is said that maturing sentient beings cannot be apprehended;

and so on, up to: because the nature of maturing sentient beings cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said that maturing sentient beings cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because herein, the nature of maturing sentient beings is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of purifying a buddha-field cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness, one says that purifying a buddha-field cannot be apprehended;

up to and including, because the nature of purifying a buddha-field cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, one says that purifying a buddha-field cannot be apprehended."
Why is this? Because herein, the nature of the purified Buddha-field is not obtainable in the past, not obtainable in the future, and not obtainable in the present, for it is ultimately pure.
"So it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, although they observe that all phenomena are non-existent and unapprehendable because they are ultimately pure, there is no one who departs by means of the Great Vehicle; yet, employing the method of non-apprehension, they mount the Great Vehicle, depart from the cycle of birth and death within the triple world, and reach the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings, continuing without interruption until the end of the future."
Chapter 16: Praising the Mahāyāna, Part One. Chapter Sixteen, "Praising the Mahāyāna," Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, you speak of the 'Mahāyāna. This Mahāyāna surpasses all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras; it is the most honored and the most sublime."

In this way, the Mahāyāna is equal to space; just as space can universally contain countless, immeasurable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Mahāyāna universally contain countless, immeasurable, and boundless sentient beings.
Furthermore, just as space cannot be seen to come, go, or abide, so too is the Mahāyāna: it cannot be seen to come, go, or abide.

Moreover, just as the prior, posterior, and middle limits of space are all unattainable, so too are the prior, posterior, and middle limits of the Mahāyāna all unattainable; because the three periods of time are equal, it is called the Mahāyāna.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.
A bodhisattva’s Great Vehicle possesses such boundless qualities as these, Subhūti!
One should know that this Mahāyāna is precisely the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

You should know that this Great Vehicle is precisely inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

You should know that this Great Vehicle is the *Vīryapāramitā-samādhi* (Samādhi of Heroic Stride), and so forth, including the *Asaṅga-ākāśa-samādhi* (Samādhi of Non-attachment like Space) and countless hundreds of thousands of such samādhi-gates.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

You should know that this Great Vehicle is precisely the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
You should know that this Great Vehicle is precisely the three samādhis, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
In this way, you should know that this Mahāyāna is precisely all the dharanī-doors, such as the dharanī of letters. Subhūti!
You should know that such immeasurable and boundless, preeminent merits are all the Mahāyāna of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! As for what you said:
'The Great Vehicle surpasses all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras; it is the most honored and the most sublime. "
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
Why is that? Subhūti!

If the realm of desire were suchness—neither false nor inverted, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of gods, humans, and asuras.

Because the desire realm is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is merely a designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
“Subhūti!

If form and the formless realm were suchness—neither false nor inverted, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the realms of form and formlessness are not suchness—they are false, inverted, and merely provisional; they are neither truth nor reality; they are impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If form were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor provisional; if it were truth, reality, permanent, eternal, unchanging, immutable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because form is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
“Subhūti!

If feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness were suchness—neither false nor inverted, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not suchness—because they are false, inverted, provisional designations, neither truth nor reality, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the eye-base were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor merely conventional; if it were truth, reality, permanent, eternal, unchanging, immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the eye-base is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind were suchness—neither false nor inverted, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be honored or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not suchness—they are false, inverted, and merely provisional; they are neither truth nor reality; they are impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—therefore this Mahāyāna is honored and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the sphere of form were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor merely conventional; if it were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.”

Because the sphere of form is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti! If the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena were suchness—neither false nor erroneous, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not suchness—they are false, inverted, mere designations, neither true nor real, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds including the devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the eye-element were suchness—neither false, nor perverted, nor a mere designation; if it were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the eye-element is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, were suchness—neither false nor inverted, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing a substantial nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are not suchness; because they are false, inverted, and merely provisional; because they are neither truth nor reality, being impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—therefore, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing and excelling all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the ear-element were suchness—neither false, nor perverted, nor merely provisional; if it were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the ear-element is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
“Subhūti!

If the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition were the *tathatā* (suchness)—if they were not false, not inverted, not merely designated, but were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are not suchness—they are false, inverted, provisional, neither truth nor reality, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

"Subhūti! If the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor merely provisional; if it were truth, reality, permanent, eternal, unchanging, immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the nose element is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor merely conventional; if they were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are not suchness; because they are false, inverted, and merely provisional; because they are neither truth nor reality; because they are impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—therefore, this Mahāyāna is honored and sublime, surpassing all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the tongue-element were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor provisional; if it were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the tongue-element is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is honored and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
Subhūti!

If the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition were the true suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor merely provisional; if they were the truth, the reality, eternal, constant, unchanging, immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are not suchness—because they are false, inverted, provisional designations, neither truth nor reality, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the body-element (kāyadhātu) were the true suchness (tathatā)—if it were not false, not inverted, not a mere designation, but were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the body-element is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition were the true suchness (tathatā)—if they were not false, not inverted, not provisional, but were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the contact of the body—as well as all feelings produced with that bodily contact as a condition—are not suchness; because they are false, inverted, and merely provisional; because they are neither truth nor reality, being impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature; therefore, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the mind-element were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor merely provisional; if it were truth, reality, permanent, eternal, unchanging, immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of gods, humans, and asuras.”

Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is not suchness—it is false, inverted, a mere designation, neither truth nor reality, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the dharma-realm, the consciousness-realm, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition were suchness—neither false nor inverted, not a mere designation, but true and real, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, possessing a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are not suchness; because they are false, inverted, provisional designations, neither truth nor reality, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—therefore, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the earth element were suchness—neither false, nor inverted, nor provisional; if it were truth and reality, eternal and constant, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the earth element is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of an intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness were the true suchness—were not false, not perverted, not merely provisional, but were truth and reality, permanent and eternal, unchanging and immutable, and possessed of a real nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are not suchness—being false, inverted, and merely provisional; being neither truth nor reality; being impermanent and non-eternal; subject to change and transformation; and entirely lacking any real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If ignorance were suchness—neither false, nor perverted, nor merely provisional; if it were the truth, the reality, eternal, constant, unchanging, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, and it would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because ignorance is not suchness—it is false, it is inverted, it is a mere designation, it is neither truth nor reality, it is impermanent and non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of a real nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair were the true suchness (tathatā)—if they were not false, not inverted, not merely provisional, but were truth, reality, permanent, eternal, unchanging, immutable, and possessed of an intrinsic nature—then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras."

Because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not suchness; because they are illusory, inverted, mere designations, neither truth nor reality, impermanent, non-eternal, subject to change and transformation, and entirely devoid of intrinsic nature—this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Fifty-Six;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Fifty-Seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The Sixteenth Chapter of the First Division, Praising the Mahāyāna, Part Two: "Furthermore, Subhūti,
if suchness were an existent nature, then this Mahāyāna would not be venerable or sublime, nor would it transcend all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."
Because true thusness (tathatā) does not possess a nature of substantial existence, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of wishlessness, the unconditioned realm, the realm of security, the realm of tranquility, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, original non-arising, and the reality-limit were substantially existent entities, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of gods, humans, and asuras."

Because the dharma-realm, up to and including the limit of reality, is not of a truly existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
“Subhūti! If internal emptiness possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because internal emptiness is not of a truly existent nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
Subhūti!

If external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence were truly existent entities, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, are not of a truly existent nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the perfection of giving possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the perfection of giving does not possess a real, intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti! If the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were of an existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not substantially existent, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
“Subhūti! If the four dhyānas possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the four dhyānas do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is honored and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!

If the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the four foundations of mindfulness possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the four foundations of mindfulness do not possess a real, intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti! If the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path possessed an intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the gods, humans, and asuras.

Because the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are not of a truly existent nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the gate of liberation of emptiness were an entity possessing intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the gate of liberation through emptiness does not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Great Vehicle is honored and sublime, surpassing and excelling all the worlds, including gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti! If the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are not of a truly existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.
“Subhūti! If the five eyes possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the five eyes do not possess the nature of real existence, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
"Subhūti!
If the six supernormal powers possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."
Because the six supernormal powers do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the ten powers of a Buddha possessed a real nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds, including the devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the ten powers of a Buddha do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is honored and sublime, surpassing all in the world, including gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti! If the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects were of a truly existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds with their devas, humans, and asuras.

Because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the ten stages of a bodhisattva possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the dharmas of the stage of pure observation, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the dharma of stream-entry, the dharma of once-returning, the dharma of non-returning, the dharma of arhatship, the dharma of the pratyekabuddha, the dharma of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, and the dharma of the samyaksaṃbuddha were of a truly existent nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the dharmas of the stage of pure observation, the stage of spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, and so forth up to the dharma of samyak-saṃbuddhahood are not of a truly existent nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the person on the stage of pure observation were to exist as a real entity, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”
Because the *pudgala* of the stage of pure observation does not exist as a substantial reality, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the lineages of individuals—the person of the lineage of the seed-ground, the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, the arhat, the pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and the samyaksaṃbuddha—were to exist as real entities, then this Great Vehicle would not be venerable or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the individuals from those of the lineage-ground up to the Samyaksaṃbuddha do not possess a real intrinsic nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras—possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras.”
Because all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras—are not of a truly existent nature, this Mahāyāna is venerable and sublime, surpassing all those in the world—gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the various minds that arise within a bodhisattva mahāsattva—from the first production of the thought of awakening until sitting upon the sublime seat of enlightenment—possessed a nature of substantial reality, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because all the mental states generated by a bodhisattva mahāsattva—from the first production of the thought of enlightenment until sitting upon the seat of sublime awakening—are not of a truly existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the diamond-like wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this Great Vehicle would not be supreme or sublime, nor would it transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras.”

Because the diamond-like wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is not of a truly existent nature, this Great Vehicle is venerable and sublime, surpassing all the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the continuity of the habitual tendencies of the afflictions severed by the vajra-like wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva possessed a real intrinsic nature, then this vajra-like wisdom that severs them would be unable to realize their total lack of intrinsic nature, and having severed them, one could not attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”

Because the continuity of the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of the afflictions—which are abandoned by the diamond-like wisdom (*vajropama-jñāna*)—is not of a truly existent nature, this diamond-like wisdom capable of abandoning them can thoroughly realize that they are entirely devoid of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*); having abandoned them, one realizes the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajña-jñāna*).

"Subhūti! If the bodies of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs—were of a truly existent nature, then the majestic radiance and sublime virtues of those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not transcend all the worlds of devas, humans, and asuras."

Because the bodies of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty secondary signs—are not of a truly existent nature, the majestic splendor and sublime virtues of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas surpass all those in the world, including devas, humans, and asuras.

“Subhūti! If the light emitted by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were of a truly existent nature, then the light emitted by those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not be able to universally illuminate all the Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions, each exceeding the sands of the Ganges in number.”

Because the light emanated by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is not of a truly existent nature, the light emanated by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is able to universally illuminate all Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions, each exceeding in number the sands of the Ganges.

“Subhūti! If the sixty melodious qualities of the voice possessed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were of a truly existent nature, then the sixty melodious qualities of the voice possessed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not be able to proclaim themselves throughout the immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges-sand-like Buddha-worlds in the ten directions.”

Because the sixty melodious qualities of the voice possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not possess the nature of substantial reality, these sixty melodious qualities of the voice possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are able to proclaim universally throughout the immeasurable, innumerable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Gaṅgā-sand-like Buddha-worlds in the ten directions.

“Subhūti! If the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were of a truly existent nature, then the wheel of Dharma turned by those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not be utterly pure, nor would it be something that cannot be turned by any śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, or Brahmās in all the world.”

Because the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas does not have the nature of real existence, the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is utterly pure, such that it cannot be turned by any śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, Māras, or Brahmās in all the world.

“Subhūti! If the sentient beings to whom the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas turn the sublime wheel of Dharma possessed a real intrinsic nature, then the wheel of Dharma turned by those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas would not enable those classes of sentient beings to have entered, are entering, or will enter parinirvāṇa in the realm of nirvana without remainder.”

Because the sentient beings reached by the turning of the sublime wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not possess a real intrinsic nature, those sentient beings are all enabled by the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas to have entered, are entering, or will enter parinirvāṇa in the realm of the wondrous nirvana without remainder.
“Subhūti! For these and countless other reasons, it is said that the Great Vehicle surpasses all the world—including its devas, humans, and asuras—and is the most honored and most sublime.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
As for what you said, 'This Great Vehicle is equal to space,' it is so! It is so!"
So it is! It is just as you have said. Why is this?
"Subhūti!

For example, just as space cannot be found to have directional divisions—east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, above, or below—the Great Vehicle is likewise; it cannot be found to have directional divisions—east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, above, or below. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space one cannot find length or shortness, squareness or roundness, height or lowness, crookedness or rectitude, nor any perceivable shape or color, so it is with the Great Vehicle: one cannot find length or shortness, squareness or roundness, height or lowness, crookedness or rectitude, nor any perceivable shape or color. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti!
