Furthermore, just as in space one cannot find manifest colors such as blue, yellow, red, white, black, purple, or indigo, so it is with the Great Vehicle: one cannot find manifest colors such as blue, yellow, red, white, black, purple, or indigo; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither past, nor future, nor present, so too is the Great Vehicle neither past, nor future, nor present; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space neither increases nor decreases, neither advances nor recedes, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna): it neither increases nor decreases, neither advances nor recedes; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”
“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither defiled nor pure, so too is the Great Vehicle neither defiled nor pure; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither born, nor ceases, nor abides, nor changes, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna): it is neither born, nor ceases, nor abides, nor changes; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither determinate nor indeterminate, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither determinate nor indeterminate. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is not seen, not heard, not sensed, and not known, so too is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna); it is not seen, not heard, not sensed, and not known. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

"Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither that which is known nor that which is realized, so too is the Great Vehicle neither that which is known nor that which is realized; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space."

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is not something to be fully known, not something to be permanently abandoned, not something to be realized, and not something to be cultivated, so too is the Great Vehicle: it is not something to be fully known, not something to be permanently abandoned, not something to be realized, and not something to be cultivated; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither a result of maturation nor a phenomenon that possesses maturation, so too is the Great Vehicle neither a result of maturation nor a phenomenon that possesses maturation; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither a phenomenon characterized by desire nor a phenomenon free from desire, so too is the Great Vehicle neither a phenomenon characterized by desire nor a phenomenon free from desire; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither a phenomenon characterized by hatred nor a phenomenon apart from hatred, so too is the Great Vehicle neither a phenomenon characterized by hatred nor a phenomenon apart from hatred; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space is neither a phenomenon characterized by delusion nor a phenomenon apart from delusion, so too is the Great Vehicle neither a phenomenon characterized by delusion nor a phenomenon apart from delusion; therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as space does not fall within the desire realm, does not fall within the form realm, and does not fall within the formless realm, so too is the Great Vehicle: it does not fall within the desire realm, does not fall within the form realm, and does not fall within the formless realm. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space the production of the mind of the first stage cannot be apprehended, up to and including the production of the mind of the tenth stage which cannot be apprehended, so it is with the Great Vehicle: the production of the mind of the first stage cannot be apprehended, up to and including the production of the mind of the tenth stage which cannot be apprehended. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Furthermore, just as in space one cannot find the stage of pure observation, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having seen the truths, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, or the stage of the Tathāgata, so it is with the Great Vehicle: one cannot find the stage of pure observation up to the stage of the Tathāgata. Therefore, it is said that the Great Vehicle is equal to space.”

“Subhūti! Because the Mahāyāna is non-existent, one should know that the "incalculable" (asaṃkhyeya) is also non-existent;
because the incalculable is non-existent, one should know that the "immeasurable" (aprameya) is also non-existent;
because the immeasurable is non-existent, one should know that the "boundless" (ananta) is also non-existent.
Because the infinite is non-existent, one should know that all phenomena are likewise non-existent.
By virtue of this principle, it is said that the Mahāyāna is universally capable of containing countless, immeasurable, and infinite sentient beings.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Whether it be from "I" up to "the seer," or the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, the vehicle of the perfectly awakened ones, or the person (pudgala); whether it be space, the Great Vehicle, the innumerable, the immeasurable, the boundless, or all phenomena—because all such things as these are non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

“Subhūti! You should know that just as the realm of nirvāṇa can universally contain and receive countless, immeasurable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Great Vehicle universally contain and receive countless, immeasurable, and boundless sentient beings.”
Subhūti! For this reason, it is said:
just as space can universally contain countless, immeasurable, and boundless sentient beings, so too does the Great Vehicle universally contain countless, immeasurable, and boundless sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! As for your statement:
'Just as space cannot be seen to come, go, or abide, so too the Great Vehicle cannot be seen to come, go, or abide.'"
"It is so! It is so! It is just as you have said."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Because all phenomena neither come nor go, and furthermore, they do not abide.
Why is this? Because all phenomena, whether moving or stationary, are unapprehendable.
"Subhūti!..."
Form has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of form has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.
The suchness of form has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.
The intrinsic nature of form neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics of form neither come nor go, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended as either moving or remaining.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The sense base of the eye neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the sense base of the eye neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic natures of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide."
The suchness of the eye-base has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases likewise has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the eye-base has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases likewise has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics of the eye-base have no coming and no going, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases likewise have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and individual characteristics—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The sphere of form (rūpāyatana) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature (prakṛti) of the sphere of form neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic natures of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide."

The suchness of the sense-base of form has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the sense-base of form has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics of the sense-base of form have no coming and no going, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the sense bases of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended as either moving or abiding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The eye-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, have neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the eye-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the form-element, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the eye-element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the eye-element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics of the eye-element have no coming and no going, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as eye-contact, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—whether moving or stationary—are all unapprehendable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The ear-element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the ear-element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the sound-element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, has no coming and no going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the ear-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the ear-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristic of the ear-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact, the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and their fundamental nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The nose element (ghrāṇadhātu) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the odor element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), and the contact of the nose (ghrāṇasamsparśa), as well as all feelings (vedanā) produced with nose-contact as a condition, neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature (prakṛti) of the nose element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the odor element, up to and including all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the nose element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the nose element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristic of the nose element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—whether their fundamental nature, suchness, self-nature, or specific characteristics are moving or stationary—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The tongue-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition have neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the tongue-element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the taste-element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the tongue element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the tongue element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristic of the tongue element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, has no coming and no going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—whether their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, or specific characteristics are moving or stationary—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The body-element (kāyadhātu) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the object-element of touch (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), as well as body-contact (kāyasparśa) and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition, neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature (prakṛti) of the body-element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the object-element of touch, up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide."

The suchness of the body element (*kāyadhātu*) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of the tangible element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the body element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of the tangible element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristic (*svalakṣaṇa*) of the body element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of the tangible element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended whether they are moving or stationary.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The mind-element (manodhātu) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact (manas-saṃsparśa), as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the mind-element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the dharma-element, up to and including all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the mind-element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristic (*svalakṣaṇa*) of the mind-element neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the mind-element, the dharma-element, and the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—whether their fundamental nature, suchness, self-nature, or specific characteristics are in motion or at rest—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The earth element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the earth element has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements has no coming and no going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the earth element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the earth element has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics of the earth element have neither coming nor going, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements have neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Because the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—whether in motion or at rest—are unapprehendable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The noble truth of suffering neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic natures of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path neither come nor go, nor do they abide."

The suchness of the noble truth of suffering neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics of the noble truth of suffering neither come nor go, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Ignorance has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of ignorance has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair has no coming and no going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of ignorance has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The intrinsic nature of ignorance has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The specific characteristic of ignorance has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

It is because ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, self-nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended, whether in motion or at rest.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

True suchness (tathatā) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from arising, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of wishlessness, the unconditioned realm, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharma-sthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharma-vyavasthāna), original non-arising, and the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) neither come nor go, nor do they abide;

the intrinsic nature of true suchness neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; and the intrinsic nature of the realm of phenomena up to the limit of reality neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide."
Suchness is without coming or going, and likewise does not abide; from the dharma-realm up to the limit of reality, suchness is without coming or going, and likewise does not abide.

The self-nature of suchness is without coming or going, and likewise does not abide; from the dharma-realm up to the limit of reality, the self-nature is without coming or going, and likewise does not abide.

The self-characteristic of suchness is without coming or going, and likewise does not abide; from the dharma-realm up to the limit of reality, the self-characteristic is without coming or going, and likewise does not abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because it is impossible to find any movement or stillness in suchness, up to and including the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), as well as in their fundamental nature, suchness, self-nature, or self-characteristic.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Internal emptiness has no coming and no going, nor does it abide. External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of internal emptiness has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence has no coming and no going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of internal emptiness neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the suchness of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.

The intrinsic nature of internal emptiness neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.

The specific characteristic of internal emptiness neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the specific characteristic of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because it is impossible to find any movement or stillness in anything from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, as well as in their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, or intrinsic characteristics.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The perfection of giving has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom have no coming and no going, nor do they abide."

The suchness of the perfection of generosity has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The specific characteristic of the perfection of generosity has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the specific characteristic of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended, whether in motion or at rest.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The four dhyānas have no coming and no going, nor do they abide; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments has no coming and no going, nor does it abide."
The suchness of the four dhyānas has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The specific characteristics of the four dhyānas have no coming and no going, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, as well as their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The four foundations of mindfulness have neither coming nor going, nor do they abide; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path have neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide."

The suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness has no coming and no going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path has no coming and no going, nor does it abide.

The specific characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness have no coming and no going, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path have no coming and no going, nor do they abide.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended as either moving or remaining.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 58; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 59.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Sixteen: Praise of the Mahāyāna, Part Four.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, the gate of liberation of emptiness neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide."

The intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The self-nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness has neither coming nor going, nor does it abide; the self-nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise has neither coming nor going, nor do they abide.

The self-characteristic of the liberation door of emptiness neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the self-characteristics of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as well as their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics, cannot be apprehended whether they are moving or abiding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The five eyes neither come nor go, nor do they abide; the six supernormal powers neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
The intrinsic nature of the five eyes neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide."
The suchness of the five eyes neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the suchness of the six supernormal powers neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.
The intrinsic nature of the five eyes neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.
The specific characteristics of the five eyes neither come nor go, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of the six supernormal powers neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the five eyes, the six supernormal powers, and their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—whether moving or abiding—are all unapprehendable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The ten powers of a Buddha neither come nor go, nor do they abide; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) neither come nor go, nor do they abide.

The intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide."

The *tathatā* (suchness) of the ten powers of a Buddha neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.

The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the ten powers of a Buddha neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; likewise, the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide.

The specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*) of the ten powers of a Buddha neither come nor go, nor do they abide; likewise, the specific characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and all-aspect knowledge—along with their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—cannot be apprehended as either moving or abiding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva neither comes nor goes, nor does he abide; awakening and a buddha likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
The intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of awakening and a buddha likewise neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide."
The *tathatā* of a bodhisattva neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the *tathatā* of awakening (*bodhi*) and the Buddha likewise neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.
The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of a bodhisattva neither comes nor goes, nor does it abide; the intrinsic nature of awakening and the Buddha likewise neither comes nor goes, nor do they abide.

The specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*) of a bodhisattva neither come nor go, nor do they abide; the specific characteristics of awakening and the Buddha likewise neither come nor go, nor do they abide.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because a bodhisattva, awakening, a buddha, and their fundamental nature, suchness, intrinsic nature, and specific characteristics—whether moving or abiding—cannot be apprehended.

"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the future gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are unattainable. Why is this? "

The future gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are themselves emptiness; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the future gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the present gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are unapprehendable. Why is this?"

The present gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are themselves emptiness; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the present gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the signless and wishless doors of liberation of the past, future, and present are unapprehendable. Why is this? "

The gateways of liberation—signlessness, wishlessness, and emptiness—of the past, future, and present are themselves empty; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the gateways of liberation—signlessness, wishlessness, and emptiness—of the past, future, and present that could be found within emptiness!

“Subhūti! The five eyes of the past are empty of the five eyes of the past; the five eyes of the future are empty of the five eyes of the future; the five eyes of the present are empty of the five eyes of the present.

The six supernormal knowledges of the past are empty of the six supernormal knowledges of the past; the six supernormal knowledges of the future are empty of the six supernormal knowledges of the future; the six supernormal knowledges of the present are empty of the six supernormal knowledges of the present.”
Why is that? "Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the five eyes of the past cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? The five eyes of the past are themselves empty; the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the five eyes of the past that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the five eyes of the future cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The five eyes of the future are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the five eyes of the future that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the five eyes of the present cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The five eyes of the present are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the five eyes of the present that could be apprehended within emptiness!
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within emptiness, the five eyes of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended. Why is this?

The five eyes of the past, future, and present are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the five eyes of the past, future, and present that could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the six supernormal powers of the past cannot be apprehended.
Why is this? Because..."

The six supernormal powers of the past are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the six supernormal powers of the past that might be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the six supernormal powers of the future are unattainable. Why is this?"

The six supernormal powers of the future are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is empty; since within emptiness even emptiness cannot be apprehended, how much less could the six supernormal powers of the future be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the six supernormal powers currently existing cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The six supernormal powers of the present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the six supernormal powers of the present that could be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the six supernormal powers of the past, future, and present are unapprehendable. Why is this?"

The six supernormal powers of the past, future, and present are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the six supernormal powers of the past, future, and present that could be found within emptiness!

“Subhūti! The ten powers of the past Buddhas are empty of the ten powers of the past Buddhas; the ten powers of the future Buddhas are empty of the ten powers of the future Buddhas; the ten powers of the present Buddhas are empty of the ten powers of the present Buddhas;
the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, and great joy of the past... [and so forth].”
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
the past four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*) up to the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects;

and the future four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), and great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*).
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—

the future [qualities] from the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*) up to the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects; and the present four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*),
great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen...
The unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—
from the four present grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*) up to the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects— are empty.
Why is that? "Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the ten powers of the Buddhas of the past cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? The ten powers of the past Buddhas are themselves emptiness, and the nature of emptiness is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ten powers of the past Buddhas be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the ten powers of future Buddhas cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The ten powers of the future Buddha are emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the ten powers of the future Buddha being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, the ten powers of the Buddhas of the present cannot be apprehended. Why is this? "

The ten powers of the present Buddha are themselves empty; even the nature of emptiness is empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the ten powers of the present Buddha being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the ten powers of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The ten powers of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the ten powers of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present that could be found within emptiness!

“Subhūti! Within emptiness, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are unapprehendable.”

Why is this? The four fearlessnesses of the past, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the four fearlessnesses of the past, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, which could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!

Within emptiness, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are unapprehendable."

Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses of the future, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are themselves empty; even the nature of emptiness is empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the four fearlessnesses of the future, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, which could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!

Within emptiness, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are unapprehendable."

Why is this? The four fearlessnesses of the present, up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the four fearlessnesses of the present, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, which could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!

Within emptiness, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are unapprehendable."

Why is this? The four fearlessnesses of the past, future, and present, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are themselves emptiness; even the nature of emptiness is empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone the four fearlessnesses of the past, future, and present, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, being apprehended within emptiness!
“Subhūti! Past ordinary beings are empty of past ordinary beings; future ordinary beings are empty of future ordinary beings; present ordinary beings are empty of present ordinary beings.

Past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are empty of past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas; future śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are empty of future śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas; present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are empty of present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas.”
Why is that? "Subhūti!
Within emptiness, past ordinary beings cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? The past ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) is itself empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone an ordinary person of the past who could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, a future ordinary person cannot be apprehended. Why is that?"

Future ordinary beings are themselves empty, and emptiness itself is empty; within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone future ordinary beings being apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti! Within emptiness, present ordinary beings cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The present ordinary person is itself emptiness, and emptiness is also empty; within emptiness, even emptiness itself cannot be apprehended, let alone an ordinary person who could be apprehended within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, ordinary beings of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

Ordinary beings of the past, future, and present are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone ordinary beings of the past, future, and present being apprehended within emptiness!
Because a self, a sentient being, and so forth, up to a knower and a viewer, cannot be apprehended. "Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas cannot be apprehended."

Why is this? The past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas that might be found within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, future śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

Future śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are themselves empty; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the apprehension of future śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the apprehension of present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas within emptiness!
"Subhūti!
Within emptiness, the past, future, and present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas cannot be apprehended. Why is this?"

The śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas of the past, future, and present are themselves emptiness; emptiness itself is also empty. Within emptiness, even emptiness cannot be apprehended, let alone the past, future, and present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas that might be found within emptiness!
Because a self, a sentient being, and even a knower or a viewer cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Form at the prior limit cannot be apprehended;
form at the posterior limit cannot be apprehended; form at the middle limit cannot be apprehended; and form within the equality of the three times also cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, form (rūpa) of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can past, future, or present form be apprehended within equality!
"Subhūti!

Feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended in the past; feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended in the future; feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended in the present; and within the equality of the three times, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, past, future, and present feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can past, future, or present feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The eye-base cannot be apprehended in the past limit, it cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and it cannot be apprehended in the middle limit; even within the equality of the three times, the eye-base cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the eye-base of the past, future, and present is entirely unattainable.
Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the sense-base of the eye be apprehended as past, future, or present within that equality!
"Subhūti!

The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases are unapprehendable in the past; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases are unapprehendable in the future; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases are unapprehendable in the present; and within the equality of the three times, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the past, future, or present sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The sphere of form (rūpāyatana) cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the sphere of form cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the sphere of form cannot be apprehended at the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the sphere of form cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the sense-sphere of form (rūpāyatana) of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.
Why is this? Even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the sense-sphere of form—past, future, or present—be apprehended within equality!

Subhūti! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended in the past; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended in the future; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended in the present; and within the equality of the three times, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena likewise cannot be apprehended.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the spheres of past, future, and present sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The eye-element cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the eye-element cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the eye-element cannot be apprehended at the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the eye-element cannot be apprehended.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present眼界 (cakṣurdhātu) are all unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the eye-element of the past, future, or present be apprehended within equality!
"Subhūti!

The form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the past limit; the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the future limit; the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can one find past, future, or present form-sphere (*rūpadhātu*), eye-consciousness-sphere (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), and eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, within that equality!

“Subhūti! The ear-element cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the ear-element cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the ear-element cannot be apprehended at the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the ear-element cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the ear-element of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ear-element of the past, future, or present be apprehended within that equality!

Subhūti! The sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the past limit; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the future limit; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are likewise unapprehendable.
Why is that? Subhūti!

Within equality, the past, future, and present spheres of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, as well as ear-contact and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could one apprehend the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, within that equality!

"Subhūti! The nose element of the past limit is unapprehendable; the nose element of the future limit is unapprehendable; the nose element of the middle limit is unapprehendable; and even within the equality of the three times, the nose element is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) are all unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the nose-element of the past, future, or present be apprehended within equality!

Subhūti! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the past limit; the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the future limit; the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are likewise unapprehendable.
Why is that? Subhūti!

Within equality, the past, future, and present fragrance element, nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could one apprehend the realm of odors, the realm of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, within that equality—whether past, future, or present!

“Subhūti! The tongue element cannot be apprehended in the past limit; the tongue element cannot be apprehended in the future limit; the tongue element cannot be apprehended in the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the tongue element cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present tongue-element (jihvā-dhātu) are all unapprehendable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the tongue-element of the past, future, or present be apprehended within equality!
"Subhūti!

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended in the past; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended in the future; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended in the present; and within the equality of the three times, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could one apprehend the element of taste, the element of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, within that equality—whether past, future, or present!

“Subhūti! The body-element cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the body-element cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the body-element cannot be apprehended at the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the body-element cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the body element of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can a past, future, or present body-element be apprehended within that equality!
"Subhūti!

The sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the past limit; the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the future limit; the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within equality, the past, future, and present spheres of tangibles (*spraṣṭavya-dhātu*), the sphere of body-consciousness (*kāya-vijñāna-dhātu*), body-contact (*kāya-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could one apprehend the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, within that equality!

“Subhūti! The mental faculty (*manodhātu*) cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the mental faculty cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the mental faculty cannot be apprehended at the intermediate limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the mental faculty cannot be apprehended.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present mind-consciousness element (manovijñānadhātu) are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the mental element (manodhātu) of the past, future, or present be apprehended within equality!
"Subhūti!

The dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the past limit; the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the future limit; the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within equality, the past, future, and present dharmadhātu, the mental consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can one apprehend within equality the past, future, and present dharmadhātu, the mental consciousness element, mental contact, or the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition!

“Subhūti! The earth element cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the earth element cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the earth element cannot be apprehended in the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the earth element cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the earth element of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the earth element of the past, future, or present be apprehended within equality!
"Subhūti!

The elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness cannot be apprehended in the past; the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness cannot be apprehended in the future; the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness cannot be apprehended in the present; and within the equality of the three times, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the past, future, or present elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! Ignorance cannot be apprehended in the past limit; ignorance cannot be apprehended in the future limit; ignorance cannot be apprehended in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, ignorance likewise cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, ignorance of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.
Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can past, future, or present ignorance be apprehended within equality!
"Subhūti!

The formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair of the past limit are unapprehendable; the formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair of the future limit are unapprehendable; the formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair of the middle limit are unapprehendable; and even the formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair within the equality of the three times are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the formations of the past, future, and present, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be past, future, or present formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, to be found within equality!

“Subhūti! The perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended at the prior limit; the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended at the posterior limit; the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended at the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the perfection of generosity of the past, future, and present is entirely unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the perfection of generosity of the past, future, or present be apprehended within that equality!

“Subhūti! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended in the past; the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended in the future; the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended in the present; and even within the equality of the three times, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the past, future, and present perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are all unattainable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can the past, future, or present perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas of the past limit are unapprehendable; the four dhyānas of the future limit are unapprehendable; the four dhyānas of the middle limit are unapprehendable; and within the equality of the three times, the four dhyānas are likewise unapprehendable.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four dhyānas of the past, future, and present are all unattainable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the four dhyānas of the past, future, and present be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended in the past; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended in the future; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions cannot be apprehended in the present; and within the equality of the three times, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions likewise cannot be apprehended."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions of the past, future, and present are all unattainable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments of the past, future, or present be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable in the past limit; the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable in the future limit; the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, the four foundations of mindfulness are likewise unapprehendable.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four foundations of mindfulness of the past, future, and present are all unattainable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the four foundations of mindfulness of the past, future, and present be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable in the past limit; the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable in the future limit; the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four right endeavors of the past, future, and present, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The gate of liberation that is the emptiness of the prior limit is unapprehendable; the gate of liberation that is the emptiness of the posterior limit is unapprehendable; the gate of liberation that is the emptiness of the middle limit is unapprehendable; and even the gate of liberation that is the emptiness within the equality of the three times is unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the doors of liberation—past, future, and present emptiness—are all unattainable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the emptiness gate of liberation of the past, future, and present be apprehended within equality?

"Subhūti! The gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is unapprehendable in the past; the gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is unapprehendable in the future; the gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is unapprehendable in the present; and within the equality of the three times, the gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is likewise unapprehendable."
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the signless and wishless doors of liberation of the past, future, and present are all unapprehendable.
Why is this? For within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the signless, wishless, and emptiness gates of liberation be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The five eyes cannot be apprehended in the past limit; the five eyes cannot be apprehended in the future limit; the five eyes cannot be apprehended in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the five eyes likewise cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the five eyes of the past, future, and present are all unattainable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the five eyes of the past, future, and present be apprehended within equality!

"Subhūti! The six supernormal powers are unattainable in the past; the six supernormal powers are unattainable in the future; the six supernormal powers are unattainable in the present; and even within the equality of the three times, the six supernormal powers are likewise unattainable."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Within equality, the six supernormal powers of the past, future, and present are all unobtainable.
