Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could the six supernormal powers of the past, future, and present be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended in the past; the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended in the future; the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended in the present; and even within the equality of the three times, the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the ten powers of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present are all unattainable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less can the ten powers of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present be apprehended within equality!

“Subhūti! The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-apprehendable in the past limit; the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects are non-apprehendable in the future limit; the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects are non-apprehendable in the middle limit; and within the equality of the three times, the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects are likewise non-apprehendable.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, the four fearlessnesses of the past, future, and present, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are all unattainable.

Why is this? Because even within equality, the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less could the four fearlessnesses of the past, future, and present, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, be apprehended within equality!
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Sixty (and Volume Sixty-One),
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter Sixteen: Praise of the Mahāyāna, Part One, Section Six. “Subhūti!

An ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) cannot be apprehended in the past limit; an ordinary person cannot be apprehended in the future limit; an ordinary person cannot be apprehended in the middle limit; and even within the equality of the three times, an ordinary person cannot be apprehended.”
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, ordinary beings of the past, future, and present are all unfindable.
Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be any distinction of past, future, or present ordinary beings within equality!
This is because a self, sentient beings, and even a knower or a viewer cannot be apprehended. Subhūti!

A śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata cannot be apprehended in the past; a śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata cannot be apprehended in the future; a śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata cannot be apprehended in the present; and within the equality of the three times, a śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, or tathāgata likewise cannot be apprehended.
Why is that? Subhūti!
Within equality, past, future, and present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas are all unapprehendable.

Why is this? Within equality, even the nature of equality itself cannot be apprehended; how much less can one apprehend past, future, or present śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas within equality!
Because a self, sentient beings, and even a knower or a viewer cannot be apprehended. "Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they abide within this mark of equality of the three times and diligently train in the knowledge of all modes; because they are free from grasping and attachment, they swiftly attain fulfillment."
"Subhūti!
This is called the mark of the Great Vehicle—the equality of the three times—of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in such a mark of the Great Vehicle, they surpass all those in the world, including devas, humans, and asuras, and will swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes, bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Excellent!”
Excellent!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has well spoken and correctly explained the Mahāyāna of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
World-Honored One!
Thus, this Mahāyāna is most honored and most sublime. The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past trained in this and have already attained the knowledge of all modes;
the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future will train in this and shall attain the knowledge of all modes;
and the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas throughout the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions in the present are training in this and are now attaining the knowledge of all modes.
"Therefore, the Mahāyāna is most honored and most sublime; it is the truly supreme basis for the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is!"
So it is! It is as you have said.

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, future, and present rely upon the Mahāyāna to practice with diligence, thereby swiftly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; for this reason, the Mahāyāna is most honored and most sublime.
Chapter Seventeen: Conforming (Anuloma-varga), Part One. At that time, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Previously, the Tathāgata instructed the Venerable Subhūti to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; why is it that he now speaks of the Mahāyāna?”
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
will what I have just said regarding the Great Vehicle not contradict the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"The Great Vehicle that you have just described is entirely in accord with the perfection of wisdom and does not deviate from it in any way. Why is this?"

Subhūti! All wholesome dharmas—whether the factors of enlightenment, the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of buddhas—all such things are without exception subsumed within the perfection of wisdom.
Then, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

what are all those wholesome dharmas, factors of enlightenment, whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or buddhas, that are all entirely subsumed within the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said:
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of patience...”
The perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom;
or the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
or the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, and the seven factors of awakening.
the eight branches of the noble path; or the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness;

or the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; or the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—the ten...
The eight qualities unique to a Buddha, Subhūti: whether it be omniscience, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the knowledge of all aspects;
whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant equanimity.

All such wholesome dharmas as these—the factors conducive to enlightenment, whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or buddhas—all of them are entirely subsumed within the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the perfection of wisdom, or the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;
whether it be form, or feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;..."
Whether it be the sense base of the eye, or the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;
whether it be the sense base of forms, or the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena;
or whether it be the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, as well as eye-contact and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
Whether it be the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition;
or the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition;
or the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Whether it be the body element, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition;
or whether it be the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, as well as mind-contact and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition;
or whether it be the earth element, or the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Whether it be the noble truth of suffering, or the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;

whether it be ignorance, or volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;
or whether it be the desire realm, or the form and formless realms.

Whether they be wholesome dharmas or unwholesome dharmas; whether they be determinate or indeterminate dharmas; whether they be with outflows or without outflows; whether they be conditioned or unconditioned dharmas; whether they be mundane or supramundane dharmas;
whether they be the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments;
or whether they be the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

Whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness; the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
whether it be the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or whether it be the five eyes or the six supernormal powers;

Whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;
or whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness, the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
or whether it be all the gateways of dhāraṇī, or all the gateways of samādhi.
Whether it be the Tathāgatas, or the Dharma and Vinaya realized and taught by the Buddhas;

or internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

Whether it be suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of abandonment, the realm of detachment, the realm of cessation, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, the unconditioned realm, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, original non-being, the limit of reality, the ultimate, or nirvana—all such dharmas are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, which is the so-called "signless."
"Subhūti!
For this reason, that which you have just described as the Great Vehicle is entirely in accord with the perfection of wisdom and does not deviate from it in any way."
Why is that? "Subhūti,
the Great Vehicle is not different from the perfection of wisdom, and the perfection of wisdom is not different from the Great Vehicle."
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts.
"Subhūti!..."

The Mahāyāna is not different from the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity; nor are the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity different from the Mahāyāna.

Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“Subhūti! The Great Vehicle is not different from the four dhyānas, and the four dhyānas are not different from the Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the four dhyānas, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two. Subhūti!
The Great Vehicle is not different from the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is so.]”
The Mahāyāna is not different from the eight liberations, and the eight liberations are not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the eight liberations, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.

Subhūti! The Great Vehicle is not different from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are not different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Mahāyāna, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“Subhūti! The Great Vehicle is not different from the four foundations of mindfulness, and the four foundations of mindfulness are not different from the Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the four foundations of mindfulness, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two. Subhūti!

The Great Vehicle is not different from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; nor are the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"Subhūti!..."
The Mahāyāna is not different from the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the gate of liberation that is emptiness is not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the gate of liberation that is emptiness, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The Great Vehicle is not different from the gateways of liberation that are signless and wishless; the gateways of liberation that are signless and wishless are not different from the Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, their nature is non-dual and indivisible. "Subhūti!
The Great Vehicle is not different from the five eyes, and the five eyes are not different from the Great Vehicle."
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the five eyes, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two. Subhūti!
The Mahāyāna is not different from the six supernormal powers, and the six supernormal powers are not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the six supernormal powers, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“Subhūti! The Great Vehicle is not different from the ten powers of a Buddha, and the ten powers of a Buddha are not different from the Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the ten powers of a Buddha, their nature is non-dual and indivisible. Subhūti!

The Great Vehicle is not different from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; nor are the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects different from the Great Vehicle.
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"Subhūti!..."
The Mahāyāna is not different from the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the quality of non-forgetfulness is not different from the Mahāyāna. Why is this?
Whether it be the Mahāyāna or the quality of non-forgetfulness, their nature is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The Great Vehicle is not different from the state of constant abiding in equanimity, and the state of constant abiding in equanimity is not different from the Great Vehicle. Why is this?
Whether it be the Great Vehicle or the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, their nature is non-dual and indivisible. "Subhūti!

The Great Vehicle is not different from the dharmas of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields; the dharmas of emptiness and non-emptiness regarding the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields are not different from the Great Vehicle."
Why is this? Whether it be the Great Vehicle, or the phenomena of the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and so forth—whether empty or non-empty—their nature is neither two nor divided into two.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."

For this reason, the Mahāyāna that you have just described is entirely in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā and does not deviate from it. To speak of the Mahāyāna is to have already spoken of the Prajñāpāramitā; to speak of the Prajñāpāramitā is to have already spoken of the Mahāyāna, because these two dharmas are without distinction.
Chapter 18: Non-Apprehension, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

The bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“World-Honored One!
Because form is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the sphere of the eye is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the sphere of form is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the eye-element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the ear-element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition (*jihvā-saṃsparśa-pratyaya-jātā vedanā*) are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) arising with body-contact as a condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as condition are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the earth element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the Noble Truth of Suffering is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because ignorance is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the perfection of giving is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the four dhyānas are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the eight liberations are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;
because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the liberation door of emptiness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the five eyes are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the six supernormal powers are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the ten powers of the Buddha are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because all dharani-doors are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless;
because all samādhi-doors are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because internal emptiness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because true suchness (*tathatā*) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-false nature, the unchanging nature, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, the unconditioned realm, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, original non-being, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the ultimate, and nirvāṇa are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is boundless, one should know that the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless;
because the Pratyekabuddha vehicle is boundless, one should know that the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Because the Mahāyāna is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
"World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is form does not exist and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva apart from form does not exist and cannot be apprehended."

Thus, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-existent and unapprehendable in a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva as the eye-base is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the eye-base, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.

Likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva as the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable as the sense-base of form; a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the sense-base of form.

Likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable as the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the eye-element; the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the eye-element.

Likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the ear-element; the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable apart from the ear-element.

Likewise, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable apart from the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the nose-element; the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the nose-element.

Likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and the contact of the nose, as well as the various sensations produced with that nose-contact as a condition; the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and the contact of the nose, as well as the various sensations produced with that nose-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the tongue-element; the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the tongue-element.

Likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with the body-element (kāyadhātu) is non-existent and unobtainable; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from the body-element is non-existent and unobtainable.

Likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), body-contact (kāyasparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition is non-existent and unobtainable; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the mind-element (*manodhātu*); the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the mind-element.

The bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.”
“World-Honored One!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with the earth element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from the earth element does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements does not exist and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the Noble Truth of Suffering; the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the Noble Truth of Suffering.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path; the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.”
“World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with ignorance is non-existent and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from ignorance is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is non-existent and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from volitional formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.”

“Bhagavān! The bodhisattva mahāsattva as the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva as the perfection of generosity, there is nothing that exists or can be apprehended.

Likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva as the perfections of ethical discipline (śīla), patience (kṣānti), diligence (vīrya), meditative concentration (dhyāna), and wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva as the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, there is nothing that exists or can be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the four dhyānas; a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the four dhyānas.

Likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable apart from the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
“World-Honored One!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the eight liberations; apart from the eight liberations, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Likewise, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities; apart from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
“World-Honored One!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended as being identical with the four foundations of mindfulness; a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended as being separate from the four foundations of mindfulness.

Likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended as being identical with the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path; nor does a bodhisattva mahāsattva exist and cannot be apprehended as being separate from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
“World-Honored One!

A bodhisattva-mahāsattva who is identical with the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable; a bodhisattva-mahāsattva who is separate from the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable.

A bodhisattva-mahāsattva who is identical with the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is non-existent and unapprehendable; a bodhisattva-mahāsattva who is separate from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is non-existent and unapprehendable.”
“World-Honored One!
A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the five eyes is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the five eyes, one is non-existent and unobtainable.

A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the six supernormal powers is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the six supernormal powers, one is non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable as the ten powers of a Buddha; apart from the ten powers of a Buddha, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; apart from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

“Bhagavān! The bodhisattva mahāsattva who possesses the knowledge of the aspects of the path does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva who possesses the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nothing exists and cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the quality of non-forgetfulness, there is nothing that exists and is unapprehendable.

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the nature of constant equanimity is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the nature of constant equanimity, there is nothing that exists and is unapprehendable.”
“World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within all dharani-doors; a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable apart from all dharani-doors.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within all samādhi-doors; a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable apart from all samādhi-doors.”

“Bhagavān! The bodhisattva mahāsattva of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva of internal emptiness, there is nothing that exists and is unapprehendable.

Likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of essential nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-characteristic (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of common characteristic (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*) are non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is nothing that exists and is unapprehendable.”
“World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is suchness itself is non-existent and unapprehendable; a bodhisattva mahāsattva apart from suchness is non-existent and unapprehendable.”

That is to say: the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the inconceivable realm, the space realm, the realm of severance, the realm of detachment, the realm of cessation, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, the realm of the unconditioned, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, original non-arising, the limit of reality, and ultimate nirvāṇa—within these, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable. Apart from the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and so forth up to the limit of reality and ultimate nirvāṇa, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.
“World-Honored One!
The śrāvaka-vehicle bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the śrāvaka-vehicle bodhisattva-mahāsattva, there is nothing existent and unapprehendable.
The pratyekabuddha-vehicle bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the pratyekabuddha-vehicle bodhisattva-mahāsattva, there is nothing existent and unapprehendable.”
That is to say, the Mahāyāna bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the Mahāyāna bodhisattva mahāsattva, there is nothing existent and nothing obtainable.
“World-Honored One!
The śrāvaka-pudgala and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva are non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the śrāvaka-pudgala and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, they are non-existent and unobtainable.

The pratyekabuddha and the mahāyāna-pudgala bodhisattva-mahāsattva are non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the pratyekabuddha and the mahāyāna-pudgala bodhisattva-mahāsattva, they are non-existent and unobtainable.”
“World-Honored One!

Regarding all dharmas, throughout all modes, in all places, and at all times, I have sought the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, yet I see nothing at all and cannot find them. How then am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas by means of the prajñāpāramitā?”
World-Honored One!

A bodhisattva-mahāsattva exists only as a provisional designation. Just as it is said that "self" and so forth are ultimately unarisen, so too are all dharmas; they are entirely devoid of intrinsic nature.
“World-Honored One!
Form and all other dharmas are ultimately unarisen; if they are ultimately unarisen, they cannot be designated as ‘form’ and so forth.
World-Honored One!”
"How could I possibly instruct or admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of the Prajñāpāramitā which is ultimately unarisen?
World-Honored One!"
Apart from that which is ultimately unborn, there is also no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. World-Honored One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva,

upon hearing this teaching, does not become startled, terrified, or afraid, and does not sink, despond, or feel regret, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"For what reason do you say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit?"
For what reason is it said that because form (*rūpa*) and so forth are limitless, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless?

For what reason is it said that the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended as being identical to form and so forth, nor does the bodhisattva mahāsattva exist and cannot be apprehended as being separate from form and so forth?

"For what reason do you say that, having sought a bodhisattva-mahāsattva among all phenomena, in every way, in every place, and at all times, I have seen none at all and cannot find them? How then am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with the perfection of wisdom?"
For what reason is it said that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation?
For what reason is it said that, just as "self" and so forth are ultimately unarisen,
all phenomena are likewise entirely devoid of intrinsic nature?
For what reason is it said that all phenomena, such as form and so forth, are ultimately unarisen?
For what reason is it said that if they are ultimately unarisen, they cannot be designated as "form" and so forth?
For what reason is it said: "How could I possibly instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the Prajñāpāramitā that is ultimately unarisen?"
For what reason is it said that even apart from ultimate non-arising, there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?

For what reason is it said that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this teaching, their mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, does not sink, does not despair, and is neither distressed nor regretful, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied to Śāriputra: "As the Venerable has asked:

'For what reason is it said that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the present?'"
"Śāriputra, because sentient beings do not exist,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because sentient beings are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits."
Because sentient beings are remote, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because sentient beings lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within sentient beings—
which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between sentient beings and non-existence; there is no difference between sentient beings and emptiness; there is no difference between sentient beings and detachment; there is no difference between sentient beings and the absence of intrinsic nature; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit and [the present]; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit and [the present]; and there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit and [the present].
Śāriputra!

If sentient beings are non-existent, if sentient beings are empty, if sentient beings are detached, and if sentient beings lack intrinsic nature—then whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the present limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and without division.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because form does not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.”
Because form is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because form is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because form has no intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.

Why is this? Śāriputra, because within form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness and their non-existence; there is no difference between form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness and their emptiness; there is no difference between form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness and their detachment; there is no difference between form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness and their lack of intrinsic nature; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit and [the absence of such]; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit and [the absence of such]; and there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit and [the absence of such].

Śāriputra! If form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are non-existent; if form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty; if form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are detached; if form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness lack intrinsic nature; and whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the eye-base does not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the sense base of the eye is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the sense-base of the eye is detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the sense base of the eye lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the eye,
ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.

Śāriputra! It is not that there is any difference between the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and their non-existence; it is not that there is any difference between the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and their emptiness; it is not that there is any difference between the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and their detachment; it is not that there is any difference between the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and their lack of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the prior limit, no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the posterior limit, and no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If the bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not exist; if the bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty; if the bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are detached; if the bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such dharmas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the sphere of form does not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.”
Because the sphere of form is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the sphere of form is detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the sense base of form lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the bases of form,

sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the non-existence of the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; there is no difference between the emptiness of the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; there is no difference between the detachment of the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; there is no difference between the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit; and there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-existent; if the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty; if the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are detached; if the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena lack intrinsic nature; and whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such dharmas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the eye-element does not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the eye-element is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the eye-element,

Śāriputra! It is not that the eye-faculty, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, possess any difference in their non-existence; it is not that they possess any difference in their emptiness; it is not that they possess any difference in their detachment; it is not that they possess any difference in their lack of intrinsic nature. Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.

because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the earth element lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the elements of earth,

water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness and their non-existence; there is no difference between the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness and their emptiness; there is no difference between the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness and their detachment; there is no difference between the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness and their lack of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the prior limit, no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the posterior limit, and no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the intermediate limit.

Śāriputra! If the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-existent; if the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are empty; if the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are detached; if the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness lack intrinsic nature; then whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the noble truth of suffering does not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the noble truth of suffering is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the noble truth of suffering is remote, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are remote, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the noble truth of suffering lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the noble truths of suffering,

its origin, its cessation, and the path— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path and non-existence; there is no difference between the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path and emptiness; there is no difference between the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path and detachment; there is no difference between the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path and the absence of intrinsic nature; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit and [the noble truths]; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit and [the noble truths]; and there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit and [the noble truths].

Śāriputra! If the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path do not exist; if the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are empty; if the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are utterly secluded; if the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the prior limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the posterior limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because ignorance does not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because ignorance is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because ignorance is far removed, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are far removed, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because ignorance lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.

Why is this? Śāriputra, because within ignorance, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the non-existence of ignorance up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and [their] non-existence; there is no difference between the emptiness of ignorance up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and [their] emptiness; there is no difference between the detachment of ignorance up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and [their] detachment; there is no difference between the lack of intrinsic nature of ignorance up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and [their] lack of intrinsic nature; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If ignorance up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-existent; if ignorance up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are empty; if ignorance up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are detached; if ignorance up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the perfection of generosity is non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the perfection of generosity is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the perfection of generosity is remote, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are remote, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the perfection of generosity lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the non-existence, emptiness, detachment,

and lack of intrinsic nature of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! It is not that the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom differ from non-existence; it is not that the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom differ from emptiness; it is not that the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom differ from detachment; it is not that the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom differ from the lack of intrinsic nature; it is not that the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the prior limit differs [from them]; it is not that the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the posterior limit differs [from them]; it is not that the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit differs [from them].

Śāriputra! If the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent; if the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty; if the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are remote; if the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the four dhyānas do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the four dhyānas are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the four dhyānas are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the four dhyānas lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the four dhyānas,

the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments and non-existence; there is no difference between the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments and emptiness; there is no difference between the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments and detachment; there is no difference between the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments and the absence of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are non-existent; if the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are empty; if the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are detached; if the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such dharmas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the eight liberations are non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.”
Because the eight liberations are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the eight liberations are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the eight liberations lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the eight liberations,

the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases on the one hand and non-existence on the other; there is no difference between them and emptiness; there is no difference between them and detachment; there is no difference between them and the absence of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-existent; if the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty; if the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are detached; if the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such dharmas are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the present.
“Śāriputra! Because the four foundations of mindfulness do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
