Because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the four foundations of mindfulness lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the non-existence, emptiness, detachment,

and lack of intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the non-existence of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path and their existence; there is no difference between the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path and [their emptiness]; there is no difference between the detachment of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path and [their detachment]; there is no difference between the lack of intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path and [their lack of intrinsic nature]; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the prior limit and [a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the prior limit]; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the posterior limit and [a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the posterior limit]; and there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit and [a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit].

Śāriputra! If the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path do not exist; if the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are empty; if the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are detached; if the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the prior, posterior, or middle limits;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the prior, posterior, or middle limits.
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within emptiness,

signlessness, and wishlessness— the liberation doors that are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and non-existence; there is no difference between the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and emptiness; there is no difference between the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and detachment; there is no difference between the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and the absence of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-existent; if the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty; if the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are detached; if the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are without intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the five eyes do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the six supernormal powers do not exist, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.”
Because the five eyes are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the six supernormal powers are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the five eyes are detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the six supernormal powers are detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the five eyes lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the six supernormal powers lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the non-existence,
emptiness, detachment, and lack of intrinsic nature of the five eyes and six supernormal powers, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the five eyes and the six supernormal powers and non-existence; there is no difference between the five eyes and the six supernormal powers and emptiness; there is no difference between the five eyes and the six supernormal powers and detachment; there is no difference between the five eyes and the six supernormal powers and the absence of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.
Śāriputra!

Whether it be the five eyes and six supernormal powers being non-existent, or the five eyes and six supernormal powers being empty, or the five eyes and six supernormal powers being detached, or the five eyes and six supernormal powers lacking intrinsic nature; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the prior limit, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the posterior limit, or the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such dharmas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the ten powers of a Buddha do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects do not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the ten powers of a Buddha lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.

Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! It is not that the ten powers of a buddha, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, differ from non-existence; it is not that the ten powers of a buddha, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, differ from emptiness; it is not that the ten powers of a buddha, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, differ from detachment; it is not that the ten powers of a buddha, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, differ from the absence of intrinsic nature. It is not that a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit differs [from these], nor that a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit differs, nor that a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit differs.
Śāriputra!

If the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent, if the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects are empty, if the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects are detached, and if the ten powers of a Buddha up to the knowledge of all aspects lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.”
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the state of constant abiding in equanimity lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the non-existence,

emptiness, detachment, and lack of intrinsic nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity; there is no difference between the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity; there is no difference between the remoteness of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity; there is no difference between the lack of intrinsic nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity; there is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity are non-existent; if the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity are empty; if the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity are detached; if the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity lack intrinsic nature; then the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Sixty-two.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Sixty-three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Part, Chapter Eighteen: On Non-apprehensibility, Section Three. "Śāriputra!
Because all dhāraṇī-doors are non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits."
Because all doors of samādhi are non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because all dhāraṇī-doors are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because all doors of samādhi are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because all dharani-doors are detached, the bodhisattva mahasattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because all samadhi-doors are detached, the bodhisattva mahasattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because all dharani-doors lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahasattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because all samadhi-doors lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahasattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because within all dhāraṇī-doors, all samādhi-doors— which are non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! It is not that all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors differ from non-existence; it is not that all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors differ from emptiness; it is not that all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors differ from detachment; it is not that all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors differ from the lack of intrinsic nature. It is not that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit differ; it is not that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit differ; it is not that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the middle limit differ.

Śāriputra! If all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors are non-existent; if all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors are empty; if all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors are detached; if all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors lack intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past limit, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future limit, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because internal emptiness is non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because internal emptiness is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;

because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Because internal emptiness is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the prior, posterior, or middle limits;

because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature, is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the prior, posterior, or middle limits.
Because internal emptiness lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because within internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature— within that which is non-existent, empty, detached, and without self-nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the middle.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the emptiness of the internal and so forth up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature and that which is non-existent; there is no difference between the emptiness of the internal and so forth up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature and emptiness itself; there is no difference between the emptiness of the internal and so forth up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature and detachment; there is no difference between the emptiness of the internal and so forth up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature and the absence of self-nature; there is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the prior limit; there is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the posterior limit; and there is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! Whether it be the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), which is non-existent; or whether it be the emptiness of the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, which is empty; or whether it be the remoteness of the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; or whether it be the lack of intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; or whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because true suchness (tathatā) is non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, equality, the nature free from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, the realm of the unconditioned, the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, primordial non-being, and the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-existent, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.”
Because True Suchness is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;
because the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and even original non-arising and the limit of reality are empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because True Suchness is detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits;

because the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and even original non-arising and the limit of reality are detached, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or present limits.
Because true thusness lacks intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the prior, subsequent, or middle limits;

because the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and even original non-existence and the limit of reality lack intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the prior, subsequent, or middle limits.

Why is this? Śāriputra, because within true thusness, the dharma-realm, up to and including original non-existence, the limit of reality, non-existence, emptiness, detachment, and the absence of intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the primordial non-existence and the limit of reality, and that which does not exist. There is no difference between suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the primordial non-existence and the limit of reality, and emptiness. There is no difference between suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the primordial non-existence and the limit of reality, and detachment. There is no difference between suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the primordial non-existence and the limit of reality, and the absence of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the prior limit; there is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the posterior limit; there is no difference between the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! If suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the original non-existence and the limit of reality are non-existent; if suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the original non-existence and the limit of reality are empty; if suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the original non-existence and the limit of reality are remote; if suchness, the dharma-realm, up to the original non-existence and the limit of reality are without intrinsic nature; and if the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the prior limit, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the posterior limit, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such dharmas are non-dual and without division.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the Śrāvaka vehicle does not exist, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the Śrāvaka vehicle is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is remote, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the prior, posterior, or middle limits;
because the Śrāvaka vehicle lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the prior, posterior, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the śrāvaka vehicle—
which is non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the Śrāvaka vehicle and non-existence; there is no difference between the Śrāvaka vehicle and emptiness; there is no difference between the Śrāvaka vehicle and detachment; there is no difference between the Śrāvaka vehicle and the lack of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, and no difference between a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! Whether it be the Śrāvaka vehicle being non-existent, the Śrāvaka vehicle being empty, the Śrāvaka vehicle being detached, or the Śrāvaka vehicle being without intrinsic nature; whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
“Śāriputra! Because the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas does not exist, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas is empty, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.”
Because the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas is remote, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas lacks intrinsic nature, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the pratyekabuddhayāna—
which is non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference in the non-existence of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle; there is no difference in the emptiness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle; there is no difference in the detachment of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle; there is no difference in the lack of intrinsic nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle. There is no difference in the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of the past limit; there is no difference in the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of the future limit; there is no difference in the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! Whether it be the pratyekabuddha vehicle as non-existent, the pratyekabuddha vehicle as empty, the pratyekabuddha vehicle as detached, or the pratyekabuddha vehicle as lacking intrinsic nature; whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the future limit, or a bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
"Śāriputra! Because the Great Vehicle is non-existent, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the Great Vehicle is empty, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits."
Because the Great Vehicle is far removed, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits;
because the Great Vehicle lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, future, or middle limits.
Why is this? Śāriputra, because within the Mahāyāna—
which is non-existent, empty, detached, and devoid of intrinsic nature— a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past, the future, or the present.

Śāriputra! There is no difference between the Great Vehicle and non-existence; there is no difference between the Great Vehicle and emptiness; there is no difference between the Great Vehicle and detachment; there is no difference between the Great Vehicle and the absence of intrinsic nature. There is no difference between the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of the past limit, no difference between the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of the future limit, and no difference between the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of the middle limit.

Śāriputra! Whether it be that the Great Vehicle is non-existent, or that the Great Vehicle is empty, or that the Great Vehicle is detached, or that the Great Vehicle lacks intrinsic nature; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the prior limit, the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the posterior limit, or the bodhisattva mahāsattva of the middle limit—all such phenomena are non-dual and indivisible.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the past limit, a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the future limit, and a bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended in the middle limit.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again replied to Śāriputra:
"As the Venerable has asked: 'For what reason is it said that because form and so forth are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless?'"
"Śāriputra, form is like space;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are like space. Why is this so?"

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.
Form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also thus: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of form is empty, and the natures of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a subsequent limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because form is limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless.
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless. "Śāriputra!
The sense base of the eye is like space; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are like space."
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.
The same applies to the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of the eye is empty, and because the natures of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both middle and extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the sense-base of the eye is limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless.
Because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless. "Śāriputra!
The sphere of form is like space; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are like space.
Why is this so? Śāriputra!

Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The same applies to the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of form is empty; because the natures of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the sphere of form is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are infinite, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also infinite. "Śāriputra!
The eye-element is like space; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended, it is called "space."

The same applies to the eye element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition: their prior limit cannot be apprehended, their posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and their middle limit cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-element is empty, and because the nature of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both middle and extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the eye-element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.

"Śāriputra, because the forms of the form realm, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are boundless, you should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise boundless."

The ear element is like space; the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The same applies to the ear-element and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; they cannot be apprehended in the past, they cannot be apprehended in the future, and they cannot be apprehended in the present.

Why is this? Because the nature of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is empty, and because the nature of the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition (*śrotra-saṃsparśa-pratyaya-ja-vedanā*) is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) cannot be apprehended, a posterior limit (*aparānta*) cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit (*madhyānta*) cannot be apprehended; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the ear-element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the sphere of sound, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are boundless, it should be known that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless. "Śāriputra!

The nose element is like space; the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The same applies to the nose element and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the nose-element is empty, and because the nature of the fragrance-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the nose-element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Śāriputra, because the realm of fragrance, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are boundless, you should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless."
The tongue element is like space; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The tongue element, and so forth up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are likewise: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is empty; because the nature of the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*), up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition (*jihvā-saṃsparśapratyaya-utpanna-vedanā*), is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the tongue-element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
“Śāriputra, because the taste element and even all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are infinite, you should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also infinite.”

The body element is like space; the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, the posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and the middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The same applies to the body element and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is empty, and because the nature of the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the body-element (kāyadhātu) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
“Śāriputra, because the objects of touch and the various feelings produced with the body as the basis for contact are boundless, you should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”

The mind-element is like space; the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended, it is called "space."

The same applies to the mental faculty (*manodhātu*) and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is empty, and because the nature of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; it is also called empty because neither middle nor extremes can be found.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the mind-element (manodhātu) is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
“Śāriputra, because the dharma-realm and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are boundless, you should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.”
The earth element is like space; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are like space.
Why is this so, Śāriputra?

Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are likewise: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the earth element is empty, and the natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; furthermore, because both middle and extremes cannot be found, it is called "empty."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the earth element is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless. Śāriputra!"
The noble truth of suffering is like space; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are like space.
Why is this so, Śāriputra?

Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are also like this: their prior limit cannot be apprehended, their posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and their middle cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because the noble truth of suffering is empty of intrinsic nature, and the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of intrinsic nature; within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a subsequent limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended. Furthermore, because both the middle and the extremes cannot be apprehended, it is called "empty."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the Noble Truth of Suffering is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless. “Śāriputra!

Ignorance is like space; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are like space.”
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended, it is called "space."

The same applies to everything from ignorance through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair: the prior limit is unapprehendable, the posterior limit is unapprehendable, and the middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of ignorance is empty, and because the nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; it is called "empty" precisely because neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because ignorance is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Śāriputra, because the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are boundless, you should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless."
The perfection of generosity is like space; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are like space.
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The same applies to the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of giving is empty; because the natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes cannot be found.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the perfection of giving is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are limitless, one should know that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are likewise limitless.
“Śāriputra! The four dhyānas are like space; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are like space. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are also like this: their prior limit cannot be apprehended, their posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and their middle cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because the nature of the four dhyānas is empty; because the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a subsequent limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the four dhyānas are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
“Śāriputra, the eight liberations are like space; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities are like space.”
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are likewise: their prior limit cannot be apprehended, their posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and their middle limit cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because the nature of the eight liberations is empty; because the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the eight liberations are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are limitless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless.
"Śāriputra!..."

The four foundations of mindfulness are like space; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are like space.
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are also like this: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is empty, and because the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; furthermore, it is called empty because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the four foundations of mindfulness are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
“Śāriputra! The gate of liberation of emptiness is like space; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are like space.”
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended, it is called "space."

The gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are likewise such that their prior limit cannot be apprehended, their posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and their middle limit cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty; because the natures of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty; because within emptiness, the prior limit cannot be apprehended, the posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and the middle limit cannot be apprehended; and furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the gate of liberation of emptiness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless. "Śāriputra!
The five eyes are like space; the six supernormal powers are like space."
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, the posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and the middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.
The five eyes and the six supernormal powers are also like this: their prior limit is unattainable, their posterior limit is unattainable, and their middle limit is unattainable. Why is this?

Because the nature of the five eyes is empty, and because the nature of the six supernormal powers is empty—within this emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes cannot be found.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the five eyes are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the six supernormal powers are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless. “Śāriputra!

The ten powers of a buddha are like space; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are like space.”
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are likewise: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is empty; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including all-aspect omniscience, is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the ten powers of a Buddha are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
"Śāriputra, because the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects are boundless, you should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless."
The quality of non-forgetfulness is like space, and the constant abiding in equanimity is like space.
Why is this so, Śāriputra?

Just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are also like this: they cannot be apprehended in the past, they cannot be apprehended in the future, and they cannot be apprehended in the present.

Why is this? Because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty, and the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a subsequent limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found; it is also because both middle and extremes cannot be found that it is called empty.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the quality of non-forgetfulness is boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Śāriputra, all doors of dhāraṇī are like space; all doors of samādhi are like space."
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.
It is the same for all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is empty, and the nature of all samādhi-doors is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a subsequent limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended; furthermore, because both middle and extremes cannot be apprehended, it is called "empty."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because all dharanī-gates are boundless, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also boundless.
Because all doors of samādhi are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise boundless.
"Śāriputra, inner emptiness is like space;

outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unobtainable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are like space."
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended, it is called "space."

It is the same for inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence: the prior limit is unapprehendable, the posterior limit is unapprehendable, and the middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because internal emptiness is empty of its own nature; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is empty of its own nature; and because within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be apprehended, a posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and a middle limit cannot be apprehended—it is called "empty" precisely because both middle and extremes are unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because internal emptiness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise boundless.
“Śāriputra! True suchness is like space;

the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of wishlessness, the realm of the unconditioned, the realm of security, the realm of tranquility, primordial non-arising, the limit of reality, and ultimate nirvāṇa are like space.”
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.
It is the same for true thusness up to ultimate nirvana: its prior limit is unattainable, its posterior limit is unattainable, and its middle is unattainable.

Why is this? Because the nature of true suchness (*tathatā*) is empty; because the nature of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to ultimate nirvana is empty. Within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found. Furthermore, it is called "empty" because both the middle and the extremes are unfindable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because true thusness is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
Because the dharma-realm and even ultimate nirvāṇa are boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise boundless.
"Śāriputra! The vehicle of the śrāvakas is like space; the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas and the Great Vehicle are like space."
Why is this so? Śāriputra,

just as the prior limit of space cannot be apprehended, its posterior limit cannot be apprehended, and its middle limit cannot be apprehended— it is called "space" because its center and boundaries cannot be apprehended.

The Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Mahāyāna are likewise: their prior limit is unapprehendable, their posterior limit is unapprehendable, and their middle limit is unapprehendable.

Why is this? Because the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle is empty, and the nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna is empty; within emptiness, a prior limit cannot be found, a posterior limit cannot be found, and a middle limit cannot be found. Furthermore, because both the middle and the extremes cannot be found, it is called "empty."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
because the Śrāvaka vehicle is boundless, one should know that the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Because the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle and the Great Vehicle are boundless, one should know that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also boundless.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again replied to Śāriputra:

"Regarding what the Venerable has said: 'For what reason do you say that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is identical with form, etc., does not exist and cannot be apprehended, and that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is separate from form, etc., does not exist and cannot be apprehended?'"
"Thus it is, Śāriputra!
Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form. Why is this so?"
In the emptiness of the nature of form, because form is non-existent and unattainable, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unattainable.
It is neither form nor is it the emptiness of the nature of form.
Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of form, form does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not [inherently existent]; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is identical with form does not exist and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is separate from form does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Thus, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-existent and unapprehendable in the bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*), the eye-base is non-existent and unobtainable; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also non-existent and unobtainable.
It is not that the eye-base is the eye-base, but rather that the eye-base is empty of its own nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the sense-base of the eye, the sense-base of the eye does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not [inherently existent], for the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended in the sense-sphere of the eye; the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended apart from the sense-sphere of the eye.

Thus, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva in the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
"Śāriputra, the sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the sense-base of form, because the sense-base of form is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
It is not the sense-base of form; it is empty of the nature of the sense-base of form.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form, the sphere of form does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, these spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the nature of the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, these bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the sphere of form (rūpāyatana), and a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable apart from the sphere of form.

The bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable apart from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Sixty-three;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Sixty-four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Eighteen, Part Four: The Non-Apprehension of the Initial Division.
“Śāriputra, the eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty.”

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the eye-faculty (*cakṣurdhātu*), the eye-faculty does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The eye-faculty is not [existent]; the nature of the eye-faculty is empty. Why?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the eye-faculty, the eye-faculty does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form realm, up to and including the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, do not belong to the form realm; indeed, the nature of all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including those belonging to the form realm, is empty.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, there is no form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition that exists or can be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva as the eye-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the eye-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—all these are non-existent and unattainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unattainable.
“Śāriputra! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*), because the ear-element is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
It is not the ear-element; it is empty of the nature of the ear-element.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the ear-element, the ear-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—the nature of the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—is empty.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are not [inherently existent]; rather, the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, there is no sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition that exists or can be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the ear-element; apart from the ear-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—these do not exist and cannot be apprehended by a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Apart from the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as apart from all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—these do not exist and cannot be apprehended by a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“Śāriputra, the nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), the nose-element is non-existent and unapprehendable; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also non-existent and unapprehendable.
It is not the nose-element, for the nose-element is empty of its own nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the nose-element, the nose-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition—the nature of these, from the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, is emptiness.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and the nose-contact, as well as all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are not [inherently existent]; rather, the nature of the fragrance element up to the sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is emptiness.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of all feelings produced with the olfactory realm up to those produced with nose-contact as a condition, there is no such thing as the olfactory realm up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition that can be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva within the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the nose-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
