The bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of odors, the sphere of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; apart from the sphere of odors, the sphere of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
“Śāriputra! The tongue element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the tongue element. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the tongue-element, because the tongue-element is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
It is not the tongue-element; it is the emptiness of the nature of the tongue-element.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the tongue-element, the tongue-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are empty of the nature of the taste element up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the taste element, up to and including the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the taste element, up to and including the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are not [inherently existent]; rather, the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the gustatory element and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, there is nothing that exists or can be apprehended; since the gustatory element and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva within the tongue-element is non-existent and unapprehendable; the bodhisattva mahāsattva apart from the tongue-element is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition—all these are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The body-element is empty of the nature of the body-element. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), because the body-element is non-existent and unattainable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unattainable.
It is not the body-element; it is empty of the nature of the body-element.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the body-element (kāyadhātu), the body-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The sphere of the tangible, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of the sphere of the tangible up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is empty.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the sense-sphere of tangibles, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, these various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are empty of the intrinsic nature of the tangible object element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of all feelings produced with the tangible realm as condition, up to and including those produced with the body-tangible contact as condition, these feelings—ranging from the tangible realm to those produced by body-tangible contact—are non-existent and unapprehendable; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva within the body-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva apart from the body-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—all these are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Apart from the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—all these are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“Śāriputra! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), because the mind-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is neither the mind-element nor is it empty of the nature of the mind-element.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), the mind-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all phenomena consisting of the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, up to the very nature of those feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are empty.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, the dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are not the dharma-element; indeed, up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, they are empty of the nature of the dharma-element and so forth.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, there is no such thing as the dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition that can be found or apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the mind-element (*manodhātu*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the mind-element, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—these, O Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, do not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
“Śāriputra, the earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the earth element, because the earth element is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
It is not the earth element; it is empty of the nature of the earth element.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the earth element, the earth element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are empty of the nature of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness do not exist and are unapprehendable; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and is unapprehendable.
The elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are not [inherently existent]; the nature of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is empty. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, these elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva as the earth element does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the earth element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; apart from the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra, the noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering, because the noble truth of suffering does not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The noble truth of suffering is not [existent], for the noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of suffering does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the Noble Truth of Suffering is non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the Noble Truth of Suffering, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—these, O Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, do not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
“Śāriputra, ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of ignorance, because ignorance is non-existent and unobtainable, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.
It is neither ignorance nor is it the emptiness of the nature of ignorance.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of ignorance, ignorance itself is non-existent and unapprehendable; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, these volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not volitional formations, nor are they up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; rather, volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, these volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is ignorance itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is apart from ignorance does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

Thus, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable in relation to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and apart from volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

Because the perfection of generosity is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
The perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity, for it is empty of the nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity, the perfection of generosity does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not [inherently existent]; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the perfection of giving, and apart from the perfection of giving, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the four dhyānas, because the four dhyānas do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The non-four-dhyānas are not the emptiness of the nature of the non-four-dhyānas. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the non-four-dhyānas, the non-four-dhyānas do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not [identical to] the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is empty. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable within the four dhyānas, and apart from the four dhyānas, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations, because the eight liberations do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva mahāsattva likewise does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The eight liberations are not [inherently existent], for the eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations, the eight liberations do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-existent and unobtainable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are not [identical to] the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the eight liberations themselves are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the eight liberations, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-existent and unobtainable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.
“Śāriputra! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, because the four foundations of mindfulness do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The non-existence of the four applications of mindfulness is not the emptiness of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the non-existence of the four applications of mindfulness, the non-existence of the four applications of mindfulness is non-existent and unapprehendable; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also non-existent and unapprehendable.

The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are not [identical to] the four right efforts, nor are they empty of the nature of the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the four foundations of mindfulness are non-existent and unapprehendable in the bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the four foundations of mindfulness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

That is to say, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable within the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; apart from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness, because the gate of liberation through emptiness is non-existent and unobtainable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.
The door of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the door of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the door of liberation that is emptiness, the door of liberation that is emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The gate of liberation of signlessness is not the gate of liberation of signlessness; the nature of emptiness of the gate of liberation of signlessness is not the gate of liberation of signlessness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness, the gate of liberation of signlessness does not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

within the gate of liberation that is emptiness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the gate of liberation that is emptiness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-existent and unapprehendable for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes, because the five eyes do not exist and cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
It is neither the five eyes nor the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes, the five eyes do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the six supernormal powers, the six supernormal powers do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The six supernormal powers are not the six supernormal powers, for they are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the six supernormal powers, the six supernormal powers do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say this:
the five eyes of a bodhisattva mahāsattva do not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the five eyes of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nothing exists and cannot be apprehended.

Thus, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas possessing the six supernormal powers are non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattvas possessing the six supernormal powers, they are non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers, because the Buddha’s ten powers are non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
The non-Buddha-ten-powers are empty of the nature of non-Buddha-ten-powers. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of non-Buddha-ten-powers, the non-Buddha-ten-powers do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, and the knowledge of all aspects—the nature of these, from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, is emptiness.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to and including all-aspect omniscience, the four fearlessnesses up to and including all-aspect omniscience do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, and the knowledge of all aspects are not empty of the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to and including all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), the four fearlessnesses up to and including all-aspect omniscience do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the ten powers of a Buddha are non-existent and unapprehendable in the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and apart from the ten powers of a Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

That is to say, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, and the knowledge of all aspects—these a bodhisattva mahāsattva has no existence and cannot be apprehended; apart from the four fearlessnesses up to the knowledge of all aspects, a bodhisattva mahāsattva has no existence and cannot be apprehended.
“Śāriputra! The knowledge of the paths is empty of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the paths. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
The wisdom of the non-characteristic of the path is empty of the nature of the wisdom of the non-characteristic of the path. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the wisdom of the non-characteristic of the path, the wisdom of the non-characteristic of the path does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s knowledge of the aspects of the path does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s knowledge of the aspects of the path, nothing exists and cannot be apprehended.
“Śāriputra! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?

Within the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness, because the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
The state of being without forgetfulness is not [identical to] the emptiness of the nature of being without forgetfulness. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of being without forgetfulness, the state of being without forgetfulness does not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The nature of the constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity, the constant abiding in equanimity does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The equanimity of non-abiding is empty of the nature of the equanimity of non-abiding. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the equanimity of non-abiding, the equanimity of non-abiding does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s state of non-forgetfulness is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s state of non-forgetfulness, [the bodhisattva mahāsattva] is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Thus, the bodhisattva mahāsattva who abides in equanimity is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva who abides in equanimity, there is nothing that exists or can be apprehended.
“Śāriputra! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
Since all dhāraṇī-doors are empty of intrinsic nature, and because all dhāraṇī-doors are non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
The gateways of all dhāraṇīs are not [inherently existent], for the nature of the gateways of all dhāraṇīs is empty. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the gateways of all dhāraṇīs, the gateways of all dhāraṇīs do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
All doors of samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all doors of samādhi. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all doors of samādhi, all doors of samādhi do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
All samādhi-gates are not [inherently existent]; all samādhi-gates are empty of the nature of all samādhi-gates. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of all samādhi-gates, all samādhi-gates do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva in all the gateways of dhāraṇī is non-existent and unapprehendable; the bodhisattva mahāsattva apart from all the gateways of dhāraṇī is non-existent and unapprehendable.
Thus, all doors of samādhi are non-existent and unapprehendable for the bodhisattva mahāsattva; apart from all doors of samādhi, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of internal emptiness, because internal emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.
It is not that internal emptiness is [merely] empty of internal emptiness; rather, it is empty by way of the emptiness of its own nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the emptiness of the internal, the internal is non-existent and unapprehendable; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unapprehendable.

The emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are non-existent and unapprehendable; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also non-existent and unapprehendable.

The emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature does not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the bodhisattva mahāsattva who is internal emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended; apart from the bodhisattva mahāsattva who is internal emptiness, nothing exists and cannot be apprehended.

Thus, from external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.
“Śāriputra, suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā*, because *tathatā* itself is non-existent and unobtainable, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.
It is not that *tathatā* is not *tathatā*; it is empty of its own nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of suchness, neither suchness nor anything non-existent can be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

The dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the inconceivable realm, the realm of space, the realm of cessation, the realm of detachment, the realm of extinction, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the realm of non-existence, the realm of signlessness, the realm of non-action, the realm of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*), the realm of peace, the realm of tranquility, primordial non-being, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), ultimate nirvāṇa, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, up to the limit of reality and the nature of ultimate nirvāṇa—all these are empty of intrinsic nature.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), up to and including the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and ultimate nirvāṇa, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, up to and including the limit of reality and ultimate nirvāṇa do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.

The non-dharmadhātu, the dharma-nature, up to the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) and ultimate nirvāṇa are not the dharmadhātu, the dharma-nature, up to the limit of reality and ultimate nirvāṇa; they are empty of the nature of the dharmadhātu, the dharma-nature, up to the limit of reality and ultimate nirvāṇa.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the nature of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of reality (*dharmatā*), up to the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and ultimate *nirvāṇa*, there is no such thing as the non-existence of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, up to the *bhūtakoṭi* and ultimate *nirvāṇa*, nor can it be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva as suchness is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from suchness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, from the dharma-realm and the nature of phenomena up to the limit of reality and ultimate nirvāṇa, is non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the dharma-realm and the nature of phenomena up to the limit of reality and ultimate nirvāṇa, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is non-existent and unobtainable.
“Śāriputra, the Śrāvaka vehicle is empty of the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle. Why is this?
Within the emptiness of the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle, because the Śrāvaka vehicle is non-existent and unattainable, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unattainable.
The vehicle of the śrāvakas is not [inherently existent], for the nature of the vehicle of the śrāvakas is empty. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the śrāvakas does not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The Pratyekabuddhayāna, the Mahāyāna Pratyekabuddhayāna, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the Mahāyāna. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna, the Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The Pratyekabuddhayāna is not [inherently existent], and the Mahāyāna is not the Pratyekabuddhayāna; the nature of the Mahāyāna is empty. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of the Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna, the Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna do not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the śrāvaka-vehicle bodhisattva-mahāsattva is non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the śrāvaka-vehicle bodhisattva-mahāsattva, there is nothing that exists and is unapprehendable.

The Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-existent and unobtainable; apart from the Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Mahāyāna Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there is nothing existent and nothing obtainable.
“Śāriputra! A śrāvaka person (pudgala) is empty of the nature of a śrāvaka person. Why is this?
Since the śrāvaka person is non-existent and unobtainable within the emptiness of the nature of the śrāvaka person, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.
The non-śrāvaka person is not [inherently] existent; the non-śrāvaka person is empty of the nature of a non-śrāvaka person. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of a non-śrāvaka person, the non-śrāvaka person does not exist and cannot be apprehended; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Pratyekabuddhas and Mahāyāna *pudgalas* are empty of the nature of Pratyekabuddhas and Mahāyāna *pudgalas*. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of Pratyekabuddhas and Mahāyāna *pudgalas*, Pratyekabuddhas and Mahāyāna *pudgalas* do not exist and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
The pratyekabuddha and the mahāyāna pudgala are empty of the nature of being a pratyekabuddha and a mahāyāna pudgala. Why is this?

Because within the emptiness of the nature of being a pratyekabuddha and a mahāyāna pudgala, neither the pratyekabuddha nor the mahāyāna pudgala exists and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva also does not exist and cannot be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the śrāvaka-pudgala and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva are non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from the śrāvaka-pudgala and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, there is nothing that exists or can be apprehended.

Pratyekabuddhas and Mahāyāna individuals, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, are non-existent and unapprehendable; apart from Pratyekabuddhas and Mahāyāna individuals, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas are non-existent and unapprehendable.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied again to Śāriputra: "As the Venerable has said:

'For what reason do you say that, though I seek a bodhisattva mahāsattva among all phenomena, in every way, in every place, and at all times, I see none at all and cannot find one; how then am I to instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the perfection of wisdom?'"
"Śāriputra, because the nature of form is empty, form does not exist and cannot be apprehended within form; form does not exist and cannot be apprehended within feeling."

Because feeling is empty of intrinsic nature, feeling is non-existent and unapprehendable within feeling; feeling is non-existent and unapprehendable within form; and form and feeling are non-existent and unapprehendable within perception.

Because the nature of perception is empty, perception is non-existent and unobtainable within perception; perception is non-existent and unobtainable within form and sensation; and form, sensation, and perception are non-existent and unobtainable within mental formations.

Because their nature is emptiness, one practices with respect to formations as being non-existent and unapprehendable; one practices with respect to form, feeling, and perception as being non-existent and unapprehendable; and one practices with respect to consciousness as being non-existent and unapprehendable within form, feeling, and perception.

Because the nature of consciousness is empty, consciousness is non-existent and unapprehendable within consciousness; consciousness is non-existent and unapprehendable within form, feeling, perception, and formations.
Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, though I seek the bodhisattva-mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, he is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
"Śāriputra!..."
Because the nature of the eye-base is empty, the eye-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-base; the eye-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the ear-base.

Because the nature of the ear-base is empty, the ear-base is non-existent and unapprehendable within the ear-base; the ear-base is non-existent and unapprehendable within the eye-base; and the eye-base and ear-base are non-existent and unapprehendable within the nose-base.

Because the nature of the nose-base is empty, the nose-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nose-base; the nose-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-base or ear-base; and the eye-base, ear-base, and nose-base do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the tongue-base.

Because the nature of the tongue-base is empty, the tongue-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the tongue-base; the tongue-base does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-base, ear-base, or nose-base; and the eye-base, ear-base, nose-base, and tongue-base do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the body-base.

Because the sphere of the body is empty of intrinsic nature, the sphere of the body is non-existent and unapprehendable within the sphere of the body; the sphere of the body is non-existent and unapprehendable within the spheres of the eye, ear, nose, and tongue; and the spheres of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body are non-existent and unapprehendable within the sphere of the mind.

Because the sphere of mind is empty of intrinsic nature, the sphere of mind does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of mind; the sphere of mind does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the spheres of eye, ear, nose, tongue, or body.
Śāriputra! Regarding such dharmas as these, though I seek for a bodhisattva mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, none exists and none can be found.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty. "Śāriputra!

Because the sphere of form is empty of intrinsic nature, the sphere of form does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of form; the sphere of form does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of sound.

Because the sphere of sound is empty of its own nature, the sphere of sound does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of sound; the sphere of sound does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of form; and both the spheres of form and sound do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of odor.

Because the nature of the sphere of fragrance is empty, the sphere of fragrance does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of fragrance; the sphere of fragrance does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the spheres of form and sound; and the spheres of form, sound, and fragrance do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of taste.

Because the sphere of taste is empty of intrinsic nature, the sphere of taste does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of taste; the sphere of taste does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the spheres of form, sound, or odor; and the spheres of form, sound, odor, and taste do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of tangibles.

Because the sphere of tangibles is empty by nature, the sphere of tangibles does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of tangibles; the sphere of tangibles does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the spheres of forms, sounds, odors, or tastes; and the spheres of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*).

Because the sphere of mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) is empty of intrinsic nature, the sphere of mental phenomena does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sphere of mental phenomena; the sphere of mental phenomena does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the spheres of form, sound, odor, taste, or tangibility.
Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, though I seek the bodhisattva-mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, he is non-existent and cannot be found.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Sixty-four.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Sixty-Five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One: Chapter Eighteen on Non-Apprehension, Section Five.

“Śāriputra! Because the nature of the eye-element is empty, the eye-element is non-existent and unapprehendable within the eye-element; the eye-element is non-existent and unapprehendable within the form-element.”

Because the nature of the form realm is empty, the form realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the form realm; the form realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-element; and both the eye-element and the form realm do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-consciousness element.

Because the nature of the eye-consciousness element is empty, the eye-consciousness element is non-existent and unapprehendable within the eye-consciousness element; the eye-consciousness element is non-existent and unapprehendable within the eye-element and the form-element; and the eye-element, the form-element, and the eye-consciousness element are non-existent and unapprehendable within eye-contact.

Because the nature of eye-contact is empty, eye-contact does not exist and cannot be apprehended within eye-contact; eye-contact does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-element, the form-element, or the eye-consciousness-element; and the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, do not exist and cannot be apprehended within eye-contact.

Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature, those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended within those very feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; furthermore, those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, or the eye-contact itself.
Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, though I seek the bodhisattva-mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, he is likewise non-existent and unobtainable.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty. "Śāriputra!

Because the nature of the ear-element is empty, the ear-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the ear-element; the ear-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sound-element.

Because the nature of the sound-element is empty, the sound-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the sound-element; the sound-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the ear-element; and both the ear-element and the sound-element do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the ear-consciousness-element.

Because the nature of the auditory consciousness element is empty, the auditory consciousness element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the auditory consciousness element; the auditory consciousness element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the auditory element or the sound element; and the auditory element, the sound element, and the auditory consciousness element do not exist and cannot be apprehended within auditory contact.

Because the nature of auditory contact is empty, auditory contact is non-existent and unapprehendable within auditory contact; auditory contact is non-existent and unapprehendable within the ear-element, the sound-element, and the ear-consciousness-element; and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition within the ear-element, the sound-element, and the ear-consciousness-element are non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature, these sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended within those very sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; furthermore, these sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, or the ear-contact itself.
Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, though I seek the bodhisattva-mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, they are non-existent and cannot be found.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty. "Śāriputra!

Because the nature of the nose-element is empty, the nose-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nose-element; the nose-element does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the odor-element.

Because the nature of the realm of fragrance is empty, the realm of fragrance does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of fragrance; the realm of fragrance does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nose-realm; and both the nose-realm and the realm of fragrance do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nose-consciousness-realm.

Because the element of nose-consciousness is empty of intrinsic nature, the element of nose-consciousness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the element of nose-consciousness; the element of nose-consciousness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the element of the nose or the element of odors; and the elements of the nose, odors, and nose-consciousness do not exist and cannot be apprehended within nose-contact.

Because the nature of nose-contact is empty, nose-contact is non-existent and unapprehendable within nose-contact; nose-contact is non-existent and unapprehendable within the nose-element, the odor-element, and the nose-consciousness-element; and the nose-element, the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-existent and unapprehendable.
