Because external emptiness is empty of emptiness, external emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within external emptiness; external emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness; and internal and external emptiness do not exist and cannot be apprehended within both internal and external emptiness.

Because internal-and-external emptiness is empty, internal-and-external emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within internal-and-external emptiness; internal-and-external emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within internal emptiness or external emptiness; and internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-and-external emptiness do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of emptiness.

Because the emptiness of emptiness is itself empty, within the emptiness of emptiness there is nothing that exists and nothing that can be apprehended; within the emptiness of emptiness, internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-and-external emptiness have no existence and cannot be apprehended; from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of emptiness, within great emptiness there is nothing that exists and nothing that can be apprehended.

Because great emptiness is empty of itself, great emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within great emptiness; great emptiness does not exist and cannot be apprehended within inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of emptiness; and inner emptiness, up to and including great emptiness, do not exist and cannot be apprehended within ultimate emptiness.

Because ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness, ultimate emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within ultimate emptiness; ultimate emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within inner emptiness up to great emptiness; and inner emptiness up to ultimate emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within conditioned emptiness.

Because the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is itself empty, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of conditioned phenomena; the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is non-existent and unapprehendable within internal emptiness up to ultimate emptiness; and internal emptiness up to the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the unconditioned.

Because the emptiness of the unconditioned is itself empty, the unconditioned emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the unconditioned; the unconditioned emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the conditioned; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the unconditioned, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the ultimate emptiness.

Because the emptiness of ultimate emptiness is itself empty, ultimate emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within ultimate emptiness; ultimate emptiness is non-existent and unapprehendable within inner emptiness, up to and including conditioned and unconditioned emptiness; and inner emptiness, up to and including ultimate emptiness, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the limitless.

Because the emptiness of the limitless is itself empty, the emptiness of the limitless is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the limitless; the emptiness of the limitless is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the ultimate; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the limitless, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of dispersion.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is empty of itself, the emptiness of dispersion is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of dispersion; the emptiness of dispersion is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the limitless; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of dispersion, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of non-alteration.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is empty, the emptiness of non-alteration is neither existent nor obtainable within the emptiness of non-alteration; the emptiness of non-alteration is neither existent nor obtainable within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of dispersion; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of non-alteration, is neither existent nor obtainable within the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty, the emptiness of intrinsic nature does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of non-alteration; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of intrinsic nature, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the emptiness of self-characteristic.

Because the emptiness of self-characteristics is itself empty, the emptiness of self-characteristics is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of self-characteristics; the emptiness of self-characteristics is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of self-characteristics, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of common characteristics.

Because the emptiness of common characteristics is itself empty, the emptiness of common characteristics is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of common characteristics; the emptiness of common characteristics is non-existent and unapprehendable within internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of self-characteristics; and internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of common characteristics, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of all phenomena.

Because the emptiness of all phenomena is itself empty, all phenomena are empty; within the emptiness of all phenomena, nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended. Within the emptiness of all phenomena, from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of common characteristics, nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended. From internal emptiness up to the emptiness of all phenomena, within the emptiness of non-apprehension, nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended.

Because the emptiness of the unapprehendable is itself empty, the emptiness of the unapprehendable is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the unapprehendable; the emptiness of the unapprehendable is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of all phenomena; and the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the unapprehendable, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of non-existence.

Because the emptiness of non-existence is empty of itself, the emptiness of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of non-existence; the emptiness of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable within internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the unapprehendable; and internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of self-nature.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of itself, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of non-existence; and the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Because the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is itself empty, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable within the emptiness of the nature of non-existence; the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is non-existent and unapprehendable within inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Śāriputra! Regarding such dharmas as these, though I seek a bodhisattva mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, none exists and none can be found.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
"Śāriputra!..."
Because the nature of true thusness is empty, true thusness is non-existent and unobtainable within true thusness; true thusness is non-existent and unobtainable within the dharma-realm.

Because the nature of the dharma-realm is empty, the dharma-realm is non-existent and unobtainable within the dharma-realm; the dharma-realm is non-existent and unobtainable within suchness; and suchness and the dharma-realm are non-existent and unobtainable within the dharma-nature.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is empty of intrinsic nature, the nature of phenomena is non-existent and unapprehendable within the nature of phenomena; the nature of phenomena is non-existent and unapprehendable within *tathatā* (suchness) and the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm); and *tathatā*, the *dharmadhātu*, and the nature of phenomena are non-existent and unapprehendable within the non-erroneous nature (*avitathatā*).

Because the nature of non-falsity is empty of its own nature, non-falsity does not exist and cannot be apprehended within non-falsity; non-falsity does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, the dharma-realm, or the dharma-nature; and suchness, up to and including non-falsity, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nature of immutability.

Because the nature of non-alteration is empty of itself, non-alteration does not exist and cannot be apprehended within non-alteration; non-alteration does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including non-falsity; and suchness, up to and including non-alteration, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the inconceivable realm.

Because the nature of the inconceivable realm is empty, the inconceivable realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the inconceivable realm; the inconceivable realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within true suchness, up to and including the nature of immutability; and true suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of space.

Because the nature of the realm of space is empty, the realm of space is non-existent and unobtainable within the realm of space; the realm of space is non-existent and unobtainable within true suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm; and true suchness, up to and including the realm of space, is non-existent and unobtainable within the realm of cessation.

Because the realm of cessation is empty of its own nature, the realm of cessation is non-existent and unapprehendable within the realm of cessation; the realm of cessation is non-existent and unapprehendable within true thusness, up to and including the realm of space; and true thusness, up to and including the realm of cessation, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the realm of detachment.

Because the realm of detachment is empty of its own nature, the realm of detachment does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of detachment; the realm of detachment does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including the realm of cessation; and suchness, up to and including the realm of detachment, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of extinction.

Because the realm of cessation is empty of intrinsic nature, the realm of cessation is non-existent and unapprehendable within the realm of cessation; the realm of cessation is non-existent and unapprehendable within true suchness, up to and including the realm of detachment; and true suchness, up to and including the realm of cessation, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the state of equality.

Because the nature of equality is empty of its own nature, equality does not exist and cannot be apprehended within equality; equality does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including the realm of cessation; and suchness, up to and including equality, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nature of non-arising.

Because the nature of being free from arising is empty of its own nature, the nature of being free from arising does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the nature of being free from arising; the nature of being free from arising does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including equality; and suchness, up to and including the nature of being free from arising, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the fixed nature of phenomena.

Because phenomena are established as emptiness by nature, phenomena are established as being non-existent and unobtainable within phenomena; phenomena are established as being non-existent and unobtainable within suchness, up to and including the state of equality; and suchness, up to and including phenomena, are established as being non-existent and unobtainable within the abiding nature of phenomena.

Because the abiding nature of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) is empty, the abiding of phenomena within the abiding of phenomena is non-existent and unapprehendable; the abiding of phenomena within suchness (*tathatā*), up to and including the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), is non-existent and unapprehendable; and suchness, up to and including the fixed nature of phenomena, abiding within the realm of non-nature (*abhāvadhatu*), is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because the realm of non-nature is empty of its own nature, the realm of non-nature is non-existent and unobtainable within the realm of non-nature; the realm of non-nature is non-existent and unobtainable within true suchness, up to and including the abiding of phenomena; and true suchness, up to and including the realm of non-nature, is non-existent and unobtainable within the realm of signlessness.

Because the signless realm is empty of its own nature, the signless realm is non-existent and unapprehendable within the signless realm; the signless realm is non-existent and unapprehendable within true suchness, up to and including the realm of non-nature; and true suchness, up to and including the signless realm, is non-existent and unapprehendable within the realm of the unconditioned.

Because the nature of the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛta-dhātu*) is empty, the unconditioned realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the unconditioned realm; the unconditioned realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness (*tathatā*) up to the signless realm (*animitta-dhātu*); and suchness up to the unconditioned realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the unconditioned realm.

Because the nature of the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) is empty, the unconditioned realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the unconditioned realm; the unconditioned realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within *tathatā* up to the realm of non-activity (*anabhisaṃskāradhātu*); and *tathatā* up to the unconditioned realm does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of peace (*kṣemadhātu*).

Because the realm of peace is empty of intrinsic nature, the realm of peace does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of peace; the realm of peace does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including the unconditioned realm; and suchness, up to and including the realm of peace, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of tranquility.

Because the realm of tranquility is empty of intrinsic nature, the realm of tranquility does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the realm of tranquility; the realm of tranquility does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including the realm of peace; and suchness, up to and including the realm of tranquility, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within original non-arising.

Because they are empty of intrinsic nature from the very beginning, that which is non-existent from the beginning is non-existent, and nothing can be apprehended therein; within non-existence from the beginning, from suchness up to the realm of quiescence, nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended; and within suchness up to non-existence from the beginning, up to the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is empty of intrinsic nature, the limit of reality does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the limit of reality; the limit of reality does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness (*tathatā*), up to and including original non-arising (*abhūtvā-bhāva*). Suchness, up to and including the limit of reality, does not exist and cannot be apprehended within ultimate *nirvāṇa*.

Because ultimate nirvāṇa is empty of intrinsic nature, ultimate nirvāṇa does not exist and cannot be apprehended within ultimate nirvāṇa; ultimate nirvāṇa does not exist and cannot be apprehended within suchness, up to and including the limit of reality.
Śāriputra! Regarding such dharmas as these, if one were to seek a bodhisattva mahāsattva through every mode, in every place, and at every time, they would likewise be non-existent and unobtainable.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty.
"Śāriputra!..."

Because the dharma-nature of the Stage of Utmost Joy is empty, the dharma of the Stage of Utmost Joy does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharma of the Stage of Utmost Joy; the dharma of the Stage of Utmost Joy does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharma of the Stainless Stage.

Because the dharmas of the Stainless Ground (vimalā-bhūmi) are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the Stainless Ground do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Stainless Ground; the dharmas of the Stainless Ground do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Joyous Ground (pramuditā-bhūmi); and the dharmas of the Joyous and Stainless Grounds do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Radiant Ground (prabhākārī-bhūmi).

Because the *dharmatā* of the Radiant Stage (*prabhākari-bhūmi*) is empty, the phenomena of the Radiant Stage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the phenomena of the Radiant Stage; the phenomena of the Radiant Stage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the phenomena of the Joyful (*pramuditā*) and Immaculate (*vimalā*) Stages; and the phenomena of the Joyful, Immaculate, and Radiant Stages do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the phenomena of the Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī*) Stage.

Because the dharmas of the Ground of Blazing Wisdom are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the Ground of Blazing Wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Ground of Blazing Wisdom; the dharmas of the Ground of Blazing Wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Grounds of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, and Radiance; and the dharmas of the Grounds of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiance, and Blazing Wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Ground Difficult to Conquer.

Because the dharma-nature of the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer is empty, the dharma of the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharma of the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer; the dharma of the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Grounds of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiant Light, and Blazing Wisdom; and the dharmas of the Grounds of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiant Light, Blazing Wisdom, and Utmost Difficulty to Conquer do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharma of the Ground of Presence.

Because the dharmas of the Ground of Presence (Abhimukhī) are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the Ground of Presence are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the Ground of Presence; the dharmas of the Ground of Presence are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the Grounds of Extreme Joy (Pramuditā), Freedom from Defilement (Vimalā), Radiance (Prabhākārī), Blazing Wisdom (Arciṣmatī), and the Extremely Difficult to Conquer (Sudurjayā); and the dharmas of the Grounds of Extreme Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiance, Blazing Wisdom, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer, and the Ground of Presence are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the Ground of Far-Going (Dūraṃgamā).

Because the *dharma-nature* of the Far-Going Ground (*dūraṅgamā-bhūmi*) is empty, the *dharma* of the Far-Going Ground does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the *dharma* of the Far-Going Ground; the *dharma* of the Far-Going Ground does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the *dharmas* of the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant Wisdom, the Very Difficult to Conquer, or the Manifest Ground; and the *dharmas* of the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant Wisdom, the Very Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, and the Far-Going Grounds do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the *dharma* of the Immovable Ground (*acalā-bhūmi*).

Because the *dharmatā* of the Immovable Ground is empty, the *dharmas* of the Immovable Ground do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the *dharmas* of the Immovable Ground. The *dharmas* of the Immovable Ground do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the *dharmas* of the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant Wisdom, the Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, or the Far-Reaching grounds. Likewise, the *dharmas* of the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant Wisdom, the Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, the Far-Reaching, and the Immovable grounds do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the *dharmas* of the Good Intelligence ground.

Because the dharmas of the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (Sādhumatī-bhūmi) are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the Stage of Excellent Intelligence are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the Stage of Excellent Intelligence; the dharmas of the Stage of Excellent Intelligence are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the Stages of Utmost Joy (Pramuditā), Freedom from Defilement (Vimalā), Radiance (Prabhākārī), Blazing Wisdom (Arciṣmatī), Difficult to Conquer (Sudurjayā), Manifestation (Abhimukhī), Far-Going (Dūraṅgamā), and Immovability (Acalā); and the dharmas of the Stages of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiance, Blazing Wisdom, Difficult to Conquer, Manifestation, Far-Going, Immovability, and Excellent Intelligence are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā) Stage.

Because the dharmas of the Dharmameghā-bhūmi are empty of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the dharmas of the Dharmameghā-bhūmi do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Dharmameghā-bhūmi; the dharmas of the Dharmameghā-bhūmi do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the Pramuditā, Vimalā, Prabhākārī, Arciṣmatī, Sudurjayā, Abhimukhī, Dūraṃgamā, Acalā, and Sādhumatī bhūmis.
Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, though I seek a bodhisattva-mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at every time, none exists and cannot be found.
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is empty.
"Śāriputra!..."

Because the Ground of Utmost Joy is empty of intrinsic nature, the Ground of Utmost Joy does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Utmost Joy; the Ground of Utmost Joy does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Stainlessness.

Because the Stainless Ground (*vimalā-bhūmi*) is empty of intrinsic nature, the Stainless Ground does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Stainless Ground; the Stainless Ground does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Joyous Ground (*pramuditā-bhūmi*); and the Joyous and Stainless Grounds do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Radiant Ground (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*).

Because the Radiant Stage is empty of intrinsic nature, the Radiant Stage does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Radiant Stage; the Radiant Stage does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Joyous Stage or the Stainless Stage; and the Joyous, Stainless, and Radiant Stages do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Blazing Wisdom Stage.

Because the nature of the Stage of Blazing Wisdom is empty, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Stage of Blazing Wisdom; the Stage of Blazing Wisdom does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Stages of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, and Radiance; and the Stages of Utmost Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiance, and Blazing Wisdom do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Stage of Difficult Victory.

Because the nature of the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer is empty, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer; the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Grounds of Supreme Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiant Light, and Blazing Wisdom; and the Grounds of Supreme Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiant Light, Blazing Wisdom, and Utmost Difficulty to Conquer do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Ground of Presence.

Because the stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*) is empty of its own nature, the stage of Presence does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of Presence; the stage of Presence does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stages of Joy (*pramuditā*), Purity (*vimalā*), Radiance (*prabhākārī*), Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī*), and Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā*); and the stages of Joy, Purity, Radiance, Blazing Wisdom, Difficult to Conquer, and Presence do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of Far-Reaching (*dūraṅgamā*).

Because the stage of Far-Going is empty of intrinsic nature, the stage of Far-Going does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of Far-Going; the stage of Far-Going does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stages of Joyful, Stainless, Luminous, Blazing Wisdom, Difficult to Conquer, or Presence; and the stages of Joyful, Stainless, Luminous, Blazing Wisdom, Difficult to Conquer, Presence, and Far-Going do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of Immovable.

Because the stage of the Immovable is empty of intrinsic nature, the stage of the Immovable does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of the Immovable; the stage of the Immovable does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stages of the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant, the Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, and the Far-Reaching; and the stages of the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant, the Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, the Far-Reaching, and the Immovable do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of the Good Intelligence.

Because the stage of Good Intelligence is empty of intrinsic nature, the stage of Good Intelligence does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stage of Good Intelligence; the stage of Good Intelligence does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the stages of Perfect Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiant Light, Blazing Wisdom, Difficult to Conquer, Presence, Far-Going, and Immovable; and the stages of Perfect Joy, Freedom from Defilement, Radiant Light, Blazing Wisdom, Difficult to Conquer, Presence, Far-Going, Immovable, and Good Intelligence do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Cloud of Dharma stage.

Because the nature of the Dharma-Cloud Ground is empty, the Dharma-Cloud Ground does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Dharma-Cloud Ground; the Dharma-Cloud Ground does not exist and cannot be apprehended within the Joyous, the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant Wisdom, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, the Far-Reaching, the Immovable, or the Good Wisdom grounds.
Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, I have sought a bodhisattva mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, yet none exists and cannot be found.
Why is this? Because its intrinsic nature is empty.
*Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 65.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Sixty-six.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One: The Chapter on Non-Apprehension, Eighteenth, Section Six.

“Śāriputra! Because the dharma-nature of the stage of ordinary beings is empty, the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings; the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of the spiritual lineage.”

Because the dharmas of the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotrabhūmi*) are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the stage of the spiritual lineage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of the spiritual lineage; the dharmas of the stage of the spiritual lineage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*); and the dharmas of the stages of ordinary beings and the spiritual lineage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*).

Because the dharmas of the eighth stage are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the eighth stage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the eighth stage; the dharmas of the eighth stage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*) or the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotrabhūmi*); and the dharmas of ordinary beings, the spiritual lineage, and the eighth stage do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of those who have seen the truth (*darśanabhūmi*).

Because the dharmas of the stage of one who has seen (darśana-bhūmi) are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the stage of one who has seen are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the stage of one who has seen; the dharmas of the stage of one who has seen are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of ordinary beings (pṛthagjana), those of the spiritual lineage (gotra), and the eighth stage (aṣṭamaka-bhūmi); and the dharmas of ordinary beings, those of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, and the stage of one who has seen are non-existent and unapprehendable within the dharmas of the stage of refinement (tanu-bhūmi).

Because the dharmas of the stage of attenuation (*tanubhūmi*) are empty of intrinsic nature, the dharmas of the stage of attenuation do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of attenuation; the dharmas of the stage of attenuation do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*), the lineage (*gotra*), the eighth [stage] (*aṣṭamaka*), or the stage of those who have seen the truth (*dṛṣṭiprāpta*); and the dharmas of the stages of ordinary beings, the lineage, the eighth, and those who have seen the truth do not exist and cannot be apprehended within the dharmas of the stage of freedom from desire (*vītarāgabhūmi*).

Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas, though I seek the bodhisattva-mahāsattva in every way, in every place, and at all times, none exists and none can be found.
Why is this? Because their intrinsic nature is empty. "Śāriputra!
For this reason, I say this:

having sought for a bodhisattva mahāsattva among all phenomena—in every way, in every place, and at every time—I do not see one at all, nor can I find one. How then can I instruct and admonish the bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the perfection of wisdom?
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied again to Śāriputra:
"As the Venerable One has asked: 'For what reason is it said that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists as nothing more than a mere designation?'"
"Śāriputra! This is because the name 'bodhisattva mahāsattva' is merely a designation applied as a guest.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason is it said that the name 'bodhisattva-mahāsattva' is merely a designation applied adventitiously?
Subhūti replied:

"Just as the names of all phenomena are merely designations applied adventitiously—coming from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere; within all phenomena there is no name, and within a name there are no phenomena; they are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely conventional designations."
Why is this? Because all phenomena and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither all phenomena nor names exist and cannot be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva. They are neither joined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘form’ is merely a guest-phenomenon, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within form there is no name, and within the name there is no form; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.”
Why is this? Because both form and name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither form nor name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names "feeling," "perception," "formations," and "consciousness" are merely subsumed under adventitious designations, they come from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness there are no names; within names there are no feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, together with name, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness nor name exist and cannot be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious factors; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva. It is neither conjoined nor separate, being merely a conventional designation.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘eye-base’ is merely comprised of adventitious factors—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; within the eye-base there is no designation, and within the designation there is no eye-base; it is neither conjoined nor separate, but is merely a conventional designation.”

Why is this? Because the sense-base of the eye, together with its designation, is empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the sense-base of the eye nor its designation exists or can be apprehended.

Just as the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are designated merely as adventitious, they come from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere; within the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind there is no name, and within the name there is no ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, together with "name," are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind nor "name" exist or can be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious factors; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists merely as a provisional designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘form-base’ is merely a guest-phenomenon, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the form-base there is no designation, and within the designation there is no form-base; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.”

Why is this? Because the sphere of form and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the sphere of form nor the name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are designated merely as adventitious, they come from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena there is no name; within the name there are no bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena. They are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, together with names, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena nor names exist and cannot be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious factors; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva. It is neither joined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a provisional designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘eye-element’ is merely a guest-phenomenon, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the eye-element there is no designation, and within the designation there is no eye-element; they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely provisionally established.”
Why is this? Because the eye-faculty and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the eye-faculty nor the name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are designated as being comprised of mere guests—coming from nowhere in the ten directions or the three times, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere; and just as within the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition there is no "name," and within the name there is no form realm, eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, or all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣu-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) arising conditioned by eye-contact, together with name (*nāman*), are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*). Within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, the feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact, nor name exist; they are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The name of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva. It is neither joined nor separated, but is merely a provisional designation.
Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are non-existent and unapprehendable. Śāriputra!
For this reason, I say:
"A bodhisattva mahāsattva has only a provisional name.
"Śāriputra!..."

Just as the designation "ear-element" is comprised merely of adventitious factors—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; within the ear-element there is no designation, and within the designation there is no ear-element; it is neither joined nor separated, but is a mere conventional designation.
Why is this? Because the ear-element and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the ear-element nor the name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are designated as being comprised solely of the adventitious; they come from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, there is no "name"; within the "name," there is no sphere of sound, sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, or any feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature together with names; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, nor all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, nor names, exist or can be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is merely comprised of adventitious factors; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva. It is neither joined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists as a mere conventional designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘nose-element’ is merely a guest-phenomenon, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the nose-element there is no designation; within the designation there is no nose-element. It is neither conjoined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.”

Why is this? Because the nose-element and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the nose-element nor the name exists or can be apprehended.

Just as the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are designated as being comprised of mere guests; they come from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, there is no "name"; within the "name," there is no fragrance-element, nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the fragrance-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, together with "name" (*nāman*), are all empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*). Within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nor nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, nor "name," exist at all and cannot be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither conjoined nor separate, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘tongue-element’ is comprised solely of adventitious factors—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three times, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; within the tongue-element there is no designation, and within the designation there is no tongue-element; it is neither joined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.”

Why is this? Because the tongue-element and its designation are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the tongue-element nor its designation exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are designated as being comprised solely of "guests"—coming from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere; and just as within the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition there is no name, and within the name there is no taste element, tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the realm of taste, the realm of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are empty of intrinsic nature together with the designation; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the realm of taste, the realm of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, the sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, nor the designation exist or can be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘body-element’ (kāyadhātu) is merely a guest-phenomenon, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the body-element there is no name, and within the name there is no body-element; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.”

Why is this? Because the body-element (*kāya-dhātu*) and "name" (*nāman*) are both non-existent and unapprehendable. Just as with the touch-element (*spraṣṭavya-dhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāya-vijñāna-dhātu*), and body-contact (*kāya-spraṣṭavya*), as well as the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, "name" is merely a designation (*prajñapti*). It comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, there is no "name"; within "name," there is no touch-element, body-consciousness-element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. They are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely conventionally established.

Why is this? Because the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the sphere of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, together with the designation (*nāman*), are all empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*). Within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, nor body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, together with the designation, exist or can be apprehended.

The name "bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva. They are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely a conventional designation.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! The designation ‘mind-element’ is merely a guest-phenomenon; it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, it goes nowhere, nor does it abide anywhere. Within the mind-element there is no designation, and within the designation there is no mind-element. It is neither conjoined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.”

Why is this? Because the mental faculty (*manodhātu*) and names are both empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*); within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the mental faculty nor names exist and cannot be apprehended.

The dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-realm, mental contact, and all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition are designated as being comprised of mere guests. They come from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, they go nowhere, and they abide nowhere. Within the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-realm, mental contact, and the sensations produced with mental contact as a condition, there is no "name"; within the "name," there is no dharma-realm, no mental consciousness-realm, no mental contact, and no sensations produced with mental contact as a condition. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and the contact of the mind, as well as the various feelings produced with that mental contact as condition, are all empty of intrinsic nature together with the designation (nāman). Within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, the contact of the mind, the various feelings produced with that mental contact as condition, nor the designation exist or can be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise so: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘earth element’ is merely a guest-phenomenon, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions and three times, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the earth element there is no designation, and within the designation there is no earth element; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely provisionally established.”

Why is this? Because the earth element and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the earth element nor the name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are comprised of what is merely adventitious—coming from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere; and just as within the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness there is no name, and within the name there are no elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness—they are neither joined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, together with name, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness nor name exist and cannot be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, nor can they be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘Noble Truth of Suffering’ is merely comprised of adventitious names—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, it goes nowhere, nor does it abide anywhere; within the Noble Truth of Suffering there is no name, and within the name there is no Noble Truth of Suffering; they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely provisionally designated.”

Why is this? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the Noble Truth of Suffering nor the name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are merely designated by adventitious conventions, they come from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere; within the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path there are no names, and within the names there are no noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path. They are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, together with "name," are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path nor "name" exist or can be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva. It is neither joined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the name ‘ignorance’ is merely a designation applied adventitiously—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; there is no name within ignorance, and no ignorance within the name; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.”
Why is this? Because ignorance and name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither ignorance nor name exists, and neither can be apprehended.

Just as the formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are designated merely as adventitious designations, they come from nowhere in the ten directions or the three times, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within the formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair there is no name; within the name there are no formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. They are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, together with name, they are empty of intrinsic nature; and within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, whether it be from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or name itself, none exist and cannot be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, being unobtainable.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the names of the four dhyānas are merely comprised of adventitious designations—coming from nowhere, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time; within the four dhyānas there are no names, and within names there are no four dhyānas; they are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.”

Why is this? Because the four dhyānas and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the four dhyānas nor their names exist or can be apprehended.

Just as the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are designated as being comprised merely of adventitious names—neither coming from anywhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, nor going anywhere, nor abiding anywhere; and just as there are no names within the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and no four immeasurables or four formless absorptions within the names—they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the four immeasurables, nor the four formless absorptions, nor their names exist or can be apprehended.

The name "bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the name ‘eight liberations’ is merely a designation applied adventitiously—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; within the eight liberations there is no name, and within the name there are no eight liberations; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the eight liberations and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the eight liberations nor the names exist and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are comprised solely of adventitious designations—coming from nowhere in the ten directions or three times, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere; such that within the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities there are no names, and within the names there are no eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, or ten totalities—they are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, nor the ten totalities, nor their names, exist or can be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the name ‘four foundations of mindfulness’ is merely comprised of adventitious designations—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions or the three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; there is no name within the four foundations of mindfulness, and there are no four foundations of mindfulness within the name—they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.”

Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the four foundations of mindfulness nor their names exist and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are comprised merely of adventitious designations—coming from nowhere in the ten directions and three times, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere—so too, within the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, there are no names; and within the names, there are no four right efforts, four bases of power, five faculties, five powers, seven factors of enlightenment, or eightfold noble path. They are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are, together with their names, empty of intrinsic nature; and because within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, nor their names exist or can be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a provisional designation.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Sixty-Six (and Sixty-Seven) Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Scroll Sixty-Seven Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree
The Eighteenth Chapter on Non-Apprehension, Part One, Section Seven:

“Śāriputra! Just as the name ‘gate of liberation through emptiness’ is merely a designation applied adventitiously, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the gate of liberation through emptiness there is no name; within the name there is no gate of liberation through emptiness. It is neither joined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.”

Why is this? Because the gate of liberation of emptiness and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the gate of liberation of emptiness nor the name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are merely comprised of adventitious designations; they come from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within the gateways of signlessness and wishlessness there are no names, and within names there are no gateways of signlessness and wishlessness. They are neither joined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness, together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, both the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness, as well as their names, are non-existent and unapprehendable.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise so: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a provisional designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the names of the five eyes are merely comprised of adventitious designations, they come from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, go nowhere, and abide nowhere. Within the five eyes there are no names, and within names there are no five eyes; they are neither joined nor separated, being merely conventional designations.”
Why is this? Because the five eyes and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the five eyes nor their names exist and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the designation "six supernormal powers" is comprised solely of adventitious names—coming from nowhere, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere throughout the ten directions and three periods of time; within the six supernormal powers there is no name, and within the name there are no six supernormal powers; they are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the six supernormal powers and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the six supernormal powers nor their names exist or can be apprehended.

The name "Bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise so: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no Bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, nor can they be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a provisional designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the name ‘the ten powers of a Buddha’ is merely a designation, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the ten powers of a Buddha there is no name, and within the name there are no ten powers of a Buddha; they are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.”

Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha and their names are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the ten powers of a Buddha nor their names exist and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are comprised merely of adventitious designations—coming from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, going nowhere, and abiding nowhere; such that within the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities there is no name, and within the name there are no four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or eighteen unique qualities; they are neither conjoined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are, together with their names, empty of intrinsic nature; and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, nor the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor their names, exist or can be apprehended.

The name of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they are neither conjoined nor separated, being merely a provisional designation.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; and within that emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists or can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a mere designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘omniscience’ is merely a guest-attribute, it comes from nowhere in the ten directions and three times, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; within omniscience there is no name, and within the name there is no omniscience. It is neither conjoined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.”
Why is this? Because all-knowledge and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither all-knowledge nor its name exists and cannot be apprehended.

Just as the names "knowledge of the aspects of the path" and "knowledge of all aspects" are subsumed under mere designations, they come from nowhere in the ten directions and three times, go nowhere, and abide nowhere; within the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects there are no names, and within names there is no knowledge of the aspects of the path or knowledge of all aspects. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely conventional designations.

Why is this? Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), together with their names, are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*); and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor the knowledge of all aspects, nor their names exist or can be apprehended.

The name "bodhisattva-mahāsattva" is likewise thus: it is comprised solely of adventitious designations; throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, it comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere. Within the bodhisattva-mahāsattva there is no name, and within the name there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva. They are neither joined nor separated, but are merely provisional designations.

Why is this? Because both the bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the name are empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the name exists, and neither can be apprehended.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva exists only as a provisional designation.

“Śāriputra! Just as the designation ‘the quality of non-forgetfulness’ is merely comprised of adventitious factors—it comes from nowhere in the ten directions and three periods of time, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere; within the quality of non-forgetfulness there is no name, and within the name there is no quality of non-forgetfulness; it is neither conjoined nor separated, but is merely a conventional designation.”

Why is this? Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and its name are both empty of intrinsic nature; within the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither the quality of non-forgetfulness nor its name exists and cannot be apprehended.
