For this reason, that which is ultimately unarisen is not called the "mind-element."
Śāriputra!

Because the dharma-realm, the mind-consciousness realm, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are by nature empty, if a phenomenon is empty by nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it is not termed the "dharma-realm" (dharmadhātu), nor even "the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.
"Śāriputra!..."
Because the element of earth is empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, that which is ultimately unarisen is not called the element of earth.

Śāriputra! Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are empty by their very nature, if a phenomenon is empty by its very nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, then it cannot be designated as the element of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness. "Śāriputra,
because the noble truth of suffering is empty of intrinsic nature, if a dharma is empty of intrinsic nature, then it cannot be conceptually established as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there were ultimately no arising, it would not be designated as the Noble Truth of Suffering.

Śāriputra, because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of intrinsic nature, and because if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, then it cannot be designated as the noble truths of origin,
cessation, or the path. "Śāriputra,
because the intrinsic nature of ignorance is empty, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, then it cannot be established as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it is not termed ignorance. Śāriputra, because the nature of volitional formations,

consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is empty of intrinsic nature, if a dharma is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, then it is not termed "volitional formations" up to "old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Śāriputra,
because internal emptiness is by nature empty, if a phenomenon is empty by nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there were absolutely no arising, it would not be called "internal emptiness.

Śāriputra, because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are by their very nature empty; therefore, regarding a phenomenon whose nature is empty, one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, it is not designated as "external emptiness" up to "emptiness of the nature of non-existence. "Śāriputra!
Because the perfection of generosity is empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there were ultimately no arising, it would not be called the perfection of generosity.

Śāriputra, because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of intrinsic nature, and because a phenomenon that is empty of intrinsic nature cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, it cannot be designated as "pure ethical discipline" up to and including "the perfection of wisdom.
Śāriputra, because the four dhyānas are empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be established as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, it cannot be designated as the four dhyānas. Śāriputra,

because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of intrinsic nature, and because a phenomenon that is empty of intrinsic nature cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, they are not designated as the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
"Śāriputra, because the eight liberations are empty of intrinsic nature, if a dharma is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be established as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there were ultimately no arising, they would not be called the eight liberations.

Śāriputra, because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of intrinsic nature, and because if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, they are not designated as the eight bases of mastery or even the ten spheres of totality.
"Śāriputra, because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty of intrinsic nature, if a dharma is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, they are not called the four foundations of mindfulness. Śāriputra, because the four right efforts,

the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, then one cannot speak of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path.

"Śāriputra, because the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there were ultimately no arising, it could not be called the gate of liberation of emptiness. Śāriputra,

because the natures of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty, if the nature of a phenomenon is empty, then one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there were absolutely no arising, they would not be called the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
*Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 69 [and] Scroll 70.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One, Chapter Eighteen, "The Non-Apprehension," Section Ten:
"Śāriputra!..."
Because the five eyes are empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, that which is ultimately unarisen is not called the "five eyes."
Śāriputra! Because the six supernormal knowledges are empty of intrinsic nature, if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be called the six supernormal powers. "Śāriputra!
Because the intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is empty, if the intrinsic nature of any phenomenon is empty, then one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be called the ten powers of a Buddha. Śāriputra, because the four fearlessnesses,

the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of intrinsic nature, and since a dharma that is empty of intrinsic nature cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there were ultimately no arising, they would not be called the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. "Śāriputra!
Because the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge is empty, if the intrinsic nature of a phenomenon is empty, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there were ultimate non-arising, it could not be called "all-knowledge" (*sarvajñatā*). Śāriputra,

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are empty of intrinsic nature, and because if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be designated as the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
"Śāriputra, because the nature of the dharmas of non-forgetfulness is empty, if a dharma is empty by its very nature, then it cannot be established as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there were ultimate non-arising, it could not be called the quality of non-forgetfulness. Śāriputra,

because the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of intrinsic nature, and because if a phenomenon is empty of intrinsic nature, one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be termed "the nature of equanimity that abides constantly. Śāriputra!
Because the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is empty, if the intrinsic nature of a phenomenon is empty, then one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there were ultimate non-arising, it could not be called "all gateways of dhāraṇī. Śāriputra,
because all gateways of samādhi are empty of intrinsic nature, if a dharma is empty of intrinsic nature, one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be called "all gateways to samādhi. Śāriputra,
because the fundamental nature of the Ground of Extreme Joy is empty, if a phenomenon is empty by its fundamental nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there were ultimately no arising, it would not be called the Ground of Utmost Joy. Śāriputra, because the Ground of Purity,

the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Ultimate Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are all empty by their very nature, and since the nature of phenomena is empty, one cannot designate them as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, it cannot be called the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, nor even the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma. "Śāriputra,
because the nature of the stage of ordinary beings is empty, if the nature of a phenomenon is empty, then one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, it is not called the stage of the ordinary person (*pṛthagjana-bhūmi*).

Śāriputra, because the stage of the lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamaka-bhūmi*), the stage of possessing vision (*darśana-bhūmi*), the stage of refinement (*tanu-bhūmi*), the stage of freedom from desire (*vītarāga-bhūmi*), the stage of completion (*kṛtāvi-bhūmi*), the stage of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha-bhūmi*), the stage of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattva-bhūmi*), and the stage of the Tathāgata (*tathāgata-bhūmi*) are by nature empty, if a dharma is empty by nature, then it cannot be designated as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it cannot be designated as the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotrabhūmi*) up to the stage of the Tathāgata.
"Śāriputra, because the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle is empty, if a phenomenon is empty by its very nature, it cannot be established as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing."
For this reason, if there is ultimate non-arising, it is not called the Śrāvaka Vehicle. Śāriputra,
because the nature of the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle and the Great Vehicle is empty, if a phenomenon is empty by its very nature, then one cannot designate it as arising, ceasing, abiding, or changing.
For this reason, if there is ultimately no arising, it cannot be designated as the Pratyekabuddhayāna or the Mahāyāna.
"Śāriputra, for this reason I say:
"If they are ultimately non-arising, they cannot be designated as 'form' and so forth,
because empty and non-arising phenomena are ineffable.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again replied to Śāriputra:

"As the Venerable One has said: 'For what reason do you say, "How could I possibly instruct and admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of the perfection of wisdom that is ultimately unarisen?"'"
"O Śāriputra! Ultimate non-arising is itself the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the perfection of wisdom is itself ultimate non-arising."
Why is this? Because ultimate non-arising and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual and not divided into two. Śāriputra!
Ultimate non-arising is itself the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva is himself ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because ultimate non-arising and the bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say this:
How could I possibly instruct and admonish bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are ultimately unarisen by means of the Prajñāpāramitā which is ultimately unarisen?
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied again to Śāriputra:
"As the Venerable has asked: 'For what reason do you say that because of ultimate non-arising there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening?'"
"Thus it is, Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the perfection of wisdom as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the bodhisattva mahāsattva as distinct from ultimate non-arising."
Why is this? Because the perfection of wisdom and the bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and indivisible from that which is ultimately unarisen.

“Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive form as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as distinct from ultimate non-arising.”
Why is this? Because form, up to and including consciousness, and ultimate non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eye-base as distinct from its ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-base as distinct from their ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the sense base of the eye, up to and including the sense base of the mind, is non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the sense base of form as distinct from its ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as distinct from their ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) up to the sphere of mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eye-element as distinct from its ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as conditions as distinct from their ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the eye-faculty, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising. "Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the ear-element as distinct from its ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as conditions as distinct from their ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the ear-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the nose element as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various sensations produced with nose-contact as conditions as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the nose element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the tongue-element as distinct from its ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as distinct from their ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the tongue element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the body-element as distinct from its ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, or the various sensations produced with body-contact as conditions as distinct from their ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the body element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the mind-element as distinct from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, or the various feelings produced with mental contact as conditions as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the mental faculty (*manodhātu*) and even the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the earth element as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the element of earth, up to and including the element of consciousness, is non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the noble truth of suffering as being distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering, up to the Noble Truth of the Path, and ultimate non-arising are non-dual and indivisible.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive ignorance as being other than absolute non-arising; nor do they perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as being other than absolute non-arising.
Why is this? Because ignorance up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive internal emptiness as distinct from that which is ultimately non-arising; nor do they perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as distinct from that which is ultimately non-arising.
Why is this? Because internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, is non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising. “Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the perfection of generosity as being distinct from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, there is no duality and no division between them and ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four dhyānas as being other than ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions as being other than ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eight liberations as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the eight liberations up to the ten totalities are non-dual with and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four applications of mindfulness as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising. "Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the door of liberation of emptiness as being different from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as being different from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the five eyes as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the six supernormal powers as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are non-dual with and indivisible from ultimate non-arising. “Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the ten powers of a buddha as distinct from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual with and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive all-knowledge as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects as distinct from ultimate non-arising.

Why is this? Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-dual with and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the state of constant abiding in equanimity as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity are non-dual with and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any dhāraṇī doors as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive any samādhi doors as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the Ground of Extreme Joy as distinct from ultimate non-arising; nor do they perceive the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of Dharma Clouds as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because from the Stage of Utmost Joy up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, they are non-dual and indivisible from that which is ultimately unarisen.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the distinctness of the stage of ordinary beings as something ultimately non-arisen; nor do they perceive the distinctness of the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of having seen, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, or the stage of the Tathāgata as something ultimately non-arisen.
Why is this? Because the stage of an ordinary person up to the stage of a Tathāgata and ultimate non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"Śāriputra!..."

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the Śrāvaka vehicle as distinct from ultimate non-arising, nor do they perceive the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Mahāyāna as distinct from ultimate non-arising.
Why is this? Because the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Mahāyāna are non-dual and indivisible from ultimate non-arising.
"Śāriputra!..."
"For this reason, I say:
apart from that which is ultimately unborn, there is no bodhisattva who can practice for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again replied to Śāriputra:

"As the Venerable One has said: 'For what reason is it stated that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such an exposition, their mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, does not sink, does not become despondent, and is neither distressed nor regretful, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?'"

"Śāriputra! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive any phenomena as having cognition or function. They see all phenomena as being like magical illusions, like dream-visions, like reflections, like echoes, like shadows, like mirages, like flowers in the sky, like cities of the gandharvas, and like transformations—all of which are utterly devoid of reality. Upon hearing it said that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is emptiness, they rejoice with profound depth of heart."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say this:

if, upon hearing these words spoken, the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, does not sink, does not become despondent, and is neither distressed nor regretful, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
19. Chapter on Contemplative Practice, Part One: Chapter Nineteen on Contemplative Practice, Section One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to form (*rūpa*), nor do they designate it as "form.

Likewise, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*), nor do they designate them as "feeling," "perception," "formations," or "consciousness."
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the sense base of the eye, nor do they designate it as the sense base of the eye;
they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, nor do they designate them as the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
“World-Honored One!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), nor do they designate it as the sphere of form.

Likewise, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects (*dharmāyatana*), nor do they designate them as the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects.”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the eye-element; nor do they designate it as the ‘eye-element.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; nor do they designate them as the ‘form-element’ up to the ‘various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the ear-element; nor do they designate it as the ‘ear-element.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; nor do they designate them as the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*); nor do they designate it as the ‘nose-element.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition; nor do they designate them as the ‘odor-element’ up to the ‘various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.’”
“World-Honored One!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*); nor do they designate it as the ‘tongue-element.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition; nor do they designate them as the ‘taste-element’ up to the ‘various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.’”

“Bhagavān! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the body-element (*kāyadhātu*); nor do they designate it as the body-element.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the element of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the element of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition; nor do they designate them as the element of tangibles, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

“Bhagavān! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the mind-element (*manodhātu*); nor do they designate it as the mind-element.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the phenomenon-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition; nor do they designate them as the phenomenon-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition.”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the earth element, nor do they designate it as the earth element;

they likewise do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor do they designate them as the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the noble truth of suffering, nor do they designate it as the noble truth of suffering;
they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, nor do they designate them as the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.”

“Bhagavān! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to ignorance, nor do they designate it as ‘ignorance.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, nor do they designate them as ‘volitional formations’ up to ‘old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), nor do they designate it as ‘internal emptiness.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor do they designate them as ‘external emptiness’ up to ‘emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the perfection of giving, nor do they designate it as ‘the perfection of giving.

Likewise, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor do they designate them as ‘the perfection of ethical discipline,’ ‘the perfection of patience,’ ‘the perfection of diligence,’ ‘the perfection of meditative concentration,’ or ‘the perfection of wisdom.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the four dhyānas, nor do they designate them as ‘the four dhyānas.

They likewise do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, nor do they designate them as ‘the four immeasurables’ or ‘the four formless attainments.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the eight liberations, nor do they designate them as ‘the eight liberations.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, nor do they designate them as ‘the eight bases of mastery,’ ‘the nine successive attainments,’ or ‘the ten totalities.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they designate them as ‘the four foundations of mindfulness.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, nor do they designate them as ‘the four right efforts’ up to ‘the eightfold noble path.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they designate it as the ‘gate of liberation of emptiness.

They do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, nor do they designate them as the ‘gates of liberation of signlessness’ or ‘wishlessness.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the five eyes, nor do they designate them as ‘the five eyes.
They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the six supernormal powers, nor do they designate them as ‘the six supernormal powers.’”
“World-Honored One!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the ten powers of a Buddha, nor do they designate them as the ten powers of a Buddha.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor do they designate them as the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

“Bhagavān! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to suchness; nor do they designate it as ‘suchness.

They do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm; nor do they designate them as the ‘realm of phenomena’ up to the ‘inconceivable realm.’”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; nor do they designate it as ‘unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

They do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñā*), or knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñā*); nor do they designate them as ‘all-knowledge,’ ‘knowledge of the aspects of the path,’ or ‘knowledge of all aspects.’”
“World-Honored One!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they designate it as the quality of non-forgetfulness;
they do not accept, grasp, cling to, or adhere to the nature of constant equanimity, nor do they designate it as the nature of constant equanimity.”
“World-Honored One!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to any of the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor do they designate them as ‘gateways of dhāraṇī.
They do not receive, grasp, cling to, or adhere to any of the gateways of samādhi, nor do they designate them as ‘gateways of samādhi.’”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive form (rūpa). Why is this?
Because the nature of form is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations,
or consciousness. Why is this?
Because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the sense-base of the eye."
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of the eye is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing;
thus, one does not perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the sphere of form.
Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of form is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena. Why is this?
Because the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu). Why is this?
Because the nature of the eye-element is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, nor the various sensations produced with eye-contact as their condition.
Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the form realm up to eye-contact is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the ear-element (śrotra-dhātu). Why is this?
Because the nature of the ear-element is empty, being without arising or cessation.
One does not perceive the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, or the various feelings produced with auditory contact as their condition.

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with auditory contact as their condition, is empty of intrinsic nature and devoid of arising and ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*). Why is this?
Because the nature of the nose element is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nor nose-contact, nor the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the fragrance-element up to nose-contact is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the tongue element.
Why is this? Because the nature of the tongue element is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition.
Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition, is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the body-element (kāyadhātu). Why is this?
Because the nature of the body element is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, nor the various sensations produced with body-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the element of tangibility up to bodily contact is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the mental faculty (*manodhātu*). Why is this?
Because the nature of the mental faculty is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, nor the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition, is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the earth element. Why is this?
Because the nature of the earth element is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive the elements of water, fire, wind, space,
or consciousness. Why is this?
Because the natures of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the Noble Truth of Suffering.”
Why is this? Because the noble truth of suffering is empty of intrinsic nature and devoid of arising and ceasing;
one does not perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.
Why is this? Because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of intrinsic nature and are without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!..."
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive ignorance (avidyā).
Why is this? Because the nature of ignorance is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.

One does not perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Why is this? It is because the nature of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!..."
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because internal emptiness is empty of its own nature and is without arising or ceasing.

One does not perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Why is this? Because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, is empty of its own nature and is without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the perfection of generosity.
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity is empty of intrinsic nature and is without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom. Why is this?
Because the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the four dhyānas. Why is this?
Because the four dhyānas are empty of intrinsic nature and are without arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions. Why is this?
Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are by nature empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eight liberations."
Why is this? Because the nature of the eight liberations is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.
Why is this? Because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are empty of intrinsic nature and are without arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!”
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four applications of mindfulness.
Why is this? Because the nature of the four applications of mindfulness is empty, being without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path. Why is this?
Because the nature of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the gate of liberation that is emptiness."
Why is this? Because the nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing;
thus, one does not perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness or wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the nature of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is empty, without arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!...”
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the five eyes.
Why is this? Because the nature of the five eyes is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the nature of the six supernormal powers is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the ten powers (daśabala) of a Buddha. Why is this?
Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,

one does not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Why is this? Because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
“World-Honored One!...”
When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive suchness.
Why is this? Because the nature of suchness is empty, being without arising or ceasing.

He does not perceive the dharma-realm, the nature of dharmas, the non-falsity of dharmas, the immutability of dharmas, the equality of dharmas, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Because unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment is empty of intrinsic nature and is without arising or ceasing.
One does not perceive all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Why is this?
Because the nature of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects is empty, being without arising or cessation.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing,
one does not perceive the nature of constant equanimity. Why is this?
Because the nature of the state of constant equanimity is empty of self-nature and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any of the dhāraṇī-doors."
Why is this? Because the nature of all dharanī-doors is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing;
thus, one does not perceive any samādhi-doors.
Why is this? Because the nature of all samādhi-gates is empty and devoid of arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"

If form does not arise, it is not form; if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not arise, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness. Why is this so?
Form is non-dual with non-arising and indivisible; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual with non-arising and indivisible. Why is this?

Because the dharma of non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different, therefore, when form is non-arising, it is not form; when feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-arising, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“World-Honored One!
If the eye-base does not arise, it is not the eye-base; if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases do not arise, they are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”

Why is this? The sense-base of the eye is non-dual with non-arising and cannot be divided into two; the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual with non-arising and cannot be divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, when the eye-base does not arise, it is not the eye-base; when the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases do not arise, they are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.
“World-Honored One!

If the sense-base of form is non-arising, it is not the sense-base of form; if the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-arising, they are not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”

Why is this? Because the sphere of form is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, when the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) does not arise, it is not the sphere of form; when the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*) do not arise, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects.
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element does not arise, it is not the eye-element; if the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not arise, they are not the form-element, nor even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the eye-element and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, from the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they are non-dual and not divided into two with non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not distinct. Therefore, the non-arising of the eye-element is not the eye-element; the non-arising of the form-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is not the form-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the ear-element is unarisen, it is not the ear-element; if the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are unarisen, they are not the sound-element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; and so too, the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the ear-element is not the ear-element; the non-arising of the sound-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is not the sound-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) does not arise, it is not the nose element; if the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), and the contact of the nose (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*), as well as the various feelings produced with the contact of the nose as a condition, do not arise, they are not the odor element, nor even the various feelings produced with the contact of the nose as a condition.”

Why is this? The nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; likewise, the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*) and even all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the nose-element is not the nose-element; the non-arising of the fragrance-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is not the fragrance-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) does not arise, it is not the tongue-element; if the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition do not arise, they are not the taste-element, up to and including all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? The tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is non-dual with non-arising and indivisible; likewise, from the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, these are non-dual with non-arising and indivisible.

Why is this? Because the unarisen dharma is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the non-arising of the tongue-element means it is not the tongue-element; the non-arising of the taste-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, means they are not the taste-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is unarisen, it is not the body-element; if the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are unarisen, they are not the touch-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? The body element (*kāyadhātu*) is non-dual with and indivisible from non-arising; likewise, the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are non-dual with and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the non-arising of the body element (*kāyadhātu*) means it is not the body element; the non-arising of the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition means they are not the contact element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the mind-element (*manodhātu*) does not arise, it is not the mind-element; if the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, do not arise, they are not the dharma-element, nor even the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, from the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, they and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the unarisen dharma is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, when the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is unarisen, it is not the mind-element; when the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are unarisen, they are not the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element is non-arising, it is not the earth element; if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are non-arising, they are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
Why is this? The earth element is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the earth element that does not arise is not the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements that do not arise are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering does not arise, it is not the noble truth of suffering; if the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path do not arise, they are not the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.”
Why is this? The noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the noble truth of suffering, being non-arisen, is not the noble truth of suffering; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, being non-arisen, are not the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance does not arise, it is not ignorance; if volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not arise, they are not volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Ignorance is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, when ignorance does not arise, it is not ignorance; when formations through to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair do not arise, they are not formations through to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“Bhagavān! If internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) does not arise, it is not internal emptiness; if external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence do not arise, they are not external emptiness, up to and including emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

Why is this so? Because inner emptiness and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness; the non-arising of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, is not external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Seventy;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Seventy-One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The Nineteenth Chapter on the Practice of Contemplation, Part Two:
“World-Honored One!

If the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) is non-arising, it is not the perfection of giving; if the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*) are non-arising, they are not the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

Why is this? The perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity; likewise, the non-arising of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is not the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas do not arise, they are not the four dhyānas; if the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not arise, they are not the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”
Why is this? The four dhyānas and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different; therefore, the non-arising of the four dhyānas is not the four dhyānas, and the non-arising of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

If the eight liberations are non-arising, they are not the eight liberations; if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-arising, they are not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.”

Why is this? The eight liberations and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the eight liberations is not the eight liberations; the non-arising of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness do not arise, they are not the four foundations of mindfulness; if the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path do not arise, they are not the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.”

Why is this? The four foundations of mindfulness and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the non-arising of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the four foundations of mindfulness; the non-arising of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is not the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

If the gate of liberation of emptiness does not arise, it is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not arise, they are not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”

Why is this? The gate of liberation of emptiness is non-dual with and indivisible from non-arising; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-dual with and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the gate of liberation of emptiness is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; the non-arising of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is not the gate of liberation of signlessness or the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!
If the five eyes are non-arising, they are not the five eyes; if the six supernormal powers are non-arising, they are not the six supernormal powers. Why is this so?
The five eyes and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; the six supernormal powers and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is this?

Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the five eyes is not the five eyes, and the non-arising of the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha do not arise, they are not the ten powers of a Buddha; if the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not arise, they are not the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of the Buddha’s ten powers is not the Buddha’s ten powers; the non-arising of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is not the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

If true suchness (*tathatā*) were not produced, it would not be true suchness; if the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equanimity, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm were not produced, they would not be the realm of phenomena, up to and including the inconceivable realm.”
Why is this? Suchness and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided; from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, they are non-dual and cannot be divided with non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if True Suchness were non-arising, it would not be True Suchness; if the Dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, were non-arising, they would not be the Dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

If unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment were non-arising, it would not be unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; if all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects were non-arising, they would not be all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”

Why is this? Unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; omniscience (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is not itself unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; the non-arising of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is not itself all-knowledge, knowledge of the aspects of the path, or knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

If the quality of non-forgetfulness does not arise, it is not the quality of non-forgetfulness; if the state of constant abiding in equanimity does not arise, it is not the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”
Why is this? The quality of non-forgetfulness and non-arising are non-dual and not divided; the state of constant equanimity and non-arising are non-dual and not divided.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different; therefore, the dharma of non-forgetfulness, being non-arising, is not the dharma of non-forgetfulness, and the state of constant equanimity, being non-arising, is not the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!
If all dharani-doors are non-arising, they are not all dharani-doors; if all samadhi-doors are non-arising, they are not all samadhi-doors.”
Why is this? All dharani-doors are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising; all samadhi-doors are non-dual and indivisible from non-arising.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-arising of all dhāraṇī-doors is not all dhāraṇī-doors; the non-arising of all samādhi-doors is not all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!
If form does not cease, it is not form; if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not cease, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
Why is this? Form and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, when form is non-extinguished, it is not form; when feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-extinguished, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“World-Honored One!
If the eye-base is not extinguished, it is not the eye-base; if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not extinguished, they are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”

Why is this? The sense base of the eye and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-extinction of the eye-base is not the eye-base; the non-extinction of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is not the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base.
“World-Honored One!
