If the sphere of form is not extinguished, it is not the sphere of form; if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are not extinguished, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena.”
Why is this? The sphere of form is non-dual and indivisible from non-extinction; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual and indivisible from non-extinction.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if the sphere of form is not extinguished, it is not the sphere of form; if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not extinguished, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element is not extinguished, it is not the eye-element; if the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are not extinguished, they are not the form-element, nor even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the eye-element and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, from the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because that which is an unceasing dharma is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct. Therefore, the eye-element that does not cease is not the eye-element; likewise, from the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, those that do not cease are not the form-element, nor are they the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the ear-element is not extinguished, it is not the ear-element; if the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are not extinguished, they are not the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? The ear-element (*śrotradhātu*) and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, from the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, they and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, the non-extinction of the ear-element is not the ear-element; likewise, the non-extinction of the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is not the sound-element, nor the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is not extinguished, it is not the nose element; if the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are not extinguished, they are not the odor element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? The nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because that which is an unceasing dharma is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, if the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is unceasing, it is not the nose-element; if the fragrance-element (*gandhadhātu*), and so forth, up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are unceasing, they are not the fragrance-element, and so forth, up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) does not cease, it is not the tongue-element; if the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), and the contact of the tongue (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings produced with the contact of the tongue as condition (*jihvā-saṃsparśa-pratyaya-ja-vedanā*), do not cease, they are not the taste-element, and so on, up to all feelings produced with the contact of the tongue as condition.”

Why is this? Because the tongue element and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible; likewise, from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, they and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible.

Why is this? Because that which is an unceasing dharma is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, the tongue-element that does not cease is not the tongue-element, and the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition that do not cease are not the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) does not cease, it is not the body-element; if the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition do not cease, they are not the touch-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? The body element (*kāyadhātu*) and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because that which is not subject to cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the non-cessation of the body element (*kāyadhātu*) means it is not the body element; likewise, the non-cessation of the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition means they are not the contact element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the mind-element (*manodhātu*) does not cease, it is not the mind-element; if the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and the mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, do not cease, they are not the dharma-element, nor even all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”

Why is this? The mind-element (*manodhātu*) and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, from the phenomenon-element (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, they and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the non-extinguished dharma is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the non-extinguished mind-element (*manodhātu*) is not the mind-element; and the non-extinguished dharmas, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are not the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element does not cease, it is not the earth element; if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements do not cease, they are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”

Why is this so? The earth element and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because that which is the dharma of non-extinction is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the earth element that does not cease is not the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements that do not cease are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering were not subject to cessation, it would not be the noble truth of suffering; if the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path were not subject to cessation, they would not be the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.”
Why is this? Because the noble truth of suffering and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided.

Why is this? Because that which is not subject to cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, if the Noble Truth of Suffering is not subject to cessation, it is not the Noble Truth of Suffering; if the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are not subject to cessation, they are not the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance does not cease, it is not ignorance; if formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not cease, they are not formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Ignorance and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are non-dual and not divided into two with non-extinction.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, the non-extinction of ignorance is not ignorance, and the non-extinction of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is not volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
“World-Honored One!

If internal emptiness does not cease, it is not internal emptiness; if external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence do not cease, they are not external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

Why is this? Internal emptiness and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible; external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible.

Why is this? Because the unceasing dharma is not one, not two, not many, and not different; therefore, if internal emptiness does not cease, it is not internal emptiness, and if external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature does not cease, it is not external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

“Bhagavān, if the perfection of generosity were not subject to cessation, it would not be the perfection of generosity; if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were not subject to cessation, they would not be the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

Why is this? The perfection of generosity is non-dual with and indivisible from non-extinction; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-dual with and indivisible from non-extinction.

Why is this? Because that which is an unceasing phenomenon is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct. Therefore, if the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) were unceasing, it would not be the perfection of generosity; likewise, if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom (*śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitā*) were unceasing, they would not be the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas do not cease, they are not the four dhyānas; if the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not cease, they are not the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
Why is this? The four dhyānas and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if the four dhyānas do not undergo extinction, they are not the four dhyānas; if the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not undergo extinction, they are not the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

If the eight liberations were not subject to cessation, they would not be the eight liberations; if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities were not subject to cessation, they would not be the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

Why is this? The eight liberations and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if the eight liberations were not extinguished, they would not be the eight liberations; if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities were not extinguished, they would not be the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, or the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness are non-extinguished, they are not the four foundations of mindfulness; if the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-extinguished, they are not the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.”

Why is this? The four foundations of mindfulness and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible; the four right endeavors, and so forth, up to the eightfold noble path and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, if the four foundations of mindfulness do not extinguish, they are not the four foundations of mindfulness, and if the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path do not extinguish, they are not the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

If the gate of liberation of emptiness were not subject to cessation, it would not be the gate of liberation of emptiness; if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness were not subject to cessation, they would not be the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”

Why is this? The gate of liberation of emptiness and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if the gate of liberation of emptiness does not extinguish, it is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not extinguish, they are not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!
The five eyes are not extinguished, and thus they are not the five eyes; the six supernormal powers are not extinguished, and thus they are not the six supernormal powers. Why is this so?
The five eyes and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; the six supernormal powers and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is this?

Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, that which is the non-extinction of the five eyes is not the five eyes, and that which is the non-extinction of the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha were not subject to extinction, they would not be the ten powers of a Buddha; if the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha were not subject to extinction, they would not be the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

Why is this so? Because the ten powers of a Buddha and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two; likewise, the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided into two.

Why is this? Because the unextinguished dharma is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if the ten powers of a Buddha were unextinguished, they would not be the ten powers of a Buddha; if the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, were unextinguished, they would not be the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

If True Suchness were not indestructible, it would not be True Suchness; if the Dharma-realm, the Dharma-nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm were not indestructible, they would not be the Dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.”
Why is this? Suchness and non-extinction are non-dual and indivisible; from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, they are non-dual and indivisible with non-extinction.

Why is this? Because that which is an undying dharma is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, if *tathatā* (suchness) were not undying, it would not be *tathatā*; if the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), up to and including the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), were not undying, they would not be the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

“Bhagavān, if unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment were not subject to cessation, it would not be unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; if all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects were not subject to cessation, they would not be all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects.”

Why is this? Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided; omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual and not divided from non-extinction.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment were not non-extinguished, it would not be unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; if all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) were not non-extinguished, they would not be all-knowledge, knowledge of the aspects of the path, and knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

If the quality of non-forgetfulness were not subject to cessation, it would not be the quality of non-forgetfulness; if the nature of constant abiding in equanimity were not subject to cessation, it would not be the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.”
Why is this? The quality of being without forgetfulness and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided; the state of constant abiding in equanimity and non-extinction are non-dual and not divided.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor different. Therefore, the dharma of non-forgetfulness, being non-extinguished, is not the dharma of non-forgetfulness; and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, being non-extinguished, is not the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
“World-Honored One!
If all dharani-gates were not subject to extinction, they would not be all dharani-gates; if all samadhi-gates were not subject to extinction, they would not be all samadhi-gates.”
Why is this? All dharani-doors are non-dual and indivisible from non-extinction; all samadhi-doors are non-dual and indivisible from non-extinction.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-extinction is not one, not two, not many, and not different. Therefore, if all dhāraṇī-gates were not extinguished, they would not be all dhāraṇī-gates; if all samādhi-gates were not extinguished, they would not be all samādhi-gates.
“World-Honored One!
If form is non-dual, it is not form; if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
“World-Honored One!
If the eye-base is non-dual, it is not the eye-base; if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are non-dual, they are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form is non-dual, it is not the sphere of form; if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

The eye-element is non-dual, and thus it is not the eye-element; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, and thus they are not the form-element, nor even the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

The ear-element is non-dual, and thus it is not the ear-element; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual, and thus they are not the sound-element, up to and including all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

The nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is non-dual, and thus it is not the nose element. The fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition—these are non-dual, and thus they are not the fragrance element, nor even the sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

The tongue-element is non-dual, and thus it is not the tongue-element; the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-dual, and thus they are not the taste-element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

The body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is non-dual, and thus it is not the body-element. The touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—these are non-dual, and thus they are not the touch-element, nor even all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

If the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is non-dual, it is not the mind-element; if the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are non-dual, they are not the dharma-element, nor even the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”
“World-Honored One!

The earth element is non-dual, and thus it is not the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are non-dual, and thus they are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
“World-Honored One!

If the Noble Truth of Suffering is non-dual, it is not the Noble Truth of Suffering; if the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are non-dual, they are not the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance is non-dual, it is not ignorance; if volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are non-dual, they are not volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
“World-Honored One!

If internal emptiness is non-dual, it is not internal emptiness; if external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are non-dual, they are not external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Bhagavān! If the perfection of generosity is non-dual, it is not the perfection of generosity; if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-dual, they are not the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas are non-dual, they are not the four dhyānas; if the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are non-dual, they are not the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
“World-Honored One!

The non-duality of the eight liberations is not the eight liberations; the non-duality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.”
“World-Honored One!

The non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the four foundations of mindfulness; the non-duality of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is not the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.”
“World-Honored One!

The non-duality of the liberation door of emptiness is not the liberation door of emptiness; the non-duality of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is not the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“World-Honored One!
If the five eyes are non-dual, they are not the five eyes; if the six supernormal powers are non-dual, they are not the six supernormal powers.
World-Honored One!”

The ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, and thus they are not the ten powers of a Buddha; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, and thus they are not the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness (*tathatā*) were non-dual, it would not be true thusness. If the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), equality (*samatā*), the state of being free from birth (*niḥsaraṇatva*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) were non-dual, they would not be the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm.”
“World-Honored One!

Unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual, and thus it is not unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, and thus they are not omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”
“World-Honored One!

The quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual, and thus it is not the quality of non-forgetfulness; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual, and thus it is not the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”
“World-Honored One!
All dharani-doors are non-dual, and thus they are not all dharani-doors; all samadhi-doors are non-dual, and thus they are not all samadhi-doors.”
“World-Honored One!
The sense-base of form enters into the category of non-dual, non-false dharmas; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness enter into the category of non-dual, non-false dharmas.
World-Honored One!”

"The sense-base of the eye enters into the category of non-dual, non-delusive dharmas; the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind enter into the category of non-dual, non-delusive dharmas.
World-Honored One!"
"The sphere of form enters the category of non-dual, non-delusive dharmas; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena enter the category of non-dual, non-delusive dharmas.
World-Honored One!"

The eye-element enters into the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition enter into the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas.
“World-Honored One!

The ear-element enters into the category of non-dual and non-false dharmas; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition enter into the category of non-dual and non-false dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The nose element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The tongue element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The body-element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The mind-element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!
The earth element enters into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The noble truth of suffering enters into the category of non-dual and non-deceptive dharmas; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path enter into the category of non-dual and non-deceptive dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

Ignorance enters into the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair enter into the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

Internal emptiness enters the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unobtainable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence enter the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.”

“Bhagavān! The perfection of generosity enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous phenomena; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

The four dhyānas enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The eight liberations enter into the reckoning of the non-dual and non-erroneous Dharma; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities enter into the reckoning of the non-dual and non-erroneous Dharma.”
“World-Honored One!

The four foundations of mindfulness enter into the category of non-dual and non-deceptive dharmas; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path enter into the category of non-dual and non-deceptive dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

The gate of liberation of emptiness enters the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness enter the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!
The five eyes enter the category of the non-dual and non-erroneous Dharma; the six supernormal powers enter the category of the non-dual and non-erroneous Dharma.
World-Honored One!”

The ten powers of a Buddha enter into the category of the non-dual and non-erroneous dharma; the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha enter into the category of the non-dual and non-erroneous dharma.
“World-Honored One!

Suchness enters the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm enter the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!

Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment enters the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) enter the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.”
“World-Honored One!
The quality of non-forgetfulness enters the category of the non-dual and non-false dharma; the state of constant abiding in equanimity enters the category of the non-dual and non-false dharma.
World-Honored One!”
"All gateways of dhāraṇī enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous phenomena; all gateways of samādhi enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous phenomena.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"Regarding what was said—'when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and contemplates all phenomena'—what is meant by 'bodhisattva mahāsattva'?"
"What is meant by 'perfection of wisdom' (prajñāpāramitā)?
What is meant by 'contemplating all phenomena'?
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied to Śāriputra:
"Regarding what the Venerable One asked, 'What is meant by a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva?

Śāriputra, one is called a Bodhisattva because they seek great enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings and possess that enlightenment themselves; furthermore, they are called a Mahāsattva because they know the characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are and do not cling to them."
Śāriputra asked:
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva know the characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are, yet remain without attachment?
Subhūti replied:

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of form as they truly are and does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are and does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the sense base of the eye as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the sphere of form as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the eye-element as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the ear-element as they truly are and does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition as they truly are, and does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the nose element as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as their condition, as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the tongue element as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the body-element (kāyadhātu) as they truly are and does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the contact-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), body-contact (kāyasparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition, as they truly are, and does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the mental element (*manodhātu*) as they truly are and does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the phenomena element (*dharmadhātu*), the mental-consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as their condition, as they truly are and does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the earth element as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the noble truth of suffering as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of ignorance as they truly are and does not cling to them; likewise, he knows the characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as they truly are, and does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristic of internal emptiness as it truly is, yet does not cling to it; they know the characteristics of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as they truly are, yet do not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the perfection of generosity as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the four dhyānas as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the eight liberations as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows, as it truly is, the characteristics of the liberation door of emptiness without clinging to them; he knows, as they truly are, the characteristics of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness without clinging to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the five eyes as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the six supernormal powers as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristic of suchness as it truly is, yet does not cling to it; he knows the characteristics of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows the characteristics of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment as they truly are, yet does not cling to them; he knows the characteristics of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as they truly are, yet does not cling to them.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows, as it truly is, the characteristic of the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) without clinging to it; he knows, as it truly is, the characteristic of the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) without clinging to it.”

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva knows, as they truly are, the characteristics of all dhāraṇī-doors without clinging to them; he knows, as they truly are, the characteristics of all samādhi-doors without clinging to them.”
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"What is called the characteristic of all phenomena?
Subhūti replied:

"If one comes to know all phenomena through such modes of activity (*saṃskāra*), characteristics (*lakṣaṇa*), and signs (*nimitta*)—that this is form, this is sound, this is odor, this is taste, this is tangible object, this is phenomenon; that this is internal, this is external; that this is with outflows (*sāsrava*), this is without outflows (*anāsrava*); that this is conditioned (*saṃskṛta*), this is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*)—these are called the characteristics of all phenomena."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti replied again to Śāriputra:
"As the Venerable has asked, 'What is called the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?'"
"Śāriputra, it is because there is a supreme and wondrous wisdom that is distantly separated from all things that it is called Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra said:
"In regard to what phenomena is this 'detachment' attained?
Subhūti replied:

"This detachment is attained in regard to all afflictions and views; this detachment is attained in regard to all six destinies and four modes of birth; this detachment is attained in regard to all aggregates, elements, and sense bases. Therefore, it is called the *prajñāpāramitā*."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Because there is a supreme and wondrous wisdom that reaches far, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra said:
"In regard to what phenomena does this reach far?
Subhūti replied, "Śāriputra!"

Because it reaches the ultimate limit regarding the true nature of form, and reaches the ultimate limit regarding the true nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far into the true nature of the eye-base, and reaches far into the true nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, it is called the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the ultimate limit of the true nature of the sphere of form, and reaches the ultimate limit of the true nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far into the true nature of the eye-element, and reaches far into the true nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, it is therefore called the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the ultimate reality of the sphere of the ear, and reaches the ultimate reality of the sphere of sounds, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition, it is therefore called the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far into the true nature of the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), and because it reaches far into the true nature of the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, it is therefore called the Perfection of Wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far into the true nature of the tongue element, and reaches far into the true nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, it is therefore called the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the ultimate limit regarding the true nature of the body element (*kāyadhātu*), and because it reaches the ultimate limit regarding the true nature of the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, it is called the Perfection of Wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far into the true nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), and because it reaches far into the true nature of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and the feeling produced with mind-contact as its condition, it is called the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far into the true nature of the earth element, and reaches far into the true nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the ultimate realization of the true nature of the noble truth of suffering, and because it reaches the ultimate realization of the true nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the ultimate limit regarding the true nature of ignorance, and reaches the ultimate limit regarding the true nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, it is therefore called the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

“Śāriputra! This has reached the ultimate limit of the true nature of internal emptiness; it has reached the ultimate limit of the true nature of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Therefore, it is called the *prajñāpāramitā*.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the perfection of giving, and because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, it is called the ‘perfection of wisdom.’”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest extent of the true nature of the four dhyānas, and reaches the farthest extent of the true nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, it is called the Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the eight liberations, and because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! This has reached the farthest limit of the true nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; it has reached the farthest limit of the true nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path. Therefore, it is called the Perfection of Wisdom.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, it is called the *prajñāpāramitā*.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest extent regarding the true nature of the five eyes, and reaches the farthest extent regarding the true nature of the six supernormal powers, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! This [perfection] reaches far into the true nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; it reaches far into the true nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Therefore, it is called the Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! This has reached the farthest limit of the true nature of suchness; it has reached the farthest limit of the true nature of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. Therefore, it is called Prajñāpāramitā.”

“Śāriputra! Because it reaches far toward the true nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and because it reaches far toward the true nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), it is called ‘perfection of wisdom’ (*prajñāpāramitā*).”

"Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of the state of constant equanimity, it is called the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."
“Śāriputra! Because it reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of all dhāraṇī-doors and reaches the farthest limit of the true nature of all samādhi-doors, it is called the Prajñāpāramitā.”
"Śāriputra! This is called the Prajñāpāramitā.

One contemplates that suchness is neither characterized by existence nor characterized by non-existence; one contemplates that the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are neither characterized by existence nor characterized by non-existence.

One contemplates that suchness is neither characterized by aspiration nor characterized by non-aspiration; one contemplates that the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are neither characterized by aspiration nor characterized by non-aspiration.

One contemplates that suchness is neither quiescent nor non-quiescent; one contemplates that the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are neither quiescent nor non-quiescent.

One contemplates that suchness is neither distant nor not distant; one contemplates that the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are neither distant nor not distant.
Śāriputra! This is called contemplating all phenomena. Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment as neither permanent nor impermanent; they contemplate all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as neither permanent nor impermanent.

They contemplate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment as neither pleasant nor painful; they contemplate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects as neither pleasant nor painful.

They contemplate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment as neither self nor non-self; they contemplate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects as neither self nor non-self.

One contemplates that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither pure nor impure; one contemplates that all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are neither pure nor impure.

One contemplates that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither empty nor non-empty; one contemplates that all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are neither empty nor non-empty.

One contemplates that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither with signs (*sanimitta*) nor signless (*animitta*); one contemplates that all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are neither with signs nor signless.

One contemplates that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither with aspiration nor without aspiration; one contemplates that all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are neither with aspiration nor without aspiration.

One contemplates that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither quiescent nor non-quiescent; one contemplates that all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects are neither quiescent nor non-quiescent.

One contemplates that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is neither detached nor non-detached; one contemplates that all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects are neither detached nor non-detached.
Śāriputra! This is called contemplating all phenomena. Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate the quality of non-forgetfulness as neither permanent nor impermanent, and they contemplate the nature of constant equanimity as neither permanent nor impermanent;
they contemplate the quality of non-forgetfulness as neither pleasant nor painful, and they contemplate the nature of constant equanimity as neither pleasant nor painful;
they contemplate the quality of non-forgetfulness as neither self nor non-self, and they contemplate the nature of constant equanimity as neither self nor non-self.
One contemplates that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither pure nor impure; one contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is neither pure nor impure.
One contemplates that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither empty nor non-empty; one contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is neither empty nor non-empty.
One contemplates that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither with signs nor signless; one contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is neither with signs nor signless.

One contemplates that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither with aspiration nor without aspiration; one contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is neither with aspiration nor without aspiration.
One contemplates that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither tranquil nor untranquil; one contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is neither tranquil nor untranquil.
One contemplates that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither detached nor undetached; one contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is neither detached nor undetached.
Śāriputra! This is called contemplating all phenomena. Śāriputra!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate all dhāraṇī-doors as neither permanent nor impermanent; they contemplate all samādhi-doors as neither permanent nor impermanent.
They contemplate all dhāraṇī-doors as neither pleasant nor painful; they contemplate all samādhi-doors as neither pleasant nor painful.
They contemplate all dhāraṇī-doors as neither self nor non-self; they contemplate all samādhi-doors as neither self nor non-self.
One contemplates all dharani-gates as neither pure nor impure; one contemplates all samadhi-gates as neither pure nor impure.
One contemplates all dharani-gates as neither empty nor non-empty; one contemplates all samadhi-gates as neither empty nor non-empty.
One contemplates all dharani-gates as neither having marks nor being markless; one contemplates all samadhi-gates as neither having marks nor being markless.
One contemplates all dharanī-gates as neither having vows nor being without vows; one contemplates all samādhi-gates as neither having vows nor being without vows.
One contemplates all dharanī-gates as neither quiescent nor non-quiescent; one contemplates all samādhi-gates as neither quiescent nor non-quiescent.
One contemplates all dharanī-gates as neither detached nor non-detached; one contemplates all samādhi-gates as neither detached nor non-detached.
Śāriputra! This is called contemplating all phenomena. Śāriputra!
"When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should contemplate all phenomena in this manner.
*The Great Perfection of Wisdom Sūtra*, Scroll 72;
*The Great Perfection of Wisdom Sūtra*, Scroll 73.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One, Chapter Nineteen on the Practice of Contemplation, Section Four.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed Subhūti, saying:
"For what reason do you say that the non-arising of form and so forth is not form and so forth?
Subhūti replied, "Śāriputra!"
Form is empty of the nature of form; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor form.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: when form is unarisen, it is not form;
when feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unarisen, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“Śāriputra! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no eye-base.

The ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are empty of the nature of the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, or mind-base.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
when the eye-base does not arise, it is not the eye-base; when the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases do not arise, they are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.
“Śāriputra! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no sphere of form.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: when the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) does not arise, it is not the sphere of form;
when the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) do not arise, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
“Śāriputra! The eye-element is empty of the nature of the eye-element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no eye-element.

The form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the eye-element does not arise, it is not the eye-element; if the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, do not arise, they are not the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The ear element is empty of the nature of the ear element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no ear element.

The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—from the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the ear-element (*śrotradhātu*) does not arise, it is not the ear-element;

if the sound-element (*śabdadhātu*) and even the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition (*śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayaja-vedanā*) do not arise, they are not the sound-element and so forth, up to the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no nose element.

The odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—from the odor element up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no odor element, up to and including the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

when the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) does not arise, it is not the nose element; when the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition do not arise, they are not the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no tongue element.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—from the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no taste element, up to and including no feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) does not arise, it is not the tongue-element; if the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*) and even the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition do not arise, they are not the taste-element and even the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The body element is empty of the nature of the body element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no body element.

The tangibility element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are empty of the nature of the tangibility element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no tangibility element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) does not arise, it is not the body-element; if the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition do not arise, they are not the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no mind-element.

The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—up to the dharma-element and the nature of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no dharma-element, up to no feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the mind-element (*manodhātu*) does not arise, it is not the mind-element;

if the dharma-element and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition do not arise, they are not the dharma-element and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no earth element.

The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the earth element is unarisen, it is not the earth element; if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unarisen, they are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
“Śāriputra! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no noble truth of suffering.

The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the noble truth of suffering does not arise, it is not the noble truth of suffering; if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path do not arise, they are not the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
“Śāriputra! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor ignorance.

Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the nature of old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor formations, up to and including old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: when ignorance does not arise, it is not "ignorance";

when formations, and so on, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair do not arise, they are not "formations," and so on, up to "old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair."
“Śāriputra! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness; within this nature of emptiness, there is neither arising nor internal emptiness.

External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—within this nature of emptiness, there is neither arising nor external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if internal emptiness does not arise, it is not internal emptiness;

if external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, do not arise, they are not external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature.
“Śāriputra! The perfection of generosity is empty of the nature of the perfection of generosity; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the perfection of generosity is non-arising, it is not the perfection of generosity; if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-arising, they are not the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“Śāriputra! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no four dhyānas.

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no four immeasurables or four formless absorptions.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

when the four dhyānas do not arise, they are not the four dhyānas; when the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not arise, they are not the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
“Śāriputra! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no eight liberations.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no eight bases of mastery, no nine successive attainments, and no ten totalities.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the eight liberations are non-arising, they are not the eight liberations; if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-arising, they are not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

“Śāriputra! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the four foundations of mindfulness do not arise, they are not the four foundations of mindfulness; if the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path, do not arise, they are not the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path.

"Śāriputra! The gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is neither arising nor the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is neither arising nor the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the gate of liberation of emptiness does not arise, it is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not arise, they are not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Śāriputra! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no five eyes.
The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising and no six supernormal powers.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the non-arising of the five eyes is not the five eyes; the non-arising of the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers.
“Śāriputra! The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—are empty of the nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the ten powers of a Buddha, if they do not arise, are not the ten powers of a Buddha; the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, if they do not arise, are not the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Śāriputra! True suchness (tathatā) is empty of the nature of true suchness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor true suchness.

The dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), sameness (samatā), the nature of freedom from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm—up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if true thusness (*tathatā*) were not produced, it would not be true thusness;
if the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), up to and including the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), were not produced, they would not be the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

“Śāriputra! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising, nor is there unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
