All-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; within this emptiness of nature, there is no arising, nor is there all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment were non-arising, it would not be unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; if all-knowledge, knowledge of the aspects of the path, and knowledge of all aspects were non-arising, they would not be all-knowledge, knowledge of the aspects of the path, and knowledge of all aspects.
“Śāriputra! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor the quality of non-forgetfulness.

The quality of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither arising nor the quality of constant abiding in equanimity.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
if the quality of non-forgetfulness does not arise, it is not the quality of non-forgetfulness; if the state of constant equanimity does not arise, it is not the state of constant equanimity.
“Śāriputra! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is no arising and no all dhāraṇī-doors.
All samādhi-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-doors; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is no arising and no all samādhi-doors.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
if all dhāraṇī-doors are non-arising, they are not all dhāraṇī-doors; if all samādhi-doors are non-arising, they are not all samādhi-doors.
Then, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason do you say that the non-extinction of form and so forth is not form and so forth?
Subhūti replied:
“Śāriputra! Form is empty of the nature of form; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor form.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: when form does not cease, it is not form;
when feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not cease, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“Śāriputra! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor an eye-base.

The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty of the nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor an ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
if the eye-base does not cease, it is not the eye-base; if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases do not cease, they are not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.
“Śāriputra! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the sphere of form.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the sphere of form is not extinguished, it is not the sphere of form;
if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not extinguished, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
“Śāriputra! The eye-element is empty of the nature of the eye-element; in this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor an eye-element.

The form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; in this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the eye-element is not extinguished, it is not the eye-element;

and if the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are not extinguished, they are not the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The ear element is empty of the nature of the ear element; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the ear element.

The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—from the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the ear-element does not cease, it is not the ear-element; and if the sound-element, up to and including the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, do not cease, they are not the sound-element, up to and including the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the nose element.

The odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition—from the odor element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the odor element, up to and including all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the nose-element does not cease, it is not the nose-element; and if the fragrance-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, do not cease, they are not the fragrance-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor a tongue element.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—from the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the taste element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the tongue element does not cease, it is not the tongue element; and if the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, do not cease, they are not the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The body element (*kāyadhātu*) is empty of the nature of the body element; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor a body element.

The object-contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—from the object-contact element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the object-contact element, up to and including all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the body element (*kāyadhātu*) does not cease, it is not the body element; if the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition do not cease, they are not the contact element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“Śāriputra! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor a mind-element.

The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—the dharma-element up to the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—are empty of their own nature; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor a dharma-element, up to and including the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the mind-element (*manodhātu*) does not cease, it is not the mind-element;

and if the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, do not cease, they are not the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.
“Śāriputra! The earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the earth element.

The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the earth element does not cease, and thus it is not the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements do not cease, and thus they are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
“Śāriputra! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the noble truth of suffering.

The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the noble truth of suffering does not cease, it is not the noble truth of suffering; if the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path do not cease, they are not the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
“Śāriputra! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor ignorance.

Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the nature of old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor formations, up to and including old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if ignorance does not cease, it is not ignorance;

if formations, and so forth, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair do not cease, they are not formations, and so forth, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
“Śāriputra! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness; within this nature of emptiness, there is neither cessation nor internal emptiness.

External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, infinite emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are each empty of their own nature. Within this nature of emptiness, there is neither cessation nor external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if internal emptiness were not subject to cessation, it would not be internal emptiness;

if external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, were not subject to cessation, they would not be external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
“Śāriputra! The perfection of generosity is empty of the nature of the perfection of generosity; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the perfection of generosity were not indestructible, it would not be the perfection of generosity; if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were not indestructible, they would not be the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“Śāriputra! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the four dhyānas.

The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the four dhyānas are not extinguished, they are not the four dhyānas; if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not extinguished, they are not the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
“Śāriputra! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the eight liberations.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the eight liberations are not extinguished, they are not the eight liberations; if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are not extinguished, they are not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

“Śāriputra! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the four foundations of mindfulness are not extinguished, they are not the four foundations of mindfulness; if the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are not extinguished, they are not the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path.

“Śāriputra! The gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is neither cessation nor the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is neither cessation nor the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the gate of liberation of emptiness is not extinguished, it is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are not extinguished, they are not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Śāriputra! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the five eyes.
The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the six supernormal powers.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
that which is not subject to cessation is not the five eyes; that which is not subject to cessation is not the six supernormal powers.
“Śāriputra! The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities—are empty of the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the ten powers of a Buddha were not subject to extinction, they would not be the ten powers of a Buddha; if the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, were not subject to extinction, they would not be the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Śāriputra! True thusness (tathatā) is empty of the nature of true thusness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor true thusness.

The realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the state of equality (samatā), the nature of freedom from birth (anupapatti-dharmatā), the fixed nature of phenomena (dharma-niyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharma-sthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu)—from the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the inconceivable realm; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the realm of phenomena, up to and including the inconceivable realm.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if suchness were not subject to cessation, it would not be suchness;
if the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, were not subject to cessation, they would not be the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

“Śāriputra! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment; within this emptiness of nature, there is no cessation and no unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.

All-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; within this emptiness of nature, there is no cessation and no all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment were not subject to cessation, it would not be unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; if omniscience, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects were not subject to cessation, they would not be omniscience, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“Śāriputra! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the quality of non-forgetfulness.

The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity; within this emptiness of nature, there is neither cessation nor the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the quality of non-forgetfulness were not extinguished, it would not be the quality of non-forgetfulness; if the state of constant abiding in equanimity were not extinguished, it would not be the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
“Śāriputra! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is no cessation and no all dhāraṇī-doors.
All samādhi-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-doors; within this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is no cessation and no all samādhi-doors.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
if all dharanī-gates were not subject to cessation, they would not be all dharanī-gates; if all samādhi-gates were not subject to cessation, they would not be all samādhi-gates.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason do you say that the non-duality of form and so forth is not form and so forth?
Subhūti replied:

“Śāriputra! Whether it be form or non-duality, whether it be feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness or non-duality—all such things as these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, which is to say: the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: form is not form when it is non-dual;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness when they are non-dual.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the eye-base as non-dual, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as non-dual—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the sense-base of the eye is non-dual, and thus it is not the sense-base of the eye; the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, and thus they are not the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) as non-dual, or the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) as non-dual—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor formless; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the sphere of form is non-dual, it is not the sphere of form;
if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual, they are not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the eye-element, or the non-duality [of it], or the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—if these are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: the eye-element is non-dual, and thus it is not the eye-element;

from the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they are non-dual, and thus they are not the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! If the ear element is non-dual, and if the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual—if all such things are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, and neither resistant nor non-resistant, they are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the ear-element is non-dual, and thus it is not the ear-element; the sound-element, and even the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-dual, and thus they are not the sound-element, nor the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), or whether it be non-dual; whether it be the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition—if these are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, and neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being signless (*animitta*).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is non-dual, and thus it is not the nose element; the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) and even all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual, and thus they are not the odor element and even all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) as non-dual, or whether it be the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition that are non-dual—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither material nor immaterial; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the tongue-element is non-dual, and thus it is not the tongue-element; the taste-element, and even the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, and thus they are not the taste-element, nor the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the body element (*kāyadhātu*) as non-dual, or the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition—if these are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither material nor immaterial; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is non-dual, and thus it is not the body-element; the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are non-dual, and thus they are not the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the mind-element (*manodhātu*), or the non-duality [of it]; whether it be the phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—if these are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, and neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is non-dual, it is not the mind-element;

if the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are non-dual, they are not the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the earth element or non-duality, or whether it be the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements or non-duality—all such things as these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the earth element is non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the earth element; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the noble truth of suffering as non-dual, or the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as non-dual—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither material nor immaterial; they are neither visible nor invisible; they are neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the Noble Truth of Suffering is non-dual, and thus it is not the Noble Truth of Suffering; the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are non-dual, and thus they are not the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.
“Śāriputra! Whether it be ignorance or non-duality;

whether it be volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—or their non-duality—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: non-duality with ignorance is not ignorance;

and from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, non-duality with these is not volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be internal emptiness or non-duality; whether it be external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, or the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence—if these are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: inner emptiness is non-dual, and thus it is not inner emptiness;

outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, and thus they are not outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the perfection of generosity as non-dual, or the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as non-dual—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

if the perfection of generosity were not non-dual, it would not be the perfection of generosity; if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were not non-dual, they would not be the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the four dhyānas or non-duality; whether it be the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, or non-duality—all such things as these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single mark, namely, the markless.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the four dhyānas are not two, and thus they are not the four dhyānas; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are not two, and thus they are not the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the eight liberations or non-duality; whether it be the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities or non-duality—all such things as these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, which is to say: the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the eight liberations being non-dual is not the eight liberations; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities being non-dual are not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness as non-dual, or the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path as non-dual—all these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither material nor immaterial; they are neither visible nor invisible; they are neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, and thus they are not the four foundations of mindfulness; the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are non-dual, and thus they are not the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the gate of liberation of emptiness or non-duality, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness or non-duality—all such things are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the five eyes or non-duality, whether it be the six supernormal powers or non-duality—all such things as these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single mark, namely, the markless.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the five eyes are non-dual, and thus they are not five eyes; the six supernormal powers are non-dual, and thus they are not six supernormal powers.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha or non-duality; whether it be the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—if they are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the ten powers of a Buddha are not the ten powers of a Buddha if they are non-dual; the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are not the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, if they are non-dual.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be suchness as non-dual, or whether it be the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm—if these are non-dual, then all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: if suchness were non-dual, it would not be suchness;
if the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, were non-dual, they would not be the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

“Śāriputra! If unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual, and if omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-dual—then all such things as these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics (*animitta*).”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the non-duality of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is not itself unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; the non-duality of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is not itself all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the knowledge of all aspects.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or non-duality, whether it be the state of constant abiding in equanimity or non-duality—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the state of non-forgetfulness is non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the state of non-forgetfulness; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual, and that which is non-dual is not the state of constant abiding in equanimity.

“Śāriputra! Whether it be all the gateways of dhāraṇī or their non-duality, whether it be all the gateways of samādhi or their non-duality—all such things are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
all dharanī-doors are non-dual, and thus they are not "all dharanī-doors"; all samādhi-doors are non-dual, and thus they are not "all samādhi-doors."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 73. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 74.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
In the fifth section of the nineteenth chapter, "The Analysis of Practice" (*Caryā-vibhaṅga*),
at that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"For what reason do you say that form and the other aggregates enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas?"
Subhūti replied:

"Śāriputra, form is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from form. Form itself is non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing itself is form."

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
form enters into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The eye-base is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the eye-base. The eye-base is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the eye-base.

The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases. The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the sense base of the eye enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind likewise enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The sphere of form is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the sphere of form. The sphere of form is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the sphere of form.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena. The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the sphere of form enters into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena likewise enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The eye-element is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the eye-element. The eye-element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the eye-element.

The form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. The form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the eye element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the form element, and so on up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The ear-element is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the ear-element. The ear-element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the ear-element.

The sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. The sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the ear element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the sound element, and even all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the nose element. The nose element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the nose element.

The odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the odor element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. The odor element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the odor element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the nose element enters into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas; and from the odor element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, they enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The tongue element is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the tongue element. The tongue element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the tongue element.

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition. The taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that the tongue element enters into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas;
and from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, they enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The body element (*kāyadhātu*) is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the body element. The body element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the body element.

The touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the touch element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. The touch element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the touch element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the body element enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the contact element, and even all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The mind-element (*manodhātu*) is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the mind-element. The mind-element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the mind-element.

The dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition. The dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the mind-element (manodhātu) enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; and from the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, they too enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The earth element is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the earth element. The earth element is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the earth element.

The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements. The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
the earth element enters into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements enter into the category of non-dual, non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The noble truth of suffering is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the noble truth of suffering. The noble truth of suffering is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the noble truth of suffering.

The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the Noble Truth of Suffering enters into the category of non-dual, non-deceptive dharmas; the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path enter into the category of non-dual, non-deceptive dharmas.

“Śāriputra! Ignorance is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from ignorance; ignorance itself is non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing itself is ignorance.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair themselves are non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing itself is volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: ignorance enters into the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas;
from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, they all enter into the category of non-dual and non-delusive dharmas.

“Śāriputra! Internal emptiness is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from internal emptiness. Internal emptiness is itself non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves internal emptiness.”

Outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Śāriputra! For this reason,
I say that internal emptiness enters the category of non-dual and non-false dharmas,
and external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, enters the category of non-dual and non-false dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The perfection of generosity is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the perfection of generosity. The perfection of generosity is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that the perfection of generosity enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas;
and the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The four dhyānas are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the four dhyānas. The four dhyānas are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the four dhyānas.

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions. The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that the four dhyānas enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas;
the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The eight liberations are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the eight liberations. The eight liberations are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the eight liberations.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities. The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the eight liberations enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities also enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The four foundations of mindfulness are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path. The four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that the four foundations of mindfulness enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas;
likewise, the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The gate of liberation of emptiness is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the gate of liberation of emptiness. The gate of liberation of emptiness is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the liberation door of emptiness enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The five eyes are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the five eyes. The five eyes are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the five eyes.

The six supernormal powers are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the six supernormal powers. The six supernormal powers are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the six supernormal powers.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that the five eyes enter into the category of non-dual,
non-false dharmas, and the six supernormal powers enter into the category of non-dual, non-false dharmas.

“Śāriputra! The ten powers of a Buddha are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the ten powers of a Buddha. The ten powers of a Buddha are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the ten powers of a Buddha enter into the category of non-dual and non-deceptive dharmas; the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, enter into the category of non-dual and non-deceptive dharmas.

“Śāriputra! True suchness (*tathatā*) is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from true suchness. True suchness is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself true suchness.

The realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the state of equality (*samatā*), the state of being free from birth (*anupapatti*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm. The realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say: True Suchness (tathatā) enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas;
from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), they all enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.

All-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects. All-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing is itself all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous phenomena;
omniscience, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects enter into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous phenomena.

“Śāriputra! The quality of non-forgetfulness is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the quality of non-forgetfulness. The quality of non-forgetfulness is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the quality of non-forgetfulness.

The nature of abiding eternally in equanimity is not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from the nature of abiding eternally in equanimity. The nature of abiding eternally in equanimity is itself non-arising and non-ceasing, and non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves the nature of abiding eternally in equanimity.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:

the quality of non-forgetfulness enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas; the state of constant abiding in equanimity enters into the category of non-dual and non-erroneous dharmas.

“Śāriputra! All dhāraṇī gates are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from all dhāraṇī gates. All dhāraṇī gates are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves all dhāraṇī gates.

All samādhi gates are not different from non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are not different from all samādhi gates. All samādhi gates are themselves non-arising and non-ceasing; non-arising and non-ceasing are themselves all samādhi gates.”
Śāriputra! For this reason, I say:
all doors of dhāraṇī enter into the category of non-dual, non-deceptive phenomena; all doors of samādhi enter into the category of non-dual, non-deceptive phenomena.
Chapter 20: On Non-arising, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the self is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;

they see that sentient beings, life-principles, born beings, nourishers, persons, individuals, mind-born ones, youths, agents, experiencers, knowers, and seers are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that form is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;
they see that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the sense base of the eye is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the sphere of form is unborn because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are unborn because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the eye-element is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;

they see that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the ear-element is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;

they see that the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*) and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;

they see that the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;

they see that the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;

they see that the phenomenon-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that the earth element is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see the Noble Truth of Suffering as non-arising because it is ultimately pure;
they see the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that ignorance is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;

they see that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that internal emptiness is unborn because it is ultimately pure;

they see that external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are unborn, because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the perfection of giving is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that the four dhyānas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
they see that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see the eight liberations as non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
they see the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities as non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the four foundations of mindfulness are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;

they see that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the gate of liberation of emptiness is unborn, because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are unborn, because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the five eyes are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
they see that the six supernormal powers are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the ten powers of a Buddha are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;

they see that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is unarisen because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the quality of non-forgetfulness is unborn because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the nature of constant equanimity is unborn because it is ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that all dharani-doors are unarisen because they are ultimately pure;
they see that all samādhi-doors are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*) are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
they see that the phenomena of ordinary beings are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the stream-enterer is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the dharmas of the stream-enterer are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the once-returner is non-arising because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the phenomena of the once-returner are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the non-returner is unborn because it is ultimately pure;
they see that the phenomenon of the non-returner is unborn because it is ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that Arhats are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
they see that the dharmas of Arhats are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that pratyekabuddhas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure;
they see that the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas are non-arising because they are ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all dharmas, they see that the bodhisattva is unborn because he is ultimately pure;
they see that the dharma of the bodhisattva is unborn because it is ultimately pure.”
“World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and contemplate all phenomena, they see that the Tathāgata is unarisen because he is ultimately pure;
they see that the dharmas of the Tathāgata are unarisen because they are ultimately pure.”
Then, Śāriputra said to Subhūti:

"As I understand the meaning of what you have said, noble sir, the self and sentient beings are non-arisen; form, sensation, and the other aggregates are non-arisen; and even the Tathāgata and the dharmas of a Tathāgata are non-arisen."

If this were so, there would be no distinction in the rebirths within the six destinies; one would not attain the fruit of a stream-enterer as a stream-enterer, nor the fruit of a once-returner as a once-returner, nor the fruit of a non-returner as a non-returner, nor the fruit of arhatship as an arhat. One would not attain pratyekabuddha-enlightenment as a solitary buddha, nor would bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain the knowledge of all aspects, nor would they attain the five types of enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If all phenomena were definitively non-arising, for what reason would a stream-enterer cultivate the path to abandon the three fetters for the sake of the fruit of stream-entry?"
For what reason does a once-returner, for the sake of the fruit of once-returning, cultivate the path that attenuates greed, hatred, and delusion?
