One does not discriminate between tranquility and non-tranquility with respect to internal emptiness, nor does one discriminate internal emptiness as being tranquil or non-tranquil;

one does not discriminate between tranquility and non-tranquility with respect to external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, nor does one discriminate external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities as being tranquil or non-tranquil.

One does not differentiate between "separation" and "non-separation" by means of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), nor does one differentiate between "internal emptiness" and "separation" or "non-separation.

One does not differentiate between "separation" and "non-separation" by means of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), nor does one differentiate between "external emptiness" up to the "emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature" and "separation" or "non-separation."
“Such persons as these never, by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, differentiate true thusness (*tathatā*); nor do they, by means of true thusness, differentiate emptiness or non-emptiness.

They do not, by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, differentiate the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), or the inconceivable realm; nor do they, by means of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, differentiate emptiness or non-emptiness.”
One does not discriminate between the characterized and the uncharacterized by means of suchness, nor does one discriminate between the characterized and the uncharacterized by means of suchness;

one does not discriminate between the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm by means of the characterized and the uncharacterized, nor does one discriminate between the characterized and the uncharacterized by means of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
One does not discriminate between the presence or absence of vows with respect to suchness, nor does one discriminate between suchness and the presence or absence of vows;

one does not discriminate between the presence or absence of vows with respect to the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, nor does one discriminate between the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm and the presence or absence of vows.
One does not discriminate between arising and non-arising with respect to *tathatā*, nor does one discriminate between *tathatā* and arising or non-arising;

one does not discriminate between arising and non-arising with respect to the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), nor does one discriminate between the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm and arising or non-arising.
One does not discriminate true suchness by means of cessation or non-cessation, nor does one discriminate cessation or non-cessation by means of true suchness;

one does not discriminate the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm by means of cessation or non-cessation, nor does one discriminate cessation or non-cessation by means of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
One does not discriminate true thusness by means of tranquility or non-tranquility, nor does one discriminate tranquility or non-tranquility by means of true thusness;

one does not discriminate the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm by means of tranquility or non-tranquility, nor does one discriminate tranquility or non-tranquility by means of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
One does not differentiate true suchness by means of remoteness or non-remoteness, nor does one differentiate remoteness or non-remoteness by means of true suchness;

one does not differentiate the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm by means of remoteness or non-remoteness, nor does one differentiate remoteness or non-remoteness by means of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

Part One, Chapter Twenty-Four, Section Two:

They do not distinguish the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
One does not differentiate the perfection of generosity by means of signs or signlessness, nor does one differentiate the perfection of generosity by means of signs or signlessness;

one does not differentiate the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom by means of signs or signlessness, nor does one differentiate the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom by means of signs or signlessness.

one does not discriminate between the perishing and the non-perishing regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor does one discriminate between the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom and the perishing or the non-perishing.

one does not discriminate between unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of wishing or wishlessness, nor does one discriminate between wishing and wishlessness by means of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

one does not differentiate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of arising or non-arising, nor does one differentiate arising or non-arising by means of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

one does not discriminate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of cessation or non-cessation, nor does one discriminate cessation or non-cessation by means of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

one does not differentiate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of remoteness or non-remoteness, nor does one differentiate remoteness or non-remoteness by means of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

one does not discriminate between the ground of Stainless, the ground of Luminous Radiance, up to the ground of Good Intelligence and the ground of Dharma Cloud, and aspiration or non-aspiration, nor does one discriminate between the ground of Stainless, the ground of Luminous Radiance, up to the ground of Good Intelligence and the ground of Dharma Cloud, and aspiration or non-aspiration.
One does not discriminate the Ground of Great Joy by means of arising or non-arising, nor does one discriminate arising or non-arising by means of the Ground of Great Joy;

one does not discriminate the Ground of Stainless, the Ground of Radiant Purity, up to the Ground of Excellent Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma Clouds by means of arising or non-arising, nor does one discriminate arising or non-arising by means of the Ground of Stainless, the Ground of Radiant Purity, up to the Ground of Excellent Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma Clouds.

one does not discriminate between extinction and non-extinction with respect to the Ground of Freedom from Defilement (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Refulgence (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), up to the Ground of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*) and the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), nor does one discriminate between the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Refulgence, up to the Ground of Good Intelligence and the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud, and extinction or non-extinction.

one does not discriminate between the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), up to the Ground of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*) and the Ground of Dharma Clouds (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) on the one hand, and tranquility or non-tranquility on the other, nor does one discriminate between the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, up to the Ground of Excellent Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma Clouds, and tranquility or non-tranquility.

one does not discriminate between remoteness and non-remoteness with respect to the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), up to the Ground of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*) and the Ground of Dharma Clouds (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), nor does one discriminate the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, up to the Ground of Good Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma Clouds as being remote or non-remote.

Part One, Chapter Twenty-Four on Receiving the Teaching, Section Three:

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiance, up to the Ground of Excellent Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma-Clouds as having marks or being markless, nor does one discriminate the dharmas of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiance, up to the Ground of Excellent Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma-Clouds as having marks or being markless.

One does not differentiate the dharmas of the Stage of Great Joy by means of "with vow" or "without vow," nor does one differentiate "with vow" or "without vow" by means of the dharmas of the Stage of Great Joy;

one does not differentiate the dharmas of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, the Stage of Radiance, up to the Stage of Excellent Intelligence and the Stage of Dharma-Cloud by means of "with vow" or "without vow," nor does one differentiate "with vow" or "without vow" by means of the dharmas of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, the Stage of Radiance, up to the Stage of Excellent Intelligence and the Stage of Dharma-Cloud.

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the Stage of Extreme Joy as arising or non-arising, nor does one discriminate between the dharmas of the Stage of Extreme Joy as arising or non-arising;

one does not discriminate between the dharmas of the Stainless Stage, the Luminous Stage, up to the Stage of Good Intelligence and the Stage of Dharma Clouds as arising or non-arising, nor does one discriminate between the dharmas of the Stainless Stage, the Luminous Stage, up to the Stage of Good Intelligence and the Stage of Dharma Clouds as arising or non-arising.

One does not discriminate between extinction and non-extinction regarding the dharmas of the Ground of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), nor does one discriminate between the dharmas of the Ground of Extreme Joy and extinction or non-extinction;

one does not discriminate between extinction and non-extinction regarding the dharmas of the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), up to the Ground of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*) and the Ground of Dharma-Clouds (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), nor does one discriminate between the dharmas of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, up to the Ground of Good Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma-Clouds, and extinction or non-extinction.

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the Ground of Great Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) as being tranquil or non-tranquil, nor does one discriminate the dharmas of the Ground of Great Joy as being tranquil or non-tranquil.

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), up to the Ground of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*) and the Ground of Dharma Clouds (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) as being tranquil or non-tranquil, nor does one discriminate the dharmas of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, up to the Ground of Good Intelligence and the Ground of Dharma Clouds as being tranquil or non-tranquil.

One does not differentiate the dharmas of the Stage of Utmost Joy by means of remoteness or non-remoteness, nor does one differentiate remoteness or non-remoteness by means of the dharmas of the Stage of Utmost Joy;

one does not differentiate the dharmas of the Stainless Stage, the Radiant Stage, up to the Stage of Excellent Intelligence and the Stage of Dharma Clouds by means of remoteness or non-remoteness, nor does one differentiate remoteness or non-remoteness by means of the dharmas of the Stainless Stage, the Radiant Stage, up to the Stage of Excellent Intelligence and the Stage of Dharma Clouds.

“Such persons as these never distinguish the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*) by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the stage of ordinary beings;

they do not distinguish the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*), the stage of one possessed of vision (*darśanabhūmi*), the stage of refinement (*tanubhūmi*), the stage of freedom from desire (*vītarāgabhūmi*), the stage of completion (*kṛtāvibhūmi*), the stage of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddhabhūmi*), the stage of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattvabhūmi*), or the stage of the Tathāgata (*tathāgatabhūmi*) by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stage of the bodhisattva, or the stage of the Tathāgata.”
One does not differentiate the stage of ordinary beings by means of signs or signlessness, nor does one differentiate signs or signlessness by means of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not differentiate the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stage of bodhisattvas and the stage of the Tathāgata by means of signs or signlessness, nor does one differentiate signs or signlessness by means of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stage of bodhisattvas and the stage of the Tathāgata.

One does not differentiate the stage of ordinary beings by means of having aspirations or being without aspirations, nor does one differentiate having aspirations or being without aspirations by means of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not differentiate the stage of the lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage by means of having aspirations or being without aspirations, nor does one differentiate having aspirations or being without aspirations by means of the stage of the lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage.
One does not differentiate the stage of ordinary beings by means of arising or non-arising, nor does one differentiate arising or non-arising by means of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not differentiate the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage by means of arising or non-arising, nor does one differentiate arising or non-arising by means of the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage.

One does not discriminate between the stage of an ordinary person (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*) by means of cessation or non-cessation, nor does one discriminate between cessation or non-cessation by means of the stage of an ordinary person;

one does not discriminate between the stage of the lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*), up to the bodhisattva stage (*bodhisattvabhūmi*) and the tathāgata stage (*tathāgatabhūmi*) by means of cessation or non-cessation, nor does one discriminate between the stage of the lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage by means of cessation or non-cessation.

One does not discriminate between the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*) and tranquility or non-tranquility; nor does one discriminate between tranquility or non-tranquility and the stage of ordinary beings.

One does not discriminate between the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage, on the one hand, and tranquility or non-tranquility on the other; nor does one discriminate between the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage, and tranquility or non-tranquility.

One does not differentiate the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana-bhūmi*) by means of detachment or non-detachment, nor does one differentiate detachment or non-detachment by means of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not differentiate the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage by means of detachment or non-detachment, nor does one differentiate the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stage and the tathāgata stage by means of detachment or non-detachment.

“Such persons as these never distinguish the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (pṛthagjana-bhūmi) by means of ‘emptiness’ or ‘non-emptiness,’ nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

they do not distinguish the dharmas of the stage of lineage (gotra-bhūmi), the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the Tathāgata by means of ‘emptiness’ or ‘non-emptiness,’ nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the Tathāgata.”

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana-bhūmi*) by means of signs or signlessness, nor does one discriminate between signs or signlessness by means of the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not discriminate between the dharmas of the stage of lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the Tathāgata, by means of signs or signlessness, nor does one discriminate between signs or signlessness by means of the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the Tathāgata.

One does not differentiate the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings by means of "with vow" or "without vow," nor does one differentiate "with vow" or "without vow" by means of the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not differentiate the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stages and the tathāgata stage by means of "with vow" or "without vow," nor does one differentiate "with vow" or "without vow" by means of the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stages and the tathāgata stage.

One does not discriminate between the state of being born and the state of being unborn with respect to the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*), nor does one discriminate between the state of being born and the state of being unborn with respect to the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings.

One does not discriminate between the state of being born and the state of being unborn with respect to the dharmas of the stage of lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*), up to the stages of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattvabhūmi*) and the stage of the Tathāgata (*tathāgatabhūmi*); nor does one discriminate between the state of being born and the state of being unborn with respect to the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the stage of the Tathāgata.

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*) by means of extinction or non-extinction, nor does one discriminate between the dharmas of extinction or non-extinction by means of the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not discriminate between the dharmas of the stage of lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*), up to the stages of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattvabhūmi*) and the Tathāgata (*tathāgatabhūmi*) by means of extinction or non-extinction, nor does one discriminate between the dharmas of extinction or non-extinction by means of the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the Tathāgata.

One does not discriminate between the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*) by means of "quiescence" or "non-quiescence," nor does one discriminate between quiescence and non-quiescence by means of the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not discriminate between the dharmas of the stage of lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*), up to the bodhisattva stages and the tathāgata stage by means of "quiescence" or "non-quiescence," nor does one discriminate between quiescence and non-quiescence by means of the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the bodhisattva stages and the tathāgata stage.

One does not differentiate the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*) by means of detachment or non-detachment, nor does one differentiate detachment or non-detachment by means of the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

one does not differentiate the dharmas of the stage of lineage (*gotrabhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamabhūmi*), up to the stages of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattvabhūmi*) and the Tathāgata (*tathāgatabhūmi*) by means of detachment or non-detachment, nor does one differentiate detachment or non-detachment by means of the dharmas of the stage of lineage, the eighth stage, up to the stages of the bodhisattva and the Tathāgata.

“Such persons as these never distinguish the conditioned realm (saṃskṛtadhātu) by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the conditioned realm;
they do not distinguish the unconditioned realm (asaṃskṛtadhātu) by means of emptiness or non-emptiness, nor do they distinguish emptiness or non-emptiness by means of the unconditioned realm.”
One does not differentiate the conditioned realm by means of the signless or the signless-free, nor does one differentiate the signless or the signless-free by means of the conditioned realm;
one does not differentiate the unconditioned realm by means of the signless or the signless-free, nor does one differentiate the signless or the signless-free by means of the unconditioned realm.
One does not differentiate the conditioned realm by means of wishing or wishlessness, nor does one differentiate wishing or wishlessness by means of the conditioned realm;
one does not differentiate the unconditioned realm by means of wishing or wishlessness, nor does one differentiate wishing or wishlessness by means of the unconditioned realm.
One does not discriminate between arising and non-arising with respect to the conditioned realm, nor does one discriminate between the conditioned realm and arising and non-arising;
one does not discriminate between arising and non-arising with respect to the unconditioned realm, nor does one discriminate between the unconditioned realm and arising and non-arising.
One does not differentiate the conditioned realm by means of extinction or non-extinction, nor does one differentiate extinction or non-extinction by means of the conditioned realm;
one does not differentiate the unconditioned realm by means of extinction or non-extinction, nor does one differentiate extinction or non-extinction by means of the unconditioned realm.

One does not discriminate between the conditioned realm (*saṃskṛtadhātu*) and tranquility or non-tranquility, nor does one discriminate between tranquility or non-tranquility and the conditioned realm;

one does not discriminate between the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) and tranquility or non-tranquility, nor does one discriminate between tranquility or non-tranquility and the unconditioned realm.
One does not discriminate between the conditioned realm (*saṃskṛtadhātu*) as being distant or not distant, nor does one discriminate between the conditioned realm and distance or non-distance;
one does not discriminate between the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) as being distant or not distant, nor does one discriminate between the unconditioned realm and distance or non-distance.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the devaputras, saying:

"This [Perfection of Wisdom] is thus profound, difficult to see, and difficult to realize; it is beyond discursive thought and transcends the sphere of discursive thought. It is subtle, serene, supreme, and foremost, realized only within the inner experience of the most noble ones. It cannot be fathomed by those of worldly wisdom, and among those who have spoken of this Perfection of Wisdom, there is truly no one capable of believing and accepting it."
Why is this? Because herein there is no dharma that can be manifested or shown; since there is no dharma to be displayed, even one who truly believes and accepts it cannot be found.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"Is it not the case that within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, the three vehicles are extensively explained—namely, the vehicle of the śrāvaka, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha, and the vehicle of the unsurpassed [Buddha]?"
This extensively explains the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path of gathering [the perfections], from the first generation of the mind of awakening up to the tenth stage, namely:
the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom;
as well as internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-and-external emptiness.
Emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned,
absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, and emptiness of non-existence.
...emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

whether it be suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm; or whether it be the noble truth of suffering...
The noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; or the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
or the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;
or the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, and the five powers.
the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path;
the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signless, and the wishless; the five eyes, the six supernormal powers;
the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity.
...the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; or the quality of non-forgetfulness, the nature of constant equanimity;
or all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
or all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi?
An extensive explanation of the superior qualities of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas’ gathering of merit is as follows:
because bodhisattva mahāsattvas diligently practice this *prajñāpāramitā*, in whatever place they are born, they always undergo miraculous birth (*upapāduka*);
they are able to sport with mastery in non-retrogressive supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), proceeding from one buddha-field to another...
In the Buddha-fields, they shall offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones;
according to their aspirations and inclinations, they shall be able to cultivate all manner of roots of goodness until they quickly attain perfection;
and in the presence of the Buddhas, they shall hear and uphold the True Dharma until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, never forgetting it nor becoming indolent or negligent.
Constantly dwelling in supreme meditative concentration and free from a distracted mind, by virtue of this condition, do you obtain unimpeded eloquence, inexhaustible eloquence,
error-free eloquence, swift eloquence, appropriate eloquence, eloquence rich in meaning and flavor in all that is expounded,
and the most wondrous and supreme eloquence in all the world?
Subhūti replied, “So it is! So it is!”
It is exactly as you have said.
Within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, the three vehicles of the Dharma are extensively expounded—namely, those of the śrāvaka, the pratyekabuddha, and the unsurpassed vehicle;

and the bodhisattva path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, from the first generation of the mind of awakening up to the tenth stage, is extensively expounded—namely, the pāramitās beginning with dāna up to all the doors of samādhi.

This extensively explains the superior qualities of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas’ gathering of merit; that is to say, because bodhisattva mahāsattvas diligently practice this *prajñāpāramitā*, wherever they are born, they always undergo miraculous birth (*upapāduka*), and so on, until they attain the most wondrous and supreme eloquence in all worlds. Furthermore, whatever they teach through such profound instruction, they employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*).
Śāriputra asked:
"With regard to what phenomena does this take non-apprehension as its means?
Subhūti replied:
“Śāriputra! This, for me, takes non-apprehension as its means;
this, for sentient beings, living beings, creatures, nourishers, persons, individuals, mind-born ones, youths, agents, experiencers, knowers, and seers, takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding form;
this is by means of non-apprehension regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding the sphere of the eye;
this is by means of non-apprehension regarding the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
“Śāriputra! This is the application of non-apprehension regarding the sphere of form;
this is the application of non-apprehension regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding the eye-element;
this is by means of non-apprehension regarding the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding the sphere of the ear;
this is by means of non-apprehension regarding the sphere of sounds, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition.”
“Śāriputra! Here, regarding the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), one employs the method of non-apprehension;

regarding the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, one employs the method of non-apprehension.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the tongue element takes non-apprehension as its means;
this [practice] regarding the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding the body-element;
this is by means of non-apprehension regarding the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding the mind-element;
this is by means of non-apprehension regarding the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”
“Śāriputra! This is the skillful means of non-apprehension regarding the earth element;
this is the skillful means of non-apprehension regarding the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
“Śāriputra! This is the application of non-apprehension with respect to the noble truth of suffering;
this is the application of non-apprehension with respect to the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.”
“Śāriputra! This [approach] takes non-apprehension as the means regarding ignorance;

this takes non-apprehension as the means regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding internal emptiness takes non-apprehension as its means;

this [practice] regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This takes non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding suchness;

this takes non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the perfection of generosity takes non-apprehension as its means;
this [practice] regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the four dhyānas takes non-apprehension as its skillful means;
this [practice] regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments takes non-apprehension as its skillful means.”
“Śāriputra! Regarding these eight liberations, one takes non-apprehension as the means;
regarding these eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities, one takes non-apprehension as the means.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the four foundations of mindfulness takes non-apprehension as its means;

this [practice] regarding the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] takes non-apprehension as the means for the liberation door of emptiness;
it takes non-apprehension as the means for the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the five eyes takes non-apprehension as its skillful means;
this [practice] regarding the six supernormal powers takes non-apprehension as its skillful means.”
“Śāriputra! Regarding these ten powers of a Buddha, one employs the method of non-apprehension;

regarding these four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one employs the method of non-apprehension.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness takes non-apprehension as its means;
this [practice] regarding the state of constant equanimity takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] takes non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all dhāraṇī-doors;
this takes non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all samādhi-doors.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding all-knowledge takes non-apprehension as its means;
this [practice] regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects takes non-apprehension as its means.”
“Śāriputra! This [path] of the Śrāvaka vehicle takes non-apprehension as its skillful means;
this [path] of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle (Anuttarayāna) likewise takes non-apprehension as its skillful means.”
“Śāriputra! This is the means of non-apprehension regarding the stream-enterer;
this is the means of non-apprehension regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat.”
“Śāriputra! This [path] for the candidate for and the fruit of stream-entry is characterized by the method of non-apprehension;

this [path] for the candidate for and the fruit of once-returning, the candidate for and the fruit of non-returning, and the candidate for and the fruit of arhatship is characterized by the method of non-apprehension.”
“Śāriputra! This is the means of non-apprehension regarding the pratyekabuddha;
this is the means of non-apprehension regarding the one who is a candidate for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.”
“Śāriputra! This is for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method;
this is for the samyaksaṃbuddha by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method.”
“Śāriputra! This [practice] regarding the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva takes non-apprehension as its skillful means;
this [practice] regarding the dharmas of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening takes non-apprehension as its skillful means.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method on the Ground of Utmost Joy;

this is by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method on the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Extreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.”
“Śāriputra! Regarding these dharmas of the Ground of Utmost Joy, one employs the method of non-apprehension;

regarding these dharmas of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Extreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, one employs the method of non-apprehension.”
“Śāriputra! This is, on the stage of ordinary beings, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method;

this is, on the stage of the lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of possessing vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of having completed what was to be done, the stage of the solitary realizer, the stage of the bodhisattva, and the stage of the Tathāgata, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method.”
“Śāriputra! This is by means of non-apprehension regarding the dharmas of the stage of ordinary beings;

this is by means of non-apprehension regarding the dharmas of the stage of the spiritual lineage, the eighth stage, the stage of possessing vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, the stage of completion, the stage of the pratyekabuddha, the stage of the bodhisattva, and the stage of the Tathāgata.”
“Śāriputra! This takes non-apprehension as the means regarding the realm of the conditioned;
this takes non-apprehension as the means regarding the realm of the unconditioned.”
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:

"For what reason, within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, does one extensively expound the three vehicles by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method—namely, the vehicles of the śrāvaka, the pratyekabuddha, and the unsurpassed vehicle?"

For what reason, within this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, is the path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—from the first generation of the mind of awakening up to the tenth stage—extensively explained by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method, including everything from the *dānapāramitā* up to all the gateways of *samādhi*?

For what reason, within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, is it taught by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) that one extensively gathers the supreme qualities of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—namely, that because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas diligently practice this Prajñāpāramitā, wherever they are born they always undergo miraculous birth (*upapāduka*), and so on, up to attaining the most wondrous and supreme eloquence in all worlds?
Subhūti replied, “Śāriputra! Because of internal emptiness,

within this profound teaching of the perfection of wisdom, one employs the method of non-apprehension to extensively explain the three vehicles of the Dharma— namely, the vehicle of the śrāvaka, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha, and the vehicle of the unsurpassed [Buddha].”
Śāriputra!

Because of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, within this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, one extensively expounds the three vehicles by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method—namely, the vehicles of the śrāvaka, the pratyekabuddha, and the unsurpassed vehicle.
“Śāriputra! Because of internal emptiness,
within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method,
the inclusion of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas from their first production of the thought of enlightenment is extensively explained.”
Up to the paths of the bodhisattvas of the ten stages— namely, the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence,
meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom; as well as internal emptiness, external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and conditioned emptiness...
Emptiness, the emptiness of the unconditioned, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— if these are true...

Suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
or the noble truth of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; or the four meditative concentrations...
the applications of mindfulness, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments; or the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities;

or the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path; or emptiness.
The gates of liberation—the gate of signlessness and the gate of wishlessness; whether it be the five eyes or the six supernormal powers;

whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the quality of non-forgetfulness.

the nature of equanimity that abides perpetually; whether it be omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
or whether it be any of the doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*) or any of the doors of samādhi (*samādhimukha*).

Śāriputra! Because of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, by means of the expedient of non-apprehension, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path—from the first generation of the mind of awakening through the ten stages—is extensively explained and encompassed, namely: the perfection of giving up to all the doors of samādhi.
"Śāriputra! Because of internal emptiness, within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, by employing the method of non-apprehension,
the superior matters of the merits that embrace Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are extensively explained."
It is said that because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas diligently practice this Prajñāpāramitā,
wherever they are born, they always undergo miraculous birth (upapāduka); they possess non-regressive supernatural powers (abhijñā) and can sport with them at will,
proceeding from one Buddha-field to another Buddha-field to make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise all [Buddhas].
O Buddha, World-Honored One, may they be able to cultivate all manner of roots of goodness according to their aspirations and wishes, swiftly attaining their full perfection;
may they hear and uphold the True Dharma from all Buddhas until reaching unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, never forgetting it nor becoming indolent or negligent;
and may they constantly abide in supreme meditative concentration, free from a distracted mind—may these serve as the conditions for this.
He attains unimpeded eloquence, inexhaustible eloquence, unerring and undisturbed eloquence, swift eloquence, responsive eloquence,
eloquence that abounds in profound meaning in all that is expounded, and the most wondrous and supreme eloquence in all the world.

“Śāriputra! Because of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, within this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful method, the superior matters of the merit of gathering in bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are extensively explained. That is to say, because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas diligently practice this *prajñāpāramitā*, wherever they are born, they always undergo miraculous birth (*upapāduka*), and so forth, until they attain the most wondrous and supreme eloquence in all worlds.”
Chapter 25: The Chapter on the Scattering of Flowers. First Part. Chapter Twenty-Five: The Chapter on the Scattering of Flowers.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and all the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven within this trichiliocosm...
In the Heaven of the Gods, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmakāyika-sabhā Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven,
the Parīttābhā Heaven, the Apramāṇābhā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara-śuddha Heaven, the Śubha Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven,
the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttabṛhatphala Heaven, the Apramāṇa... [Heaven].
The gods of Vast Measure, Vast Fruit, No Affliction, No Heat, Good Appearance, Good Vision, and the Ultimate of Form all thought to themselves:

"Now the Venerable Subhūti, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, is raining down the great Dharma rain for the sake of all sentient beings. For the purpose of making offerings, we should each manifest various exquisite celestial flowers and scatter them over Śākyamuni Tathāgata, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the community of bhikṣus, and the Venerable Subhūti; we shall also scatter them over the profound Prajñāpāramitā that is being taught, thereby making our offerings."

At that time, having formed this thought, the hosts of devas each manifested various kinds of exquisite fragrant flowers and scattered them as offerings over the Tathāgata, the bodhisattvas, and the others.

At that time, this great trichiliocosm Buddha-world was completely filled with flowers; through the Buddha’s spiritual power, these flowers combined in the void to form a flower pedestal, exquisitely adorned and magnificent, covering the entire great trichiliocosm.
When the Venerable Subhūti beheld this event, he thought to himself:

"As for these flowers now scattered, I have never before seen such exquisite flowers among the celestial realms; they certainly were not produced from grass, trees, water, or land, but must have been emanated from the minds of the devas for the purpose of making offerings."
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having understood the thoughts in Subhūti’s mind, said to Subhūti:
"These scattered flowers are truly not produced from grasses, trees, water, or land; nor were they actually emanated by the mind—they are merely a manifestation!"
The Venerable Subhūti said to Śakra:
"These flowers are unarisen; therefore, they are not flowers.
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked Subhūti:
"Is it only these flowers that do not arise, or are other phenomena likewise so?
Subhūti replied, "It is not only these flowers that do not arise; all other phenomena are likewise so."
What does this mean? "Kauśika!
Form (*rūpa*) is likewise unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not form."
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and thus it cannot be designated as form or any other such category.
“Kauśika! The sense-base of the eye is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the sense-base of the eye.
The sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as the sense-base of the eye (*cakṣur-āyatana*) or any other such bases. "Kauśika!..."
The sense-base of form is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the sense-base of form.

The sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as the sense-base of form (*rūpāyatana*) or any other such category. "Kauśika!..."
The eye-element also does not arise; since it does not arise, it is not the eye-element.

The form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition also do not arise; since they do not arise, they are not the form-element, nor even the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is also non-arising; since it does not arise, it is not the ear-element.

The sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are also non-arising; since they do not arise, they are not the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the ear-element (*śrotradhātu*) or any other such category. "Kauśika!..."
The nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the nose element.

The odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*) and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the odor element, nor even the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) also does not arise; since it does not arise, it is not the tongue element.

The taste element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*) and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition (*pratyaya*) also do not arise; since they do not arise, they are not the taste element, nor even the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) and cannot be designated as the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) or any other such category. "Kauśika!..."
The body element (*kāyadhātu*) is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the body element.

The tangible object element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition (*pratyaya*) are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the tangible object element, nor even the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) or other such categories. "Kauśika!..."
The mind-element (*manodhātu*) is also not produced; since it is not produced, it is not the mind-element.

The dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition, are also not produced; since they are not produced, they are not the dharma-element, nor even the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the mind-element (*manodhātu*) or any other such categories. "Kauśika!..."
The earth element is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the earth element.
The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as the earth element or any other such category. "Kauśika!..."
The noble truth of suffering is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the noble truth of suffering.
The noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the Noble Truth of Suffering or any other. "Kauśika!..."
Ignorance (*avidyā*) also does not arise; since it does not arise, it is not ignorance.

Formative forces (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) also do not arise; since they do not arise, they are not formative forces, nor even old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as ignorance (*avidyā*) or anything else. "Kauśika!..."
Internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not internal emptiness.

External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as "inner emptiness" and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
Suchness (*tathatā*) is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not Suchness.

The realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the realm of phenomena, nor even the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as such things as *tathatā* (suchness). "Kauśika!..."
The perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) or any other such [perfections]. "Kauśika!..."
The four dhyānas are also non-arising; since they do not arise, they are not the four dhyānas.
The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are also non-arising; since they do not arise, they are not the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The eight liberations are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the eight liberations.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and thus it cannot be designated as the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The four foundations of mindfulness are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The gate of liberation of emptiness is also non-arising; since it is non-arising, it is not the gate of liberation of emptiness.
The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The five eyes are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the five eyes.
The six supernormal powers are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the six supernormal powers.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and it cannot be designated as the five eyes or other such things. "Kauśika!..."
The ten powers of a Buddha are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the four fearlessnesses up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and thus cannot be designated as the ten powers of a Buddha or other such qualities. "Kauśika!..."
The quality of non-forgetfulness is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the quality of non-forgetfulness.
The state of constant equanimity is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the state of constant equanimity.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as things such as the quality of non-forgetfulness. "Kauśika!..."
All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not all-knowledge.
Knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not knowledge of the paths nor knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as "all-knowledge" (*sarvajñatā*) and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
All dhāraṇī-doors are likewise non-arising; since they do not arise, they are not all dhāraṇī-doors.
All samādhi-doors are likewise non-arising; since they do not arise, they are not all samādhi-doors.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as any of the gateways to dhāraṇī and so forth. "Kauśika!..."
The stream-enterer is also non-arising; since this is non-arising, it is not a stream-enterer.
The once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are also non-arising; since these are non-arising, they are not once-returners, non-returners, or arhats.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and thus it cannot be designated as a "stream-enterer" and so forth. "Kauśika!..."

The candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry nor the fruit of stream-entry.

The candidate for the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the candidate for the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the candidate for the fruit of arhatship and the fruit of arhatship are also non-arising; since they are non-arising, they are not the candidate for the fruit of once-returning nor the fruit of once-returning, not the candidate for the fruit of non-returning nor the fruit of non-returning, and not the candidate for the fruit of arhatship nor the fruit of arhatship.

Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as the stage of entering the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, or any such states. "Kauśika!..."
The Pratyekabuddha also does not arise; since this does not arise, it is not a Pratyekabuddha.
The candidate for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha also does not arise; since this does not arise, it is not the candidate for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as a Pratyekabuddha or any such state. "Kauśika!..."
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise unarisen; since he is unarisen, he is not a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
The samyaksaṃbuddha is likewise unarisen; since he is unarisen, he is not a samyaksaṃbuddha.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), it cannot be designated as a bodhisattva mahāsattva or the like. "Kauśika!..."
The dharmas of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the dharmas of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
Unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) and cannot be designated as the dharma of a bodhisattva mahāsattva or the like. "Kauśika!..."
The Śrāvaka vehicle is also unarisen; since it is unarisen, it is not the Śrāvaka vehicle.
The Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle are also unarisen; since they are unarisen, they are not the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
Why is this? Because the dharma of non-arising is free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) and cannot be designated as the Śrāvaka vehicle or any other.
—From the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 84.

Chapter Twenty-Six: Training in Prajñā. Part One: Training in Prajñā, Section Twenty-Six, Part One.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, conceived this thought:
"The Venerable Subhūti possesses profound wisdom; he teaches the nature of dharmas without destroying conventional designations.
The Buddha, knowing his intention, then confirmed his words:
"Just as Kauśika has conceived in his mind, the Venerable Subhūti possesses profound wisdom; he teaches the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) without destroying conventional designations.
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"In what manner does the Venerable Subhūti teach the nature of phenomena without destroying conventional designations?"
The Buddha told Kauśika:

"Form is merely a provisional designation; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations of form and so forth when he speaks of the nature of phenomena of form and so forth."
Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of form and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The sense base of the eye is merely a conventional designation; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are merely conventional designations. Such conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these conventional designations of the sense base of the eye and so forth when he speaks of the dharmatā of the sense base of the eye and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharmic nature of the sense bases, such as the eye, is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The sphere of form is merely a conventional designation; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are merely conventional designations. Such conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these conventional designations of the sphere of form and so forth when he speaks of the nature of phenomena of the sphere of form and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharmas such as the sense-sphere of form have a nature that is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has said is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The eye-element is merely a conventional designation; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are merely conventional designations. Such conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these conventional designations of the eye-element and so forth, speaks of the *dharmatā* of the eye-element and so forth.

Why is this so? Because the dharmic nature of the eye-faculty and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The ear-element is merely a provisional designation; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these provisional designations such as the ear-element, speaks of the nature of phenomena of the ear-element and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the ear-element and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The nose element is merely a provisional designation; the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are also merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these provisional designations such as the nose element, speaks of the nature of phenomena of the nose element and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharmic nature of the nose-element and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The tongue element is merely a provisional designation; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā); thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations of the tongue element and so forth when he speaks of the dharmatā of the tongue element and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharmic nature of the tongue-element and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The body element is merely a provisional designation; the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are also merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these provisional designations such as the body element, speaks of the nature of phenomena of the body element and so forth.

Why is this so? Because the dharmic nature of the body-element and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The mind-element (*manodhātu*) is merely a conventional designation; the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as a condition, are also merely conventional designations. Such conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these conventional designations such as the mind-element, speaks of the nature of phenomena of the mind-element and so forth.

Why is this? Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) such as the mind-element (manodhātu) is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The earth element is merely a provisional designation; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti speaks of the nature of phenomena such as the earth element without destroying these provisional designations of the earth element and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharmic nature of the earth element and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The noble truth of suffering is merely a provisional designation; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are also merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations of the noble truth of suffering and so forth when he speaks of the *dharmatā* of the noble truth of suffering and so forth.

Why is this so? Because the dharma-nature of the Noble Truth of Suffering and the other truths is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.
“Kauśika! Ignorance is merely a provisional designation;

volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are merely provisional designations. These provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these provisional designations such as ignorance, yet he speaks of the nature of phenomena of ignorance and the other factors.”

Why is this? Because the nature of phenomena such as ignorance is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

Internal emptiness is merely a provisional designation; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the dharmatā; thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without subverting these provisional designations such as internal emptiness, speaks of the dharmatā of internal emptiness and the other categories.

Why is this? Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), such as internal emptiness and so forth, is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

“Tathatā is merely a conventional designation; dharmadhātu, dharmatā, the nature of non-erroneousness, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are all merely conventional designations. These conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these conventional designations such as Tathatā when he speaks of the dharmatā of Tathatā and so forth.”

Why is this so? Because the dharmatā of suchness and other phenomena is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The perfection of generosity is merely a conventional designation; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are also merely conventional designations. Such designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these conventional designations such as the perfection of generosity, speaks of the *dharmatā* of the perfection of generosity and the other perfections.

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the perfection of generosity and the other perfections is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! The four dhyānas are merely conventional designations; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are merely conventional designations. Such conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these conventional designations of the four dhyānas and so forth when he speaks of the nature of phenomena of the four dhyānas and so forth.”
Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the four dhyānas and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! The eight liberations are merely provisional designations; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these provisional designations of the eight liberations and so forth when he speaks of the nature of phenomena of the eight liberations and so forth.”
