Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the eight liberations and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! The four foundations of mindfulness are merely designations; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are merely designations. Such designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these designations of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth when he speaks of the nature of phenomena of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth is neither destroyed nor undestroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor undestroyed.

“Kauśika! The gate of liberation of emptiness is merely a provisional designation; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these provisional designations of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth, yet he speaks of the nature of phenomena of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharmic nature of the gateways to liberation such as emptiness is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, that which is spoken by Subhūti is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! The five eyes are merely provisional designations; the six supernormal powers are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the dharma-nature. The Venerable Subhūti, without subverting these provisional designations such as the five eyes, speaks of the dharma-nature of the five eyes and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharmic nature of the five eyes and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. “Kauśika!

The ten powers of a Buddha are merely provisional designations; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); thus, the Venerable Subhūti speaks of the nature of phenomena regarding the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth, without destroying these provisional designations of the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth.

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the Buddha’s ten powers and so forth is neither destructible nor indestructible; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destructible nor indestructible.

“Kauśika! The quality of non-forgetfulness is a mere designation; the state of constant equanimity is a mere designation. Such designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). The Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these designations such as ‘non-forgetfulness,’ yet he speaks of the nature of phenomena of non-forgetfulness and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the nature of phenomena such as the "absence of forgetfulness" is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! ‘All-knowledge’ (sarvajñatā) is merely a provisional designation; ‘knowledge of the paths’ (mārgākārajñatā) and ‘knowledge of all aspects’ (sarvākārajñatā) are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not destroy these provisional designations such as ‘all-knowledge,’ yet he speaks of the dharmatā of all-knowledge and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of all-knowledge and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, that which is spoken by Subhūti is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! All dhāraṇī-doors are merely provisional designations; all samādhi-doors are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these provisional designations of all dhāraṇī-doors and so forth, speaks of the nature of phenomena of all dhāraṇī-doors and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the nature of all dharmas, such as the gateways of dhāraṇī, is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! ‘Stream-enterer’ is merely a provisional designation; ‘once-returner,’ ‘non-returner,’ and ‘arhat’ are also merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the dharmatā. The Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations of stream-enterers and so forth when he speaks of the dharmatā of stream-enterers and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of those such as the stream-enterers is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

The candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry are merely conventional designations; the candidate for the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the candidate for the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the candidate for the fruit of arhatship and the fruit of arhatship are merely conventional designations. Such conventional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti, without undermining these conventional designations of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry, speaks of the *dharmatā* of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry.

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of those such as the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! ‘Pratyekabuddha’ is merely a provisional designation; ‘one progressing toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha’ is also merely a provisional designation. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations such as ‘pratyekabuddha’ when he speaks of the dharmatā of pratyekabuddhas and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the Pratyekabuddhas and others is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed. "Kauśika!..."

A bodhisattva mahāsattva is merely a provisional name, and a samyaksaṃbuddha is merely a provisional name; such provisional names do not depart from the dharma-nature. The Venerable Subhūti, without destroying these provisional names of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas and the like, speaks of the dharma-nature of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas and the like.

Why is this? Because for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and others, the dharma-nature is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! The dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are merely provisional designations; unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is also merely a provisional designation. Such provisional designations do not depart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva when he speaks of the nature of phenomena of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

Why is this so? Because for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, the dharmas and the dharma-nature are neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, what Subhūti has spoken is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.

“Kauśika! The Śrāvaka vehicle is merely a provisional designation; the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle are merely provisional designations. Such provisional designations do not depart from the dharma-nature (dharmatā). Thus, the Venerable Subhūti does not subvert these provisional designations of the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth when he speaks of the dharma-nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth.”

Why is this? Because the dharma-nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth is neither destroyed nor not destroyed; therefore, that which is spoken by Subhūti is likewise neither destroyed nor not destroyed.
“Kauśika! The Venerable Subhūti teaches the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) without destroying conventional designations.
The Venerable Subhūti said to Śakra:
“Kauśika! So it is! So it is!”
As the Buddha has taught, there are no phenomena whatsoever that are not merely provisional designations. Kausika!
Having realized that all phenomena are but provisional designations, a bodhisattva mahasattva should study the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in form, nor does he train in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as something in which one can train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the sphere of the eye, nor does he train in the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the sense-base of the eye as something in which one can train, nor do they perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as things in which one can train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in the sphere of form, nor do they train in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a sphere of form in which one can train, nor does he perceive a sphere of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in the eye-element; they do not train in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, or in eye-contact, nor in the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a visual-sphere (*cakṣur-dhātu*) in which one might train, nor does he perceive a sphere of forms (*rūpa-dhātu*), up to and including the various sensations (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, in which one might train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train in the ear element; they do not train in the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ear-element as something in which one may train, nor does he perceive the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as things in which one may train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in the nose element; they do not train in the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nor in nose-contact, nor in the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as something in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train in the tongue element; they do not train in the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the tongue-element as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as things in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the body element; he does not train in the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, nor in the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a body-element (*kāyadhātu*) in which one might train, nor does he perceive a touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*)—up to and including the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition—in which one might train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, he does not train in the mind-element (manodhātu), nor does he train in the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), or the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a mental sphere (*manodhātu*) in which one might train, nor does he perceive a dharma-sphere (*dharmadhātu*), up to and including those sensations produced with mental contact as condition (*manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayaja-vedanā*), in which one might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, he does not train in the earth element, nor does he train in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a earth-element in which one may train, nor does he perceive a water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness-element in which one may train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the noble truth of suffering, nor does he train in the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.”
Why is this? Kausika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the Noble Truth of Suffering as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, or the Path as things in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, he does not train in ignorance; he does not train in volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive ignorance as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive anything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as something in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in internal emptiness; nor does he train in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive internal emptiness as something in which they can train, nor do they perceive external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence and self-existence, as something in which they can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in suchness; they do not train in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

This is because that bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a *tathatā* (suchness) in which one might train, nor does he perceive a *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), up to and including the *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm), in which one might train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in the perfection of generosity; they do not train in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive a perfection of giving in which they might train, nor do they perceive a perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom in which they might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train in the four dhyānas, nor do they train in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four dhyānas as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as something in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the eight liberations, nor does he train in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the eight liberations as something in which they can train, nor do they perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten universal bases as something in which they can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not train in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as something in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor does he train in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive a gate of liberation of emptiness in which they might train, nor do they perceive a gate of liberation of signlessness or wishlessness in which they might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they do not train in the five eyes, nor do they train in the six superknowledges. Why is that?

Kauśika! This is because that bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the five eyes as something in which one can train, nor does he perceive the six supernormal powers as something in which one can train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train in the ten powers of a buddha; they do not train in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha as something in which they should train, nor do they perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as something in which they should train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor does he train in the state of constant equanimity.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any "dharma of non-forgetfulness" in which one might train, nor does he perceive any "nature of constant equanimity" in which one might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train in all-knowledge, nor do they train in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor in the knowledge of all aspects.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive an all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) in which one might train, nor does he perceive a knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) or an all-aspect knowledge (sarvākārajñatā) in which one might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in any of the dhāraṇī-doors, nor does he train in any of the samādhi-doors.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharanī-doors in which one might train, nor does he perceive any samādhi-doors in which one might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train for the sake of the stream-enterer, nor for the sake of the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a stream-enterer in whom one might train, nor does he perceive a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat in whom one might train.

“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, he does not train for the fruit of stream-entry nor for the path of stream-entry; he does not train for the fruit of once-returning nor the path of once-returning, nor for the fruit of non-returning nor the path of non-returning, nor for the fruit of arhatship nor the path of arhatship.”
Why is this? Kausika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive a candidate for the fruit of stream-entry or the fruit of stream-entry as something in which they should train; nor do they perceive a candidate for the fruit of once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, a candidate for the fruit of non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or a candidate for the fruit of arhatship or the fruit of arhatship as something in which they should train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train for the sake of a pratyekabuddha, nor do they train for the sake of the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a pratyekabuddha in whom one might train, nor does he perceive a candidate for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha in whom one might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor does he train in the samyaksaṃbuddha.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a bodhisattva mahāsattva in whom one may train, nor does he perceive a samyaksaṃbuddha in whom one may train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, he does not train in the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor does he train in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma of a bodhisattva mahāsattva in which one might train, nor does he perceive any unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in which one might train.
“Kauśika! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they do not train in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, nor do they train in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas or the unsurpassed vehicle.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive a śrāvaka vehicle in which they might train, nor do they perceive a pratyekabuddha vehicle or a supreme vehicle (anuttarayāna) in which they might train.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Subhūti: "Venerable One,
for what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive form, and does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness?"
“Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the sense-base of the eye, nor perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind?
“Venerable sir! [The Buddha replied:]
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the sphere of form, nor perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena?
"Venerable One!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the eye-element, nor perceive the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition?"
“Venerable One!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the ear element, nor perceive the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition?”
“Venerable Sir!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the nose element, nor perceive the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition?”
“Venerable One!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the tongue element, nor the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, nor tongue-contact, nor the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition?”
“Venerable One!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor perceive the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as their condition?”
“Venerable sir!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor perceive the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mind-contact as their condition?”
“Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the earth element, nor perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements?
“Venerable sir! [he asked.]
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the noble truth of suffering, nor perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?
"Venerable sir!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive ignorance, nor perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?"
“Venerable One!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive internal emptiness, nor perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Venerable Sir!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive true suchness (tathatā), nor perceive the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu), or the inconceivable realm?”
“Venerable sir!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the perfection of generosity, nor perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
"Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the four dhyānas, nor perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments?
"Venerable sir!"
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the eight liberations, nor perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities?
"Venerable Sir!"

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, nor perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path?
“Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?
“Venerable sir! [The interlocutor continued.]
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not see the five eyes, nor see the six supernormal powers?
"Venerable One!

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not see the ten powers of a buddha, nor see the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?"
"Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor perceive the nature of constant equanimity?
"Venerable sir! [he replied.]

"For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)?
Venerable sir,
for what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor perceive any of the doors of samādhi?"
“Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive a stream-enterer, nor perceive a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat?
“Venerable sir! [he continued.]

For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry nor the fruit of stream-entry; nor the candidate for the fruit of once-returning nor the fruit of once-returning; nor the candidate for the fruit of non-returning nor the fruit of non-returning; nor the candidate for the fruit of arhatship nor the fruit of arhatship?
“Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive a pratyekabuddha, nor perceive one who is practicing toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha?
“Venerable sir! [he asked.]
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor perceive a samyaksaṃbuddha?
"Venerable sir!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the dharma of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor perceive unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Venerable One!
For what reason does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive the vehicle of the śrāvakas, nor the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, nor the unsurpassed vehicle?
Subhūti replied:
“Kauśika! Because form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form;

because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form, he does not train in form;
because he does not perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, he does not train in feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of form as the emptiness of form; one cannot see the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Kauśika! One should not train in the emptiness of form by means of the emptiness of form; nor should one train in the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness by means of the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“Kauśika! Because the sense-base of the eye is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense-base of the eye, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sense-base of the eye;

because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sense base of the eye, he does not train in the sense base of the eye;
because he does not perceive the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, he does not train in the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the eye-base as the emptiness of the eye-base; one cannot see the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-bases as the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-bases.

Kauśika! One should not train in the emptiness of the eye-faculty as being empty of the eye-faculty; nor should one train in the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-faculties as being empty of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-faculties.
“Kauśika! Because the sphere of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sphere of form;

because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sphere of form, they do not train in the sphere of form;
because they do not perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, they do not train in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the sphere of form by means of the emptiness of the sphere of form; nor can one see the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena by means of the emptiness of those respective spheres.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the sphere of form by means of the emptiness of the sphere of form; nor can one train in the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena by means of the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
“Kauśika! Because the eye-element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-element;

because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-element, they do not train in the eye-element;

because they do not perceive the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they do not train in the form-element, nor even in the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
Why is this so? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the eye-element as the eye-element being empty; nor can one see the emptiness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition as being the emptiness of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Kauśika! One should not train in the emptiness of the eye-element by means of the emptiness of the eye-element; nor should one train in the emptiness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition by means of the emptiness of the form-element, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“Kauśika! Because the ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ear-element;

because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ear-element, they do not train in the ear-element;

because they do not perceive the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, they do not train in the sound-element, up to and including the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the ear-element as being the emptiness of the ear-element; nor can one see the emptiness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition as being the emptiness of the sound-element, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Kauśika! One should not train in the emptiness of the ear-element as being empty of the ear-element; nor should one train in the emptiness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as being empty of the sound-element, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
“Kauśika! Because the nose-element is empty of the nature of a nose-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the nose-element;

because the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), they do not train in the nose element;

because they do not perceive the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), or the various sensations (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, they do not train in the odor element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the nose-element as the nose-element being empty; nor can one see the emptiness of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, by means of the odor-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition being empty.

Kauśika! One should not train in the emptiness of the nose-element by means of the emptiness of the nose-element; nor should one train in the emptiness of the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, by means of the emptiness of those [elements] from the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“Kauśika! Because the tongue-element is empty of the nature of a tongue-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the tongue-element;

because the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are empty of the nature of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the element of the tongue, they do not train in the element of the tongue;

because they do not perceive the element of tastes, the element of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, or the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, they do not train in the element of tastes up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the tongue-element as the tongue-element being empty; nor can one see the emptiness of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as being the emptiness of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Kauśika! One should not train in the emptiness of the tongue-element as being empty of the tongue-element; nor should one train in the emptiness of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as being empty of the taste-element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“Kauśika! Because the body-element (kāyadhātu) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the body-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the body-element;

because the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), as well as body-contact (kāyasparśa) and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition are empty of the intrinsic nature of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), they do not train in the body-element;

because they do not perceive the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various sensations (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, they do not train in the touch-element up to the various sensations produced with body-contact as a condition.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

Because one cannot perceive the emptiness of the body-element as being empty of the body-element; nor can one perceive the emptiness of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, as being empty of the touch-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the body-element by means of the emptiness of the body-element; nor can one train in the emptiness of the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, by means of the emptiness of the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“Kauśika! Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is empty of the nature of a mind-element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the mind-element;

because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition are empty of the nature of the dharma-element up to the feelings produced with mental contact as condition, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the dharma-element up to the feelings produced with mental contact as condition.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the mind-element (*manodhātu*), he does not train in the mind-element;

because he does not perceive the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, he does not train in the dharma-element, nor even in the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.
Why is this? Kausika!

One does not perceive the emptiness of the mental faculty by means of the emptiness of the mental faculty; one does not perceive the emptiness of the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness-realm, mental contact, or the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, by means of the emptiness of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition. Thus, because of the emptiness of these things, one does not perceive them.

Kauśika! The unconditioned mind-element is empty because of its emptiness of the mind-element; it is because the unconditioned dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are empty because of their emptiness of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, that they are the training.
“Kauśika! Because the earth element is empty of the nature of the earth element, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the earth element;

because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the earth element, they do not train in the earth element;
because they do not perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, they do not train in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of the earth element as the earth element being empty; one cannot perceive the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as those very elements being empty.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the earth element as being empty of the earth element; nor can one train in the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being empty of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Eighty-Five [and] Scroll Eighty-Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
First Division: Chapter on Training in Prajñā, Part Twenty-Six, Section Two. “Kauśika!
Because the noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the noble truth of suffering.”

Because the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the noble truth of suffering, they do not train in the noble truth of suffering;
because they do not perceive the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, they do not train in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering as the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering; nor can one perceive the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

Kauśika! It is not by learning that the noble truth of suffering is empty of the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering; it is not by learning that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
“Kauśika! Because ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive ignorance;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the nature of old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive volitional formations up to and including old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive ignorance, they do not train in ignorance;

because they do not perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, they do not train in anything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of ignorance as being empty of ignorance; nor can one perceive the emptiness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as being empty of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. This is because they are empty.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of ignorance by means of the emptiness of ignorance; nor can one train in the emptiness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair by means of the emptiness of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Thus it is for all these.
“Kauśika! Because internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive internal emptiness.

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are each empty of their respective natures—ranging from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive external emptiness, nor does he perceive [any of them] up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive internal emptiness, he does not train in internal emptiness;

because he does not perceive external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, he does not train in external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of internal emptiness within internal emptiness, nor can one perceive the emptiness of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature within external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of internal emptiness by means of the emptiness of internal emptiness; nor can one train in the emptiness of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence, by means of the emptiness of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.
“Kauśika! Because true thusness (*tathatā*) is empty of the nature of true thusness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive true thusness;

because the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive suchness, they do not train in suchness;
because they do not perceive the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, they do not train in the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of suchness as the emptiness of suchness; one cannot see the emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, as the emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the emptiness of suchness by means of the emptiness of suchness; nor can one train in the emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, by means of the emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
“Kauśika! Because the perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the perfection of generosity;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the perfection of generosity, they do not train in the perfection of generosity;

because they do not perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they do not train in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because one cannot perceive the emptiness of the perfection of giving as being empty of the perfection of giving; nor can one perceive the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being empty of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Kauśika! The perfection of generosity is not empty of the practice of the emptiness of the perfection of generosity; nor is the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom empty of the practice of the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom. Therefore, they are not to be learned as being empty.
“Kauśika! Because the four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four dhyānas;

because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four dhyānas, he does not train in the four dhyānas;
because he does not perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, he does not train in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the four dhyānas as being empty of the four dhyānas; one cannot see the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as being empty of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the four dhyānas by means of the emptiness of the four dhyānas; nor can one train in the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments by means of the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
“Kauśika! Because the eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eight liberations;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eight liberations, he does not train in the eight liberations;

because he does not perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, he does not train in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the eight liberations as the emptiness of the eight liberations; one cannot see the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the eight liberations by means of the emptiness of the eight liberations; nor can one train in the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities by means of the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

“Kauśika! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not train in the four foundations of mindfulness;

because they do not perceive the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path, they do not train in the four right endeavors up to and including the eightfold noble path.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

Because one cannot perceive the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness as being the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness; nor can one perceive the emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path as being the emptiness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the four applications of mindfulness by means of the emptiness of the four applications of mindfulness; nor can one train in the emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path by means of the emptiness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

“Kauśika! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the gate of liberation of emptiness;

because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the gate of liberation of emptiness, they do not train in the gate of liberation of emptiness;
because they do not perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they do not train in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness as being empty of the gate of liberation of emptiness; nor can one perceive the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as being empty of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

Kauśika! This is because the emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness is not empty of the study of the gate of liberation of emptiness; likewise, the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is not empty of the study of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Kauśika! Because the five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the five eyes;
because the six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the six supernormal powers.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the five eyes, they do not train in the five eyes;
because they do not perceive the six supernormal powers, they do not train in the six supernormal powers.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the five eyes by means of the emptiness of the five eyes, nor can one see the emptiness of the six supernormal powers by means of the emptiness of the six supernormal powers.

"Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the five eyes by means of the emptiness of the five eyes, nor can one train in the emptiness of the six supernormal powers by means of the emptiness of the six supernormal powers.
Therefore, Kauśika!"
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—are empty of the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ten powers of a buddha, they do not train in the ten powers of a buddha;

because they do not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they do not train in the four fearlessnesses up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the Buddha’s ten powers by means of the emptiness of the Buddha’s ten powers; nor can one see the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha by means of the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the Buddha’s ten powers by means of the emptiness of the Buddha’s ten powers; nor can one train in the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha by means of the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Kauśika! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness;

because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness, he does not train in the quality of non-forgetfulness;
because he does not perceive the state of constant equanimity, he does not train in the state of constant equanimity.
Why is this? Kauśika!

Because one cannot perceive the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness within the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor can one perceive the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity within the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness by means of the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness; nor can one train in the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity by means of the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity.
“Kauśika! Because the omniscience of all-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive all-knowledge;

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they do not train in all-knowledge;

because they do not perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they do not train in the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of all-knowledge by means of the emptiness of all-knowledge; one cannot perceive the emptiness of the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects by means of the emptiness of the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. This is because they are empty.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of all-knowledge by means of the emptiness of all-knowledge; nor can one train in the emptiness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects by means of the emptiness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects. Therefore, it is not so.
“Kauśika! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dhāraṇī-doors;
because all samādhi-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-doors, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any samādhi-doors.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dhāraṇī-doors, they do not train in any dhāraṇī-doors;
because they do not perceive any samādhi-doors, they do not train in any samādhi-doors.
Why is this? Kauśika!

Because one cannot perceive the emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors through the emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor can one perceive the emptiness of all samādhi-doors through the emptiness of all samādhi-doors.

Kauśika! It is not by training in the emptiness of all dharanī-doors as being empty of the emptiness of all dharanī-doors that one trains; it is not by training in the emptiness of all samādhi-doors as being empty of the emptiness of all samādhi-doors that one trains.
“Kauśika! Because the stream-enterer is empty of the nature of a stream-enterer, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a stream-enterer;

because the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are empty of the nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, and an arhat, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a stream-enterer, he does not train for the sake of a stream-enterer;
because he does not perceive a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, he does not train for the sake of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because one cannot perceive the emptiness of a stream-enterer as being the stream-enterer’s emptiness; nor can one perceive the emptiness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat as being the once-returner, non-returner, or arhat’s emptiness.

Kauśika! It is not that the emptiness of a stream-enterer is learned through the emptiness of a stream-enterer; it is not that the emptiness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat is learned through the emptiness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.

“Kauśika! Because the state of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself are empty of intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry or the fruit of stream-entry.

Because the state of the candidate for the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the candidate for the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the candidate for the fruit of arhatship and the fruit of arhatship—from the candidate for the fruit of once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship—are empty of intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the candidate for the fruit of once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.”

Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of the stream-enterer, he does not train for the sake of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of the stream-enterer.

Because he does not perceive the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of the once-returner, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of the non-returner, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship, he does not train for the sake of the stage of entering once-returning, up to and including the fruit of arhatship.
Why is this? Kausika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of the stream-enterer’s path or the emptiness of the fruit of stream-entry as being distinct from the emptiness of the stream-enterer’s path or the fruit of stream-entry; nor can one perceive the emptiness of the once-returner’s path or fruit, the non-returner’s path or fruit, or the arhat’s path or fruit as being distinct from the emptiness of the once-returner’s path up to the fruit of arhatship. This is because they are empty.

Kauśika! The stage of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the fruit of stream-entry; the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the stage of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry. This is because the training is empty of the fruit of stream-entry. Likewise, the stage of the candidate for the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, the stage of the candidate for the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the stage of the candidate for the fruit of arhatship, and the fruit of arhatship are all empty of the fruit of once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship, because the training is empty of them.
“Kauśika! Because the Pratyekabuddha is empty of the nature of a Pratyekabuddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not perceive a Pratyekabuddha;

because the candidate for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha is empty of the nature of a candidate for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not perceive a candidate for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a pratyekabuddha, he does not train in the path of a pratyekabuddha;
because he does not perceive one who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, he does not train in the path leading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot perceive the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha as being the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha; one cannot perceive the emptiness of the path leading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha as being the emptiness of the path leading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha by means of the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha, nor can one train in the emptiness of the emptiness of the state of being a candidate for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha by means of the emptiness of the state of being a candidate for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.
“Kauśika! Because the nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the nature of a samyaksaṃbuddha is empty, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a samyaksaṃbuddha.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a bodhisattva mahāsattva, he does not train in a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because he does not perceive a samyaksaṃbuddha, he does not train in a samyaksaṃbuddha.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because one cannot perceive the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor can one perceive the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha by means of the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha.

Kauśika! It is not possible for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to train in the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; nor is it possible to train in the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha by means of the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha.
“Kauśika! Because the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are empty of the nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;

because unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment is empty of the nature of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, he does not train in the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because he does not perceive unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he does not train in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? Kauśika!

Because one cannot see the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva within the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor can one see the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment within the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Kauśika! It is not possible for the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva to train in the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor is it possible for the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to train in the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Kauśika! Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is empty of the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the Śrāvaka vehicle;

because the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle are empty of the nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.”
Kauśika! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the vehicle of the śrāvakas, he does not train in the vehicle of the śrāvakas;
because he does not perceive the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas or the unsurpassed vehicle, he does not train in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas or the unsurpassed vehicle.
Why is this? Kauśika!

One cannot see the emptiness of the Śrāvaka vehicle by means of the emptiness of the Śrāvaka vehicle; one cannot see the emptiness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle by means of the emptiness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.

Kauśika! One cannot train in the emptiness of the Śrāvaka vehicle by means of the emptiness of the Śrāvaka vehicle; nor can one train in the emptiness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle by means of the emptiness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in emptiness, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in emptiness. Why is this?
Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of form, nor train in the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of form, and for the sake of training in the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."
Why is this? Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the sense-base of the eye, nor train in the emptiness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of the sense-base of the eye, and for the sake of training in the emptiness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the sphere of form, nor train in the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of the sphere of form, and for the sake of training in the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the eye-element, nor train in the emptiness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the eye-element, and is training in the emptiness of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.
