Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the ear-element, nor train in the emptiness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the ear-element, and is training in the emptiness of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the nose element, nor in the emptiness of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the nose element, and is training in the emptiness of the odor element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the tongue element, nor train in the emptiness of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the tongue element, and is training in the emptiness of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the body element (*kāyadhātu*), nor train in the emptiness of the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as their condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the body element, and is training in the emptiness of the contact element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the mental faculty (*manas*), nor train in the emptiness of the phenomena (*dharma*), the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the mental faculty, and is training in the emptiness of the phenomena up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the earth element, nor train in the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the earth element, and is training in the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering, nor train in the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering, and for the sake of training in the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of ignorance, nor train in the emptiness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of ignorance, and is training in the emptiness of everything from volitional formations through old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the internal, nor in the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the internal, and is training in the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature.
Why is this? Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of *tathatā*, nor train in the emptiness of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of *tathatā*, and is training in the emptiness of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in emptiness regarding the perfection of generosity, nor train in emptiness regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in emptiness regarding the perfection of generosity, and is training in emptiness regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Why is this? Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the four dhyānas, nor train in the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of the four dhyānas that this bodhisattva mahāsattva trains, and it is for the sake of training in the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions that they train.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the eight liberations, nor train in the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in the emptiness of the eight liberations, and is training in the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor train in the emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness, and is training in the emptiness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
Why is this? Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor train in the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and is training in the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the five eyes, nor train in the emptiness of the six supernormal powers, it is because that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in the emptiness of the five eyes and training in the emptiness of the six supernormal powers.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the Buddha’s ten powers, nor train in the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the Buddha’s ten powers, and is training in the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor train in the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity, it is because that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness and training in the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of all-knowledge, nor train in the emptiness of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of all-knowledge, and is training in the emptiness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor train in the emptiness of all samādhi-doors, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors and training in the emptiness of all samādhi-doors.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. “Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the stream-enterer, nor train in the emptiness of the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat, it is precisely for the sake of training in the emptiness of the stream-enterer, and for the sake of training in the emptiness of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the stream-enterer’s path and the stream-enterer’s fruit, nor in the emptiness of the once-returner’s path and the once-returner’s fruit, the non-returner’s path and the non-returner’s fruit, or the arhat’s path and the arhat’s fruit, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in the emptiness of the stream-enterer’s path and the stream-enterer’s fruit, and is training in the emptiness of the once-returner’s path and the once-returner’s fruit, the non-returner’s path and the non-returner’s fruit, and the arhat’s path and the arhat’s fruit.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha, nor train in the emptiness of the path toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, it is because that bodhisattva mahāsattva is training in the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha and training in the emptiness of the path toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor train in the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and training in the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor train in the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and training in the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the emptiness of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor train in the emptiness of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is indeed training in the emptiness of the śrāvaka vehicle, and is training in the emptiness of the pratyekabuddha vehicle and the unsurpassed vehicle.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of form because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness because there is no duality.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the sense base of the eye because it is non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the sphere of form because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the eye-element because it is without duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, because they are without duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the ear-element because it is without duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, because they are without duality.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the nose element because it is without duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, because they are without duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the tongue element because it is non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the body-element because it is non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the mental element (*manodhātu*), because it is non-dual;

and trains in the emptiness of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the earth element because it is non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering because it is non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of ignorance because it is non-dual;

and trains in the emptiness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the internal as empty because it is non-dual;

and trains in the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—all because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of *tathatā* (suchness), because there is no duality;

if they train in the emptiness of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the perfection of generosity because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the four dhyānas because they are non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the eight liberations because they are non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness because they are non-dual;

and if they train in the emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness because there is no duality.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the five eyes because they are non-dual,
and trains in the emptiness of the six supernormal powers because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the ten powers of a buddha because they are non-dual;

and trains in the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the nature of constant equanimity, because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors because they are non-dual;
and trains in the emptiness of all samādhi-doors because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the stream-enterer because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the stream-enterer’s path and the stream-enterer’s fruit, because they are non-dual;

and if they train in the emptiness of the once-returner’s path and the once-returner’s fruit, the non-returner’s path and the non-returner’s fruit, and the arhat’s path and the arhat’s fruit, because they are non-dual.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the pratyekabuddha, because there is no duality;
and if they train in the emptiness of the one who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, it is because there is no duality;
if they train in the emptiness of a samyaksaṃbuddha, it is because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment because there is no duality.”
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the emptiness of the śrāvaka vehicle because there is no duality;
and trains in the emptiness of the pratyekabuddha vehicle and the unsurpassed vehicle because there is no duality.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the perfection of generosity, and is able to train in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in internal emptiness; they are able to train in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in suchness; they are able to train in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the noble truth of suffering, and is able to train in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this?
Because there is no duality.
“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the four dhyānas, and is able to train in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the eight liberations, and is able to train in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities. Why is this?
Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the four foundations of mindfulness; he is able to train in the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path."
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the gate of liberation of emptiness, and is able to train in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Why is this?
Because they are non-dual. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the five eyes and is able to train in the six supernormal powers."
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the ten powers of a buddha, and is able to train in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the quality of non-forgetfulness and is able to train in the nature of constant equanimity.
Why is this? Because there is no duality.
“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in all-knowledge, and is able to train in the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.”
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in all dhāraṇī-doors and is able to train in all samādhi-doors. Why is this?
Because they are non-dual. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the stage of a stream-enterer, and is able to train in the stages of a once-returner, a non-returner, and an arhat."
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; he is able to train in the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the path of the pratyekabuddha and is able to train toward the fruit of the pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Because there is no duality.
“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the training of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and is able to train in the training of a samyaksaṃbuddha. Why is that?
Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and is able to train in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Because there is no duality. "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, and is able to train in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas and the unsurpassed vehicle. Why is this?
Because there is no duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? Because they are non-dual.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry because there is no duality;

and is able to train in the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship because there is no duality.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can train in the stage of a pratyekabuddha because there is no duality;
and can train in the stage of one heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha because there is no duality.”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in a bodhisattva mahāsattva because there is no duality;
and is able to train in a samyaksaṃbuddha because there is no duality.”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? Because there is no duality.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva because there is no duality;
and is able to train in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment because there is no duality.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? Because there are no two parts.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the vehicle of the śrāvakas because there is no duality;
and is able to train in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas and the unsurpassed vehicle because there is no duality.”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas.
Why is this? Because they are non-dual.

“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, that bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of form, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
Why is this? Because the aggregate of form and the others are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sense-base of the eye, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
Why is this? Because the sense-base of the eye and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the sphere of form, nor does he train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because the sphere of form and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the eye-element, nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the eye-element and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the ear-element, nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the ear-element and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of the increase or decrease of the nose element, nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the nose element and so forth are without duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, that bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the tongue-element, nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the tongue element and so forth have no duality. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the body-element (*kāya-dhātu*), nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavya-dhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāya-vijñāna-dhātu*), body-contact (*kāya-saṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the body-element and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the sphere of mind and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, incalculable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the earth element, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because the earth element and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the noble truth of suffering, nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
Why is this? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth are without duality. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of the increase or decrease of ignorance; nor do they study for the sake of the increase or decrease of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
Why is this? Because ignorance and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, incalculable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing internal emptiness; nor does he train for the sake of increasing or decreasing external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharma emptiness, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Why is this? Because inner emptiness and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing *tathatā* (suchness); nor do they train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because suchness and so forth are without duality. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the perfection of generosity, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity and the others are non-dual. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the four dhyānas, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
Why is this? Because the four dhyānas and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the eight liberations, nor does he train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.
Why is this? Because the eight liberations and so forth are non-dual and without division. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth are non-dual and without division. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the five eyes, nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the six supernormal powers.
Why is this? Because the five eyes and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the ten powers of a Buddha, nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Why is this? Because the ten powers of the Buddha and so forth are non-dual and without division. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor does he train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the nature of constant equanimity.
Why is this? Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth are non-dual and without division. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Why is this? Because all-knowledge is undivided and without duality. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of any dharani-doors, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of any samādhi-doors.
Why is this? Because all dharani-doors, etc., are non-dual and without division. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of a stream-enterer, nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.
Why is this? Because the stream-enterers and others are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship.
Why is this? Because the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, and so forth, are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to train in the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the pratyekabuddha, nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the path toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Because Pratyekabuddhas and others do not possess the two divisions. "Kauśika!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the state of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the state of a samyaksaṃbuddha.
Why is this? Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are equal and without duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? Because for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, the Dharma is equal and without duality. "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to study the immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, and inconceivable pure Buddha-dharmas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor does he study for the sake of increasing or decreasing the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
Why is this? Because the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of form, because there is no duality;
nor does he train for the sake of the increase or decrease of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, because there is no duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the grasping or the destruction of form; nor does he train for the sake of the grasping or the destruction of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because the aggregate of form and the others are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sense base of the eye, because it is non-dual;
nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or the destruction of the sense-base of the eye, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or the destruction of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
Why is this? Because the sense-base of the eye and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sphere of form, because it is non-dual;
nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of grasping at or destroying the sphere of form; nor does he train for the sake of grasping at or destroying the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the eye-element, because it is non-dual;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the eye-element, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition.
Why is this? Because the eye-element and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the ear element, because it is non-dual;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of grasping or destroying the ear element, nor does he train for the sake of grasping or destroying the sound element, up to and including those feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the ear-element and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the nose element, because it is non-dual;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of grasping or destroying the nose element, nor does he train for the sake of grasping or destroying the fragrance element, up to and including those sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the nose-element and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the tongue element, because it is non-dual;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the tongue-element, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the taste-element, up to and including those feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the tongue element and so forth are without duality. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), because it is without duality;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, because they are without duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or the destruction of the body-element, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or the destruction of the touch-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because the body-element and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), because it is non-dual;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the mental faculty element (*manodhātu*), nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition.
Why is this? Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the earth element, because it is without duality;
nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, because they are without duality.

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the earth element, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because the earth element and so forth are not divided into two. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the noble truth of suffering, because there is no duality;
nor for the sake of increasing or decreasing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, because there is no duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of grasping or destroying the noble truth of suffering, nor does he train for the sake of grasping or destroying the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
Why is this? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of ignorance, because it is non-dual;

nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of being grasped by or destroyed by ignorance, nor does he train for the sake of being grasped by or destroyed by anything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
Why is this? Because ignorance and so forth are not divided into two parts. "Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing internal emptiness, because there is no duality;

nor for the sake of increasing or decreasing external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, because there is no duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of being grasped by or destroyed by internal emptiness, nor does he train for the sake of being grasped by or destroyed by external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
Why is this? Because internal emptiness and so forth are without duality. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing true thusness (*tathatā*), because it is without duality;

nor for the sake of increasing or decreasing the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), or the inconceivable realm, because they are without duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of being grasped by or destroyed by suchness; nor does he train for the sake of being grasped by or destroyed by the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because suchness and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the perfection of generosity, because there is no duality;
nor for the sake of increasing or decreasing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, because there is no duality.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the perishing caused by being grasped by the perfection of generosity; nor does he train for the sake of the perishing caused by being grasped by the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity and the others are non-dual. "Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the four dhyānas, because they are non-dual;
nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the four dhyānas, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
Why is this? Because the four dhyānas and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the increase or decrease of the eight liberations, because they are non-dual;
nor for the sake of the increase or decrease of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the eight liberations; nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.
Why is this? Because the eight liberations and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the four foundations of mindfulness, because they are non-dual;

nor for the sake of increasing or decreasing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does he train for the sake of the appropriation or destruction of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path.
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth are non-dual. "Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the gate of liberation of emptiness, because it is non-dual;
nor does he train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of being subsumed by or destroyed through the gate of liberation of emptiness; nor does he train for the sake of being subsumed by or destroyed through the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth are non-dual and without division. "Kauśika!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the five eyes, because they are non-dual;
nor does he train for the sake of increasing or decreasing the six supernormal powers, because they are non-dual.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of the five eyes being grasped or destroyed, nor does he train for the sake of the six supernormal powers being grasped or destroyed. Why is that?
Because the five eyes and so forth are without duality. "Kauśika!
