nor is it apart from the suchness of the ear-element, nor apart from the suchness of the sound-element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the ear-element, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the sound-element, up to and including the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition;

nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the ear-element, nor apart from the suchness of the sound-element, up to and including the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the nose element; it should not be sought within the suchness of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the nose element; nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the odor element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the nose-element, or the suchness of the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; whether it be apart from the suchness of the nose-element, or apart from the suchness of the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)—if one seeks them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the nose element; it is not the suchness of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, nor the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the suchness of the nose element, nor apart from the suchness of the fragrance element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Because all these things are non-existent in nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the nose element, nor the suchness of the odor element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition;

it is not apart from the suchness of the nose element, nor apart from the suchness of the odor element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the tongue-element; it should not be sought within the suchness of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the tongue-element, nor apart from the suchness of the taste-element, up to and including the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*), or the suchness of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; whether it be apart from the suchness of the tongue-element, or apart from the suchness of the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)—if one seeks them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the tongue-element; it is not the suchness of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, nor the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the suchness of the tongue element, nor apart from the suchness of the taste element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because all these are of a nature that is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the tongue element, nor is it the suchness of the taste element, up to and including the suchness of the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

nor is it apart from the suchness of the tongue element, nor is it apart from the suchness of the taste element, up to and including the suchness of the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the tongue element, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the tongue element, nor apart from the suchness of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor should it be sought within the suchness of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as their condition.

It should not be sought apart from the suchness of the body-element, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition.”

Why is this? Whether it be the suchness of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), or the suchness of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-touch as a condition; whether it be the suchness apart from the body-element, or the suchness apart from the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-touch as a condition; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, none are with form nor without form, none are visible nor invisible, none are resistant nor non-resistant; they all share one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor is it the suchness of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the suchness of the body element, nor apart from the suchness of the touch element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Because all these are non-existent by nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the body element, nor the suchness of the contact element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition;

yet it is not apart from the suchness of the body element, nor apart from the suchness of the contact element, up to and including the suchness of the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor should it be sought within the suchness of the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as their condition;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the body-element, nor apart from the suchness of the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor should it be sought within the suchness of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the mind-element, nor apart from the suchness of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), or the suchness of the dharma-element up to the suchness of the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; whether it be apart from the suchness of the mind-element, or apart from the suchness of the dharma-element up to the suchness of the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the seeking of such [things]—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor is it the suchness of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various sensations (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as their condition.

It is not apart from the suchness of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor apart from the suchness of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) up to the suchness of all sensations produced with mental contact as condition. Why is this?
Because all these are non-existent in nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor the suchness of the phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*) up to the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition;
yet it is not separate from the suchness of the mind-element, nor is it separate from the suchness of the phenomena-element up to the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor should it be sought within the suchness of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the suchness of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the mind-element, nor apart from the suchness of the dharma-realm up to the suchness of all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the earth element, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the earth element, nor apart from the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”

Why is this? Whether it be the suchness of the earth element, or the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; whether it be the suchness apart from the earth element, or the suchness apart from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the earth element, nor is it the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
It is not apart from the suchness of the earth element, nor apart from the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements. Why is this?
Because all these are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the suchness of the earth element, nor the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;
it is not apart from the suchness of the earth element, nor apart from the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the earth element, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the earth element, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor apart from the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, or the suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; whether it be the suchness of being free from the noble truth of suffering, or the suchness of being free from the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.
It is not the suchness apart from the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the suchness apart from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. Why is this?
Because all these are non-existent by nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
it is not the suchness apart from the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the suchness apart from the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.

Therefore, the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of ignorance; it should not be sought within the *tathatā* of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of ignorance, nor apart from the *tathatā* of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of ignorance, or the suchness of volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; or whether it be the suchness apart from ignorance, or the suchness apart from volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; or whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these things—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless.
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the suchness of ignorance, nor is it the suchness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
It is not apart from the suchness of ignorance, nor is it apart from the suchness of formative forces up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Why is this?
Because all these are non-existent in nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because all things are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the *tathatā* (suchness) of ignorance, nor the *tathatā* of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair;
nor is it apart from the *tathatā* of ignorance, nor apart from the *tathatā* of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of ignorance, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair;
nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of ignorance, nor apart from the *tathatā* of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of internal emptiness; nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, non-apprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of internal emptiness, nor apart from the *tathatā* of external emptiness, up to the *tathatā* of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of internal emptiness, or the suchness of external emptiness up to the suchness of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; whether it be apart from the suchness of internal emptiness, or apart from the suchness of external emptiness up to the suchness of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the prajñāpāramitā—when seeking them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless.

Why is this so, Kauśika? Because the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of internal emptiness, nor the suchness of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

It is not apart from the suchness of internal emptiness, nor is it apart from the suchness of external emptiness, up to and including the suchness of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because nothing exists and is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the suchness of internal emptiness, nor the suchness of external emptiness, up to and including the suchness of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature;
it is not apart from the suchness of internal emptiness, nor is it apart from the suchness of external emptiness, up to and including the suchness of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of internal emptiness, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of external emptiness, up to and including the *tathatā* of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence;

nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of internal emptiness, nor apart from the *tathatā* of external emptiness, up to and including the *tathatā* of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of *tathatā*; it should not be sought within the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, *avitathatā*, *ananyathābhāvatā*, *samatā*, *anirodhatā*, *dharmaniyāmatā*, *dharmasthititā*, *bhūtakoṭi*, *ākāśadhātu*, or the *acintyadhātu* of *tathatā*.
Nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of *tathatā*, nor apart from the *tathatā* of the *dharmadhātu* up to the *acintyadhātu*.”

Why is this? Whether it be the suchness of suchness, the suchness of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, the suchness of that which is apart from suchness, or the suchness of that which is apart from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of suchness; it is not the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm of suchness.
It is not that *tathatā* is apart from *tathatā*, nor is it that *tathatā* is apart from the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*). Why is this so?
Because all such things are non-existent by nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of suchness, nor is it the suchness of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm;
it is not the suchness apart from suchness, nor is it the suchness apart from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of suchness, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), up to and including the inconceivable realm;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of suchness, nor apart from the suchness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Ninety-Five;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Ninety-Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The First Division, Chapter Twenty-seven, Part Eight: Seeking Prajñāpāramitā. “Kauśika!

The prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the perfection of giving; it should not be sought within the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”

One should not seek it apart from the suchness of the perfection of generosity; one should not seek it apart from the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Why is this? Whether it be the suchness of the perfection of generosity, or the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; whether it be apart from the suchness of the perfection of generosity, or apart from the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom—seeking them in this way, all of these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the perfection of generosity, nor is it the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

It is not apart from the suchness of the perfection of generosity, nor is it apart from the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Why is this? Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and unattainable.

Since they are non-existent and unattainable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the *tathatā* (suchness) of the *dānapāramitā*, nor is it the *tathatā* of the *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, or *prajñāpāramitā*.

It is not apart from the suchness of the perfection of generosity; it is not apart from the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the perfection of generosity; it should not be sought within the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

Nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the perfection of generosity; nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the four dhyānas, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the four dhyānas, nor apart from the *tathatā* of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the four dhyānas, the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, the suchness apart from the four dhyānas, or the suchness apart from the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share one single characteristic, which is called "signlessness" (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor is it the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
It is not apart from the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor apart from the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor is it the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
yet it is not apart from the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor is it apart from the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of the eight liberations; it should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.

Nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the eight liberations; nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the eight liberations, or the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities; whether it be apart from the suchness of the eight liberations, or apart from the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the eight liberations, nor is it the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.

It is not apart from the suchness of the eight liberations, nor is it apart from the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities. Why is this so?
All these are of a nature that is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness (*tathatā*) of the eight liberations, nor is it the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
yet it is not apart from the suchness of the eight liberations, nor is it apart from the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of the eight liberations; it should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases.

Nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the eight liberations; nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the four applications of mindfulness; it should not be sought within the suchness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path.
Nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the four applications of mindfulness, nor apart from the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the suchness of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path; whether it be the suchness apart from the four foundations of mindfulness, or the suchness apart from the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom, or the seeking of these—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness; it is not the suchness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
It is not apart from the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor apart from the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path. Why is this?
Because all these things are non-existent by nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the suchness (tathatā) of the four applications of mindfulness, nor is it the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path;
nor is it apart from the suchness of the four applications of mindfulness, nor is it apart from the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

Therefore, the practice of the perfection of wisdom by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the four applications of mindfulness, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the four applications of mindfulness, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the suchness apart from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the suchness apart from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom—if one seeks these, all are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the emptiness gate of liberation, nor is it the suchness of the signless or wishless gates of liberation.
It is not apart from the suchness of the emptiness liberation door, nor apart from the suchness of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because of the non-existence and unattainability [of all things], the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the *tathatā* (suchness) of the emptiness gate of liberation, nor the *tathatā* of the signless and wishless gates of liberation;
it is not separate from the *tathatā* of the emptiness gate of liberation, nor is it separate from the *tathatā* of the signless and wishless gates of liberation.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the five eyes, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the six supernormal powers;
it should not be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the five eyes, nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the six supernormal powers.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the five eyes, the suchness of the six supernormal powers, the suchness apart from the five eyes, or the suchness apart from the six supernormal powers; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the five eyes, nor is it the suchness of the six supernormal powers;
It is not apart from the suchness of the five eyes, nor is it apart from the suchness of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the five eyes, nor is it the suchness of the six supernormal powers;
yet it is not apart from the suchness of the five eyes, nor is it apart from the suchness of the six supernormal powers.

Therefore, the practice of the *prajñāpāramitā* of a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of the five eyes, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the six supernormal powers;
nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the five eyes, nor apart from the *tathatā* of the six supernormal powers.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the ten powers of a buddha, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the ten powers of a buddha, nor apart from the suchness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

Why is this? Whether it be the *tathatā* (suchness) of the Buddha’s ten powers, or the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; whether it be apart from the *tathatā* of the Buddha’s ten powers, or apart from the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the *prajñāpāramitā*, or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha; it is not the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
It is not apart from the suchness of the Buddha’s ten powers, nor is it apart from the suchness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Why is this so?
All these are of a nature that is non-existent and unobtainable.

Because they are non-existent and unobtainable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the *tathatā* of the Buddha’s ten powers, nor is it the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
yet it is not apart from the *tathatā* of the Buddha’s ten powers, nor is it apart from the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the Buddha’s ten powers, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the Buddha’s ten powers, nor apart from the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

“Kauśika! The practice of the *prajñāpāramitā* of a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the constant abiding in equanimity;
it should not be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the constant abiding in equanimity.”

Why is this? Whether it be the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, the suchness of the state of constant equanimity, the suchness apart from the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the suchness apart from the state of constant equanimity; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share one and the same characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kausika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor is it the suchness of the state of constant equanimity.
It is not apart from the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor is it apart from the suchness of the nature of constant equanimity. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the *tathatā* of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor is it the *tathatā* of constant abiding in equanimity;
yet it is not apart from the *tathatā* of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor is it apart from the *tathatā* of constant abiding in equanimity.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the constant abiding in equanimity;
nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the constant abiding in equanimity.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor should it be sought within the suchness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of all-knowledge, nor apart from the suchness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the suchness of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); whether it be the suchness apart from all-knowledge, or the suchness apart from the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the seeking of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of all-knowledge, nor is it the suchness of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
It is not apart from the suchness of all-knowledge, nor is it apart from the suchness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is not the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor is it the suchness of the knowledge of paths (*mārgajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
yet it is not apart from the suchness of all-knowledge, nor is it apart from the suchness of the knowledge of paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

Therefore, the practice of the perfection of wisdom by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor should it be sought within the suchness of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of all-knowledge, nor apart from the suchness of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought within the suchness of all samādhi-doors;
it should not be sought apart from the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of all samādhi-doors.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of all dharani-doors, the suchness of all samadhi-doors, the suchness apart from all dharani-doors, or the suchness apart from all samadhi-doors; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahasattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the pursuit of these—none of them are associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor without form, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single mark, namely, the markless.
Why is this? Kausika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor is it the suchness of all samādhi-doors.
It is not apart from the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor is it apart from the suchness of all samādhi-doors. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor is it the suchness of all samādhi-doors;
it is not apart from the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor is it apart from the suchness of all samādhi-doors.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought within the suchness of all samādhi-doors;
it should not be sought apart from the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of all samādhi-doors.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor should it be sought within the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor apart from the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of a stream-enterer, the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat; whether it be apart from the suchness of a stream-enterer, or apart from the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat; whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)—if one seeks them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.
It is not apart from the suchness of the stream-enterer, nor apart from the suchness of the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat;
yet it is not apart from the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor apart from the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor should it be sought within the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of a stream-enterer, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness (*tathatā*) of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; it should not be sought within the suchness of the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship.

Nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry, nor apart from the suchness of the stages of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, or the suchness of the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship; whether it be the suchness apart from the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, or the suchness apart from the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless.
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the stream-enterer’s path or the fruit of stream-entry; it is not the suchness of the once-returner’s path or the fruit of once-returning, nor the non-returner’s path or the fruit of non-returning, nor the arhat’s path or the fruit of arhatship.

It is not that the suchness apart from the state of one proceeding toward the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry is [different], nor is it that the suchness apart from the state of one proceeding toward the fruit of once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship is [different]. Why is this so?
All these are of a nature that is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the stream-enterer’s path or fruit, nor is it the suchness of the once-returner’s path up to the arhat’s fruit;
yet it is not apart from the suchness of the stream-enterer’s path or fruit, nor is it apart from the suchness of the once-returner’s path up to the arhat’s fruit.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought in the suchness of the stage of entering the stream (*srotāpatti-pratipannaka*) or the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*); it should not be sought in the suchness of the stage of entering once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmi-pratipannaka*) up to the fruit of arhatship (*arhattva-phala*); nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of a pratyekabuddha, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the state of heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha;
it should not be sought apart from the suchness of a pratyekabuddha, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the state of heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of a pratyekabuddha, or the suchness of one who is training for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, or the suchness apart from a pratyekabuddha, or the suchness apart from one who is training for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha; whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of these things—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, which is to say: the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of a pratyekabuddha, nor is it the suchness of the state of a pratyekabuddha who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.
It is not apart from the suchness of the pratyekabuddha, nor is it apart from the suchness of the one who is training for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because of the non-existence and unattainability [of all things], the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the *tathatā* of a pratyekabuddha nor the *tathatā* of one who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha;
it is not separate from the *tathatā* of a pratyekabuddha, nor is it separate from the *tathatā* of one who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of a pratyekabuddha, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the state of heading toward pratyekabuddhahood or the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of a pratyekabuddha, nor apart from the suchness of the state of heading toward pratyekabuddhahood or the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the suchness of a samyaksaṃbuddha;
it should not be sought apart from the suchness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of a samyaksaṃbuddha.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the *tathatā* (suchness) of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, the *tathatā* of a samyaksaṃbuddha, the *tathatā* apart from a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the *tathatā* apart from a samyaksaṃbuddha; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the *prajñāpāramitā*, or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the suchness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor is it the suchness of the samyaksaṃbuddha.
It is not apart from the *tathatā* of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, nor is it apart from the *tathatā* of the samyaksaṃbuddha. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because of the non-existence and unattainability [of all things], the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the suchness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva nor the suchness of the samyaksaṃbuddha;
yet it is not apart from the suchness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor is it apart from the suchness of the samyaksaṃbuddha.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of a samyaksaṃbuddha;
it should not be sought apart from the *tathatā* of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of a samyaksaṃbuddha.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
it should not be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Why is this? Whether it be the true suchness (*tathatā*) of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the true suchness of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment; whether apart from the true suchness of the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or apart from the true suchness of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the seeking of these—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this so? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the true suchness (tathatā) of the dharma of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor is it the true suchness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
It is not apart from the suchness of the dharmas of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, nor is it apart from the suchness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because all these things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because of non-existence and non-apprehensibility, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the *tathatā* (suchness) of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dharmas, nor the *tathatā* of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
yet it is not apart from the *tathatā* of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dharmas, nor is it apart from the *tathatā* of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dharmas, nor should it be sought within the suchness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dharmas, nor apart from the suchness of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the suchness of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor should it be sought within the suchness of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle;
nor should it be sought apart from the suchness of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor apart from the suchness of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the suchness of the Śrāvaka vehicle, the suchness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle (Anuttarayāna), or the suchness apart from the Śrāvaka vehicle, or the suchness apart from the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle; whether it be the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, or the Prajñāpāramitā, or the seeking of these—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the suchness of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor is it the suchness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
It is not apart from the suchness of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor is it apart from the suchness of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle (Anuttarayāna). Why is this?
Because all these are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the *tathatā* of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor is it the *tathatā* of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle;
yet it is not apart from the *tathatā* of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor is it apart from the *tathatā* of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *tathatā* (suchness) of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor should it be sought within the *tathatā* of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle;
nor should it be sought apart from the *tathatā* of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor apart from the *tathatā* of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of form; it should not be sought within the dharma-nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of form; nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of form, or the dharma-nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; whether it be apart from the dharma-nature of form, or apart from the dharma-nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the prajñā-pāramitā—when seeking them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of form, nor is it the dharma-nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Why is this? Kausika!

Why is this? Kauśika!

The prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the dharma-nature of the sense-base of form, nor is it the dharma-nature of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the eye-element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the eye-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a non-existent nature and cannot be apprehended.

Whether it be the dharma-nature of the ear-element, or the dharma-nature of the sound-element, up to the dharma-nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; or whether it be apart from the dharma-nature of the ear-element, or apart from the dharma-nature of the sound-element, up to the dharma-nature of the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; or whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the prajñāpāramitā—if one seeks them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahasattva is not the dharma-nature of the ear-element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the ear-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. Why is this?

nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the ear-element, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Chapter One: The Search for Prajñāpāramitā, Part Twenty-seven, Section Nine. “Kauśika!

The prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the nose element; it should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”

One should not seek the dharma-nature apart from the nose-element; one should not seek the dharma-nature apart from the fragrance-element, nor even apart from the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. Why is this?

Whether it be the dharma-nature of the nose element, or the dharma-nature of the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; whether it be the dharma-nature apart from the nose element, or the dharma-nature apart from the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the nose element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the nose-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the fragrance-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the nose element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the odor element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition;
