nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the nose element, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the odor element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*), nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the tongue-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*), or the dharma-nature of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; whether it be apart from the dharma-nature of the tongue-element, or apart from the dharma-nature of the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or such seeking—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!

The Prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the tongue-element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the tongue-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharmatā of the tongue-element, nor is it the dharmatā of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

yet it is not apart from the dharmatā of the tongue-element, nor is it apart from the dharmatā of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the tongue-element, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the tongue-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition.

It should not be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the body-element, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the touch-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the body-element (*kāya-dhātu*), or the dharma-nature of the contact-element (*spraṣṭavya-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; whether it be the dharma-nature apart from the body-element, or the dharma-nature apart from the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share one single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this so, Kauśika?

Because the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the body-element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, or the various sensations produced with body-contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the dharmatā of the body-element, nor apart from the dharmatā of the contact-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and unobtainable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the dharma-nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor is it the dharma-nature of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-touch as a condition;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of the body-element, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-touch as a condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the body-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the mind-element (manodhātu), nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), or the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.

Nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the mind-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the dharmatā of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), or the dharmatā of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; whether it be apart from the dharmatā of the mind-element, or apart from the dharmatā of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; or whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)—if one seeks them in this way, all of these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the mind-element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the phenomenon-element, the mind-consciousness-element, or mental contact, nor the dharma-nature of the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.

It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the mind-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a non-existent nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because all things are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharmatā of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor the dharmatā of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), nor even the dharmatā of the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition;

yet it is not apart from the dharmatā of the mind-element, nor apart from the dharmatā of the dharma-element, nor apart from the dharmatā of the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the mind-element, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor should it be sought within the dharma-natures of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor apart from the dharma-natures of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the earth element, or the dharma-nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; whether it be the dharma-nature apart from the earth element, or the dharma-nature apart from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the prajñāpāramitā—when seeking them in this way, all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (*animitta*).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor apart from the dharma-natures of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unattainable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor is it the dharma-nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor should it be sought within the dharma-natures of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the earth element, nor apart from the dharma-natures of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, or the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; whether it be the dharma-nature of being free from the noble truth of suffering, or the dharma-nature of being free from the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, which is to say, the markless.
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because all things are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path;
it is not the dharma-nature apart from the noble truth of suffering, nor is it the dharma-nature apart from the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of ignorance; it should not be sought within the dharma-nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of ignorance, nor apart from the dharma-nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of ignorance, or the dharma-nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; or whether it be the dharma-nature apart from ignorance, or the dharma-nature apart from volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; or whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the prajñā-pāramitā—if one seeks them in such a manner, all of these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kausika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahasattva is not the dharma-nature of ignorance; it is not the dharma-nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of ignorance, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because all things are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the dharma-nature of ignorance, nor the dharma-nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of ignorance, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

Nor should it be sought apart from the *dharmatā* of *tathatā*, nor apart from the *dharmadhātu* up to the *dharmatā* of the inconceivable realm.”

Why is this? Whether it be the *dharmatā* of true thusness (*tathatā*), or the *dharmatā* of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), or the *dharmatā* apart from true thusness, or apart from the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the *prajñāpāramitā*, or the seeking of such things—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (*animitta*).

yet it is not separate from the *dharmatā* of suchness, nor is it separate from the *dharmatā* of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

Why is this? Kausika!

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the perfection of generosity; it should not be sought within the dharma-natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the four dhyānas, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;

Nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the eight liberations, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.”

“Kauśika! Why is this? Kauśika!

Whether it be the dharma-nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness, the dharma-nature of the state of constant equanimity, the dharma-nature apart from the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the dharma-nature apart from the state of constant equanimity; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or such a seeking—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. “Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of all-knowledge; it should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.

Whether it be the dharma-nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the dharma-nature of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), or the dharma-nature apart from all-knowledge, or the dharma-nature apart from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the seeking thereof—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant. The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of all-knowledge, nor is it the dharma-nature of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of all-knowledge, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

it should not be sought apart from the dharmatā of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought apart from the dharmatā of all samādhi-doors.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of all dhāraṇī-doors, the dharma-nature of all samādhi-doors, the dharma-nature apart from all dhāraṇī-doors, the dharma-nature apart from all samādhi-doors, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the prajñāpāramitā—if one seeks them in such a manner, they are all neither associated nor dissociated; neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kausika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the dharma-nature of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor is it the dharma-nature of all samādhi-doors.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of all samādhi-doors. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and unobtainable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the dharma-nature of all *dhāraṇī* gates, nor is it the dharma-nature of all *samādhi* gates;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of all *dhāraṇī* gates, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of all *samādhi* gates.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of all samādhi-doors;
it should not be sought apart from the dharma-nature of all dhāraṇī-doors, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of all samādhi-doors.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*), nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of a once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmin*), a non-returner (*anāgāmin*), or an arhat;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer, nor apart from the dharma-nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer, or the dharma-nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat; whether it be apart from the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer, or apart from the dharma-nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat; whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of one single mark, namely, the markless (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer, nor is it the dharma-nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the stream-enterer, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because all things are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer, nor the dharma-nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of a stream-enterer, nor apart from the dharma-nature of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of stream-enterers, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of once-returners, non-returners, or arhats;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of stream-enterers, nor apart from the dharma-nature of once-returners, non-returners, or arhats.

“Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; it should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship.

Nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the stages of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship; the dharma-nature apart from the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; or the dharma-nature apart from the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship; whether it be the bodhisattva mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the seeking of such things—all are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; it is not the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship.

It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; it is not apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship. Why is this so?
All these are of a nature that is non-existent and unattainable.

Because they are non-existent and unattainable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; it is not the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.

Nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream (*srotāpanna-pratipannaka*) or the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpanna-phala*); it should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmin-pratipannaka*) up to the fruit of arhatship (*arhat-phala*).

Nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.

Chapter One: The Search for Prajñāpāramitā, Part Twenty-seven, Section Ten. “Kauśika!

The prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the pratyekabuddhas, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the factors leading to pratyekabuddhahood or the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood.”

One should not seek the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha apart from it, nor should one seek the dharma-nature of the path toward a pratyekabuddha and the fruit of a pratyekabuddha apart from it. Why is this?

Whether it be the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha, the dharma-nature of the path toward a pratyekabuddha and the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, the dharma-nature apart from a pratyekabuddha, the dharma-nature apart from the path toward a pratyekabuddha and the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, or whether it be a bodhisattva mahāsattva, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or such seeking—all of these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They all share a single characteristic, which is namely "signlessness" (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The practice of the perfection of wisdom by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha, nor the dharma-nature of the path toward or the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the pratyekabuddha, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the one who has entered the path toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is neither the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha nor the dharma-nature of the path leading to the fruit of a pratyekabuddha;
it is neither separate from the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha nor separate from the dharma-nature of the path leading to the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the path of a pratyekabuddha or the fruit of a pratyekabuddha;
it should not be sought apart from the dharma-nature of a pratyekabuddha, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the path of a pratyekabuddha or the fruit of a pratyekabuddha.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the *dharmatā* of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the *dharmatā* of a samyaksaṃbuddha;
it should not be sought apart from the *dharmatā* of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought apart from the *dharmatā* of a samyaksaṃbuddha.”

Why is this so? Whether it be the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, the dharma-nature of a samyaksaṃbuddha, the dharma-nature apart from a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, the dharma-nature apart from a samyaksaṃbuddha, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva himself, or the prajñāpāramitā—if one seeks them in such a manner, all of these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither with form nor without form; neither visible nor invisible; neither resistant nor non-resistant. They are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!
The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva nor the dharma-nature of a samyaksaṃbuddha.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the samyaksaṃbuddha. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and unobtainable.

Because they are non-existent and unapprehendable, the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is neither the dharma-nature of a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva nor the dharma-nature of a Samyaksaṃbuddha;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of a Samyaksaṃbuddha.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of a samyaksaṃbuddha;
it should not be sought apart from the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of a samyaksaṃbuddha.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharmas or the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

It should not be sought apart from the dharmas or the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s dharmas, or the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; whether apart from the dharma-nature of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s dharmas, or apart from the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; whether it be the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, or the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)—if one seeks them in such a manner, all of these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they are all of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the dharma-nature of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s dharmas, nor is it the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
It is not apart from the dharma-nature of the dharmas of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because all such things are of a nature that is non-existent and unapprehendable.

Because nothing exists and nothing can be apprehended, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is neither the dharma-nature of the bodhisattva mahāsattva nor the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharmas or the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharmas or the dharma-nature of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor apart from the dharma-nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! The *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor should it be sought within the nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle;
nor should it be sought apart from the nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor apart from the nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.”

Why is this? Whether it be the dharma-nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle, the dharma-nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the dharma-nature of the Unsurpassed Vehicle; whether it be apart from the dharma-nature of the Śrāvaka vehicle, apart from the dharma-nature of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or apart from the dharma-nature of the Unsurpassed Vehicle; whether it be the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, or the Prajñāpāramitā, or the seeking of such things—all these are neither associated nor dissociated, neither with form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant; they all share a single characteristic, which is to say, the characteristic of signlessness (animitta).
Why is this? Kauśika!

The practice of the perfection of wisdom by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not the dharma-nature of the vehicle of the śrāvakas, nor is it the dharma-nature of the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas or the unsurpassed vehicle.
It is not apart from the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) of the Śrāvaka vehicle; it is not apart from the nature of phenomena of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
Why is this? Because all these are of a non-existent nature and cannot be apprehended.

Because they are non-existent and unattainable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not the dharma-nature of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor is it the dharma-nature of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle;
yet it is not apart from the dharma-nature of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor is it apart from the dharma-nature of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle.

Therefore, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be sought within the dharma-nature of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor should it be sought within the dharma-nature of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle;
nor should it be sought apart from the dharma-nature of the śrāvaka vehicle, nor apart from the dharma-nature of the pratyekabuddha vehicle or the unsurpassed vehicle.
Chapter 28: Praising the Multitude of Virtues, Part One. At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed Subhūti, saying:
"Venerable One!..."
The perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is a great perfection, an immeasurable perfection, and a boundless perfection.
Those who are stream-enterers train in this and attain the fruit of stream-entry;
those who are once-returners train in this and attain the fruit of once-returning;
those who are non-returners train in this and attain the fruit of non-returning.
The various arhats train in this and attain the fruit of arhatship;
the various pratyekabuddhas train in this and attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
the various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this and are able to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Subhūti replied: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said,
Kauśika! The perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is a great perfection, an immeasurable perfection, and an infinite perfection."
Kauśika! Whether in the past, the present, or the future, all those who are stream-enterers train in this and attain the fruit of stream-entry;
all those who are once-returners train in this and attain the fruit of once-returning.
Those who are non-returners train in this and attain the fruit of non-returning;
those who are arhats train in this and attain the fruit of arhatship;
those who are pratyekabuddhas train in this and attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this, they are able to bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Kauśika! Because form is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the past, present, and future limits of the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*) and so forth are all unapprehendable, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the sense base of the eye is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) and so forth cannot be apprehended in their prior, middle, or subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) is great, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the past, present, and future limits of the sense-base of form (*rūpāyatana*) and so forth are all unapprehendable, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the eye-element is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;

because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the beginning, middle, and end of the eye-element (*cakṣur-dhātu*) and so forth are all unapprehendable, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the ear-element is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;

because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the ear-element (*śrotradhātu*) and so forth are unapprehendable in their prior, middle, and subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is great, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;

because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are great, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the past, present, and future limits of the nose-element and so forth are all unapprehendable, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the tongue element is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;

because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the beginning, middle, and end of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) and so forth are all unapprehendable, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;

because the tangible object element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), like all other elements, cannot be apprehended at its prior, middle, or subsequent limits, it is called "great. Because it is great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;

because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as a condition are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*), and so forth, cannot be apprehended in the past, present, or future limits, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the earth element is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the earth element, and so forth, cannot be apprehended in its prior, middle, or subsequent limits, it is called "great. Because it is great, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the noble truth of suffering is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering, and so forth, cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or subsequent limits, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because ignorance is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because ignorance and the other [afflictions] cannot be apprehended at their prior, middle, or subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because internal emptiness is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;

because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the past, present, and future limits of the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) and so forth are all unapprehendable, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because True Suchness (tathatā) is great, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;

because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this so? Because True Suchness (tathatā) and the like are unapprehendable throughout the prior, middle, and subsequent limits, it is called "Great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "Great."
“Kauśika! Because the perfection of giving is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the beginning, middle, and end of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) and the others cannot be apprehended, they are called "great"; and because they are great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the four dhyānas are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the four dhyānas, etc., are unapprehendable throughout their prior, middle, and subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the eight liberations are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the eight liberations and so forth cannot be apprehended at their prior, middle, or posterior limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth cannot be apprehended at their prior, middle, or subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) cannot be apprehended at its prior, middle, or subsequent limits, it is called "great. Because it is great, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the five eyes are great, the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;
because the six supernormal powers are great, the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the five eyes and so forth cannot be apprehended in their prior, middle, or subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this so? Because qualities such as the absence of forgetfulness cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or final limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because omniscience (sarvajñatā) is great, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and so forth cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or subsequent limits, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;
because all samādhi-doors are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the beginning, middle, and end of all dharani-doors and so forth are unapprehendable, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the stream-enterer is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;
because the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this so? Because the stream-enterer and others cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or final limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;

because the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the stages of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself are all unapprehendable in their prior, middle, and subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the pratyekabuddhas are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because the pratyekabuddha who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the Pratyekabuddhas and others cannot be apprehended in the past, present, or future limits, they are said to be "great. Because they are great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas is also said to be great.
“Kauśika! Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great;
because the samyaksaṃbuddha is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”

Why is this? Because the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or subsequent limits, they are called "great. Because of that greatness, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the dharma of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great;
because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the dharma of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva cannot be apprehended at the prior, middle, or subsequent limits, it is called "great. Because of that greatness, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great;
because the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle are great, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also great.”

Why is this? Because the beginning, middle, and end of the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth are all unfindable, it is called "great"; and because it is great, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also called "great."
“Kauśika! For this reason, I say that because form and the other aggregates are great,
the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also great.”
“Kauśika! Because form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.”
Why is that? Because the measure of the aggregate of form and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the aggregate of form and the other aggregates cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the aggregate of form and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the aggregate of form and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the sense base of the eye is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable; [and so on for the other sense bases]."
Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of the sense base of the eye and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the sense-base of the eye and the others cannot have their measure apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the sense-base of the eye and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the sense base of the eye and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the sense base of form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable."
Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable (*apramāṇa*). Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the sense-base of form and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the sense-base of form and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the eye-sphere (*cakṣurāyatana*) is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable."

Because the form realm, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the eye-element and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the eye-element and the other elements cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the eye-element and the other elements are also immeasurable.
Because the eye-element and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the ear-element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable; [and so on for the other elements]."

Because the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the ear-element and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
For example, just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the ear-element and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the ear-element and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the ear-element and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the nose-element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable."

Because the realm of fragrance, the realm of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of the nose-element and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the nose-element and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the nose-element and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the nose element and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the tongue element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable; [and so on for the other elements]."

Because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the tongue element and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the tongue-element and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the tongue-element and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the tongue element and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the body element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable."

Because the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable. Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) and other elements cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the body-element and other elements are also immeasurable.
Because the body-element and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the mind-element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable."

Because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the mental realm (*manodhātu*) and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable. Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the mental element (*manodhātu*) and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the mental element and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the mental constituent (*manodhātu*) and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the earth element (*pṛthivīdhātu*) and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable."
Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the earth element and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
For example, just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the earth element and the other elements cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the earth element and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the earth element and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the noble truth of suffering is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable; [the same applies to the other truths]."
Because the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. Why is this so?
Because the noble truth of suffering and so forth cannot be measured, they are said to be immeasurable. Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be found, so too the noble truth of suffering and so forth cannot be measured.
Kauśika! Because space is immeasurable, the Noble Truth of Suffering and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the Noble Truth of Suffering and the others are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
“Kauśika! Because ignorance is immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.”
Why is this? Because the measure of ignorance and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of ignorance and the other [afflictions] cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, ignorance and the others are also immeasurable.
Because ignorance and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.

"Kauśika! Because internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable; [and so on for the other forms of emptiness]."

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of inner emptiness and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable. Kausika!
For example, just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of internal emptiness and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, internal emptiness and the others are also immeasurable.
Because inner emptiness and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because *tathatā* is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable."

Because the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of suchness and so forth cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of suchness and the other [dharmas] cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, suchness and the others are also immeasurable.
Because suchness and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the perfection of giving is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable; [and so on for the other perfections]."

Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the perfection of generosity and the others cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the perfection of generosity and the other perfections cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the perfection of generosity and the other perfections are also immeasurable.
Because the perfection of giving and the other perfections are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the four dhyānas are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the four dhyānas and so forth cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the four dhyānas and so forth are also immeasurable.
Because the four dhyānas and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the eight liberations are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the eight liberations and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the eight liberations and other such states cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the eight liberations and other such states are also immeasurable.
Because the eight liberations and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the four foundations of mindfulness and the other [perfections] cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the four foundations of mindfulness and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the four applications of mindfulness and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the gate of liberation of emptiness and the others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the gate of liberation of emptiness and the others are also immeasurable.
Because the gateways to liberation, such as emptiness, are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. “Kauśika!
Because the five eyes are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because the six supernormal powers are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of the five eyes and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
For example, just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the five eyes and so forth cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the five eyes and so forth are also immeasurable.
Because the five eyes and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
"Kauśika! Because the ten powers of the Buddha are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable; [and so on for the other qualities]."

Because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be measured by any standard, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the Buddha’s ten powers and other qualities cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the Buddha’s ten powers and other qualities are also immeasurable.
Because the ten powers of the Buddha and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because qualities such as the absence of forgetfulness cannot be measured, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the dharmas such as the absence of forgetfulness cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the dharmas such as the absence of forgetfulness are also immeasurable.
Because the dharmas such as non-forgetfulness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of all-knowledge cannot be apprehended, it is said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of all-knowledge and the like cannot be apprehended.
Kauśika! Because space is immeasurable, all-knowledge and the like are also immeasurable.
Because all-knowledge and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because all dharani-doors are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because all samādhi-doors are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of all dharani-doors and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of all the gateways of dhāraṇī and the like cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, all the gateways of dhāraṇī and the like are also immeasurable.
Because all *dhāraṇī* gates and so forth are immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
*Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 98; *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 99.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One, Chapter Twenty-Eight, Part Two: Praising the Merits of the Assembly. “Kauśika!
Because the stream-enterers are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because the once-returners, non-returners, and arhats are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of those such as the stream-enterers cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kauśika!
