Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of those such as the stream-enterers cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, those such as the stream-enterers are also immeasurable.
Because the stream-enterers and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because those who are candidates for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable."

Because the candidates for the fruit of Once-returner, the fruit of Once-returner, the candidates for the fruit of Non-returner, the fruit of Non-returner, the candidates for the fruit of Arhat, and the fruit of Arhat are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also immeasurable.
Why is this? Because the measure of those who are entering the stream and those who have attained the fruit of the stream-enterer cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the stream-enterer candidate and the fruit of stream-entry, etc., cannot have their measure apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the stream-enterer candidate, the fruit of stream-entry, and so forth, are also immeasurable.

Because the candidates for the fruit of stream-entry and those who have attained the fruit of stream-entry, and so forth, are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the pratyekabuddhas are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because those who are coursing toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of the Pratyekabuddhas and others cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable, Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the Pratyekabuddhas and others cannot be apprehended.
Kausika, because space is immeasurable, the Pratyekabuddhas and others are also immeasurable.
Because the Pratyekabuddhas and others are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. “Kauśika!
Because Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.”
Because the Samyaksaṃbuddha is immeasurable, the Prajñāpāramitā practiced by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also immeasurable. Why is this so?
Because the measure of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and so forth cannot be apprehended, they are said to be immeasurable. Kausika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and so forth cannot be apprehended.
Kauśika! Because space is immeasurable, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also immeasurable.
Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
“Kauśika! Because the dharmas of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment is immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.”
Why is that? Because the dharma of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is immeasurable (*apramāṇa*) since it cannot be apprehended as having any measure;
thus it is called "immeasurable," Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the Dharma of the bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be apprehended.
Kausika! Because space is immeasurable, the Dharma of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise immeasurable.
Because the Dharma of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable;
because the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle are immeasurable, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
Why is that? Because the measure of the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth cannot be apprehended,
it is called "immeasurable," Kauśika!
Just as the measure of space cannot be apprehended, so too the measure of the Śrāvakayāna and other vehicles cannot be apprehended.
Kauśika, because space is immeasurable, the Śrāvakayāna and other vehicles are also immeasurable.
Because the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable. "Kauśika!
For this reason, I say:
because form and so forth are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also immeasurable.
“Kauśika! Because form (*rūpa*) is infinite, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also infinite;
because feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are infinite, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also infinite.”
Why is this? Because the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*) and the others cannot be apprehended either in their middle or at their limits, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the sense base of the eye is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless.”
Why is this? Because the sense-base of the eye, and so forth, cannot be apprehended either as having a middle or an end; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the sphere of form is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless.”
Why is this? Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) and so forth cannot be apprehended either in the middle or at the extremes; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) is boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the form-element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the eye-element and so forth cannot be apprehended as either having a middle or an end; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the ear-element and so forth—whether in the middle or at the extremes—are all unapprehendable; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) and so forth—whether central or peripheral—are all unapprehendable, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the tongue-element and so forth—whether central or peripheral—are all unapprehendable, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the tangible object element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because within the realm of the body (*kāyadhātu*), neither a middle nor an extreme can be apprehended; therefore, it is said to be "boundless.
Because that is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless;

because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as a condition are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the mental realm (*manodhātu*) and so forth cannot be apprehended as either central or peripheral, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the earth element is boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because the earth element, whether in its center or its periphery, is entirely unapprehendable; therefore, it is said to be boundless.
Since that is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the noble truth of suffering is boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering and the others cannot be apprehended either in their middle or at their extremes; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because ignorance is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because ignorance and the other [afflictions] cannot be apprehended either in the middle or at the extremes; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Because they are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because internal emptiness is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because through the emptiness of the internal and so forth, neither middle nor extreme can be apprehended; therefore, it is said to be "boundless.
Since that is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because true suchness (*tathatā*) is boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.

Because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because in suchness and so forth, neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended; therefore, it is said to be "boundless.
Since that is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the perfection of generosity is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;

because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) and the others cannot be apprehended either in their middle or at their extremes; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the four dhyānas are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because the four dhyānas, whether in their middle or at their limits, are all unapprehendable; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the eight liberations are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the eight liberations and so forth—whether in their middle or at their limits—are all unapprehendable;
therefore, they are said to be "boundless. Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth—whether in their middle or at their limits—are all unapprehendable, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because within the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) and the others, neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended;
therefore, it is said to be "boundless. Since that is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the five eyes are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the six supernormal powers are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the five eyes and so forth cannot be apprehended either in their middle or at their limits; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the ten powers of the Buddha and so forth cannot be apprehended either in their middle or at their extremes; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the nature of constant equanimity is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because such qualities as the absence of forgetfulness cannot be apprehended either in the middle or at the extremes; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because omniscience (sarvajñatā) is boundless, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and so forth cannot be apprehended either in their middle or at their limits; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because all dharanī-doors are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because all samādhi-doors are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because all the gateways of dhāraṇī, whether central or peripheral, are unattainable; therefore, they are said to be boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the stream-enterer is infinite, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also infinite;
because the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are infinite, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also infinite.”
Why is this? Because for those such as the stream-enterers (*srotāpanna*), neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;

because the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the candidates for the fruit of stream-entry and those who have attained the fruit of stream-entry, whether in the middle or at the extremes, are all unapprehendable;
therefore, they are said to be "boundless. Because they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the pratyekabuddhas are limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless;
because the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless.”
Why is this? Because for the Pratyekabuddhas and others, neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended; therefore, they are said to be "boundless.
Since they are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva is infinite, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also infinite;
because the samyaksaṃbuddha is infinite, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also infinite.”
Why is this? Because for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others, neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended; therefore, it is said to be "boundless.
Since that is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the dharmas of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this? Because the dharma of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is equal; since neither its middle nor its extremes can be apprehended, it is said to be "boundless.
Because that is boundless, the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! Because the Śrāvaka vehicle is boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless;
because the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle are boundless, the prajñāpāramitā practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
Why is this so? Because within the Śrāvaka vehicle and the others, neither the middle nor the extremes can be apprehended; therefore, it is said to be "boundless.
Since those are boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also said to be boundless.
“Kauśika! For this reason, I say that because form and so forth are boundless,
the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika,
because the object of focus is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless."
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked Subhūti:
"Venerable One,
why is it that because the object of focus is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is also limitless?"
Subhūti replied, “Kauśika!
Because the objective referent of the knowledge of all modes is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika,
because the objective referent of the dharma-realm is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless."
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Subhūti:
"Venerable One,
why is it that because the objective referent of the dharma-realm is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also boundless?"
Subhūti replied, “Kauśika!
Because the dharma-realm is boundless, its objects of focus are also boundless.”
Because the objects of focus are limitless, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is also limitless.
Because the objects of focus within the dharma-realm are limitless, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also limitless.
"Furthermore, Kauśika,
because the object of focus of suchness is limitless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also limitless."
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Subhūti:
"Venerable One,
why is it that because the object of focus of true suchness is boundless, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also boundless?"
Subhūti replied, “Kauśika!
Because true suchness (tathatā) is limitless, its object of focus is also limitless.”
Because the object of focus is boundless, true suchness (tathatā) is also boundless.
Because the object of focus of true suchness is boundless, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva is also boundless.
"Furthermore, Kauśika,
because sentient beings are infinite, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is also infinite."
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Subhūti:
"In what way is it that because sentient beings are infinite, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also infinite?"
Subhūti replied, "Kauśika, what do you think?"
"As for what is called 'sentient beings,' what dharma does the term 'sentient beings' designate as a metaphor?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
"Venerable One!"

Regarding what is called "sentient beings," the term "sentient being" is not a designation for a dharma, nor is it a designation for a non-dharma; rather, it is comprised of adventitious names, comprised of names without a real basis, and comprised of names without an objective referent.
Subhūti spoke again:
"Kauśika, what do you think?"
"In this Prajñāpāramitā, is there also shown to exist a real sentient being?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied, "No!"
"Venerable One!
Subhūti replied, "Kauśika!
Within this Prajñāpāramitā, since no real sentient beings are manifested, it is said to be "boundless," because neither its center nor its limits can be apprehended.
“Kauśika! What do you think?

If all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were to remain for as many eons as there are sands in the Ganges River and speak the names of sentient beings, would there, within that context, be any sentient being who is born or who passes away?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: "No,
Venerable Sir!"
"Why is this? Because all sentient beings are pure by nature, and they have been non-existent from the very beginning.
Subhūti replied:
“Kauśika! For this reason, I say:
because sentient beings are infinite, the perfection of wisdom practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas is also infinite.”

Chapter 29: On Gathering (Saṃgraha-varga), Part One. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the hosts of gods from the Desire Realm; Brahmā, King of the Gods, and the various deities of the Form Realm; as well as Īśāna, the ṛṣis, and celestial maidens—all simultaneously raised their voices three times and proclaimed:
“Excellent!”
Excellent!

Venerable Subhūti, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority and relying upon the Buddha as his support, has well analyzed and revealed for us—the world of devas and humans—the subtle and sublime True Dharma, namely the Prajñāpāramitā.
If there is a bodhisattva who, regarding this Prajñāpāramitā, is able to practice according to what is taught and does not depart from it, we shall honor and serve them as we do the Buddha.

“In this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, no dharma can be apprehended; that is to say, herein no form (*rūpa*) can be apprehended, and no feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*) can be apprehended;
no eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) can be apprehended, and no ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-base (*manas-āyatana*) can be apprehended;
no form-object (*rūpa-āyatana*) can be apprehended, and no sound-, odor-, taste-, touch-, or mental-object-base (*dharma-āyatana*) can be apprehended.”
The eye-element is not to be apprehended; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are not to be apprehended.
The ear-element is not to be apprehended; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are not to be apprehended.

The nose-element is not to be apprehended; the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are not to be apprehended.

The tongue element cannot be apprehended; nor can the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition be apprehended.

The body element cannot be apprehended; nor can the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition be apprehended.

The mind element cannot be apprehended; nor can the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, or the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition be apprehended.
The earth element cannot be apprehended; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements cannot be apprehended;
the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended; the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended;

ignorance cannot be apprehended; and formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cannot be apprehended.

One cannot apprehend internal emptiness; nor can one apprehend external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One cannot apprehend suchness; nor can one apprehend the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.
The perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended;
the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended;
the eight liberations cannot be apprehended; and the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities cannot be apprehended.

The four foundations of mindfulness are not to be apprehended; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are not to be apprehended;
the gate of liberation of emptiness is not to be apprehended; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are not to be apprehended;
the five eyes are not to be apprehended; and the six supernormal powers are not to be apprehended.

The ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended;
the quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be apprehended; the nature of constant abiding in equanimity cannot be apprehended;
omniscience cannot be apprehended; and the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended.
There is no attainment of any dharani-doors; there is no attainment of any samadhi-doors.
There is no attainment of a stream-enterer; there is no attainment of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.

There is no attainment of the path of a stream-enterer or the fruit of a stream-enterer; there is no attainment of the path of a once-returner or the fruit of a once-returner, the path of a non-returner or the fruit of a non-returner, or the path of an arhat or the fruit of an arhat.
There is no pratyekabuddha to be found, nor is there any realization of the fruit of a pratyekabuddha to be found;
there is no bodhisattva mahāsattva to be found, nor is there any samyaksambuddha to be found;
there are no dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva to be found, nor is there any unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to be found.
There is no Śrāvaka vehicle to be found, no Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and no Unsurpassed Vehicle to be found.

Although none of these dharmas can be apprehended, there is nevertheless the provisional establishment of the teachings of the three vehicles, namely: the teaching of the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, and the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the celestial sages and others: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.
Within this profound teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, although no phenomena such as form can be apprehended, there is nonetheless the establishment of the teachings of the three vehicles.

If there is a bodhisattva who, regarding this Prajñāpāramitā, practices as it has been taught by employing the skillful means of non-apprehension and does not depart from it, you celestial beings and seers should honor and serve that bodhisattva just as you would the Tathāgata.
“You should know this!
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the perfection of generosity, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the perfection of generosity.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with internal emptiness, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from internal emptiness;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with suchness, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from suchness;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the Noble Truth of Suffering, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the Noble Truth of Suffering;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the four dhyānas, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the four dhyānas;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the eight liberations, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the eight liberations;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the four foundations of mindfulness, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the four foundations of mindfulness;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the gate of liberation of emptiness;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the five eyes, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the five eyes;
the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the six supernormal powers, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the six supernormal powers.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the ten powers of a Buddha, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the ten powers of a Buddha;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the quality of non-forgetfulness;
the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the nature of constant equanimity, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the nature of constant equanimity.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with omniscience, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from omniscience;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with all dhāraṇī-doors, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from all dhāraṇī-doors;
the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with all samādhi-doors, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from all samādhi-doors.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the stream-enterer, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the stream-enterer;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry; nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship; nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the stage of entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the Pratyekabuddha, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the Pratyekabuddha;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the one practicing for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha, nor can he be apprehended as being separate from the one practicing for the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha.
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical to the samyaksaṃbuddha, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the samyaksaṃbuddha.

The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;

the Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as being identical with unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, nor can the Tathāgata be apprehended as being separate from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Tathāgata cannot be found as identical with the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor can the Tathāgata be found apart from the Śrāvaka vehicle;

the Tathāgata cannot be found as identical with the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle (Anuttarayāna), nor can the Tathāgata be found apart from the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
“O celestial beings!
You should know this:

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, is able to diligently practice and study all dharmas—namely, studying the perfection of generosity, and studying the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;”

They study internal emptiness; they study external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They study suchness; they study the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They study the noble truths.
They train in the four dhyānas; they train in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
they train in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they train in the four foundations of mindfulness, and they train in the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They study the gate of liberation of emptiness, and they study the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they study the five eyes, and they study the six supernormal powers;

they study the ten powers of a Buddha, and they study the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
One trains in the quality of non-forgetfulness; one trains in the constant abiding in equanimity;
one trains in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), one trains in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and one trains in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
one trains in all doors of dhāraṇī and one trains in all doors of samādhi.
One trains in the stage of stream-enterer; one trains in the stages of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat.
One trains in the path toward the fruit of stream-entry; one trains in the path toward the fruit of once-returning; one trains in the path toward the fruit of non-returning;
one trains in the path toward the fruit of arhatship. One trains in the stage of pratyekabuddha; one trains in the path toward the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the state of a samyaksaṃbuddha;
they train in the dharmas of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and they train in unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
they train in the vehicle of the śrāvaka, and they train in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha and the unsurpassed vehicle.

In this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom correctly and never depart from it; therefore, you all should honor and serve that bodhisattva as you would the Tathāgata.
“You should know this!

In the past, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dīpaṃkara appeared in the world, I saw him at the crossroads of the city of Puṣpāvatī. Having scattered five stalks of flowers and spread my hair to cover the mud, I heard the unsurpassed Dharma. Because I took ‘non-apprehension’ as my skillful means, I was able to remain inseparable from the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom.”

He does not depart from inner emptiness, nor from outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

he does not depart from suchness, nor from the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
he does not depart from the noble truths.
They are not separated from the four dhyānas; they are not separated from the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
they are not separated from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;

they are not separated from the four foundations of mindfulness, nor from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
They do not depart from the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they do not depart from the five eyes, nor from the six supernormal powers;

they do not depart from the ten powers of a Buddha, nor from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They are not separate from the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor are they separate from the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they are not separate from all-knowledge, nor are they separate from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
they are not separate from all doors of dhāraṇī, nor are they separate from all doors of samādhi.
Without being separated from any other immeasurable Buddha-dharmas,
at that time Dīpaṃkara Buddha immediately bestowed upon me the prediction of Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi, saying these words:
"O son of good family!..."

In a future age, after one incalculable great eon has passed, within this world during the Bhadrakalpa, you shall become a Buddha, named Śāntamati Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān.
At that time, the celestial beings and sages addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This *prajñāpāramitā* is most rare and extraordinary; it enables the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly grasp the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), by employing the method of non-apprehension.”
That is to say: by means of neither grasping nor rejecting form; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the sense-base of the eye; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the sense-base of forms; and by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.

By means of neither grasping nor rejecting the eye-element; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition;

by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the ear-element; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition;

by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the nose-element; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition.

By means of neither grasping nor rejecting the tongue element; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the body element; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition;

by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the mind element; and by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, and all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.
By means of neither grasping nor rejecting the earth element; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;
by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the noble truth of suffering; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path;

by means of neither grasping nor rejecting ignorance; and by means of neither grasping nor rejecting volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

By means of neither grasping nor rejecting internal emptiness; and by means of neither grasping nor rejecting external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; by means of these as skillful methods.

Because they employ the means of neither grasping nor rejecting true suchness; because they employ the means of neither grasping nor rejecting the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

because they employ the means of neither grasping nor rejecting the perfection of generosity; because they employ the means of neither grasping nor rejecting the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
and because they employ the means of neither grasping nor rejecting the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.

Because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the eight liberations; because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;

because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the four foundations of mindfulness; because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
and because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the gate of liberation of emptiness, as well as the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Because they employ the skillful means of neither grasping nor rejecting the five eyes; because they employ the skillful means of neither grasping nor rejecting the six supernormal powers;

because they employ the skillful means of neither grasping nor rejecting the ten powers of a Buddha; because they employ the skillful means of neither grasping nor rejecting the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

because they employ the skillful means of neither grasping nor rejecting the quality of non-forgetfulness; and because they employ the skillful means of neither grasping nor rejecting the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
By means of neither grasping nor rejecting all-knowledge; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
by means of neither grasping nor rejecting any door of dhāraṇī; by means of neither grasping nor rejecting any door of samādhi;
by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the stage of stream-entry; and by means of neither grasping nor rejecting the stages of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship.
By means of neither grasping nor abandoning the stage of entering the stream (*srotāpatti-pratipannaka*) or the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*);

by means of neither grasping nor abandoning the stage of entering once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmi-pratipannaka*), the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning (*anāgāmi-pratipannaka*), the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship (*arhat-pratipannaka*) or the fruit of arhatship;

by means of neither grasping nor abandoning the state of a pratyekabuddha, nor the stage of entering pratyekabuddhahood or its fruit; by means of neither grasping nor abandoning the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor the samyaksaṃbuddha.

Because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the dharmas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the vehicle of the śrāvakas; and because they employ the method of neither grasping nor rejecting the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas or the supreme vehicle.
