The Second Part of the Twenty-ninth Chapter on Gathering,
Section One. At that time, the World-Honored One, having clearly perceived the fourfold assembly— namely, the bhikṣus,
bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās— as well as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the gods of the Four Great Kings...
The gods of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven,
the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven,
the Brahmakāyika-sabhāgata Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, and the Ābhāsvara-viśuddha Heaven.
The Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven,
the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Puṇyaprasava Heaven, the Anabhraka Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven,
the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven— all assembled together in harmony to provide illumination.
Having realized this,
he then looked toward Śakra, the Lord of Devas, and said: "Kauśika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, or a bhikṣu, a bhikṣuṇī, an upāsaka, or an upāsikā, or any sons of the gods, or daughters of the gods, or any sons of good family, or daughters of good family, do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yogena*), uphold, recite, diligently practice, correctly contemplate, explain to others, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that these individuals cannot be harmed or troubled by any evil Māras or their retinues who find an opportunity [to obstruct them].
Why is this? "Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of form; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. One cannot find an opportunity against emptiness by means of emptiness, nor can one find an opportunity against signlessness by means of signlessness, nor can one find an opportunity against wishlessness by means of wishlessness."

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*) and the others are all empty, and thus neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of affliction can be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the sense-base of the eye; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the sense bases, such as the eye, is empty; thus, the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the sphere of form; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain mastery over emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain mastery over signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain mastery over wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the sense base of form and so forth is entirely empty, for the afflictor, the afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell skillfully in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the eye-element; they dwell skillfully in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-sphere and so forth is entirely empty, and thus the afflictor, the afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the ear-element; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. They cannot find an opportunity through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opportunity through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opportunity through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the ear-element and so forth is entirely empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the nose-element; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and the sensations produced with nose-contact as condition. They cannot find an opportunity for emptiness through emptiness, nor can they find an opportunity for signlessness through signlessness, nor can they find an opportunity for wishlessness through wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the nose element and so forth is entirely empty; for that which causes affliction, that which is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the tongue-element; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the tongue-element and so forth are all empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the body-element; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact, as well as all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to grasp emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to grasp signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to grasp wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the body-element and so forth is entirely empty, for the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction itself cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the mind-element; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the mental faculty (*manodhātu*) and so forth are all empty, and thus neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of affliction can be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the earth element; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements. One cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can one find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can one find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the earth element and so forth is entirely empty, for the afflictor, the afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the Noble Truth of Suffering; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path. They cannot find an opportunity against emptiness by means of emptiness, nor can they find an opportunity against signlessness by means of signlessness, nor can they find an opportunity against wishlessness by means of wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the noble truth of suffering and so forth are empty of intrinsic nature, for the afflictor, the afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell skillfully in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of ignorance; they dwell skillfully in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. One cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can one find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can one find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of ignorance and the rest is entirely empty, for the afflictor, the afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness of the internal, signlessness, and wishlessness; they dwell well in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—all of which are signless and wishless. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to grasp emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to grasp signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to grasp wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness and so forth is entirely empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of *tathatā* (suchness); they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-vyavasthāna*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. They cannot find an opportunity for emptiness by means of emptiness; they cannot find an opportunity for signlessness by means of signlessness; they cannot find an opportunity for wishlessness by means of wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the self-nature of the dharmadhātu and so forth is entirely empty, for neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of causing affliction can be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the perfection of giving; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. One cannot find an opening through emptiness by means of emptiness, nor can one find an opening through signlessness by means of signlessness, nor can one find an opening through wishlessness by means of wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity and the others is entirely empty, and thus neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of affliction can be apprehended.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the four dhyānas; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions. One cannot find an opportunity against them through emptiness, nor can one find an opportunity through signlessness, nor can one find an opportunity through wishlessness.”

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas and so forth is empty, and thus neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of afflicting can be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the eight liberations; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations and so forth is entirely empty, and thus the one who torments, the one who is tormented, and the act of tormenting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the four foundations of mindfulness; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path. They cannot find an opportunity for emptiness through emptiness, nor can they find an opportunity for signlessness through signlessness, nor can they find an opportunity for wishlessness through wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth is empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the gate of liberation of emptiness; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. They cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the gateways to liberation, such as emptiness, is itself empty; for the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the five eyes; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the six supernormal powers. One cannot find an opportunity for emptiness through emptiness, nor can one find an opportunity for signlessness through signlessness, nor can one find an opportunity for wishlessness through wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the five eyes and so forth is entirely empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the Buddha’s ten powers; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. One cannot find an opportunity against emptiness by means of emptiness, nor find an opportunity against signlessness by means of signlessness, nor find an opportunity against wishlessness by means of wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha and so forth are all empty, and thus neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of affliction can be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the quality of non-forgetfulness; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the nature of constant equanimity. One cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can one find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can one find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the self-nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth is empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of all-knowledge; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. One cannot gain an advantage over them through emptiness, nor can one gain an advantage over them through signlessness, nor can one gain an advantage over them through wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the self-nature of all-knowledge and so forth is empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of all *dhāraṇī* gates; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of all *samādhi* gates. They cannot find an opportunity through emptiness to gain an advantage over emptiness, nor can they find an opportunity through signlessness to gain an advantage over signlessness, nor can they find an opportunity through wishlessness to gain an advantage over wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-gates and so forth is empty, for neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of affliction can be apprehended.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the stream-enterer; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat. One cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness; one cannot find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness; one cannot find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.”

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of those such as the stream-enterers is entirely empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of afflicting cannot be apprehended. “Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship. They cannot find an opportunity through emptiness to gain access to emptiness, nor can they find an opportunity through signlessness to gain access to signlessness, nor can they find an opportunity through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of those in the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of the stream-enterer, and so forth, are all empty; for the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the pratyekabuddha; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the pratyekabuddha who is heading toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha. One cannot find an opening through emptiness against emptiness, nor can one find an opening through signlessness against signlessness, nor can one find an opening through wishlessness against wishlessness.”
Why is this? Because the self-nature of the Pratyekabuddhas and others is entirely empty, and thus the afflictor, the afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended. "Kauśika!..."

These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the samyaksaṃbuddhas. One cannot find an opportunity through emptiness to gain an advantage over emptiness, nor can one find an opportunity through signlessness to gain an advantage over signlessness, nor can one find an opportunity through wishlessness to gain an advantage over wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the self-nature of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others is entirely empty, and thus neither the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, nor the act of affliction can be apprehended.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; they dwell well in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. One cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain an advantage over emptiness, nor can one find an opening through signlessness to gain an advantage over signlessness, nor can one find an opening through wishlessness to gain an advantage over wishlessness.”

Why is this? Because for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, the dharmas and their own intrinsic nature are all empty, and thus the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of causing affliction cannot be apprehended.

“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family are well-established in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the Śrāvaka Vehicle; they are well-established in the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle. One cannot find an opening through emptiness to gain access to emptiness; one cannot find an opening through signlessness to gain access to signlessness; one cannot find an opening through wishlessness to gain access to wishlessness.”

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the Śrāvaka vehicle and so forth is entirely empty; thus, the one who causes affliction, the one who is afflicted, and the act of affliction cannot be apprehended.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
These sons and daughters of good family cannot be harmed or disturbed by humans or non-humans who seek an opportunity to do them wrong. Why is this?

Because these sons and daughters of good family, employing the method of non-apprehension, have well-cultivated the minds of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity toward all sentient beings.
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall never be harmed or afflicted by various perilous and evil conditions, nor shall they die an untimely death.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family practice the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) in order to properly nourish and sustain all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

In this great trichiliocosm, among all those belonging to the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, and the Bṛhatphala Heaven, who have already resolved upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—if they have not yet heard, received, upheld, recited, diligently practiced, or correctly contemplated this Prajñāpāramitā—they should now, without departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen with a sincere heart to this Prajñāpāramitā, receive it, uphold it, recite it, diligently practice it, and contemplate it according to the principle.

Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience, and by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method, listen with a sincere heart to this Prajñāpāramitā, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and contemplate it according to the principle—then these good sons and good daughters, whether in an empty house, in a wilderness, on a perilous path, or in a place of danger, shall never feel fear, alarm, or horripilation.

Why is this? It is because these sons and daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they have well cultivated internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*); and because they have well cultivated external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersive emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

At that time, all the devas of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, the Yāma heaven, the Tuṣita heaven, the Nirmāṇarati heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven, the Brahmakāyika heaven, the Brahmapurohita heaven, the Brahmakāyika-sabhāgata heaven, the Mahābrahmā heaven, the Ābhāsvara heaven, the Parīttābha heaven, the Apramāṇābha heaven, the Ābhāsvara-śuddha heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna heaven, the Parīttaśubha heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna heaven, the Bṛhatphala heaven, the Avṛha heaven, the Atapa heaven, the Sudṛśa heaven, the Sudarśana heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha heaven within this trichiliocosm, together addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind set on omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the practice of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), are able to constantly uphold, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, we shall always follow them with respect and protection, ensuring that no calamities or afflictions may harm them.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are themselves bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"World-Honored One!"

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that all sentient beings are caused to forever sever the various perilous and evil destinies, such as those of the hells, animals, hungry ghosts, and asuras.
“World-Honored One!
Because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all devas and humans shall forever be free from all calamities, epidemics, poverty, hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and other such sufferings.”
“World-Honored One!
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the ten paths of wholesome action exist in the world.
World-Honored One!”
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there are in the world the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
"World-Honored One! [they said.]
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the perfection of generosity, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there come to be in the world: internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
“World-Honored One!

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm.”
“World-Honored One!

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin [of Suffering], the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path.
World-Honored One!”

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.”
“World-Honored One!
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the world possesses the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
World-Honored One!”

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
World-Honored One!”

"It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exists in the world all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
World-Honored One!"
"It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world all the gates of dhāraṇī and all the gates of samādhi.
World-Honored One!"

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist in the world great clans of kṣatriyas, great clans of brahmins, great clans of householders, and great clans of lay merchants, as well as various minor kings, universal monarchs (cakravartin), and their attendant ministers and officials.
“World-Honored One!

World-Honored One!”

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the devas, nāgas, asuras, and others: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that all sentient beings are enabled to forever sever [rebirth in] the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, the asuras, and so forth.”
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that all devas and humans are forever freed from all calamities, epidemics, poverty, hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and other such sufferings.”
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the ten paths of wholesome action appear in the world. Kauśika!”
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments appear in the world. "Kauśika!
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases appear in the world.

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the perfection of generosity, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! “Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of its origin, the noble truth of its cessation, and the noble truth of the path appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the gate of liberation of emptiness, as well as the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the five eyes and the six supernormal powers appear in the world. Kauśika!”

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha appear in the world.
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity appear in the world. Kauśika!”

It is because of these bodhisattva mahāsattvas that all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) appear in the world. "Kauśika!..."
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors appear in the world. "Kauśika!

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that great kṣatriya clans, great brahmin clans, great householder clans, and great merchant clans, as well as minor kings, universal monarchs (cakravartin), and their ministers and officials appear in the world.

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, Ābhāsvara, Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Bṛhatphala devas appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the gods of the Sphere of Infinite Space, the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, the Sphere of Nothingness, and the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! “Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that pratyekabuddhas and those who are candidates for the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood appear in the world. Kauśika!”
It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas appear in the world to bring sentient beings to maturity and to adorn and purify buddha-fields. "Kauśika!

It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
“Kauśika! It is because of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus appear in the world. Kauśika!”

For this reason, you—gods, nāgas, asuras, and others—should constantly follow this bodhisattva mahāsattva, making offerings, showing respect, honoring, and praising him, while diligently guarding him so that no calamities or afflictions may harm him.

“Kauśika! If there is anyone who can make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, you should know that this person is making offerings to, revering, respecting, and praising me, as well as all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions. Therefore, all of you—devas, nāgas, asuras, and so forth—should constantly follow this bodhisattva mahāsattva, making offerings to, revering, respecting, and praising them, and diligently providing protection so that no calamities or afflictions may harm them.”

“Kauśika! Suppose Jambudvīpa were entirely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a dense thicket of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them. If some sons or daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all manner of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of pleasure, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them for as long as they live;”

Furthermore, if there were another person who, for even a brief moment, were to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has first resolved their mind upon awakening and does not depart from the six pāramitās, the former merit compared to this mass of merit would not equal even one hundredth part; it would not equal one thousandth part; it would not equal one hundred-thousandth part; it would not equal one koṭi-th part; it would not equal one hundred-koṭi-th part; it would not equal one thousand-koṭi-th part; it would not equal one hundred-thousand-koṭi-th part; nor would it equal any fraction, calculation, reckoning, analogy, or even an upaniṣad-part.

“Kauśika! Suppose Jambudvīpa and Pūrvavideha were entirely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a field of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them. If some sons or daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all kinds of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of pleasure, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them for as long as their lives lasted;”

Furthermore, if there were another person who, for even a brief moment, made offerings to, honored, respected, and praised a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly resolved to attain awakening and does not depart from the six pāramitās, the former mass of merit would not equal even a hundredth part of this accumulation of merit; it would not equal a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor even a *upaniṣad* (fractional) part.

“Kauśika! Suppose Jambudvīpa, Pūrvavideha, and Aparagoyānī were entirely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a grove of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them. If some sons or daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all kinds of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of enjoyment, honoring, respecting, revering, and praising them for as long as their lives lasted;”

Furthermore, if there were another person who, for even a brief moment, were to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly resolved their mind and does not depart from the six pāramitās, the former mass of merit would not equal even a hundredth part of this accumulation of merit; it would not equal a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor even a *upaniṣad* part. It would not equal even a fraction thereof.

“Kauśika! Suppose the entire continent of Jambudvīpa, Pūrvavideha, Aparagodānīya, and Uttarakuru were filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a dense grove of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them. If some sons and daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all kinds of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of pleasure, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them for as long as they lived;”

Furthermore, if there were another person who, for even a brief moment, made offerings to, honored, respected, and praised a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly resolved their mind and does not depart from the six pāramitās—the former merit compared to this mass of merit would not equal one-hundredth part, nor one-thousandth part, nor one-hundred-thousandth part, and so on, up to and including even a fraction of an *upaniṣad*. It would not equal even that.

“Kauśika! Suppose that the four continents were entirely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a field of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space left between them. If some sons or daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all kinds of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of pleasure, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them for as long as their lives lasted;”

Furthermore, if there were another person who, for even a brief moment, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly resolved their mind and does not depart from the six pāramitās, then compared to this mass of merit, the former merit would not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part; it would not even equal a fraction of an *upaniṣad*.

“Kauśika! Suppose a small thousand-world system were completely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a thicket of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space left between them; and suppose there were sons and daughters of good family who, throughout their entire lives, made offerings, paid homage, revered, and praised those fields of merit with immeasurable kinds of supreme and exquisite articles of enjoyment.

If, moreover, there were another person who, for even a brief moment, were to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has first resolved their mind upon awakening and does not depart from the six pāramitās, the former mass of merit would not equal one hundredth part of this accumulation of merit; it would not equal one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part, nor even one *upaniṣad* (fractional) part.

“Kauśika! Suppose the middle thousandfold world system were completely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a grove of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them; and suppose some sons or daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all kinds of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of enjoyment, honoring, respecting, revering, and praising them for as long as their lives lasted.”

Furthermore, if there were another person who, for even a brief moment, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has first resolved upon awakening and does not depart from the six pāramitās, then compared to this mass of merit, the former merit would not equal one-hundredth part, nor one-thousandth part, nor one-hundred-thousandth part, nor even one-ubiniṣatma-part.

“Kauśika! Suppose the world-system of three thousandfold great thousand worlds were entirely filled with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, like a grove of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them; and suppose there were sons and daughters of good family who, throughout their entire lives, honored, venerated, respected, and praised those fields of merit with immeasurable kinds of supreme and exquisite articles of enjoyment.

If, moreover, there were another person who, for even a brief moment, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised a single Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has newly resolved their mind and does not depart from the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), compared to this mass of merit, the former merit would not equal one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part, and so on, up to not even a fraction of an *upaniṣad*.

“Kauśika! Suppose that throughout the infinite and boundless worlds of the ten directions, śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas were as densely packed as a field of sugarcane, reeds, bamboo, rice, hemp, or thickets, with no space between them. If some sons and daughters of good family were to provide those fields of merit with all kinds of immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite articles of enjoyment, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them for as long as their lives lasted;”

Furthermore, if there is another person who, for even a brief moment, makes offerings to, honors, respects, and praises a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly resolved their mind and does not depart from the six pāramitās, the former mass of merit cannot compare to this accumulation of merit; it does not approach even one hundredth part, one thousandth part, or one hundred-thousandth part, nor even an *upaniṣad* (infinitesimal) fraction of it.
Why is this? "Kauśika!

It is not because of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world; [rather, it is because of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that they appear]."
It is solely due to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all tathāgatas, arhats, and samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world.

Therefore, all you gods, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, should constantly protect, make offerings to, revere, respect, honor, and praise these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, so that no calamities or afflictions may ever invade or distress them.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How extraordinary!
How marvelous!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, upholds, recites, diligently studies, reflects upon according to the principle, transcribes, explains, and causes it to be widely disseminated;

they thus acquire such merits in the present life, bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and proceed from one buddha-field to another, drawing near to and serving the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
In accordance with whatever excellent roots of goodness they delight in, through making offerings, showing respect, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, these shall be brought to fulfillment.

From the presence of the Buddhas, they shall hear the true Dharma and, until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never forget the essential points of the Dharma they have heard. They will swiftly be able to acquire the perfection of lineage, the perfection of mother, the perfection of birth, the perfection of retinue, the perfection of the primary and secondary marks, the perfection of radiance, the perfection of the eyes, the perfection of the ears, the perfection of the voice, the perfection of dhāraṇīs, and the perfection of samādhis.

Furthermore, by the power of skillful means, he transforms his body to resemble that of a Buddha and proceeds from one world-system to another, reaching even those buddhaless lands, where he praises and expounds the perfection of generosity; he praises and expounds the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

and he praises and expounds inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They praise and speak of suchness; they praise and speak of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They praise and speak of the noble truth of suffering; they praise and speak of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
They praise and speak of the four dhyānas; they praise and speak of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
They praise and speak of the eight liberations; they praise and speak of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they praise and speak of the four foundations of mindfulness; they praise and speak of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they praise and speak of the gateway of liberation of emptiness; they praise and speak of the gateway of liberation of signlessness and the gateway of liberation of wishlessness.
They praise and speak of the five eyes; they praise and speak of the six supernormal powers;

they praise and speak of the ten powers of a Buddha; they praise and speak of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they praise and speak of the quality of non-forgetfulness; and they praise and speak of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
They praise and speak of all-knowledge; they praise and speak of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
they praise and speak of all doors of dhāraṇī; they praise and speak of all doors of samādhi;
they praise and speak of the Buddha Jewel; and they praise and speak of the Dharma Jewel and the Saṅgha Jewel of Bhikṣus.

Furthermore, by the power of skillful means, he proclaims the essential teachings of the Dharma for all sentient beings, establishing them within the vehicles of the Threefold Vehicle according to their needs, so that they may forever be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, and death, and realize the realm of nirvana without remainder;
or else, he rescues them from the sufferings of the evil realms, causing them to experience various joys among gods and humans.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 103. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 113.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One! [The third part of the twenty-ninth chapter, ‘The Section on Appropriation’].”

The perfection of wisdom is exceedingly rare. If one embraces the perfection of wisdom, then one embraces the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

If one embraces the perfection of wisdom, then one embraces internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

If one embraces the *prajñāpāramitā*, one embraces suchness (*tathatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the sphere of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm;
if one embraces the *prajñāpāramitā*, one embraces the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin, the noble truth of cessation, and the noble truth of the path;
if one embraces the *prajñāpāramitā*, one embraces the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.

If one embraces the *prajñāpāramitā*, one thereby embraces the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*).

If one embraces the *prajñāpāramitā*, one thereby embraces the four foundations of mindfulness (*catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni*), the four right efforts (*catvāri samyakprahāṇāni*), the four bases of psychic power (*catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ*), the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*), the five powers (*pañca balāni*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*saptabodhyaṅgāni*), and the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*).

If one embraces the *prajñāpāramitā*, one thereby embraces the gateway of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatāvimokṣamukha*), the gateway of liberation of signlessness (*animittavimokṣamukha*), and the gateway of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihitavimokṣamukha*).
If one embraces the Prajñāpāramitā, one embraces the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

if one embraces the Prajñāpāramitā, one embraces the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one embraces the Prajñāpāramitā, one embraces the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity.
If one embraces the perfection of wisdom, then one embraces all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;
if one embraces the perfection of wisdom, then one embraces all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;
if one embraces the perfection of wisdom, then one embraces the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.
If one embraces the perfection of wisdom, one embraces the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
if one embraces the perfection of wisdom, one embraces the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
if one embraces the perfection of wisdom, one embraces unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"If one embraces the perfection of wisdom, then one embraces all mundane and supramundane wholesome dharmas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: "So it is!"
So it is! It is just as you have said.

The perfection of wisdom is most rare; if one can embrace the perfection of wisdom, then one can embrace the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace suchness (*tathatā*), the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm;

if one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering], the noble truth of cessation, and the noble truth of the path;

if one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*).

If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*).

If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the four foundations of mindfulness (*catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni*), the four right efforts (*catvāri samyakprahāṇāni*), the four bases of psychic power (*catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ*), the five faculties (*pañcendriyāṇi*), the five powers (*pañca balāni*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*saptabodhyaṅgāni*), and the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*).

If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the gateway of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gateway of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gateway of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*).
If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

if one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity.
If one can embrace the perfection of wisdom, then one can embrace all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
if one can embrace the perfection of wisdom, then one can embrace all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors;
if one can embrace the perfection of wisdom, then one can embrace the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.
If one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
if one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of a bodhisattva;
if one is able to embrace the *prajñāpāramitā*, then one is able to embrace unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
If one is able to embrace the Prajñāpāramitā, then one is able to embrace all mundane and supramundane wholesome dharmas.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family should uphold, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this *prajñāpāramitā*, these sons and daughters of good family will attain the meritorious benefits and supreme advantages in both their present life and future lives.
"You should listen attentively and apply your mind with great care; I shall analyze and explain it for you.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
"Indeed! I shall do so."
"O Great Sage!
We pray that you will explain this for us at this time; we long to hear it.
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are various non-Buddhist brahmins, or evil Māras and their retinues, or others who are violent, cruel, and arrogant, who wish to create enmity, insult, or harm toward this bodhisattva mahāsattva, as soon as they give rise to such thoughts, they will swiftly encounter calamity and misfortune; they shall naturally be extinguished and fail to achieve their desires.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes, employing non-apprehension as the means, has for a long night practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, taking great compassion and vows as their primary guide.

If sentient beings, out of stinginess and greed, engage in strife for a long night, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*).

If sentient beings violate the precepts for a long night, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*).

If sentient beings harbor anger and resentment for a long night, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).

If sentient beings have long been indolent, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*);

if sentient beings have long had distracted minds, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*);

if sentient beings have long been ignorant, this bodhisattva mahāsattva relinquishes all internal and external phenomena and employs skillful means to establish them in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
If there are sentient beings who wander through birth and death, constantly disturbed throughout the long night by the afflictions and impurities of the latent tendencies of greed,
hatred, and delusion, this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able, through various skillful means,
to cause them to sever and extinguish these [afflictions] so that they may forever leave birth and death, or to establish them so that they abide in internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā).
External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness,
conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness,
essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, and the [emptiness of] the unapprehendable...
They attain emptiness, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
or they establish those [beings] so that they abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusoriness, immutability, equality,
the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, and the void.

Whether it be the element of space or the inconceivable realm, one may establish them so that they abide in the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin, the noble truth of cessation, or the noble truth of the path;

or one may establish them so that they abide in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments; or one may establish them so that they abide in the eight liberations, the eight... [liberation-spheres].

The bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), or establishing them so that they abide in the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*),

the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), the five faculties (*indriya*), the five powers (*bala*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*),
or establishing them so that they abide in the gateway of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatāvimokṣamukha*) and the gateway of liberation of signlessness (*animittavimokṣamukha*).
The door of liberation, and the door of liberation through wishlessness; or establishing them so they may abide in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

or establishing them so they may abide in the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Or they establish them so that they dwell in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;
or they establish them so that they dwell in all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;
or they establish them so that they dwell in all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi; or they establish them...
They cause them to abide in the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship;
or they establish them so that they abide in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; or they establish them so that they abide in the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
or they establish them so that they abide in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; or they establish them so that they abide in...

“Kauśika! These are called the benefits and merits in this present life obtained by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who upholds, recites, diligently practices, reflects upon according to the principle, transcribes, explains, and disseminates the *prajñāpāramitā*, including all mundane and supramundane wholesome dharmas.”

“Kauśika! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva upholds, recites, diligently practices, correctly contemplates, transcribes, explains, and widely disseminates this perfection of wisdom, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in a future life. They will turn the sublime wheel of Dharma and deliver immeasurable multitudes, establishing sentient beings according to their original vows, causing them to reach the ultimate in the training of the three vehicles, even unto the realization of nirvana without remainder.”

Kauśika! These are called the subsequent dharma merits and benefits obtained by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who upholds, recites, diligently practices, reflects upon according to the principle, transcribes, explains, and disseminates the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If sons and daughters of good family receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, then in that place, whether there be evil Māras and their retinues, or various non-Buddhist brahmins, or other violent and arrogant individuals who, out of envy for the Prajñāpāramitā, wish to create obstacles, rebuke, oppose, or cause it to quickly disappear—they shall ultimately be unable to succeed."

Because they have briefly heard the sound of the Prajñāpāramitā, their manifold evils gradually perish and their merits gradually arise; subsequently, by relying on the Three Vehicles, they shall reach the end of suffering. Kausika!

Suppose there is a wondrous medicine called Makī; by its majestic power, it can neutralize all poisons. If a great venomous snake, famished and wandering in search of food, should encounter a living being and wish to bite and devour it, that creature, terrified of death, flees to seek refuge in the wondrous medicine. Upon smelling the scent of the medicine, the snake immediately retreats and runs away.
Why is this? Kausika!
It is because this moxibustion herb possesses great power; it is able to subdue all poisons and benefit one's physical life.
One should know that the Prajñāpāramitā possesses great power in this very same way.

If sons or daughters of good family receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the truth, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate it, then whatever evil deeds the Māras and their like intend to commit against these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas shall, by the majestic spiritual power of this Prajñāpāramitā, be naturally extinguished in that very place.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because this Prajñā possesses great majestic power, being able to destroy unwholesome dharmas and increase all manner of wholesome qualities.
“Kauśika! How is it that the perfection of wisdom can extinguish unwholesome dharmas and increase all wholesome ones? Kauśika!”
In this way, the Perfection of Wisdom can extinguish greed, hatred, and delusion, and increase their respective antidotes. "Kauśika!..."

In this way, the perfection of wisdom can extinguish ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—this entire great mass of suffering—and it increases their antidotes.
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all hindrances, obscurations, latent tendencies, entanglements, stains, fetters, and bonds, and it increases their respective antidotes.”

“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the view of a self, the view of a sentient being, the view of a life-principle, the view of a living soul, the view of a nourisher, the view of a person, the view of a pudgala, the view of a mind-born being, the view of a youth, the view of an agent, the view of an experiencer, the view of a knower, and the view of a seer; it increases their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all views of eternalism, nihilism, existence, non-existence, and even the various other evil views, while increasing their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all stinginess, greed, violation of precepts, anger, indolence, distraction, and delusion, while increasing their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all notions of permanence, pleasure, self, and purity, and increase their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all tendencies toward greed, hatred, delusion, pride, and doubt-and-view, while increasing their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping at form and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish the grasping at feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! In this way, the perfection of wisdom can extinguish the grasping at the sense base of the eye and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish the grasping at the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and increase their antidotes.”
It can extinguish grasping at the sense base of form and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish grasping at the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and increase their antidotes.
“Kauśika! In this way, the perfection of wisdom can eliminate the grasping of the eye-element and increase its antidote;
it can eliminate the grasping of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and increase their antidotes.”
One is able to extinguish grasping at the ear element and increase its antidote;
one is able to extinguish grasping at the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and increase their antidotes;
one is able to extinguish grasping at the nose element and increase its antidote.

One is able to extinguish the grasping toward the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, thereby increasing their antidotes;
one is able to extinguish the grasping toward the tongue element, thereby increasing its antidote;

one is able to extinguish the grasping toward the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, thereby increasing their antidotes.
One is able to extinguish the grasping of the body-element and increase its antidote;

one is able to extinguish the grasping of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and increase their antidotes;
one is able to extinguish the grasping of the mind-element and increase its antidote.

One is able to extinguish the grasping at the dharma-element, the consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, thereby increasing their antidotes. "Kauśika!..."
In this way, the perfection of wisdom can extinguish grasping at the earth element and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish grasping at the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, and increase their antidotes.
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can eliminate grasping at the noble truth of suffering and increase its antidote;
it can eliminate grasping at the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and increase their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish the grasping of ignorance and increase its antidote;

it is able to extinguish the grasping of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping at internal emptiness and increase its antidote;

it can extinguish the grasping at external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, while increasing their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! In this way, the perfection of wisdom can eliminate the grasping at suchness and increase its antidote;

it can eliminate the grasping at the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), and increase their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish the grasping at the dānapāramitā and increase its antidote;
it is able to extinguish the grasping at the śīla-, kṣānti-, vīrya-, dhyāna-, and prajñāpāramitās and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping at the four dhyānas and increase their antidotes;
it can extinguish the grasping at the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can eliminate the grasping at the eight liberations and increase their antidotes;
it can eliminate the grasping at the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! In this way, the perfection of wisdom can eliminate the grasping at the four foundations of mindfulness and increase their respective antidotes;

it can eliminate the grasping at the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and increase their respective antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can eliminate the grasping at the liberation door of emptiness and increase its antidote;
it can eliminate the grasping at the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! In this way, the Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping of the five eyes and increase their respective antidotes;
it can extinguish the grasping of the six supernormal powers and increase their respective antidotes.”

“Kauśika!
