In this way, the perfection of wisdom can eliminate the grasping at the ten powers of a Buddha and increase their antidotes; it can eliminate the grasping at the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! In this way, the perfection of wisdom can eliminate the grasping at the quality of non-forgetfulness and increase its antidote;
it can eliminate the grasping at the nature of constant equanimity and increase its antidote.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish all grasping at omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and increase its antidote;
it is able to extinguish grasping at the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish all grasping at the gateways of dhāraṇīs and increase their respective remedies;
it can extinguish all grasping at the gateways of samādhis and increase their respective remedies.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping of stream-enterers and increase their antidotes;
it can extinguish the grasping of once-returners, non-returners, and arhats, and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping for the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, and increase their respective remedies;

it can extinguish the grasping for the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship, and increase their respective remedies.”
“Kauśika! Thus, this prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping of a pratyekabuddha and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish the grasping of one who is progressing toward the fruit of a pratyekabuddha and increase its antidote.”
“Kauśika! This prajñāpāramitā can extinguish the grasping of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish the grasping of the samyaksaṃbuddhas and increase its antidote.”
“Kauśika! In this way, the perfection of wisdom can extinguish the grasping at phenomena by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and increase its antidote;
it can extinguish the grasping at unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening and increase its antidote.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is able to extinguish the grasping of the Śrāvaka vehicle and increase its antidote;
it is able to extinguish the grasping of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Unsurpassed Vehicle (Anuttarayāna) and increase their antidotes.”
“Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā, even unto its capacity to extinguish the grasping for parinirvāṇa, increases its antidote. Kauśika!”

Thus, this Prajñāpāramitā can extinguish all dharmas in which Māras abide and can cause all wholesome matters to grow; for this reason, the Prajñāpāramitā possesses immeasurable and great majestic spiritual power.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
If good sons and good daughters, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold,
read and recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, and write down this Prajñāpāramitā..."

Those who write it down, explain it, and cause it to circulate widely—these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are constantly attended by the four great kings of the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system, as well as Śakra, Lord of the Devas; Mahābrahmā, Lord of the Sahā World;
the Ābhāsvara devas; the Śubhakṛtsna devas; the Bṛhatphala devas; and the Śuddhāvāsa devas, and so forth.

All benevolent deities will collectively protect them, ensuring that no calamities or afflictions may invade or distress them; whatever they seek in accordance with the Dharma shall be fully realized.

Furthermore, the Buddhas currently residing throughout the worlds of the ten directions will also constantly guard and mind such Bodhisattvas, causing unwholesome dharmas to be extinguished and wholesome dharmas to increase.

That is to say, they cause the perfection of generosity to increase without diminishing, and they cause the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom to increase without diminishing.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.

They cause internal emptiness to increase without diminution; they cause external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence to increase without diminution.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.

They cause true thusness (*tathatā*) to increase and prevent it from diminishing; they cause the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) to increase and prevent them from diminishing.
Why is this? Because they take non-attainment as their skillful means.
They cause the Noble Truth of Suffering to increase without diminution, and they cause the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path to increase without diminution.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.
They increase the four dhyānas so that they do not diminish, and they increase the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments so that they do not diminish.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.

They increase the eight liberations so that they do not diminish, and they increase the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases so that they do not diminish.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.

They cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness so that they do not diminish; they cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path so that they do not diminish.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.
They cause the gate of liberation of emptiness to increase without diminution, and they cause the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness to increase without diminution.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.
They cause the five eyes to increase without diminution, and they cause the six supernormal powers to increase without diminution.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.

They cause the ten powers of a Buddha to increase without diminution, and they cause the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha to increase without diminution.
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.
They increase the quality of being free from forgetfulness so that it does not diminish, and they increase the quality of constant abiding in equanimity so that it does not diminish.
Why is this? Because they employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*).

"They cause all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) to increase without diminution, and they cause the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) to increase without diminution."
Why is this? Because they take non-apprehension as their skillful means.
They cause all doors of dhāraṇī to increase without diminution, and they cause all doors of samādhi to increase without diminution.
Why is this? Because it takes non-apprehension as its skillful means. "Kauśika!..."

When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva speaks, his words are majestic and solemn, and all who hear them receive them with reverence. His discourse is measured and his speech free from confusion; he deeply understands kindness and righteousness and steadfastly serves virtuous friends. He is not obscured by stinginess, envy, anger, resentment, concealment, vexation, flattery, deception, or hypocrisy.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva-mahāsattva personally abstains from taking life, teaches others to abstain from taking life, speaks in praise of the dharma of abstaining from taking life, and joyfully extols those who abstain from taking life;

he personally abstains from taking what is not given, teaches others to abstain from taking what is not given, speaks in praise of the dharma of abstaining from taking what is not given, and joyfully extols those who abstain from taking what is not given.

He himself abstains from sexual misconduct, teaches others to abstain from sexual misconduct, speaks in praise of the practice of abstaining from sexual misconduct, and joyfully commends those who abstain from it;
he himself abstains from false speech, teaches others to abstain from false speech, speaks in praise of the practice of abstaining from false speech, and joyfully commends those who abstain from it;

he himself abstains from divisive speech, teaches others to abstain from divisive speech, speaks in praise of the practice of abstaining from divisive speech, and joyfully commends those who abstain from it.

He himself abstains from harsh speech, teaches others to abstain from harsh speech, speaks in praise of the practice of abstaining from harsh speech, and joyfully commends those who abstain from harsh speech;

he himself abstains from frivolous chatter, teaches others to abstain from frivolous chatter, speaks in praise of the practice of abstaining from frivolous chatter, and joyfully commends those who abstain from frivolous chatter;

he himself abstains from covetousness, teaches others to abstain from covetousness, speaks in praise of the practice of abstaining from covetousness, and joyfully commends those who abstain from covetousness.
One personally abandons ill will and teaches others to abandon ill will; one praises the teaching on abandoning ill will and joyfully extols those who have abandoned ill will.
One personally abandons wrong views and teaches others to abandon wrong views; one praises the teaching on abandoning wrong views and joyfully extols those who have abandoned wrong views.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally practices the perfection of generosity, teaches others to practice the perfection of generosity, speaks in praise of the dharma of the perfection of generosity, and joyfully extols those who practice the perfection of generosity;

he personally practices the perfection of ethical discipline, teaches others to practice the perfection of ethical discipline, speaks in praise of the dharma of the perfection of ethical discipline, and joyfully extols those who practice the perfection of ethical discipline.”

They personally practice the perfection of patience, teach others to practice the perfection of patience, speak in praise of the dharma of the perfection of patience, and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of patience;

they personally practice the perfection of diligence, teach others to practice the perfection of diligence, speak in praise of the dharma of the perfection of diligence, and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of diligence;

they personally practice the perfection of meditative concentration, teach others to practice the perfection of meditative concentration, speak in praise of the dharma of the perfection of meditative concentration, and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

They practice the perfection of wisdom themselves, teach others to practice the perfection of wisdom, speak in praise of the dharma of the perfection of wisdom, and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva himself dwells in internal emptiness, teaches others to dwell in internal emptiness, praises and speaks of the dharma of internal emptiness, and joyfully lauds those who dwell in internal emptiness;

he himself dwells in external emptiness, teaches others to dwell in external emptiness, praises and speaks of the dharma of external emptiness, and joyfully lauds those who dwell in external emptiness.”

They themselves abide in internal and external emptiness, teach others to abide in internal and external emptiness, praise and speak of the dharma of internal and external emptiness, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in internal and external emptiness;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of emptiness, teach others to abide in the emptiness of emptiness, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of emptiness, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in the emptiness of emptiness;
they themselves abide in great emptiness, teach others to abide in great emptiness, praise and speak of the dharma of great emptiness, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in great emptiness.

They themselves abide in the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, teach others to abide in the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in the emptiness of the ultimate meaning;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of the conditioned, teach others to abide in the emptiness of the conditioned, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of the conditioned, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in the emptiness of the conditioned;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of the unconditioned, teach others to abide in the emptiness of the unconditioned, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of the unconditioned, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in the emptiness of the unconditioned.

They themselves abide in ultimate emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), teach others to abide in ultimate emptiness, praise and speak of the dharma of ultimate emptiness, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in ultimate emptiness;

they themselves abide in boundless emptiness (*anavaraṇa-śūnyatā*), teach others to abide in boundless emptiness, praise and speak of the dharma of boundless emptiness, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in boundless emptiness;

they themselves abide in dispersed emptiness (*vibhava-śūnyatā*), teach others to abide in dispersed emptiness, praise and speak of the dharma of dispersed emptiness, and rejoice in and extol those who abide in dispersed emptiness.

They themselves abide in the emptiness of non-alteration, teach others to abide in the emptiness of non-alteration, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of non-alteration, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of non-alteration;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of essential nature, teach others to abide in the emptiness of essential nature, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of essential nature, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of essential nature;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of self-characteristic, teach others to abide in the emptiness of self-characteristic, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of self-characteristic, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of self-characteristic.

They themselves abide in the emptiness of common characteristics, teach others to abide in the emptiness of common characteristics, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of common characteristics, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of common characteristics;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of all dharmas, teach others to abide in the emptiness of all dharmas, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of all dharmas, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of all dharmas;

they themselves abide in the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, teach others to abide in the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of non-apprehensibility.

They themselves abide in the emptiness of non-existence and teach others to abide in the emptiness of non-existence; they praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of non-existence, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of non-existence.

They themselves abide in the emptiness of self-nature and teach others to abide in the emptiness of self-nature; they praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of self-nature, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of self-nature.

They themselves abide in the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence and teach others to abide in the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence; they praise and speak of the dharma of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence, and joyfully extol those who abide in the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva abides himself in suchness (*tathatā*), teaches others to abide in suchness, speaks in praise of the dharma of suchness, and joyfully extols those who abide in suchness;

he abides himself in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), teaches others to abide in the realm of phenomena, speaks in praise of the dharma of the realm of phenomena, and joyfully extols those who abide in the realm of phenomena.”

Abiding personally in the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), they teach others to abide in the nature of phenomena, praise the teaching of the nature of phenomena, and joyfully extol those who abide in the nature of phenomena;

abiding personally in the nature of non-falsity, they teach others to abide in the nature of non-falsity, praise the teaching of the nature of non-falsity, and joyfully extol those who abide in the nature of non-falsity;

abiding personally in the nature of immutability, they teach others to abide in the nature of immutability, praise the teaching of the nature of immutability, and joyfully extol those who abide in the nature of immutability.

One abides in the nature of equality oneself, teaches others to abide in the nature of equality, speaks in praise of the dharma of the nature of equality, and joyfully extols those who abide in the nature of equality;

one abides in the nature of freedom from birth oneself, teaches others to abide in the nature of freedom from birth, speaks in praise of the dharma of the nature of freedom from birth, and joyfully extols those who abide in the nature of freedom from birth;

one abides in the fixed nature of phenomena oneself, teaches others to abide in the fixed nature of phenomena, speaks in praise of the dharma of the fixed nature of phenomena, and joyfully extols those who abide in the fixed nature of phenomena.

They themselves abide in the abiding of the Dharma and teach others to abide in the abiding of the Dharma; they praise and speak of the Dharma of abiding in the Dharma, and they rejoice in and extol those who abide in the abiding of the Dharma.

They themselves abide in the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) and teach others to abide in the reality-limit; they praise and speak of the Dharma of the reality-limit, and they rejoice in and extol those who abide in the reality-limit.

They themselves abide in the realm of empty space and teach others to abide in the realm of empty space; they praise and speak of the Dharma of the realm of empty space, and they rejoice in and extol those who abide in the realm of empty space.

Abiding oneself in the inconceivable realm, teaching others to abide in the inconceivable realm, praising and explaining the Dharma of the inconceivable realm, and joyfully extolling those who abide in the inconceivable realm.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva abides himself in the noble truth of suffering, teaches others to abide in the noble truth of suffering, speaks in praise of the dharma of the noble truth of suffering, and joyfully extols those who abide in the noble truth of suffering;

he abides himself in the noble truth of the origin [of suffering], teaches others to abide in the noble truth of the origin, speaks in praise of the dharma of the noble truth of the origin, and joyfully extols those who abide in the noble truth of the origin.”

One abides oneself in the noble truth of cessation, teaches others to abide in the noble truth of cessation, speaks in praise of the Dharma of the noble truth of cessation, and joyfully commends those who abide in the noble truth of cessation;

one abides oneself in the noble truth of the path, teaches others to abide in the noble truth of the path, speaks in praise of the Dharma of the noble truth of the path, and joyfully commends those who abide in the noble truth of the path.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the first dhyāna, teaches others to cultivate the first dhyāna, speaks in praise of the dharma of the first dhyāna, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the first dhyāna;

he personally cultivates the second dhyāna, teaches others to cultivate the second dhyāna, speaks in praise of the dharma of the second dhyāna, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the second dhyāna.”
They personally cultivate the third dhyāna, teach others to cultivate the third dhyāna, speak in praise of the qualities of the third dhyāna, and joyfully extol those who cultivate the third dhyāna;

they personally cultivate the fourth dhyāna, teach others to cultivate the fourth dhyāna, speak in praise of the qualities of the fourth dhyāna, and joyfully extol those who cultivate the fourth dhyāna.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates immeasurable loving-kindness (*maitrī*), teaches others to cultivate immeasurable loving-kindness, speaks in praise of the dharma of immeasurable loving-kindness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate immeasurable loving-kindness;

he personally cultivates immeasurable compassion (*karuṇā*), teaches others to cultivate immeasurable compassion, speaks in praise of the dharma of immeasurable compassion, and joyfully extols those who cultivate immeasurable compassion.”

One personally cultivates immeasurable loving-kindness, teaches others to cultivate immeasurable loving-kindness, speaks in praise of the dharma of immeasurable loving-kindness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate immeasurable loving-kindness;

one personally cultivates immeasurable equanimity, teaches others to cultivate immeasurable equanimity, speaks in praise of the dharma of immeasurable equanimity, and joyfully extols those who cultivate immeasurable equanimity.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the concentration of the sphere of infinite space, teaches others to cultivate the concentration of the sphere of infinite space, speaks in praise of the dharma of the concentration of the sphere of infinite space, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the concentration of the sphere of infinite space;

he personally cultivates the concentration of the sphere of infinite consciousness, teaches others to cultivate the concentration of the sphere of infinite consciousness, speaks in praise of the dharma of the concentration of the sphere of infinite consciousness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the concentration of the sphere of infinite consciousness.”

One personally cultivates the meditative absorption of the sphere of nothingness, teaches others to cultivate the meditative absorption of the sphere of nothingness, speaks in praise of the dharma of the meditative absorption of the sphere of nothingness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the meditative absorption of the sphere of nothingness;

one personally cultivates the meditative absorption of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, teaches others to cultivate the meditative absorption of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, speaks in praise of the dharma of the meditative absorption of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the meditative absorption of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the eight liberations, teaches others to cultivate the eight liberations, speaks in praise of the dharma of the eight liberations, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the eight liberations;

he personally cultivates the eight bases of mastery, teaches others to cultivate the eight bases of mastery, speaks in praise of the dharma of the eight bases of mastery, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the eight bases of mastery.”

They personally cultivate the nine successive attainments, teach others to cultivate the nine successive attainments, praise and expound the dharma of the nine successive attainments, and rejoice in and commend those who cultivate the nine successive attainments;

they personally cultivate the ten spheres of totality, teach others to cultivate the ten spheres of totality, praise and expound the dharma of the ten spheres of totality, and rejoice in and commend those who cultivate the ten spheres of totality.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, teaches others to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, speaks in praise of the dharma of the four foundations of mindfulness, and joyfully commends those who cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness;

he personally cultivates the four right efforts, teaches others to cultivate the four right efforts, speaks in praise of the dharma of the four right efforts, and joyfully commends those who cultivate the four right efforts.”

They themselves cultivate the four bases of psychic power and teach others to cultivate the four bases of psychic power; they praise and speak in praise of the dharma of the four bases of psychic power, and rejoice in and extol those who cultivate the four bases of psychic power.

They themselves cultivate the five faculties and teach others to cultivate the five faculties; they praise and speak in praise of the dharma of the five faculties, and rejoice in and extol those who cultivate the five faculties.

They themselves cultivate the five powers and teach others to cultivate the five powers; they praise and speak in praise of the dharma of the five powers, and rejoice in and extol those who cultivate the five powers.
One personally cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment, teaches others to cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment, speaks in praise of the dharma of the seven factors of enlightenment;
one rejoices in and commends those who cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment.

One personally cultivates the eight factors of the noble path, teaches others to cultivate the eight factors of the noble path, speaks in praise of the dharma of the eight factors of the noble path, and rejoices in and commends those who cultivate the eight factors of the noble path.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, teaches others to cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, speaks in praise of the dharma of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness;

he personally cultivates the gate of liberation of signlessness, teaches others to cultivate the gate of liberation of signlessness, speaks in praise of the dharma of the gate of liberation of signlessness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the gate of liberation of signlessness.”

One cultivates the liberation door of wishlessness for oneself, teaches others to cultivate the liberation door of wishlessness, speaks in praise of the dharma of the liberation door of wishlessness, and joyfully commends those who cultivate the liberation door of wishlessness.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the five eyes, teaches others to cultivate the five eyes, speaks in praise of the dharma of the five eyes, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the five eyes;

he personally cultivates the six supernormal powers, teaches others to cultivate the six supernormal powers, speaks in praise of the dharma of the six supernormal powers, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the six supernormal powers.”

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the ten powers of a buddha, teaches others to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, speaks in praise of the dharma of the ten powers of a buddha, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the ten powers of a buddha;

he personally cultivates the four fearlessnesses, teaches others to cultivate the four fearlessnesses, speaks in praise of the dharma of the four fearlessnesses, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the four fearlessnesses.”

One cultivates the four analytical knowledges oneself, teaches others to cultivate the four analytical knowledges, speaks in praise of the dharma of the four analytical knowledges, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the four analytical knowledges.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), teaches others to cultivate great loving-kindness, speaks in praise of the dharma of great loving-kindness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate great loving-kindness;

he personally cultivates great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), teaches others to cultivate great compassion, speaks in praise of the dharma of great compassion, and joyfully extols those who cultivate great compassion.”

One personally cultivates great sympathetic joy, teaches others to cultivate great sympathetic joy, speaks in praise of the dharma of great sympathetic joy, and joyfully extols those who cultivate great sympathetic joy;
one personally cultivates great equanimity, teaches others to cultivate great equanimity, speaks in praise of the dharma of great equanimity, and joyfully extols those who cultivate great equanimity.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, teaches others to cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, speaks in praise of the dharma of the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 114 (and Scroll 123),
translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under imperial decree.
Chapter Twenty-nine, Part Four: The Section on Gathering. "Kauśika!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the dharma of non-forgetfulness, teaches others to cultivate the dharma of non-forgetfulness, speaks in praise of the dharma of non-forgetfulness, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the dharma of non-forgetfulness."

One personally cultivates the constant abiding in equanimity, teaches others to cultivate the constant abiding in equanimity, speaks in praise of the dharma of the constant abiding in equanimity, and joyfully commends those who cultivate the constant abiding in equanimity.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates all dhāraṇī-doors, teaches others to cultivate all dhāraṇī-doors, speaks in praise of the dharma of all dhāraṇī-doors, and joyfully extols those who cultivate all dhāraṇī-doors;

he personally cultivates all samādhi-doors, teaches others to cultivate all samādhi-doors, speaks in praise of the dharma of all samādhi-doors, and joyfully extols those who cultivate all samādhi-doors.”

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), teaches others to cultivate all-knowledge, speaks in praise of the dharma of all-knowledge, and joyfully extols those who cultivate all-knowledge;

he personally cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), teaches others to cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path, speaks in praise of the dharma of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path.”

One cultivates the knowledge of all aspects oneself, teaches others to cultivate the knowledge of all aspects, speaks in praise of the dharma of the knowledge of all aspects, and joyfully extols those who cultivate the knowledge of all aspects.

“Kauśika! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās, the practice of the dāna-pāramitā is performed with non-apprehension as the means, and is dedicated together with all sentient beings toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
the practice of the śīla-pāramitā is protected with non-apprehension as the means, and is dedicated together with all sentient beings toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
The perfection of patience that he cultivates, employing the method of non-apprehension, he dedicates together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
the perfection of diligence that he arouses, employing the method of non-apprehension, he dedicates together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

the perfection of meditative concentration that he enters, employing the method of non-apprehension, he dedicates together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Prajñāpāramitā that one studies, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, is dedicated together with all sentient beings toward anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Kauśika! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās, he constantly reflects:

‘If I do not practice the pāramitā of generosity, I shall be born into a poor and lowly family and will lack even basic influence; by what means then could I mature sentient beings and purify a buddha-field?’”
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I do not protect the perfection of pure ethical discipline, I shall be reborn in the various evil destinies; I would not even obtain the body of a lowly human being, so by what means could I mature sentient beings or purify a Buddha-field?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I do not cultivate the perfection of patience, my faculties will be impaired and my appearance will be ugly; I shall not possess the perfect physical body of a bodhisattva. If one attains the perfect physical body of a bodhisattva and practices the bodhisattva conduct, sentient beings who see such a person will surely attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If I do not obtain this perfect physical body, I will be unable to mature all sentient beings or purify the Buddha-fields, let alone be able to attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I were to be indolent and fail to give rise to the perfection of diligence, I would not even be able to attain the supreme path of a bodhisattva; how much less could I bring all sentient beings to maturity or purify the buddha-fields?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If my mind were distracted and I did not enter the perfection of meditative concentration, I would not even be able to give rise to the sublime samādhis of a bodhisattva; by what means, then, could I mature sentient beings or purify the buddha-fields?
How much less could I possibly attain the knowledge of all modes!

If I were without wisdom and did not study the perfection of wisdom, I would not even be able to attain the skillful means and wisdom that transcend the stages of the two vehicles; by what means then could I mature sentient beings or purify the Buddha-fields?
"How much less could they possibly attain the knowledge of all modes! "Kauśika!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva, training in the six perfections, constantly reflects in this way:"

"I should not follow the power of stinginess; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of generosity would not be fulfilled, and if my perfection of generosity were not fulfilled, I could never achieve the knowledge of all modes.

I should not follow the power of immoral conduct; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of ethical discipline would not be fulfilled, and if my perfection of ethical discipline were not fulfilled, I could never achieve the knowledge of all modes.

I should not follow the power of anger and resentment; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of patience would not be fulfilled, and if my perfection of patience were not fulfilled, I could never achieve the knowledge of all modes."

I must not follow the power of indolence; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*) would not be fulfilled, and if my perfection of diligence is not fulfilled, I will ultimately be unable to achieve the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

I must not follow the power of mental distraction; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*) would not be fulfilled, and if my perfection of meditative concentration is not fulfilled, I will ultimately be unable to achieve the knowledge of all modes.

I must not follow the power of ignorance; if I were to follow that power, my perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*) would not be fulfilled, and if my perfection of wisdom is not fulfilled, I will ultimately be unable to achieve the knowledge of all modes.

“Kauśika! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), receives, upholds, recites, diligently practices, reflects upon according to the principle, transcribes, explains, and widely disseminates this Prajñāpāramitā, thereby attaining such meritorious benefits and advantages in both the present life and future lives.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is truly rare; it subdues the bodhisattva so as to prevent arrogance, while enabling them to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.”
The Buddha said:
“Kauśika! How does the perfection of wisdom subdue a bodhisattva so that they do not become conceited, yet are able to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mundane perfection of giving, if they practice giving toward the Buddha, they form this thought:”
"I am able to give to the Buddha.
If one practices giving toward bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, the destitute, the aged and the sick, travelers on the road, or beggars, one then forms this thought:
"I am able to give to bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, the destitute, the aged and the sick, travelers on the road, and beggars."
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices giving without skillful means, he consequently gives rise to a haughty mind and is unable to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the worldly perfection of ethical discipline, they think:
"I am able to practice the perfection of ethical discipline; I am able to fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices pure ethical discipline without skillful means, they consequently give rise to a sense of superiority and are unable to dedicate it toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mundane perfection of patience, they think:
"I am able to practice the perfection of patience; I am able to fulfill the perfection of patience."
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices patience without skillful means, they consequently give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate it toward the knowledge of all modes.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the worldly perfection of diligence, they think:
"I am able to practice the perfection of diligence; I am able to fulfill the perfection of diligence."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices diligence without skillful means, they consequently give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate it toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mundane perfection of meditative concentration, they form this thought:
"I am able to practice the perfection of meditative concentration; I am able to fulfill the perfection of meditative concentration."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices meditative concentration without skillful means, they consequently give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mundane perfection of wisdom, they form this thought:
"I am able to practice the perfection of wisdom; I am able to fulfill the perfection of wisdom."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, they consequently give rise to a haughty mind and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in internal emptiness, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to dwell in internal emptiness.’”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in internal emptiness while being disturbed by the grasping of "I" and "mine," they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to dwell in external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, being disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in *tathatā*, if they should think:
‘I am able to abide in *tathatā*.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells in suchness while being disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, he consequently gives rise to pride and is unable to dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to dwell in the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells within the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm while being disturbed by the grasping of "self" and "mine," they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the noble truth of suffering, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to dwell in the noble truth of suffering.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells in the Noble Truth of Suffering, being disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to dwell in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path while being disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the four dhyānas, if they form this thought:
‘I am able to practice the four dhyānas.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the four dhyānas while being disturbed by the grasping of a self and what belongs to a self, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, if they should think:
"I am able to practice the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions," [they do not truly practice them].

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, they consequently give rise to conceit and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the eight liberations, if they form this thought:
‘I am able to practice the eight liberations.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the eight liberations while being disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self, they consequently give rise to pride and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping of a self and what belongs to a self while practicing the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness.’”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four foundations of mindfulness while being disturbed by the grasping of a self and what belongs to a self, they consequently give rise to conceit and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to cultivate the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while practicing the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, he consequently gives rise to arrogance and is unable to dedicate [the roots of goodness] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gate of liberation that is emptiness, if they should think:
‘I am able to cultivate the gate of liberation that is emptiness.’”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the gate of liberation of emptiness while being disturbed by the grasping of "I" and "mine," they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to cultivate the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while practicing the signless and wishless doors of liberation, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the five eyes, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to cultivate the five eyes.’”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping of a self and what belongs to a self while practicing the five eyes, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates the six supernormal powers, if they form the thought,

"I am able to cultivate the six supernormal powers," then because that bodhisattva-mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while cultivating the six supernormal powers, they consequently give rise to pride and are unable to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping of a self and what belongs to a self while cultivating the ten powers of a buddha, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, if they should form this thought:

"I am able to cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping of "I" and "mine" while practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dharma of non-forgetfulness, if they should think:
‘I am able to cultivate the dharma of non-forgetfulness.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping of "I" and "mine" while practicing the dharma of non-forgetfulness, they consequently give rise to conceit and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, if they form this thought:

"I am able to cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity," then because that bodhisattva mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while cultivating the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates all the gates of dhāraṇī, if they should think:
‘I am able to cultivate all the gates of dhāraṇī.’”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while practicing all the dhāraṇī-doors, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all the gateways of samādhi, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to practice all the gateways of samādhi."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all gateways of samādhi while being disturbed by the grasping of "I" and "mine," they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge, if they should form this thought:
‘I am able to cultivate all-knowledge.’”

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while practicing for the sake of all-knowledge, they consequently give rise to arrogance and are unable to dedicate their merit toward the knowledge of all modes.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the knowledge of the characteristics of the path and the knowledge of all characteristics, if they should form this thought:
"I am able to cultivate the knowledge of the characteristics of the path and the knowledge of all characteristics."

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed by the grasping of "I" and "mine," they fail to cultivate the knowledge of the characteristics of the path and the knowledge of all characteristics; consequently, they give rise to conceit and are unable to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings sentient beings to maturity, if they should think:
‘I am able to bring sentient beings to maturity.’”

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while maturing sentient beings, he consequently gives rise to arrogance and is unable to dedicate [the roots of merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva purifies a buddha-field, if they should think,

"I am able to purify a buddha-field," then because that bodhisattva-mahāsattva is disturbed by the grasping at a self and what belongs to a self while purifying the buddha-field, they consequently give rise to pride and are unable to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

Thus, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva relies on a worldly mind to cultivate various wholesome dharmas, because they lack skillful means in practicing generosity and so forth, and because their minds are disturbed by the grasping at ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ although they cultivate the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not yet attain it; consequently, they cannot truly subdue a haughty mind, nor can they truly dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*).”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of giving, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend a giver, do not apprehend a recipient, and do not apprehend the act of giving. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of giving by relying on the perfection of wisdom, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not apprehend ethical discipline, nor do they apprehend one who possesses ethical discipline. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of ethical discipline by relying on the perfection of wisdom, they are able to subdue the arrogant mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*), they do not apprehend patience, nor do they apprehend one who possesses patience. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of patience by relying on the perfection of wisdom, they are able to subdue the haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of diligence, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend diligence, nor do they apprehend one who possesses diligence. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of diligence by relying on the perfection of wisdom, they are able to subdue an arrogant mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*), because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not apprehend meditative concentration, nor do they apprehend one who possesses meditative concentration. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom while practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of wisdom, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend wisdom, nor do they apprehend one who possesses wisdom, nor do they apprehend any phenomena whatsoever. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to practice the perfection of wisdom, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when dwelling in internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), because of skillfully cultivating the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), neither apprehends internal emptiness nor apprehends one who dwells in internal emptiness—then, by virtue of relying on the perfection of wisdom to dwell in internal emptiness, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to subdue the haughty mind and is also able to dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness,
great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness,
essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, and common characteristic emptiness;
When all phenomena are empty, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom,

they do not apprehend external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nor do they abide in external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in reliance upon the perfection of wisdom— from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities—
they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while abiding in suchness, skillfully cultivates the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and thus neither apprehends suchness nor apprehends one who abides in suchness, then by virtue of relying on the perfection of wisdom to abide in suchness, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to subdue an arrogant mind and is also able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñatājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapatti-dharmatā), the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniveśanatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu)—because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)—they do not apprehend the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, nor do they apprehend dwelling in the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to dwell in the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while abiding in the noble truth of suffering, skillfully cultivates the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) such that they do not apprehend the noble truth of suffering, nor apprehend one who abides in the noble truth of suffering—then because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to abide in the noble truth of suffering, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while dwelling in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, skillfully cultivates the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) and thus does not apprehend the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, nor apprehends dwelling in those noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—then because that bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to dwell in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the four dhyānas, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), does not apprehend the four dhyānas nor the one who practices the four dhyānas, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by relying on the perfection of wisdom to practice the four dhyānas, is able to subdue a haughty mind and is also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions, nor do they apprehend one who practices the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to practice the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the eight liberations, because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the eight liberations, nor do they apprehend the one who cultivates the eight liberations. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the eight liberations, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ*), and the ten totalities (*daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni*), because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not apprehend the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities; nor do they apprehend one who cultivates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the four foundations of mindfulness, does not apprehend the four foundations of mindfulness nor the practice of the four foundations of mindfulness because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by relying on the perfection of wisdom to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, is able to subdue a haughty mind and is also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience.”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path; nor do they apprehend the cultivation of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the gate of liberation of emptiness, well-cultivates the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) such that they do not apprehend the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they apprehend one who practices the gate of liberation of emptiness—then because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to practice the gate of liberation of emptiness, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, nor do they apprehend one who cultivates the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the five eyes, because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the five eyes, nor do they apprehend one who cultivates the five eyes. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the five eyes, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the six supernormal powers, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the six supernormal powers, nor do they apprehend one who cultivates the six supernormal powers. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the six supernormal powers, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when cultivating the ten powers of a Buddha, well cultivates the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) such that they do not apprehend the ten powers of a Buddha nor the one who cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, then because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).”
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion,
great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom,
they do not apprehend the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the great...
Loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—
those who cannot cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness,
great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon prajñāpāramitā.
Because they cultivate the pāramitās, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion,
great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha,
they are able to subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dharma of non-forgetfulness, because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the dharma of non-forgetfulness, nor do they apprehend one who cultivates the dharma of non-forgetfulness. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the dharma of non-forgetfulness, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the nature of constant equanimity, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the nature of constant equanimity, nor do they apprehend the one who cultivates the nature of constant equanimity. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the nature of constant equanimity, they are able to subdue an arrogant mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all the gates of dhāraṇī, because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend any gate of dhāraṇī, nor do they apprehend one who cultivates all the gates of dhāraṇī. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate all the gates of dhāraṇī, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all the gateways of samādhi, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend any gateway of samādhi, nor do they apprehend one who practices all the gateways of samādhi. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to practice all the gateways of samādhi, they are able to subdue the haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), because they skillfully cultivate the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not apprehend all-knowledge, nor do they apprehend the cultivation of all-knowledge. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate all-knowledge, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects; nor do they apprehend the cultivation of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva relies on the perfection of wisdom to cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, they are able to subdue the haughty mind and are also able to dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva brings sentient beings to maturity, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the maturing of sentient beings. Since they do not apprehend the maturing of sentient beings, this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by relying on the perfection of wisdom to mature sentient beings, is able to subdue the haughty mind and is also able to dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna).”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies a buddha-field, because they have skillfully cultivated the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not apprehend the purification of a buddha-field. Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not apprehend the purification of a buddha-field, by relying on the perfection of wisdom to purify the buddha-field, they are able to subdue a haughty mind and also dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).
“World-Honored One!

Because such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate wholesome dharmas by relying on supramundane prajñāpāramitā, they are able to subdue their arrogant minds as they truly are, and they are also able to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) as it truly is. For this reason, I say:
‘This prajñāpāramitā is most rare, for it subdues the bodhisattva so that they do not become arrogant, while enabling them to dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes.’”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters are able to wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, these good sons and good daughters will always have bodies in peace and security and minds in constant joy; they shall not be afflicted by any calamities or misfortunes.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters receive, uphold, read, recite, draw near to, make offerings to, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, then when these good sons and good daughters are amidst military forces engaged in battle, if they mindfully recite this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere heart, they shall not be harmed or killed by blades or clubs; their adversaries will all give rise to thoughts of loving-kindness; even if they wish to inflict injury, [the attackers] will naturally retreat and be defeated; it is impossible for them to lose their lives in the military fray."
Why is this? Kauśika!

These sons and daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience; employing the method of non-apprehension, they have cultivated the six pāramitās throughout the long night, thereby removing for themselves the swords and staves of craving, and are likewise able to remove the swords and staves of craving from others.
Having personally eliminated the sword and staff of hatred, they are also able to eliminate the sword and staff of hatred in others;
having personally eliminated the sword and staff of delusion, they are also able to eliminate the sword and staff of delusion in others;
having personally eliminated the sword and staff of evil views, they are also able to eliminate the sword and staff of evil views in others.
They personally eliminate the weapons of the fetters and defilements, and are likewise able to eliminate the weapons of the fetters and defilements in others;
they personally eliminate the weapons of the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), and are likewise able to eliminate the weapons of the latent tendencies in others;
they personally eliminate the weapons of evil karma, and are likewise able to eliminate the weapons of evil karma in others.

Kauśika! For this reason, even if these sons and daughters of good family should enter the midst of an army, they will not be wounded or killed by swords or staves; all their adversaries will give rise to a mind of loving-kindness; and even if they wish to inflict injury, they will naturally retreat and be defeated. It is simply impossible that they should lose their lives in the military fray.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as their expedient, constantly listen to, reverently worship, honor, praise, uphold, recite, reflect upon according to principle, diligently practice, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere heart—then these good sons and good daughters cannot be harmed by any poisons, sorcery, demons, curses, or incantations; they cannot be drowned by water nor burned by fire; and they cannot be injured by blades or staves, wild beasts, enemies or bandits, evil spirits, various heterodox deities, or malevolent ghosts."

Why is this so? Kausika! This Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is a great illuminating mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the mantra of the unequaled; this Prajñāpāramitā is the king of all mantras, supreme and most wondrous, with none able to equal it. Possessing great majestic power, it can subdue all things and cannot be subdued by anything.
These sons and daughters of good family who diligently practice and study this king of mantras will not harm themselves, nor harm others, nor harm both.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family who study this Prajñāpāramitā realize that both self and others are equally unapprehendable.

“Kauśika!
