These are adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures; they are one *yojana* in height, with a width half that of the height. These fill the four continents without leaving any empty space. Moreover, throughout their entire lives, they offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise with all kinds of celestial and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, various wonders, rare musical instruments, and lamps.
"What do you think?
Is the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family on account of this cause and condition not great?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very much so,
World-Honored One!
Very much so!”
“Excellent, Sugata!
The Buddha said: “Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this *prajñāpāramitā*, and with a sincere heart listen to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and reflect upon it according to the principle; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it, adorning it in various ways, and offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise; and further, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, musical performances, and lamps— [The merit of these individuals] shall be immeasurable. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the mother of all Buddhas, the source of all Buddhas, and the guide of all Buddhas. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all Buddhas of the past have attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; all Buddhas of the future will attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā*; and all Buddhas of the present who abide in the ten directions also attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā*. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a vast and immeasurable accumulation of merit. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the supreme vehicle, the unsurpassed vehicle, the peerless vehicle, and the vehicle that leads to the ultimate destination. Those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall be protected, shielded, and guarded by the Buddhas of the ten directions. Furthermore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall not be harmed by humans or non-humans, nor shall they fall into the three evil realms. They shall quickly attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. For what reason? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the great spell, the unsurpassed spell, the unequaled spell, and the spell that pacifies all suffering; it is true and not false. As it is said in the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "This is the great spell, the spell of great knowledge, the unsurpassed spell, the unequaled spell, which pacifies all suffering. It is true and not false. One should know this spell as the *prajñāpāramitā*. Thus it is said. Therefore, one should know that the merit of those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* is truly immeasurable and boundless. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the root of all wholesome dharmas, the foundation of all Buddhas, and the source of all bodhisattvas. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas realize their respective fruits. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is far more immeasurable than the aforementioned. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the treasury of all dharmas, the light that illuminates all dharmas, and the eye that sees all dharmas. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all dharmas are manifested. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is infinitely superior to the aforementioned. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the sovereign of all dharmas, the master of all dharmas, and the leader of all dharmas. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all dharmas are brought to fulfillment. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the path of all bodhisattvas, the vehicle of all bodhisattvas, and the gate through which all bodhisattvas enter. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all bodhisattvas traverse the stages and reach the ultimate fruit. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is truly immeasurable and beyond calculation. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the ultimate truth, the ineffable truth, and the truth that transcends all conceptualization. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all Buddhas realize the nature of reality (*dharmatā*). Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is the most supreme, the most excellent, and the most sublime among all merits. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the source of all Buddhas, the origin of all dharmas, and the foundation of all virtues. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all Buddhas and bodhisattvas achieve liberation. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is truly immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the great ocean of wisdom, the mountain of Dharma, and the sun that dispels the darkness of ignorance. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all sentient beings cross over the river of birth and death and reach the shore of nirvana. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is the greatest, the most profound, and the most difficult to fathom among all merits. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the inexhaustible storehouse of all dharmas, the unobstructed gate of all dharmas, and the mirror that reflects all dharmas. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all Buddhas manifest their bodies and preach the Dharma. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is truly immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the king of spells, the queen of spells, and the crown jewel of all spells. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all Buddhas subdue all māras and heretics. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is the most powerful, the most majestic, and the most invincible among all merits. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the ultimate refuge, the final reliance, and the eternal dwelling place for all sentient beings. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all sentient beings find peace and security. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is truly immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Why is this? Because this *prajñāpāramitā* is the seed of all Buddhas, the sprout of all dharmas, and the trunk of the tree of enlightenment. It is by relying on this *prajñāpāramitā* that all Buddhas bring forth the fruit of the Dharma. Therefore, those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and practice this *prajñāpāramitā* shall generate a merit that is the most fundamental, the most essential, and the most primary among all merits. “By this causal condition, the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family is far greater than that, immeasurable and boundless.

Furthermore, suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of various Tathāgatas, erect stūpas made of the seven excellent precious substances for the purpose of making offerings to the Buddha’s relics. These are adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures; they are one yojana in height and half that in width, filling the entire intermediate thousandfold world system without any gaps. Moreover, throughout their entire lives, they offer worship, respect, honor, and praise with various celestial flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, various exquisite and rare items, music, and lamps.
"What do you think?
Is the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family on account of this cause and condition not great?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:

World-Honored One!
Very much so!”
“Excellent, Sugata!
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!”

If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this *prajñāpāramitā*, and with sincere hearts listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, and reflect upon it according to the principle; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it and adorn it in various ways, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it; and furthermore, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, many wonderful and rare items, music, and lamps— [This is the full translation of the provided text.]
"The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this cause and condition is far greater than that [of the former], immeasurable and boundless.
The Buddha told Kauśika:
"Set aside the small chiliocosm."

Furthermore, suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgatas, erect stūpas made of the seven excellent precious gems to enshrine the Buddha’s relics. These are adorned with various rare and wonderful ornaments; they are one yojana in height and half that in width, filling the entire middle thousandfold world-system without any gaps. Moreover, for as long as their lives last, they offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise with all kinds of celestial flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags, canopies, various exquisite and rare objects, music, and lamps.
"What do you think? Is the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family on account of this cause and condition much or not?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
"It is very much!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!

If sons and daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and reflect upon this Prajñāpāramitā in accordance with the truth; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they write it down and provide various adornments, offerings, reverence, respect, and praise; and furthermore, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, myriad wonderful and rare items, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain great merit].”
"The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this causal condition is far greater than that [of the former], being immeasurable and boundless.
The Buddha told Kauśika:
"Set aside the intermediate chiliocosm."

Furthermore, suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of various Tathāgatas, erect stūpas made of the seven precious jewels for the purpose of making offerings to the Buddha’s relics. These stūpas are adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures; they are one yojana in height and half that in width, filling the entire trichiliocosm without leaving any empty space. Moreover, throughout their entire lives, they offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise, using various celestial and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.
"What do you think?
Would the mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family on account of this cause and condition be great?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied:
“Very much so,
World-Honored One!
Very much so!”
“Excellent, Sugata!
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this *prajñāpāramitā*, and with sincere hearts listen to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and contemplate it according to the principle; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it, adorning it in various ways and making offerings, paying homage, respecting, and praising it; and furthermore, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, diverse wonders, rare treasures, musical instruments, and lamps—[they shall gain immeasurable merit].
"The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this cause and condition is far greater than that, immeasurable and boundless.
The Buddha told Kausika:
"Set aside one trichiliocosm."

Furthermore, suppose all sentient beings within a trichiliocosm, after the Tathāgata has entered parinirvāṇa, were each to erect stūpas for the worship of the Buddha’s relics using exquisite seven precious gems, adorned with various rare and wonderful ornaments; these stūpas would be one yojana in height and half a yojana in width, filling the entire trichiliocosm without any gaps. Moreover, throughout their entire lives, they would offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise, presenting various celestial and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, myriad wonderful rarities, music, and lamps.
What do you think?
Would the mass of merit produced by all the sentient beings in such a great trichiliocosm as a result of these causes and conditions be great?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: “Very many,
World-Honored One!”
"Very many,
Sugata! the Buddha said.

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this Prajñāpāramitā—listening to it with a sincere heart, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, diligently practicing and studying it, reflecting upon it according to the principle, and extensively proclaiming and disseminating it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they write it down, adorning it with various ornaments, and making offerings to it with reverence, respect, honor, and praise; and furthermore, make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, clothing, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain great merit].”
"The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this causal condition is far greater than that [previous merit], immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying: "It is so! It is so!"
So it is! It is truly as the Holy Teaching declares.

If good sons or good daughters offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to this Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that these good sons and good daughters are thereby offering worship, honor, respect, and praise to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present.

Suppose that all sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in each of the ten directions were, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, to erect stūpas for the worship of the Buddha’s *śarīra*. These stūpas would be made of the seven wonderful precious jewels, adorned with various rare and exquisite ornaments, one *yojana* in height and half a *yojana* in width, filling the entire trichiliocosm without leaving any empty space. Furthermore, they would offer various celestial flower garlands, powdered and scattered perfumes, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags, canopies, manifold wonders, rare treasures, music, and lamps, for the duration of an eon or more, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them.
“World-Honored One!
Would the mass of merit produced by these sentient beings through this cause and condition be great?
The Buddha said:
“Very much so!
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

“If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), should with sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this Prajñāpāramitā in accordance with the truth; and should widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or should write it down, adorning it in various ways and making offerings to it with reverence, respect, honor, and praise; and furthermore, should make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—[the merit would be immeasurable].”

The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this cause and condition is far greater than that [previous merit], being immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.
Why is this? "World-Honored One!
It is because this Prajñāpāramitā is able to comprehensively encompass and preserve all wholesome dharmas."
That is to say, the ten paths of wholesome action; or the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
or the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;
or the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, and the seven factors of enlightenment...
The factors of enlightenment and the branches of the noble eightfold path; the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness;
the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin, the noble truth of cessation, and the noble truth of the path;
the five eyes of a Buddha; the six supernormal powers; and the perfection of generosity.
the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence,
the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom; as well as internal emptiness, external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.
unconditioned emptiness, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration,
emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility,
emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and suchness.
The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth,
the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space,
the inconceivable realm; as well as all doors of dhāraṇī, all doors of samādhi, and the Buddhas.
The ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity,
and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness,
the state of constant equanimity, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, or any other [qualities].
The boundless qualities of a Buddha are all subsumed within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
“World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the true seal of the Dharma for all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; it is also the true seal of the Dharma for all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.”
"Bhagavān!

Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have constantly and diligently studied this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they have realized, will realize, and are currently realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Bhagavān!

Because all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas have constantly and diligently studied this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they have reached the other shore, will reach the other shore, and are currently reaching the other shore."
“World-Honored One!

For this reason, if sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the practice of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this *prajñāpāramitā* according to the principle; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they write it down, adorn it in various ways, and offer it with reverence, respect, honor, and praise; and furthermore, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain immeasurable merit].”
The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this cause and condition is far greater than that, being immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

If sons and daughters of good family, not departing from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), employ the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and with sincere hearts listen to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, and reflect upon it according to the principle; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they transcribe it, adorning it in various ways, and offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise; and further, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, many wonderful and rare items, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain great merit]."

The mass of merit produced by these sons and daughters of good family through this causal condition is far greater than that [previous merit], being immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable.
Why is this? "Kauśika!
It is because it is by means of this perfection of wisdom that all the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are brought forth."

“Kauśika! It is because by means of this *prajñāpāramitā*, all forms of emptiness—internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—are made manifest.”

“Kauśika! It is because by means of this perfection of wisdom, all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are made manifest.”
“Kauśika! It is because by means of this prajñāpāramitā, the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin, the noble truth of cessation, and the noble truth of the path are made manifest.”
“Kauśika! It is because all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions arise by means of this prajñāpāramitā.”
“Kauśika! It is because all eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive meditative attainments, and ten totalities arise by means of this perfection of wisdom.”

“Kauśika! It is because it is by means of this perfection of wisdom that all the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are brought forth.”
“Kauśika! It is because all the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are brought forth by means of this perfection of wisdom.”
“Kauśika! It is because all five eyes and six supernormal powers arise by means of this perfection of wisdom. Kauśika!”

It is because it is through this perfection of wisdom that all Buddhas’ ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are brought forth.
“Kauśika! It is because it is through this perfection of wisdom that all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are brought forth.”
“Kauśika! It is because all the gateways of dhāraṇīs and all the gateways of samādhis arise from this perfection of wisdom.”
“Kauśika! It is because it is by means of this perfection of wisdom that all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are brought forth.”
“Kauśika! It is by means of this perfection of wisdom that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, thereby attaining accomplishment.”
“Kauśika! It is because by means of this prajñāpāramitā, all the Śrāvakayāna, Pratyekabuddhayāna, and Anuttarayāna are brought forth.”

“Kauśika! It is because by means of this perfection of wisdom that all those in the path of the stream-enterer and the fruit of stream-entry, those in the path of the once-returner and the fruit of once-returning, those in the path of the non-returner and the fruit of non-returning, and those in the path of the arhat and the fruit of arhatship appear.”
“Kauśika! It is by means of this perfection of wisdom that all those who are candidates for the fruit of a pratyekabuddha appear as pratyekabuddhas. Kauśika!”

It is because it is through this perfection of wisdom that all the merits of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—from their first generation of the mind of awakening up until the diamond-like samādhi—come into manifestation.
“Kauśika! It is because of this perfection of wisdom that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and the great parinirvāṇa of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear.”

“Kauśika! For this reason, if sons or daughters of good family do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of the practice of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yoga*), they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this *prajñāpāramitā* in accordance with the truth; and if they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; or if they write it down, adorning it in various ways, and offer it worship, respect, honor, and praise; and further, if they make offerings with various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, diverse wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—[they shall obtain great merit].”

Compared to this mass of merit, the merit from the stūpas previously constructed does not approach even a hundredth part; it does not approach a thousandth part; it does not approach a hundred-thousandth part; it does not approach a koṭi-th part; it does not approach a hundred-koṭi-th part; it does not approach a thousand-koṭi-th part; it does not approach a hundred-thousand-koṭi-th part; it does not approach a hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-th part. It does not approach even a numerical part, a calculable part, a reckonable part, a comparable part, or even a fraction of an upaniṣad.
Why is this? "Kauśika!

If this Prajñāpāramitā dwells among the people of Jambudvīpa, then the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṃgha of Bhikṣus will all abide in this world without perishing."

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would constantly possess the ten paths of wholesome action, as well as the virtues of giving, ethical discipline, and cultivation; it would know gratitude and repay kindness, and it would make offerings to the noble and holy ones.”

“Kauśika! If this perfection of wisdom were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, then the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom would always exist in the world.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, then the world would constantly possess internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, then the world would constantly possess true thusness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, then the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering, and the Noble Truth of the Path would always exist in the world.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would constantly possess the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be in the world the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭābhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana).”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would constantly possess the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would constantly possess the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would constantly possess the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would constantly possess the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four kinds of unhindered understanding, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be in the world the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, then all the dhāraṇī-doors and all the samādhi-doors would always exist in the world.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always exist in the world omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be great clans of Kṣatriyas, great clans of Brāhmaṇas, great clans of Śreṣṭhins, and great clans of Gṛhapatis in the world.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the world would always have the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, the Yāma heaven, the Tuṣita heaven, the Nirmāṇarati heaven, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin heaven.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the worlds would constantly have the gods of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika-pariṣad, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, Ābhāsvara-śuddhi, Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Bṛhatphala heavens.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always exist in the world the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha devas.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always exist in the world the devas of the Sphere of Infinite Space, the devas of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, the devas of the Sphere of Nothingness, and the devas of the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-perception.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, the Śrāvakayāna, Pratyekabuddhayāna, and Anuttarayāna would always exist in the world.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be in the world those practicing for the fruit of stream-entry and those who have attained the fruit of stream-entry; those practicing for the fruit of once-returning and those who have attained the fruit of once-returning; those practicing for the fruit of non-returning and those who have attained the fruit of non-returning; and those practicing for the fruit of arhatship and those who have attained the fruit of arhatship.”
“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be Pratyekabuddhas in the world who are directed toward the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the world who practice the bodhisattva path, bring sentient beings to maturity, and purify buddha-fields.”

“Kauśika! If this Prajñāpāramitā were to abide among the people of Jambudvīpa, there would always be Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the world who realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, and deliver immeasurable multitudes.”

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
