At that time, all the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmakāyika-parṣadya Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara-śuddha Heaven, the Śubha Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Vahula Heaven, the Parīttabṛhatphala Heaven, the Apramāṇabṛhatphala Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven within this trichiliocosm raised their voices in unison and addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"O Great Sage!..."
"O Great Sage, this Prajñāpāramitā should be received in this way;
this Prajñāpāramitā should be upheld in this way."
"O Great Sage!
You should study this Prajñāpāramitā.
O Great Sage!"
One should recite this Prajñāpāramitā.
Great Sage!
One should diligently practice and study this Prajñāpāramitā.
O Great Sage!
You should contemplate this Prajñāpāramitā in accordance with reality.
O Great Sage!
One should offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to this Prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this? "O Great Sage!

If one can receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise this Prajñāpāramitā, then all unwholesome dharmas will diminish and wholesome dharmas will increase.
“Great Seer!

If there are those who uphold, recite, diligently study, correctly contemplate, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise this Prajñāpāramitā, they will cause the hosts of all devas to increase and the factions of the asuras to diminish.”
“Great Seer!

If anyone upholds, recites, diligently studies, reflects upon according to the principle, makes offerings to, reveres, honors, and praises this Prajñāpāramitā, they shall cause the Buddha-eye not to perish, the Dharma-eye not to perish, and the Saṅgha-eye not to perish.”
“Great Seer!

If there are those who uphold, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, and honor, revere, respect, and praise this Prajñāpāramitā, they shall cause the lineage of the Buddha Jewel not to be severed, the lineage of the Dharma Jewel not to be severed, and the lineage of the Saṅgha Jewel not to be severed.”

“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there appears in the world the perfection of generosity, as well as the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

"Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there appear in the world: internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature."

“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, there appear in the world suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”

“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin, the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path appear in the world.”
"O Great Sage, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments appear in the world."

"O Great Sage, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities appear in the world."

"Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there appear in the world the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path."
"O Great Sage, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there appear in the world the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness."
“Great Seer, you should know!
Because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers appear in the world.
Great Seer, you should know!”

Because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never interrupted, there appear in the world the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
"O Great Sage, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there appear in the world the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity."
"Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors appear in the world."

“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) appear in the world.”
"O Great Sage, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, there appear in the world the Śrāvaka-yāna, the Pratyekabuddha-yāna, and the Anuttara-yāna."

"O Great Sage, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, there appear in the world those who have attained the stages of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, and Arhat."

"Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, there appear in the world those who have entered the stream and attained the fruit of stream-entry; those who are candidates for and have attained the fruit of once-returning; those who are candidates for and have attained the fruit of non-returning; and those who are candidates for and have attained the fruit of arhatship."
"Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, Pratyekabuddhas and those who are candidates for the fruit of Pratyekabuddhahood appear in the world."
“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world.”

"Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, there appear in the world Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the dharmas such as the ten stages (bhūmis) of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."

“Great Seer, you should know that because the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed, there appear in the world Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and the attainment of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
"Therefore, Great Sage!
You should receive, uphold, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise this Prajñāpāramitā."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika! You should receive this profound *prajñāpāramitā*;

you should uphold this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; you should read this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; you should recite this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; you should apply yourself with diligence to the study of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; you should contemplate this profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the principle; and you should offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is this? Kauśika!
If the faction of the fierce and rebellious Asuras should give rise to such evil thoughts:

"If we are to engage in battle and conflict with the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, at that time, you and your retinues of devas should each, with sincere hearts, recite this profound Prajñāpāramitā, making offerings, paying homage, honoring, and praising it; then the fierce and rebellious followers of the asuras will have their evil intentions extinguished and will not arise again."
“Kauśika! If any sons of the gods or daughters of the gods manifest the five signs of decline, their minds will become terrified and fearful of falling into the evil destinies.
At that time, you and your retinues of devas should stand before them and, with a sincere mind, recite this Prajñāpāramitā.”

At that time, whether they were sons of the gods or daughters of the gods, by virtue of the power of the roots of goodness of this *prajñāpāramitā* and because they had conceived pure faith in this *prajñāpāramitā*, the five signs of impending death vanished and their bodies and minds became serene. Even if their lives were to end, they would return to their original abodes, where they would experience celestial wealth and pleasure far exceeding what they had before.
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because the merit and majestic power of hearing and placing faith in the Prajñāpāramitā are exceedingly vast and great.

“Kauśika! If any sons or daughters of good family, or any devaputras and devakanyās, hear this Prajñāpāramitā even once, by the power of that root of goodness, they will certainly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Kauśika!

All the Buddhas of the past and their disciples studied this very Prajñāpāramitā; having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they entered the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder.
All future Buddhas and their disciples shall likewise study this Prajñāpāramitā; they shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and enter the realm of nirvana without remainder.

All the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions and their disciples who currently exist likewise study this very Prajñāpāramitā; they have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and entered the realm of nirvana without remainder.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because this Prajñāpāramitā universally encompasses all factors conducive to enlightenment (bodhipākṣikadharma); it fully includes whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of tathāgatas.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One! This Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is a great illuminating mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unequaled mantra; this Prajñāpāramitā is the king of all mantras—most supreme and most wondrous, able to subdue all things, yet itself never subdued by anything.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
Because this Prajñāpāramitā is able to eliminate all evil and unwholesome dharmas, and is able to encompass and cause all wholesome dharmas to grow.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

This Prajñāpāramitā is a great mantra, a great illuminating mantra, an unsurpassed mantra, an unequaled mantra, and the king of all mantras; it is most supreme and most wondrous, capable of subduing all things, yet itself never being subdued by anything."
Why is this? Because all the Buddhas of the past, by relying upon this very profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, have already realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
All future Buddhas shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by relying upon this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā.

All the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions in the present rely upon this profound Great Dharani King of Prajñāpāramitā, and thereby now realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? "Kauśika!
It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the ten paths of wholesome action appear in the world."

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the dharmas of giving, observing the fasts, and maintaining the precepts appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the five supernormal powers, and so forth appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the pāramitās of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the following appear in the world: internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying on and depending upon this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the world manifests the appearance of suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, sameness, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering, and the Noble Truth of the Path appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying on and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying on and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is by relying on and depending upon this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the five eyes and the six supernormal powers appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying on and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is by relying on and depending upon this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that all the gates of dhāraṇī and all the gates of samādhi appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying on and depending upon this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, and arhats appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that those who are candidates for the fruit of stream-entry and those who have attained the fruit of stream-entry; those who are candidates for the fruit of once-returning and those who have attained the fruit of once-returning; those who are candidates for the fruit of non-returning and those who have attained the fruit of non-returning; and those who are candidates for the fruit of arhatship and those who have attained the fruit of arhatship appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is by relying on and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by relying on and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is by relying upon and because of this profound Great Dharani King, the Prajñāpāramitā, that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi appear in the world.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
It is by relying upon and because of this profound Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, that Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas appear in the world."
“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the ten paths of wholesome action appear in the world. Kauśika!”
“Kauśika, it is by depending upon bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the dharmas such as giving, observing the fast, and maintaining the precepts appear in the world. Kauśika,
it is by depending upon bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the world manifests: inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Kauśika! It is because of, and by depending upon, the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the world manifests the true suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path appear in the world.”
“Kauśika! It is because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path appear in the world.”

“Kauśika! It is because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the world manifests the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.”
“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the five eyes and the six supernormal powers appear in the world. Kauśika!”

It is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha appear in the world.
“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity appear in the world. Kauśika!”
"Kauśika, it is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that all the gateways of dhāraṇī and all the gateways of samādhi appear in the world."

"Kauśika, it is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that omniscience (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) appear in the world."
"It is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the world manifests the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat. Kausika!"

It is by depending on bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the world manifests the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, the stage of entering once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship.
“Kauśika! It is by depending upon and because of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas appear in the world. Kauśika!”
“Kauśika, it is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattvas that bodhisattva mahāsattvas and the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas appear in the world.”
It is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi appear in the world.

“Kauśika! For example, because of the full moon disk as their cause and condition, all medicinal herbs, stars, mountains, and seas attain increased brilliance. Likewise, because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva as their cause and condition, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things—the ten paths of wholesome action in the world—attain increased brilliance.

Likewise, because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva as their cause and condition, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—such as the dharmas of giving, observing the fast, and maintaining the precepts—attain increased brilliance.”

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—such as the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges—all become increasingly bright.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—such as the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—all become increasingly bright.

Thus, by virtue of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s full moon disc acting as the cause, all medicinal herbs and categories of things—namely, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—all attain increased brilliance.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and entities of the world—namely, suchness (*tathatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the reality limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—all attain increased clarity.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and entities of the world—namely, the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkha-āryasatya*), the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] (*samudaya-āryasatya*), the noble truth of cessation (*nirodha-āryasatya*), and the noble truth of the path (*mārga-āryasatya*)—all attain increased clarity.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—namely the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases—all become increasingly bright and radiant.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—namely the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path—all become increasingly bright and radiant.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disk of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—namely the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness—all become increasingly bright and radiant.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—the five eyes and the six supernormal powers—attain increased brilliance.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—attain increased brilliance.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and categories of things in the world—the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity—attain increased brilliance.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all medicinal herbs and substances of all the world’s gateways of dhāraṇī and all gateways of samādhi attain increased brilliance;

thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all medicinal herbs and substances of all the world’s knowledge (*jñāna*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) attain increased brilliance;

thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all medicinal herbs and substances of all the world’s candidates for and fruits of stream-entry (*srotāpatti*), candidates for and fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmin*), candidates for and fruits of non-returning (*anāgāmin*), candidates for and fruits of arhatship (*arhat*), and candidates for and awakening of a pratyekabuddha attain increased brilliance.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the medicinal herbs and species—the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) and other practices, as well as *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*—of all the world’s bodhisattva mahāsattvas become increasingly radiant.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the stars and constellations—the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, those in training (*śaikṣa*), and those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*)—of all the world become increasingly radiant.

Thus, by depending upon and because of the full moon disc of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, all the mountains, great oceans, bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of all the world become increasingly radiant.

“Kauśika! When the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have not yet appeared in the world, it is only the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, possessing skillful means, correctly proclaim all mundane and supramundane dharmas for the sake of sentient beings.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
You should know that it is because the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able to give birth to all the vehicles of humans, gods, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the unsurpassed vehicle.
“Kauśika! All the skillful means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are produced and grow from this very profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), they are able to practice the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*), and they are able to practice the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), they are able to practice internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*); they are able to practice external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersed emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), unchanging emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*).”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to practice true suchness (tathatā), and are able to practice the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), they are able to practice the noble truth of suffering, and they are able to practice the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, and they are able to practice the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to practice the gate of liberation of emptiness, and they are able to practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to attain the five eyes and are able to attain the six supernormal powers.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), they are able to attain the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha; they are able to attain the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), great compassion (*karuṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*muditā*), great equanimity (*upekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*).”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), they are able to attain the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) and are able to attain the state of constant abiding in equanimity (upekṣā).”
“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), they are able to attain all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), they are able to attain all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to attain the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks of physical excellence.”
“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they do not fall into the stage of the śrāvaka, nor do they realize the stage of the pratyekabuddha.”
“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to bring sentient beings to maturity and are able to adorn and purify buddha-fields.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means, they are able to fully acquire the perfection of lifespan; they are able to fully acquire the perfection of requisites, the perfection of the pure land, the perfection of lineage, the perfection of physical form and strength, and the perfection of retinue.”

“Kauśika! Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), they are able to practice the ten stages (bhūmi) and other such practices of a bodhisattva, and are able to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).”
“Kauśika! Thus, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and all their skillful means are accomplished through the perfection of wisdom.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters with sincere hearts hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, they shall achieve the meritorious benefits and superior advantages of both the present and the future."
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, how shall they achieve the accomplishment of present meritorious benefits?”
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, with sincere hearts, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, these good sons and good daughters shall, in the present life, not be struck by poison, harmed by weapons, burned by fire, or drowned by water; they shall even not meet an untimely death from the four hundred and four diseases, except for those karmic results fixed in the past that must be experienced in the present life.”

“Kauśika! If these sons and daughters of good family encounter legal troubles or are oppressed by enemies and bandits, and they recite this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere heart, when they arrive at those places, they will ultimately not be subjected to punishment or harm by them.”
Why is this? It is because the majestic power and influence of such Prajñāpāramitā cause phenomena to be thus. "Kauśika!

If these sons and daughters of good family go to the presence of kings, princes, or ministers, and with a sincere heart recite this Prajñāpāramitā, they will certainly be greeted with joy, questioned with courtesy, and honored with praise by those kings and others.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are always not separated from the minds of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity toward sentient beings.

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, copy, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, they shall achieve various such meritorious benefits and advantages in the present life.”
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters with sincere hearts hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, how shall they achieve the future merits and benefits?”
The Buddha said:
“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a sincere mind, [engage] with this Prajñāpāramitā...”
Those sons and daughters of good family who hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study,
reflect according to principle, transcribe, explain, and cause [this teaching] to be widely disseminated, will, in whatever place they are born,
never be separated from the ten paths of wholesome action; such are these sons and daughters of good family.
In whatever place these good men and good women are born, they shall never be separated from such practices as generosity, observing the fasts, and upholding the precepts;

likewise, in whatever place they are born, they shall never be separated from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers. These good men...
These virtuous women, wherever they are born, will never be separated from the perfection of generosity,
the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence,
the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom; these sons and daughters of good family—
Women and others, wherever they are born, shall never be separated from internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness,
the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, and self-emptiness.
The emptiness of marks, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unobtainable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— by these, sons and daughters of good family,
wherever they may be born, shall never be separated from suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and the non-illusory.
Nature, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*),
the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)— in whatever place these sons and daughters of good family are born,
they shall never be separated from the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin [of Suffering], and the Noble Truth of Cessation.

The Noble Truths and the Noble Truth of the Path: these sons and daughters of good family, wherever they are born, will never be separated from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;
these sons and daughters of good family, wherever they are born, will never be separated from the four foundations of mindfulness.
The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment,
and the eightfold noble path— by virtue of these, good sons and good daughters, wherever they are born,
shall never be separated from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. This is...
These sons and daughters of good family shall achieve the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
these sons and daughters of good family shall achieve the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges,
great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities.
By means of these unique qualities of a Buddha, these sons and daughters of good family shall achieve the quality of non-forgetfulness and abide eternally in equanimity;
these sons and daughters of good family shall achieve all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi. These sons and daughters of good family...
These virtuous women shall attain the realization of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

These sons and daughters of good family shall never fall into any of the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of hungry ghosts, except when they intentionally take birth in those states through the power of their vows in order to mature sentient beings. This is the excellence [of these virtuous ones].
These sons and daughters of good family will, in whatever place they are born, always possess all their faculties and limbs without deficiency;

these sons and daughters of good family will never be born into poverty, low station, the households of artisans, various mixed classes, or the families of *pukkasa*s; these sons and daughters of good family will forever...
These sons and daughters of good family will not be born into the families of butchers, fishermen, hunters, thieves, jailers, or *caṇḍālas*; rather,
they will always be born into noble and prestigious families— whether those of *kṣatriyas*, *brāhmaṇas*,
or various elders and householders— and they will never be born among the *śūdras*.
The Luo family;

these sons and daughters of good family, wherever they are born, will have their bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics, so that all sentient beings who see them will rejoice;
these sons and daughters of good family will mostly be reborn in the pure lands where Buddhas dwell, being born by transformation from lotus flowers and refraining from committing evil karma.

These sons and daughters of good family shall never be separated from swift supernatural powers; according to their wishes, they shall travel through various Buddha-fields, proceeding from one Buddha-land to another, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they shall hear the True Dharma, bring sentient beings to maturity, adorn and purify Buddha-fields, and gradually realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with sincere hearts, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, transcribe, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, they shall achieve all such various merits and benefits of the future.”
"For this reason, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters wish to attain such benefits and merits in the present and the future, and never be separated from them until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, write down, explain, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā. Furthermore, they should make offerings with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, many wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps."
At that time, a great multitude of non-Buddhist brahmins came to where the Buddha was in order to seek out the Buddha’s faults.
When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw them, he thought to himself:
"Now these many non-Buddhist brahmins are approaching this Dharma assembly seeking to find shortcomings in the Buddha; could this not be an obstacle created by Prajñā?"
"I shall recite the profound Prajñāpāramitā as I have received it from the Buddha, so that those followers of heterodoxy may return by the way they came.
Having thought this, he then recited the profound Prajñāpāramitā.

Thereupon, the various non-Buddhist ascetics and brahmins who had come there manifested signs of reverence from afar, circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right, and withdrew to their original places.
At that time, Śāriputra, having seen this, thought to himself:
"For what reason did they come and then depart?"
The Buddha, knowing their thoughts, addressed Śāriputra:

"Those non-Buddhists have come together seeking an opportunity against me; however, by the power of the Great King of Mantras, the Prajñāpāramitā, recited by Śakra, Lord of the Devas, they have been made to turn back."
Śāriputra! I do not see even a single wholesome dharma among those non-Buddhists; they all harbor evil intentions and come to me for the sake of finding an opportunity against me.
Śāriputra!

Among all beings in the world—whether gods, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, or those of other paths—I do not see anyone who would dare to harbor ill intent and come seeking the Prajñāpāramitā with the hope of finding an opportunity [to harm it].
Why is this? Śāriputra!
Within this trichiliocosm, all the gods of the Four Great Kings and the Heaven of the Thirty-three...
The gods of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven,
the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, all the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods,
the Mahābrahmā gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Parīttābha gods, the Apramāṇābha gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, and the Śubhakṛtsna gods.
The Śuddhāvāsa deities, the Apramāṇaśubha deities, the Śubhakṛtsna deities, the Vṛhatphala deities, the Parīttaśubha deities,
the Apramāṇaśubha deities, the Bṛhatphala deities, the Avṛha deities, the Atapa deities,
the Sudṛśa deities, the Sudarśana deities, and the Akaniṣṭha deities— all śrāvakas and all pratyekabuddhas— [attain this].
All bodhisattva mahāsattvas, myself, and all those endowed with great power—
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
mahoragas, humans, and non-humans alike— all together shall protect this Prajñāpāramitā.
They shall not cause any evil obstacles.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
This is because all these devas and others are born from the *prajñāpāramitā*.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, in each of the Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas; all śrāvakas; all pratyekabuddhas; all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all together protect this *prajñāpāramitā*, so that no evil may cause obstacles or hindrances.
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because all those Buddhas and others are born from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
At that time, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:

"Now the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is surrounded by the fourfold assembly, and all the devas and humans of the desire and form realms have gathered together to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā. Within this assembly, there will surely be a bodhisattva mahāsattva who receives a prediction of his future attainment of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; I should go there to destroy his vision."
Having formed this thought, he manifested the fourfold army and, displaying fierce and sharp valor, approached the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw him and thought:
"Could it be that the Evil Māra has manifested these things, coming here wishing to vex the Buddha and create obstacles for the Prajñāpāramitā?"

Why is this? These four divisions of troops are so magnificently adorned and exquisite that they cannot be equaled by the fourfold superior forces of King Bimbisāra of Magadha; nor can they be equaled by the fourfold superior forces of King Prasenajit of Kośala; nor can they be equaled by the fourfold superior forces of the Śākya royal clan of Kapilavastu; nor can they be equaled by the fourfold superior forces of the Licchavi clan of Vaiśālī; nor can they be equaled by the fourfold superior forces of the Malla royal clan of Aṅga. Observing these four divisions of troops in this way, it is certain that they have been conjured by the Evil Māra.

For a long night, Māra has constantly watched for the Buddha’s shortcomings, seeking to destroy the sublime deeds cultivated by sentient beings; I shall now recite the profound Prajñāpāramitā as received from the Buddha, so that this evil Māra may be sent back on his way.

Then, having thought this, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, recited the profound Prajñāpāramitā; thereupon the evil Māra retreated to his own abode, because he had been driven away by the power of the Great Dharani King of the profound Prajñāpāramitā.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 105 [and] Fascicle 106.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirty-Four: The First Section on Measuring Merit.

At that time, all those present in the assembly, from the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, simultaneously manifested various celestial flowers, robes, necklaces, and fragrant garlands. Leaping into the air, they scattered them over the Buddha, joined their palms in reverence, and together addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We pray that this Prajñāpāramitā may long abide among the people of Jambudvīpa."

Why is this? As long as the *prajñāpāramitā* circulates among the people of Jambudvīpa, it should be known that in this place the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Bhikṣu Saṃgha will abide for a long time without perishing. It is likewise so throughout this trichiliocosm, and even in the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless Buddha-fields of the ten directions; by this, the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and their sublime practices may also be understood.
"Bhagavān!

In whatever region there may be sons or daughters of good family who, with pure faith, write down, uphold, revere, and make offerings to this profound Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that in those places there will be wondrous radiance; it shall dispel darkness and give rise to manifold benefits."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the other hosts of devas, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

As long as the *prajñāpāramitā* circulates among the people of Jambudvīpa, you should know that in this place the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus will abide for a long time without perishing. It is likewise so throughout this trichiliocosm and even in the infinite, countless, and boundless buddha-fields of the ten directions; by this, the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas and their sublime practices may also be known.

In whatever region or town there may be sons or daughters of good family who, with pure faith, write down, uphold, revere, and make offerings to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that in those places there will be sublime radiance; it shall dispel all darkness and give rise to manifold benefits.
Then, the hosts of devas further manifested various kinds of exquisite celestial flowers, garments, necklaces, and fragrant garlands, scattering them over the Buddha, and addressed him again, saying:

"If good sons and good daughters, with a sincere mind, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, and contemplate according to principle this Prajñāpāramitā, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings..."

These sons and daughters of good family will find no opportunity for Māra and his retinue; we gods shall also constantly follow these sons and daughters of good family, diligently providing protection so that they suffer no harm or affliction.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are honored and served by us gods as if they were Buddhas, or because we respect the Dharma as if it were close to the Buddha.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If sons or daughters of good family wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this Prajñāpāramitā according to the truth, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings—these sons or daughters of good family have not accomplished this through meager roots of virtue. They must have, in previous lives, accumulated many roots of virtue in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas, made many true aspirations, made many offerings to the Buddhas, and been sustained by many spiritual friends; only then can they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this profound Prajñāpāramitā according to the truth, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings.
"Blessed One!

Those who wish to attain the all-knowing wisdom of all Buddhas should seek the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā); those who wish to attain the perfection of wisdom should seek the all-knowing wisdom of all Buddhas."

Why is this? Because all the omniscient wisdom attained by the Buddhas arises from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and likewise, this perfection of wisdom arises from the omniscient wisdom of all the Buddhas.

Why is this so? The knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) attained by the Buddhas is not different from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and this perfection of wisdom is not different from the knowledge of all modes attained by the Buddhas. One should know that the knowledge of all modes attained by the Buddhas and this perfection of wisdom are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
As you have said, Kauśika!

Those who wish to attain the all-knowledge of all Buddhas should seek the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā); those who wish to attain the perfection of wisdom should seek the all-knowledge of all Buddhas.

Why is this? Because all the omniscient wisdom attained by the Buddhas arises from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and likewise, this perfection of wisdom arises from the omniscient wisdom of all the Buddhas.

Why is this so? The omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas is not different from the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*); likewise, this perfection of wisdom is not different from the omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas. One should know that the omniscient wisdom attained by all Buddhas and this perfection of wisdom are non-dual and cannot be divided into two parts; therefore, the merit and majestic power of the perfection of wisdom are most rare and marvelous.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One,

for what reason do you not extensively praise the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, and the perfection of meditative concentration, but instead only extensively praise the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason do you not extensively praise internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, but instead extensively praise only the *prajñāpāramitā*?”

“World-Honored One, for what reason do you not extensively praise suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, but instead extensively praise only the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason do you not extensively praise the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin, the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path, but instead extensively praise only the Perfection of Wisdom?”
