How does one cultivate the four dhyānas by dedicating them toward omniscience?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the four dhyānas; this is called cultivating the four dhyānas while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; this is called cultivating the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the eight liberations by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!”

By employing non-duality as a means, non-arising as a means, and non-apprehension as a means, one cultivates the eight liberations; this is called cultivating the eight liberations while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes while cultivating the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?
“Ānanda! [The Buddha replied.]

Using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; this is called cultivating the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By employing non-duality as a means, non-arising as a means, and non-apprehension as a means, one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness; this is called cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

How does one cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes?”

“Ānanda! By means of non-duality as the skillful method, non-arising as the skillful method, and non-apprehension as the skillful method, one cultivates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path. This is called cultivating the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path while dedicating them toward omniscience.”
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness by dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!

Using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the gate of liberation that is emptiness; this is called cultivating the gate of liberation that is emptiness while dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the gateways of signlessness and wishlessness while dedicating [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!”

Using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; this is called cultivating the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness while dedicating [the merit] toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the five eyes by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the five eyes; this is called cultivating the five eyes while dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the six supernormal powers by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one cultivates the six supernormal powers; this is called cultivating the six supernormal powers while dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!

By means of non-duality as a skillful method, non-arising as a skillful method, and non-apprehension as a skillful method, one cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha; this is called cultivating the ten powers of a Buddha while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!

How does one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes while cultivating the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. This is called dedicating toward omniscience while cultivating the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness by dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness; this is called cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness by dedicating it toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity while dedicating it toward omniscience?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, one cultivates the constant abiding in equanimity; this is called cultivating the constant abiding in equanimity while dedicating it toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate all-knowledge by dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!”

Using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates all-knowledge; this is called dedicating toward the knowledge of all modes while cultivating all-knowledge.
“World-Honored One!
How does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) while cultivating the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)?
“Ānanda! [the Buddha replied.]

By means of non-duality as the skillful method, non-arising as the skillful method, and non-apprehension as the skillful method, one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and all-aspect knowledge; this is called cultivating the knowledge of the aspects of the path and all-aspect knowledge while dedicating them toward omniscience.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate all dharani-doors by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes?
“Ananda! [the Buddha replied.]

By employing non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, one cultivates all dharani-doors; this is called dedicating toward the knowledge of all modes while cultivating all dharani-doors.
“World-Honored One!
How does one cultivate all gateways of samādhi by dedicating them toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!”

By employing non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, one cultivates all gateways to samādhi; this is called dedicating toward the knowledge of all modes while cultivating all gateways to samādhi.
“World-Honored One!
How does one practice the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path by dedicating it toward omniscience? “Ānanda!”

By employing non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means, one cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is called cultivating the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva by dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“World-Honored One!
How does one practice unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by dedicating [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes? “Ānanda!”

By employing non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, one cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; this is called cultivating unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment while dedicating it toward the knowledge of all modes.
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

By means of non-arising as the skillful method and non-apprehension as the skillful method, how does one dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?”

By means of non-arising as the expedient and non-apprehension as the expedient, how does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
By means of non-arising as the expedient and non-apprehension as the expedient, how does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm?
“World-Honored One!
By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”

By means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means, how does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?
“World-Honored One!
By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?”

By means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means, how does one dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”

By means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means, how does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?

“Bhagavān, by means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

By means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means, how does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”

By means of non-arising as the expedient and non-apprehension as the expedient, how does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?
“World-Honored One!
By what means of non-duality does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?
By what means of non-arising and by what means of non-apprehension does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 106 (and 107).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter One: Section on the Measurement of Merit, Part Thirty-Five.
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

By means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means, how does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
“World-Honored One!
By means of what non-duality as a skillful means do they dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”

By means of what skillful means of non-arising and skillful means of non-apprehension does one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?
“World-Honored One!

By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the knowledge of all, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”

By means of what skillful method of non-arising and skillful method of non-apprehension does one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the knowledge of all modes, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?
“World-Honored One!
By means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”

By means of what skillful means of non-arising and skillful means of non-apprehension does one dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?
“World-Honored One!
By means of what non-duality as a skillful means do they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?

By means of what non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of what non-apprehension as a skillful means, do they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Bhagavān, by means of what non-duality as a skillful means does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed,

perfect enlightenment? By means of what non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of what non-apprehensibility as a skillful means, does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?”
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

You should now know that by means of the non-duality of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñājñāna), abiding in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge and dwells in internal emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), abiding in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the state of non-falsity, the state of non-alteration, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu).

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge, abiding in suchness and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;

by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path."
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;

by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path."
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six superknowledges;

by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six superknowledges.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates toward all-knowledge and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), and cultivates all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).

By means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge, and cultivates all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors;

by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors."
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;

by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:
by means of the non-duality of form, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;

by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment."
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*), by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

and by means of the non-duality of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, one dedicates toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and abides in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of own-marks, emptiness of common marks, emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of own-nature, and the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence.”

By means of the non-duality of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*). One abides in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension as the method for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.”

The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha,

saying: “World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
The Buddha said,
“Ānanda! Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form.”
Why is this? Because the nature of form is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form. Why is this?

“Ānanda! Feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty of the nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Why is this?

“Ānanda! Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of form is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

"Because the nature of the sense-field of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?"
“Ānanda! The sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is non-dual and indivisible from internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in internal emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-base and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and abides in suchness (tathatā), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The sense base of form is empty of the nature of the sense base of form. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense-base of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this so?
Because the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?"
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty, it is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-bases such as the eye, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sphere of form is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
"World-Honored One!

How, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?"
“Ānanda! The sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and dwells in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?
“Ānanda! The sense-base of the eye is empty of the nature of the sense-base of the eye. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-sphere of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The sense base of form is empty of the nature of the sense base of form. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense-field of form is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?

“Ānanda! The sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena. Why is this?

Because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and because it is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of emptiness of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?

“Because the nature of the sense-field of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—are empty of their own nature. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of an eye-base. Why is this?

Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

by means of the non-duality of the eye-base and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?

Because the nature of the sense-base of form is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and is thus non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the gates of liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?"

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sense-base of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?"
“Ānanda! The bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the gates of liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How, by means of the non-duality of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
Why is this? Because...”
Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The sense-base of form is empty of the nature of the sense-base of form. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sense-base of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is non-dual with and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-field of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?

Because the nature of the sense-field of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
