by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāra*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?

“Because the nature of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*).

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?

Because the nature of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-sphere of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sphere of form is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and is thus non-dual and indivisible from omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?
This is because the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?
“Because the nature of emptiness of the sense-field of form is non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, by means of their non-arising, and by means of their non-apprehensibility, dedicate toward the knowledge of all-knowledge and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and because this is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-sphere of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sense base of the eye is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of emptiness of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-dual with and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The sense-base of form is empty of the nature of the sense-base of form. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sense-field of form is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?
Because the nature of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and this is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Thus it is, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-base, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The eye-base is empty of the nature of the eye-base. Why is that?
"Because the nature of the eye-base is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! The sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Why is this?
Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is non-dual with and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of the eye and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of form, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The sphere of form is empty of the nature of the sphere of form. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the sense-field of form is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—is empty. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is empty, and is therefore non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the sense-base of form and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty. Why is this?
This is because the nature of the eye-sphere is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition—these are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact—as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-faculty and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] to omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?
Because the nature of the ear-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of sounds, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition—the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nose-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?
Because the nature of the nose element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact—and of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—the nature of these fragrance element, nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the nose-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] to the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the tongue-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehensibility, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) while practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The body element is empty of the nature of the body element. Why is this?
Because the nature of the body-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality, the non-arising, and the non-apprehensibility of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the contact of the body—as well as all feelings produced with that bodily contact as a condition—dedicate [these merits] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the body-contact that arises with body-contact as its condition—namely, all feelings—is empty, and is thus non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the body-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the mental element (*manodhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) while practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the mental faculty (*manodhātu*) is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, and mental contact—and by means of that which is produced with mental contact as its condition, namely sensation—employ the skillful means of non-arising and the skillful means of non-apprehension to dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and thereby cultivate the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the mind-consciousness realm, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—the nature of these is empty. The dharma-realm, the mind-consciousness realm, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are by nature empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, the mental-consciousness realm, and the contact of the mind—as well as all sensations produced with that mental contact as a condition—is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the mind-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the eye-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from that inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition—these, Ānanda, are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, is non-dual and indivisible from internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-faculty and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and dwells in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and dwell in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the ear-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from that inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehension, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the body-contact that arises with body-contact as its condition—the various feelings produced therefrom—is non-dual and indivisible from internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the body-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and abides in internal emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the mind-element (*manodhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”

“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising, by means of non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”

Because the nature of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are empty of intrinsic nature; they are non-dual and indivisible from suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

“World-Honored One!
