Part One: Chapter Thirty, Section Thirteen: "The Measurement of Merit. "World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?"
“Ānanda! The eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty. Why is this?

Because the nature of the eye-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these merits] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—these have the nature of emptiness. The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-faculty and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the ear-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality, the non-arising, and the non-apprehensibility of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—dedicate [these roots of goodness] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and the various feelings arising with ear-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nose-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the nose element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition—the nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and the sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the nose-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The tongue element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the tongue element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the tongue-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these roots of goodness] toward all-knowledge wisdom (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—the nature of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience while cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The body element is empty of the nature of the body element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the body-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the contact of the body—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is empty of intrinsic nature, and is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the body-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the mind-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the mind-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact—and by means of that which is produced with mental contact as its condition, as well as by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—all these have the nature of emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and the contact of the mind, as well as the various feelings produced with that mental contact as a condition, is empty of intrinsic nature; and because it is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the mind-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty. Why is this?

“Because the nature of the eye-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of non-duality, non-arising, and non-apprehension regarding the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, dedicate [these merits] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition—these are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, is empty (*śūnya*) and non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gate of liberation of signlessness (*ānimitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the form realm and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the ear-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings arising with ear-contact as their condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The element of sound, the element of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—the nature of the element of sound, the element of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and the contact of the ear—as well as all sensations produced with that contact as a condition—is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nose-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the nose-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—the nature of these, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and the sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is emptiness; and because this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the nose-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the tongue-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these merits] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*)?”
“Ānanda! The body element is empty of the nature of a body element. Why is this?

“Because the nature of the body-element is empty and non-dual, indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these roots of merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of these elements of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the tangible-object element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), and the body-contact (*kāyasparśa*)—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—is emptiness, and this is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the body-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the mind-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Why is this?

“Because the nature of the mind-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact—as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—the nature of these is empty. The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, the consciousness-realm, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness liberation gate, the signlessness liberation gate, and the wishlessness liberation gate.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the mind-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the eye-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—these, Ānanda, are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is emptiness, and this is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-faculty and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the ear-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One!

How, by means of the non-duality of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"

“Ānanda! The element of sound, the element of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—the nature of the element of sound, the element of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nose-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the nose-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and the contact of the nose—as well as the various feelings produced with that nose-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"

“Ānanda! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are empty of the intrinsic nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the realm of fragrance, the realm of nose-consciousness, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the nose-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the tongue-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the five eyes and the six superknowledges?"

“Ānanda! The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The body element is empty of the nature of the body element. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), and the body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), as well as the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising (*anutpāda*) as the skillful means and non-apprehension (*anupalambha*) as the skillful means—dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”

“Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of these elements of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the body-contact that arises with body-contact as its condition—all these feelings—are empty of intrinsic nature, and they are non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the body-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the mind-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).
“World-Honored One!

How, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition—by means of non-arising (*anutpāda*) and non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha*)—does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the five eyes and the six superknowledges?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—the nature of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and the contact of the mind—as well as all feelings produced with that mental contact as a condition—is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the mental element (*manodhātu*) and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The eye-element is empty of the nature of the eye-element. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the eye-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—these are empty of the intrinsic nature of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers (*daśabala*), four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the ear-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these merits] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The element of sound, the element of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—the nature of the element of sound, the element of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nose-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the nose-element is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the realm of fragrance, the realm of nose-consciousness, and nose-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—the nature of these, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the nose-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element (*jihvādhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The tongue element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the tongue element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the tongue-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition—these have the nature of emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The body element is empty of the nature of the body element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the body-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact—as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these merits] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of these elements of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and the body-contact that arises with body-contact as its condition—all such feelings—are empty of intrinsic nature, and they are non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the body-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the mind-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The mind-element is empty of the nature of the mind-element. Why is this?

Because the nature of the mind-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the consciousness-realm, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—by means of non-arising and non-apprehension—dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—the nature of these is empty. The dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the mind-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eye-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The eye-faculty is empty of the nature of the eye-faculty. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the eye-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact— as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition— by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [these merits] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! The form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—the nature of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eye-faculty and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the roots of virtue] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the ear-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The ear-element is empty of the nature of the ear-element. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāra*).

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition— by means of non-arising (*anutpāda*) and non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha*)— dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”

“Ānanda! The sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition—the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition, is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and all sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nose-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The nose element is empty of the nature of the nose element. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the nose-element is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact— and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition— by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! The fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition—the nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the nose-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?
“Ānanda! The tongue element is empty of the nature of the tongue element. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is empty, it is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*).

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) arising with tongue-contact as a condition, and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension, dedicate [these] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā-jñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—these, Ānanda, are empty of the intrinsic nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is empty, and this is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the tongue-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the body-element, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The body-element is empty of the nature of the body-element. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*).

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition— by means of non-arising (*anutpāda*) as the expedient and non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha*) as the expedient— dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—the nature of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is empty.”

Why is this? “Ānanda! The element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—the nature of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—is empty.”

by means of the non-duality of the ear-element and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
