How does one, by means of the non-duality of ignorance, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of ignorance and the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual and indivisible.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, dedicate [these roots of goodness] toward all-knowledge, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—these formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of ignorance and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of ignorance, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of ignorance is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

"World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—these formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Because the nature of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of ignorance and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of ignorance, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of ignorance is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!...”

How does one, by means of non-duality, non-arising, and non-apprehension regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, dedicate [these] toward the knowledge of all aspects and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?

“Ānanda! Formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—these formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Because the nature of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of ignorance and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the roots of virtue] toward omniscience and cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of ignorance, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of ignorance is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of non-duality, non-arising, and non-apprehension regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?

“Ānanda! Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the nature of volitional formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of ignorance and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of ignorance, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of ignorance and the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and indivisible.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"

“Ānanda! Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—these formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of ignorance and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of ignorance, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! Ignorance is empty of the nature of ignorance. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of ignorance and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and not divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—these, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, are empty of the nature of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

Why is this? Because the nature of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of ignorance and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
Because inner emptiness is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, those perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [the merit] to the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of that [emptiness] itself, are non-dual and indivisible from those perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension—such as internal emptiness and so forth—one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all dharmas, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
Because inner emptiness is empty of its own nature, and because it is non-dual and indivisible from that inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, ...”
The emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration,
emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable,
emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The two are skillful means; non-arising is skillful means; non-apprehension is skillful means.

One dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and abides in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, and non-...

What are the emptiness of limits, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abides in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 117; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Scroll 118.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Part One: Chapter Thirty, Section Sixteen: “The Evaluation of Merit. “World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of internal emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the nature of being free from birth (anupapattidharmatā), the fixed nature of dharmas (dharmasthititā), the stability of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu)?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
Because inner emptiness is empty of itself and is non-dual and indivisible from suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, and ultimate emptiness...”
The emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The two are skillful means, non-arising is skillful means, and non-apprehension is skillful means; they dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes,
abiding in suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the state of non-falsity,
the state of non-alteration, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, and the stability of phenomena.
“The reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the sphere of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable sphere (*acintyadhātu*)? “Ānanda!

The emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal-external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth (*paramārthaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), the absolute emptiness (*atyantaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāraśūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāraśūnyatā*), the emptiness of essential nature (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*), the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambhaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāvaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāvaśūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*). From the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, these are the emptinesses.”
Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, is non-dual and indivisible from suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and abides in suchness up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
"Because inner emptiness is empty of itself, it is non-dual and indivisible from the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising, non-apprehension, and non-attainment as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience while abiding in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?"

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
Because inner emptiness as emptiness and the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are non-dual and not divided into two.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience while cultivating the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
"Because inner emptiness as emptiness and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and not divided into two.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases?

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are themselves empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and emptiness itself, are non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”

Because inner emptiness is empty and non-dual, indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”

"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising as a skillful means and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of essential nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—all are empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of emptiness itself, are non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
Because inner emptiness is empty of itself and is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— by means of non-arising as a skillful means and non-apprehension as a skillful means— dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six superknowledges?”

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of emptiness itself, are non-dual with and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness. Why is this?

Because inner emptiness as emptiness and the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unobtainable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising as a skillful means and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of the nature of things themselves, are non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness. Why is that?
“Because inner emptiness is empty of itself and non-dual and indivisible from the qualities of non-forgetfulness and constant equanimity.

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the qualities of non-forgetfulness and constant equanimity?”

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the nature of emptiness itself, are non-dual with and indivisible from the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
This is because inner emptiness as emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising as a skillful means and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of the nature of non-existence itself, are non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
Because inner emptiness is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!...”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are all empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of emptiness itself, are non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
"Because inner emptiness is empty of itself and is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising as a skillful means and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, limitless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), and the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! Internal emptiness is empty of the nature of internal emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”
"Because inner emptiness is empty of itself, it is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are empty.”

Why is this? Because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the emptiness of that [emptiness] itself, are non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as internal emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of suchness is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the dharma-realm, and so forth, up to the nature of the inconceivable realm.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence?”
“Ānanda! True suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is non-dual and indivisible from that inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*).
[Subhūti said: 'World-Honored One!
How is it that the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the non-alteration (*ananyathātā*), and the level..."

By means of the non-duality of sameness, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*),
and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*); by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension,
they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-and-external emptiness.
Emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned,
absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,

the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, and the emptiness of non-existence.
“Emptiness, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence? “Ānanda!

The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—their nature is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of suchness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! True suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) and that *tathatā*, up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!

How, by means of the non-duality of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm; and by means of non-arising as the expedient and non-apprehension as the expedient, does one dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and abide in *tathatā*, the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsehood, the non-alteration, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature.”
Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of suchness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! True suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness. Why is this?”
“Because the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; by means of non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and abide in the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsehood, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the dharma-realm, and so forth, up to the nature of the inconceivable realm.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of suchness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and dwells securely in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality in true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of suchness and the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience while practicing the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the dharma-realm, and so forth, up to the nature of the inconceivable realm.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of true thusness and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*)?

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! True thusness is empty of the nature of true thusness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of suchness is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension—through the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm—dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsehood of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the inconceivable realm.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?

"Because the nature of true thusness (tathatā) being empty and the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsehood of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature of phenomena free from arising, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?
“Because the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) and emptiness are non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”

“Ānanda! The realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the realm of phenomena.”
Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness (*tathatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 118. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Measuring Merit, Number Thirty, Section Seventeen. “World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of true thusness and the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means—through the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsehood of phenomena, the unchanging nature of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm—dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness (*tathatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?

“Because the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) and the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the unchanging nature (*ananyathābhāvatā*), equality (*samatā*), the nature of being free from birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—by means of non-arising (*anutpāda*) as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha*) as the skillful means—dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as *tathatā*, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of true thusness is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!...”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

“Ānanda!
