The dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm—these, from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, are empty of their own nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as *tathatā*, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! True suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of true thusness is non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi?

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsehood of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the nature of the dharma-realm, and so forth, up to the nature of the inconceivable realm.”
Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness (*tathatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! Suchness is empty of the nature of suchness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) and the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśa-dhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintya-dhātu*)—by means of non-arising as the skillful means and non-apprehension as the skillful means—dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of their own nature.”
Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! True suchness is empty of the nature of true suchness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of *tathatā* (suchness) and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension—dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—all these are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is non-dual with and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality such as true thusness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

This is because the noble truth of suffering is empty of intrinsic nature and is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

"Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because..."

Because the nature of emptiness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the nature of departure from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”

“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding the noble truth of suffering, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering,

origin, cessation, and the path. "Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?"
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation,
and the path, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless concentrations?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
"Because the nature of emptiness of the noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience while cultivating the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience while cultivating the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”

“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—these noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality regarding the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of goodness] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—these noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the four applications of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

This is because the noble truth of suffering, being empty of intrinsic nature, is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
"Because the nature of emptiness of the noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the noble truth of suffering is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—these noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
"World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of its non-arising, and by means of its non-apprehensibility, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?

Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
"World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”

Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), and cultivates all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all-knowledge and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is that?
This is because the emptiness of the nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Noble Truth of Suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
“Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”

“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the nature of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the noble truth of suffering is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment. "World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward all-knowledge and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! The noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the nature of the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the noble truth of suffering and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and the others, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and abides in inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas (dharmasthititā), the stability of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient for the perfection of giving, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience while cultivating the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and the other perfections, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of giving is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving.
Why is this? Because—”

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience while cultivating the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of their non-arising; and by means of their non-apprehensibility, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience while cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate the perfection of giving toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the liberation door of emptiness, the liberation door of signlessness, and the liberation door of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of the non-arising [of phenomena]; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?”

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and the others, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity.
Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.

"World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient—namely, the perfection of generosity and the others—one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 119. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Measuring Merit, Number Thirty, Section Eighteen. "World-Honored One!..."

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate the perfection of generosity toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward omniscience, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity and the quality of non-forgetfulness, as well as the state of constant equanimity, are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [these merits] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?

“Ānanda! The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the very nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of the perfection of giving, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?

“Because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?

“Ānanda! The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
This is because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of generosity is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi?”

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and the other perfections, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva through the perfection of giving?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of giving is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient—namely, the perfection of generosity and the others—one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfection of giving, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The perfection of giving is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving. Why is this?
"Because the nature of emptiness of the perfection of generosity and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! The perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the nature of these perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the perfection of generosity and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four dhyānas as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the four dhyānas is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehensible, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the four immeasurables and four formless attainments are empty of intrinsic nature.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the nature of emptiness are non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four dhyānas and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four dhyānas as a method of non-duality, as a method of non-arising, and as a method of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the four dhyānas is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and abide in inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence?”
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions—the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions—are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, being empty by nature, are non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four dhyānas and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and abides in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four dhyānas as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the four dhyānas is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm. “World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions—the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions—are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?
Because the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the nature of emptiness are non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of the four dhyānas and so forth, employing non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), abiding in suchness (tathatā) up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four dhyānas as a non-dual expedient, as an expedient of non-arising, and as an expedient of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the four dhyānas is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the four dhyānas and so forth, employing non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the four dhyānas is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the four immeasurables and four formless attainments are empty of intrinsic nature.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four dhyānas, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four dhyānas as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the four dhyānas is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments—are empty of intrinsic nature. Why is this?

This is because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, being empty by nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four dhyānas and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten pervasive bases.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four dhyānas as a non-dual expedient, as an expedient of non-arising, and as an expedient of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“World-Honored One!

by means of the non-duality of the four dhyānas and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.

Because the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.

by means of the non-duality of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“Ānanda! The four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are empty of intrinsic nature.

Because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, being empty by nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.

By means of the four dhyānas and so forth, employing non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

by means of the non-duality of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
