“Ānanda! The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases; by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"

“Ānanda! The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the eight liberations as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*)—using non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehensibility as the skillful means—dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative absorptions, and the ten universal bases is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 123, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Measuring Merits, Number Thirty, Section Nineteen. “World-Honored One!...”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; by means of non-arising as the expedient and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! The eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases is emptiness, and this is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations as a skillful means, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?

“Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*)—using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

“Ānanda! The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations is non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
"World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten universal bases (*kṛtsnāyatana*)—using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?

“Ānanda! The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases is non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations as a skillful means, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations and the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and indivisible.

"World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward all-knowledge wisdom and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"

“Ānanda! The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities—is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases is non-dual with and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations as a skillful means, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the eight liberations and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! The eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—the nature of the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases is empty, and thus they are non-dual with and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the eight liberations and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The four applications of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of the four applications of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four applications of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the four right endeavors, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—by means of non-duality as the method, non-arising as the method, and non-apprehension as the method—dedicate [the roots of virtue] to the knowledge of all modes and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and abides in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The four applications of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the space-element, and the inconceivable realm?"

“Ānanda! The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty, and is thus non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and abides in suchness (tathatā), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and dwells in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The four applications of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and indivisible.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?”

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [these] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
This is because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness and the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means—dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty, and this emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The four applications of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six superknowledges?"

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal knowledges.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The four applications of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—using non-duality as the means, non-arising as the means, and non-apprehension as the means—dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"

“Ānanda! The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path—by means of non-duality as the method, non-arising as the method, and non-apprehension as the method—dedicate [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?

“Ānanda! The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—through the skillful means of non-duality, the skillful means of non-arising, and the skillful means of non-apprehension—dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī gates and all samādhi gates.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness and the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual and indivisible.

"Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatā) and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"

“Ānanda! The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the nature of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path is empty.”

Why is this? Because the nature of emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient—namely, the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth—one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is that?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path—are empty of intrinsic nature.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness. Why is that?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the door of liberation of emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the signless and wishless doors of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gateways to liberation such as emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as a non-dual expedient, as an expedient of non-arising, and as an expedient of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness as the gate of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from internal emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—as a skillful means, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth as non-dual, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and dwells in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
“Because the nature of emptiness as a door of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?
Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the doors of liberation— signlessness and wishlessness— is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
For this reason, it is said:

by means of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth as non-dual, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness as a door of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the liberation door of emptiness and so forth as non-dual, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge and dwells in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
"World-Honored One!..."

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?
This is because the nature of emptiness of the signless and wishless doors of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.

by means of the non-duality of the gateways to liberation such as emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of the liberation door of emptiness, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness as a gate of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases.

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—as a skillful means, and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the emptiness liberation door and the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-dual and indivisible.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—as a skillful means, and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the signless and wishless doors of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gateways to liberation such as emptiness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the liberation door of emptiness, the liberation door of signlessness, and the liberation door of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness as a door of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the door of liberation of emptiness, the door of liberation of signlessness, and the door of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the gateway of liberation of emptiness, the gateway of liberation of signlessness, and the gateway of liberation of wishlessness?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the signless and wishless gates of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of the liberation door of emptiness, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gates of liberation through signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six superknowledges?"
