Because the nature of emptiness of the doors of liberation— signlessness and wishlessness— is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

Using the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth as the means of non-duality, using non-arising as the means, and using non-apprehension as the means, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
"Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—as a skillful means, and by means of non-arising and non-apprehension as skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 121. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Measuring Merits, Number Thirty, Section Twenty. "World-Honored One!..."

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness characterized by non-duality, characterized by non-arising, and characterized by non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness and the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the gates of liberation through signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the gateways to liberation— signlessness and wishlessness— is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the gate of liberation of emptiness as non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient of the liberation door of emptiness, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the door of liberation through emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?
“Ānanda! The gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are empty of the nature of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates all-knowledge, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of the liberation door of emptiness, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī gates and all samādhi gates.
"World-Honored One!..."

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-gates and all samadhi-gates?

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?
This is because the nature of emptiness of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī gateways and all samādhi gateways.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the gate of liberation of emptiness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharanī-gates and all samādhi-gates.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
“Because the nature of emptiness as a door of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
“World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the doors of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?”

“Ānanda! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the signless and wishless doors of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the liberation door of emptiness and others as non-dual, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the liberation door of emptiness as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The gate of liberation that is emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness as a door of liberation is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the doors of signlessness and wishlessness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the nature of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the doors of liberation— signlessness and wishlessness— is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of the liberation door of emptiness and so forth—employing non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means—one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehensible, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The six supernormal knowledges are empty of the nature of the six supernormal knowledges. Why is this?

This is because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the five eyes is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature. "Bhagavān, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the six superknowledges,

by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of own-marks, emptiness of common marks, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature?"
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the five eyes as non-dual, as unarisen, and as unobtainable, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the state of non-falsity, the state of non-alteration, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

"Because the nature of the five eyes is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm. "World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the six supernormal powers,

by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?"
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
"Because the nature of emptiness of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the six supernormal powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?"
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation,
and the path. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of the five eyes as non-dual, as unarisen, and as unapprehendable, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while cultivating the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:

Using the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth as a skillful means, using non-arising as a skillful means, and using non-apprehension as a skillful means, they dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

“Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehensible, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?
“Ānanda! The six superknowledges are empty of the nature of the six superknowledges. Why is that?

This is because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

Because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

“Because the nature of the five eyes is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

This is because the six supernormal powers, being empty by nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
"World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the six supernormal powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the six supernormal powers is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-dual, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

This is because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the five eyes is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
"World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the six supernormal powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
"World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects, and cultivate the knowledge of all aspects, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all characteristics?
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

Because the six supernormal knowledges, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the five eyes is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the six supernormal powers as non-duality, as non-arising, and as non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?
“Ānanda! The six supernormal powers are empty of the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Ānanda, this is because the six supernormal powers, being empty of intrinsic nature, are non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the five eyes and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the five eyes, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The five eyes are empty of the nature of the five eyes. Why is this?

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is non-dual and indivisible from all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Buddha’s ten powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the Buddha’s ten powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha. Why is this?
"Because the nature-emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha and the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; by means of non-arising as the expedient; and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"

"Ānanda! The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—the nature of these four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is emptiness."

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Buddha’s ten powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the Buddha’s ten powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

“Ānanda! The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—the nature of these four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is emptiness.”

Why is this? Because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is empty, and it is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the Buddha’s ten powers, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension—the absence of forgetfulness—dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”

Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-forgetfulness, the non-duality of all phenomena, non-arising, and non-apprehension as their skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the state of constant dwelling in equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of own-marks, common emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the dharmas of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the nature of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehensibility as the skillful means of the quality of non-forgetfulness, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness has the nature of emptiness regarding non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual with and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of equanimity that abides perpetually, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation,
and the path. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the dharma of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!...”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
For this reason it is said:

by means of non-forgetfulness and the non-duality of phenomena as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and not divided into two.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-forgetfulness, the non-duality of all phenomena, non-arising, and non-apprehension as skillful means, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient—characterized by the absence of forgetfulness—dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual with and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-forgetfulness, the non-duality of all phenomena, non-arising, and non-apprehension as skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality through the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are non-dual and indivisible.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?

This is because the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity (*upekṣā*) and its emptiness (*śūnyatā*) are non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*).
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the dharmas of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual with and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of the quality of non-forgetfulness, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness has the nature of emptiness regarding non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity and the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-forgetfulness, the non-dual, non-arising, and non-apprehension as skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from non-forgetfulness itself, and because it is non-dual and indivisible from the state of constant equanimity.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the state of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity and the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual and not divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the qualities of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality through the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the state of constant equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of non-forgetfulness and the non-duality of phenomena as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the constant abiding in equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of non-forgetfulness and the non-duality of all phenomena as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of non-forgetfulness and the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity and the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and indivisible.
Therefore, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality through the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening?”
“Ānanda! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness. Why is this? Because...”
"Because the emptiness of the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment. "World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the quality of non-forgetfulness and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of omniscience is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge as a skillful means, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is non-dual and indivisible from that emptiness of the internal, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*). "Blessed One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), by means of non-arising as the method, and by means of non-apprehension as the method, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārthaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), the absolute emptiness (*atyantaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāraśūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāraśūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*), the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambhaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāvaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāvaśūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*)?"
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects and abides in internal emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and that suchness (*tathatā*), up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), are non-dual and not divided into two. "Bhagavān, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all-knowledges (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharmas (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?"
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), abiding in suchness (*tathatā*) and even the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising as a means, and by means of non-apprehension as a means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin,
cessation, and the path.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?
“Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge and the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are non-dual and not divided into two.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all-knowledge while cultivating the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality through all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and indivisible.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality through all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of omniscience and the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-dual and indivisible.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge and the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
“World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all-knowledge and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”

“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge.
Why is this? Because...”
"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the five eyes and six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are non-dual and indivisible.
"Bhagavān, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), by means of non-arising (*anutpāda*), and by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā-jñāna*) and cultivate the five eyes and six supernormal powers?"
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
