“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?

"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*), as well as the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), are non-dual and cannot be divided into two. "Blessed One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity?"
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge and so forth, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all aspects, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the knowledge of all modes, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects?
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the knowledge of all things, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the characteristics of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all-knowledge and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?

“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this? Because...”
This is because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva are non-dual and indivisible.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā-jñāna*) and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"

“Ānanda! The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the skillful means of the non-duality of all-knowledge, the skillful means of non-arising, and the skillful means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! All-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of the nature of all-knowledge and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and cannot be divided into two. "World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, by means of non-arising as a skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! The knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects—the nature of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is empty. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

Using omniscience as the means—characterized by non-duality, non-arising, and non-apprehension—they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 123. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Measuring Merits, Number Thirty-two. "World-Honored One!..."

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all dharani-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of all doors of samādhi is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī gateways are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī gateways. Why is this?
"Because the nature-emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors and that [emptiness] ranging from internal emptiness to the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature are non-dual and not divided into two.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-gates is non-dual and indivisible from the emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
For this reason, it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all *dhāraṇī* gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) and dwells in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the nature of departure from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
“Because the nature-emptiness of all dhāraṇī-doors and that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual and not divided into two.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding all gateways of samādhi, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of all doors of samādhi is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:

By means of all the gateways of dhāraṇī as non-dual, as non-arising, and as unobtainable, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, abiding in suchness up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
"Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of all dharani-doors is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and the Path.
"World-Honored One!"

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding all doors of samādhi, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”
Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all doors of samādhi is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, its origin,
its cessation, and the path.
For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of all dharanī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of all dharani-doors, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?
Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of all doors of samādhi is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of all dharanī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of all dhāraṇī-doors, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding all doors of samādhi, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”
This is because the nature-emptiness of all samādhi-gates is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means of all dhāraṇī gates, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) while cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of all samādhi-gates is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! All dharanī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dharanī-doors. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of all dharani-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation through emptiness, the gate of liberation through signlessness, and the gate of liberation through wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”

This is because all gateways to samādhi are, by their very nature, empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the gateway to liberation of emptiness, the gateway to liberation of signlessness, and the gateway to liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all dhāraṇī gates, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! All dharanī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dharanī-doors. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of all dharani-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How, by means of the non-duality of all samadhi-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, does one dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?
Because the nature of all samādhi-gates is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of all dharani-doors as non-dual, as non-arising, and as unattainable, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī gateways are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī gateways. Why is this?

This is because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding all samādhi-doors, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”

This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-gates is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all dhāraṇī gates, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is that?
“Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding all doors of samādhi, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?
Because all gateways to samādhi are empty of intrinsic nature and are non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:

By means of all dharani-gates as non-dual, as unarisen, and as unobtainable, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all dharani-doors, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all aspects, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”
Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all doors of samādhi is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
This is because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all dharanī-doors is non-dual and indivisible from all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension regarding all doors of samādhi, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi?”
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-gates is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-gates and all samādhi-gates.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī gates, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dhāraṇī gates and all samādhi gates.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
"Because the nature of emptiness of all dharani-doors is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of all samādhi-doors, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of all samādhi-gates is empty and is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of all dhāraṇī-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding all dhāraṇī gates, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! All dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors. Why is this?
"Because the nature of emptiness of all dharani-doors is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. "World-Honored One, how does one,

by means of the non-duality of all samadhi-doors, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! All gateways to samādhi are empty of the intrinsic nature of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of all samādhi-gates is emptiness, and this is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:
By means of all dharani-doors as non-dual, as unarisen, and as unobtainable, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatā) and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the state of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How do those who are candidates for the fruit of once-returning, candidates for the fruit of non-returning, and candidates for the fruit of arhatship—by means of non-duality as their skillful means, non-arising as their skillful means, and non-apprehension as their skillful means—dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returner, up to and including the fruit of arhatship—the candidate for the fruit of once-returner, up to and including the fruit of arhatship—is empty of intrinsic nature. Why is that?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are all empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the state of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
"World-Honored One! [he said.]

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the approach to the fruit of once-returner, the approach to the fruit of non-returner, and the approach to the fruit of arhatship; by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—the stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—is empty of intrinsic nature. Why is that?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of the stream-enterer, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of dharmas (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are all empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of the once-returner’s path toward the fruit of once-returning, the stage of the non-returner’s path toward the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of the arhat’s path toward the fruit of arhatship; by means of non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?

“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of Once-Returner, up to and including the fruit of Arhatship, is empty of the nature of the stage of one heading toward the fruit of Once-Returner, up to and including the fruit of Arhatship.
Why is this? Because...”
Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness up to the inconceivable realm.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of the stream-enterer, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in suchness up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the stream-enterer’s fruit, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The stage of entering the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is this?

"Because the nature of emptiness of the state of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
"World-Honored One!"

How is it that one who is a candidate for the fruit of once-returning, a candidate for the fruit of non-returning, or a candidate for the fruit of arhatship, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path?
“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the stage of an arhat, and the nature of the fruit of once-returning, up to the nature of an arhat, are all empty.
Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge and abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!”

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate the practice of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) for the sake of the fruit of the once-returner, the fruit of the non-returner, and the fruit of the arhat?

“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—the stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—is empty of intrinsic nature. Why is that?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) while cultivating the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭābhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) as a candidate for the fruit of stream-entry?”
“Ānanda! The stream-enterer’s path, the fruit of stream-entry, the stream-enterer’s path, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is that?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate the state of being a candidate for the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning; the state of being a candidate for the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning; and the state of being a candidate for the fruit of arhatship, the fruit of arhatship—toward omniscience (sarvajñajñāna), while cultivating the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?”

“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returner, up to and including the fruit of arhatship, is empty of the nature of the candidate for the fruit of once-returner, up to and including the fruit of arhatship. Why is that?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are all empty. Why is this?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How do those who are practicing for the fruit of a once-returner, for the fruit of a non-returner, or for the fruit of an arhat—by means of non-duality as their skillful means, non-arising as their skillful means, and non-apprehension as their skillful means—dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”

“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the stage of an arhat, and the nature of the fruit of once-returning, up to the nature of the fruit of arhatship, are all empty. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is that?

This is because the nature of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is empty, and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How do those who are candidates for the fruit of once-returning, candidates for the fruit of non-returning, and candidates for the fruit of arhatship, by means of non-duality as their skillful means, by means of non-arising as their skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as their skillful means, dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”

“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to and including the fruit of arhatship, is empty of the nature of the candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to and including the fruit of arhatship. Why is that?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The stream-enterer’s path, the fruit of stream-entry, and the nature of the stream-enterer’s path and fruit are empty. Why is this?
This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the once-returner and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering the non-returner and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship; by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six superknowledges?”

“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—the stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—is empty of intrinsic nature. Why is that?
Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six superknowledges.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the stages of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The stream-enterer’s path, the fruit of stream-entry, the stream-enterer’s path, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is that?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate the state of being a candidate for the fruit of Once-Returner, the fruit of Once-Returner itself, the state of being a candidate for the fruit of Non-Returner, the fruit of Non-Returner itself, and the state of being a candidate for the fruit of Arhatship, the fruit of Arhatship itself, toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and thereby cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—the candidate for once-returning, up to the arhat—has the nature of emptiness.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The stream-enterer’s path, the fruit of stream-entry, the stream-enterer’s path, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is that?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]

How is it that, by means of the non-duality of the stage of the once-returner heading toward the fruit of once-returning, the stage of the non-returner heading toward the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of the arhat heading toward the fruit of arhatship; by means of non-arising; and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [these roots of goodness] to the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?
“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the stage of one heading toward the fruit of arhatship, as well as the nature of these stages, are empty.
Why is this? Because...”

Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the fruit of once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of paths (mārgajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of the stream-enterer, the path of the stream-enterer, and the nature of the fruit of the stream-enterer are empty. Why is that?

Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!...”

How does one, by means of non-duality as the skillful means, by means of non-arising as the skillful means, and by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means, dedicate the state of being a candidate for the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the state of being a candidate for the fruit of arhatship toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and thereby cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)?

“Ānanda! The stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship, is empty of the nature of the stage of one heading toward the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship.
Why is this? Because...”

This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The stage of entering the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are all empty. Why is this?
This is because the nature of emptiness of the state of one entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.
“World-Honored One!

How do those who are candidates for the fruit of once-returning, candidates for the fruit of non-returning, and candidates for the fruit of arhatship, by means of non-duality as their skillful means, non-arising as their skillful means, and non-apprehension as their skillful means, dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—the nature of the candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—is empty.
Why is that? Because...”
This is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The one who has entered the stream, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of the one entering the stream, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are all empty.
Why is this? Because...”
Because the nature of emptiness of the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of stream-entry itself is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of that bodhisattva mahāsattva.

“World-Honored One, how does one, by means of the non-duality of the candidate for the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of once-returning, the candidate for the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of non-returning, and the candidate for the fruit of arhatship and the fruit of arhatship; by means of non-arising as the expedient and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”

“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to and including the fruit of arhatship, is empty of the nature of the candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to and including the fruit of arhatship. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of the fruit of a once-returner up to that of an arhat is non-dual and indivisible from the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Thus it is, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stream-enterer’s path and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The stream-enterer’s path, the fruit of stream-entry, the stream-enterer’s path, and the nature of the fruit of stream-entry are empty. Why is that?
"Because the nature of emptiness of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the once-returner and the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering the non-returner and the fruit of non-returning, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship; by means of non-arising and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Ānanda! The candidate for the fruit of once-returning, up to the fruit of arhatship—the nature of the candidate for once-returning, up to the nature of the arhat—is empty.
Why is this? Because...”
Ānanda, this is because the nature of emptiness of the stage of a once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship is non-dual and indivisible from unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 124. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on the Measurement of Merits, Number Thirty, Section Twenty-three. "World-Honored One!..."

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient—pertaining to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha—dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the roots of virtue] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and that [emptiness] ranging from internal emptiness to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities are non-dual and indivisible.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual and not divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the skillful means, non-arising as the skillful means, and non-apprehension as the skillful means regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?

This is because the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty and non-dual with, and indivisible from, the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the five eyes and six supernormal powers are non-dual and not divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?

This is because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-bodhi, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
"Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is this?"
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the quality of non-forgetfulness, as well as the state of constant abiding in equanimity, are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
For this reason it is said:

by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the practice of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:
