By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and that of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and indivisible. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by means of non-duality as their skillful means, non-arising as their skillful means, and non-apprehension as their skillful means, dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path, its nature is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path, its nature is emptiness. Why is this?

Because, Ānanda, the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva and the emptiness of intrinsic nature— ranging from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature— are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
For this reason it is said:

By means of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of departure from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva mahāsattva practice has emptiness as its nature. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness practiced by the bodhisattva mahāsattva and that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual and not divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path has emptiness as his nature. Why is this?

This is because, Ānanda, the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual with and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
For this reason it is said:

By employing the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as a skillful means, employing non-arising as a skillful means, and employing non-apprehension as a skillful means, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?”
“Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path, its nature is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because, Ānanda, the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual and not divided into two, as they are with the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions.
For this reason it is said:

By employing non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, the bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva mahāsattva course is, by nature, empty. Why is this?

This is because the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual and indivisible from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path, its nature is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the nature of emptiness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice and the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [the roots of virtue] toward omniscience and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path has emptiness of intrinsic nature as his practice. Why is this?

This is because the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By employing the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as a skillful means, employing non-arising as a skillful means, and employing non-apprehension as a skillful means, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva mahāsattva practice has emptiness as its nature. Why is this?
Because for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By employing the non-duality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice as a skillful means, employing non-arising as a skillful means, and employing non-apprehension as a skillful means, they dedicate [their merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?”
“Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path, its nature is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva mahāsattva practice has emptiness as its nature. Why is this?

Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the quality of non-forgetfulness, as well as the state of constant abiding in equanimity, are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By employing the practice of non-duality as a skillful means, the practice of non-arising as a skillful means, and the practice of non-apprehension as a skillful means, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates [their merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?”
“Ānanda! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path, its nature is emptiness. Why is this?

This is because, Ānanda, the nature of emptiness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice and omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-dual and cannot be divided into two. Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the bodhisattva mahāsattva path has emptiness as his nature. Why is this?
This is because the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-dual and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice, by means of the unarisen, and by means of the non-apprehensible, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva mahāsattva practice has emptiness of intrinsic nature as his nature. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice and that bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice itself are non-dual and indivisible.
Ānanda, for this reason it is said:

By means of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! The bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva mahāsattva practice has emptiness as its nature. Why is this?
Because the nature of emptiness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s practice and that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice of non-duality as a skillful means, non-arising as a skillful means, and non-apprehension as a skillful means, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

Because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening is empty of intrinsic nature and is non-dual and indivisible from that emptiness of the internal, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, Ānanda!
For this reason it is said:

By means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in inner emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and abide in suchness (tathatā), the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Because...”
Because the emptiness of the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from that suchness, up to the inconceivable realm. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and abides in suchness, up to the inconceivable realm.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient for unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Because...”

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual with and indivisible from those noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and abides in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Because...”

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and cultivate the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭābhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana)?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

This is because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, which is empty of intrinsic nature, and the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Because...”

Because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening is empty of intrinsic nature, and is non-dual and indivisible from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, one dedicates [merit] toward omniscience and cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehensibility as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening is non-dual and indivisible from the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, dedicate [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of the non-duality of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, by means of non-arising, and by means of non-apprehension, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience and cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward omniscience, and cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?

Ānanda, this is because the emptiness of nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening is non-dual and indivisible from omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [the roots of virtue] toward the knowledge of all modes, and cultivates omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient for unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual with and indivisible from all dhāraṇī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
Ānanda! For this reason it is said:

by means of non-duality as the expedient, by means of non-arising as the expedient, and by means of non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [merit] toward all-knowledge and cultivates all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and the practice of those bodhisattva mahāsattvas are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
For this reason, Ānanda, it is said:

By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they dedicate [their merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“World-Honored One!

How does one, by means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, dedicate toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“Ānanda! Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of the nature of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the emptiness of the nature of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-dual and indivisible from that unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment. Ānanda,
for this reason it is said:

By means of non-duality as the expedient, non-arising as the expedient, and non-apprehension as the expedient, one dedicates [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes and cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Ānanda, you should know this!

It is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because it enables the cultivation of the *pāramitās* of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom to reach their ultimate consummation through such dedication to omniscience, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the leader among those *pāramitās* of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration.”

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to cause [the mind] to abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, thereby reaching their ultimate consummation. Therefore, among those—from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*). Furthermore, because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to cause [beings] to abide in suchness (*tathatā*), the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathābhāvatā*), equality (*samatā*), the nature of being free from birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), thereby reaching their ultimate consummation. Therefore, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for all things from suchness up to the inconceivable realm.”

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to establish others in the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin, the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path, leading them to ultimate realization. Therefore, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for those Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*). Furthermore, because it is through dedication toward the knowledge of all modes that one is able to bring the cultivation of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments to their ultimate consummation, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to bring the cultivation of the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) to their ultimate consummation. Therefore, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because it is through dedication toward omniscience that one is able to bring the cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path to ultimate perfection, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this perfection of wisdom that one can dedicate [merit] toward omniscience; and because, through dedicating toward omniscience, one is able to bring the cultivation of the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness to ultimate completion, this perfection of wisdom is the most honored and the guide for these three gates of liberation.”

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one can dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because through dedication to the knowledge of all modes one is able to bring the cultivation of the five eyes and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) to ultimate perfection, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.”

"Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because it is through dedication toward omniscience that one is able to bring to ultimate perfection the cultivation of the Buddha’s ten powers (*daśabala*), the four fearlessnesses (*caturvaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisaṃvidah*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because through dedication toward the knowledge of all modes one is able to bring the cultivation of the qualities of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāra*) to ultimate perfection, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the sovereign and the guide for the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.”

“Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this perfection of wisdom that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience; furthermore, because it is through dedication toward omniscience that the cultivation of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is brought to ultimate fulfillment, this perfection of wisdom is the most honored and the guide for all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.”

"Ānanda, you should know that it is by means of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*). Furthermore, because of this dedication toward omniscience, one is able to bring the cultivation of all *dhāraṇī* gates and all *samādhi* gates to ultimate perfection. Therefore, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for all those *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates."
“Ānanda, you should know this:

it is because of this *prajñāpāramitā* that one is able to dedicate [merit] toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*); and furthermore, because through dedicating toward the knowledge of all modes one is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices to ultimate consummation, this *prajñāpāramitā* is the most honored and the guide for those bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:

it is by means of this perfection of wisdom that one can dedicate [merit] toward omniscience; and because one can dedicate toward omniscience, one is able to bring the cultivation of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to its ultimate consummation. Therefore, this perfection of wisdom is the sovereign and the guide for that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Thus, because this perfection of wisdom and the omniscience to which it is dedicated serve as the basis and the foundation for all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors, causing them to grow and flourish; and because this perfection of wisdom is the most honored and the guide among all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors, I praise only the perfection of wisdom extensively.
“Ānanda, you should know this!

For example, when seeds are scattered upon the great earth, they grow through the convergence of various conditions. You should understand that the great earth serves as the basis for the growth of the seeds and acts as their support.”

Since this perfection of wisdom and the omniscience toward which it is dedicated serve as the basis for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas’ practice, as that which establishes it, and cause it to grow and flourish; and since this perfection of wisdom is the sovereign and the guide for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas’ practice, I praise only the perfection of wisdom extensively.
“Ānanda, you should know this!

For example, when seeds are scattered upon the great earth, they grow through the convergence of various conditions. You should understand that the great earth serves as the basis and the support for the growth of those seeds.”

Since this perfection of wisdom and the omniscience toward which it is dedicated serve as the basis for, and the foundation upon which, that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is established and allowed to grow, and since this perfection of wisdom is the sovereign and the guide for that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I praise only this perfection of wisdom extensively.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Even now, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has not yet finished expounding all the merits of this Prajñāpāramitā.”
Why is this so? The merit of the *prajñāpāramitā* received by me from the World-Honored One is profound and vast, its measure being without limit.

Any sons or daughters of good family who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, contemplate according to principle, and widely proclaim and disseminate this *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of sentient beings, shall likewise obtain merit that is without limit.

If one were to transcribe this Prajñāpāramitā and adorn it in various ways, further making offerings, paying homage, showing respect, and praising it with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, myriad wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—whatever all such things may be—the merit obtained would likewise be boundless.
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the ten paths of wholesome action will appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the five supernormal powers, and so forth, appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that the *dāna-pāramitā*, *śīla-pāramitā*, *kṣānti-pāramitā*, *vīrya-pāramitā*, *dhyāna-pāramitā*, and *prajñā-pāramitā* appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, there shall appear in the world the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of both internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, there shall appear in the world suchness (*tathatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, it is by virtue of this that the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin, the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) will appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path will appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is by virtue of this that the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the five eyes and the six supernormal powers will appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*) will appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, all *dhāraṇī* gates and all *samādhi* gates will appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that great clans of Kṣatriyas, great clans of Brāhmaṇas, great clans of householders, and great clans of lay merchants appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven will appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, the gods of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika-pariṣadya, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, Ābhāsvara-śuddha, Śubhakṛtsna, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Parītta-bṛhatphala, Apramāṇa-bṛhatphala, and Bṛhatphala heavens will appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, by virtue of this, the Avṛha devas, the Atapa devas, the Sudṛśa devas, the Sudarśana devas, and the Akaniṣṭha devas will appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, contemplate according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, it is by virtue of this that the gods of the Sphere of Infinite Space, the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, the Sphere of Nothingness, and the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that the stream-enterers (*srotāpanna*), once-returners (*sakṛdāgāmin*), non-returners (*anāgāmin*), and arhats, as well as those proceeding toward the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship, appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound Prajñāpāramitā, it is because of this that Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas appear in the world.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who, with a sincere mind, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is because of this that Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and the practice of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas appear in the world.”

“Bhagavān! If there are those who, with a sincere heart, hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, reflect upon according to the principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of this, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, will appear in the world.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
I do not say that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses only the merits previously described.”
Why is this? Because this perfection of wisdom is endowed with boundless, supreme qualities. Kausika!

I do not say that those sons or daughters of good family who listen to this *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere mind, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings; who further transcribe it and adorn it in various ways; and who, moreover, offer worship, respect, honor, and praise with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—using all that they possess—possess only the merits previously described.
Why is this? Kausika!
If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), by means of non-apprehension...

This serves as a skillful means: to listen to, receive and uphold, read and recite, diligently practice and study, and reflect upon this *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere heart; to extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings;
or to write it down, adorn it in various ways, and further offer immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite flowers.
With garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners,
flags and canopies, various wonders, rarities, music, and lamps— offering all these with total devotion,
honoring, respecting, revering, and praising them— these good sons and good daughters achieve immeasurable and supreme excellence.
He achieves the aggregate of morality; he achieves the immeasurable, sublime aggregate of concentration; he achieves the immeasurable, sublime aggregate of wisdom;
he achieves the immeasurable, sublime aggregate of liberation; and he achieves the immeasurable, sublime aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation.
“Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family are like the Buddha. Why is this?
Because they are definitively directed toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, Kauśika!
These sons and daughters of good family surpass the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Why is this? Because it liberates one from the inferior minds of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Kausika!

The aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation achieved by all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, a koṭi-th part, a hundred-koṭi-th part, a thousand-koṭi-th part, a hundred-thousand-koṭi-th part, or a hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-th part of the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation achieved by these sons and daughters of good family; they do not even bear comparison by way of number, calculation, reckoning, analogy, or even the infinitesimal fraction (upaniṣad).
Why is this? Kausika!

These sons and daughters of good family transcend all inferior mental states associated with the Hearers and Solitary Realizers; they never praise the vehicles of the Hearers or Solitary Realizers, and regarding all phenomena, there is nothing they do not know—meaning they correctly realize that absolutely nothing exists.
“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*),
and by means of the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen with sincere devotion to this Prajñāpāramitā and receive it...”
They uphold, recite, diligently study, and contemplate according to the principle; they extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings,
or again, they transcribe it with various adornments, and furthermore, offer immeasurable, supreme,
and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, and multitudes [of other offerings].
With exquisite, rare, and wonderful music, lamps, and all that they possess, these sons and daughters of good family offer worship,
reverence, respect, and praise; I declare that such individuals shall attain immeasurable and boundless,
preeminent merit in both the present and the future.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If good sons and good daughters do not depart from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), and by means of non-attachment...”
This shall serve as a skillful means for them to wholeheartedly hear,
receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate this *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of sentient beings;
or alternatively, to transcribe it, adorn it with various jewels, and further offer it with diverse kinds of exquisite flowers.
With garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, parasols,
various wondrous and rare objects, music, and lamps— offering all these with complete devotion, respect, reverence, and praise—
we gods shall constantly follow and protect them, ensuring that no humans or non-humans cause them harm.
“They are afflicted and harmed by various evil conditions such as those of human beings.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), should receive, uphold, read, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā, at that time immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras will assemble there to hear the Dharma; filled with joy and exultation, they will reverently receive this most profound Prajñāpāramitā.

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), proclaim such dharmas associated with this profound Prajñāpāramitā, at that time immeasurable devaputras will all assemble; through their celestial power, they shall cause the speaker’s eloquence to increase so that they may expound it exhaustlessly.”

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing the method of non-apprehension (anupalambha), proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā, at that time immeasurable devaputras will assemble out of their reverence for the Dharma. By the power of the devas, the eloquence of the speaker will be unimpeded, and even if obstacles or difficulties should arise, they shall not be able to interrupt it.”
“Kauśika! Those sons and daughters of good family who, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*),
employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), listen to this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere heart and receive it...”
To uphold, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon according to the principle; to extensively proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings;

or to transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and further to offer it with all kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, and the like.
By offering all that they possess— wondrous and rare objects, music, and lamps— and by honoring,
revering, respecting, and praising [the Buddha], these good sons and good daughters shall, in the present life, obtain boundless merit and benefits,
such that the hosts of Māras and their retinues will be unable to harass or disturb them.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters proclaim such profound *prajñāpāramitā* among the fourfold assembly, their minds will be free from fear or intimidation, and they shall not be overcome by any form of debate or challenge."
Why is this? It is because they are sustained by the empowerment of such profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Furthermore, within this secret treasury of *prajñāpāramitā*, all phenomena (*dharma*) are fully and extensively analyzed.
Therefore, it refers to: whether they are wholesome dharmas, unwholesome dharmas, or indeterminate dharmas;
whether they are past dharmas, future dharmas, or present dharmas; whether they are dharmas pertaining to the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm;
or whether they are dharmas of those in training, dharmas of those beyond training, or dharmas of those who are neither in training nor beyond training.
Whether they be dharmas to be abandoned by seeing, dharmas to be abandoned by cultivation, or dharmas not to be abandoned;
whether they be mundane dharmas or supramundane dharmas; whether they be tainted dharmas or untainted dharmas;
whether they be conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas; whether they be visible dharmas or invisible dharmas; or whether they be material dharmas or immaterial dharmas—
As for the dharmas— whether common or uncommon dharmas, whether the dharmas of śrāvakas,
pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas— all such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of various dharma-gates are subsumed within this.
Furthermore, by means of this, these sons and daughters of good family dwell well in internal emptiness,
dwell well in external emptiness, dwell well in internal-and-external emptiness, dwell well in the emptiness of emptiness, dwell well in great emptiness,
dwell well in the emptiness of the ultimate, dwell well in the emptiness of the conditioned, and dwell well in the emptiness of the unconditioned.
He is thoroughly established in ultimate emptiness, thoroughly established in boundless emptiness, thoroughly established in dispersed emptiness,

thoroughly established in unchanging emptiness, thoroughly established in essential nature emptiness, thoroughly established in self-characteristic emptiness, thoroughly established in common characteristic emptiness,
thoroughly established in the emptiness of all phenomena, thoroughly established in the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, and thoroughly established in the emptiness of non-existence.
Because they are well-established in the emptiness of intrinsic nature and well-established in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
they do not perceive anyone who can raise an objection, nor do they perceive anything that is being objected to,
nor do they perceive any Prajñāpāramitā that is being taught.
For this reason, Kauśika,
because these sons and daughters of good family are sustained by the great majestic power of this Prajñāpāramitā, they cannot be overcome by the challenges and debates of any heterodox schools.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons and good daughters, with sincere hearts, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to principle, explain, transcribe, and widely disseminate this Prajñāpāramitā, these good sons and good daughters will have minds that are not startled, not terrified, and not afraid; their minds will neither sink nor feel regret."
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family do not perceive any dharma that could cause them to be startled, terrified, frightened, submerged, or filled with regret.

Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family wish to obtain such present, boundless merits and benefits, they should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, reflect upon according to the principle, and extensively proclaim and disseminate this profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of sentient beings; or else, having transcribed it and adorned it with various jewels, they should further offer all that they possess—various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, wonderful and rare treasures, music, and lamps—to honor, revere, respect, and praise it.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
If good sons and good daughters, with a mind directed toward the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and employing non-apprehension as their means,
listen to and receive this Prajñāpāramitā with a sincere heart..."
They uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon it according to the principle; they widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings;

or they transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and further honor it with diverse kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, and multitudes of...
With exquisite, rare, and wondrous music, lamps, and all manner of offerings,
these sons and daughters of good family constantly pay homage, show respect, honor, and praise their parents,
teachers, elders, kinsmen, friends, acquaintances, kings, ministers, and all śramaṇas.
...loved and respected by Brahmins and others, and likewise cherished and remembered by all the Tathāgatas,
Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Arhats, Anāgāmins, Sakṛdāgāmins,
and Srotāpannas throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions, as well as by all those in the world..."
They are protected by devas, māras, brahmās, humans, non-humans, asuras, and so forth.
These sons and daughters of good family achieve the most excellent and uninterrupted eloquence;

these sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom without ever ceasing or exhausting them.

These sons and daughters of good family, dwelling securely in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, shall never be exhausted or interrupted.

These sons and daughters of good family dwell securely in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, remaining forever without cessation or exhaustion;

these sons and daughters of good family dwell securely in the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin, the noble truth of cessation, and the noble truth of the path, remaining forever without cessation or exhaustion;
these sons and daughters of good family practice the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, remaining forever without cessation or exhaustion.

These sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases without interruption or exhaustion;

these sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path without interruption or exhaustion;

these sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness without interruption or exhaustion.
These sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers without interruption or exhaustion;

these sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha without interruption or exhaustion;
these sons and daughters of good family constantly practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of ever-abiding equanimity without interruption or exhaustion.

These sons and daughters of good family cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) without ever ceasing;
these sons and daughters of good family cultivate all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors without ever ceasing;
these sons and daughters of good family bring sentient beings to maturity and purify Buddha-fields without ever ceasing.
These sons and daughters of good family will achieve the sublime supernatural powers of a bodhisattva, traveling through all buddha-fields with sovereign ease and without obstruction;
these sons and daughters of good family will not be overcome by the heterodox arguments of any non-Buddhist schools, but will themselves be able to subdue those heterodox arguments.

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family wish to obtain such benefits and merits—uninterrupted and inexhaustible—in both the present and the future, they should with a sincere heart hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently study, and reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the truth. They should also widely proclaim and disseminate it for the sake of sentient beings. Furthermore, they should transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and offer it all that they possess as worship, reverence, respect, and praise, using immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
If good sons and good daughters write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, adorn it in various ways, and place it in a pure location, making offerings to it, honoring, respecting, and praising it."

At that time, all those belonging to the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven within this trichiliocosm who had already resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* would constantly come to this place to behold and pay homage to, recite, make offerings to, revere, respect, praise, circumambulate clockwise, and prostrate before this *prajñāpāramitā*, and then depart with palms joined.

All those among the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, Ābhāsvara, Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Bṛhatphala devas who have already resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* constantly come to this place to behold and pay homage to, read and recite, make offerings to, revere, respect, praise, circumambulate clockwise, and prostrate themselves before this *prajñāpāramitā*, and then depart with palms joined.

All the gods of the Pure Abodes—namely, the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha—heavenly beings—also constantly come here to behold and pay homage to this Prajñāpāramitā, to read and recite it, and having made offerings, shown reverence, honored, praised, and circumambulated it to the right, they depart with palms joined.

At that time, there were also nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans of great majesty and power in this world-system who constantly came to this place to behold and pay homage to, read and recite, make offerings to, revere, respect, praise, circumambulate clockwise, and prostrate themselves before this Prajñāpāramitā, then departed with palms joined.

"At that time, all those belonging to the Cāturmahārājakāyika, Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens throughout the boundless worlds of the ten directions who have already resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* will constantly come to this place to behold and pay homage to, read and recite, make offerings to, revere, respect, praise, circumambulate to the right, and prostrate before this *prajñāpāramitā*, and then depart with palms joined."

All those among the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, Ābhāsvara, Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Bṛhatphala devas who have already resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* constantly come to this place to behold and pay homage to, recite, make offerings to, revere, respect, praise, circumambulate clockwise, and prostrate before this *prajñāpāramitā*, and then depart with palms joined.

All the gods of the Pure Abodes—namely, the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha—heavenly beings—also constantly come here to behold and pay homage to this Prajñāpāramitā, to read and recite it, and having made offerings, shown reverence, honored, praised, and circumambulated it clockwise, they depart with palms joined.

At that time, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others of great majesty from that world also constantly come here to behold and pay homage to this Prajñāpāramitā, to read and recite it, and to offer worship, reverence, respect, praise, circumambulation, and prostration before departing with palms joined.
“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:
‘Now, all that exists within this trichiliocosm and the other infinite worlds of the ten directions...’”
The Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven,
the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven,
the Mahābrahma Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, and the Ābhāsvara Heaven.
The Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven,
the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven,
the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, and other [deities]...
Nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans,
and others of great power and majesty constantly come here to behold,
pay homage to, and recite this profound Prajñāpāramitā that I have written down.
‘Having made offerings, paid homage, shown respect, offered praise, circumambulated them to the right, and prostrated, I shall depart with palms joined;
by this, I shall have already established the gift of Dharma.
Having formed this thought, one rejoices and leaps for joy, causing the merit obtained to increase twofold.
“Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family, by virtue of this,
[will receive offerings from] all the Cāturmahārājakāyika devas and Trāyastriṃśa devas throughout this trichiliocosm as well as the infinite worlds of the ten directions.”
The Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven,
the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmakāyika-sabhāgata Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven,
the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, and the Parīttaśubha Heaven.
The Heaven of Immeasurable Purity, the Heaven of Universal Purity, the Vast Heaven, the Heaven of Limited Vastness,
the Heaven of Immeasurable Vastness, the Heaven of Vast Results, the Heaven Without Affliction, the Heaven Without Heat,
the Heaven of Excellent Appearance, the Heaven of Excellent Vision, and the Heaven of the Ultimate Form, as well as other immeasurable nāgas and yakṣas of great majesty and power.
Gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans,
and others will constantly come here to follow and protect them, so that they shall not be harmed by any humans or non-humans,
except for those karmic causes of fixed evil deeds from past lives that must ripen in the present.
Or they may transform heavy karma so that it is experienced lightly in this present life. "Kauśika!
