Furthermore, through the empowerment of their profound and vast power of great compassion, they ensure that after the Parinirvāṇa of a Tathāgata, whoever obtains even a single grain the size of a mustard seed and makes various offerings to it will gain boundless merit. Such a person shall enjoy sublime pleasures among gods and humans, until finally reaching the end of suffering. Therefore, the merit of one who gives [relics] to others is greater.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 129. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Measuring Merits, Number Thirty, Section Twenty-eight. At that time, the Buddha praised Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Excellent!"
Excellent!
It is as you have said, Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, adorn it with various jewels, and offer all that they possess—immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense scents, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—to honor, revere, respect, and praise it; and if they rely on this sutra to contemplate according to the truth.

If there are sons or daughters of good family who write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and bestow it upon others so that they may receive, uphold, and widely disseminate it, the latter of these two accumulations of merit will be greater.
Why is this? Because by giving to others, one enables immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to attain the joy of the Dharma.
"Furthermore, Kausika!

If sons or daughters of good family can, according to the meaning and intent as taught in the Prajñāpāramitā, extensively analyze and explain it for sentient beings so that they attain correct understanding, the mass of merit obtained by these sons or daughters of good family will be hundreds of thousands of times greater than the merit of giving this sūtra to others.
“Kauśika! You should revere this Dharma-preacher as you would revere a Buddha, and serve him as you would serve a venerable fellow-practitioner of the holy life. Why is this?

Kauśika! You should know that the perfection of wisdom is itself the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; you should know that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is himself the perfection of wisdom.

You should know that the perfection of wisdom is not different from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; you should know that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is not different from the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Kausika!
All Buddhas of the past, future, and present have diligently practiced and studied the Prajñāpāramitā, thereby realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! You should know that those who practice the noble holy life are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling on the stage of non-retrogression; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also rely upon the *prajñāpāramitā* to train with diligence and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Kauśika! A person belonging to the lineage of the śrāvakas also diligently trains in this very profound perfection of wisdom and realizes the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
a person belonging to the lineage of the pratyekabuddhas also diligently trains in this very profound perfection of wisdom and gradually realizes the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.

A person of the bodhisattva lineage, by likewise diligently training in this profound perfection of wisdom, transcends the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enters the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, and further gradually practices until attaining unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"For this reason, Kauśika!

If sons or daughters of good family wish to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to the present Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with immeasurable and exquisite flower garlands, scented unguents and incense, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—using all that they possess—they should write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā and offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to it with immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, scented unguents and incense, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps, using all that they possess."
Kauśika! Contemplating this meaning, when I first attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, I reflected thus:
"Upon what shall I rely for my dwelling?"
"Who is capable of receiving my offerings, respect, honor, and praise?
While he was reflecting thus, he did not see anyone in the entire world—whether among gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, humans, or non-humans—who was his equal, let alone his superior.
Furthermore, he reflected to himself:

"Relying upon this Dharma, I have already realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. This Dharma is subtle, profound, and tranquil; I shall dwell in reliance upon this very Dharma, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising it."
"What is this dharma?
It is the Prajñāpāramitā. Kausika!..."

Since I have already attained Buddhahood, I still abide by relying upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, making offerings, paying homage, respecting, and praising it; how much more so should sons and daughters of good family who seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment not take refuge with a sincere heart in this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and diligently study it, offering all they possess—limitless varieties of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes for scattering, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps—to make offerings, pay homage, respect, and praise it?

“Kauśika! If sons or daughters of good family who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas should also take refuge in this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with a sincere heart and apply themselves diligently to its cultivation, they should offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise with all their possessions—using immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

It is because this Prajñāpāramitā gives birth to the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; from these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas arise, and it is by depending upon those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas that Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas come into being.
For this reason, Kauśika!

All sons and daughters of good family who seek the Great Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, or the Śrāvaka Vehicle, should with a sincere heart take refuge in and diligently study this profound Prajñāpāramitā. They should offer worship, honor, respect, and praise with all their possessions—using immeasurable kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes for smearing and scattering, robes, necklaces, jeweled banners, pennants, canopies, various wonderful and rare objects, music, and lamps.
Why is this? Those who seek the state of a śrāvaka, by diligently training in this Prajñāpāramitā, will ultimately realize the fruit of arhatship;
those who seek the state of a pratyekabuddha, by diligently training in this Prajñāpāramitā, will ultimately realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
Those who seek the Mahāyāna, by diligently practicing and studying this Prajñāpāramitā, will ultimately realize unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika,
if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to teach all sentient beings throughout Jambudvīpa to practice and study the ten paths of wholesome action, what do you think?”
"Would these sons and daughters of good family, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of Devas, replied:
"Very much!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha said,

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and give it to others to read and recite, or if they copy it out again and cause it to be widely circulated, the mass of merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters will be far greater than the former.”
Why is this? "Kauśika!

Within this secret treasury of the Prajñāpāramitā, all untainted (anāsrava) dharmas are extensively expounded. If individuals belonging to the śrāvaka lineage practice and study these dharmas, they will swiftly enter the state of right determination free from outflows (samyaktva-niyāma-avakrānti) and attain the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpatti-phala), the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmi-phala), the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmi-phala), and the fruit of arhatship (arhat-phala)."

A person of the pratyekabuddha lineage who trains in this Dharma will swiftly enter the state of rightness and departure from birth (samyaktva-niyāma), gradually realizing the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;

a person of the bodhisattva lineage who trains in this Dharma will swiftly enter the state of rightness and departure from birth, gradually practicing all the bodhisattva deeds, and realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Kauśika! Within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, all untainted (*anāsrava*) dharmas are extensively explained;
that is to say, the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*)...”
The perfection of generosity, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration,
and the perfection of wisdom; internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness,
the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, and the emptiness of the limitless.
emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and the non-erroneous nature;

The nature of non-alteration, equality, freedom from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*);
the knowledge of the noble truth of suffering, the knowledge of the noble truth of the origin, the knowledge of the noble truth of cessation, and the knowledge of the noble truth of the path;
and the four untainted meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*).
the four formless absorptions, the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment,
the eight branches of the noble path, the gate of liberation of emptiness, and the gate of liberation of signlessness.
the doors of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity—all these...
Knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects;
all the doors of dhāraṇī, all the doors of samādhi, and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas—
all these are the untainted (anāsrava) dharmas explained herein.

“Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to instruct a single sentient being to abide in the fruit of stream-entry, the mass of merit they would obtain would be far superior to that of instructing all the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa and causing them all to practice the ten paths of wholesome action.”
Why is this? Kausika!

There are those who practice the ten paths of wholesome action yet still fail to escape the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts; whereas if sentient beings abide in the fruit of a stream-enterer, they immediately attain permanent liberation from the three evil destinies. How much more so, then, regarding the mass of merit obtained by teaching others to abide in the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat—how could that not surpass the former?

“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa so that they all abide in the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, the mass of merit they would obtain would not equal that of a person who instructs a single sentient being to establish them in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.”
Why is this? Kausika!
Because all the merits of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha surpass those of a Stream-enterer and others by a hundred-thousandfold.

“Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to instruct all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa and cause them to abide in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, the mass of merit they would obtain would not equal that of someone who instructs a single sentient being to set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
If one instructs sentient beings to incline toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then one ensures that the Buddha-eye in the world shall not be interrupted.

"Why is this? It is because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there exist the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
it is because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there are Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there exist the Buddha-jewel, the Dharma-jewel, and the Saṃgha-jewel, upon whom all the world relies and makes offerings.
For this reason, Kauśika!

All those in the world—whether devas, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, asuras, humans, or non-humans—should, with immeasurable and most excellent flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, various wonders, rare treasures, music, and lamps, offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to the bodhisattva mahāsattva with all that they possess.

“Kauśika! By this you should know that if a son of good family or a daughter of good family writes down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and gives it to others to read and recite, or copies it again and causes it to be widely circulated, the mass of merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless, surpassing the previous mass of merit.”
Why is this? Because within this secret treasury of the Prajñāpāramitā, all the supreme and wholesome dharmas of both the mundane and supramundane realms are extensively expounded.

"Because the Dharma is taught within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there come to be established in the world the great clans of kṣatriyas, the great clans of brahmins, the great clans of householders, and the great clans of laymen;

because the Dharma is taught within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there come to be established in the world the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;

because the Dharma is taught within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there come to be established in the world the Heaven of the Brahma-multitude, the Heaven of the Brahma-ministers, the Heaven of the Brahma-congregation, and the Heaven of Mahābrahmā."
Because the Dharma is taught within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there is the designation of the Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, and Ābhāsvara-śubha devas in the world;
because the Dharma is taught within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there is the designation of the Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna devas in the world;
because the Dharma is taught within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there is the designation of the Bṛhatphala, Parīttabṛhatphala, Apramāṇabṛhatphala, and Bṛhatphala devas in the world.

"Furthermore, Kauśika!

Śakra, Lord of Devas, replied:

"World-Honored One!

The Buddha said,

Why is this so? Kauśika!

Within this secret treasury of the Prajñāpāramitā, all untainted (anāsrava) dharmas are extensively expounded. When individuals belonging to the śrāvaka lineage practice and study these dharmas, they swiftly enter the state of right determination beyond birth (samyaktva-niyāma), and attain the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpanna), the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmin), the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmin), and the fruit of arhatship (arhattva).

A person of the pratyekabuddha lineage who trains in this Dharma will swiftly enter the state of rightness and departure from birth (samyaktva-niyāma), gradually realizing the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;

a person of the bodhisattva lineage who trains in this Dharma will swiftly enter the state of rightness and departure from birth, gradually practicing all the bodhisattva deeds, and realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Kauśika! Within this secret treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, all untainted (*anāsrava*) dharmas are extensively explained;

Why is this? Kausika!

There are those who practice the ten paths of wholesome action yet still fail to escape the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts; whereas if sentient beings abide in the fruit of a Stream-enterer, they immediately attain eternal liberation from the three evil destinies. Why is this so? Kauśika!
Because all the merits of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment surpass those of the stream-enterers and others by a hundred thousandfold.

Why is this? Kauśika!
If one instructs sentient beings to incline toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then one ensures that the Buddha-eye in the world will not be severed.

For this reason, Kauśika!

Why is this? Kauśika!
If one instructs sentient beings to lead them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, then one ensures that the Buddha-eye in the world shall not be interrupted.

"Why is this? It is because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there are the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
it is because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that there are Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Because there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, there exist the Buddha-jewel, the Dharma-jewel, and the Saṅgha-jewel, upon whom all the world relies and makes offerings.
For this reason, Kauśika!

All those in the world—whether devas, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, asuras, humans, or non-humans—should, with immeasurable and most excellent flower garlands, powdered and scattered perfumes, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, various wonders, rare treasures, music, and lamps, offer all they possess to worship, revere, honor, and praise the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

“Kauśika! By this you should know that if a son of good family or a daughter of good family writes down such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and gives it to others to read and recite, or transcribes it and causes it to be widely disseminated, the mass of merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless, surpassing the previous mass of merit.”
Why is this? Because within this secret treasury of the Prajñāpāramitā, all the supreme and virtuous dharmas of both the mundane and supramundane realms are extensively expounded.
