"This rejoicing and dedication thus generated is the foremost, the most excellent, the most sublime, the highest, the most wondrous, the most subtle, the superior, the unsurpassed, the peerless, and the equal to the unequaled among all other meritorious deeds that have been generated."
"What do you think,
Maitreya Mahāsattva?

When that bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of sympathetic joy and dedication directed toward such objects, does that object of focus exist in the same manner as the marks apprehended by that bodhisattva mahāsattva?"

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 168. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Thirty-one, Section Two: Dedication through Rejoicing. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya addressed the Elder Subhūti, saying:
"Venerable One!..."

That bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of sympathetic joy and dedication conditioned by such objects; yet, in reality, there are no such objects as they are apprehended through signs by that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The Venerable Subhūti said:
"O Great Being!

If there were no objective referent corresponding to the marks as they are grasped, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind of sympathetic joy and dedication, employing the grasping of marks as a means, would universally take as its object the countless, immeasurable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions. Within each of those worlds, he would collect together and bring before him all the roots of virtue—from the first generation of the thought of enlightenment until the extinction of the Dharma—of all the Buddhas who have already entered parinirvāṇa, as well as all the roots of virtue of their disciples and others; he would then rejoice in them with sympathetic joy and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Is this rejoicing and dedication thus generated not, then, a perversion?
It would be like regarding the impermanent as permanent—this being a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view;
or regarding suffering as pleasure—this being a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
To conceive of what is non-self as self is a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view;
to conceive of what is impure as pure is a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
In this regard, one grasps at signs within that which is signless; it should also be understood in this way:
"O Great Being!
Just as the object of focus is in reality non-existent, so too is the mind of sympathetic joy and dedication. All wholesome [dharmas]..."
The faculties and so forth are likewise; unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is likewise;
form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are likewise; the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise;
and the sense bases of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena are likewise.
The same applies to the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, as well as eye-contact and all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition;
the same applies to the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition;
and the same applies to the nose element, the odor element, and the nose-consciousness element.
The same applies to the nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as their condition;
the tongue-element, taste-element, tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition, are likewise so;
and the body-element, touch-element, body-consciousness-element, and body-contact, as well as [the feelings produced with body-contact as their condition], are likewise so.

All feelings are likewise; the mind element, the mental-object element, and the mind-consciousness element, as well as mind-contact and all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are likewise;
the earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are likewise;
and ignorance, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, and the six sense bases are likewise.
Contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are also like this;

so too are the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom;
and likewise, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and the emptiness of emptiness.
...great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness,
common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, and emptiness of intrinsic nature...
Emptiness and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are also like this;

so too are suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm; as well as suffering.
The noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are likewise; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are likewise;
the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are likewise;
and the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and the four bases of psychic power are likewise.
The five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are also thus;
the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are also thus; the five eyes and the six supernormal knowledges are also thus;
as are the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and great compassion.
Great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, as well as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are also like this;
the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are also like this;
all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are also like this; and all doors of dhāraṇī and all samādhis are also like this.
The gates are also like this; the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and those of the Mahāyāna are also like this.
"O Great Being!
If the reality of the objects of focus is in fact non-existent, then the mind of sympathetic joy and dedication is also like this. All...
The same applies to the roots of goodness and so forth; the same applies to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
the same applies to form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the same applies to the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;
and the same applies to the sense objects of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and phenomena.
It is so: the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as eye-contact and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are likewise;

the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are likewise; the nose-element, the odor-element, the nose-consciousness...
The same applies to the element of the nose, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as condition;
likewise for the element of the tongue, the element of taste, the element of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as condition;
and likewise for the element of the body, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and [all sensations produced with body-contact as condition].

The arising of all feelings is also like this; the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are also like this; the earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also like this;
and ignorance, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, and the six sense bases are also like this.
...contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are also like this;
the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are also like this;
and internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and emptiness [of emptiness] are also like this.
Emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, and emptiness of self-...
The emptiness of nature and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence are also like this; so too are suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature,
the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth,
the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are also like this; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are also like this;
the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities are also like this;
and the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and the four bases of psychic power are also like this.
The five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are also thus;
the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are also thus; the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are also thus;
as are the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and great compassion.
...Great Compassion, Great Joy, and Great Equanimity; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) are also thus;
the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*) are also thus;
all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are also thus; all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*) and all samādhis...
The gateways of the stages are also like this; as it is with the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Mahāyāna, what is their object of focus?
What is their objective reality?
What is the mind of sympathetic joy and dedication?
What are the various roots of goodness and so forth?
And what is unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
"And how does that bodhisattva mahāsattva, taking such matters as an object, give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy and dedicate it toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Maitreya Bodhisattva said:
"Virtuous One!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has already made offerings to immeasurable buddhas, has planted roots of goodness in past lives and long since formulated great vows, and has been sustained by virtuous friends, having well studied the meaning of the self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) of all phenomena—this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able, regarding the objects of focus, the mind of sympathetic joy and dedication, all roots of goodness, unsurpassed enlightenment, and all dharmas, to remain without grasping at their marks (*animitta*), yet is able to initiate the sympathetic joy and dedication toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Thus, through this sympathetic rejoicing and dedication, by means of the skillful means that are neither dual nor non-dual, neither characterized nor uncharacterized, neither attainable nor unattainable, neither defiled nor pure, and neither arising nor ceasing, one is able to refrain from grasping at signs regarding the objects of focus, up to and including unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Because one does not grasp at signs, one is not subsumed under cognitive inversion.

If there are bodhisattvas who have not long practiced the six pāramitās, who have never made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, who have not previously planted roots of virtue, who have not long since generated the great vow, who have not been sustained by spiritual friends, and who have not well studied the self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) of all phenomena—these bodhisattvas, regarding the objects of focus, the bases, the rejoicing, the dedication, the various roots of virtue, unsurpassed enlightenment, and all phenomena, still grasp at their marks (*nimitta*) and give rise to rejoicing and dedication toward unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Such rejoicing and dedication, because they involve grasping at marks, are still subsumed under perversion (*viparyāsa*).

"Furthermore, Venerable Sir, one should not proclaim the *prajñāpāramitā* to those who are newly trained in the Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, nor before them; nor should one proclaim the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* pāramitās to those who are newly trained in the Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, nor before them."

One should not proclaim inner emptiness to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim it in their presence. Likewise, one should not proclaim outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim these in their presence.

One should not proclaim *tathatā* (suchness) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them; nor should one proclaim the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them.

One should not proclaim the Noble Truth of Suffering to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them; nor should one proclaim the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, or the Path to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them.

One should not proclaim the four dhyānas to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna nor in their presence; nor should one proclaim the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna nor in their presence.

One should not proclaim the eight liberations to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna nor in their presence, nor should one proclaim the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna nor in their presence.

One should not proclaim the four foundations of mindfulness to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence; nor should one proclaim the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence;

nor should one proclaim the liberation door of emptiness to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence.

One should not proclaim the five eyes to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence; nor should one proclaim the six supernormal powers to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence.

One should not proclaim the ten powers of a buddha to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence; nor should one proclaim the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor should one proclaim them in their presence.

One should not proclaim the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them; one should also not proclaim the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-svabhāva*) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them.

One should not proclaim all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them; nor should one proclaim the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them.

One should not proclaim all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them; nor should one proclaim all doors of samādhi (*samādhimukha*) to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor before them.
One should not proclaim the meaning of the emptiness of the intrinsic characteristics of all phenomena to those newly trained bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna, nor in their presence. Why is this?
"Venerable Sir!

Although newly initiated bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna may possess a small measure of faith, reverence, and affection for such teachings as these, upon hearing them, they immediately forget them all, because they give rise to alarm, doubt, fear, and trepidation, and thus produce slander."
"Furthermore, Venerable Sir!

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long ago made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity."

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of both internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

If there are non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and are sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

If there are irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and are sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin, the Noble Truth of Cessation, and the Noble Truth of the Path.

If there are irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and are sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.

If there are irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, who have planted roots of goodness and long since made great vows, and who are sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

If there are irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, who have planted roots of goodness and long since made great vows, and who are sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) before them.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long since made great vows, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain all dharani-doors and all samādhi-doors before them.

If there is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva who has made offerings to immeasurable buddhas in the past, planted roots of goodness, long ago generated the great vow, and is sustained by spiritual friends, one should extensively explain before them the meaning of the emptiness of the specific characteristics of all phenomena.
Why is this so? Venerable One!

Because such non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—who have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past, who have planted roots of goodness and long since made great vows, and who are sustained by spiritual friends—will, upon hearing this Dharma, be able to receive and uphold it without ever forgetting it; for their minds will not be startled or doubtful, nor will they be terrified, cowed, or disparaging.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Bodhisattva Maitreya, saying:

“A bodhisattva mahāsattva should dedicate such meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. That is to say, the mind which performs the dedication of sympathetic joy—this mind is subject to exhaustion, cessation, detachment, and transformation; and those objects of focus as well as all those roots of virtue are likewise, like that mind, subject to exhaustion, cessation, detachment, and transformation.”
In this context, what is the mind that is employed?
Furthermore, by means of what objects of focus and what roots of goodness does one speak of sympathetic joy and the dedication [of merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?

This mind should not engage in rejoicing or dedication with respect to the nature of the mind, because two minds cannot arise simultaneously; nor can the mind rejoice in or dedicate itself to its own intrinsic nature.
“O Mahāsattva!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are able to know, as it truly is, that form is non-existent, and that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-existent;
that the sense-base of the eye is non-existent, and that the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-existent.”
The sphere of form does not exist; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not exist.
The eye-element does not exist; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition do not exist.
The ear-element does not exist; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition do not exist.
The nose element is non-existent; the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-existent.
The tongue element is non-existent; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-existent.
The body element is non-existent; the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are non-existent.

The mind-element is non-existent; the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are non-existent.
The earth element is non-existent; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are non-existent.

Ignorance is non-existent; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are non-existent.
The perfection of generosity is non-existent; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are non-existent.

Inner emptiness is non-existent; outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are non-existent.

Suchness is non-existent; the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are all non-existent.
The noble truth of suffering is non-existent; the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path are non-existent.
The four dhyānas are non-existent; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-existent.
The eight liberations are non-existent; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-existent.

The four foundations of mindfulness are non-existent; the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are non-existent.
The gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-existent.
The five eyes are non-existent; the six supernormal powers are non-existent;

the ten powers of a Buddha are non-existent; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-existent;
the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-existent; and the state of constant abiding in equanimity is non-existent.
All-knowledge is non-existent; the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent;
all doors of dhāraṇī are non-existent; all doors of samādhi are non-existent;
the fruit of stream-entry is non-existent; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-existent.
Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-existent;
the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-existent;
unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-existent.
“O Great Being!

Since this bodhisattva mahāsattva knows, as it truly is, that all phenomena are non-existent, he dedicates the meritorious deeds associated with sympathetic joy toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. This is called the non-perverted dedication of sympathetic joy toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:
"Virtuous One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the Great Vehicle hears such a teaching as this, will his mind not be startled, doubtful, or terrified?"
"Venerable One!
How should a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva who has set out in the Mahāyāna dedicate all the roots of goodness he has cultivated toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
"Venerable One!

How should a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva who has set out in the Mahāyāna embrace the various meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
Then, the Venerable Subhūti, empowered by the spiritual authority of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: "Kauśika!
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they embrace the perfection of wisdom by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient;

if they practice the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, they embrace the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient.
If one dwells in internal emptiness, employing the means of non-apprehension and the means of signlessness, one embraces internal emptiness;

if one dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, employing the means of non-apprehension and the means of signlessness, one embraces external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
If one abides in suchness (*tathatā*), by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means and signlessness as the skillful means, one embraces suchness;

if one abides in the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means and signlessness as the skillful means, one embraces the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
If one dwells in the noble truth of suffering, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, one embraces the noble truth of suffering;

if one dwells in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, one embraces the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
If one cultivates the four dhyānas, doing so by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, one thereby embraces the four dhyānas;

if one cultivates the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, doing so by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, one thereby embraces the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
If one cultivates the eight liberations, doing so with non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the eight liberations;

if one cultivates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, doing so with non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
If one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, one thereby embraces the four foundations of mindfulness;

if one cultivates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, one thereby embraces the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
If one cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, using non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the gate of liberation of emptiness;

if one cultivates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, using non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
If one cultivates the five eyes, one takes non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means to embrace the five eyes;
if one cultivates the six supernormal powers, one takes non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means to embrace the six supernormal powers.
If one cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, using non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the ten powers of a Buddha;

if one cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, using non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
If one cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness, by means of the expedient of non-apprehension and the expedient of signlessness, one embraces the quality of non-forgetfulness;
if one cultivates the nature of constant equanimity, by means of the expedient of non-apprehension and the expedient of signlessness, one embraces the nature of constant equanimity.
If one cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), one embraces all-knowledge by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means and signlessness as the skillful means;

if one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one embraces the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means and signlessness as the skillful means.
If one cultivates all dharani-doors, taking non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one embraces all dharani-doors;
if one cultivates all samadhi-doors, taking non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one embraces all samadhi-doors.
If one cultivates the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, taking non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one thereby embraces the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

If one cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, by employing non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, one embraces unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Kauśika! By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva has great faith and resolve in the perfection of wisdom; he has great faith and resolve in the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;

he has great faith and resolve in internal emptiness; and he has great faith and resolve in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

They have great faith and understanding in *tathatā* (suchness); they have great faith and understanding in the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
they have great faith and understanding in the noble truth of suffering; they have great faith and understanding in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
they have great faith and understanding in the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*); and they have great faith and understanding in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
They have great faith and resolve in the eight liberations; they have great faith and resolve in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases;

they have great faith and resolve in the four foundations of mindfulness; they have great faith and resolve in the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they have great faith and resolve in the gate of liberation of emptiness; and they have great faith and resolve in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
They have great faith and understanding in the five eyes; they have great faith and understanding in the six supernormal powers;

they have great faith and understanding in the ten powers of a Buddha, and great faith and understanding in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they have great faith and understanding in the quality of non-forgetfulness, and great faith and understanding in the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.

They have great faith and understanding in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); they have great faith and understanding in the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they have great faith and understanding in all doors of dhāraṇī; they have great faith and understanding in all doors of samādhi;
and they have great faith and understanding in the conduct of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
They have great faith and resolve in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. "Kauśika!

By virtue of these causes and conditions, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are always sustained by spiritual friends. Such spiritual friends, through immeasurable gateways and with skillful words and meanings, explain for them the dharmas associated with the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity. By instructing and teaching them with such dharmas, they cause them to eventually enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*), and ensure they are never separated from the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity."

By instructing and admonishing them with such teachings, he causes them to eventually enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), and to never be separated from internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

By instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, they cause them to eventually enter the Bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), remaining forever not separated from suchness (*tathatā*), the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathātā*), equality (*samatā*), the nature of departure from birth (*niyāmatā*), the fixed nature of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharmas (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*);

by instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, they cause them to eventually enter the Bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, remaining forever not separated from the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkha-āryasatya*), the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] (*samudaya-āryasatya*), the noble truth of cessation (*nirodha-āryasatya*), and the noble truth of the path (*mārga-āryasatya*).

By instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, he causes them to eventually enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, never being separated from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;

by instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, he causes them to eventually enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, never being separated from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

by instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, he causes them to eventually enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, never being separated from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

By instructing and admonishing them with such dharmas, they cause them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), never being separated from the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), and the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*);

by instructing and admonishing them with such dharmas, they cause them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, never being separated from the five eyes (*pañca-cakṣus*) and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*);

by instructing and admonishing them with such dharmas, they cause them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, never being separated from the ten powers of a Buddha (*daśa-tathāgatabala*), the four fearlessnesses (*catvāri vaiśāradyāni*), the four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisaṃvidah*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*).

By means of such teachings and instructions, he causes them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), remaining forever not separated from the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*) and abiding constantly in equanimity (*upekṣā*).

By means of such teachings and instructions, he causes them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, remaining forever not separated from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

By means of such teachings and instructions, he causes them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, remaining forever not separated from all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*) and all doors of samādhi (*samādhimukha*).

By instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, they cause them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*) and never be separated from the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;

by instructing and exhorting them with such teachings, they cause them to enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination and never be separated from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
Furthermore, they shall explain various demonic deeds so that, having heard them, their minds will neither increase nor decrease in regard to those demonic deeds.
Why is this? Because the nature of all demonic activities is non-existent and unattainable.

He also instructs and exhorts them with this very Dharma, causing them to eventually enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), never being separated from the Buddhas, the Bhagavāns. Having planted various roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas, and because they are sustained by those roots of goodness, they are always born into the family of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they shall never be separated from these roots of goodness.

“Kauśika! If a newly initiated bodhisattva mahāsattva who has set out in the Mahāyāna can thus, by means of non-apprehension as a skillful means and signlessness as a skillful means, embrace all merits and possess deep faith and understanding in those merits; if they are constantly sustained by virtuous friends and, upon hearing such a teaching, their mind is not startled, doubtful, terrified, or afraid—[then they will attain this samādhi].”
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

A newly initiated bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the Great Vehicle, in accordance with the practice and accumulation of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, should, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, together with all sentient beings, dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

In accordance with their dwelling in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—one should, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method and signlessness as the skillful method, together with all sentient beings, dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

In accordance with the true suchness (*tathatā*), the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) in which one abides, one should, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means and signlessness as the skillful means, together with all sentient beings, dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

In accordance with the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin, the noble truth of cessation, and the noble truth of the path in which one abides, one should, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful means and signlessness as the skillful means, together with all sentient beings, dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Whatever four dhyānas, four immeasurables, and four formless attainments they cultivate and accumulate, they should do so with non-apprehension as their means and signlessness as their means, dedicating them together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

whatever eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities they cultivate and accumulate, they should do so with non-apprehension as their means and signlessness as their means, dedicating them together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Whatever four foundations of mindfulness, four right efforts, four bases of power, five faculties, five powers, seven factors of enlightenment, or eight branches of the noble path one has cultivated and accumulated, one should, by means of non-apprehension and by means of signlessness, dedicate them all together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Whatever gate of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, or wishlessness—one has cultivated and accumulated, one should, by means of non-apprehension and by means of signlessness, dedicate them all together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Whatever five eyes and six supernormal powers one cultivates and accumulates, one should do so with non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, dedicating them together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

whatever ten powers of a Buddha, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha one cultivates and accumulates, one should do so with non-apprehension as the means and signlessness as the means, dedicating them together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Whatever *dharmas* of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) they have cultivated and accumulated, they should dedicate them together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension and the skillful means of signlessness;

whatever *sarvajñatā*, *mārgākārajñatā*, and *sarvākārajñatā* they have cultivated and accumulated, they should dedicate them together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension and the skillful means of signlessness;

whatever doors of *dhāraṇī* and doors of *samādhi* they have cultivated and accumulated, they should dedicate them together with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension and the skillful means of signlessness.

In accordance with whatever bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices one cultivates and accumulates, one should, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, together with all sentient beings, dedicate them all toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

in accordance with whatever unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment one cultivates and accumulates, one should, by means of non-apprehension as the expedient and signlessness as the expedient, together with all sentient beings, dedicate it all toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!
A newly initiated bodhisattva mahāsattva of the Mahāyāna should, throughout the countless, immeasurable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions—
in each and every world where there are countless, immeasurable, and boundless ways to sever the paths of existence— [practice as follows...]"
The path that has cut off conceptual proliferation, the casting off of all heavy burdens, the destruction of the thorns of the village,
the exhaustion of all fetters of existence, the perfection of right knowledge, and the mind well-liberated—

the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, and wisdom accomplished by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as their disciples, and their skillful exposition of the essential points of the Dharma.
The aggregate of liberation, the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, and the various merits produced therein;
as well as the roots of goodness planted in those places— namely, the roots of goodness planted by great clans of kṣatriyas,
great clans of brahmins, great clans of householders, and great clans of laymen— and if the four great [elements]...
The roots of goodness planted by the gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven,
and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven; as well as those planted by the gods of the Brahmakāyika,
Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika-parṣadya, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, and Apramāṇābhā heavens.

The roots of goodness planted by the gods of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parītta-śubha Heaven, the Apramāṇa-śubha Heaven, the Śubha-kṛtsna Heaven;

the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parītta-bṛhatphala Heaven, the Apramāṇa-bṛhatphala Heaven, and the Bṛhatphala Heaven; as well as the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, and the Sudarśana Heaven.

The roots of goodness planted by the gods of Akaniṣṭha Heaven and others—all such [roots] are gathered together, weighed, and brought before one’s mind to give rise to a heart of sympathetic joy that, compared to all other roots of goodness, is the most supreme, the most excellent, the most honored, the highest, the most sublime, the most exquisite, the superior, the unsurpassed, the peerless, and the equal to the unequaled. Furthermore, one dedicates these meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, together with all sentient beings, toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya asked the Venerable Subhūti:
"Virtuous One!..."

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, recollecting all the merits of the Buddhas and their assemblies of disciples, as well as the roots of goodness planted by humans, devas, and others—collecting, weighing, and bringing all such things before him—generates a heart of sympathetic joy that, compared to other roots of goodness, is the most supreme, the most excellent, the most honored, the highest, the most wondrous, the most subtle, the most superior, the unsurpassed, the peerless, and the equal to the unequaled; and if he further dedicates these roots of goodness born of sympathetic joy together with all sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—how does this bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid falling into perversion of perception, perversion of mind, and perversion of view?
The Venerable Subhūti replied:

"Great Being! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding all the virtues of the Buddhas they recollect and their assemblies of disciples, does not give rise to the conceptualization of 'Buddhas' or 'disciples' and their virtues;..."
Regarding the roots of goodness planted among humans, devas, and others, they do not give rise to the notion of "humans, devas, and others" as the planters of those roots;

furthermore, regarding the mind that initiates sympathetic joy and dedication toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, they likewise do not give rise to the notion of "the mind that initiates sympathetic joy and dedication toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. This sympathetic joy and dedication initiated by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is free from the perversion of perception, free from the perversion of mind, and free from the perversion of view.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding all the merits of the Buddha and his assembly of disciples whom they bring to mind, grasps at the signs of those merits of the Buddha and disciples;
regarding the roots of goodness planted by humans, devas, and others, grasps at the signs of those roots of goodness and the humans, devas, and others [who planted them];

and regarding the mind they have generated for rejoicing and dedicating toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, grasps at the signs of that generated mind of rejoicing and dedication toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—then the rejoicing and dedication generated by this bodhisattva mahāsattva involves a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
"Furthermore, Great Being!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, with such a mind of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*), contemplates the roots of merit and wholesome qualities of all Buddhas and their assemblies of disciples, he correctly knows that this mind is subject to cessation, extinction, detachment, and transformation, and thus is not capable of sympathetic joy; he correctly knows that those dharmas are likewise by nature [empty], and thus are not objects of sympathetic joy; furthermore, he correctly realizes that the nature of the mind that performs the dedication (*pariṇāmanā*) is also thus, and thus is not capable of dedication; and he correctly realizes that the nature of the dharmas to which there is dedication is also thus, and thus are not objects of dedication."
If there are those who can rely upon this aforementioned rejoicing and dedication—which is correct and not erroneous—all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas should likewise rejoice and dedicate in this manner.
"Furthermore, Great Being! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva,
with respect to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present—
from their first generation of the mind of awakening until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and even until the extinction of the Dharma—
Whatever merit exists therein— including the roots of goodness arising from that Buddha’s Dharma by his disciples and the various Pratyekabuddhas,
the roots of goodness planted by ordinary beings upon hearing his teaching,
and those of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and garuḍas—
The kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others who hear his teaching of the Dharma and plant roots of merit;

as well as those of great kṣatriya clans, great brahmin clans, great householder clans, and great merchant clans who hear his teaching of the Dharma and plant roots of merit; and those of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings—
The gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven,
and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven heard his teaching of the Dharma and planted roots of goodness;
as did the gods of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika-pariṣad, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Parīttābha, and Apramāṇābha heavens.

The gods of the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven,

the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Anabhraka Heaven,

the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, and the Sudarśana Heaven— having heard his teaching of the Dharma, they planted roots of goodness. Furthermore, the gods of the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, and the Sudarśana Heaven...
The gods of the Sudarśana Heaven and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, hearing the roots of goodness planted by that teaching of the Dharma,
if there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, upon hearing the taught Dharma, resolve their minds toward unexcelled, perfect,
and complete enlightenment and diligently cultivate the various practices of a bodhisattva.

Having thus gathered all these together and weighed them before one, this mind of sympathetic joy—which surpasses other roots of goodness as the most supreme, the most excellent, the most honored, the highest, the most sublime, the most exquisite, the superior, the unsurpassed, the peerless, and the equal to the unequaled—is further dedicated, together with all sentient beings, toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of such roots of goodness born of sympathetic joy.

"At such a time, if one correctly understands that all phenomena which can be rejoiced in and dedicated are exhausted, ceased, detached from, and transformed, and that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena which are rejoiced in and dedicated is empty—then, despite knowing this, one is able to rejoice in and dedicate [merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Furthermore, at that time, if one correctly understands that there is no dharma whatsoever that can be rejoiced in or dedicated toward a dharma.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all dharmas is empty; within emptiness, there is absolutely no dharma that can act as the agent of rejoicing or dedication, nor any dharma that is the object thereof.
Although they know this, they are able to rejoice in [these merits] and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva can thus rejoice and dedicate, and practices the perfection of wisdom, as well as the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, they are free from the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, and the inversion of view.

Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the mind of sympathetic joy, nor does he give rise to attachment toward the roots of merit and goodness that are the object of that joy; he does not give rise to attachment toward the mind of dedication, nor does he give rise to attachment toward the unsurpassed enlightenment to which it is dedicated. By being without attachment, he does not fall into perversions.
In this way, the mind of sympathetic joy and dedication generated by a bodhisattva mahāsattva is called the unsurpassed sympathetic joy and dedication.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 169, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter 31 (Part 3): Sympathetic Joy and Dedication. "Furthermore, Great Being!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding all the meritorious deeds they cultivate, correctly knows them to be detached from form, and detached from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;
correctly knows them to be detached from the sense base of the eye, and detached from the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;
and correctly knows them to be detached from the sense base of forms, and detached from the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.

He correctly knows the separation from the eye element, the separation from the form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition;

he correctly knows the separation from the ear element, the separation from the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition;

he correctly knows the separation from the nose element, the separation from the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as their condition.
He correctly knows the separation from the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings arising with tongue-contact as condition;
he correctly knows the separation from the body element, the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings arising with body-contact as condition;
he correctly knows the separation from the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, and all feelings arising with mind-contact as condition.
He correctly knows detachment from the earth element, and detachment from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;

he correctly knows detachment from ignorance, and detachment from volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair;
he correctly knows detachment from the perfection of generosity, and detachment from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

He correctly knows [them] as being apart from internal emptiness, apart from external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

he correctly knows [them] as being apart from suchness, apart from the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of non-arising, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
he correctly knows [them] as being apart from the noble truth of suffering, and apart from the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
He correctly knows detachment from the four dhyānas, detachment from the four immeasurables, and detachment from the four formless attainments;
he correctly knows detachment from the eight liberations, detachment from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

he correctly knows detachment from the four foundations of mindfulness, detachment from the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
He correctly knows detachment from the gate of liberation of emptiness, and detachment from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
he correctly knows detachment from the five eyes, and detachment from the six supernormal powers;

he correctly knows detachment from the ten powers of a Buddha, and detachment from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Right knowledge is detached from the quality of non-forgetfulness and detached from the nature of constant equanimity;
right knowledge is detached from all-knowledge, detached from the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and detached from the knowledge of all aspects;
right knowledge is detached from all dharani-doors and detached from all samadhi-doors.
They correctly know that they are detached from the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
they correctly know that they are detached from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses such correct knowledge regarding all the meritorious deeds they have performed, they are able to correctly rejoice in them and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Great Being!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva correctly knows that the various meritorious deeds associated with sympathetic joy (anumodanā) are devoid of the intrinsic nature of those meritorious deeds associated with sympathetic joy; correctly knows that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is devoid of the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; and correctly knows that all the qualities of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the qualities of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;

and correctly knows that Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas are devoid of the intrinsic nature of Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas; and correctly knows that the roots of goodness cultivated by Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the roots of goodness of Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas..."

He correctly knows that the bodhicitta is devoid of the intrinsic nature of bodhicitta; he correctly knows that the mind of dedication is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the mind of dedication; he correctly knows that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment toward which one dedicates is devoid of the intrinsic nature of that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

He correctly knows that the perfection of wisdom is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom; he correctly knows that the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.

With correct knowledge, one understands that inner emptiness is devoid of the intrinsic nature of inner emptiness; and with correct knowledge, one understands that outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are devoid of the intrinsic nature of outer emptiness, up to and including the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

He correctly knows that suchness is devoid of the intrinsic nature of suchness; he correctly knows that the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm;

he correctly knows that the noble truth of suffering is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering; he correctly knows that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;

he correctly knows that the four dhyānas are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas; he correctly knows that the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

They correctly know that the eight liberations are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations; they correctly know that the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they correctly know that the four foundations of mindfulness are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; they correctly know that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path;

they correctly know that the gate of liberation of emptiness is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness; and they correctly know that the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

They correctly know that the five eyes are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the five eyes; they correctly know that the six supernormal powers are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers.

They correctly know that the ten powers of a Buddha are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; they correctly know that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They correctly know that the quality of non-forgetfulness is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness; they correctly know that the state of constant dwelling in equanimity is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the state of constant dwelling in equanimity.

He correctly knows that all-knowledge is devoid of the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge; he correctly knows that the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are devoid of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
he correctly knows that all dharani-doors are devoid of the intrinsic nature of all dharani-doors; he correctly knows that all samadhi-doors are devoid of the intrinsic nature of all samadhi-doors;
and he correctly knows that the bodhisattva-mahasattva practice is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the bodhisattva-mahasattva practice.
Knowing that the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is devoid of the intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,

this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom that is free from intrinsic nature, and is thus able to correctly rejoice in and dedicate [merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Great Being!

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas wish to generate a mind of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*) and dedicate toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment the roots of virtue and merit of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples who have already entered parinirvāṇa, they should perform such dedication with sympathetic joy by forming this thought:

'Just as all those Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples have already passed into extinction, so too are their roots of virtue and merit; likewise is the nature of the mind of sympathetic joy and dedication toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment that I have generated, and the unexcelled enlightenment toward which it is dedicated.'"
"In this way, one rejoices in and dedicates [merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment without conceptual inversion, without mental inversion, and without view-inversion.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom by means of grasping at signs, and rejoices in and dedicates all the roots of virtue and merit of those Buddhas and their disciples while grasping at signs, this is not a skillful rejoicing or dedication."

Because the merit and roots of goodness of the past Buddhas and their assemblies of disciples are not objects to be grasped through signs or signlessness, yet this bodhisattva mahāsattva initiates rejoicing and dedicates it toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment by grasping at signs; therefore, this is not a skillful rejoicing or dedication. By reason of this, they fall into perversion of perception, perversion of mind, and perversion of view.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom by means of non-apprehension of signs, and rejoices in and dedicates all the roots of virtue and merits of those Buddhas and their disciples toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment while remaining free from signs, this is called "skillful rejoicing and dedication.
