it does not make form accumulate or disperse, nor does it make feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of form as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of form as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of form as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the sphere of the eye great or small; it likewise does not make the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind great or small.
It does not make the sphere of the eye accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of the eye-base as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the eye-base as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of the eye-base as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a conception as this:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make form large or small; it likewise does not make sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or phenomena large or small.
It does not make form accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or phenomena accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the sphere of form, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the sphere of form, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the sphere of form, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the eye-element great or small; it does not make the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, or the eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition great or small;
it does not make the eye-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the eye-element as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the eye-element as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the eye-element as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the ear-element great or small; it does not make the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition great or small;
it does not make the ear-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the sound-element, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the ear element as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the sound element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the ear element as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the sound element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the ear element as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the sound element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the nose-element great or small; it does not make the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition great or small;

it does not make the nose-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the odor-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the nose element as finite nor as infinite; one does not conceive of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the nose element as broad nor as narrow; one does not conceive of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the nose element as powerful nor as powerless; one does not conceive of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the tongue element great or small; it does not make the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition great or small.

It does not make the tongue element accumulate or disperse; it does not make the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the tongue element, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the tongue element, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the tongue element, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfections of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), diligence (*vīrya*), patience (*kṣānti*), ethical discipline (*śīla*), and generosity (*dāna*), gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) great or small; it likewise does not make the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, great or small.

It does not make the body-element accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the contact-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the body element (*kāyadhātu*), one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the body element, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the contact element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the body element, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the contact element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the mind-element large or small; it does not make the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, or the mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition large or small;
it does not make the mind-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the mind-element, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the dharma-element, and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the mind-element, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the dharma-element, and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the mind-element, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the dharma-element, and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the earth element great or small; it likewise does not make the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements great or small.
It does not cause the earth element to gather or disperse; it likewise does not cause the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements to gather or disperse."
One does not conceive of the earth element as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the earth element as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of the earth element as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make ignorance great or small; it likewise does not make volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair great or small;
it does not make ignorance accumulate or disperse, nor does it make volitional formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, accumulate or disperse."

One does not regard ignorance as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not regard the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as finite or infinite.

One does not regard ignorance as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not regard the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as broad or narrow.

One does not regard ignorance as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not regard the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the perfection of generosity great or small; it likewise does not make the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom great or small.
It does not make the perfection of generosity accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the perfection of generosity, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the perfection of generosity, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the perfection of generosity, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 174. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Praise of Prajñā, Chapter Thirty-Two, Section Four. “Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make inner emptiness great or small; nor does it make outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature great or small."

One does not effect accumulation or dispersal regarding internal emptiness; one likewise does not effect accumulation or dispersal regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One does not effect finitude or infinitude regarding internal emptiness; one likewise does not effect finitude or infinitude regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One does not effect expansion or contraction regarding internal emptiness; one likewise does not effect expansion or contraction regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One does not regard inner emptiness as having power nor as being powerless; one likewise does not regard outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, as having power nor as being powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make true suchness (tathatā) great or small; it likewise does not make the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm great or small;
it does not make true suchness accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of *tathatā* as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), as finite or infinite.
One does not conceive of *tathatā* as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm, as broad or narrow.
One does not conceive of *tathatā* as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the noble truth of suffering great or small; it likewise does not make the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path great or small.
It does not make the noble truth of suffering accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the four meditative concentrations great or small; it likewise does not make the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions great or small.
It does not make the four meditative concentrations accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the four dhyānas, they do not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise do not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the four dhyānas, they do not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise do not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the four dhyānas, they do not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise do not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the eight liberations great or small; it likewise does not make the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities great or small.
It does not make the eight liberations gathered or dispersed; it likewise does not make the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities gathered or dispersed."

Regarding the eight liberations, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the eight liberations, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the four foundations of mindfulness great or small; nor does it make the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path great or small.
It does not make the four foundations of mindfulness gathered or dispersed; nor does it make [anything] from the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path gathered or dispersed."

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the door of liberation of emptiness great or small, nor does it make the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness great or small;
it does not make the door of liberation of emptiness accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
“This perfection of wisdom does not make the five eyes great or small, nor does it make the six supernormal powers great or small;

Regarding the five eyes, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the six supernormal powers, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.
Regarding the five eyes, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the six supernormal powers, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), diligence (*vīrya*), patience (*kṣānti*), ethical discipline (*śīla*), and generosity (*dāna*), gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the ten powers of a buddha great or small; it likewise does not make the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), great compassion (*karuṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*muditā*), great equanimity (*upekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) great or small.
It does not make the ten powers of a buddha accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the quality of non-forgetfulness great or small, nor does it make the state of constant equanimity great or small;
it does not make the quality of non-forgetfulness accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the state of constant equanimity accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not conceive of it as limited nor as limitless; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not conceive of it as limited nor as limitless.

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes all-knowledge great nor small; it likewise neither makes the knowledge of the paths nor the knowledge of all aspects great nor small.
It neither collects all-knowledge nor disperses it; it likewise neither collects the knowledge of the paths nor the knowledge of all aspects, nor disperses them."

Regarding all-knowledge, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding all-knowledge, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding all-knowledge, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make all doors of dhāraṇī great or small, nor does it make all doors of samādhi great or small;
it does not make all doors of dhāraṇī gathered or dispersed, nor does it make all doors of samādhi gathered or dispersed."
Regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding all samādhi-doors, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.
Regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding all samādhi-doors, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.
Regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding all samādhi-doors, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the stream-enterer great or small; it does not make the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat great or small.
It does not make the stream-enterer accumulate or disperse; it does not make the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the stream-enterer, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the stream-enterer, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the stream-enterer, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry great or small; it likewise does not make the stage of entering once-returning or the fruit of once-returning, the stage of entering non-returning or the fruit of non-returning, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship great or small.

It does not make the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry accumulated or dispersed; it likewise does not make [the stages] from entering once-returning up to the fruit of arhatship accumulated or dispersed."

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom is neither great nor small toward the pratyekabuddha, nor is it neither great nor small toward the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
it is neither accumulated nor dispersed toward the pratyekabuddha, nor is it neither accumulated nor dispersed toward the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;"
One does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha as finite nor as infinite; one does not conceive of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha as broad nor as narrow; one does not conceive of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha as powerful nor as powerless; one does not conceive of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva great nor small, nor does it make the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva great or small;
it neither makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva accumulate nor disperse, nor does it make the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as having measure nor as being without measure; one does not conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as having measure nor as being without measure.
One does not conceive of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being broad nor as being narrow; one does not conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being broad nor as being narrow.

One does not conceive of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being powerful nor as being powerless; one does not conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being powerful nor as being powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas great nor small, nor does it make the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment great or small;
it neither causes the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas to gather nor disperse, nor does it cause the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to gather or disperse."

One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as finite, nor does one conceive of them as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as finite, nor does one conceive of it as infinite.

One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as broad, nor does one conceive of them as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as broad, nor does one conceive of it as narrow.

One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as powerful, nor does one conceive of them as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as powerful, nor does one conceive of it as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make all phenomena great or small; it does not make them gathered or dispersed; it does not make them finite or infinite; it does not make them broad or narrow; it does not make them powerful or powerless."
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes form large or small; it likewise makes feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness large or small;
it makes form accumulate or disperse, and it likewise makes feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness accumulate or disperse."
One regards form as finite or infinite; one likewise regards feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as finite or infinite.
One regards form as vast or narrow; one likewise regards feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as vast or narrow.
One regards form as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly initiated bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the sphere of the eye large or small; it likewise makes the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind large or small;
it gathers together the sphere of the eye or disperses it, and likewise gathers together or disperses the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind."
One regards the eye-base as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as finite or infinite.
One regards the eye-base as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as broad or narrow.
One regards the eye-base as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the sphere of form large or small; it likewise makes the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena large or small;
it gathers together the sphere of form or disperses it, and likewise gathers together or disperses the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena."
One regards the sphere of form as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as finite or infinite.
One regards the sphere of form as vast or narrow; one likewise regards the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as vast or narrow.
One regards the sphere of form as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a perception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the eye-element great or small; it also makes the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, great or small;
it collects the eye-element or disperses it, and likewise collects or disperses the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition."
One regards the eye-element as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the form-element, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as finite or infinite.
One regards the eye-element as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the form-element, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as broad or narrow.
One regards the eye-element as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the form-element, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the ear-element great or small; it also makes the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, great or small;
it makes the ear-element accumulate or disperse, and it also makes the sound-element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."
One regards the ear-element as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the sound-element, and even all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as finite or infinite.
One regards the ear-element as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the sound-element, and even all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as broad or narrow.
One regards the ear-element as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the sound-element, and even all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the nose element great or small; it also makes the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition great or small;
it makes the nose element accumulate or disperse, and it also makes the odor element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the nose element, one conceives it as finite or infinite; regarding the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the nose element, one conceives it as vast or narrow; regarding the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as vast or narrow.

Regarding the nose element, one conceives it as powerful or powerless; regarding the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the tongue element great or small; it also makes the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition great or small;
it makes the tongue element accumulate or disperse, and likewise makes the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the tongue element, one conceives it as finite or infinite; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the tongue element, one conceives it as broad or narrow; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the tongue element, one conceives it as powerful or powerless; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying upon the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the body-element large or small; it likewise makes the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition—large or small;
it makes the body-element accumulate or disperse, and likewise makes the contact-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the body element, one conceives it as finite or infinite; regarding the tangible object element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the body element, one conceives it as broad or narrow; regarding the tangible object element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the body element, one conceives it as powerful or powerless; regarding the tangible object element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the mind-element large or small; it also makes the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness element, and mental contact—as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—large or small;
it collects or disperses the mind-element, and likewise collects or disperses everything from the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition."

Regarding the mind-element (*manodhātu*), he conceives it as finite or infinite; regarding the mental-object-element (*dharmadhātu*) and even all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, he likewise conceives them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the mind-element, he conceives it as broad or narrow; regarding the mental-object-element and even all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, he likewise conceives them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the mind-element, he conceives it as powerful or powerless; regarding the mental-object-element and even all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, he likewise conceives them as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the earth element large or small; it likewise makes the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness large or small;
it gathers together or disperses the earth element, and likewise gathers together or disperses the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness."
One conceives of the earth element as limited and as limitless; one likewise conceives of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as limited and as limitless.
One conceives of the earth element as broad and as narrow; one likewise conceives of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as broad and as narrow.
One conceives of the earth element as powerful and as powerless; one likewise conceives of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as powerful and as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a conception as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes ignorance great or small; it likewise makes formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair great or small;
it collects ignorance or disperses it, and likewise collects or disperses formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."
One regards ignorance as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as finite or infinite.
One regards ignorance as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the formative forces up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as broad or narrow.
One regards ignorance as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the formative forces up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the perfection of generosity great or small; it likewise makes the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom great or small;
it gathers together the perfection of generosity or disperses it, and likewise gathers together or disperses the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom."
One conceives of the perfection of generosity as finite or infinite; one likewise conceives of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom as finite or infinite.
One conceives of the perfection of generosity as broad or narrow; one likewise conceives of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom as broad or narrow.
One conceives of the perfection of generosity as powerful or powerless; one likewise conceives of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to this thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the internal emptiness great or small; it likewise makes the external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharmas emptiness, unapprehendable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, and non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness great or small."
One performs the gathering and dispersing of internal emptiness, and likewise performs the gathering and dispersing of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
one performs the finite and the infinite of internal emptiness, and likewise performs the finite and the infinite of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
one performs the broad and the narrow of internal emptiness, and likewise performs the broad and the narrow of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

"One might regard inner emptiness as having power or lacking power; one might likewise regard outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, as having power or lacking power.
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a perception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Blessed One, if a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva,
relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a perception as this:

"In this way, this Prajñāpāramitā makes the *tathatā* (suchness) large or small; it likewise makes the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, *avitathatā*, *ananyathābhāvatā*, *samatā*, *anirodhatā*, *dharmasthititā*, *dharmaniyāmatā*, *bhūtakoṭi*, *ākāśadhātu*, and *acintyadhātu* large or small.
It makes the *tathatā* accumulate or disperse, and likewise makes the *dharmadhātu* up to the *acintyadhātu* accumulate or disperse.
It makes the *tathatā* finite or infinite, and likewise makes the *dharmadhātu* up to the *acintyadhātu* finite or infinite."
They conceptualize *tathatā* as broad or narrow; they likewise conceptualize the *dharmadhātu*, up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), as broad or narrow.
They conceptualize *tathatā* as having power or lacking power; they likewise conceptualize the *dharmadhātu*, up to the inconceivable realm, as having power or lacking power.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the noble truth of suffering great or small; it likewise makes the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path great or small;
it collects or disperses the noble truth of suffering; and it likewise collects or disperses the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."
One regards the noble truth of suffering as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as finite or infinite.
One regards the noble truth of suffering as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as broad or narrow.
One regards the noble truth of suffering as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the four meditative concentrations great or small; it also makes the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions great or small;
it gathers together the four meditative concentrations or disperses them, and it also gathers together or disperses the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions."

Regarding the four dhyānas, they practice them as limited and as limitless; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise practice them as limited and as limitless.
Regarding the four dhyānas, they practice them as expansive and as narrow; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise practice them as expansive and as narrow.

Regarding the four dhyānas, they practice them as powerful and as powerless; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise practice them as powerful and as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the eight liberations great or small; it also makes the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities great or small;
it gathers the eight liberations and disperses them, and it also gathers the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities and disperses them."

Regarding the eight liberations, they conceive of them as limited or unlimited; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they likewise conceive of them as limited or unlimited.

Regarding the eight liberations, they conceive of them as extensive or narrow; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they likewise conceive of them as extensive or narrow.

Regarding the eight liberations, they conceive of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the four foundations of mindfulness great or small; it also makes the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path great or small;
it gathers together the four foundations of mindfulness and disperses them, and likewise gathers together and disperses the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path."

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one regards them as limited or as limitless; regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, one likewise regards them as limited or as limitless.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one regards them as broad or as narrow; regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, one likewise regards them as broad or as narrow.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one regards them as powerful or as powerless; regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, one likewise regards them as powerful or as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the door of liberation of emptiness large or small; it also makes the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness large or small;
it makes the door of liberation of emptiness accumulate or disperse; it also makes the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, they conceive of it as finite or infinite; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise conceive of them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, they conceive of it as broad or narrow; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise conceive of them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, they conceive of it as powerful or powerless; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the five eyes great or small; it also makes the six supernormal powers great or small;
it gathers the five eyes together or disperses them; it also gathers the six supernormal powers together or disperses them."
Regarding the five eyes, they conceive of them as finite or infinite; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise conceive of them as finite or infinite.
Regarding the five eyes, they conceive of them as broad or narrow; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise conceive of them as broad or narrow.
Regarding the five eyes, they conceive of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the ten powers of a Buddha great or small; it also makes the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha great or small.
It collects the ten powers of a Buddha or disperses them; it also collects or disperses the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they treat them as finite and infinite; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise treat them as finite and infinite.

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they treat them as broad and narrow; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise treat them as broad and narrow.

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they treat them as powerful and powerless; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise treat them as powerful and powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the state of non-forgetfulness great or small, and likewise makes the nature of constant equanimity great or small;
it gathers the state of non-forgetfulness or disperses it, and likewise gathers the nature of constant equanimity or disperses it."
Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, they conceive of it as finite or infinite; regarding the state of constant equanimity, they likewise conceive of it as finite or infinite.
Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, they conceive of it as broad or narrow; regarding the state of constant equanimity, they likewise conceive of it as broad or narrow.
Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, they conceive of it as powerful or powerless; regarding the state of constant equanimity, they likewise conceive of it as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*.

*The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 175, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter Praising Prajñā, Thirty-Two, Section Five. "Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom performs great and small deeds for all-knowledge; it likewise performs great and small deeds for the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
it performs the gathering and the dispersing of all-knowledge; it likewise performs the gathering and the dispersing of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects."
They treat all-knowledge as finite or infinite; they treat the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects likewise as finite or infinite.
They treat all-knowledge as broad or narrow; they treat the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects likewise as broad or narrow.
They treat all-knowledge as powerful or powerless; they treat the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects likewise as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a perception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom makes all doors of dhāraṇī large or small; it also makes all doors of samādhi large or small;
it gathers together all doors of dhāraṇī and disperses them; it also gathers together all doors of samādhi and disperses them."
Regarding all *dhāraṇī* gates, they make them finite and make them infinite; regarding all *samādhi* gates, they likewise make them finite and make them infinite.
Regarding all *dhāraṇī* gates, they make them broad and make them narrow; regarding all *samādhi* gates, they likewise make them broad and make them narrow.
Regarding all *dhāraṇī* gates, they make them powerful and make them powerless; regarding all *samādhi* gates, they likewise make them powerful and make them powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the stream-enterer great or small; it likewise makes the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat great or small;
it gathers the stream-enterer or disperses them, and likewise gathers or disperses the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat."
Regarding stream-enterers, they conceive of them as finite or infinite; regarding once-returners, non-returners, and arhats, they likewise conceive of them as finite or infinite.
Regarding stream-enterers, they conceive of them as broad or narrow; regarding once-returners, non-returners, and arhats, they likewise conceive of them as broad or narrow.
Regarding stream-enterers, they conceive of them as powerful or powerless; regarding once-returners, non-returners, and arhats, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry great or small; it also makes the stage of entering the once-returner and the fruit of the once-returner, the stage of entering the non-returner and the fruit of the non-returner, and the stage of entering arhatship and the fruit of arhatship great or small;

it gathers together or disperses the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, and likewise gathers together or disperses everything from the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship."

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one conceives of them as finite or infinite; regarding the stages from entering the once-returner up to arhatship, one likewise conceives of them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one conceives of them as broad or narrow; regarding the stages from entering the once-returner up to arhatship, one likewise conceives of them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one conceives of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the stages from entering the once-returner up to arhatship, one likewise conceives of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the pratyekabuddha great or small; it also makes the pratyekabuddha's enlightenment great or small;
it makes the pratyekabuddha gathered or dispersed; it also makes the pratyekabuddha's enlightenment gathered or dispersed."
Regarding the pratyekabuddhas, they conceive of them as finite or infinite; regarding the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas, they likewise conceive of it as finite or infinite.
Regarding the pratyekabuddhas, they conceive of them as broad or narrow; regarding the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas, they likewise conceive of it as broad or narrow.
Regarding the pratyekabuddhas, they conceive of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas, they likewise conceive of it as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva great or small; it also makes the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva great or small;
it makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva gather or disperse; it also makes the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva gather or disperse."
They conceive of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as having limits or being limitless; they also conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as having limits or being limitless.
They conceive of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being vast or narrow; they also conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being vast or narrow.
They conceive of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being powerful or powerless; they also conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom performs great and small deeds for all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and it also performs great and small deeds for the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas;
it gathers and disperses all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and it also gathers and disperses the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas."
To regard the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as finite or infinite, and likewise to regard the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as finite or infinite;
to regard the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as vast or narrow, and likewise to regard the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as vast or narrow;

to regard the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as possessing power or lacking power, and likewise to regard the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as possessing power or lacking power.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes all phenomena large or small, gathered or dispersed, finite or infinite, broad or narrow, powerful or powerless."
“World-Honored One!
