Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, or the perfection of generosity, should give rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make form great or small; it does not make feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness great or small.
It does not make form accumulate or disperse; it does not make feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of form as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of form as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of form as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the sphere of the eye great or small; it likewise does not make the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind great or small.
It does not make the sphere of the eye accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of the eye-base as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the eye-base as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of the eye-base as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make form large or small; it likewise does not make sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or phenomena large or small.
It does not make form accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not make sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or phenomena accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of the sphere of form as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the sphere of form as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the sphere of form as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the eye-element great or small; it does not make the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition great or small;
it does not make the eye-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the form-element, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the eye-element as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the eye-element as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the eye-element as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the ear-element great or small; it does not make the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, or the ear-contact, nor the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, great or small;
it does not make the ear-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the sound-element, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the ear element as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the sound element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the ear element as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the sound element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the ear element as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the sound element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, should give rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the nose-element great or small; it does not make the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition great or small;

it does not make the nose-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the odor-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the nose element as finite nor as infinite; one does not conceive of the odor element, nor even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the nose element as broad nor as narrow; one does not conceive of the odor element, nor even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the nose element as powerful nor as powerless; one does not conceive of the odor element, nor even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the tongue-element great or small; it does not make the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, or the tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition great or small;
it does not make the tongue-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the taste-element, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the tongue element, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the tongue element, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the tongue element, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the body-element great or small; it does not make the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, or the body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition great or small;
it does not make the body-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the contact-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the body-element, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the contact-element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the body-element, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the contact-element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the mind-element great or small; it does not make the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, or the feeling produced with mind-contact as its condition great or small;
it does not make the mind-element accumulate or disperse, nor does it make anything from the dharma-element up to the feeling produced with mind-contact as its condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the mind-element (*manodhātu*), one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the mind-element, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the dharma-element and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the mind-element, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the dharma-element and even the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, should give rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the earth element great or small; it likewise does not make the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements great or small.
It does not cause the earth element to accumulate or disperse; it likewise does not cause the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements to accumulate or disperse."
One does not conceive of the earth element as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the earth element as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of the earth element as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom neither makes ignorance great nor small; it likewise neither makes volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, nor old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair great nor small;
it neither accumulates ignorance nor disperses it, and it likewise neither accumulates nor disperses volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."

Regarding ignorance, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding ignorance, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding ignorance, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the perfection of generosity great or small; it likewise does not make the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom great or small;
it does not make the perfection of generosity accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the perfection of generosity, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the perfection of generosity, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the perfection of generosity, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make inner emptiness great or small; nor does it make outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence great or small."

One does not effect accumulation or dispersion regarding internal emptiness, nor does one effect accumulation or dispersion regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

one does not effect finitude or infinitude regarding internal emptiness, nor does one effect finitude or infinitude regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

one does not effect expansion or contraction regarding internal emptiness, nor does one effect expansion or contraction regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

One does not conceive inner emptiness as having power or lacking power; one likewise does not conceive outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, as having power or lacking power.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make true thusness (tathatā) great or small; nor does it make the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm great or small;
nor does it make true thusness gathered or dispersed, nor does it make the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm gathered or dispersed."
One does not conceive of *tathatā* as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), as finite or infinite.
One does not conceive of *tathatā* as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm, as broad or narrow.

One does not conceive of *tathatā* as possessing power nor as lacking power; one likewise does not conceive of the *dharmadhātu*, up to and including the inconceivable realm, as possessing power or lacking power.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the noble truth of suffering great or small; it likewise does not make the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path great or small;
it does not make the noble truth of suffering accumulate or disperse, nor does it make the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one does not conceive it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise does not conceive them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one does not conceive it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise does not conceive them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one does not conceive it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise does not conceive them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the four meditative concentrations great nor small; it likewise neither makes the four immeasurables nor the four formless absorptions great nor small;
it neither makes the four meditative concentrations accumulate nor disperse, and it likewise neither makes the four immeasurables nor the four formless absorptions accumulate nor disperse."

Regarding the four dhyānas, he does not conceive of them as limited nor as unlimited; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, he likewise does not conceive of them as limited nor as unlimited.

Regarding the four dhyānas, he does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, he likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the four dhyānas, he does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, he likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the eight liberations great or small; it likewise does not make the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities great or small;
it does not make the eight liberations gathered or dispersed; it likewise does not make the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities gathered or dispersed."

Regarding the eight liberations, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the eight liberations, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the eight liberations, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the four applications of mindfulness great or small; nor does it make the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path great or small;
it does not make the four applications of mindfulness collected or dispersed, nor does it make the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path collected or dispersed."

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes no distinction of great or small regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness; it likewise makes no distinction of great or small regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
It neither accumulates nor disperses regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness; it likewise neither accumulates nor disperses regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the five eyes great nor small, nor does it make the six superknowledges great or small;
it neither causes the five eyes to gather nor disperse, nor does it cause the six superknowledges to gather or disperse."
Regarding the five eyes, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the six supernormal powers, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.
Regarding the five eyes, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the six supernormal powers, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.
Regarding the five eyes, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the six supernormal powers, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the ten powers of a buddha great nor small; it likewise neither makes the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha great nor small;

it neither causes the ten powers of a buddha to gather nor to disperse, and it likewise neither causes the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha to gather nor to disperse."

One does not conceive of the Buddha’s ten powers as finite nor as infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as finite nor as infinite.

One does not conceive of the Buddha’s ten powers as broad nor as narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as broad nor as narrow.

One does not conceive of the Buddha’s ten powers as powerful nor as powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the state of non-forgetfulness great nor small, nor does it make the state of constant equanimity great nor small;
it neither accumulates the state of non-forgetfulness nor disperses it, nor does it accumulate the state of constant equanimity nor disperse it."

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, should give rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes all-knowledge great nor small; it likewise neither makes the knowledge of the paths nor the knowledge of all aspects great nor small;
it neither gathers all-knowledge nor disperses it; it likewise neither gathers the knowledge of the paths nor the knowledge of all aspects, nor disperses them."

Regarding all-knowledge, one does not conceive of it as finite nor as infinite; regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding all-knowledge, one does not conceive of it as broad nor as narrow; regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding all-knowledge, one does not conceive of it as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make all doors of dhāraṇī great or small, nor does it make all doors of samādhi great or small;
it does not make all doors of dhāraṇī gather or disperse, nor does it make all doors of samādhi gather or disperse."
Regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, they do not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding all samādhi-doors, they likewise do not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.
Regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, they do not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding all samādhi-doors, they likewise do not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.
Regarding all dhāraṇī-doors, they do not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding all samādhi-doors, they likewise do not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom does not make the stream-enterer great or small; it likewise does not make the once-returner, non-returner, or arhat great or small;
it does not make the stream-enterer gathered or dispersed, and it likewise does not make the once-returner, non-returner, or arhat gathered or dispersed."

Regarding the stream-enterer, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the stream-enterer, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the stream-enterer, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry great or small; it likewise does not make the stage of entering the once-returner or the fruit of once-returner, the stage of entering the non-returner or the fruit of non-returner, or the stage of entering arhatship or the fruit of arhatship great or small;

it does not make the stage of entering the stream or the fruit of stream-entry accumulated or dispersed, nor does it make anything from the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship accumulated or dispersed."

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite; regarding the stages from entering once-returning up to arhatship, one likewise does not conceive of them as finite nor as infinite.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow; regarding the stages from entering once-returning up to arhatship, one likewise does not conceive of them as broad nor as narrow.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, one does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless; regarding the stages from entering once-returning up to arhatship, one likewise does not conceive of them as powerful nor as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom is neither great nor small toward a pratyekabuddha, and it is neither great nor small toward the awakening of a pratyekabuddha;
it neither accumulates nor disperses toward a pratyekabuddha, and it neither accumulates nor disperses toward the awakening of a pratyekabuddha."
One does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha as finite nor as infinite; one does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha’s enlightenment as finite nor as infinite.
One does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha as broad nor as narrow; one does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha’s enlightenment as broad nor as narrow.
One does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha as powerful nor as powerless; one does not conceive of the pratyekabuddha’s enlightenment as powerful nor as powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva great nor small, nor does it make the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva great or small;
it neither makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva accumulate nor disperse, nor does it make the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva accumulate or disperse."

One does not conceive of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as having measure nor as being immeasurable; one does not conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as having measure nor as being immeasurable.
One does not conceive of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being broad nor as being narrow; one does not conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being broad nor as being narrow.

One does not conceive of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being powerful nor as being powerless; one does not conceive of the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva as being powerful nor as being powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom neither makes the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas great nor small; it also neither makes the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment great nor small.
It neither causes the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas to gather nor to disperse; it also neither causes the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment to gather nor to disperse."

One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as being finite, nor does one conceive of them as being infinite; one likewise does not conceive of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as being finite, nor does one conceive of it as being infinite.

One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as being broad, nor does one conceive of them as being narrow; one likewise does not conceive of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as being broad, nor does one conceive of it as being narrow.

One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as being powerful, nor does one conceive of them as being powerless; one likewise does not conceive of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment as being powerful, nor does one conceive of it as being powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom does not make all phenomena great or small, does not make them gathered or dispersed, does not make them finite or infinite, does not make them broad or narrow, and does not make them powerful or powerless."
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, he is not practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*.
*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 176, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Praising Prajñā, Thirty-Two, Section Six. “World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, or the perfection of generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes form large or small; it likewise makes feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness large or small;
it makes form accumulate or disperse; it likewise makes feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness accumulate or disperse."
One regards form as finite or infinite; one likewise regards feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as finite or infinite.
One regards form as vast or narrow; one likewise regards feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as vast or narrow.
One regards form as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the eye-faculty large or small; it likewise makes the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-faculties large or small;
it makes the eye-faculty gather or disperse; it likewise makes the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-faculties gather or disperse."
One regards the eye-base as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as finite or infinite.
One regards the eye-base as vast or narrow; one likewise regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as vast or narrow.
One regards the eye-base as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a conception as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the sphere of form large or small; it likewise makes the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena large or small;
it makes the sphere of form gather or disperse; it likewise makes the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena gather or disperse."

Regarding the sphere of visible forms, one conceives of them as finite or infinite; regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, one likewise conceives of them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the sphere of visible forms, one conceives of them as vast or narrow; regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, one likewise conceives of them as vast or narrow.

Regarding the sphere of visible forms, one conceives of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, one likewise conceives of them as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the eye-element large or small; it also makes the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, large or small;
it collects the eye-element or disperses it, and likewise collects or disperses the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition."
One regards the eye-element as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the form-element, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as finite or infinite.
One regards the eye-element as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the form-element, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as broad or narrow.
One regards the eye-element as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the form-element, and even the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the ear-element large or small; it also makes the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, large or small;
it causes the ear-element to aggregate or disperse, and likewise causes the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition to aggregate or disperse."
He regards the ear-element as finite or infinite; he likewise regards the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition, as finite or infinite.
He regards the ear-element as broad or narrow; he likewise regards the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition, as broad or narrow.
He regards the ear-element as powerful or powerless; he likewise regards the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition, as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the nose-element great or small; it also makes the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition great or small;
it makes the nose-element accumulate or disperse, and it also makes the odor-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the nose element, one conceives it as finite or infinite; regarding the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the nose element, one conceives it as broad or narrow; regarding the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the nose element, one conceives it as powerful or powerless; regarding the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, one likewise conceives them as powerful or powerless.

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the tongue-element large or small; it also makes the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact—as well as all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition—large or small;
it causes the tongue-element to gather or disperse, and likewise causes the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition to gather or disperse."
One regards the tongue element as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as finite or infinite.
One regards the tongue element as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as broad or narrow.
One regards the tongue element as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the body-element large or small; it also makes the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—large or small;
it makes the body-element accumulate or disperse, and it also makes the contact-element, up to and including all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, accumulate or disperse."
One regards the body element as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the contact element, and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition, as finite or infinite.
One regards the body element as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the contact element, and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition, as broad or narrow.
One regards the body element as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the contact element, and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition, as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the mind-element great or small; it also makes the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, and the feeling produced with mind-contact as its condition great or small;
it collects or disperses the mind-element, and likewise collects or disperses everything from the dharma-element up to the feeling produced with mind-contact as its condition."

Regarding the mind-element (*manodhātu*), one conceives it as finite or infinite; regarding the phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*) and even the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, one likewise conceives them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the mind-element, one conceives it as vast or narrow; regarding the phenomena-element and even the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, one likewise conceives them as vast or narrow.

Regarding the mind-element, one conceives it as powerful or powerless; regarding the phenomena-element and even the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, one likewise conceives them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the earth element large or small; it likewise makes the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements large or small;
it gathers the earth element together or disperses it, and likewise gathers the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements together or disperses them."
Regarding the earth element, they conceive it as finite and infinite; regarding the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, they likewise conceive them as finite and infinite.
Regarding the earth element, they conceive it as broad and narrow; regarding the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, they likewise conceive them as broad and narrow.
Regarding the earth element, they conceive it as powerful and powerless; regarding the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, they likewise conceive them as powerful and powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes ignorance great or small; it likewise makes formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair great or small;
it collects ignorance or disperses it, and likewise collects or disperses formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."
One regards ignorance as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the formative forces up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as finite or infinite.
One regards ignorance as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the formative forces up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as broad or narrow.
One regards ignorance as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the formative forces up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), diligence (*vīrya*), patience (*kṣānti*), ethical discipline (*śīla*), and generosity (*dāna*), gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the perfection of generosity great or small; it also makes the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom great or small;
it gathers together the perfection of generosity or disperses it, and likewise gathers together or disperses the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom."
One conceives of the perfection of generosity as being limited or unlimited; one likewise conceives of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom as being limited or unlimited.
One conceives of the perfection of generosity as being vast or narrow; one likewise conceives of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom as being vast or narrow.
One conceives of the perfection of generosity as being powerful or powerless; one likewise conceives of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom as being powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, should give rise to such a thought:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the internal emptiness great or small; it likewise makes the external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharmas emptiness, unobtainable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, and non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness great or small."
One performs the gathering and dispersing of internal emptiness, and likewise performs the gathering and dispersing of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
one performs the finite and the infinite of internal emptiness, and likewise performs the finite and the infinite of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;
one performs the broad and the narrow of internal emptiness, and likewise performs the broad and the narrow of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

"One might regard inner emptiness as having power or lacking power, and likewise regard outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, as having power or lacking power.
"World-Honored One! [the interlocutor said.]
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom. "Furthermore, Blessed One,

if a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva who has set out in the Great Vehicle does not rely upon the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, yet gives rise to such a notion as this:"

"In this way, this *prajñāpāramitā* makes the *tathatā* (suchness) large or small; it likewise makes the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), *avitathatā* (non-falsity), *ananyathābhāvatā* (unchanging nature), *samatā* (equality), *anirodhatā* (nature free from arising), *dharmasthititā* (stability of phenomena), *dharmadhātusthititā* (stability of the dharma-realm), *bhūtakoṭi* (the limit of reality), *ākāśadhātu* (space-element), and *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm) large or small;
it makes the *tathatā* gathered or dispersed, and likewise makes the *dharmadhātu* up to the *acintyadhātu* gathered or dispersed;
it makes the *tathatā* finite or infinite, and likewise makes the *dharmadhātu* up to the *acintyadhātu* finite or infinite."

Regarding *tathatā*, they conceive of it as expansive or restricted; regarding the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), they likewise conceive of them as expansive or restricted.
Regarding *tathatā*, they conceive of it as having power or lacking power; regarding the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm, they likewise conceive of them as having power or lacking power.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the noble truth of suffering great or small; it likewise makes the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path great or small;
it gathers together or disperses the noble truth of suffering; it likewise gathers together or disperses the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."
Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one conceives of it as finite or infinite; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise conceives of them as finite or infinite.
Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one conceives of it as broad or narrow; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise conceives of them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the noble truth of suffering, one conceives of it as powerful or powerless; regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one likewise conceives of them as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the four meditative concentrations great or small; it also makes the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions great or small;
it makes the four meditative concentrations gathered or dispersed; it also makes the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions gathered or dispersed."

Regarding the four dhyānas, they practice them as limited and as limitless; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise practice them as limited and as limitless.
Regarding the four dhyānas, they practice them as expansive and as narrow; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise practice them as expansive and as narrow.

Regarding the four dhyānas, they practice them as powerful and as powerless; regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they likewise practice them as powerful and as powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the eight liberations great or small; it likewise makes the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities great or small;
it collects the eight liberations or disperses them, and likewise collects or disperses the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."

Regarding the eight liberations, they conceive of them as finite or infinite; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they likewise conceive of them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the eight liberations, they conceive of them as broad or narrow; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they likewise conceive of them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the eight liberations, they conceive of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the four applications of mindfulness great or small; it likewise makes the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path great or small;
it gathers together or disperses the four applications of mindfulness, and likewise gathers together or disperses the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path."

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, he regards them as limited or limitless; regarding the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, he likewise regards them as limited or limitless.
Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, he regards them as broad or narrow; regarding the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, he likewise regards them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, he regards them as powerful or powerless; regarding the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, he likewise regards them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the gate of liberation of emptiness large or small; it likewise makes the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness large or small;
it makes the gate of liberation of emptiness accumulate or disperse; it likewise makes the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the liberation door of emptiness, they conceive of it as finite or infinite; regarding the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise conceive of them as finite or infinite.
Regarding the liberation door of emptiness, they conceive of it as vast or narrow; regarding the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise conceive of them as vast or narrow.

Regarding the liberation door of emptiness, they conceive of it as powerful or powerless; regarding the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the five eyes great or small, and likewise makes the six supernormal powers great or small;
it gathers the five eyes together or disperses them, and likewise gathers the six supernormal powers together or disperses them."
Regarding the five eyes, they conceive of them as finite or infinite; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise conceive of them as finite or infinite.
Regarding the five eyes, they conceive of them as broad or narrow; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise conceive of them as broad or narrow.
Regarding the five eyes, they conceive of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise conceive of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the ten powers of a Buddha great or small; it also makes the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha great or small;
it makes the ten powers of a Buddha gathered or dispersed, and it also makes [everything] from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha gathered or dispersed."

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they treat them as finite and infinite; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise treat them as finite and infinite.

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they treat them as broad and narrow; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise treat them as broad and narrow.

Regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they treat them as powerful and powerless; regarding the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise treat them as powerful and powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"
If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the state of non-forgetfulness great or small; it also makes the state of constant equanimity great or small;
it collects the state of non-forgetfulness or disperses it; it also collects the state of constant equanimity or disperses it."
Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, they conceive of it as finite or infinite; regarding the state of constant equanimity, they likewise conceive of it as finite or infinite.
Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, they conceive of it as broad or narrow; regarding the state of constant equanimity, they likewise conceive of it as broad or narrow.
Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, they conceive of it as powerful or powerless; regarding the state of constant equanimity, they likewise conceive of it as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom performs great and small deeds regarding all-knowledge; it likewise performs great and small deeds regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
it performs gathering and dispersing regarding all-knowledge; it likewise performs gathering and dispersing regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects."
They conceive of all-knowledge as finite or infinite; they likewise conceive of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects as finite or infinite.
They conceive of all-knowledge as broad or narrow; they likewise conceive of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects as broad or narrow.
They conceive of all-knowledge as powerful or powerless; they likewise conceive of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes all dhāraṇī-doors great or small; it also makes all samādhi-doors great or small;
it gathers together all dhāraṇī-doors and disperses them; it also gathers together all samādhi-doors and disperses them."
Regarding all dharanī-doors, they make them finite and they make them infinite; regarding all samādhi-doors, they likewise make them finite and they make them infinite.
Regarding all dharanī-doors, they make them broad and they make them narrow; regarding all samādhi-doors, they likewise make them broad and they make them narrow.
Regarding all dharanī-doors, they make them powerful and they make them powerless; regarding all samādhi-doors, they likewise make them powerful and they make them powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the stream-enterer great or small; it also makes the once-returner, non-returner, and arhat great or small;
it gathers the stream-enterer or disperses them, and it likewise gathers or disperses the once-returner, non-returner, and arhat."
One regards the stream-enterer as finite or infinite; one likewise regards the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat as finite or infinite.
One regards the stream-enterer as broad or narrow; one likewise regards the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat as broad or narrow.
One regards the stream-enterer as powerful or powerless; one likewise regards the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat as powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a perception, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, should give rise to such a thought as this:

"This perfection of wisdom makes the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry great or small; it likewise makes the stage of entering once-returning and its fruit, the stage of entering non-returning and its fruit, and the stage of entering arhatship and its fruit great or small;
it makes the stage of entering the stream and its fruit accumulate or disperse, and it likewise makes the stages from entering once-returning up to arhatship accumulate or disperse."

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, he conceives of them as finite or infinite; regarding the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship, he likewise conceives of them as finite or infinite.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, he conceives of them as broad or narrow; regarding the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship, he likewise conceives of them as broad or narrow.

Regarding the stage of entering the stream and the fruit of stream-entry, he conceives of them as powerful or powerless; regarding the stage of entering the once-returner up to the fruit of arhatship, he likewise conceives of them as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the solitary realizer great or small; it also makes the awakening of a solitary realizer great or small;
it makes the solitary realizer gather or disperse; it also makes the awakening of a solitary realizer gather or disperse."
One conceives of the pratyekabuddha as finite or infinite, and likewise conceives of the pratyekabuddha’s enlightenment as finite or infinite;
one conceives of the pratyekabuddha as vast or narrow, and likewise conceives of the pratyekabuddha’s enlightenment as vast or narrow;
one conceives of the pratyekabuddha as powerful or powerless, and likewise conceives of the pratyekabuddha’s enlightenment as powerful or powerless.
"World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a notion, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!"

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, gives rise to such a thought as this:
"This perfection of wisdom makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva great or small; it also makes the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva great or small;
it makes the bodhisattva mahāsattva gather or disperse; it also makes the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva gather or disperse."
They conceive of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as having measure or being immeasurable; they likewise conceive of the practice of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as having measure or being immeasurable.
They conceive of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as being broad or narrow; they likewise conceive of the practice of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as being broad or narrow.
They conceive of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as being powerful or powerless; they likewise conceive of the practice of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as being powerful or powerless.
“World-Honored One!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”

If a newly trained bodhisattva mahāsattva, not relying on the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, should give rise to such a thought as this:
