Why? Because the prior limit of the eight liberations has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of the eight liberations."

The eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are neither bound nor liberated at their prior limit. Why is this?

Because the prior limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the state of non-existence; it is because the prior limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is their very intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*).
“The prior limit of the four foundations of mindfulness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the prior limit of the four foundations of mindfulness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the prior limit of the four foundations of mindfulness.”

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are neither bound nor liberated at the prior limit.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of the prior limit of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path constitutes the intrinsic nature of the prior limit of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.
"The prior limit of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the prior limit of the gate of liberation that is emptiness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the prior limit of the gate of liberation that is emptiness."
The prior limit of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is neither bound nor liberated.

Why? Because the prior limit of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the prior limit of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“The prior limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the prior limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva.”
"The prior limit of the five eyes is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the prior limit of the five eyes has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of the five eyes."
The prior limit of the six supernormal powers is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the prior limit of the six supernormal powers has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of the six supernormal powers.
“The ten powers of a Buddha are neither bound nor liberated in the past.
Why? Because the past of the ten powers of a Buddha has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the past of the ten powers of a Buddha.”

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are, from the perspective of the prior limit, neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of a prior limit for the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha constitutes the very nature of the prior limit of those four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“The dharma of non-forgetfulness is neither bound nor liberated at its prior limit.
Why? Because the dharma of non-forgetfulness has the nature of non-existence at its prior limit, which constitutes the intrinsic nature of the dharma of non-forgetfulness at its prior limit.”
The nature of equanimity abiding constantly is neither bound nor liberated in the past. Why is this?
Because the nature of equanimity abiding constantly has no existence in the past, as this is the very intrinsic nature of the past of the nature of equanimity abiding constantly.
“The prior limit of omniscience is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the prior limit of omniscience has the nature of non-existence, as it is the very self-nature of the prior limit of omniscience.”
The knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are neither bound nor liberated at the prior limit. Why is this?

Because the prior limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
“The prior limit of all dhāraṇī-gates is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the prior limit of all dhāraṇī-gates has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of all dhāraṇī-gates.”
The prior limit of all samādhi-gates is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the prior limit of all samādhi-gates has the nature of non-existence, as it is the intrinsic nature of the prior limit of all samādhi-gates.
“The prior limit of the fruit of stream-entry is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the prior limit of the fruit of stream-entry has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the prior limit of the fruit of stream-entry.”
The prior limit of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the prior limit of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship has the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the very self-nature of the prior limit of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.
"The prior limit of pratyekabuddha-bodhi is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the prior limit of pratyekabuddha-bodhi has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the prior limit of pratyekabuddha-bodhi."
“The prior limit of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the prior limit of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices has the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the very self-nature of the prior limit of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices.”
“The prior limit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the prior limit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the prior limit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The future limit of form is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
The non-existence of the future limit of form is because the future limit of form is its own intrinsic nature.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated at their future limit.

Why is this? Because the posterior limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
“The future limit of the eye-base is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the eye-base has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the eye-base.”
The future limit of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the future limit of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
"The future limit of the sphere of form is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the sphere of form has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the sphere of form."
The posterior limit of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the posterior limit of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of those spheres.
"The future limit of the eye-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the eye-element has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the future limit of the eye-element."

The future limit of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

Because the future limit of the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the future limit of the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
"The future limit of the ear-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the ear-element has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the future limit of the ear-element."
The future limit of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and auditory contact, as well as all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition, is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the future limit of the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition, has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition.
“The future limit of the nose-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the nose-element has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the future limit of the nose-element.”
The future limit of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the future limit of the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.
"The ultimate limit of the tongue-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the ultimate limit of the tongue-element has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the ultimate limit of the tongue-element."
The future limit of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the future limit of the taste element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the taste element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.
“The future limit of the body-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the body-element has the nature of non-existence, for that is the intrinsic nature of the future limit of the body-element.”

The sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are neither bound nor liberated at their posterior limit. Why is this?

Because the non-existence of the sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition constitutes the very nature of the posterior limit of the sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“The future limit of the mind-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the mind-element has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the mind-element.”
The ultimate limit of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the ultimate limit of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the ultimate limit of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition.
"The future limit of the earth element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the earth element has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the future limit of the earth element."
The future limit of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the future limit of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of those elements.
"The future limit of ignorance is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of ignorance has the nature of non-existence, for that is the very self-nature of the future limit of ignorance."

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are neither bound nor liberated at their posterior limit.

Why is this? Because the nature of the non-existence of the posterior limit of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is the very self-nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
“The posterior limit of the perfection of generosity is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the posterior limit of the perfection of generosity has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of the perfection of generosity.”
The ultimate limit of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the ultimate limit of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the non-existence of intrinsic nature; it is the very intrinsic nature of the ultimate limit of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom.
“The posterior limit of internal emptiness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the posterior limit of internal emptiness has the nature of non-existence, for that is the intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of internal emptiness.”

The emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—these do not bind nor liberate at the posterior limit.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of the posterior limit of the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, constitutes the intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature.
"The ultimate limit of suchness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the ultimate limit of suchness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the ultimate limit of suchness."

The realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-illusory nature, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm—these are neither bound nor liberated at their posterior limit.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of the posterior limit of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, constitutes the intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
“The future limit of the noble truth of suffering is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the future limit of the noble truth of suffering has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the future limit of the noble truth of suffering.”
The future limit of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is neither bound nor liberated. Why?

Because the future limit of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
“The posterior limit of the four dhyānas is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the posterior limit of the four dhyānas has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the posterior limit of the four dhyānas.”
The future limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is neither bound nor liberated.

Why? Because the future limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
“The posterior limit of the eight liberations is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the posterior limit of the eight liberations has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the posterior limit of the eight liberations.”
The posterior limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the posterior limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases.
“The posterior limit of the four foundations of mindfulness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the posterior limit of the four foundations of mindfulness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the posterior limit of the four foundations of mindfulness.”

The four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are neither bound nor liberated at their posterior limit.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of a posterior limit for the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path constitutes the intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
"The future limit of the liberation door of emptiness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the future limit of the liberation door of emptiness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the liberation door of emptiness."
The future limit of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the future limit of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness.
“The ultimate limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the ultimate limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the ultimate limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva.”
“The ultimate limit of the five eyes is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the ultimate limit of the five eyes has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the ultimate limit of the five eyes.”
The future limit of the six supernormal powers is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the future limit of the six supernormal powers has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the future limit of the six supernormal powers.
“The future limit of the ten powers of a Buddha is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the future limit of the ten powers of a Buddha has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the ten powers of a Buddha.”

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are, at their ultimate limit, neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of a posterior limit in the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, constitutes the intrinsic nature of the posterior limit of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
"The state of non-forgetfulness is neither bound nor liberated at its posterior limit.
Why? Because the state of non-forgetfulness has no existence at its posterior limit, as this is the very nature of the state of non-forgetfulness at its posterior limit."
The future limit of the state of constant equanimity is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the future limit of the state of constant equanimity has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the state of constant equanimity.
“The posterior limit of all-knowledge is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the posterior limit of all-knowledge has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the posterior limit of all-knowledge.”
The ultimate limit (*paścimakoṭi*) of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is neither bound nor liberated. Why?

Because the ultimate limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects has the nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāvatā*), which constitutes the very intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the ultimate limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
"The ultimate limit of all dharani-gates is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the ultimate limit of all dharani-gates has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the ultimate limit of all dharani-gates."
The posterior limit of all samādhi-gates is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the posterior limit of all samādhi-gates has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the posterior limit of all samādhi-gates.
"The future limit of the fruit of stream-entry is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the future limit of the fruit of stream-entry has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the future limit of the fruit of stream-entry."
The future limit of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

Because the future limit of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship has the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the intrinsic nature of the future limit of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.
“The limit of the future of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the limit of the future of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the limit of the future of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.”
“The final limit of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the final limit of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the final limit of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
“The ultimate limit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the ultimate limit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas has the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the very self-nature of that ultimate limit.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The middle limit of form is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
The nature of the absence of anything whatsoever in the middle limit of form is because that is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of form.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated in their middle limits.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
“The intermediate limit of the eye-base is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the intermediate limit of the eye-base has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the intermediate limit of the eye-base.”
The middle limit of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
"The middle limit of the sense-base of form is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the sense-base of form has the nature of non-existence, which is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the sense-base of form."
The middle limit of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

Because the middle limit of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of those spheres.
“The middle limit of the eye-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the eye-element has the nature of non-existence, for that is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the eye-element.”

Within the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period. Why is this?

Because the form realm, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, have no existence in their middle period; for this absence of existence is the very intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the form realm, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.
“The middle limit of the ear-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the middle limit of the ear-element has the nature of non-existence, as this is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the ear-element.”

Within the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period.

Why is this? Because the middle period of the sphere of sound up to the feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle period of the sphere of sound up to the feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition.
“The middle limit of the nose-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the middle limit of the nose-element has the nature of non-existence, as it is the very self-nature of the middle limit of the nose-element.”

Within the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period.

Why is this? Because the middle period of the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle period of the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.
“The middle limit of the tongue-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the middle limit of the tongue-element has the nature of non-existence, for it is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the tongue-element.”
Within the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle.

Why is this? Because the taste element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, have no existence in their middle state; this is because the very nature of the taste element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is that very absence of existence.
“The middle limit of the body-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the middle limit of the body-element has the nature of non-existence, as this is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the body-element.”

Within the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period. Why is this?

Because the middle period of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle period of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.
“The middle limit of the mind-element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the mind-element has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the mind-element.”

Within the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period. Why is this?

Because the non-existence of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition constitutes the intrinsic nature of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition in the middle period.
“The middle limit of the earth element is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the earth element has the nature of non-existence, as that is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the earth element.”
Within the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness.
“Ignorance in the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because ignorance in the middle limit has the nature of non-existence, as this is the intrinsic nature of ignorance in the middle limit.”

In volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the factors from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is the nature of non-existence, as it is the intrinsic nature of the factors from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 182. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Two: "Within the perfection of giving, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated."
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the perfection of generosity has the nature of non-existence, as that is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the perfection of generosity.
Within the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom is the non-existence of anything [intrinsic], which constitutes the very nature of the middle limit of the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom.
"In the emptiness of the internal, the limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the limit of the emptiness of the internal has the nature of non-existence, for that is the intrinsic nature of the limit of the emptiness of the internal."

In the emptiness of the external, the internal-external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is neither bondage nor liberation at their limits.

Why is this? Because within the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, there is no such thing as a limit; for the limit of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the intrinsic nature of that limit.
"In the middle limit of suchness, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of suchness has the nature of non-existence, as it is the very self-nature of the middle limit of suchness."

Within the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of the middle limit within the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, constitutes the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
“Regarding the noble truth of suffering, its middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the middle limit of the noble truth of suffering has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the noble truth of suffering.”
The middle limit of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?

Because the middle limit of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
"In the four dhyānas, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the four dhyānas has the nature of non-existence, which is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the four dhyānas."
Within the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
"In the middle limit of the eight liberations, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the eight liberations has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the middle limit of the eight liberations."
Within the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
“Within the four foundations of mindfulness, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the four foundations of mindfulness has the nature of non-existence, which is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the four foundations of mindfulness.”

Among the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, there is neither bondage nor liberation in the middle period.

Why is this? Because the non-existence of a middle limit within the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path constitutes the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.
"In the emptiness gate of liberation, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
Because the emptiness gate of liberation has the nature of non-existence as its own-nature at the middle limit."
Within the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because within the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, the middle limit has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
"In the middle limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva has the nature of non-existence, as it is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the ten stages of a bodhisattva."
“The middle limit of the five eyes is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the five eyes has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the middle limit of the five eyes.”
Within the six supernormal powers, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because within the six supernormal powers, the middle limit has the nature of non-existence, being the very self-nature of the middle limit of the six supernormal powers.
“Among the ten powers of a Buddha, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the middle limit of the ten powers of a Buddha has the nature of non-existence, for it is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the ten powers of a Buddha.”

Within the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because within the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the nature of the absence of a middle limit is the very self-nature of those four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
"In the state of non-forgetfulness, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why? Because the state of non-forgetfulness has no intrinsic nature in its middle limit; such is the very self-nature of the state of non-forgetfulness."
The middle limit within the state of constant abiding in equanimity is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit within the state of constant abiding in equanimity is the nature of non-existence, which constitutes the intrinsic nature of the middle limit within the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
"In omniscience, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of omniscience has the nature of non-existence, as it is the very self-nature of the middle limit of omniscience."
The middle limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
"In all dharani-doors, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of all dharani-doors has the nature of non-existence, for it is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of all dharani-doors."
Within all gateways of samādhi, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of all gateways of samādhi has the nature of non-existence, which is the very intrinsic nature of the middle limit of all gateways of samādhi.
"In the fruit of stream-entry, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the fruit of stream-entry has the nature of non-existence as its own-being (svabhāva) at the middle limit."
The intermediate limit of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is neither bound nor liberated.

Why? Because the intermediate limit of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the intermediate limit of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.
“In the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha has the nature of non-existence, which is the very self-nature of the middle limit of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha.”
“In all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated.

Why is this? Because the middle limit of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has the nature of non-existence, as it is the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
"In the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, the middle limit is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
Because the nature of non-existence constitutes the intrinsic nature of the middle limit of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Those individuals who do not exert diligence, have not planted roots of goodness, possess unwholesome roots, are influenced by evil friends, follow the course of Māra’s power, are dominated by indolence, have feeble vigor, and are characterized by loss of mindfulness and faulty wisdom—it is truly difficult for them to believe in and understand this Prajñāpāramitā.”
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, Subhūti! It is so!"
It is so! It is as you have said.

For those individuals who do not exert diligent effort, who have not planted roots of virtue, who possess unwholesome roots, who are influenced by evil friends, who follow the course of Māra’s power, for whom indolence predominates, whose diligence is feeble, and who are characterized by loss of mindfulness and faulty wisdom, it is truly difficult to have faith and understanding in this *prajñāpāramitā*.
Why is that? "Subhūti!
The purity of form is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of form."
Why is this? Because this purity of form and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because this purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of the sense base of the eye is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the sense base of the eye. Why is this?
The purity of the eye-base and the purity of the fruit are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
The purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is itself the purity of the fruit, and the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

Why is this? Because the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not two, there is no division, no distinction, and no separation.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the sphere of form. Why is this?
The purity of the sphere of form and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the eye-element is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the eye-element. Why is this?
The purity of the eye-element and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the form-element up to all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of these forms, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ear-element is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the ear-element. Why is this?
The purity of the ear-element and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the sound-element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nose element is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the nose element. Why is this?
The purity of this nose-element and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the odor-element up to and including all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the realm of fragrance, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the tongue-element is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the tongue-element. Why is this?
The purity of this tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the body element is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the body element. Why is this?
This purity of the body element and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the tangible-object element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of tangibles, up to the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as a condition, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the mind-element is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the mind-element. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-element and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because this purity of the dharma-realm, up to the purity of the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the earth element is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the earth element. Why is this?
The purity of the earth element and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of non-arising is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of non-arising. Why is this?
This purity of the clear and luminous is the purity of the fruit; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Because the purity of these factors—from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair—is non-dual with the purity of the fruit; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of the perfection of giving is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the perfection of giving."
Why is this? Because this purity of the perfection of giving and the purity of its fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom.

Why is this? Because this purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of internal emptiness is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of internal emptiness. Why is this?
This purity of internal emptiness and purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the fruit; and the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Why is this? Because the purity of this emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of suchness is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of suchness. Why is this?
This purity of suchness is the purity of the fruit; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
Why is this? Because the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the noble truth of suffering is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the noble truth of suffering. Why is this?
The purity of the noble truth of suffering and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
Why is this? Because the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the fruit, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the four dhyānas is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the four dhyānas. Why is this?
This purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of their fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

Why is this? Because these four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, as well as their purity and the purity of their fruits, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the eight liberations is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the eight liberations. Why is this?
This purity of the eight liberations and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

Why is this? Because these eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities, as well as the purity of their fruits, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
The purity of these four foundations of mindfulness and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. Why is this?
The purity of the emptiness liberation door and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors.
Why is this? Because the purity of the signless and wishless doors of liberation and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Why is this?
This purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the five eyes is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the five eyes. Why is this?
Because the purity of the five eyes and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
The purity of the six superknowledges is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the six superknowledges. Why is this?
Because the purity of the six superknowledges and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha. Why is this?
The purity of the ten powers of a Buddha and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness. Why is this?
The purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the state of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the state of constant equanimity.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of all-knowledge is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of all-knowledge. Why is this?
This purity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual with the purity of the fruit; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of all dhāraṇī-gates is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of all dhāraṇī-gates.”
Why is this? Because the purity of all these dhāraṇī-gates and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of all gateways to samādhi is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of all gateways to samādhi. Why is this?
This purity of all gateways to samādhi and the purity of its fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the fruit of stream-entry is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the fruit of stream-entry. Why is this?
Because this purity of the fruit of stream-entry and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.

Why is this? Because the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is identical to the purity of the fruit itself; they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha. Why is this?
This purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices.
Why is this? Because this purity of the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the purity of its fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of these Buddhas and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of form is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of form."
Why is this? Because the purity of form and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because this purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sense base of the eye is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the sense base of the eye.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this sphere of the eye and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is itself the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

Why is this? Because the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the sphere of form.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of form and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

Why is this? Because the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the eye-element is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the eye-element.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the eye-element and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the form realm, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the form realm, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ear-element is itself the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is itself the purity of the ear-element.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this ear-element and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nose element is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the nose element.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this nose-element and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the odor element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the olfactory realm up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from nothing, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the tongue element is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the tongue element.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this tongue-element and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the body element is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the body element.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this body-element and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition, is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of tangibles, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of the mind-element is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the mind-element."
Why is this? Because this purity of the mental faculty and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as condition, is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the dharma-element up to and including all feelings produced with mental contact as condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of this dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, they are not separate, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the earth element is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the earth element.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the earth element and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of non-arising is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of non-arising.”
Why is this? Because this purity of non-arising and the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā* are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purification of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purification of the perfection of wisdom; the purification of the perfection of wisdom is the purification of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Because the purity of these factors, from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the perfection of generosity.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of giving and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.

The purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to meditative concentration.

Why is this? Because the purity of these perfections, from the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of meditative concentration, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of internal emptiness.”
Why is this? Because this purity of internal emptiness and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*; the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā* is the purity of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of suchness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of suchness."
Why is this? Because the purity of suchness and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

Why is this? Because the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the noble truth of suffering.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this noble truth of suffering and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
