Why is this? Because the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the four dhyānas.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these four dhyānas and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four immeasurables and the four formless attainments and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the eight liberations.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these eight liberations and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

Why is this? Because the purity of these eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is non-dual with the purity of the perfection of wisdom; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these four foundations of mindfulness and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct from one another, and there is no separation between them.

“Subhūti! The purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this gate of liberation of emptiness and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Why is this? Because the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! The purification of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purification of the perfection of wisdom; the purification of the perfection of wisdom is the purification of the ten stages of a bodhisattva.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the ten stages of this bodhisattva and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 183. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Part Three. "Subhūti!
The purity of the five eyes is the purity of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the five eyes. Why is this?
This purity of the five eyes and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the six superknowledges is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the six superknowledges.
Why is this? Because the purity of these six supernormal powers and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this quality of non-forgetfulness and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Why is this? Because the purity of this ever-abiding equanimity and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of all-knowledge.”
Why is this? Because the purity of omniscience and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual with the purity of the perfection of wisdom; it is not divided into two, is not distinct, and is not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors.”
Why is this? Because the purity of all these dhāraṇī-doors and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of all samādhi-gates is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of all samādhi-gates.
Why is this? Because the purity of all these gateways of samādhi and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the fruit of stream-entry and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat.

Why is this? Because the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is non-dual with the purity of the perfection of wisdom; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and it is not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! The purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is itself the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is itself the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the practice of all these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the purity of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! The purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the perfection of wisdom; the purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of these Buddhas and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct neither in nature nor in substance.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of form is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of form. Why is this?
This purity of form and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because this purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sense base of the eye is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense base of the eye. Why is this?
The purity of this eye-base and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

Why is this? Because the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sense-sphere of form is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-sphere of form. Why is this?
The purity of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*) is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.

Why is this? Because the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena is non-dual with the purity of the knowledge of all modes; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the eye-element is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eye-element. Why is this?
The purity of the eye-element and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of these forms, up to and including the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ear-element is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the ear-element. Why is this?
This purity of the ear-element and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nose-element is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nose-element. Why is this?
The purity of this nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the odor-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of fragrance, up to and including the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the tongue-element. Why is this?
The purity of this tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the taste-element up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of the body element is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the body element. Why is this?
The purity of this body-element (*kāyadhātu*) and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing; the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing is itself the purity of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of these feelings—arising with the sense-field of touch as a condition, up to those arising with body-touch as a condition—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the mind-element. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.

Why is this? Because the purity of this dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual; they are not two distinct things, they are without differentiation, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the earth element is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the earth element. Why is this?
The purity of the earth element and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

Why is this? Because the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of non-arising is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of non-arising. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance is the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna); they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Because the purity of these factors—from formative volitions up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair—is non-dual with the purity of the knowledge of all modes; they are not two, cannot be divided into two, are not distinct, and are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the perfection of giving is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the perfection of giving.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of giving and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom.

Why is this? Because the purity of these [perfections] from pure ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of internal emptiness. Why is this?
This purity of internal emptiness and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Why is this? Because the purity of this emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of suchness is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of suchness. Why is this?
The purity of suchness is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; they are non-dual, not divided, distinct, nor discontinuous.

The purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

Why is this? Because the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the noble truth of suffering.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this noble truth of suffering and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

Why is this? Because the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the four dhyānas is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the four dhyānas.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these four dhyānas and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these eight liberations and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

Why is this? Because the purity of these eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases is non-dual with the purity of the knowledge of all modes; they are not two, cannot be divided into two, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous.

“Subhūti! The purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness.”

Why is this? Because the purity of these four foundations of mindfulness and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! The purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this gate of liberation of emptiness and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

Why is this? Because the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the ten stages of this bodhisattva and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the five eyes is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the five eyes. Why is this?
This purity of the five eyes and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the six supernormal powers.
Why is this? Because the purity of these six supernormal powers and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! The purification of the ten powers of a Buddha is itself the purification of the knowledge of all modes; the purification of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purification of the ten powers of a Buddha.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because the purity of these four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Why is this? Because the purity of this quality of non-forgetfulness and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
This purity of the nature of constant equanimity and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge; the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge is the purity of all-knowledge. Why is this?
The purity of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is non-dual with the purity of the knowledge of all-knowing; they are not two, cannot be divided into two, are not distinct, and are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors.”
Why is this? Because the purity of all these doors of dhāraṇī and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge; the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is the purity of all gateways to samādhi.

Why is this? Because the purity of all these gates of samādhi and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the fruit of stream-entry is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of the fruit of stream-entry.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the fruit of stream-entry and the purity of omniscient wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.

Why is this? Because the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is non-dual with the purity of all-knowledge; it is not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is itself the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is itself the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the practice of all these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! The purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of these Buddhas and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the realm of odors, the realm of nose-consciousness, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the realm of odors up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the various sensations produced with conditions ranging from the fragrance-element up to nose-contact are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the agent is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the agent is the purity of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the various sensations produced with the nose-constituent as a condition, up to those produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate."

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the various feelings produced with the nose-contact as condition—up to the realm of fragrance—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the knower is the purity of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*); the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”

The purity of the knower is the purity of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition; the purity of the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as condition is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all feelings produced with the nose-element as a condition, up to those produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"The purity of the seer is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of all feelings produced with the olfactory realm up to the contact of the nose as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are undivided, they are distinctless, and they are uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the self. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

My purity is the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is my purity.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the tongue element; the purity of the tongue element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the tongue element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element up to tongue-contact as conditions are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition; the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the various feelings produced with the tongue-contact as condition, up to the taste-element, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the being is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element, up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is the purity of the being.

Why is this? This purity of birth and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element as object, up to those produced with tongue-contact as condition, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.”

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nourisher is pure and the sensations produced with the taste-element as object, up to those produced with tongue-contact as condition, are pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the person is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the person is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*), and the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the person is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all feelings produced with the taste-element as object, up to those produced with tongue-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the youth is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the youth.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element and so forth, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the agent is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the agent is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the various feelings arising with the taste element as condition, up to those arising with tongue-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the knower is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the knower is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the seer is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.”

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition; the purity of the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer and the purity of the various feelings arising with the gustatory element as their object, up to those arising conditioned by tongue-contact, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not severed.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll One Hundred and Eighty-Five. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division: Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Five, "Difficult to Believe and Understand. Furthermore, Subhūti:
My purity is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is my purity. Why is this?
Because this purity of mine and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the self is the purity of the contact element, the body-consciousness element, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the contact element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the various feelings arising with the contact element as condition, up to those arising with body-contact as condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the various feelings arising with contact as a condition, up to those arising with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all feelings produced with contact as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the various feelings arising with contact as a condition—from the sphere of contact up to the body-contact—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the contact element, the body-consciousness element, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the contact element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nourisher is pure and the various feelings produced with the contact element as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the person is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the person is the purity of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of everything from the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the various feelings produced with contact as a condition—up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*); the purity of the body-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”

The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the sensations produced with contact as a condition—from the sphere of contact up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of the various feelings produced with the contact element as condition, up to those produced with body-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*); the purity of the body-element is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the youth is the purity of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact; and the purity of body-contact and all sensations produced with body-contact as condition is the purity of the youth. The purity of the element of tangibles up to all sensations produced with body-contact as condition is the purity of the youth.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of the various feelings produced with contact as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the agent is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the agent is the purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the various feelings arising with contact as a condition—from the sphere of touch up to the body—are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.
"The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the feeler and the purity of the various feelings arising with contact as a condition—up to those arising with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, undivided, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the knower is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the knower is the purity of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as condition; the purity of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as condition is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all feelings arising with contact as a condition—from the sphere of contact up to those arising with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the seer is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the seer is the purity of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer and the purity of the various feelings produced with the contact element—up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the mental faculty (manodhātu), and the purity of the mental faculty is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the self is the purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as their condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition is the purity of the self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—up to and including the dharma-realm—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*); the purity of the mind-element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the dharma-realm, the consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-realm up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the mental constituent (*manodhātu*); the purity of the mental constituent is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the mental constituent are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not two, indivisible, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable."

The purity of the living being is the purity of the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition is the purity of the living being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nourisher is pure and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“The purity of the person is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the person is the purity of the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—up to and including the dharma-realm—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*); the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”

The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the mental consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition; conversely, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition; the purity of the dharma-realm up to all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, not separate, and not discontinuous.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*); the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

“The purity of the agent is the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*); the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?

“The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is the purity of the mind-born.

“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is the purity of the agent.

The purity of the knower is the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is the purity of the knower.

The purity of the seer is the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness is the purity of the seer.

"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of non-self; the purity of non-self is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of self is the purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), clinging (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of nirvāṇa; the purity of nirvāṇa is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of nirvāṇa are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purification of sentient beings is the purification of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purification of volitional formations through to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purification of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of conditioned formations up to aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; the purity of volitional formations up to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because the purity of this life-principle and the purity of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

Because this purity of the nurturer and this purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“The purity of the person is the purity of space, and the purity of space is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of space are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of conditioned formations up to aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of non-arising (*anutpāda*); the purity of non-arising is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and this purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”

The purity of the person is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and this purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

“The purity of the agent is the purity of non-action; the purity of non-action is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and this purity of non-action are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the agent is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the self."
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of my self is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of my self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the pure precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is itself the purity of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

This purity of the one who is born is non-dual with the purity of the perfection of generosity; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and there is no separation between them.

“The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the perfection of generosity; it is not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*); the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline (śīla), patience (kṣānti), diligence (vīrya), meditative concentration (dhyāna), and wisdom (prajñā); the purity of these perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (Māṇavaka) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"The purity of the agent is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
