Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the pure precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the recipient is the purity of the perfection of giving; the purity of the perfection of giving is the purity of the recipient. Why is this?
The purity of the recipient and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the recipient is itself the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is itself the purity of the recipient.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll One Hundred and Eighty-Seven. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Seven. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The purity of the self is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because the purity of the self and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of my self is the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is the purity of my self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”

Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the knower is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“The purity of the seer is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the seer is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the self is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual;
they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because this purity of sentient beings and this purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.”
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate."

The purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) is the purity of the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate."
The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; these two are non-dual, not divided, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is the purity of the nurturer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the person is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”
The purity of the person is the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity; the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the person is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.
The purity of the person is itself the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the equanimity of constant abiding; the purity of the equanimity of constant abiding is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the equanimity of constant abiding are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”
The purity of Māṇavaka is the purity of the constant abiding in equanimity; the purity of the constant abiding in equanimity is the purity of Māṇavaka. Why is this?
Because this purity of Māṇavaka and the purity of the constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“The purity of the agent is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”
The purity of the agent is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“The purity of the knower is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and this purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
The purity of the knower is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"The purity of the seer is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable."
The purity of the seer is the purity of the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 188. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter on Difficult Faith and Understanding, Part 34-8. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
The purity of the self is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because the purity of the self and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the self is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of sentient beings is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous."

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the knowledge of paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the life-principle is the purity of omniscience, and the purity of omniscience is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and all-aspect omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the sentient being is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the nurturer is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nurturer and this purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nurturer’s purity and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“The purity of the person is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the person is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the person is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of the mind-born is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born [body] and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.”

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the agent is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted."

The purity of the agent is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the experiencer is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“The purity of the knower is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

The purity of the knower is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the seer is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the seer is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the self."
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
My purity is the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of all gateways to samādhi is my purity. Why is this?
This purity of mine and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of sentient beings."
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all gateways of samādhi; the purity of all gateways of samādhi is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the life-principle.
Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all gateways of samādhi; the purity of all gateways of samādhi is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the being is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the being.
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the sentient being is the purity of all gateways of samādhi; the purity of all gateways of samādhi is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
This purity of the one who gives birth is non-dual with, indivisible from, undifferentiated from, and inseparable from the purity of all doors of samādhi.
This purity of the nurturer is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the nurturer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the nurturer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of all gates of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of the person is the purity of all dharani-doors; the purity of all dharani-doors is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the person is itself the purity of all samadhi-doors; the purity of all samadhi-doors is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the person is the purity of all dharani-doors; the purity of all dharani-doors is the purity of the person."
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
The purity of the person is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this *pudgala* and the purity of all gateways to *samādhi* are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"The purity of the mind-born is the purity of all dharani-doors; the purity of all dharani-doors is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of all dharani-doors; it is not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of all samadhi-doors, and the purity of all samadhi-doors is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of all dharanī-doors; the purity of all dharanī-doors is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of all samādhi-doors, and the purity of all samādhi-doors is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the agent is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors;
the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the agent is itself the purity of all samādhi-doors; the purity of all samādhi-doors is itself the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the recipient is the purity of all dharani-doors; the purity of all dharani-doors is the purity of the recipient. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of all samādhi-doors; the purity of all samādhi-doors is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the knower is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the knower is itself the purity of all samadhi-doors, and the purity of all samadhi-doors is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the seer is the purity of all dharani-doors; the purity of all dharani-doors is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
The purity of the seer is itself the purity of all samadhi-doors; the purity of all samadhi-doors is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the self. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
My purity is itself the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is itself my purity.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because this purity of sentient beings and this purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable."

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because the purity of this life-principle and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the being is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the being and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”

The purity of the one being born is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the one being born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not severed.”

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the person is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the person is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the person is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the agent is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and this purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”

The purity of the agent is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the recipient is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the recipient. Why is this?
Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous."

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this recipient and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the knower is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption."

The purity of the knower is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the seer is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.”

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of mine and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of sentient beings."
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”
“The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”
"The purity of the nurturer is the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of this nurturer and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"The purity of the person is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the person."
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the person is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”
“The purity of the agent is the purity of pratyekabuddha-awakening; the purity of pratyekabuddha-awakening is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of pratyekabuddha-awakening are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”
“The purity of the experiencer is the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”
"The purity of the knower is the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable."
“The purity of the seer is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the self."
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of sentient beings."

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the life-principle."

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of birth is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of birth."
Why is this? This purity of birth and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the nurturer is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the nurturer."
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the person is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because this person’s purity and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the person (pudgala) is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this *pudgala* and the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“The purity of the mind-born is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the mind-born.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the agent is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the agent."
Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the recipient is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the recipient."
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the knower is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the knower."
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"The purity of the seer is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the seer."
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The purity of the self is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the self."
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

"The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is the purity of sentient beings."

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the sentient being."
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

"The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the nurturer."

Why is this? Because the purity of this nurturer and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

“The purity of the person is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

"The purity of the person is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is the purity of the person."

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the mind-born."

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī."

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"The purity of the agent is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the agent."

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

"The purity of the recipient is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the recipient."

Why is this? Because the purity of this recipient and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“The purity of the knower is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the knower.”

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

"The purity of the seer is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the seer."

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 189. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Nine. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
The purity of the self is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because the purity of the self and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the self is the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the purity of the self. Why is this so?
This purity of mine and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because this purity of the self and the purity of the eye-base are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
The purity of the self is the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! My purity is the purity of the sense-sphere of form; the purity of the sense-sphere of form is my purity. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of the sphere of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of self is the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the purity of self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from nothing, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the self. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

My purity is the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is my purity.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the self. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

My purity is the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is my purity.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sphere of sound up to ear-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

This purity of the self is the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as their condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as their condition is the purity of the self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the various feelings produced with the olfactory realm up to the contact of the nose as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the self. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

My purity is the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is my purity.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the various feelings produced with the gustatory element up to tongue-contact as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of the body element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of self is the purity of the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch element up to all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the various feelings produced with the touch-element and so forth, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the mental faculty (manodhātu), and the purity of the mental faculty is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the self is the purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as their condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition is the purity of the self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! My purity is the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the earth element is my purity. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
My purity is the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is my purity.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the markless; the purity of the markless is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of self is the purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), clinging (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; the purity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of [the factors] from formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! My purity is the purity of the perfection of giving; the purity of the perfection of giving is my purity.”
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of my self is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of my self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the pure precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the self is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, limitless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of own-marks, emptiness of common marks, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of own-nature, and the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence. The purity of external emptiness, up to the purity of the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence, is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the self is the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. The purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
This purity of self is the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is this purity of self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! My purity is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the four dhyānas is my purity. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
This purity of self is the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is this purity of self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of self and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of self is the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is the purity of self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the four applications of mindfulness; the purity of the four applications of mindfulness is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the self is the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! My purity is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is my purity. Why is this?
My purity and the purity of the emptiness liberation door are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
My purity is the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors; the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is my purity.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! My purity is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is my purity. Why is this?
This purity of mine and the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because the purity of the self and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the self is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because the purity of the self and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.

This purity of the self is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the self.

Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The purity of the self is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of the self and the purity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the self is the purity of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the self.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! My purity is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is my purity.”
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
My purity is the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of all gateways to samādhi is my purity. Why is this?
This purity of mine and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable. "Subhūti!
The purity of the self is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the self. Why is this?
Because the purity of the self and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
My purity is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is my purity.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the purity of the self. Why is this?
This purity of mine and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
My own purity is the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is my own purity.
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of the self is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the self.”
Why is this? Because my purity and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the sense base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct from nothing, and there is no discontinuity between them.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element through to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the forms of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the nose element; the purity of the nose element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the nose element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the various feelings produced with the nose-object as condition, up to the nose-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the tongue element; the purity of the tongue element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element and so forth—up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, undivided, inseparable, and not distinct.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, and the body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the various feelings arising with contact as a condition, up to those arising with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
