“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
"Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of non-existence; the purity of non-existence is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of conditioned formations up to aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of sentient beings.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is itself the purity of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the four right endeavors, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the emptiness gate of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of sentient beings is itself the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation; the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation is itself the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
This purity of sentient beings and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the five eyes is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the six supernormal knowledges; the purity of the six supernormal knowledges is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the six supernormal knowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
The purity of sentient beings and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of sentient beings.”
Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all gateways of samādhi; the purity of all gateways of samādhi is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
This purity of sentient beings and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual; they are not divided into two, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the purity of sentient beings and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the fruits of the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of sentient beings. Why is this?
This purity of sentient beings and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of sentient beings is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of sentient beings.

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of sentient beings is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is the purity of sentient beings.”

Why is this? Because the purity of these sentient beings and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and this purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; and the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the life-principle.
Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*); the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is itself the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to the form realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all feelings produced with the fragrance-element up to the feeling produced with nose-contact as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is itself the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
The purity of this living being and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the living being is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the living being.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the various feelings produced with the gustatory element as object and with tongue-contact as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition; and the purity of the contact-element up to all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the various feelings produced with the contact-element, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the mental constituent; the purity of the mental constituent is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the mental element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness element, and the feeling produced with mental contact as its condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the feeling produced with mental contact as its condition is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the non-existent; the purity of the non-existent is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of non-arising (*anutpāda*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is the purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because the purity of this life-principle and the purity of the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll One Hundred and Ninety-three, translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Ten. "Subhūti!..."
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*); and the purity of these perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the pure precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersal emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), non-alteration emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential nature emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), common characteristic emptiness (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), unapprehendable emptiness (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*). The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of suchness (*tathatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharma (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is itself the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because the purity of this life-principle and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is itself the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
The purity of this life-principle and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the signless and wishless doors of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle (*jīva*) and the purity of the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), great compassion (*karuṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*muditā*), great equanimity (*upekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*). The purity of these qualities, from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities, is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is itself the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
The purity of this life-principle and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the life-principle.
Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
The purity of this living being and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the living being is itself the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is itself the purity of the living being.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the life-principle.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all dhāraṇī-gates are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all doors of samādhi; the purity of all doors of samādhi is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the life-principle is itself the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is itself the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the life-principle. Why is this?
This purity of the life-principle and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the life-principle is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the life-principle.

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the life-principle is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the life-principle.”

Why is this? Because this purity of the life-principle and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the one who is born is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the one who is born and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? This purity of birth and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
The purity of the being and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the being.
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the being and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
The purity of the being and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
The purity of the being and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu), and the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
This purity of the being and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the various feelings produced with the olfactory element up to those produced with nose-contact as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
The purity of the being and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as object, up to those produced with tongue-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
This purity of the being and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the various feelings produced with contact as a condition—extending from the sphere of contact up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the mental element (manodhātu); the purity of the mental element is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the being and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—up to the dharma-realm—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
This purity of the being and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the being is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the being.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of non-arising; the purity of non-arising is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the one who is born and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is the purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), clinging (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the being is itself the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is itself the purity of the being.”

Why is this? Because this purity of the one who gives birth and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the being is the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the being.

Why is this? This purity of birth and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the "one who is born" and the purity of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is the purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersed emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), unchanging emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*). The purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the one who is born and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. The purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the purity of the one who is born.
Why is this? Because the purity of this arising and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of birth is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of birth. Why is this?
The purity of this "one who is born" and the purity of the Noble Truth of Suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is itself the purity of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path; the purity of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path is itself the purity of the one who is born.
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
The purity of this "one who is born" and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the one who is born.
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the one who is born and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the one who is born is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the one who is born. Why is that?
The purity of this arising is non-dual with the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not severed.

The purity of arising is itself the purity of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of arising.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the emptiness gate of liberation; the purity of the emptiness gate of liberation is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
The purity of this arising and the purity of the emptiness liberation door are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of arising is itself the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors; the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is itself the purity of arising.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of birth is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of birth. Why is this?
This purity of birth and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the six supernormal powers; the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of the one who is born is non-dual with, indivisible from, undifferentiated from, and inseparable from the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers.

The purity of the one who is born is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
The purity of this "being born" and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the being born is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the being born.
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of birth is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of birth. Why is this?
This purity of the one who is born is non-dual with the purity of all-knowledge; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and it is not severed.

The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the one who is born.

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of birth is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of birth.”
Why is this? This purity of birth and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the sentient being is the purity of all doors of samādhi; the purity of all doors of samādhi is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
This purity of birth and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the sentient being is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the sentient being. Why is this?
Because this purity of the sentient being and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the person is the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this birth and the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the one who is born is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the one who is born. Why is this?
This purity of birth and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the being is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the being.
Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of birth is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of birth.”

Why is this? Because this purity of birth and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; and the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the sphere of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition. The purity of the form-element, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nurturer’s purity and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. The purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nurturer’s purity and the purity of all feelings arising with ear-contact as a condition, up to and including the sound-element, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, undivided, inseparable, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nurturer is pure, and the various sensations produced with the fragrance-element and even nose-contact as conditions are pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition. The purity of the taste-element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nurturer is pure and the various feelings produced with the taste element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the body element; the purity of the body element is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the body element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the contact element, the body-consciousness element, and the feeling produced with body-contact as its condition; the purity of the contact element up to the feeling produced with body-contact as its condition is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nourisher is pure and the various feelings produced with contact as a condition—up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition; conversely, the purity of the dharma-element up to all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this nurturer’s purity and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the nourisher.
Why is this? Because this nourisher is pure and the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nourisher is the purity of non-arising; the purity of non-arising is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of ignorance; these two are non-dual, not divided, without distinction, and inseparable.

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the nurturer.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the nurturer.
Why is this? Because this nurturer’s purity and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of internal emptiness; these two are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. The purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of suchness; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. The purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? This purity of the nourisher and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nurturer and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the nurturer is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the eight liberations; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? This purity of the nourisher is non-dual with the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; these two are non-dual, not divided, distinct, nor discontinuous.

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the nurturer.”
Why is this? This purity of the nurturer and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the signless and wishless gates of liberation; the purity of the signless and wishless gates of liberation is the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness, wishlessness, and emptiness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the nurturer.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the six supernormal powers; the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nourisher is non-dual with the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the nourisher is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the nourisher.

Why is this? Because the purity of this nurturer and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the nurturer.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the equanimity of constant abiding; the purity of the equanimity of constant abiding is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
This purity of the nourisher and the purity of the constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the nourisher. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? Because this nourisher’s purity and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nourisher is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the nourisher.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the nourisher is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the nourisher.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nourisher and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
