“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the nurturer. Why is this?
The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; these two are non-dual, not divided, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is the purity of the nurturer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this nurturer and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the nourisher is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the nourisher."
Why is this? Because the purity of this nurturer and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the nurturer.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the nurturer and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! The purity of the nurturer is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the nurturer."

Why is this? Because the purity of this nurturer and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the person is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the sense-sphere of form; the purity of the sense-sphere of form is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the sphere of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is itself the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the forms of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual, undivided, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the sounds-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the various feelings produced with the nose-element and so forth as conditions for contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, and the body-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the various feelings produced with the contact element as condition, up to those produced with body-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and the feelings produced with mental-contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to the feelings produced with mental-contact as condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the person. Why is that?
The purity of this person and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the noble silence; the purity of the noble silence is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because this person’s purity and the purity of the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is itself the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the emptiness gate of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation; the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is itself the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the person is the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the person is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the person is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of this person is the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā); the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of this person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is itself the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the person is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the person is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the person. Why is this?
Because this purity of the person and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the person is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable. "Subhūti!
The purity of the person is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the person is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the eye-base are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the person is itself the purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; the purity of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the person. Why is that?
The purity of this person and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is itself the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the forms of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the sounds-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person (*pudgala*) and the purity of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition; and the purity of the odor-element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the various feelings produced with the fragrance-element up to the nose-contact as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the tongue element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the taste element, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the body element (*kāyadhātu*); the purity of the body element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person (*pudgala*) and the purity of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the sensations produced with contact as a condition, from the sphere of contact up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of everything from the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of non-arising; the purity of non-arising is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of the person (*pudgala*) and the purity of ignorance are non-dual; they are not divided into two, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the person is the purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), clinging (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person (*pudgala*) and the purity of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is itself the purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersion emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), non-alteration emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential nature emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), common characteristic emptiness (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*). The purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person (pudgala) is the purity of suchness (tathatā), and the purity of suchness is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person (*pudgala*) and the purity of suchness (*tathatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the person is the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the Noble Truth of Suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The purity of the person is the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
The purity of the person is the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the person."
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*); the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the emptiness gate of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

The purity of the person is the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person (pudgala) is the purity of the ten stages (bhūmi) of a bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this *pudgala* and the purity of the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is itself the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the person is itself the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is itself the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this *pudgala* and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the person (pudgala) is the purity of the state of constant equanimity; the purity of the state of constant equanimity is the purity of the person. Why is this?
This purity of the person and the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is the purity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and the purity of omniscience is the purity of the person. Why is this?
The purity of this person (*pudgala*) and the purity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the person is the purity of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the person is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the person.
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is itself the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is itself the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the person is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the person.

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the person (*pudgala*) is itself the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is itself the purity of the person.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the person is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is the purity of the person.”

Why is this? Because the purity of this person and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll One Hundred and Ninety-Two. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter Thirty-Four on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding, Part Twelve. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind is the purity of the sense-sphere of the eye; the purity of the sense-sphere of the eye is the purity of the mind. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the sense-base of the eye; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and it is not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born is non-dual with, indivisible from, undifferentiated from, and inseparable from the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the mind. Why is this?
The purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the sense-base of form; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the mind. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the eye-element; it is not divided into two, is not distinct, and is not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition. The purity of the form-element, up to and including all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all feelings arising with eye-contact as a condition, up to the form realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the mind. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the ear-element; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and it is not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and the ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition. The purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the mind is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the mind. Why is this?
This purity of the mental faculty (*manas*) and the purity of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct, and they are not severed.

The purity of the mental faculty is itself the purity of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) as a condition. The purity of the odor-element up to the sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the mental faculty.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all feelings produced with the nose-object as condition, up to the nose-contact as condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind is itself the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is itself the purity of the mind. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the tongue-element; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and it is not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition. The purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element up to tongue-contact as conditions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mental faculty is itself the purity of the body element; the purity of the body element is itself the purity of the mental faculty. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the body element; it is not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the touch element, the body-consciousness element, and the body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. The purity of the touch element, up to and including all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of all feelings produced with contact as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition; and the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the earth element; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the unconditioned; the purity of the unconditioned is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born and this purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of [the links of dependent origination] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the perfection of giving; the purity of the perfection of giving is the purity of the mind-born.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of internal emptiness; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. The purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the noble truth of suffering; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the four dhyānas; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [consciousness] and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is itself the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the eight liberations; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; it is not divided into two, is not distinct, and is not severed.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.

This purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; this purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-made body and the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born is non-dual with the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and there is no separation between them.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is itself the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
The purity of the mind-born and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is itself the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [wisdom] and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is itself the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is itself the purity of the mind-born.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of all doors of samādhi; the purity of all doors of samādhi is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the mind-born. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the mind-born.

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the mental faculty is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the mental faculty. Why is this?
This purity of the mind-born and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the mind-born is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the mind-born.
Why is this? Because this purity of the mind-born and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the mind-born is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the mind-born.”

Why is this? Because the purity of this mind-born [nature] and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the sense-base of the eye; the purity of the sense-base of the eye is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the sense-base of form; the purity of the sense-base of form is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the sphere of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth is non-dual with, indivisible from, undifferentiated from, and inseparable from the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to the form realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the auditory element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the sound element, the auditory consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (Māṇavaka) and the purity of the various sensations produced with the fragrance-element up to the nose-contact as condition are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the various feelings produced with conditions ranging from the taste-element up to tongue-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the body-element (kāyadhātu), and the purity of the body-element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of the body-element (kāyadhātu) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth is itself the purity of the contact-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), and the feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the contact-element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is itself the purity of the youth.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of all feelings produced with contact as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the mind-element (manodhātu) are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalaka) and the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the light of wisdom; the purity of the light of wisdom is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the youth.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of the precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. The purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of dharma (dharmasthititā), the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (Māṇavaka) and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The purity of the youth is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.
