Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (Māṇavaka) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is itself the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is itself the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita)—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the Youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the six supernormal powers; the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇavaka) and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of omniscience; the purity of omniscience is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is itself the purity of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is itself the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (maṇḍalika) and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the youth."
Why is this? Because this purity of the youth and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
This purity of the Youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī. Why is this?
Because this purity of the youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the youth. Why is this?
This purity of the Youth Mañjuśrī and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the youth Mañjuśrī is the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī.

Why is this? Because this purity of the youth (mañjuśrī) and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the youth is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the youth.”

Why is this? Because the purity of this youth and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the agent is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; and the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the sense-field of form; the purity of the sense-field of form is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to the sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to the form realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the auditory element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the sound element, the auditory consciousness element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the soundsphere, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as condition is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the various sensations produced with the nose-sphere as a condition, up to those produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the various feelings produced with the gustatory element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition; the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as their condition is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the various feelings arising with the sphere of touch as a condition, up to those arising with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are non-dual, undivided, inseparable, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of all feelings arising with mind-contact as a condition—up to and including the dharma-realm—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the agent is the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of non-action; the purity of non-action is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is the purity of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), clinging (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; the purity of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the perfection of giving; the purity of the perfection of giving is the purity of the agent.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
This purity of the agent and the purity of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersion emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), non-alteration emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential nature emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), common characteristic emptiness (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), unapprehendable emptiness (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*). The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
This purity of the agent and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm; the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the four right endeavors, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the emptiness liberation door are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors; the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
This purity of the agent and the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of the agent is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The purity of the agent is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.
The purity of the agent is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
The purity of the agent and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā); the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the agent.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the agent is the purity of all gateways of samādhi; the purity of all gateways of samādhi is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
This purity of the agent and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the agent is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

The purity of the agent is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the agent.

Why is this? Because the purity of the agent and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the agent. Why is this?
This purity of the agent and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the agent is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the agent.
Why is this? Because this purity of the agent and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the agent is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the agent.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this agent and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the feeler is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the feeler. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the sense-sphere of form; the purity of the sense-sphere of form is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the sphere of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; the purity of the form-element through to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of all feelings arising with eye-contact as a condition, up to those of the form realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of all feelings arising with conditions such as the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and the contact of the nose, as well as all feelings produced with that nose-contact as a condition; and the purity of the odor-element up to all feelings produced with that nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the various feelings produced with the nose-contact as a condition, extending from the fragrance-element onwards, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual; they are not divided, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition. The purity of the taste-element, up to and including all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the various feelings arising with the taste element as a condition, up to those arising with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the contact-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the various feelings produced with contact as a condition—extending from the sphere of contact up to the body-contact—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the mind-element (manodhātu), and the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of all feelings arising with mind-contact as a condition, up to the dharma-realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from nothing, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of ignorance; the purity of ignorance is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the recipient is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the recipient.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the recipient and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the recipient is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of the recipient.

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the pure precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the nature of non-falsity, the nature of non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this experiencer and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this recipient and the purity of the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is itself the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this recipient and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
This purity of the recipient and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the recipient is the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the recipient. Why is this?
Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the experiencer and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the experiencer and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the experiencer is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the experiencer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
The purity of the recipient and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the recipient is the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā); the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the recipient.
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the experiencer.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the experiencer is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
This purity of the recipient and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the recipient is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the recipient. Why is this?
Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is the purity of the experiencer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha is the purity of the experiencer. Why is this?
This purity of the recipient and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the recipient is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the recipient.
Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! The purity of the experiencer is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the experiencer."

Why is this? Because this purity of the recipient and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the knower is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of form are non-dual, not two, distinct, and inseparable.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the sense-sphere of form; the purity of the sense-sphere of form is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and phenomena is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct from nothing, and there is no separation between them.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the eye-consciousness-element; the purity of the eye-consciousness-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; the purity of the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the forms of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all feelings produced with the sound-element and even ear-contact as conditions are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and the sensations produced with nose-contact as their condition; and the purity of the odor-element up to the sensations produced with nose-contact as their condition is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all feelings produced with the nose-element as a condition, up to those produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as a condition, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the body-element (kāyadhātu) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), as well as body-contact (kāyasparśa) and all feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the various feelings produced with the sphere of touch as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
The purity of the knower and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—up to the dharma-realm—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of non-arising; the purity of non-arising is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of everything from formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the perfection of giving; the purity of the perfection of giving is the purity of the knower.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline up to wisdom is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the pure precepts, up to and including the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersed emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), unchanging emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-characteristic (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of common characteristic (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*). The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is itself the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the emptiness gate of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation; the purity of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 194, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Thirty-Four, Section Fourteen: "Difficult to Believe and Understand. "Subhūti!..."
The purity of the knower is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the knower is the purity of the six supernormal powers; the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and inseparable.

The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the knower is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
This purity of the knower and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the knower is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is itself the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is itself the purity of the knower.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all dharani-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the knower is the purity of all doors of samādhi; the purity of all doors of samādhi is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Thus, the purity of this knower and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the knower is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the knower is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the knower.

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the knower. Why is this?
Thus, the purity of this knower and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the knower is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the knower.
Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the knower is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the knower.”

Why is this? Because this purity of the knower and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of the seer is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the sphere of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to the purity of all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, inseparable, and not distinct.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of all feelings arising with ear-contact as a condition, up to the sound-element, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the nose-element; the purity of the nose-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of all feelings produced with the nose-object as a condition, up to the nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of all feelings arising with tongue-contact as a condition—extending from the taste-element—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the body-element (kāyadhātu) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), body-contact (kāyasparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition; likewise, the purity of the touch-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the various feelings produced with contact as a condition—up to and including those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the mind-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition. The purity of the dharma-element up to the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, up to and including the dharma-realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
