“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the earth element are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the elements of water, fire, air, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of non-arising; the purity of non-arising is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of everything from formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of the seer.”
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; and the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is itself the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gateway to liberation that is emptiness is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the emptiness liberation door are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the signless and wishless liberation doors; the purity of the signless and wishless liberation doors is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the signless and wishless doors of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted. "Subhūti!
The purity of the seer is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the seer is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and this purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
The purity of the seer and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of the seer is itself the purity of the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is itself the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of the seer.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of the seer is the purity of all doors of samādhi; the purity of all doors of samādhi is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
This purity of the seer and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of the seer is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of the seer. Why is this?
Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of the seer is the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of the seer.

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of the seer. Why is that?
This purity of the seer and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti!..."
The purity of the seer is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of the seer.
Why is this? Because this purity of the seer and the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of the seer is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of the seer.”

Why is this? Because the purity of this seer and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the self is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, if the purity of form, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because I am pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the self, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the sense base of the eye, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the self, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of self, purity of the sense-sphere of form, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the self, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, if there is purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and if there is purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the self is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because I am pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the self is pure, if the sphere of sound up to the sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because I am pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If my purity, if the purity of the nose element, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because I am pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure; because the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the self is pure, if the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, and if all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the self is pure, and if the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the body-element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of the body-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because I am pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the self is pure, and if the objects of touch up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because my intention is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the mental realm (*manodhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because I am pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as their condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the self is pure, and if the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the self, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be my own purity, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because my formations are pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the self, or the purity of [the factors] from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the self, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of self, purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of self, purity of internal emptiness, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because I am pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, if there is purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and if there is purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be my own purity, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the self, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of self, purity of the noble truth of suffering, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because I am pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because I am pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because I am pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because I am pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the self, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because I am pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

If there is purity of self, purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because I am pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the self, the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be my own purity, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because I am pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be my purity, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If my purity, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the self is pure, the purity of the state of equanimity (*upekṣā*) is constant; because the purity of the state of equanimity is constant, the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is realized. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the self, the purity of the state of equanimity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because I am pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowing is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of the self, purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), purity of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the self, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because I am pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because I am pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If my purity, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because I am pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the self, the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because I am pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If my purity, the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because I am pure, all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it is my own purity, the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because I am pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because my purity, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because sentient beings are pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the sense base of the eye, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the sense-base of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sound element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if sentient beings are pure, and if the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 195. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Fifteen: "Subhūti!
Because sentient beings are pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it is the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if sentient beings are pure, if the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the body realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if sentient beings are pure, and if the objects of touch up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the sentient beings are pure, the mind-element (manodhātu) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the mental constituent (*manodhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because sentient beings are pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of non-sentient things, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of [the links of dependent origination] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because sentient beings are pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because sentient beings are pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if sentient beings are pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because sentient beings are pure, the six superknowledges are pure; because the six superknowledges are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the six superknowledges, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because sentient beings are pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because sentient beings are pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because sentient beings are pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because sentient beings are pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure; because all gateways to meditative concentration are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because sentient beings are pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because sentient beings are pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of sentient beings, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the life-principle is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*), the sphere of ear-consciousness (*śrotravijñānadhātu*), ear-contact (*śrotrasaṃsparśa*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the life-principle is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

"Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
