Because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle (*jīva*), the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the life-principle is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) is pure; because the unconditioned is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the non-self, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the self is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, or the purity of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the self is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. Because there is the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, there is the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the immutability, the equanimity, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharma (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle (*jīva*), the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the self is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the self is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the life-principle is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the life-principle is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the life-principle is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the life-principle (*jīva*) is pure, the state of abiding in equanimity (*upekṣā*) is pure; because the state of abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of omniscience, or the purity of the knowledge of omniscience, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the self is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the life-principle is pure, the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is pure; because the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the life-principle (*jīva*), the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the life-principle, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because birth is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of form, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because birth is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because arising is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the sense base of the eye, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

If there is purity of birth, purity of the sense-base of form, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because birth is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the realm of sentient beings is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the arising is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the producer is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if birth is pure, and if the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Because the producer is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the birth [of phenomena] is pure, if the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the arising is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the producer is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if birth is pure, and if the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of the body element, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the producer is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are pure. Because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the sense-field of contact up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the mental constituent (*manodhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the sense-sphere of phenomena is pure, the sphere of mental consciousness, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of phenomena up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of birth, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because birth is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of arising, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because birth is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, or the purity of the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 196. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Sixteen. "Subhūti!..."
Because the producer is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the producer is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of internal emptiness, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the producer is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of arising, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the producer is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of the noble truth of suffering, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
Because birth is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of arising, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of the four dhyānas, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because birth is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is purity of birth, purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because arising is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of the eight liberations, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because birth is pure, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if birth is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of birth, purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because birth is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of arising, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of arising, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because birth is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of arising, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the one who is born is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the one who is born, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If birth is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the producer is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the birth [of a Buddha] is pure, if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of arising, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because birth is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If birth is pure, if the nature of constant equanimity is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If birth is pure, if omniscience is pure, and if the knowledge of omniscience is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because birth is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because arising is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because birth is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of arising, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the state of being born is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of one who is born, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because birth is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of birth, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the nourisher is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the one who nurtures is pure, and if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nourisher is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the one who nurtures is pure, if the eye-base is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nourisher is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because if the nourisher is pure, and if the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nourisher is pure, if the sense-base of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nourisher is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, and if all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the nourisher is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nurturer is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is pure, the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the realm of form up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the one who nurtures, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the nourisher is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nourisher is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nourisher is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the sphere of sound up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nourisher is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nourisher is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nourisher is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the objects of fragrance, up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure, and if all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, then these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nourisher is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the nourisher is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure. Because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the nourisher is pure, and if the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, then these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nourisher is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nurturer is pure, if the body-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nourisher is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, and body-contact—as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are pure. Because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the feelings produced with contact as a condition—ranging from the element of tangibility up to body-contact—are pure, and if all-knowledge is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the nurturer is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?
If the realm of nourishment is pure, if the mental element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the sphere of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is pure, the sphere of mental consciousness (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of phenomena up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the dharma-realm, up to and including all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the nourisher is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nurturer is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nourisher is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nourisher is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the nourisher is pure, if the one who clarifies is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nourisher is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the nourisher is pure, then everything from the process of existence up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is pure; and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the one who nurtures, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

Because the nurturer is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the one who nurtures is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the nourisher is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the one who nurtures is pure, and if the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nurturer, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the nourisher is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the one who nurtures, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the nurturer is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all aspects (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?"
If the one who nurtures is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if all-knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nourisher is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.
