Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the mind-born is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born [consciousness], the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the mind-born is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the mind is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born [consciousness], the purity of the sphere of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the mind-born is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the mind is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born [consciousness], the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the mind-born is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the sphere of contact up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the mind, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the mind is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are pure. Because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind-born is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the mind is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, non-duality is pure; because non-duality is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of non-discrimination, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the mind-born is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born [consciousness], the purity of the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the mind-born is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the mind-born, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the mind-born is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because of the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born [wisdom], the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the mind-born is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind-born is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the mind-born is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the mind-born, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the mind-born is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the mind-born, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the mind-born is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born [body], the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, are non-dual; they are not two, they are undifferentiated, and there is no division between them.
"Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the mind-born, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the mind-born is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the mental faculty is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll One Hundred and Ninety-eight. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Eighteen. "Subhūti!
Because the mind-born is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the mind-born is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the mind-born is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the mind-born is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the mind-born, if the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the mind-born, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the mind-born is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the mind-born is pure, all gateways of samādhi are pure; because all gateways of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the mind-born, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the mind-born is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the mind is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the mind-born, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct neither in nature nor in substance.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the youth is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the youth, the purity of the sense-field of the eye, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth, the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the youth is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (maṇḍalaka), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure. Because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (maṇavaka), the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the youth, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), or the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the youth is pure, if the nose-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), the purity of the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the youth is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the youth is pure, if the sphere of tangibles—and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the realm of mind is purified through the purification of the noble youth’s intention, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is purified because the realm of mind is purified. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī, the purity of the mental realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), or the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the youth Mañjuśrī, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), the purity of the stainless one (Vimala), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the youth Mañjuśrī is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth (Māṇavaka), or the purity of the factors from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the youth, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the youth is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Nineteen: The Chapter on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, because the recipient is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the recipient, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the experiencer is pure, all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the recipient, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the recipient is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the recipient, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knower is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the knower is pure, and if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the eye-base is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knower is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, if the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure. Because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knower is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure. Because the sound element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, and if the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, and if all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knower is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, if the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the body element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knower is pure, the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the sphere of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure. Because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, and if the objects of touch, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the mental faculty (manodhātu) is pure; because the mental faculty is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, or the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if non-manifestation is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knower is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, and if everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knower is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knower, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knower is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knower, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knower is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
Because the knower is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knower, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knower is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of the knower, purity of the eight liberations, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knower is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knower is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the knower is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the knower is pure, if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knower is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knower, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if all-knowledge is pure, and if the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knower is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowing is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of all dharani-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knower is pure, all gateways of samādhi are pure; because all gateways of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knower is pure, if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knower is pure, the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knower, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knower is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knower, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred.
